# Gradus for Android — Product Requirements Document

**Status:** Draft v1 for review · **Owner:** Mariah Gillespie · **Author:** Claude Code · **Date:** 2026-10-11 · **Amended:** 2026-10-13 (Mariah's answers, A41–A49; iOS decisions #51–#54) · 2026-10-14 (A37: direct link-out, no External Content Links) · 2026-10-17 (Show, don't tell design system; iOS changes through gradus-ios c8f83d6, decision #55)
**Repos:** backend and web `mariah-gill/gradus-coach-start` (this PRD lives at `docs/android/PRD.md`, A9) · iOS reference implementation `mariah-gill/gradus-ios` at HEAD `c8f83d6` (reconciled 2026-10-17; the PRD was first written against `91c6af2`, contract pinned to web `fd543a12`; decisions #51–#53 read at `fd78810`, #54 at `0dc28a9`, #55 and every iOS commit through `c8f83d6` reconciled 2026-10-17, contract web `c678ccf4`) · native Android app `mariah-gill/gradus-android` (to be created, A7) · **Web app:** https://gradus.training · **applicationId:** `training.gradus.app` (phone and Wear OS, one Play listing) · **iOS spec this mirrors:** `docs/ios/PRD.md` (decisions #1–#55)

This document specifies the native Kotlin app for Android phones and Wear OS watches. It does not invent a product. Mariah made every product decision once, in the iOS PRD and in the iOS app; this PRD applies each of them to Android and names, for every iOS-native element, the Android-native element that replaces it. It is written to be executed by Claude Code with Mariah reviewing, so it names endpoints, screens, copy, flags, limits and tests, and it records the decisions already made so later sessions do not re-litigate them.

**How to read it.** Sections 1–5 are the "why" and the rules; §4.3 is the parity contract that governs every other section. Section 6 is the architecture, which is the iOS architecture with Android components swapped in and a short list of server additions (§5.1, Appendix A). Section 7 is the feature inventory, one subsection per iOS §7 subsection, each requirement cited to its iOS source as (iOS §x.y / #nn / path). Sections 8–9 are design and engineering standards; §10 is the milestone sequence; §11–§12 are risks and open decisions. Appendix G is the iOS→Android platform mapping table that every section leans on. Where the iOS PRD text and the iOS code (read at `91c6af2`, reconciled through `c8f83d6`) disagree, the **code wins** (A2), and the place where it matters says so. Decision numbers: **#n** is an iOS decision (iOS PRD §0); **An** is an Android decision (§0 table 1).

**Contents**

## 0. Decision log

Three tables. Table 1 holds the Android decisions: A1–A10 are settled (Mariah, 2026-10-11); A11 onward are **proposed** by this PRD for Mariah's confirmation and stand as defaults until she changes them. Table 1b records Mariah's later iOS decisions that live only in the iOS code or handoffs. Table 2 takes every iOS decision, #1 through #55, and states what it means on Android. None is skipped.

**Table 1 — Android decisions**

| # | Decision | Status | Choice |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | First Play release | **Settled** 2026-10-11 | The native Kotlin app is the **first Google Play release, version 1.0** (`versionName 1.0.0`), applicationId `training.gradus.app`. The Capacitor Android shell never ships; this closes iOS §12 #14 and drops iOS milestone C2 and Appendix F Phase D. The web repo's `android/`, `capacitor.config.ts`, `native/` and `@capacitor/*` dependencies can be removed once Mariah agrees (they are inert on the web; iOS §9.1, §7.14). |
| A2 | Full parity with iOS 1.0 | **Settled** | Android applies **every** iOS product decision identically: copy, flows, rules, flags, limits, privacy and consent rules, and what is hidden in 1.0 (Ask Gradus behind a release flag, #22; library-rights filtering, #23; minors text-only, #32/#48; and the rest of table 2). The only permitted differences are where iOS uses an iOS-native behavior or component; Android then uses the Android-native equivalent (Appendix G). When the iOS PRD and the iOS code at HEAD disagree, the **code wins**, and the PRD says so where it matters. |
| A3 | Wear OS in 1.0 | **Settled** | A Wear OS app ships in 1.0, **in the same Play listing**, with the same five headphones-first workflows as the Apple Watch app (#36, #47, #48; iOS §6.15): voice→plan (adult athlete, coach), deploy a plan, plan→audio with a full read, the pre-lesson briefing spoken on tap only, and the post-lesson wrap-up by voice. Design §6.15, requirements §7.15. |
| A4 | Phones only in 1.0 | **Settled** | Mirrors #50. Tablets and foldables can install the app and get the phone layout (single column, max readable width, no list-detail panes, no navigation rail). Targeting API 36 means the system ignores orientation, resizability and aspect-ratio restrictions on displays ≥ 600 dp, so the phone layout must be fully resizable and edge-to-edge there without relying on letterboxing (§4.2). Adaptive layouts (window size classes) are specified and deferred, like iPad. Play listing carries phone screenshots only; no tablet screenshots (§11 risk A-22 covers Play's large-screen quality signals). |
| A5 | Sign-in methods | **Settled** | **Google** (Credential Manager, Sign in with Google), **email or username + password**, and **Sign in with Apple through a web flow**, so an account created with Apple on an iPhone signs in on Android to the same Gradus account. Same auth-broker design as iOS §6.4: the API mints the Supabase session; Android never depends on a provider setting Lovable Cloud does not expose. Unlike iOS at HEAD, where the Google button is hidden until `GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID` exists (`SignInModel.isGoogleAvailable`, `StubGoogleSignInProvider` in `Gradus/Dependencies.swift`), Android shows Google from 1.0; the same "hide when not configured" rule applies if the Android client is not configured at build time. |
| A6 | SDK levels | **Settled** | `minSdk 29` (Android 10). `targetSdk` = the level Google Play requires at submission (API 36 for new apps since 2026-08-31, §4.2). `compileSdk` = latest stable. |
| A7 | Start now, same working model | **Settled** | Android work starts now, in parallel with iOS QA. Repo `mariah-gill/gradus-android` (#13). Claude Code builds, Mariah reviews daily; milestone-driven, no time estimates or dates (#11, #12). |
| A8 | Play Console account | **Settled** | No Google Play Console account exists yet. It must be an **Organization** account for **Gradus Sports, Inc.**, using the D-U-N-S number from Apple enrollment. Until it exists: no internal testing track, no Play App Signing key (so no final App Links certificate fingerprint and no final Android OAuth client), no Play Integrity linkage, no listing. FCM needs only a Firebase project and is not blocked. |
| A9 | Where the PRD lives | **Settled** | `gradus-coach-start/docs/android/PRD.md`, beside `docs/ios/PRD.md`. |
| A10 | Storefront and payments | **Settled** | **US only** at launch (#25): Play country availability = United States. **No in-app purchase** (#8): no Play Billing purchase flow. Entitlement is displayed; the "Manage your plan at gradus.training" link-out appears for US users only, under Google Play's US external-link rules (§4.2, §6.8). |
| A11 | Stack | Proposed | Kotlin 2.x; Jetpack Compose + Material 3 themed with Gradus tokens (**no dynamic color**, #10); Navigation Compose with type-safe routes; coroutines + Flow; Hilt; Room (offline store and outbox); DataStore (preferences); WorkManager (sync drain, the iOS `BGAppRefreshTask` role); OkHttp + Retrofit client generated from `openapi.json` with openapi-generator (`kotlin`, kotlinx.serialization), subject to the OpenAPI 3.1 generation spike in the foundation milestone (§11 A-26); supabase-kt for Auth session, Realtime and Storage only (the supabase-swift scope, iOS §6.3); Firebase Cloud Messaging only (no Firebase Analytics, no Crashlytics); Credential Manager; BiometricPrompt; Android Keystore + Tink-encrypted DataStore; Play Integrity; Media3 ExoPlayer; MediaRecorder (AAC `.m4a`, 24 kHz, mono, ~32 kbps, iOS §6.7); Android TextToSpeech; photo picker + the system camera (`ActivityResultContracts.TakePicture`, no `CAMERA` permission; CameraX is not needed for a single shot, §7.2.15); Glance widgets; ongoing notifications (Android 16 Live Updates where eligible); Compose for Wear OS + Data Layer API; Gradle version catalogs; JUnit 5, Turbine, Robolectric, Compose UI tests, Roborazzi screenshots; GitHub Actions + Gradle Play Publisher; Baseline Profiles. §9 owns the detail. |
| A12 | Live Activities → notifications | Proposed | **Session timer:** an ongoing notification with a chronometer (`setUsesChronometer`, base = start timestamp minus accumulated pause), local only (iOS §12 #10 default), promoted as an Android 16 Live Update where the system allows. The timer is timestamp-based (iOS §6.5), so **no foreground service** is needed for correctness; the notification is presentation only. It shows `planTitle` and the athlete's and coach's first names (`GradusActivities/SessionActivityAttributes.swift`: `planTitle`, `athleteFirstName`, `coachFirstName`; tap opens `gradus://plans/<planId>`). Because Android 14+ lets the user swipe away an ongoing notification not tied to a foreground service (§4.2), **dismissing it never stops or changes the session**: a `deleteIntent` marks it dismissed for this session (persisted with the session), and it is **not** re-posted until a new session starts, matching iOS, where a dismissed Live Activity is not re-requested (§7.6.4 owns the rules). **"Still practicing?"** (`LiveSessionReminders`, `FeatureSessions/SessionActivityController.swift`) is a one-shot `AlarmManager.setAndAllowWhileIdle` (inexact, Doze-safe, no `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM`), scheduled when the app backgrounds **from the runner screen** with a running timer (iOS scope, §6.6.7; an app-wide hook is §12 N52), firing after `max(60 s, delay)` with the nominal delay one hour (§4.3 rule 5); title "Still practicing?", body "Your session on \(planTitle) is still running. Open Gradus to pause or end it." verbatim; cancelled on foreground or session end; skipped when notifications are not allowed (permission was asked when the session started, §4.2). Not WorkManager: it can be deferred for hours in the rare/restricted standby buckets. **Live Board:** an FCM data message for a followed skater posts or updates an ongoing notification (skater, start position, lane state, score; compact text "#4 of 12"), the push-to-start equivalent; removed when the event is final; app-driven updates while foregrounded (iOS §6.9). |
| A13 | US-storefront check | Proposed | iOS gates every link-out on `Storefront.current?.countryCode == "USA"` at five sites since iOS #156 removed the invoicing gate: `FeatureGuardians/Team/TeamGuardiansSection.swift`, `FeatureOnboarding/PlanStatusView.swift`, `FeatureResources/UploadResourceSheet.swift`, `FeatureSettings/Account/CoachPlanView.swift`, `FeatureSettings/Parent/TeamPlanView.swift`. A sixth link, "Choose Coach Pro on gradus.training" in `FeatureSettings/Profile/CoachSportsView.swift`, is **ungated on iOS**; Android gates it like the rest because Google Play's external-link rules are US-only (§6.8 table; §12 N61). Android has **one `StorefrontRepository`** (§6.8, `isUSStorefront`) used at these six link-out points, each also gated on the `androidExternalLinksEnabled` remote kill switch (A37: default true, on at launch; no External Content Links enrollment), with a test per site that the link is absent for non-US and unknown. Android uses the Play Billing Library's `BillingClient.getBillingConfigAsync()` **country code only** (no product is ever queried or sold) and shows the link only when it returns `US`. Unknown, error, or no Play services → **no link** (iOS treats a nil storefront as non-US). Result cached per process. |
| A14 | Read-aloud voice on Android | Proposed | #47 applied: Android `TextToSpeech`, **on-device voices only**; a voice with `isNetworkConnectionRequired == true` or the `KEY_FEATURE_NETWORK_SYNTHESIS` feature is never used (nothing leaves the device). **Automatic** = the most natural installed `en-US` voice (`Voice.quality` `QUALITY_VERY_HIGH` > `QUALITY_HIGH` > lower), a woman's where one is as natural. Android exposes no voice gender, so gender comes from a small in-repo table of known engine voice names (Google speech services' `en-us-x-…` voices first); unknown voices are treated as gender-unknown and ranked by quality only (§12 N10). The picker (`FeatureSettings/Account/ReadAloudVoiceView.swift`) lists English voices, American first, then other English; **each row, and Automatic, plays a short sample** (the iOS sample text and accessibility labels "Play a sample of the automatic voice" / "Play a sample of \(name), \(quality)"; a sample stops when the app leaves the foreground). iOS excludes novelty, Eloquence, classic Mac and Personal Voice voices (`GradusCore/Narration/NarrationVoice.swift` `isNovelty`, `isPersonalVoice`); Android excludes voices whose features include `KEY_FEATURE_NOT_INSTALLED` or network synthesis, voices whose locale is not English, and `QUALITY_VERY_LOW`/`QUALITY_LOW` voices unless nothing else is installed. The two iOS explanation strings ("The most natural voices are free downloads from Apple. …" and "Uses \(voice.name) (\(quality)). Download a Premium voice for a more natural sound.") are rewritten through the §4.3 substitution table, with "Very high quality" / "High quality" / "Standard" for Premium / Enhanced / Standard; §6.7.5 owns the exact Android strings, the "Open voice settings" button, the saved identifier (`"<enginePackage>/<voiceName>"` under `narration.voiceIdentifier`) and the display-name rule. Choice kept per device; the watch uses its own Automatic pick (#47). |
| A15 | Legacy WebM voice notes | **Settled** 2026-10-13 (A43) | iOS at HEAD shows "Can't play this note here yet" for web-recorded WebM notes (`FeatureMessages/Components/Bubbles.swift`; iOS §6.7 policy item 2 was never built). Media3 ExoPlayer decodes WebM/Opus natively on every supported Android version, so Android **plays** them. This is a platform capability, not a product change: the transcript under every voice note (iOS §6.7 item 3, P4) still shows on Android exactly as on iOS. Closes iOS §12 #6 for Android. |
| A16 | Builds and distribution | Proposed | Android App Bundle signed with an **upload key** held in GitHub Actions secrets and backed up offline (Mariah's password manager plus one offline copy); **Play App Signing** holds the app signing key. GitHub Actions builds every push to `main` and, once the Play Console exists (A8), publishes to the **internal testing** track with Gradle Play Publisher (the Xcode Cloud "Archive main to TestFlight" equivalent, iOS §12 #11). `versionCode` is stamped by CI; phone and Wear OS builds in the same listing never share a `versionCode` (phone = `100000 + GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER`, Wear = `200000 + GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER`, §9.6) (verify against Play's multi-form-factor rules). Before the Play Console exists, the interim install channel is A39. |
| A17 | Sign in with Apple web flow | Proposed | Apple publishes no Android SDK, so Android opens Apple's authorize page in an **Auth Tab** (`androidx.browser` `AuthTabIntent`; plain Custom Tab plus App Link fallback where unsupported) with an Apple **Services ID** (proposed `training.gradus.app.signin`, Lovable secret `APPLE_SIWA_SERVICES_ID`) **grouped with the primary App ID `training.gradus.app`** in team `79RN82HXPZ`, so Apple returns the same team-scoped `sub` an iPhone sign-in produced. `response_mode=form_post` to a new server callback `https://gradus.training/api/public/auth/apple/callback` (S-7), which verifies the identity token (audience = the Services ID, in addition to the existing `training.gradus.app`), runs the existing identity lookup and session mint, and redirects to an App Link carrying a one-time, short-lived code that the app exchanges for the session (tokens never appear in a URL). Revocation on account deletion uses the client id that issued the token. §6.4 owns the detail; Appendix A lists the endpoints. |
| A18 | Google on Android | Proposed | Credential Manager `GetSignInWithGoogleOption` (button) and `GetGoogleIdOption` (no auto-select on first run) with a **web OAuth client ID as `serverClientId`** and a hashed nonce; the ID token goes to the existing `POST /auth/google`, whose audience check today accepts only `GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID` (`src/lib/api/provider-verify.ts`) and must also accept `aud == GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID` when `azp` is one of the Android OAuth clients (new secrets `GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_ANDROID_CLIENT_IDS`; server addition S-5; build field `BuildConfig.GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID`). An Android OAuth client (package + SHA-1 of the debug, upload and Play signing certificates) is registered in the same Google Cloud project. Resolves iOS §12 #3 for Android as **broker**. |
| A19 | Diagnostics | Proposed | No third-party crash SDK (iOS §6.11). Caught errors go to `POST /errors` with version and build (the `reportClientError` mirror). The server today writes `platform: "ios"` on **every** row (`src/lib/errors.server.ts`, called via `reportIosError` from `src/routes/api/v1/errors.ts`; `errors-schema.ts` has no platform field, `kind` ∈ `error` / `crash` / `hang`), so an additive server fix comes first: derive the platform from `X-Gradus-Client` (`parseClientHeader`, `src/lib/api/client.ts`), falling back to an optional request field `platform` (request enums may widen, §4.1 rule 15). Android ANRs report `kind: "hang"`, JVM and native crashes `kind: "crash"`. Test: an Android-tagged report appears as Android in the admin errors dashboard. Crashes are captured by an uncaught-exception handler that writes a report to disk and uploads it on next launch; ANRs and native crashes are read from `ActivityManager.getHistoricalProcessExitReasons` (`ApplicationExitInfo`, API 30+) on next launch: the MetricKit equivalent. Play Console Android vitals is the second source once A8 is done. |
| A20 | Age signals on Android | Proposed | #33 applied with Google's equivalent: the **Play Age Signals API** replaces Declared Age Range (iOS §6.13 B1; the iOS PRD already says "Kotlin later uses Google's Play Age Signals API in B's place"). The response carries `ageRangeSource` (TIER_A..D, or null), `ageLower`/`ageUpper`, `significantChangeStatus` (`APPROVED` / `PENDING` / `DECLINED`), `significantChangeApprovalDate` and `installId` (developer.android.com/google/play/age-signals, checked 2026-10-11). **(1) Tighten-only routing:** `ageUpper < 18` blocks coach, parent and adult-athlete sign-up on that device exactly as iOS does; `ageUpper < 13` routes to the parent-only screen; an 18+ result never loosens anything; a null source means "not shared" and never blocks; an unavailable or erroring API falls back to the birthdate path and never blocks. Play's **default** bands (0–12, 13–15, 16–17, 18+) already equal Apple's gates `ageGates: 13, 16, 18`, so **no custom age ranges are configured in Play Console** (each custom minimum can change only once a year; §6.13 B) (`Gradus/Shell/AgeAssurance.swift`, `GradusCore/Onboarding/AgeSignals.swift`). The age band itself stays on the device. **(2) Significant-change gate:** `significantChangeStatus == PENDING` shows the iOS blocking screen (`SignificantChangeCoordinator`, `AgeAssurance.swift`) with its copy verbatim: title "Ask a parent to approve this update", intro "Gradus changed in a way that needs a parent or guardian's OK before you keep using it:", waiting "Once they approve on their device, Gradus opens again here." (kept as-is); `DECLINED` shows `declinedMessage` "Your parent or guardian didn't approve this update, so Gradus stays closed on this device. You can ask again."; the `unavailable` copy is rewritten per §4.3. Significant changes are declared by Mariah in Play Console, mirroring the iOS significant-change registry (`GradusCore/Onboarding/SignificantChanges.swift`). **(3) Revocation parity with `RESCIND_CONSENT`:** Google does **not** signal revoked approvals to the app; it lists them by `installId` in Play Console → Age signals → Revoked app approvals (CSV, kept 90 days) and tells developers to store `installId` on their backend. So athlete sessions only send `installId` to an additive endpoint (proposed `POST /me/play-install`, table `play_age_signal_installs` plus `play_revoked_installs` for ids revoked before anyone bound them, S-11; many-to-many like `app_store_app_transactions` behind `POST /me/app-transaction`, iOS PRD §6.13 B4); an admin job or admin page imports the revoked-`installId` CSV **at least weekly**, inside the 90-day window, and applies the existing pause logic, so Admin → Membership → Paused athletes restores work unchanged (iOS §12 #29). This adds a stored identifier: the Data safety form and the privacy policy (§12 i24) declare it; counsel confirms. **(4)** Play Integrity is recommended alongside Age Signals calls (A21). Texas signals cover only accounts created after 2026-05-28. §12 N12 owns the open points. |
| A21 | Play Integrity | Proposed | The App Attest equivalent (iOS §6.4 "Bot protection", I15, `POST /auth/attest/register`). **Dormant and log-only** in 1.0, exactly as the iOS App Attest plumbing is server-side (web #101): Android attaches a standard Play Integrity token to auth requests; the server verifies and logs and never refuses on it. Needs the Play Console linkage (A8). |
| A22 | Landscape | Proposed | Phones support landscape on every screen, as iOS does since the pre-QA gate (handoff-preQA §2.1 item 4; `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations` in gradus-ios `project.yml`). No screen locks orientation (on ≥ 600 dp displays targetSdk 36 would ignore a lock anyway, §4.2); every screen handles insets in both orientations, including the display cutout on the side in landscape. |
| A23 | Devices without Google Play services | Proposed | Not supported. The app is distributed only through Google Play, and FCM, Credential Manager and Play Age Signals need Play services. If Play services are missing or too old, sign-in by email/password still works and push silently degrades to foreground refresh; no other workaround is built. |
| A24 | Backup and restore | Proposed | Android Auto Backup and device-to-device transfer **exclude** the session, the Room store, cached PDFs and voice notes (`dataExtractionRules` / `fullBackupContent`), mirroring iOS's this-device-only Keychain items (`kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`). Only non-sensitive per-device preferences (appearance, read-aloud voice, "Remember me" identifier, board follows and history) may be backed up. A restored install starts signed out. |
| A25 | Strings | Proposed | English only (iOS §7.13). Android string resources are generated from the iOS copy (and the shared direct-notice text source, #40) by a script, never retyped, and every user-facing iOS string is quoted verbatim except the platform nouns in the §4.3 substitution table. |
| A26 | Wear OS is non-standalone | Proposed | The Wear app declares `com.google.android.wearable.standalone = false`, because it needs the phone app's session over the Data Layer, exactly like the Apple Watch app's dependency on the iPhone for sign-in (iOS PRD §6.15: independent app, but the session is minted by `POST /auth/companion` and handed over from the phone; no watch-native push tokens, "the phone's notifications mirror"). It is found and installed from the same listing through Google Play (on the watch, or from the phone's Play choosing the watch); there is **no in-app "install on watch" prompt** in 1.0, because the iPhone app has no watch UI (§6.15.2). Phone notifications bridge to the watch by default. The one exception is message notifications while the Wear app is signed in and allowed to post: it excludes them from bridging and posts its own copy, forwarded by the phone over the Data Layer, so a tap opens the conversation on the watch (A51, #54, §6.15.8). Verify Play's current Wear quality requirements for non-standalone apps at the Wear foundation milestone. |
| A27 | `gradus://` custom scheme | Proposed | iOS registers the `gradus` scheme (`CFBundleURLSchemes: [gradus]`, gradus-ios `project.yml`) and routes `gradus://board/<slug>`, `gradus://settings/<section>`, `gradus://plans[/<id>]`, `gradus://p/<token>`, `gradus://g/<token>`, `gradus://team/<token>` and the legacy `gradus://reset-password#…` intercept (gradus-ios `docs/README.md`; push payload routes use the same paths). Android registers a `gradus` scheme intent filter with the same path grammar as iOS `RouteParser`, beside the App Links https filters; the legacy reset-password intercept stays. **One parser** serves scheme links, App Links and FCM route strings, and the iOS routing test vectors are reused. |
| A28 | Debug mock mode | Proposed | The `-GradusMock signedOut|noRole|coach|parent|athlete|athleteMinor|foundingUnclaimed|foundingOnPro` and `-GradusAgeRange under13|teen|…` launch arguments and the bundled demo-board JSON (gradus-ios `Gradus/Dependencies.swift`, `docs/README.md`) become a **debug-only launch extra** with the same scenario names and seeded invented data (§4.1 rule 20): `adb shell am start -n training.gradus.app.debug/training.gradus.app.MainActivity --es gradusMock coach` (debug package per A38) (plus `--es gradusAgeRange …`), and the bundled `demo-board.json`. Roborazzi screenshots, store screenshot capture and the accessibility audits (§11 A-23) use it. Never compiled into release. |
| A29 | Celebration cover and back | Proposed | System back and predictive back on the connection celebration behave as "Maybe later": the group is acked and the cover closes (iOS `fullScreenCover` has no dismissal that skips the ack; §7.7.16). |
| A30 | "Code copied" feedback | Proposed | The "Code copied" toast shows only on API ≤ 32; on Android 13+ the system clipboard confirmation stands in for it (§7.1.17, §7.7.2, §8.3). Copies with no iOS toast (message bubble Copy) show none on any version. |
| A31 | Share text shape | Proposed | Share intents put the iOS `ShareLink` message and URL in one `EXTRA_TEXT`, as "{message} {url}" (§7.2.13, §7.7.2). |
| A32 | Test tags | Proposed | Compose `testTag`s reuse the iOS accessibility identifier strings exactly, and the root, every `Dialog`/`ModalBottomSheet` root and the celebration cover set `testTagsAsResourceId = true` (§7.7.21, §8.3). |
| A33 | Reduce Motion and foreground | Proposed | "Reduce Motion" = `ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE == 0` read through one observed helper (`LocalReduceMotion`, §8.5); "foreground" = `ProcessLifecycleOwner` `ON_START` everywhere. |
| A34 | Per-user snapshot caches | Proposed | Per-user JSON snapshot files (iOS file names) live under `noBackupFilesDir/Gradus/<userId>/`, excluded from backup and wiped at sign-out; the coach-visibility "seen" signature is device-wide DataStore and survives sign-out (§6.5, §7.7.2). |
| A35 | Parent settings load guard | Proposed | `ParentSettingsViewModel` gets the same monotonic load-sequence guard as the guardian list models (iOS `ParentSettingsModel.load()` has none; hardening with no visible change; §7.7.2). |
| A36 | Sensitive clipboard | Proposed | Athlete invite codes and guardian team-invite codes are copied with `ClipDescription.EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE` on API 33+; the coach's own invite code is not (§7.7.2, §8.3). |
| A37 | US link-out: direct link to gradus.training, no External Content Links | **Settled** 2026-10-14 (Mariah; supersedes her 2026-10-13 choice to enroll) | Android does **not** enroll in Google Play's US External Content Links (ECL) program. US users get a plain link out to the Gradus web app at gradus.training, where subscriptions are bought and managed (Stripe on the web, as today). Purpose: avoid Google's fee. The link opens gradus.training in the default browser exactly like iOS's Safari link (iOS §6.8 rule 3): same copy ("Manage your plan at gradus.training" and the other §6.8 labels), same six sites (A13), US Play country only via `getBillingConfigAsync` (A13). No ECL APIs, no Google information screen, no `externalTransactionToken`, no Stripe → Play transaction reporting, no Google fees, no enrollment milestone; the Play Billing Library stays only for the `getBillingConfigAsync` country code. | A44 | Flow-state scale | **Settled** 2026-10-13 (Mariah) | **Replaces #18's labels and changes the scale's meaning.** The five-point scale now runs from **Hard** to **Easy**, and the **middle is the target**. On screen it shows three anchors with a subtitle each: point 1 **"HARD"** / "frustrated", point 3 **"JUST RIGHT"** / "engaged", point 5 **"EASY"** / "comfortable"; points 2 and 4 carry no label on the scale. Where there is no picture (practice log rows, toasts, notifications, TalkBack, Wear OS speech), the five points read **"Hard"**, **"A bit hard"**, **"Just right"**, **"A bit easy"**, **"Easy"**. Neither end is a bad result: every point is just data. The coach-facing signal is a **run** of sessions stuck at Hard or at Easy, which tells the coach the work needs adjusting. **Wire values are unchanged** (`stateIndex` 0–4); index 0 = Hard … 4 = Easy, read under the new meaning by the AI briefings, the athlete profile (§6.7) and every client. One string table keyed by `stateIndex` serves every surface. The same change lands on iOS and the web (owed there). **No per-point descriptions** (Mariah, 2026-10-13): a selected point shows its label only. The three-bar summary groups Hard (0+1) / Just right (2) / Easy (3+4) (§7.6.6). **Present the data, never interpret it:** a Hard session can be challenging or frustrating depending on the notes, and an Easy one can mean mastery or boredom, so the coach interprets; the AI briefings and summaries report the counts, the run and the athlete's notes without labeling Hard or Easy as good, bad, struggle, mastery or boredom (§6.7). **Updated UI (settled 2026-10-14):** the "Show, don't tell" handoff (`docs/design/show-dont-tell-handoff.md` and its canvas), as built on iOS at `c8f83d6`, replaces the earlier layout: the check-in asks **"How was practice today?"** of athletes and parents alike; the five dots carry the three anchors; FlowBars captions add the feeling word under each label ("HARD" / "frustrated"); the in-between points read **"A bit hard"** / **"A bit easy"** everywhere (Mariah, 2026-10-14); the athlete card shows sessions on the practice line, whose shaded ideal zone runs from A bit hard to A bit easy (§7.2.9, §8.6.7). §7.6.5 and §7.6.6 are final. **The three-bar grouping above stands** (Hard 0+1 / Just right 2 / Easy 3+4): iOS and the web still group FlowBars as Hard (0) / Just right (1+2+3) / Easy (4) and owe the back-port (§12 N90, A65). |

| A51 | Message notifications on the wrist (#54) | Proposed | While the Wear app is signed in and allowed to post notifications, it excludes the phone's message notifications from bridging (`BridgingManager`, bridge tag `gradus_message`). The phone forwards each room's notification over the Data Layer, and the watch posts its own copy, whose tap opens the conversation in the Wear app and whose Reply sends with the watch's session. In every other state, bridging is the default and the phone's copy, with its Reply, reaches the wrist. Narrows A26's "the Wear app posts none of its own". §6.15.8. |

| A53 | Replies and reactions in Messages | **Settled** 2026-10-14 (Mariah) | Matches iOS (web #234). **Reply:** long-press a message → Reply; the composer shows the quote; the send carries `replyToId`; the bubble shows `replyTo` (sender first name + `excerpt`, "Voice note" for voice, "Message removed" for a deleted sender) as one line above it. **React:** long-press → one of 👍 ❤️ 😂 🔥 👏; **one per person, swappable**, choosing yours again clears it (`PUT /api/v1/messages/{id}/reaction {emoji \| null}`, optimistic, put back on refusal). The pill sits on the bubble's top corner (trailing for others, leading for mine), each emoji once with a count when more than one person chose it. **No push and no unread** for a reaction. Neither shows while a parent has paused the room. Realtime: a separate `reactions:<roomId>` channel on `message_reactions` INSERT and UPDATE filtered by `room_id`/`direct_room_id` (clearing is an UPDATE to null, never a DELETE), then refetch. `replyTo` and `reactions` are optional in the contract. TalkBack: the bubble reads "…, replying to Maeve: <quote>…, reactions ❤️ 2 👏", with Reply and each reaction as custom actions. |

Transcription is therefore on **API 33+ only**, from the recorded file decoded to PCM, en-US, never downloading a model. **API 29–32 send `transcript: null`.** Never fall back to omitting the key, which would bring ElevenLabs back and make the shared AI-permission copy untrue. Snapshots in DataStore `widget_snapshots`, cleared at sign-out. §6.9.7. |

| A62 | Increase Contrast on Android | Proposed | `LocalIncreasedContrast` is true when `UiModeManager.getContrast() > 0f` (API 34+, the system contrast level, observed with `addContrastChangeListener`) **or**, on API 36+, `AccessibilityManager.isHighContrastTextEnabled()` (observed with `addHighContrastTextStateChangeListener`; verify both names). It is false on API 29–33, and the hidden `Settings.Secure` key is never read. When true, Android applies everything iOS applies under Increase Contrast. It also restores **every** borderless surface's edge through a contrast-aware `cardEdge`: cards, toasts, roster cards, receipts and lists. iOS restores only `GradusCard`'s edge (back-port: §12 N92). §8.5. |

JVM golden vectors are shared with iOS (§12 N94). §8.6.4. |

## 1. Summary

Gradus is a coaching platform for the time between lessons: coaches write practice plans, athletes and parents run them with a session timer and log how practice felt, everyone messages in one shared room, and coaches get AI briefings before each lesson. A public Live Board shows who is on the ice, latest scores, and who is up next at U.S. Figure Skating competitions (iOS §1).

The iOS app rebuilt that experience natively in SwiftUI against one backend (iOS §6.1). Android users today have only the progressive web app, with no push, no offline use and no reliable timer. This project builds the same app natively in **Kotlin and Jetpack Compose**, for Android phones and **Wear OS** watches, as the first Google Play release (A1). It consumes the same `/api/v1` through a client generated from the same OpenAPI contract that generates the Swift client, reaches Supabase directly only where iOS does (session, Realtime on messages, voice-note storage), and keeps **exactly one backend**. The web app is not forked, migrated, or changed in any user-visible way (§4.1).

The product is already decided. The iOS PRD's fifty decisions and the iOS code at `91c6af2` are the specification; this PRD's job is translation, not design (A2, §4.3). Every iOS-native element has a named Android-native counterpart (Appendix G): Live Activities become ongoing notifications and Android 16 Live Updates, WidgetKit becomes Glance, APNs becomes FCM, universal links become App Links, Face ID becomes BiometricPrompt, Sign in with Apple becomes a web flow (A17) alongside Credential Manager for Google (A18), Declared Age Range becomes Play Age Signals (A20), App Attest becomes Play Integrity (A21), the Apple Watch app becomes a Wear OS app (A3), and `AVSpeechSynthesizer` becomes `TextToSpeech` (A14).

**What changes for Android users:** the app works offline, the session timer survives the phone locking and the process being killed, messages and plan assignments arrive as push notifications, a fingerprint or face unlock can lock the app, a followed skater's lane state shows in a live notification and a home-screen widget, and a watch can speak a plan through earbuds. **What does not change:** their account (including one created with Apple on an iPhone, A5), their data, their coach connections, their subscription, and the web app they use today.

**Store presence.** One Play listing, `training.gradus.app`, version 1.0, United States only, free, phone and Wear OS form factors (A1, A3, A10). Nobody migrates from a shell. The listing cannot exist until the Play Console organization account does (A8); every milestone that does not need it proceeds meanwhile (§10).

### Non-goals

- **Anything iOS 1.0 does not ship.** Ask Gradus and Saved answers stay hidden (#22); the iPad-style adaptive layout stays unbuilt (#50, A4); the custom cloud narration voice stays deferred (#47, iOS §12 #35); server-side watch session revocation stays a point-release item (iOS §10.11 W0 notes); the learned pace model stays post-launch (#14, iOS §12 #17).
- **Android-only features.** No Material You dynamic color, no extra widgets or notification types beyond the iOS set, no Wear OS Tiles (the Apple Watch app's only watch-face surface is its complication, #51, which Android ships as a Wear OS complication, A50; §12 N76), no Google Assistant or App Actions integration, no Android Auto, no Android TV, no Android XR, no ChromeOS-specific layout, no Quick Settings tile.
- **Tablet- and foldable-optimized layouts** (A4).
- Org admin or internal admin features (#2).
- **Purchasing subscriptions in-app**, Play Billing products, or an embedded Stripe page (#8, A10).
- **Third-party analytics or crash SDKs**: no Firebase Analytics, Crashlytics, Performance Monitoring, Remote Config or any ad SDK (iOS §6.11, #19, A11, A19).
- On-device ML, on-device transcription, or on-device training (iOS §6.7 "No on-device model"); speech-to-text stays on the server, including on Wear OS where a recognizer might exist (iOS §6.15, §4.2 here).
- Migrating off Lovable Cloud or changing the Supabase project; changing AI prompts, the IJS scraper, email, Stripe webhooks or any server behavior not required for the Android client (iOS §1 Non-goals).
- Redesigning the product. Screens may be reorganized to fit Android idioms (bottom navigation, top app bars, Material sheets and dialogs), but information architecture, copy, and flows are ported from iOS, not reinvented.
- Localization beyond English (iOS §7.13); multi-account mode (iOS §6.4).
- Distribution outside Google Play (no APK downloads, no other stores) and support for devices without Google Play services (A23).
- The Capacitor Android shell (A1).

## 2. Goals and success metrics

**Product goals**

The six iOS goals (iOS §2), unchanged in substance, for Android users:

1. **A coach can run their week from the rink** on an Android phone: roster, today's lessons, the athlete's plan, the pre-lesson briefing and messaging work with no or intermittent connectivity.
2. **A practice session is effortless to log.** Start the timer, lock the phone, come back, end, rate the flow state. Never lose a session, including when the OS or an OEM battery manager kills the process (§11 A-3).
3. **Nothing important is missed.** New messages, plan assignments, lesson wrap-up prompts, lesson reminders, practice nudges and Live Board moments arrive as FCM notifications in the right notification channel and open the right screen.
4. **The Live Board is the best way to follow a competition on an Android phone.** Scan a rink QR code, follow your skaters, watch the live notification and the home-screen widget.
5. **Feature parity with iOS 1.0** for coaches, parents and athletes, so the web can be sunset for those roles (#6, iOS §10.4 item 4).
6. **Gradus learns each athlete and answers from vetted sources**, through the same server-side profile and corpus (#14, #15); Android contributes the coach "why" answers.

Plus one Android-specific goal:

7. **The watch works wrist-down.** A coach, parent or athlete hears a full plan through Bluetooth earbuds from a Wear OS watch with the screen off, and a coach or adult athlete dictates or edits a plan with one tap (A3, iOS §6.15).

**Success metrics (measure from launch)**

| Metric | Target | Source |
|---|---|---|
| User-perceived crash rate (Play Android vitals) | **< 1.09%** of daily users (Play's bad-behavior threshold; staying under it keeps Play visibility), internal target ≤ 0.5% | Play Console vitals (the rate); `POST /errors` crash uploads (A19) for diagnosis only |
| User-perceived ANR rate (Play Android vitals) | **< 0.47%** of daily users (Play's threshold), internal target ≤ 0.2% | Play Console vitals (the rate); `ApplicationExitInfo` uploads for diagnosis only |
| Crash-free sessions (parity with iOS) | ≥ 99.5% | Play Console vitals (`/errors` has no session counts) |
| Per-device crash/ANR rates on the 10 most-used device models | each under the Play per-device thresholds (8% crash, 8% ANR) (verify current values) | Play vitals |
| Cold start to interactive (cached account) | **< 1.5 s on a Pixel 6a-class device** (iOS "< 1.5 s on iPhone 12"); never in Play's slow-cold-start band (≥ 5 s) | Macrobenchmark in CI with Baseline Profiles; Play vitals startup |
| Wear OS cold start to first spoken word of a cached plan | < 3 s (proposed) | Macrobenchmark on the QA watch |
| Sessions started offline that sync successfully | ≥ 99% | **Source to be decided**: no existing iOS endpoint or analytics event reports outbox state; measuring it needs a new event type, which is a decision (§4.3 rule 8) |
| Message send → recipient FCM notification delivered (p50) | < 5 s | Server send log (FCM accept time) only; **client receipt time is not collected** and would need a new event type (decision, §4.3 rule 8) |
| Live Board data age shown to a viewer (p50) | ≤ 45 s behind IJS | unchanged server metric |
| Excessive partial wake locks / excessive wakeups (Play vitals) | below Play's bad-behavior thresholds | Play vitals |
| Google Play rating after 60 days | ≥ 4.6 | Play Console |
| Web weekly actives among coaches/parents/athletes 90 days after **both** native launches | trending to zero, gating the sunset (iOS §10.4) | web analytics |
| Ask Gradus answers citing ≥ 1 corpus source | ≥ 80% (server metric; not measurable from Android while #22 hides Ask Gradus) | server |
| Bench and move-removal prompts a coach answers rather than skips | ≥ 60% (Android coaches counted with iOS) | `athlete_skill_events` |
| Athletes with ≥ 1 labeled or protocol-derived skill event 60 days after launch | ≥ 70% of athletes with an active plan | server |
| Accessibility | WCAG 2.2 AAA on every screen, with 3.3.5 (contextual help) partial by design, as on iOS (iOS §10.6; handoff-preQA §2.1 item 4) | audit harness (§9) |

**Guardrails (must not regress during the build)**

- Web error rate in the admin errors dashboard.
- Web sign-in success rate.
- Email deliverability health.
- Web p75 page load, re-checked after every backend publish (iOS §2).
- **iOS crash-free rate and iOS decode success.** No server change made for Android may break an installed iOS build: every response change is an optional field, never a new value in an enum iOS decodes (§4.1 rule 15). iOS `/errors` volume is checked after every Android-driven publish.
- **APNs delivery** for iOS while the FCM sender is added beside it (§4.1 rule 7).

## 3. Users and roles

Gradus resolves a signed-in user's role server-side from which profile rows exist (`getMyRole`): coach if a coach profile exists, else parent, else athlete, else org admin. The Android app uses the same resolution through `GET /me` and **never infers role client-side** (iOS §3).

| Role | Who | In Android 1.0 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Coach** | Private-lesson coaches, mostly figure skating; also multi-sport and strength & conditioning | Yes (phone and Wear OS) | Tiers: Coach, Coach Pro, Club (via organization). Founding Coaches (onboarded before 2026-11-01) free for life; Android launches after that date, so new Android coaches meet the paywall flag state of the day (iOS §6.8 rule 6, §12 #8). |
| **Parent / guardian** | Parent of a minor athlete; up to three guardians per athlete on the Team plan | Yes (phone and Wear OS plan→audio) | Creates athletes, links coaches, runs sessions for young athletes, manages the athlete's login. Adult-verified once through KWS when linking a minor (#29). |
| **Athlete (minor)** | Created by a parent, signs in with a **username** (no email) | Yes (phone and Wear OS, no voice input) | Restricted messaging persona, Safe Sport resources, text only (#32, #48), no Ask Gradus (#22 and the server age gate). 13–17 may self-sign-up into a **provisional** account; under 13 never self-sign-up (#30, #31). |
| **Athlete (adult, self-managed)** | Signs up directly, links coaches themselves | Yes (phone and Wear OS, including voice→plan) | Invite code for coaches; manages own schedules and goals; authors own plans (#35). |
| Org admin | Club purchaser or director | **No** (web) | #2. |
| Internal admin | Gradus staff | **No** (web) | #2; the API rejects impersonation tokens. |

**Minors on Android.** The app never markets to children (iOS §3). The iOS posture of not enrolling in Apple's Kids Category maps to **not joining any Google Play kids program or badge**. Play's **Target audience and content** declaration, unlike Apple's, must state who actually uses the app, and under-13 athletes do (parent-created accounts), so the default is to declare the true age groups, which brings the Families policy into scope, and to comply with it (§12 N3, Appendix D; counsel to confirm). Whether the Families policy affects the US link-out is unverified (verify). Athlete birthdates are collected by the parent; the app surfaces age-appropriate personas exactly as iOS and the web do. Every parent account linked to a minor is a verified adult, and a minor's account, coach links and rooms wait on that verification (#29–#31). On a device whose Play Age Signals result is under 18, only athlete accounts can be created (A20). A child on a **Family Link**-supervised Google account installs through the parent's Play approval; that is Google's gate, not Gradus's, and Gradus's own consent ledger remains the record (iOS §6.13 B2 "The ledger, not Apple, is the record").

**Who uses Wear OS.** All three roles with plan→audio and with messages (read, and reply in text, from a notification or the Messages screen, #54); coaches with briefing, wrap-up, voice→plan, deploy and the watch-face complication (#51); adult athletes with voice→plan and deploying their own plans; minor athletes with drafts, listening and activating their own plans but no "Record a plan" (iOS §6.15 "Minors on the wrist", #48). A Wear OS watch pairs only with an Android phone, so every watch user is also an Android phone user.

## 4. Non-negotiable constraints

These protect current web users and the shipping iOS app. Every backend pull request made for Android is checked against them before merge, and they are restated in the Android CI checklist (§9).

### 4.1 Zero-disruption guarantees for the web app (inherited)

Rules 1–13 are iOS §4.1, inherited **verbatim in force**; Android adds rules 14–20.

1. **No change to web-facing server functions.** Every `createServerFn` keeps its name, input schema, return shape and behavior. Shared-logic extraction is behavior-preserving and verified by `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, and a manual smoke pass in Lovable preview before publish.
2. **Additive database changes only** until the web is sunset: new tables, nullable columns, indexes, RLS policies, functions. No renames, drops, type changes, or tightened constraints on existing tables. Every new `public` table ships with GRANTs and RLS in the same migration.
3. **No change to Supabase Auth settings the web depends on.** Captcha stays on; the Lovable-managed Google provider stays as is; email templates stay as is. Android gets what it needs through the API's auth broker (§6.4), never by changing shared settings.
4. **The API is additive and isolated** under `src/routes/api/v1/`, shares nothing with the web client bundle, and keeps its kill switch `API_V1_ENABLED` (Android, like iOS, shows its offline cache on 503).
5. **Same deploy path, smaller steps.** Backend changes ship through the Lovable publish in small, independently revertible PRs, never bundled with unrelated web work; shared-table migrations go to Lovable preview first, then publish in US evening hours.
6. **Web bundle budget unchanged.** No new client-side web dependencies; new server code in `.server.ts` files only.
7. **Push is best-effort.** An FCM send failure, like an APNs failure, never fails the underlying action. The FCM sender is added **beside** the APNs path in `src/lib/push-notify.server.ts` (which today selects `platform = 'ios'` tokens only); a failure or exception in either sender never affects the other.
8. **Observe after every publish**: admin errors dashboard and email health; a regression triggers a revert first and a diagnosis second.
9. **Sunset is a separate decision** (iOS §10.4); until then the web for all roles is fully supported.
10. **No credential or key moves.** The Supabase publishable key, service role key, Stripe and AI keys stay where they are. Android ships only the publishable key, the Google server client ID, the Apple Services ID name, and the Firebase client config (`google-services.json`, which is not a secret). The FCM HTTP v1 service-account key lives only in Lovable Cloud secrets.
11. **Migration files merged through GitHub are not applied by a Lovable publish.** Every backend PR with a migration ends with: ask Lovable to apply pending migrations, then run the `docs/api/SMOKE.md` precheck. Nothing that reads a new relation is enabled before both are done; code guarding public write endpoints fails closed.
12. **Service-role-only database functions revoke EXECUTE from `anon` and `authenticated` explicitly**, verified by an anonymous `/rest/v1/rpc/<fn>` call returning permission denied.
13. **Billing and membership columns on profile tables are server-only** (`20260905200000_protect_billing_columns` triggers); written only through the admin client.
14. **Optional across the deploy gap.** Merging to `main` updates only the Lovable preview; production changes on Mariah's Publish, while Android CI builds from `main` continuously. Any response field the Android app reads is **optional** in the zod contract (the server always sends it), so an Android build never fails to decode a response from an unpublished server (handoff-2026-10-04 §8).
15. **Never break the installed iOS app.** Enums in responses are closed sets on iOS: a server change for Android **adds a field, never a value** to an enum iOS decodes. Request-body enums may widen (iOS never decodes them): `analytics/events.platform` gains `"android"`, as `devices.platform` already allows. `meta/client-policy.minSupportedVersion` gains an optional `android` property beside the required `ios`.
16. **No Android-only product endpoints.** Server additions for Android are platform plumbing only (Appendix A): the FCM sender, the Apple web-flow callback and code exchange, the Google audience, `/.well-known/assetlinks.json`, Play Integrity verification, the platform field additions, `/errors` platform derivation (today it stores `platform: "ios"` unconditionally; derive from `X-Gradus-Client` via `parseClientHeader`, falling back to an optional request field `platform`; Android ANRs report `kind: "hang"`, crashes `kind: "crash"`; A19), the Play `installId` store and revoked-list import (`POST /me/play-install`, A20), the optional `pausedVia` field (§6.13 B4), the `androidExternalLinksEnabled` link-out kill switch (A37), and the account-deletion web page Play requires (`/delete-account`, §11 A-5). Appendix A numbers them S-1 to S-17. Any product behavior Android needs that iOS lacks is a parity bug in the plan, not a new endpoint.
17. **The contract is shared.** Android vendors the same `docs/api/openapi.json`, `docs/api/vectors/` and `docs/api/design-tokens.json` the iOS repo vendors, pinned by commit; CI fails if the generated Kotlin client or color resources drift from the vendored contract.
18. **`X-Gradus-Client: android/<versionName>+<versionCode>`** on every API request (the iOS `ios/1.0.0+N` format, iOS §6.2), so server logs, rate limits and `/errors` can tell the clients apart.
19. **Claude sessions never** merge, publish, apply migrations, set Lovable secrets, toggle `API_V1_ENABLED` or `PARENT_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED`, upload to Play, or change Play Console settings without Mariah's explicit say-so for that batch (handoff-remaining-prd §6, handoff-2026-10-05 §1).
20. **Mock, demo, test and screenshot data use invented names only**, from the established invented cast (Renata Pruitt, Greta Halvorsen and family, Tobias and Owen Fairbank, Elsie Varga, the Abbotts, the demo-board skaters; handoff-2026-10-04 §3). Before adding anyone new, invent the name and `git grep -w -i` it in all three repos.

### 4.2 Android platform constraints (facts, checked 2026-10-11)

Items marked (verify) could not be confirmed against a primary source in this pass and are re-checked at the milestone that depends on them.

- **Target API.** Since **2026-08-31**, new apps and updates on Google Play must target **Android 16 (API 36)**; an extension to 2026-11-01 can be requested. Wear OS (and Automotive) apps must target **API 35 or higher**; the Wear module uses 36 like the phone unless a Wear library blocks it. Existing apps must target 35+ (Wear 33+) to stay visible to new users on newer devices. The bar rises every August (API 37 expected for 2027), so the release train must budget one target-SDK migration a year (§11 A-7). Source: developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/target-sdk.
- **minSdk 29 (A6).** Android 10 is the floor. APIs used above it are guarded: `ApplicationExitInfo` (30+), `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` runtime permission (33+), photo picker (native on 33+, back-ported through Google Play services below), predictive back (opt-in from 33, system default from 15/16), Credential Manager (works from API 21 through Play services), Live Updates / promoted ongoing notifications (Android 16, API 36) (verify the permission and eligibility rules: progress-centric `Notification.ProgressStyle`, `POST_PROMOTED_NOTIFICATIONS`, `requestPromotedOngoing`).
- **Notifications are opt-in from Android 13.** Request `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` (API 33+) in exactly the iOS places, never at launch (iOS §6.6 token lifecycle; `PushPermission.requestIfNeeded()` callers): when a message room opens (`FeatureMessages/RoomView.swift:45`), when a practice session starts so "Still practicing?" can fire (`FeatureSessions/SessionActivityController.swift`, "the contextual moment"), and from Settings → Device (`FeatureSettings/Account/DeviceView.swift:151`). On every launch where permission is already granted, refresh the FCM token and `POST /devices` (the `Gradus/Shell/AppDelegate.swift` re-registration). On 29–32 notifications are on by default but every notification still goes to a named **notification channel** the user can turn off; Settings → Device reflects the real per-channel state.
- **Background limits.** Doze, App Standby buckets and OEM battery managers defer WorkManager jobs and can kill processes; foreground services need a declared type on Android 14+; only the **Wear OS** app uses one (`mediaPlayback` for wrist-down narration, §6.15.1), and the phone app uses none (no `dataSync` for sync, no expedited work that would need one on API 29–30, no `microphone` service, no session-timer service, §6.5, §6.7.4, §7.6.4). Exact alarms (`SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM`) are restricted; nothing in Gradus needs exact timing on the device (lesson reminders and practice nudges are server-driven pushes, iOS §6.6; "Still practicing?" is an inexact `AlarmManager.setAndAllowWhileIdle`, A12). Since Android 14, an ongoing notification not attached to a foreground service, media session or CallStyle can be swiped away on an unlocked device, so no correctness may rest on a notification staying up (A12). **The phone app starts no foreground service in 1.0**: phone read-aloud pauses when the app leaves the screen, as on iOS (§6.7.4), recording happens only while its screen is up, and the session timer is timestamp-based (§7.6.4).
- **Foreground service declaration.** Apps targeting API 34+ that use foreground service types complete Play Console → App content → **Foreground service permissions**, with a description and a demo video per type. Gradus declares one: `mediaPlayback`, for the Wear OS app's wrist-down plan reading (§6.15). Listed in Appendix D and §11 A-5.
- **Edge-to-edge and large screens (forced by targetSdk 36).** Targeting API 35+ enforces edge-to-edge and API 36 removes the opt-out (`windowOptOutEdgeToEdgeEnforcement`): every screen handles `WindowInsets` (status, navigation and IME bars, display cutout) through `Scaffold`/insets padding, and screenshot tests run with both gesture and 3-button navigation. Targeting API 36 also makes the system ignore orientation, resizability and aspect-ratio restrictions on displays ≥ 600 dp: the phone layout must work resizable, in any orientation, without relying on letterboxing (it centers at a max readable width) (A4, A22, §11 A-22). Predictive back is on and `onBackPressed` is no longer called: back handling uses only `BackHandler` / `PredictiveBackHandler` and `OnBackPressedDispatcher`.
- **Supabase Auth captcha** (unchanged from iOS §4.2): enforced on the password grant, sign-up and recovery; skipped for `id_token`, `refresh_token`, `pkce` grants and service-role calls. Android therefore uses the same broker endpoints as iOS (`/auth/password`, `/auth/signup/*`, `/auth/recover`).
- **No Sign in with Apple provider in Lovable Cloud and no Apple SDK on Android.** Android's Apple sign-in is a web flow through an Apple Services ID and our own callback (A17). The broker today hard-codes `APPLE_CLIENT_ID = "training.gradus.app"` for verification and for `POST https://appleid.apple.com/auth/revoke` (`src/lib/api/auth-broker.ts`, `provider-verify.ts`), so the Services ID must be added as an accepted audience and as the revocation client for tokens it issued.
- **Google sign-in is brokered.** The web's Google sign-in runs on Lovable's broker; Android uses Credential Manager and our `/auth/google` (A18). The broker's audience check reads only `GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID` today.
- **Server logic depends on the service role** (49 of 67 server-function files, iOS §4.2); RLS alone cannot power a native client. Android, like iOS, goes through the API.
- **Cloudflare Workers can reach FCM.** The FCM HTTP v1 API needs an OAuth 2.0 access token minted from a Google service-account key (RS256 JWT signed with WebCrypto, exchanged at `oauth2.googleapis.com`), which a Worker can do as it already signs the APNs JWT. The push path today sends only to `platform = 'ios'` rows of `device_tokens`; `POST /devices` already accepts `platform: "android"`, so Android tokens can register before the sender exists and simply receive nothing until it ships.
- **TLS certificates rotate** (Cloudflare-managed, ~90 days). **No certificate pinning** on Android either: default Network Security Config, cleartext disabled in release, `localhost` cleartext allowed only in the debug build's config for the local API (reached through `adb reverse` on emulators and devices alike, §9.6).
- **App Links and shared passwords need `/.well-known/assetlinks.json`**, carrying **both** `delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls` and `delegate_permission/common.get_login_creds` for `training.gradus.app`, so Credential Manager and Autofill share saved gradus.training passwords (the iOS `webcredentials:gradus.training` associated domain, gradus-ios `project.yml` and `Gradus/Gradus.entitlements`). The sign-in fields carry autofill content types username/password (Compose `ContentType.Username` / `ContentType.Password` semantics; iOS `textContentType(.username/.password)` in `SignInView`), and Credential Manager `GetPasswordOption` is offered alongside Google. The file lists `training.gradus.app` with the SHA-256 fingerprints of every signing certificate that should open links (debug and upload keys now; the **Play App Signing** key once the Play Console exists, A8). Unlike Apple's AASA, the **paths are declared in the app's manifest intent filters**, not in the server file, so the app's path list must reproduce the AASA include/exclude rules exactly (iOS §6.10; web `src/lib/apple-app-site-association.ts`). No `assetlinks.json` route exists in the web repo today.
- **Play Console organization account (A8)** requires the organization's D-U-N-S number, a verified organization website and contact details, and Google's developer identity verification; new **personal** accounts must run a closed test with at least 12 testers for 14 days before production, a rule that does not apply to organization accounts (verify both at account creation).
- **Google Play US external-link rules.** A US court injunction in Epic v. Google (in effect from late October 2025, running to 2027-11-01) bars Google from prohibiting links to external purchase in the US; Google runs US "external content links" and alternative-billing programs and has announced that enrolled developers report transactions and pay service fees from **2026-10-01** (Play Console Help answer 15582165) Google Play's US payments policy requires enrollment in its program before linking US users to purchase outside Play, and the court-ordered rules are still contested. §6.8 and §12 N7 carry the decision: Gradus does **not** enroll in the US External Content Links program and ships a direct US link to gradus.training in 1.0, behind the `androidExternalLinksEnabled` kill switch, to avoid Google's fee (A37, Mariah 2026-10-14, superseding the 2026-10-13 choice to enroll). The policy risk is §11 A-27.
- **Play Age Signals API** returns, for eligible US users, `ageRangeSource` (TIER_A..D), `ageLower`/`ageUpper` (default buckets 0–12, 13–15, 16–17, 18+; custom minimum ages settable in Play Console), `significantChangeStatus` (APPROVED/PENDING/DECLINED), `significantChangeApprovalDate` and `installId`, so apps can meet Texas SB 2420 and similar laws. **Revoked parental approvals are not signalled to the app**: Play Console → Age signals → Revoked app approvals lists them by `installId` (CSV, kept 90 days), and Google advises storing `installId` on the backend. Texas signals cover only accounts created after 2026-05-28. Google recommends Play Integrity alongside Age Signals calls. (Checked against developer.android.com/google/play/age-signals 2026-10-11; verify GA status and current enforcement before the age-signals milestone.) A20 owns the design.
- **Play policy surfaces that iOS does not have:** the **Data safety** form; **Target audience and content** and the Families policy (§3); **account deletion** — apps that let users create accounts must offer in-app deletion **and** a web resource where deletion can be requested, linked in Data safety (verify); **User Data** policy prominent disclosure for any sensitive permission; **Photo and video permissions** policy (use the photo picker; never `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES`); **Foreground service permissions** declaration with demo videos (`mediaPlayback`, `microphone`; above); **Health** and **Financial features** declarations (answer "no" / invoices are records, iOS §6.8 rule 5) (verify the declaration list at listing time).
- **Wear OS.** Wear OS apps on Play are built with Compose for Wear OS; a watch talks to the phone over the **Data Layer API** (`MessageClient`, `DataClient`, `CapabilityClient`) only between apps with the **same applicationId and signing key**. The manifest meta-data `com.google.android.wearable.standalone` governs Play install and discovery, and Play's Wear quality rules differ between standalone and non-standalone apps; Gradus's Wear app is **non-standalone** (A26). Some watches offer an on-device speech recognizer, but parity keeps the iOS model: voice in is a recorded clip transcribed by the server (iOS §6.15, #48), voice out is on-device TTS. Wear OS watches pair only with Android phones.
- **Developer machine.** Mariah has a MacBook Pro (Apple silicon) and a Google Pixel phone, and no Android tooling yet. Android Studio (stable) is the Xcode equivalent: it bundles the SDK manager, emulator (arm64 system images run natively on Apple silicon), Wear OS emulator pairing, profiler, Layout Inspector and Compose previews. §5.2 owns the setup steps. Unlike iOS, Android builds and unit tests run on Linux, so cloud Claude Code sessions can build and test the Android app (instrumented tests still need an emulator or device).

### 4.3 Parity rules

These govern every section of this PRD and every Android pull request.

1. **Every requirement traces to iOS.** Each behavior cites its iOS source (iOS PRD section or decision, or a gradus-ios file path). A behavior with no iOS source is either an Android-native substitution listed in Appendix G or it does not ship.
2. **Code at HEAD wins.** gradus-ios at `91c6af2` is the reference implementation. Where it differs from the iOS PRD text, Android follows the code and the Android PRD notes the difference. Known instances: Google sign-in is hidden on iOS (stub provider) while Android ships it by decision A5; native password reset is on (`GRADUS_NATIVE_RESET: true` in `project.yml`, iOS #124 auth-confirm links), although the iOS README still describes it as default off; legacy WebM notes are unplayable on iOS (`Bubbles.swift`) where Android plays them by decision A15; Billing reads **"Invoicing"** (iOS #117, web #205); "Add a sport" is replaced by **"Request a sport"** (iOS #118); error toasts persist with a visible ✕ and clear on tab or screen change (iOS #114); the plan editor's "Assign to" sits above Activate & Share as an empty dashed box "Choose who this is for" (iOS #116); every email link opens the app with the web as fallback (iOS #120, #124; web #211); **parent confirms**, with the pending-claims card on the parent's Plans (iOS #121, web #207; Table 1b b1); signed in, **Live is a top-app-bar action on every root screen** opening a full-screen destination, not a tab (gradus-ios `docs/README.md` I2; Table 1b b2).
3. **Copy is verbatim.** User-facing strings are taken from the iOS app, not rewritten. Only platform nouns change, per this table; anything not listed stays word for word:

   | iOS wording | Android wording |
   |---|---|
   | Face ID / Touch ID / passcode | "biometric unlock" (fingerprint or face) / "screen lock" |
   | Safari / "opens Safari" | "your browser" / "opens in your browser" |
   | App Store / Apple's App Store | Google Play |
   | iOS Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → Voices | Android Settings → Accessibility → Text-to-speech output → Preferred engine settings → Install voice data |
   | Lock Screen / Dynamic Island / Live Activity | lock screen / notification / live notification |
   | Home Screen widget | home screen widget |
   | Apple Watch / the watch | your watch (Wear OS) |
   | AirPods | earbuds / Bluetooth headphones |
   | share sheet | share menu |
   | "Apple Account on this device" (Declared Age Range copy) | "Google Account on this device" (Play Age Signals copy) |
   | iPhone ("your iPhone", e.g. the watch strings "Signing in from your iPhone…", "This also signs you out on your iPhone.", "Can't reach your iPhone. Keep it nearby with Gradus signed in, then try again.", "check it on your iPhone"; `FeatureWatch/`) | "phone" ("your phone") |
   | "iOS Settings" / "the Settings app" (e.g. "Microphone access is off. Allow it in iOS Settings to record.", `FeatureMessages/Components/Composer.swift`) | "your phone's Settings", with a button that deep-links to the app's system settings page (`Settings.ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS` / `ACTION_APP_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS`) where possible |
   | "Premium" / "Enhanced" voice quality (`ReadAloudVoiceView.swift`) | "Very high quality" / "High quality" (from `Voice.QUALITY_VERY_HIGH` / `QUALITY_HIGH`) |
   | "Asking a parent needs iOS 26.2 or later…" (`AgeAssurance.swift` `unavailable`) | "Asking a parent needs an up-to-date Google Play…" (the Play Age Signals requirement), rest of the sentence verbatim |
   | "Gradus's age rating on the App Store has changed…" (`GradusCore/Onboarding/SignificantChanges.swift`, StoreKit age-rating watcher) | **No Android equivalent**: Play has no age-rating watcher; the string is not shipped and the gap is recorded in Appendix G |

   Rule: any iOS string naming Apple hardware, an Apple OS, an Apple service or an Apple settings path is either listed here or flagged in review; the string-generation script (A25) fails on an unlisted match for `iPhone|iPad|iOS|Apple|App Store|Safari|Face ID|Touch ID|AirPods|Premium voice|Enhanced`.

4. **Same flags, same values.** `ReleaseFlags.ASK_GRADUS_ENABLED = false` (#22). Native reset on (rule 2). Server flags from `GET /meta/config` (paywall, Coach Pro, Founding cutoff, minimum version) and `/me` (`athleteVoiceToPlan`, `parentVerified`, the `verification` object, terms version, entitlement) drive Android exactly as they drive iOS; a missing optional flag means **off / the conservative state**.
5. **Same limits.** Voice FAB 90 s per clip (180 s / 18 MB server cap); invite and club codes 8 characters from the unambiguous alphabet (no O/0/I/1), the field stops at 8; motivation card ≤ 500 characters; no cap on active plans, for coaches (#52) or on an athlete's own plans; a move-draft hint of up to 200 characters, and 30 drafts per hour per coach (server, #53); 15-minute lesson reminder; 30 s Live Board refresh, stale after 3 min, 20 recent boards; messages are **not** cached on disk (code wins over iOS §6.5's "newest 200 per room", §6.5, §12 N22); analytics buffer 1,000 events / 7 days, batches of ≤ 100 every 60 s in the foreground, on background and at launch, screen stretches capped at 30 min; "Still practicing?" one hour after backgrounding with a running timer; KWS email resend after 60 s; 14-day watch lease (`WatchLease.defaultDuration`); terms version from `/me` compared to `CURRENT_TERMS_VERSION`. §7 cites each at its point of use.
6. **Lenient decoding, conservative interpretation.** The Kotlin client ignores unknown keys and decodes server "plain string" fields as `String` (`method`, `source`, and the others iOS keeps open), so a new server value never crashes an installed Android build. Age and consent are conservative everywhere: no birthdate means minor; unknown verification means unverified; a missing `athleteVoiceToPlan` means no voice.
7. **Only Android-native substitutions.** Where iOS uses an iOS-native behavior or component, Android uses the equivalent in Appendix G, and nothing else differs. Where Android has no exact equivalent (for example the Dynamic Island's compact "#4 of 12"), the closest platform surface carries the same information and the degradation is recorded in Appendix G. Where Android can do something iOS cannot, Android does **not** add it unless it is the natural platform behavior of a parity feature (A15 is the model: same feature, platform decoder).
8. **Same privacy surface.** Android collects exactly the data iOS collects, for the same purposes, and its Play Data safety answers match the iOS App Privacy answers in `docs/ios/app-store-submission.md` §4, adjusted only for platform processors (FCM token, Play Integrity verdict). No new data type ships without a decision.
9. **Same accessibility bar.** WCAG 2.2 AAA as on iOS (iOS §10.6), tested with TalkBack, Switch Access, Voice Access, a hardware keyboard, font scale up to 200%, display size at maximum, high-contrast text, color correction, and "Remove animations" (the Reduce Motion equivalent). Touch targets ≥ 48 dp (the Android counterpart of iOS's 44 pt).
10. **Same QA.** Every row in `docs/ios/QA.md` has an Android row in `docs/android/QA.md`, with the platform nouns swapped, plus Android-only rows (notification permission and channels, battery optimization, predictive back, process death, App Links verification, Wear OS pairing).
11. **Moving target.** iOS keeps changing during iOS QA. A **parity ledger** (`docs/android/parity-ledger.md` in gradus-android) records the gradus-ios commit last reconciled; each Android milestone starts by diffing gradus-ios and the iOS docs since that commit and adding any new behavior to the backlog.
12. **Milestones, not dates** (#12).

### 5.1 What is reused, rebuilt, or added server-side for Android

**Reused as-is (no server change).** Everything iOS reuses (iOS §5 "What is reused as-is"): database schema and RLS, all business logic behind `/api/v1`, Stripe (web checkout and portal), AI prompts and the gateway, ElevenLabs transcription, the email system, the IJS scraper and snapshots, invites, account deletion and tombstoning, report and block, terms versioning, KWS parent verification and its webhook (`/api/public/webhooks/kws`, `/verified`), the consent ledger and account states (iOS §6.13 A), athlete-authored plans (iOS §6.14), `POST /auth/companion` for the watch session (iOS §10.11 W0 notes; Wear OS uses it unchanged, §6.15), `POST /auth/password`, `POST /auth/recover`, `/auth/username/*`, every `/signup/*` route, `GET /me` with `athleteVoiceToPlan` (#48) and `parentVerified`, the `/auth/confirm` email-link route (web #211), lesson-reminder and practice-nudge cron hooks (iOS §6.6), and the admin demo-account tool (#26). The OpenAPI document is the contract; Android adds **no Android-only endpoint** for product features (iOS §11 risk 14).

**Rebuilt natively on Android.** Every screen, navigation, auth UI, offline store and outbox, push handling, Live Board presentation, voice capture and playback, camera capture for schedule import, PDF viewing, share sheet, haptics, biometric gate, home-screen widget, ongoing/Live Update notifications, read-aloud (TextToSpeech), the Wear OS app, and the error and analytics reporters (iOS §5 "What is rebuilt natively", mapped per Appendix G).

| S-9 | Play Integrity verdict check, **log-only** on `POST /auth/password`, mirroring App Attest's dormant posture (`src/lib/app-attest.server.ts`: "never enforcing") | iOS §6.4 "Bot protection", §6.11, work package 3.8 | SA6 (after A8) |

(`src/routes/support.tsx`) and the admin page line "Which curated documents the iOS app may show" (`src/routes/_authenticated/admin.library-rights.tsx`) say "the app" or name both platforms. With KL, the retired-route redirect for mobile browsers (iOS §10.4 item 5, App Store for mobile Safari) also sends Android browsers to the Play listing, alongside the "Get the app" banner (§10.4) | Copy parity on the web for Android users | SA7 (copy); KL (redirect) |

New Lovable Cloud secrets: `FCM_PROJECT_ID`, `FCM_CLIENT_EMAIL`, `FCM_PRIVATE_KEY` (SA2); `GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_ANDROID_CLIENT_IDS` (SA3); `APPLE_SIWA_SERVICES_ID` (SA4; the existing `APPLE_SIWA_KEY_P8`/`APPLE_SIWA_KEY_ID`/`APPLE_TEAM_ID` sign its client secret); `PLAY_INTEGRITY_CLIENT_EMAIL`, `PLAY_INTEGRITY_PRIVATE_KEY` (SA6; may be the same service account as FCM). The feedback path `android/settings` needs no change (S-12). Set by Mariah in Lovable Cloud secrets, read with `process.env`, like the existing ones (iOS §9.4). No secret is ever committed to gradus-android; the app holds only the Supabase publishable key, the Google **web** client ID (public, used as `serverClientId`), and the public Firebase config in `google-services.json` (iOS §6.11 "Secrets").

### 5.2 Toolchain on a Mac and a Pixel

Mariah has a MacBook Pro and a Google Pixel phone and has installed no Android tooling. **Android Studio (stable channel) is the Xcode equivalent**: one app with the editor, Gradle build, SDK manager, emulators, device manager, Compose previews, Logcat, debugger, profiler, Layout Inspector and the signed-bundle wizard. Claude Code drives the same SDK from the terminal with `./gradlew` and `adb`.

**Xcode → Android Studio map**

| iOS (what Mariah knows) | Android (what replaces it) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Xcode | Android Studio (stable) | Download from developer.android.com/studio; current stable release name and version (verify at install) |
| `xcodebuild`, `project.yml` + XcodeGen | Gradle (`./gradlew`), `settings.gradle.kts`, `build.gradle.kts`, `gradle/libs.versions.toml` | Gradle files are plain text, so there is no generated-project step like XcodeGen |
| Swift Package Manager packages | Gradle modules (`:core:*`, `:feature:*`) and Maven dependencies in the version catalog | Table in §9.1 |
| Simulator | Android Emulator, devices defined as AVDs in **Device Manager** | Phone and Wear OS images |
| Instruments | Android Studio **Profiler** (CPU, memory, energy, network), Macrobenchmark for startup | |
| SwiftUI Previews / Interface Builder | **Compose Previews** (`@Preview`), Layout Inspector | Previews read the mock repositories, like iOS previews |
| Accessibility Inspector | **Accessibility Scanner** app on the device, Layout Inspector semantics, TalkBack | Compose UI tests run the Accessibility Test Framework |
| Console.app / Xcode console | **Logcat** | |
| `xcrun simctl` | `adb`, `emulator`, `avdmanager` | e.g. `adb shell am start -d gradus://board/demo` |
| Keychain | Android Keystore (+ Tink-encrypted DataStore) | §9.2 |
| TestFlight (internal / external) | Play **internal testing** (up to 100 testers, no review) / **closed testing** | Needs the Play Console (A8) |
| App Store Connect | **Play Console** | Organization account (A8) |
| Xcode Cloud | **GitHub Actions** (Linux runners) + Gradle Play Publisher | §9.6 |
| Apple Developer portal (App IDs, keys) | Play Console (app, signing), **Google Cloud Console** (OAuth clients, service accounts, Play Integrity API), **Firebase console** (FCM) | |
| Provisioning profiles, certificates | One **upload keystore** you keep; Google holds the app signing key (**Play App Signing**) | Back up the upload key; Play support can reset a lost upload key |
| `.ipa` archive | `.aab` Android App Bundle (Play), `.apk` (direct install) | |

**Step-by-step setup (Mariah, once; about 40 GB free disk is a comfortable margin (verify))**

1. **Check the Mac's chip.** Apple menu → About This Mac. "Apple M…" means Apple silicon: every emulator image below is the `arm64-v8a` variant. "Intel" means `x86_64` images. Record which in the daily update so sessions pick the right images.
2. **Install Android Studio.** Download "Android Studio for Mac (Apple chip)" (or Intel) from developer.android.com/studio, open the `.dmg`, drag to Applications. (Alternative: `brew install --cask android-studio`.) Open it; choose **Standard** in the Setup Wizard; accept every license. The wizard installs the Android SDK at `~/Library/Android/sdk`, Platform-Tools (`adb`), the Emulator, and one system image.
3. **JDK.** Use the **bundled JetBrains Runtime (JBR, Java 21)**; install no separate JDK. In Android Studio: Settings → Build, Execution, Deployment → Build Tools → Gradle → **Gradle JDK = jbr-21** (or "Embedded JDK").
4. **SDK Manager** (Settings → Languages & Frameworks → Android SDK):
   - *SDK Platforms:* the platform matching `compileSdk` (the latest stable, §9.2), **Android 16 (API 36)**, **Android 10 (API 29)** (the minSdk, A6).
   - *System images* (tick "Show Package Details"): API 36 **Google Play** phone image; API 29 **Google APIs** phone image; **Wear OS 6 (API 36)** and **Wear OS 4 (API 33)** images (the Wear minimum, §12 N5) (verify the current Wear OS image names in SDK Manager).

Nothing like CocoaPods or XcodeGen is needed.
7. **Emulators (Device Manager → Create virtual device).** Create these, named exactly, so automation never runs on Mariah's own devices (the iOS rule: automation never runs on Mariah's simulator or phone, handoff-2026-10-09 §1; the exact Android rule, including the little a session may do on her Pixel with her go-ahead, is the device rule in §10.1):
