Then Settings → System → **Developer options**: turn on **USB debugging**; turn on **Wireless debugging**. Connect by cable once and accept "Allow USB debugging?" (tick "Always allow from this computer"), or in Android Studio Device Manager → **Pair devices using Wi-Fi** and scan the QR code from Settings → Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with QR code. Verify `adb devices` lists the Pixel. Developer options do not change everyday use; "Revoke USB debugging authorizations" undoes the pairing. Record the Pixel model and Android version in the first daily update (it is the primary QA device, like Mariah's iPhone 17 Pro).
8a. **Wear OS watch and headphones (hardware, part of G0).** The iOS watch app is QA'd on Mariah's Apple Watch Series 10 and W1's done criterion is hearing a full plan through AirPods with the wrist down (iOS #36, §10.11). A3 ships Wear OS in 1.0, so buy a current **Wear OS 5 or 6** watch (proposal: a Pixel Watch, which pairs with her Pixel) and pair it through the **Pixel Watch** app. On the watch: Settings → System → About → tap **Build number** seven times → Developer options → turn on **ADB debugging** and **Wireless debugging**, then pair it in Android Studio Device Manager (Pair devices using Wi-Fi). Pair Bluetooth headphones **to the watch** (Settings → Connectivity → Bluetooth) for KW1 and KW2. Run the web repo locally with `API_V1_ENABLED=true bun run dev`, then `adb reverse tcp:8080 tcp:8080` for each connected device or emulator so `localhost` on the device reaches the Mac. Cleartext HTTP is allowed for `localhost` in debug only (network security config), mirroring the iOS ATS localhost exception. Release builds use `https://gradus.training`.

Android clients carry no secret; they authorize the package and signature.

Project settings → Add app → Android → package `training.gradus.app`, nickname "Gradus", debug SHA-1 → download `google-services.json` and hand it to the session (it is committed; it holds public identifiers only). Add a second Android app for `training.gradus.app.debug`. Project settings → Service accounts → generate a private key for the Firebase Admin SDK service account → copy `project_id`, `client_email`, `private_key` into Lovable secrets `FCM_PROJECT_ID`, `FCM_CLIENT_EMAIL`, `FCM_PRIVATE_KEY`, then delete the downloaded JSON. Cloud Messaging API (V1) is on by default for new projects (verify); the legacy server key is not used.

In Android Studio: Build → Generate Signed App Bundle or APK → Android App Bundle → **Create new…** keystore `gradus-upload.jks`, alias `gradus-upload`, RSA 2048, validity 25+ years, organization "Gradus Sports, Inc.", country US. The existing Sign in with Apple key is reused. Send the identifier to the session (`APPLE_SIWA_SERVICES_ID`).
15. **Google Play Console Organization account (A8).** Done by Mariah as the **account holder**; it gates internal testing, Play App Signing, Play Integrity and the store listing.
    1. Confirm the D-U-N-S record for **Gradus Sports, Inc.** (the one used for Apple enrollment): legal name and address must match exactly what is entered in Play Console; fix mismatches with Dun & Bradstreet first (it can take up to 30 days).
    2. Sign in at play.google.com/console/signup with the Google account that will own Gradus's apps long-term (a gradussports.com account, not a personal Gmail).

    4. Enter the **developer contact** name, email (support@gradussports.com is shown on the store listing) and phone; verify both by one-time code.

**What runs where (cloud vs Mac).** Unlike iOS (iOS §9.6: SwiftUI cannot build on Linux), the Android app **builds and unit-tests on Linux**: cloud Claude Code sessions can run `./gradlew` (Robolectric, Roborazzi screenshot tests, lint, contract drift) once the environment has the Android command-line SDK (a setup script installs `cmdline-tools`, `platforms;android-<compileSdk>`, `build-tools`). Emulators need hardware virtualization and are expected to be unavailable in cloud sessions (verify); instrumented tests run on GitHub Actions Linux runners with KVM (verify) or locally. Cloud builds need the environment's network allowlist to include `dl.google.com`, `maven.google.com`, `services.gradle.org`, `plugins.gradle.org` and `repo.maven.apache.org`; without them Gradle and `sdkmanager` fail and Android work stays on the Mac (Mariah sets this in the cloud environment's network settings). Anything touching Mariah's Pixel, a Wear device, push delivery, the microphone, the camera, biometrics or App Link verification runs in a **local session on the Mac**.

## 6. Architecture

Android adds a third client to the same backend. Nothing in this section changes how the web or iOS behave. Every server change listed here is **additive** under the iOS PRD §4.1 rules, which Android inherits as §4.1 of this document: no change to web-facing server functions, additive migrations only, Supabase Auth settings untouched, small revertible PRs, and "ask Lovable to apply pending migrations, then run the `docs/api/SMOKE.md` precheck" after any migration (iOS §4.1 rules 1–13).

**Source of truth.** Where the iOS PRD text and the iOS code at gradus-ios HEAD `91c6af2` disagree, Android follows the code (A2). Each such case is marked **[code wins]** below, with the file that shows it.

### 6.1 One backend, three clients

```
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                │  Lovable Cloud (Supabase project sdqfaqxmdmujxqhwlqdi)        │
                │  Postgres + RLS · Auth (GoTrue) · Storage · Realtime · pg_cron│
                └───────────────▲──────────────────────────────▲───────────────┘
                                │ service role                 │ publishable key + user JWT
                                │                              │ (auth session + refresh, realtime
┌───────────────────────────────┴───────────────┐              │  on messages, storage uploads)
│  gradus.training  (Cloudflare Worker,          │              │
│  TanStack Start app, repo gradus-coach-start)  │              │
│  Web UI (SSR+SPA)        /api/v1/* (JSON, OpenAPI 3.1)        │
│        └──────► src/lib/*.server.ts ◄──────┘                  │
│  Stripe · AI gateway · ElevenLabs · IJS scraper               │
│  APNs sender (iOS) · FCM HTTP v1 sender (NEW, Android)        │
│  /.well-known/apple-app-site-association · assetlinks.json (NEW)
└───────────────────────────────▲──────────────────────────────┘
                                │ HTTPS, Bearer <Supabase access token>
      ┌─────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
      │ Web browser / PWA       │ Gradus for iOS + watchOS  │ Gradus for Android + Wear OS (NEW)
      │ (unchanged)             │ (gradus-ios)              │ (mariah-gill/gradus-android)
      └─────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┴──────────────┬───────────┘
                                                                          └── direct to Supabase for the auth
                                                                              session, Realtime on `messages`,
                                                                              Storage uploads (§6.3)
```

**Why this keeps all three clients in step.** There is one database, one set of auth users, one set of storage buckets, and one copy of the business logic. The web reaches that logic through TanStack server functions; iOS and Android reach it through `/api/v1`. A rule change published once lands on every client (iOS §6.1). Android adds **no** Android-only business logic on the server. The only Android-specific server work is platform plumbing: FCM sending, Play Integrity verification, the Apple web sign-in flow, the Google audience, Digital Asset Links, Play age signals, and widening a few `platform` enums from `ios` to `ios | android` (Appendix A, "Android-specific server additions").

**Repositories and contract.** Android lives in `mariah-gill/gradus-android` (A7; iOS decision #13). The backend stays in `gradus-coach-start`. The contract is the OpenAPI document `docs/api/openapi.json` (OpenAPI 3.1, generated from zod by `bun run openapi`; CI fails when it is stale). Android vendors it the way gradus-ios does (`gradus-ios/Contract/`):

| gradus-android path | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Contract/openapi.json` | The API contract | `gradus-coach-start/docs/api/openapi.json` |
| `Contract/design-tokens.json` | Colour, radius and shadow tokens (§8) | `gradus-coach-start/docs/api/design-tokens.json` |
| `Contract/vectors/*.json` | Shared test vectors: `analytics-events.json`, `coach-sports.json`, `event-key.json`, `lesson-recurrence.json`, `name-normalization.json`, plus `README.md` | `gradus-coach-start/docs/api/vectors/` (same files as `gradus-ios/Contract/vectors/`) |
| `Contract/SOURCE_COMMIT` | The web-repo commit the three items above were copied from | iOS pins `fd543a12…` at HEAD |

A script (`scripts/sync-contract.sh <commit>`) copies all of it from one web commit and rewrites `SOURCE_COMMIT`. Unit tests run every shared vector against the Kotlin implementation, so Android computes lesson recurrence, name normalization, the board event key, sport lists and analytics event shapes exactly as iOS and the server do.

**Why not Supabase Edge Functions or a separate Android backend.** Same answer as iOS §6.1: the logic already lives in this Worker with the service role, Stripe, AI and transcription wired in, and moving it would require re-pointing the web, which §4.1 forbids.

### 6.2 Backend API v1

Android uses the **same `/api/v1` surface iOS uses**, with no forked or Android-only routes for product behaviour. Conventions are in iOS §6.2 and `docs/api/README.md`. This section restates what the Android client must implement, with the iOS file each behaviour comes from.

**Base URLs.**

| Build | API base (`BuildConfig.API_BASE_URL`, §9.6) | Supabase URL | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `debug` (emulator or Pixel) | `http://localhost:8080` after `adb reverse tcp:8080 tcp:8080` for each connected device or emulator (one rule, §9.6; `10.0.2.2` is not used) | `https://sdqfaqxmdmujxqhwlqdi.supabase.co` | iOS Debug uses `http://localhost:8080` (gradus-ios `project.yml`). The local server runs with `API_V1_ENABLED=true` on port 8080 (`docs/api/README.md` shows port 3000; pass the port explicitly (verify the `bun run dev` port flag)). Overridable by the Gradle property `gradus.apiBaseUrl`. |
| `release` (internal, closed and production tracks) | `https://gradus.training` | same | The only Supabase project is production; every build uses it with the **publishable key only** (iOS §4.1 rule 10; the key value is the one in gradus-ios `project.yml`). |

Cleartext HTTP is allowed only in the `debug` source set, through `res/xml/network_security_config.xml` with `cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"` for `localhost` only. This is the Android equivalent of the iOS `NSExceptionDomains: localhost` entry. Release: platform defaults, HTTPS only, user-installed CAs not trusted, **no certificate pinning** (iOS §4.2, §6.11; gradus.training certificates rotate about every 90 days). Debug builds show the API base in Settings → Debug, as iOS does (`SettingsView.debugSection`).

**Generated client.** `openapi-generator` (generator `kotlin`, library `jvm-retrofit2`, `serializationLibrary=kotlinx_serialization`, `enumUnknownDefaultCase=true`) generates the client into a `:core:api` Gradle module from `Contract/openapi.json` at build time. It is never hand-edited. Method names come from each operation's `operationId`, which is part of the v1 contract (`docs/api/README.md`). If the generator mis-handles a schema (multipart, discriminated unions such as `POST /auth/signup/coach`'s `confirmationRequired` union, `POST /rooms/ensure`), that one operation gets a hand-written Retrofit method in `:core:api`, pinned by a contract test, as iOS pins its hand-built outbox paths (`…PathsContractTests`). Ktor client is an acceptable alternative if the Retrofit output proves awkward. The choice stays behind the repository interfaces (§9).

**Writes go through a raw JSON transport, not the generated client** (gradus-ios `LivePlansRepository.send`, `PlansRepository.swift` ~L268; same pattern in `RosterRepository`, `SettingsRepositories`, `LiveGuardianRepositories`, `ResourcesRepository`, `ErrorReporter`, `UsageAnalytics`, `MessagesRepository`, `LiveDeviceTokenUploader` in `LiveMeRepository.swift`, `AttendanceRecorder`). Every outbox-capable write (roster, plans, athlete plans, moves, sessions, settings, guardians, resources, messages, board follows, attendance, devices, errors, analytics) uses `MutationTransport` (raw OkHttp JSON, §6.5) for the **live** call as well as for the queued replay:

- Path builders `RosterPaths`, `PlansPaths`, `AthletePlansPaths`, `SettingsPaths`, `GuardianPaths`, `ResourcesPaths`, `ErrorPaths`, `UsageAnalyticsPaths` are ported 1:1 from gradus-ios. Each is pinned by a contract test asserting that every built `method + path` exists in `Contract/openapi.json` (ports of `PlansPathsContractTests`, `LiveActivityTokenPathsTests` and siblings).
- A body is encoded **once** (kotlinx.serialization → `JsonObject`, keys sorted recursively, compact; iOS `JSONEncoder.outputFormatting = [.sortedKeys]`). The same bytes go out live and, on status 0 or 5xx, into the `pending_mutation` row, so the live call and the queued row are byte-identical.
- **Every** raw request carries `Idempotency-Key`, including `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE`: the coroutine's `IdempotencyKey` context element if present, else a fresh lowercase UUID (`IdempotencyKey.current ?? IdempotencyKey.new()`).
- `Accept: application/json` always; `Content-Type: application/json` only when a body exists (`LiveMutationTransport.send`).
- A non-2xx reply with a server envelope throws that `ApiError`; with no decodable envelope (an HTML 502 from Cloudflare, an empty 404) it throws `ApiError(status, "http_<status>", "The server returned <status>.")` (`APIError.http`). A 2xx reply whose body cannot be decoded throws `malformed_response` with status 200.
- The generated client is used for **reads** (with `If-None-Match`) and for calls that are never queued (auth, billing, voice, AI, schedule import).

**JSON.** One shared `Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true; explicitNulls = false; coerceInputValues = true }`. The server adds optional fields within v1, and an installed build must never fail to decode a field or enum value it has not learned. (Decision #38 made `method` a plain string for this reason; `enumUnknownDefaultCase` covers every other enum.) Outgoing bodies are compact, with no pretty-printing and no slash escaping. This matches gradus-ios `GradusAPIClient.jsonEncodingOptions = [.withoutEscapingSlashes]`.

**Interceptor chain** (OkHttp, in this order; mirrors gradus-ios `GradusAPIClient.make` middlewares):

| # | Interceptor | Behaviour | iOS source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ClientHeaderInterceptor` | Sets `X-Gradus-Client: android/<versionName>+<versionCode>`, for example `android/1.0.0+1`. The Wear OS app sends `wearos/<versionName>+<versionCode>`. Sets `Accept: application/json` when absent. The server's `parseClientHeader` pattern `^([a-z0-9_-]+)\/(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)\+(\d+)$` already accepts both. `versionName` must always be three-part `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. | `ClientHeaderMiddleware`, `APIEnvironment.clientHeaderValue` |
| 2 | `IdempotencyKeyInterceptor` | Adds `Idempotency-Key` when the calling coroutine carries an `IdempotencyKey` context element. This is the equivalent of Swift's `@TaskLocal IdempotencyKey.current`, set with `withContext(IdempotencyKey(key)) { … }`. It never overwrites a header already set. Keys are lowercase UUIDs (`IdempotencyKey.new()`). `IdempotencyKey.derive(attempt, payload)` = `"$attempt-" + first 12 bytes of SHA-256(payload) as hex`, so a retry of the same attempt replays and an edited form does not. | `IdempotencyKeyMiddleware`, `IdempotencyKey` |
| 3 | `IntegrityInterceptor` | **Only on `postAuthPassword`.** Attaches a Play Integrity token, log-only (see §6.4 "Bot protection"). It fails open on every error and never adds more than 1,500 ms. | `AppAttestAssertionMiddleware` |
| 4 | `BearerInterceptor` | Adds `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` when a session exists. The token comes from `SessionManager.accessToken()` (§6.4), which refreshes an expired token first and falls back to the stored token if the refresh fails. There is **no OkHttp `Authenticator` and no automatic retry on 401**, as on iOS. | `BearerAuthMiddleware`, `SupabaseSessionManager.accessToken()` |
| 5 | Error mapping (call adapter) | Every failure becomes one `ApiError(status, code, message, retryAfterSeconds)`. See the table below. | `TransportErrorMiddleware`, `performAPI`, `APIError` |

**Error model.** The server envelope `{"error":{"code","message","details"}}` decodes into `ApiError`. `details.retryAfterSeconds` maps to `retryAfterSeconds`. Client-side codes and the single place for user copy (`ApiError.userMessage`) are copied verbatim from gradus-ios `APIError.swift`:

| Code | Raised when | `userMessage` (verbatim) |
|---|---|---|
| `api_disabled` (503) | Kill switch off | "Gradus is briefly unavailable. Your changes are saved and will sync shortly." |
| `invalid_credentials` (401) | Password sign-in refused | "Incorrect email/username or password." |
| `unauthenticated` (401) | No or expired session | "Please sign in again." |
| `rate_limited` (429) | Limiter | "Too many attempts. Please wait a moment and try again." |
| `rate_limiter_unavailable` (503) | Limiter table unreachable (fails closed) | "Please try again in a moment." |
| `offline` (client) | No usable network. Android: `ConnectivityManager` reports no active network with `NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET`, or `UnknownHostException` while it reports none | "You're offline. Check your connection and try again." |
| `unreachable` (client) | A network exists but the server can't be reached (DNS, refused, timeout, TLS) | "Can't reach Gradus right now. Please try again in a moment." |
| `cancelled` (client) | Coroutine cancelled or OkHttp call cancelled, including wrapped. **Not a failure:** screens skip it (`isCancellation`), never toast it | "That was interrupted. Please try again." |
| `malformed_response` (client) | Decoding failed | "Something went wrong. Please try again." |
| `session_not_stored` (client) | A minted session could not be written to or read back from secure storage | "The session could not be stored on this device." |
| `validation_failed` (400) | zod | "Some of that didn't look right. Please check and try again." |
| `internal` (500) | | "Something went wrong. Please try again." |
| `roster_full` (409) | Roster cap | "Your roster is full on your current plan." (never the server's wording, never an upgrade CTA; iOS §6.8 rule 2) |
| `ai_consent_required` (403) | An AI route without the account's AI permission | The server's "Turn on AI features to use this."; also emits `AiConsentEvents`, which brings the permission screen back (§6.7.1a) |
| `ai_unavailable_for_minors` (403) | AI for an athlete under 18 or with no birthdate | The server's message |
| `auth_update_failed` (client, 400) | `updateUser` failed | The Supabase error description |
| `http_<status>` (client) | Non-2xx with no decodable envelope, e.g. an HTML 502 from Cloudflare (`APIError.http`) | "The server returned <status>." (the message itself, as "anything else") |
| `terms_deferred` (client, status 200) | `POST /me/terms/accept` answered `deferred: true` (`LiveMeRepository.acceptTerms`) | "Finish setting up your profile on gradus.training, then accept the terms here." |
| `upload_failed` (client) | Storage upload failed while online (`VoiceNoteStorage`, `ResourceUploadStorage`) | "Couldn't upload the voice note. Please try again." / "Couldn't upload the file. Please try again." |
| `unauthenticated` (client, 401) | A voice-note upload is attempted with no access token | "Please sign in again." |
| `account_email_missing` (409) | `/auth/google`, `/auth/apple`, Apple web exchange: the identity has no email to sign in with | The server's message: "This account has no email on file to sign in with." |
| `invalid_identity_token` (401) | `/auth/google`, `/auth/apple`, Apple web callback: token failed verification | The server's message |
| anything else | | The server's `message` |

In `debug` builds only, the `offline` / `unreachable` copy is suffixed with ` (host:port, <exception>)` so a wrong base URL is obvious. Release copy never names the host (`APIError.offline`). Helper predicates mirror iOS: `isTransportFailure` (status 0 and `offline`/`unreachable`), `isAuthFailure` (401 or `unauthenticated`), `isRetryable` (≥ 500, 429, or status 0). `ApiError.isConnectivityMessage(message)` (prefix "You're offline." or "Can't reach Gradus right now.") keeps connectivity notices out of `POST /errors` (gradus-ios `AppModel.start`).

**Conventions the client honours** (iOS §6.2 table; the server is unchanged):

| Concern | Android client rule |
|---|---|
| Versioning | Only `/api/v1`. Additive changes are tolerated by the JSON settings above. |
| Force update | On every cold start, before restoring the session, `GET /meta/client-policy`. Android reads `minSupportedVersion.android`, which the server must add (Appendix A, server addition S-1). A missing `android` key counts as `0.0.0`, so there is never a forced update. If the current `versionName` parses (`SemanticVersion`: accepts `2`, `2.0`, `2.0.0`, an optional leading `v`, compared numerically) and is lower, show the blocking **Update Gradus** screen with the server `message` or the iOS copy "This version of Gradus is no longer supported. Please update to keep going." An unreachable policy endpoint never blocks launch (gradus-ios `AppModel.start`). **Android-native difference:** the action follows §7.1.0: "Open gradus.training in your browser" until the Play listing exists (`BuildConfig.PLAY_LISTING_LIVE = false`), then "Update on Google Play" opening `market://details?id=training.gradus.app` (https fallback); iOS's button reads "Open gradus.training in Safari" (`RootView`). Play In-App Updates is not used in 1.0 (§12 N37). |
| `GET /meta/config` | Fetched at launch (best effort) for `paywallEnabled`, `coachProEnabled`, `foundingCoachCutoff`, `termsVersion` (gradus-ios `MetaConfigRepository`). |
| Content | JSON in and out; multipart for audio (`audio/mp4`, filename `*.m4a`) and images; ISO 8601 UTC dates; UUID strings; money as integer cents plus currency. |
| Idempotency | Every creating POST the server marks `idempotent` gets a key: online writes set it through the context element, and queued writes carry their key from creation (§6.5). The server replays a stored response for 24 h per `(user_id, key)`. `409 idempotency_key_reused` / `idempotency_key_in_progress` are conflicts (§6.5). **Exception copied from iOS:** `POST /devices` sends `Idempotency-Key: device-<token>`, which the server deliberately ignores (the route is not `idempotent`, so re-registering after a sign-out within 24 h still writes the row). `DELETE /devices/{token}` sends `device-unregister-<token>` (gradus-ios `LiveMeRepository`). |
| ETag | Small per-user collections are fetched with `If-None-Match: <stored etag>`. `304` keeps the cached body. Repositories return a sealed `Fresh(body, etag)` / `NotModified` (gradus-ios `PlansRepository` `.fresh/.notModified`). A queued (not yet sent) optimistic edit **drops the stored ETag**, so the next load always hits the network and the cache heals to the server's truth (`RosterModel.invalidateIfQueued`). OkHttp's HTTP cache is **not** used; the server sends `no-store` and caching is explicit (§6.5). |
| Pagination | `?limit&cursor` → `{ items, nextCursor }` on `GET /rooms/{id}`, plan sessions, invoices. |
| Rate limiting | `429` with `retryAfterSeconds` (envelope) and/or `Retry-After` (header). Generated-client calls surface the envelope value in `ApiError.retryAfterSeconds`. The outbox reads **only the `Retry-After` header**, for 429 and 5xx alike (gradus-ios `OutboundResponse.retryAfterSeconds`; §6.5). |
| Kill switch | `503 api_disabled`: screens render from cache, writes queue (§6.5), the copy above is shown once. |
| Composite `/me` | `GET /me` is the launch read: role, onboarding state, terms, `sports`, parent verification, athlete `account_state`, `athleteVoiceToPlan`, unread and so on (iOS Appendix A; gradus-ios `MeSummary`). `athleteVoiceToPlan` missing means **false** (decision #48). Live Board visibility = `sports` contains `figure_skating`, or `sports` unknown (gradus-ios `MeSummary.showsLiveBoard`). **[code wins]** iOS §6.2 also names a composite `GET /coach/home?week=`; it was never built (no route under `src/routes/api/v1/coach/`). Android calls `GET /coach/roster`, `/coach/roster/practice-summaries` and `/coach/wrap-ups/pending` as iOS does. |
| Auth header | `Authorization: Bearer <Supabase access token>`, verified server-side by `auth.getClaims`. Public routes (`[pub]`) are called with the bearer when one exists, so the server can attribute (for example `POST /errors`). |
| Impersonation | The API rejects impersonation tokens; the app never holds one. |

**Platform tags the Android client sends.** Several request bodies carry a platform today and the server must accept Android's value (Appendix A, server additions S-1 to S-4): `POST /devices {token, platform: "android"}` (already accepted: `registerDeviceTokenInput` is `z.enum(["ios","android"])` and `device_tokens.platform` CHECK allows `android`); `POST /analytics/events {platform: "android", …}` (today `z.enum(["ios"])`, which must widen); `POST /errors` (today tagged `platform: "ios"` server-side by `reportIosError`, which must take the platform from `X-Gradus-Client`); `POST /feedback {path: "android/settings"}` (iOS sends `ios/settings`, `AccountModel.feedbackPath`).

**Tests (Android).** (1) Interceptor order and headers on a MockWebServer: `X-Gradus-Client` matches the server regex; `Idempotency-Key` present only when set; integrity headers only on `postAuthPassword`. (2) Every row of the error table maps to the listed copy (a port of the iOS `APIError` tests). (3) `SemanticVersion` parsing and comparison vectors from the iOS tests. (4) A contract test per hand-written path and per path builder (`RosterPaths` … `UsageAnalyticsPaths`): every built method + path exists in `Contract/openapi.json`. (5) Decoding a `/me` body with an unknown field and an unknown enum value succeeds. (6) A 502 with an HTML body yields code `http_502` and "The server returned 502." (7) A raw `PATCH` and `DELETE` through `MutationTransport` carry an `Idempotency-Key`; the live body bytes equal the bytes stored when the same write is enqueued.

### 6.3 What Android talks to Supabase about directly

The same four uses as iOS §6.3, through **supabase-kt** (`io.github.jan-tennert.supabase`). Everything else goes through `/api/v1`. The app never issues an ad-hoc table query.

| Use | How on Android | iOS reference |
|---|---|---|
| Session storage and refresh | supabase-kt **Auth** (`auth-kt`) with `autoRefreshToken = true`, `alwaysAutoRefresh` on, and a custom `SessionManager` backed by the encrypted store in §6.4. Broker-minted sessions are **imported** (§6.4 "Adopting a session"). Uses: `refresh_token` grant (captcha-exempt), `updateUser` (email/password change), `verifyEmailOtp` with a token hash (recovery and email-change links), and `signOut(SignOutScope.LOCAL)`. **Stack note:** the recommended stack lists supabase-kt for Realtime and Storage only. iOS also uses supabase-swift's Auth module (`import Auth` in `SupabaseSessionManager.swift`), so parity requires Auth too. | `SupabaseSessionManager.swift` |
| Realtime messages | `realtime-kt`, `postgres_changes` **INSERT** on `public.messages`. One channel per open room: topic `room:<roomId>`, filter `room_id=eq.<id>` for athlete rooms or `direct_room_id=eq.<id>` for direct rooms. One unfiltered channel `rooms:<random uuid>` for the rooms list and the unread badge. Auth: the `apikey` header plus the user's access token, from the same `SessionManager`. The client connects on the first subscribe and disconnects when the last channel goes away. **A signal is only a refetch trigger:** the record yields `{id, room_id, direct_room_id, sender_user_id}` and the screen refetches through the API (`GET /rooms/{id}`, `GET /messages/unread-total`). If the channel drops, the room refetches on foreground. Realtime is a refinement, never a dependency (iOS §6.6). | `Realtime.swift` (`SupabaseMessagesRealtime`) |
| Voice-note upload | `storage-kt` upload to bucket `voice-notes` at `<roomId>/<userId>/<uuid>.m4a`, `contentType = "audio/mp4"`, `upsert = false`, bearer = current access token (a fresh client config per upload, so the bearer is never stale). Then `POST /rooms/{id}/messages` with `audioPath`. Bucket RLS admits room participants. Upload errors: an `IOException` maps to `offline`/`unreachable`; anything else to code `upload_failed` with "Couldn't upload the voice note. Please try again." If the upload is refused or fails while online, the app sends the note **inline** (`voiceInline`, base64 `audio/mp4` with `durationSeconds`) and the server stores it, as the web does. Voice notes need a connection; offline, the copy is "Voice notes need a connection. Try again when you're back online." **[code wins]** iOS §6.5 says voice notes queue offline; gradus-ios `RoomSession.sendVoiceNote` refuses them. With no access token the upload fails with `401 unauthenticated` "Please sign in again." (`VoiceNoteStorage`). Minors never record (decision #32; `/me`). | `VoiceNoteStorage.swift`, `RoomSession.swift` |
| Coach resource upload | `POST /coach/resources/upload-url` mints a signed `{path, token}`. `storage-kt` `uploadToSignedUrl` on bucket `resource-pdfs` with **no bearer** (the signed token is the credential) and `upsert = false`. The returned path goes to `POST /coach/resources` as `storagePath`. Failure copy: "Couldn't upload the file. Please try again." | `ResourceUploadStorage.swift` |
| Resource download | `POST /resources/{id}/signed-url`, then a plain OkHttp GET of the signed URL into `cacheDir/Gradus/ResourceFiles/<resourceId>.<ext>`. Concurrent opens of one resource share one in-flight download (a per-id `Deferred` in a `Mutex`-guarded map). A cached file is reused. | `ResourceViewerSheet.swift` (`ResourceFileCache`) |

**Not direct:** schedule-import images (`POST /coach/schedule-import/parse`, multipart `image` part) and voice capture for plans (`POST /voice/transcribe`, `/voice/build-plan`, `/athlete/voice/build-plan`, multipart `audio` + `mode` + optional `planId`) go to the API (gradus-ios `ScheduleImportUpload.swift`, `VoiceUpload.swift`). **Wear OS** (gradus-ios `GradusWatch/GradusWatchApp.swift` L73-75, `CompanionSession.swift`). The watch app uses supabase-kt **Auth only**: its own `SessionManager` on the watch (the same Tink AEAD + Android Keystore design as §6.4, auto refresh with the `refresh_token` grant) holds the **companion session** minted by `POST /auth/companion` on the phone and delivered over the Data Layer. It is a second, independent session: the phone never hands the watch its own refresh token, because Supabase refresh tokens are single-use and two holders would invalidate each other. The watch never uses Realtime or Storage. It calls the API through its own generated client and `MutationTransport` with `X-Gradus-Client: wearos/<versionName>+<versionCode>` (iOS `watchos/<v>+<b>`, `WatchConfig`). Its token storage follows the §6.4 storage and restore rules (not backed up; undecryptable → signed out, file deleted).

**Tests.** A Realtime channel test against a fake socket (subscribe → insert → one refetch; cancel → `removeChannel`). Voice upload builds the exact path pattern and falls back to inline on a refused upload. The resource cache de-duplicates two concurrent opens.

### 6.4 Authentication and account

**Design: the API is the identity broker** (iOS §6.4, unchanged). The Worker holds the service role, so it bypasses Turnstile captcha and can mint sessions. Lovable Cloud exposes no Apple provider, and the web's Google sign-in is a Lovable-brokered web redirect, so every native sign-in goes through `/api/v1/auth/*`, and the client then imports the minted Supabase session. Android adds **no** change to Supabase Auth settings (§4.1 rule 3).

**Sign-in methods on Android (A5).**

| Method | Android client | Server | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Email or username + password** | Native form ("Email or username", "Password", "Remember me", "Sign in", "Forgot password?"; copy and layout in §7.1, from gradus-ios `SignInView`). Trims the identifier. Calls `POST /auth/password {identifier, password}`. Model rules (gradus-ios `SignInModel`): "Sign in" is enabled when the identifier trimmed of whitespace is non-empty, the password is non-empty, and no sign-in is running; phases `Idle`, `SigningIn(method ∈ password/apple/google)`, `Failed(message)`, with the spinner on the button of the running method only; "Remember me" starts **on** exactly when a remembered identifier exists (off on first launch) and the field is pre-filled with it; after **any** successful method (password, Apple, Google) the identifier field's trimmed content is stored (toggle on) or the key removed (toggle off), and the password is cleared; every failure shows `ApiError.userMessage` inline. | Unchanged. If the identifier has no `@`, the username resolves to the synthetic `athlete-<id>@users.gradus.training` email (`resolveSignInEmail`). GoTrue password grant with the **service-role bearer** (captcha-exempt, `src/lib/api/gotrue.ts`). Rate limits: 20/min per IP and 10/min per identifier. Every failure answers the generic `401 invalid_credentials`. | Exists |
| **Google** | Credential Manager, `GetSignInWithGoogleOption(serverClientId = <Web client ID>)` from the "Continue with Google" button (an explicit button, not a one-tap sheet at launch; iOS 1.0 shows no Google button at all, see the cross-platform note below). Takes `GoogleIdTokenCredential.idToken` and calls `POST /auth/google {idToken}`. The returned ID token has `aud = Web client ID` and `azp = Android client ID`. **The button is shown only when `BuildConfig.GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID` is non-empty** (the parity rule from gradus-ios `GoogleSignInProvider.isConfigured`: never show a button that can only fail). A user cancel (`GetCredentialCancellationException`) is silent. `NoCredentialException` (no Google account on the device) and other Credential Manager failures show the Android copy in §7.1.2a (Google has no iOS counterpart in 1.0, so these strings are new). | `verifyGoogleIdToken` today accepts only `aud == GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID`. **Server addition S-5:** keep the iOS path (`aud == GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID`) unchanged; additionally accept `aud == GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID` **only when `azp` ∈ `GOOGLE_ANDROID_CLIENT_IDS`** (500 `internal` if no audience secret is set; wrong `azp` → `401 invalid_identity_token`). Identity lookup, email match (only when Google vouches `email_verified`) and the session mint are unchanged. | Needs S-5 and Google Cloud setup |
| **Sign in with Apple** (so accounts made with Apple on iPhone can sign in on Android) | **Web flow.** There is no native Apple SDK on Android. Sequence below. | **Server additions S-6 to S-8:** start, form_post callback, exchange. | New |
| **Coach email sign-up** | Native form → `POST /auth/signup/coach {email, password (≥ 8), promoCode?, inviteCode?}`. A `{confirmationRequired: false, accessToken, …}` answer imports the session. `{confirmationRequired: true}` shows the "check your email" state (§7.1). | Unchanged (GoTrue `/signup` with the project's own confirmation setting; 10/min). | Exists |
| **Parent, minor athlete, adult athlete sign-up** | `/signup/*` flows (§7.1), onboarding before the account (decision #27). | Unchanged. | Exists |
| **Forgot password** | Sheet "Reset password": "Enter the email on your account and we'll send a link to reset your password." Field "Email", button "Send reset link". It is pre-filled when the sign-in identifier contains `@`. Calls `POST /auth/recover {email}` **without** `client` (gradus-ios `ForgotPasswordModel`: the email links to `https://gradus.training/auth/confirm` whichever client asked; `client: "app"` and its `gradus://reset-password` redirect are not used). Sent state: "Check your email" / "If an account exists for {email}, a reset link is on its way. The link opens Gradus so you can set a new password." **[code wins]** `BuildConfig.GRADUS_NATIVE_RESET = true`, matching gradus-ios `project.yml` L131 `GRADUS_NATIVE_RESET: true` at `91c6af2`, so Android always uses this sentence (§7.1.3 must say the same). Model rules (gradus-ios `ForgotPasswordModel`, `SignInView`): "Send reset link" is enabled when the email contains "@" and nothing is sending; the email is trimmed before sending; errors (`userMessage`) show inline; the sent state's button is "Done"; the sheet's top bar has "Cancel". | Unchanged: always `{ok: true}` (no enumeration oracle), 10/min. | Exists |
| **Change password / email** | Settings → Account & security (§7.12) through supabase-kt `updateUser` (authenticated, no captcha). Failures map to `auth_update_failed` with the Supabase description. Shown only for accounts whose providers include `email` (providers = `app_metadata.providers`, else `app_metadata.provider`, else `identities[].provider`). | Unchanged. | Exists |
| **Wear OS companion session** | The phone calls `POST /auth/companion` and hands the result to the watch over the Wear Data Layer (§6.15). The watch never signs in on its own. | Unchanged. The route's summary text says "Apple Watch"; behaviour is platform-neutral. | Exists |

**Sign in with Apple on Android, end to end.** This subsection is the **single owner** of the Apple web-flow contract; §7.1 (sign-in screen copy and placement) and Appendix A S-6/S-7 reference it and must not restate a different shape.

1. The app creates a random `codeVerifier` (43–128 chars, base64url) and calls **`POST /api/v1/auth/apple/web/start {codeChallenge: base64url(SHA-256(codeVerifier))}`** (S-6, `[pub]`, 20/min per IP). The server creates a row in the new `auth_web_handoffs` table (state hash, code challenge, random raw nonce; **the row expires 10 minutes** after start). It answers `{authorizeUrl}` = `https://appleid.apple.com/auth/authorize?client_id=<APPLE_SIWA_SERVICES_ID>&redirect_uri=https://gradus.training/api/public/auth/apple/callback&response_type=code%20id_token&response_mode=form_post&scope=name%20email&state=<state>&nonce=<SHA-256 hex of raw nonce>`. `response_mode=form_post` is required whenever `scope` is requested.
2. The app opens `authorizeUrl` in an **Auth Tab** (`androidx.browser` 1.9+, `AuthTabIntent`) with an **https redirect** to the verified App Link `https://gradus.training/auth/apple/done` where the browser supports https Auth Tab redirects (verify the minimum Chrome version). Where Auth Tab is unsupported, androidx falls back to a Custom Tab; the result then arrives as an App Link (or the custom-scheme fallback below) through `onNewIntent` on the single activity that owns both intent filters. Both paths are handled (verify the current androidx fallback behaviour). Apple's own pages handle the Apple ID and two-factor; no Gradus UI runs inside the tab.
3. Apple POSTs `code`, `id_token`, `state` and (first authorization only) `user` (JSON with `name.firstName`, `name.lastName`, `email`) to **`POST /api/public/auth/apple/callback`** (S-7, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, outside `/api/v1` because it is browser-facing and not JSON; it still honours `API_V1_ENABLED`). The server:
   - looks up the handoff row by `state` (unexpired, unused);
   - verifies `id_token` against Apple's JWKS with `iss = https://appleid.apple.com`, **`aud = APPLE_SIWA_SERVICES_ID`**, and `nonce` = SHA-256 of the stored raw nonce;
   - runs `findOrCreateIdentityUser(provider: "apple", providerSub: sub, …, name)` exactly as `POST /auth/apple` does. Apple's `sub` is team-scoped, so an account created with Apple on iPhone (team `79RN82HXPZ`) matches the same `auth_identities` row (verify that the Services ID is grouped under the primary App ID `training.gradus.app`);
   - exchanges `code` for Apple's refresh token with `client_id = APPLE_SIWA_SERVICES_ID`, and stores it with **`apple_client_id = APPLE_SIWA_SERVICES_ID`** (new nullable column, S-8) so account deletion can revoke it;
   - writes `user_id` and `is_new_user` on the row, creates a one-time `handoffCode` **valid for 2 minutes** and bound to the row's `codeChallenge`, and stores only its hash.

   It answers **`303`** to `https://gradus.training/auth/apple/done?handoff=<handoffCode>&state=<state>` (on any error: `…/auth/apple/done?error=<code>`). That path is an Android **App Link** (§6.10; S-10 lists it). The web page served at `/auth/apple/done` (for a browser where the link did not open the app) says "Return to the Gradus app to finish signing in." and shows a "Continue to Gradus" button linking to the **custom-scheme fallback** `training.gradus.app://auth/apple?handoff=…&state=…` (or `?error=…`), because a Custom Tab may keep a redirect without a user gesture inside the tab instead of handing it to the app. **No Supabase token ever appears in a URL.**
4. The app checks `state` against the one it started with and calls **`POST /api/v1/auth/apple/web/exchange {handoffCode, codeVerifier}`** (S-6, `[pub]`, 20/min per IP). The server checks SHA-256(verifier) against the stored challenge, marks the row consumed, mints the session with `mintSessionForEmail` (the same admin magic-link mint Apple, Google and the companion use), and answers `{accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn, isNewUser}`, the same shape as `POST /auth/apple`. A replayed handoff, an expired one, or a wrong verifier → `401 invalid_identity_token`.
5. The app adopts the session (below) and continues exactly as after the iOS Apple sign-in (`isNewUser` → role chooser and onboarding, §7.1). The start and exchange calls run inside the sign-in model's `run(.apple)`, so the Apple button shows the spinner and the remembered identifier is persisted on success, as on iOS.

The custom-scheme fallback is acceptable here, where iOS rejected `gradus://` for password reset links ("any app could claim the scheme", `ForgotPasswordModel`): an intercepted `handoffCode` is useless without the `codeVerifier`, which never leaves the app process, and it expires in 2 minutes.

**Failure copy** (one rule, from gradus-ios `AppleSignInButton.handle` and `SignInModel.run`; §7.1 uses this table):

| Outcome | Shown |
|---|---|
| (a) The tab is closed or the app resumes with no handoff (the `ASAuthorizationError.canceled` equivalent) | Nothing; the button re-enables |
| (b) The return carries `?error=…`, the `state` does not match, or Apple's side failed (the non-cancel `ASAuthorization` failure equivalent) | "Sign in with Apple isn't available on this build yet. Use your email or username for now." (`AppleSignInButton.unavailableMessage`) |
| (c) `POST /auth/apple/web/start` or `/auth/apple/web/exchange` fails | `ApiError.userMessage`, exactly as `SignInModel.run`: offline "You're offline. Check your connection and try again.", unreachable, `rate_limited`, `account_email_missing` / `invalid_identity_token` server message, and so on |

There is no Android-only Apple failure string. The Apple button appears wherever it appears on iOS: the sign-in screen and the sign-up forms (§7.1). Its styling follows Apple's guidelines: black on light and white on dark, 48 dp tall, `GradusRadius.md` corners, 45% opacity when disabled (gradus-ios `AppleSignInButton`).

**Cross-platform note on Google.** gradus-ios injects `StubGoogleSignInProvider()` (`Gradus/Dependencies.swift` L40, L192; `isConfigured = false`), so iOS 1.0 hides Google until `GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID` exists (iOS §6.4, 2026-09-19 note). Google is therefore **Android-only in 1.0**. A user who creates an account with Google on Android has no password and no Google button on iPhone; that account reaches iPhone through "Forgot password?" (which sets a password on the same email) and then email sign-in. Whether to ship the iOS Google provider in the same window is §12 N19.

**Bot protection, captcha and attestation** (iOS §6.4 last paragraph, decision log I15).

- **No Turnstile in the app, ever.** gradus-ios contains no captcha code. Every captcha-guarded GoTrue call (password grant, sign-up, recovery) is made server-side with the service-role bearer, which Supabase exempts (iOS §4.2). Abuse control is server rate limiting, generic errors, and attestation **logged, never enforced**.
- **App Attest → Play Integrity.** iOS registers an App Attest key once per device (fire-and-forget on password sign-in, `POST /auth/attest/register`) and attaches `X-Gradus-Attest-Key-Id` / `X-Gradus-Attest-Assertion` to `postAuthPassword` only. The server logs the outcome and never changes the response (`password.ts` "never enforcing" test). Android equivalent:
  - At app start, warm up a Play Integrity **Standard** token provider: `StandardIntegrityManager.prepareIntegrityToken(cloudProjectNumber)`. Failures are ignored.
  - On `postAuthPassword` only, `IntegrityInterceptor` builds the canonical body `{"identifier":<json string>,"password":<json string>}` **by hand**, escaping each string exactly as ECMAScript `JSON.stringify` does (the server hashes `JSON.stringify({identifier, password})`): `\"`, `\\`, `\b`, `\f`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`; every other U+0000–U+001F as lowercase `\u00xx`; lone surrogates as lowercase `\udxxx`; `/` and non-ASCII left unescaped. Vector tests compare the bytes with Node's `JSON.stringify` output. (gradus-ios `jsonString` in `AppAttestAssertionMiddleware.swift` writes U+0008/U+000C as `\u0008`/`\u000c`, so its hash differs from the server's for passwords containing those characters; log-only and harmless, §12 N24.) It requests a token with `requestHash = lowercase hex SHA-256` of those bytes, raced against a **1,500 ms** deadline (`AppAttestAssertionMiddleware.defaultAssertionDeadline`; an abandoned request is never awaited). It sets `X-Gradus-Integrity-Token: <token>`. Any failure or timeout sends the request without the header.
  - There is no registration call: Play Integrity has no key-registration step, so Android never calls `POST /auth/attest/register` and has no `app_attest_keys` row.
  - **Server addition S-9:** `password.ts` also reads `x-gradus-integrity-token`, decodes it with the Play Integrity `decodeIntegrityToken` API (service-account credentials as a Lovable secret), checks `requestDetails.requestHash`, `requestDetails.requestPackageName == training.gradus.app`, and `appIntegrity.appRecognitionVerdict`, and **logs** `[play-integrity] password sign-in {present, outcome}`. It never changes the response, guarded by the same try/catch and a "never enforcing" test.
  - **Blocked by A8:** decoding needs the Google Cloud project linked to the app in Play Console. Until then the client still sends tokens (the request fails or the server logs `unverifiable`), which proves the plumbing.

**Adopting a session** (gradus-ios `SupabaseSessionManager.adopt`). Import `{accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn}` into supabase-kt (`auth.importSession(UserSession(…))`, then `auth.retrieveUserForCurrentSession(updateSession = true)` (verify the API names in the supabase-kt version chosen)). The server user fetch is required, not optional: iOS `client.setSession(accessToken:refreshToken:)` validates (and if needed refreshes) with the server before the session is trusted, then reads back `currentSession`. Then **read the session back from storage**. If it is not readable, throw `session_not_stored`, so a failed secure-storage write never leaves the user making unauthenticated calls. On success the session state becomes `SignedIn(userId lowercase)`, then the shell runs the signed-in entry sequence (below). Remember-me: on success, if "Remember me" is on, store the trimmed identifier under `gradus.auth.rememberedIdentifier` (DataStore Preferences, device-wide), otherwise remove it. The password field is cleared (gradus-ios `SignInModel`).

**Token storage.** iOS keeps the session in the Keychain with `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly` (service `training.gradus.app.auth`), readable by background sync after first unlock and never migrated. Android equivalent:

- supabase-kt's custom `SessionManager` writes the serialized session to a **DataStore file encrypted with a Tink AEAD** (`AES256_GCM`). The Tink keyset is wrapped by an **Android Keystore** master key (`android-keystore://gradus_auth_master`), hardware-backed where available, with **no user-authentication requirement** (background sync must read it).
- The file lives in credential-encrypted storage, which is available after the first unlock since boot. That is the Android meaning of "after first unlock". The app is **not** `directBootAware`.
- **Backup: see §6.11.** `android:allowBackup="true"` with `data_extraction_rules.xml` (API 31+) and `backup_rules.xml` (API 29–30) that back up **only** the device-preference DataStore allow-list (§6.5 preference table) and exclude the session DataStore file, the Tink keyset prefs, every Room database, everything under `noBackupFilesDir`, and caches. A restored or transferred install therefore starts **signed out**, the `ThisDeviceOnly` equivalent (iOS Keychain items are device-only while `UserDefaults` such as the remembered identifier, appearance and read-aloud voice are in device backups). A Keystore key cannot be restored anyway, so a restored blob would be undecryptable. If decryption ever fails, treat it as signed out and delete the file, never crash.
- The **Wear OS app** stores its companion session the same way (its own Keystore key and Tink keyset on the watch), excluded from backup, with the same undecryptable → signed-out rule.
- `EncryptedSharedPreferences` (androidx.security-crypto) is **not** used (deprecated).
- The Play Integrity provider needs no storage. iOS's separate App Attest keychain item has no Android counterpart.
- Never log a token: presence, expiry and error types only (gradus-ios `authLog`). Release builds strip debug logging (R8 `-assumenosideeffects` on the debug logger).

**Restore and refresh.** `restore()` reads the stored session **locally only**: an expired token with no network must not sign the user out. `accessToken()` returns the current token, refreshing if expired, and on refresh failure falls back to the stored token (gradus-ios `SupabaseSessionManager.accessToken`). **Refreshes are single-flight:** Supabase refresh tokens are single-use (gradus-ios `CompanionSession.swift`), and Android has more concurrent callers than iOS (WorkManager drain worker, the silent-push worker, the foreground drain, Realtime auth, storage uploads). `SessionManager.accessToken()` guards refresh with a `Mutex`: one refresh in flight, every other caller awaits its result and re-reads the stored session. Test: two concurrent callers with an expired token → exactly one `refresh_token` grant, both get the new token. The background worker additionally skips its pass when it cannot obtain a non-expired token (§6.5). The **only** automatic sign-out is a `401`/`unauthenticated` from `GET /me`: show "Please sign in again." as an error toast, then sign out (gradus-ios `AppModel.loadMe`).

**Signed-in entry sequence** (gradus-ios `AppModel.start`, `enterSignedIn`, `apply`). In order:

**Launch (`start`)**:

1. Start the Wear OS companion link (Data Layer listener, §6.15), the usage-analytics flush loop (§6.12), error reporting of error toasts (connectivity notices excluded), and the connectivity monitor with its back-online hook (drain, then refresh `/me`).
2. Client-policy check (§6.2). A forced update stops here.
3. `GET /meta/config` (best effort).
4. Restore the session (local only).
5. **Signed in:** lock if the biometric lock is on; tell the watch the phone is signed in (`phoneDidSignIn`: a watch with its app open and no session gets a companion session, best effort, §6.15); run **enter signed-in** (below).
6. **Signed out:** show Sign in. A pending route that does not require a session (a Live Board link that arrived during launch, `AppRoute.requiresSession == false`) opens now.
7. After the shell has settled, in the background and never blocking launch: the **Play age-signal check** (§6.13; the Android counterpart of iOS `ageSignals.refreshOnLaunch()`, which asks Apple's Declared Age Range), **then** the significant-change check (`significantChanges.run()`, §6.13).

**After a sign-in (`handle(session)`)**: adopt the session (`session_not_stored` if it cannot be read back); stamp the pending sign-up with the user id (`PendingSignUp.stamp`, key `gradus.onboarding.pendingSignUp`); `phoneDidSignIn` (best effort); **enter signed-in**.

**Enter signed-in (`enterSignedIn`)**, in order: create the per-user outbox/`SyncEngine` (§6.5); create the per-user `ActiveSessionStore` (`active-session.json`) if none; clear any `/me` load error; if `me.json` is cached, **apply** it and resolve the onboarding gate at once; `GET /me` (initial load), save it to `me.json`, **apply**, resolve the onboarding gate; drain the outbox; register the FCM token if one is known (`POST /devices`; notification permission is never asked here); **begin Live Board reporting** (below); refresh unread and subscribe to the unfiltered Realtime channel.

**Apply `/me` (`apply`)**, on every successful `/me` (cached or fresh):

1. When `/me` shows a different user or role than the models were built for, drop every session-scoped model (gradus-ios `dropSessionModels`).
2. Set the signed-in phase; align guardian stores to the role.
3. Tab selection: when the role changed or the current tab is not available for it, select the role's home tab, **except** when the previous role was none, a Live Board was open (the signed-out Live cover had a path) and the role has the Live tab: then close the cover and select Live, keeping the board on screen (the web's "return to board").
4. Open the pending route, if any.
5. `GET /me/celebrations` (`refreshCelebrations`, only with a session and an outbox).
6. Coach only: send an unsent pre-account sport request (`gradus.onboarding.unsentSportRequest`, `UnsentSportRequest`; cleared once sent or refused for good; one at a time).
7. iOS athlete only: the `AppTransactionReporter` (`POST /me/app-transaction`, weekly). **Android has no counterpart and makes no call** (Appendix A; §6.13 owns the Play age-signal equivalent).

**`/me` failures (`loadMe`)**: `401`/`unauthenticated` → toast "Please sign in again." and sign out (above). Cancelled → silent. Anything else: with nothing cached, render a **placeholder summary** (the user id, role none, onboarding unknown, terms treated as accepted) with the error message and a **Retry** action (`retryLoadMe`, an initial load); with a cache, keep it and toast only on non-initial loads.

**Live Board reporting begin/end** (Android meaning of iOS `deps.activities.beginTokenReporting()` / `endTokenReporting()`, which upload ActivityKit tokens). Android has no such tokens. **Begin** = start the app-driven Live Board notification planner for followed skaters (§6.9) and accept server `board_activity` FCM data messages (S-13). **End** = stop the planner; posted `live_board` notifications are **not** cancelled (iOS `endTokenReporting` only unregisters tokens and leaves running activities; §6.9.6 "Sign-out"), and once the device token is deleted the server sends no more. Neither makes a network call.

**Terms gate** (iOS §6.4 "Terms"; gradus-ios `TermsSheet`). When `/me.terms.accepted` is false and a role exists, a blocking full-screen sheet (no swipe or back dismissal; predictive back is disabled on it) shows:

- Eyebrow "Updated {version as a long date, e.g. June 29, 2026}"
- Title "Our terms have changed"
- Body "Please review and accept the updated Terms of Service and Privacy Policy to keep using Gradus."
- Rows "Terms of Service" (`https://gradus.training/terms`) and "Privacy Policy" (`https://gradus.training/privacy`), opened in the default browser (§7.12 Legal; iOS opens Safari)
- Checkbox "I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy"
- Primary button "Accept and continue" (enabled only when checked) → `POST /me/terms/accept`
- Secondary "Sign out instead"

`deferred` answers mean no role exists yet; the sheet is never shown to a role-less session (iOS §6.4, 2026-10-02 amendment). If `POST /me/terms/accept` nevertheless answers `deferred: true`, the client raises `terms_deferred` and shows "Finish setting up your profile on gradus.training, then accept the terms here." (`LiveMeRepository.acceptTerms`).

- **Precedence:** the Terms gate is suppressed while the significant-change flow (§6.13) is blocking: `termsNeeded = !significantChanges.isBlocking && role != null && !terms.accepted` (gradus-ios `AppModel.termsNeeded`).
- **On accept:** replace `me.terms` with the returned terms, save `me.json`, and play the success haptic (`HapticFeedbackConstants.CONFIRM` on API 30+, `CONTEXT_CLICK` on API 29, §8.5; iOS `Haptics.success()`).

**Biometric lock** (iOS §6.4 "Session and device security"; gradus-ios `BiometricGate`, `LockScreenView`, `LockWindow`). A **local convenience lock, not an auth mechanism.**

- Opt-in per device. Preference key `gradus.security.biometricLock` in DataStore.
- Locks at launch when a session exists, and on return to the foreground after **≥ 30 s** in the background. Each background trip counts once; the app's own prompt closing does not relock it.
- Unlock uses `androidx.biometric.BiometricPrompt` with the authenticators fixed in §6.11.4 (`BIOMETRIC_STRONG or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` on API 30+, `BIOMETRIC_WEAK or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` on API 29, where the strong combination is unsupported; one `LockAuthenticators.forSdk` shared with the availability check); both fall back to PIN/pattern/password, like `.deviceOwnerAuthentication`. Prompt title "Unlock Gradus". **No negative button:** androidx throws `IllegalArgumentException` if `setNegativeButtonText` is set while `DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` is allowed, so the system's own cancel is used. iOS's `localizedCancelTitle = "Not now"` has no Android equivalent and is dropped. User, app and system cancels clear the error; other errors show their message under the title.
- **Auto-prompt:** the prompt opens once by itself when the lock appears (iOS `LockScreenView .task { await gate.unlock() }`); "Unlock" reopens it. Re-entrant unlock calls while a prompt is up are ignored (`isEvaluating` guard).
- **Turning the setting off unlocks immediately** (`BiometricGate.isEnabled` setter clears `isLocked`).
- Lock screen copy: "Gradus is locked", button "Unlock", text button "Sign out". Icon: face or fingerprint per the device's enrolled biometric (from `BiometricManager`/`PackageManager.FEATURE_FACE` vs `FEATURE_FINGERPRINT`; iOS `faceid`/`touchid` by `biometryType`), a generic lock icon when only a device credential exists.
- **Android-native equivalent of the lock window** (iOS `LockWindow`, a window above the app's window): a `LockActivity` (the one design; §6.6.7 and §6.11.4 fix its manifest attributes and tests, and §7.1.0, §8.5 and Appendix G follow it) **without** `noHistory`, `launchMode="singleTop"`, the app's own `taskAffinity`, `excludeFromRecents="false"`, finished **only** by a successful unlock or sign-out. (`noHistory` would finish the lock as soon as the user leaves it, so Home then reopen would show the unlocked app.) Either way it covers every dialog, bottom sheet and alert underneath, hides that content from TalkBack (`importantForAccessibility = noHideDescendants`), and takes focus so the keyboard goes down. Drafts and open sheets stay as they were and are there again after unlock. Back from the lock moves the task to the background, never into the app.
- Sign-out resets the preference to off, so the next account starts unlocked.
- **Tests:** Home while locked, reopen → still locked; the prompt auto-opens once; a second unlock call during a prompt is ignored; toggling the setting off while locked unlocks; no `IllegalArgumentException` building the prompt on API 29 and 35.
- Device availability: `BiometricManager.canAuthenticate(LockAuthenticators.forSdk(...))`, the same set as the prompt (§6.11.4). Settings → Device shows the toggle (§7.12).

**Recovery and email-change links** (gradus-ios `RecoveryLink.swift`, `ResetPasswordModel`, `AppModel.open(url:)`). Reset and email-change emails link to `https://gradus.training/auth/confirm?token_hash=…&type=recovery|email_change`. Android claims that path as a verified **App Link** (§6.10; assetlinks S-10). The app parses it as `EmailLinkConfirmation`: only `https`, host `gradus.training`, path `auth/confirm`, a non-empty `token_hash`, and `type` ∈ {`recovery`, `email_change`}. Anything else is not ours.

- **Recovery** (gradus-ios `presentRecovery`). First dismiss any Live Board presentation (the reset screen presents from the root). If a reset is already pending, or no account is signed in, just replace the pending credential. Otherwise remember the signed-in user and unregister this device's FCM token from it (`DELETE /devices/{token}`) **before** the reset screen appears, because the code may belong to another household member. Present the full-screen reset flow (iOS copy, verbatim):
  - "Verifying your reset link…"
  - expired: "This reset link has expired" / "Ask for a new one and we'll send a fresh link to your email." / "Request a new link"
  - offline (the code never reached the server, so it is still unspent): "You're offline" / "Connect and try again. Your reset link still works." / "Try again" / "Not now"
  - form: title "New password", "Choose a new password for your account.", fields "New password" (placeholder "At least 8 characters") and "Confirm new password" ("Type it again"), button "Set new password", hints "Use at least 8 characters." / "The passwords don't match."
  - done: "Password updated" / "Sign in with your new password."

  The code is exchanged with `verifyEmailOtp(type = RECOVERY, tokenHash)`. A response without a session is treated as expired. Saving runs `updateUser(password)`, signs the recovery session out locally, toasts "Password updated", then runs the full sign-out (below) and also wipes the store of the account that was signed in before the link. An expired link puts the previous account's push registration back.
- **Email change.** `verifyEmailOtp(type = EMAIL_CHANGE, tokenHash)`:
  - a session comes back: toast "Your email is updated."; then, if it belongs to another account than the one on screen, switch accounts (below); if the phone was **signed out** (no previous user, signed-out phase), `phoneDidSignIn` and run **enter signed-in** for that user; if it is the same account, refresh `/me` (gradus-ios `confirmEmailChange`);
  - no session (the first half of a two-address change; iOS sees a decode error here): toast "Confirmed. If we also emailed your other address, open that link too." and refresh `/me`;
  - offline (both `offline` and `unreachable` count, gradus-ios `AppModel.isOffline`; also used for the recovery flow's offline state): "You're offline. Open the link again once you're connected.";
  - anything else: "That link has expired or was already used. Change your email again in Settings › Account."
- The older fragment form `gradus://reset-password#access_token=…&refresh_token=…&type=recovery` is still **parsed** for parity (A27, §6.10.3 item 1, iOS `RecoveryLink`), but no server email generates it: `/auth/recover` is never called with `client: "app"`, and `gradus://reset-password` stays off the Supabase redirect allow-list (§6.11.5).

**Sign out** (gradus-ios `AppModel.signOut`, `SettingsView`). Settings → "Sign out" asks "Sign out of Gradus?" with buttons "Sign out" (destructive) and "Cancel". The message is "{n} change(s) still waiting to send will be discarded." when the outbox has pending or in-flight rows, else "Your data stays safely on the server." **[code wins]** iOS QA.md says a sign-out while offline is refused; the code warns and allows it. Then, in order:

1. Tell the Wear OS app to end its session (§6.15; a queued Data Layer message with no secret in it). Skipped when the sign-out came from the watch (trigger 2).
2. `DELETE /devices/{token}` (best effort; the FCM token is URL-path-encoded because it contains `:`; 200 and 404 both count as success, gradus-ios `LiveDeviceTokenUploader.unregister`).
3. **End Live Board reporting** (defined under the entry sequence: stop the planner; notifications stay; no network call).
4. Flush, then clear, the usage-analytics buffer (§6.12).
5. supabase-kt `signOut(LOCAL)`: local scope only, because a global revoke would sign the user out of the web.
6. Wipe the outbox, drop the `SyncEngine` and `ActiveSessionStore`, delete the per-user directory (§6.5).
7. **If the lock is up** and no password-reset flow is pending: dismiss every dialog, bottom sheet and alert **without animation**, still under the lock, so nothing animates out over the fading lock. A pending reset flow stays: it outlives the sign-out.
8. Reset the biometric preference (off, unlocked); cancel the unread listener and clear unread; drop every session model; clear pending feedback, wrap-up and briefing requests; close the Live Board presentation; clear navigation back stacks, the sign-up path, plan-setup and onboarding-gate state and any pending link route; clear the pending sign-up (`gradus.onboarding.pendingSignUp`); clear the `/me` load error.
9. Select the Sign in tab; land on Sign in.

**Trigger 2: sign-out from the Wear OS app** (gradus-ios `AppModel.signOutForWatch`; `WatchRootView` alert "Sign out of Gradus?" / "This also signs you out on your iPhone.", which Android words "This also signs you out on your phone."). The watch sends a Data Layer message. The phone, which may have been cold-started by that message, calls `restore()` first (idempotent) so the stored session is read and the sign-out is not lost; if no one is signed in it stops. Otherwise it runs steps 2–9 without telling the watch again.

Device registration (gradus-ios `registerDeviceTokenIfPossible`): `POST /devices` runs only when signed in and a token is known; any failure is logged in debug builds only, never surfaced, and retried on the next launch or token change (`onNewToken`).

The device-wide board follows and history survive (§6.5).

**Account switch through an email link** (gradus-ios `switchAccount`). The same teardown for the previous user (tell the watch the previous user signed out, end Live Board reporting, wipe the outbox and per-user store, clear unread, drop session models, clear feedback/wrap-up/briefing requests and back stacks), except that the session is not signed out and no device token is unregistered (storage already holds the new session; registering for the new account moves the token, the upload is keyed by token), and the analytics buffer is **cleared without flushing**, so events never go out under the wrong account. Then `phoneDidSignIn` and **enter signed-in** for the new user.

**Delete account** (iOS §6.4, §6.11; gradus-ios `DeleteAccountFlow`, `AccountModel.deleteAccount`). Online-only. `GET /me/deletion-impact`, then `DELETE /me {confirmPhrase: "DELETE ACCOUNT", minorChoices[]}` (the typed phrase is checked client-side first: "Type DELETE ACCOUNT to confirm."). Offline: "You're offline. Deleting your account needs a connection." Success: toast "Your account has been deleted." and the sign-out teardown. The UI and copy are specified in §7.12. Server-side Apple revocation already runs for every linked Apple identity (`revokeAppleIdentitiesForUser`). **Server addition S-8:** revoke with `client_id = auth_identities.apple_client_id ?? "training.gradus.app"`, because a refresh token obtained through the Services ID can only be revoked with that client ID. Google needs no revocation.

**Account switching / multiple accounts.** None in 1.0. The local store is keyed by user id, and sign-out wipes it (iOS §6.4).

**Configuration the Android build needs** (Mariah's console steps are listed in §10 and Appendix D):

| Item | Where | Blocked by A8? |
|---|---|---|
| Google Cloud OAuth consent screen (external, scopes `openid email profile`) and a **Web** OAuth client. Its ID becomes `BuildConfig.GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID` and the Lovable secret `GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID` | Google Cloud Console, in a Gradus-owned project (not Lovable's managed Google provider) | No |
| **Android** OAuth clients for package `training.gradus.app`, one per signing certificate SHA-1: the debug keystore (each dev Mac), the upload key, and the **Play App Signing key** | Google Cloud Console; their client IDs, comma-separated, become the Lovable secret `GOOGLE_ANDROID_CLIENT_IDS` (S-5 `azp` check) | The Play App Signing SHA-1 only exists after the Play Console app is created. Debug and upload-signed builds work before that. |
| Apple **Services ID** (for example `training.gradus.app.signin`) with Sign in with Apple enabled, grouped with the primary App ID `training.gradus.app`, domain `gradus.training`, return URL `https://gradus.training/api/public/auth/apple/callback`. Lovable secrets `APPLE_SIWA_SERVICES_ID` (the existing `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, `APPLE_SIWA_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_SIWA_KEY_P8` sign the client secret (verify that the existing key is usable for the Services ID)) | Apple Developer → Identifiers | No |
| Firebase project for FCM (no Analytics or Crashlytics SDKs), `google-services.json` in the app module, FCM service-account secret for the Worker | Firebase console | No (A8) |
| Play Integrity: Cloud project number in `BuildConfig`, the Play Console ↔ Cloud project link, a service account for `decodeIntegrityToken` | Play Console + Google Cloud | Yes |

**Tests.** Port of the iOS sign-in, reset and terms model tests. Session adopt fails with `session_not_stored` when the fake storage drops writes. Restore offline with an expired token stays signed in. A `/me` 401 signs out with the toast. Apple web flow: a state mismatch shows the unavailable copy, a cancelled tab is silent, the exchange is called with the verifier, an offline exchange shows "You're offline. Check your connection and try again.", both the App Link and the custom-scheme return are accepted, a replayed or expired handoff is refused (server). Google: a token with the Web `aud` and a wrong `azp` → `401 invalid_identity_token` (server). Sign-in model: Remember me starts off on a fresh install and on when an identifier is stored; the identifier is persisted after an Apple or Google success too. Integrity canonical body matches Node `JSON.stringify` vectors including U+0008, U+000C and a lone surrogate. Watch-initiated sign-out on a cold phone restores first, then signs out without messaging the watch. The Google button is hidden when the client ID is empty. Sign-out runs its steps in order (fakes record calls). An email-change link with no session yields the "Confirmed…" toast. The biometric lock relocks after 30 s and not after 29 s. The integrity interceptor adds nothing on non-password operations and returns within the deadline when the provider hangs.

### 6.5 Offline and sync

**Principle** (iOS §6.5, decision #9). Screens render from a local cache and treat the network as a way to refresh it and to drain a queue of pending writes. A user never sees a spinner for something already loaded, and never loses a session log or a message to a dead rink signal.

**[code wins] What iOS actually stores.** iOS §6.5 describes SwiftData models for every entity, each with a `syncState`. gradus-ios HEAD does something simpler:

- **SwiftData holds only the outbox** (`PendingMutation`, `StoreContainer.schema`) and the device-wide Live Board follow store (`BoardLocalStore`).
- Each feature caches its last API response as a **per-user JSON snapshot file** with its ETag and `fetchedAt`.
- Optimistic edits patch the in-memory model and the snapshot.

Android mirrors HEAD. **Room** is used where iOS uses SwiftData. JSON snapshot files (kotlinx.serialization, written atomically with `AtomicFile`) are used where iOS writes JSON.

**Layout on disk.**

| iOS (Application Support, `completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication`) | Android (`noBackupFilesDir`, credential-encrypted storage) | Scope | Wiped at sign-out |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Gradus/<userId>/store.sqlite`: SwiftData `PendingMutation` | `Gradus/<userId>/store.db`: Room `GradusUserDatabase` with entity `pending_mutation` | Per user | Yes (whole directory) |
| `Gradus/<userId>/me.json` (`MeCache`) | `Gradus/<userId>/me.json` | Per user | Yes |
| `roster.json` (`RosterCache`: roster, etag, practice summaries, fetchedAt) | `roster.json` | Per user | Yes |
| `plans.json` (`PlansCache`: lists per filter key with etag and fetchedAt, move library and etag, plan details by id, parent plans and etag, athlete plans and etag) | `plans.json` | Per user | Yes |
| `parent-settings.json`, `athlete-settings.json` (`SettingsRepositories`) | same names | Per user | Yes |
| `resources.json` (`ResourcesCache`) | `resources.json` | Per user | Yes |
| `team-guardians.json` (`TeamGuardiansCache`) | `team-guardians.json` | Per user | Yes |
| `coach-visibility-parent.json`, `coach-visibility-mine.json` (`CoachVisibilityCache`) | same names | Per user | Yes |
| `celebration-dismissals.json` (`CelebrationDismissalStore`) | `celebration-dismissals.json` | Per user | Yes |
| `active-session.json` (`ActiveSessionStore`: the one running practice session) | `active-session.json` | Per user | Yes |
| `Gradus/board/board.sqlite`: SwiftData `BoardFollowRecord`, `BoardMuteRecord`, `BoardVisitRecord` (history ≤ 20) | `Gradus/board/board.db`: Room `BoardDatabase` with entities `board_follow (id = "<slug>\|<key>", slug, name, key, createdAt)`, `board_mute (id, slug, key, createdAt)`, `board_visit (slug PK, name, visitedAt)` | **Device-wide** (a signed-out viewer's follows survive sign-in and sign-out, like the web's localStorage) | No |
| `usage-analytics.json` (≤ 1,000 events, ≤ 7 days, batches of 100) | `usage-analytics.json` | Device-wide; flushed then cleared at sign-out (§6.12) | Cleared |
