| `UserDefaults` keys (full list below) | DataStore Preferences `gradus_device_prefs`, same key names | Device-wide | See the preference table |

**Device-wide preferences** (every `UserDefaults` key in gradus-ios at `91c6af2`). Android stores each in the DataStore file `gradus_device_prefs` under the **same key name**. "Backed up" defines the §6.11 backup allow-list: iOS `UserDefaults` are in device backups, so Android backs up the same non-sensitive keys; per-account transient state is excluded because a restored install starts signed out.

| Key (iOS source) | Content | Backed up (§6.11) | Sign-out |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gradus.auth.rememberedIdentifier` (`SignInModel`) | Trimmed sign-in identifier when "Remember me" is on | Yes | Kept |
| `gradus.security.biometricLock` (`BiometricGate`) | Lock on/off | No (a restored install is signed out, so off is correct) | **Reset to off** |
| `gradus.appearance` (`AppearancePreference.storageKey`) | System / light / dark | Yes | Kept |
| `narration.voiceIdentifier` (`NarrationVoice`) | Read-aloud voice; on Android a `TextToSpeech` voice name (§6.7) | Yes | Kept |
| `gradus.sampleAthleteDismissed` | Coach dismissed the sample athlete | Yes | Kept |
| `gradus.coachVisibilitySeen` | Coach-visibility banner seen | Yes | Kept |
| `gradus.onboarding.pendingSignUp` (`PendingSignUp`) | Sign-up stash before the account exists; stamped with the user id after sign-in | No | **Cleared** |
| `gradus.onboarding.unsentSportRequest` (`UnsentSportRequest`) | A pre-account sport request whose first send failed, keyed by user | No | Kept (cleared once sent or refused) |
| `gradus.significantChanges.handled`, `gradus.significantChanges.firstVersion`, `gradus.significantChanges.ageRating` (`SignificantChangeLedger`) | Significant-change ledger (§6.13) | Yes | Kept |
| `gradus.appTransaction.reported.<userId>` (`AppTransactionReporter`) | Weekly AppTransaction report marker | **iOS only; no Android key** | n/a |
| App Group `GoalWidgetStore` keys (account, practice snapshot, coach snapshot, `coachTodayPage`) | Practice goals and Today widget snapshots (#55) | Android: DataStore `widget_snapshots` (§6.9.7), not backed up | **Cleared** |
| `gradus.watch.lastPhoneContact` (`UserDefaultsLeaseStore`, **on the watch**) | Watch lease timestamp | Wear OS app's own DataStore, not backed up | Per §6.15 |

**Messages are not cached on disk at HEAD.** gradus-ios keeps rooms and thread pages in memory only (`RoomSession`; no messages cache exists). iOS §6.5 says "newest 200 messages per room". Android matches HEAD; adding a disk cache is §12 N22. Queued outgoing messages **are** on disk (the outbox) and are shown in the thread.

**The outbox: Room entity `pending_mutation`** (field-for-field from gradus-ios `PendingMutation`):

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID text, PK | |
| `createdAt` | epoch ms | Queue order |
| `method` | text | `POST` / `PUT` / `PATCH` / `DELETE` |
| `path` | text | Absolute API path including `/api/v1`, optionally with a query (for example `/api/v1/plans/{id}/moves/{moveId}?reason=landed_it`). The query is encoded once, defensively, so a bad query can never crash a replay (`LiveMutationTransport.url`) |
| `body` | blob, nullable | JSON. Object keys are emitted in **sorted order** (iOS encodes `.sortedKeys`) so a hash of a body is stable |
| `idempotencyKey` | text | Assigned at creation and reused for every retry |
| `attempts` | int | |
| `nextAttemptAt` | epoch ms | |
| `state` | text | `pending`, `inFlight`, `failed`, `conflicted` |
| `lastErrorCode`, `lastErrorMessage` | text, nullable | |
| `entityKind`, `entityID`, `entityLabel` | text, nullable | For per-screen counts and thread rows, for example `lessonSlot`, `wrapUp`, `plan`, `move`, `session`, `message`, `settings`, `resource`, `boardFollows`; the label is user copy such as "Wrap-up for {athlete}" or "Delete {plan title}" |

All outbox access goes through one `OutboxStore` (Room DAO with `suspend` functions): `enqueue`, `all()` (oldest first), `due(now)` (pending rows with `nextAttemptAt ≤ now`, oldest first), `markInFlight` (increments `attempts`), `complete` (delete), `scheduleRetry`, `park(state)`, `reset` (back to pending, now), `discard`, `wipe`. In-flight rows found at process start are reset to `pending`. Android addition: a killed process must not strand rows; iOS has no equivalent step.

**Write path: online first, outbox fallback** (gradus-ios `RosterModel.perform`/`queue`, the same pattern in Plans, Resources, Settings, Guardians, Goals, Sessions, Messages):

1. Generate an idempotency key.
2. If `ConnectivityMonitor.isOnline` is false, **enqueue** at once with that key.
3. Otherwise send live with the key. On success, apply the server's answer.
4. On a **transport error (status 0) or a 5xx**, enqueue **with the same key**, so if the server did receive the first attempt it replays instead of duplicating.
5. On any other error, show its `userMessage` as an error toast and roll back the optimistic change.
6. A queued write keeps the optimistic change on screen, toasts "Saved — it syncs when you're back online." (messages: "Saved — it will send when you're back online."), and drops the screen's stored ETag.
7. If enqueue itself fails: "Couldn't save the change." (messages: "Couldn't save the message."). With no outbox available: "You're offline. Try again when you're back online."

**Online-only writes (never queued)** (gradus-ios `InvoicingModel` header comment, `handoff-I12-onward.md` "Money-critical writes are online-only"; and each model's `isOnline` pre-check). Offline, these refuse up front with a clear message:

- invoicing: rate, create, status, delete;
- Founding Coach claim and restore;
- account deletion; email and password change; password reset;
- every sign-in, sign-up, invite, claim and guardian-claim flow;
- KWS verification;
- voice notes, voice transcription and voice plan build (**[code wins]** `RoomSession.sendVoiceNote` refuses voice notes offline although iOS §6.5 says they queue);
- schedule import;
- Ask Gradus.

**Drainer** (gradus-ios `SyncEngine`). A process-wide singleton per signed-in user.

- **Single-flight:** a `drain()` call made while a pass is running returns the **last completed report immediately**; it does not wait for or join the running pass (gradus-ios `if isDraining { return lastReport }`). Guard with a `Mutex`-protected `isDraining` flag.
- Each pass re-queries `due(now)` and sends the rows oldest first, repeating until `due` comes back empty, so rows that became due during the pass are sent in the same pass. Each row goes through `MutationTransport` (§6.2): a plain OkHttp call with `X-Gradus-Client`, bearer, the row's `Idempotency-Key`, `Accept: application/json` always and `Content-Type: application/json` only when the row has a body (`LiveMutationTransport.send`).
- **Ordering rule:** a retryable failure **stops the pass**, so later writes never overtake the one that failed. Parked rows are skipped, so one bad write cannot block the queue.
- After a pass, schedule the next pass at the earliest future `nextAttemptAt`.

Response handling, exactly as gradus-ios `SyncEngine.send` / `retryOrGiveUp` and `OutboundResponse.retryAfterSeconds`. `attempt` = the row's `attempts + 1`. "Envelope" = the server's `{"error":{code,message}}` if the body decodes.

| Response | Action | Stored `lastErrorCode` | Stored `lastErrorMessage` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2xx | `complete` (delete row) | | |
| 409, 422 | `park` as **conflicted** | envelope code, else `conflict` | envelope message, else none |
| 429 | retry or give up (below) | envelope code, else `rate_limited` | envelope message |
| other 4xx (**including 401**) | `park` as **failed** (iOS behaviour; the Android background worker avoids stale-token 401s, see "When the drainer runs") | envelope code, else `http_<status>` | envelope message, else none |
| 5xx (including 503 `api_disabled`) | retry or give up | envelope code, else `http_<status>` | envelope message |
| transport error (no response) | retry or give up | `transport` | the exception's description (`ApiError.offline/unreachable` message) |

**Retry or give up:** if `attempt ≥ 12`, park as **failed** with code `gave_up` and message = the last server/transport message if there is one, otherwise "Gave up after {attempt} attempts ({code})." Otherwise schedule the next attempt at now + **the HTTP `Retry-After` header in seconds** (read for 429 **and** 5xx; numeric seconds only; the envelope's `details.retryAfterSeconds` is **not** used by the outbox) or, with no header, the backoff delay.

**Backoff** (`BackoffPolicy.default`): `min(300 s, 2 s × 2^(attempt−1)) × uniform(0.75 … 1.25)`, max 12 attempts. The random source is injectable for tests.

**When the drainer runs.**

| Trigger | iOS (HEAD) | Android |
|---|---|---|
| Signed-in entry, after `/me` | `enterSignedIn` | Same |
| App to foreground | `scenePhaseChanged(.active)`: drain, then refresh `/me` and unread | `ProcessLifecycleOwner` `ON_START`: same three calls |
| Connectivity regained | `ConnectivityMonitor.onBackOnline`: drain + refresh `/me` | `ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback` reports a default network with `NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET` after none (no `VALIDATED` gate, §7.13.4): same |
| Next retry time | `scheduleNextDrainIfNeeded` timer | Same, a coroutine `delay` in the app scope |
| Silent push | `didReceiveRemoteNotification`: drain + refresh `/me` | FCM **normal-priority data** message with no visible notification (§6.6.8, S-3): `onMessageReceived` enqueues the unique, **non-expedited** `silent-push-sync` `OneTimeWorkRequest` (`KEEP`, `NetworkType.CONNECTED`) that drains through the same singleton `SyncEngine` and refreshes `/me`; in the foreground the two calls run directly |
| App closed with rows still pending | Not handled. iOS declares the `BGTaskScheduler` identifier `training.gradus.app.sync` in `Info.plist` but never registers a task (no `BGTaskScheduler` call in gradus-ios) | **WorkManager** unique work `gradus-outbox-drain`, `OneTimeWorkRequest` with `NetworkType.CONNECTED`, enqueued whenever a row is enqueued or scheduled for retry and whenever the app goes to the background with pending rows. Rules below. This is the Android-native form of the iOS PRD §6.5 "drains … in a `BGAppRefreshTask`" intent and changes no foreground behaviour. The worker calls the same singleton `SyncEngine` (Hilt `@HiltWorker`), so it never races the foreground drain. No periodic work is scheduled. |

**Background drain worker rules** (Android-only; each has a test):

1. **Policy `APPEND_OR_REPLACE`**, not `KEEP`: `KEEP` silently drops a request made while the worker is running, so a retry scheduled during a background pass would be lost. When the worker's pass ends with due-later rows still pending, it enqueues a follow-up with `setInitialDelay(earliest nextAttemptAt − now)` (or returns `Result.retry()` when the pass stopped on a retryable failure with no later `nextAttemptAt`).
2. **No expedited work:** neither the drain worker nor the silent-push worker is expedited, so no worker runs as a foreground service on API 29–30, no `getForegroundInfo()` notification or extra channel is needed, and no `dataSync` foreground-service type is declared (the phone runs no foreground service, §4.2).
3. **No stale-token 401s:** before a background pass the worker calls `SessionManager.accessToken()` and checks the result is unexpired. If refresh failed and only an expired token is available (iOS falls back to it, `SupabaseSessionManager.accessToken`), the worker skips the pass and returns `Result.retry()`, so a 401 caused by a stale token never parks rows as `failed` (which would be invisible outside messaging, since HEAD has no Sync Center). Foreground drains are unchanged (iOS behaviour). With no session at all, the worker does nothing and returns success.

**Connectivity** (gradus-ios `ConnectivityMonitor`): `isOnline = pathIsOnline && !simulateOffline`; `isExpensive` = metered network. Debug builds have Settings → Debug → "Simulate offline" (iOS §9.5).

**Conflict policy** (iOS §6.5, as built):

- Append-only writes (messages, sessions, reports, feedback, wrap-ups) cannot conflict; idempotency makes their retries safe.
- Scalar edits are last-writer-wins by server time. After a successful write the screen reloads or takes the server's returned record.
- Structural rejections (409/422: reorder conflicts, `roster_full`, and a queued activation replayed against a server not yet published with #52, which still answers 409 `bench_choice_required`) park as **conflicted**. A queued `replaceId` that is no longer one of the athlete's active plans benches nothing, and the activation still goes through (web #223).

**[code wins] Where pending and failed writes surface.** iOS §6.5 specifies a Sync Center (Settings → "Pending changes", retry and discard, a Settings badge when anything has failed). gradus-ios HEAD has **no such screen**: `AppRoute.SettingsSection` has no `pendingChanges` case, and `SettingsView` has no row, even though `gradus-ios/docs/README.md` still lists one. What HEAD ships, and Android copies:

- **Per-screen "{n} to sync" chips** (sync icon + text), counting this screen's pending or in-flight rows by path prefix: Roster, Plans list, Resources, Settings → My athletes and each athlete's detail, Team plan guardians, Coach visibility.
- **In the message thread**, queued and failed sends appear inline, oldest first: queued rows marked queued, failed or conflicted rows showing `lastErrorMessage` or "Couldn't send.", each with **Retry** (`reset` then drain) and **Delete** (`discard`). When the outbox shrinks, the thread refetches.
- The **sign-out warning** counts pending and in-flight rows (above).
- Failed or conflicted rows outside messaging are kept but not listed anywhere. The engine still exposes `retry`, `retryAll`, `discard` and `discardAllNeedingAttention`, so a Pending changes screen can be added without engine work. Whether to add one to both apps is §12 N21.

**Refresh policy as built** (iOS §6.5 table, corrected to HEAD):

| Data | When fetched | Stale tolerance in code |
|---|---|---|
| `/me` | Launch (cache first), foreground, back online, silent push | Cache used without age limit while offline |
| Roster + practice summaries | Tab open (cache first, then network with `If-None-Match`). On foreground only if `fetchedAt` is ≥ 4 h old. Wrap-ups refresh on every foreground | 4 h foreground threshold |
| Parent and athlete settings | Open, then foreground if ≥ 4 h old | 4 h |
| Coach visibility (mine) | Open, then foreground if ≥ 15 min old | 15 min |
| Plans lists, details, move library, parent and athlete plan lists | Tab or plan open, with ETag | Cache used offline |
| Resources list; downloaded files | Tab open; files kept in cache | Cache used offline |
| Rooms, messages, unread | Open plus Realtime; unread on foreground | In memory only |
| Live Board | Every 30 s while visible; "Updated Xs ago"; stale after 180 s ("Not updated for {age}") | `BoardDependencies.staleAfter = 180` |

**What works offline** (iOS §6.5, adjusted to HEAD):

| Works fully | Works with queueing | Needs a connection |
|---|---|---|
| Roster, week schedule, athlete details already loaded; plans, moves, plan detail; the session timer end to end (persisted per user in `active-session.json`, start timestamp plus pause intervals, so it is correct after a kill); cached resources and downloaded files; Live Board follows and history | Lesson slots (create, edit, delete, cancel or reschedule an occurrence, clear an override); wrap-ups; plan fields, moves add/reorder/remove (with the optional "why" `reason`), activate/bench, delete; move archive; session submit; text messages; parent and athlete settings, goals, motivation; team guardian invites; coach-visibility answers; celebration acks; guardian email; resource delete; saved answers (while Ask is hidden by the release flag the queue path is unreachable); board follows (`PUT /boards/{slug}/follows`); feedback | Sign in and sign up, invites and claims, billing and invoicing, account deletion, password and email changes, voice notes (**[code wins]** `RoomSession.sendVoiceNote`; iOS §6.5 said queued), voice transcription and plan build (minors never: decision #48), schedule import, AI summaries and briefings refresh, AI move drafts and New move's "Save to library & add" (#53), Ask Gradus, the Live Board itself, a new conversation with someone not already loaded, reading message history after relaunch |

**Encryption at rest.** The per-user directory sits in credential-encrypted storage under `noBackupFilesDir`. Room and the snapshots are **not** additionally encrypted (iOS uses file protection, not SQLCipher). Tokens are encrypted as in §6.4.

**Tests** (ports of the gradus-ios `SyncEngine`, `OutboxStore` and model tests):

- A 503 stops the pass, and a later row is not sent.
- 409 and 422 park as conflicted; 400 and 401 park as failed.
- 429 honours the `Retry-After` header; a 503 with `Retry-After: 30` schedules the next attempt at +30 s; an envelope `retryAfterSeconds` without the header falls back to backoff; backoff values are checked with pinned jitter; the 12th attempt parks as `gave_up` with the last server message, or "Gave up after 12 attempts (http_503)." when there was none.
- A 404 with no envelope parks as failed with code `http_404`; a 409 with no envelope parks as conflicted with code `conflict`; a thrown transport error schedules a retry with code `transport`.
- A `drain()` during a running pass returns the previous report at once; rows that become due during a pass are sent in the same pass.
- Replay sends the same `Idempotency-Key`; two concurrent drains send each row once.
- Rows left `inFlight` are pending again after a process restart.
- Offline write → chip "1 to sync" → back online → drained → chip gone.
- Sign-out with 2 pending shows "2 changes still waiting to send will be discarded."
- The WorkManager drain worker (`TestListenableWorkerBuilder`) drains with the network constraint met; a retry scheduled while the worker runs is not dropped (`APPEND_OR_REPLACE`); neither worker is built as expedited (Robolectric `@Config(sdk = [29, 30])` runs both without a foreground-info crash); with only an expired token and a failing refresh the worker returns `retry` and parks nothing.
- Snapshot files round-trip and are deleted by sign-out; `board.db` survives sign-out.

### 6.6 Realtime and push notifications

**Sources.** iOS §6.6; gradus-ios `Gradus/Shell/AppDelegate.swift`, `Gradus/Shell/AppModel.swift` (`deviceTokenDidChange`, `registerDeviceTokenIfPossible`, `refreshUnread`, `listenForUnread`, `signOut`, `presentRecovery`, `scenePhaseChanged`), `Packages/GradusCore/Sources/GradusCore/Push/PushPermission.swift`, `Packages/GradusAPI/Sources/GradusAPI/Realtime.swift`, `Packages/FeatureSettings/Sources/FeatureSettings/Account/DeviceView.swift`, `Packages/FeatureMessages/Sources/FeatureMessages/RoomView.swift`, `Packages/FeatureSessions/Sources/FeatureSessions/SessionActivityController.swift` (`LiveSessionReminders`), `RunnerPlanDetailModel.swift`; web `src/lib/push.server.ts`, `src/lib/push-notify.server.ts` and every `notifyUsers(` call site (listed in the trigger table below).

**Decision numbers in this group.** A1–A10 are Mariah's settled Android decisions. Every A-number from A11 up is a **proposed** decision listed in §0 Table 1 and in §12, awaiting Mariah; this group labels each one "proposed" and cites the iOS source it applies. Items this group raises for Mariah (both apps) are in §12: suppressing a message push for the open room (6.6.4, N25); clearing delivered notifications at sign-out (6.6.6, N26); athlete `connection` push landing (6.6.3, N27); "Still practicing?" tap route (6.6.7, N28); adding the route to toast error reports (6.11.8, N29); Recents thumbnail while locked (6.11.4, N30); the push unread count (6.6.9, N31); a shared routes vector file (6.10.2, N33); a global offline banner (7.13.4, N32); presence (7.13.1, N23).

#### 6.6.1 Realtime

Same design as iOS: **Realtime is a refinement over polling, not a dependency** (iOS §6.6; `Realtime.swift`). The stream only signals "something changed"; the caller refetches through API v1.

| Item | iOS (reference) | Android |
|---|---|---|
| Library | supabase-swift `RealtimeClientV2`, URL `<supabaseURL>/realtime/v1`, header `apikey: <publishable key>`, `accessToken` closure from the session | supabase-kt Realtime module only (§6.3), same URL, same `apikey` header, access token supplied from the session store on every (re)connect |
| Event | `postgres_changes`, `INSERT`, schema `public`, table `messages` (RLS scopes rows to room participants) | Same |
| One room | Channel topic `room:<id>`, filter `eq(room_id, <id>)` for athlete rooms, `eq(direct_room_id, <id>)` for direct rooms (the web's channel name) | Same topic and filters |
| Rooms list and unread badge | Unfiltered channel, topic `rooms:<random uuid lowercased>` | Same |
| Payload used | `id`, `room_id`, `direct_room_id`, `sender_user_id` → `MessageInsert`; `conversationID = roomID ?? directRoomID` | Same data class `MessageInsert`, same fallback |
| Connection lifetime | Client connects on first subscribe, disconnects when the last channel is removed (`removeChannel` on stream termination) | Same: a `callbackFlow` per subscription; `awaitClose { removeChannel }`; the client disconnects when no channel remains |
| Room screen | `RoomView` activates on appear and on return to active, deactivates on disappear and when the app leaves active | Room `ViewModel` subscribes while the room's `NavBackStackEntry` is at least `STARTED` **and** the process is started (`repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED)`); on every return to foreground it refetches the thread |
| Unread total | `listenForUnread()` from sign-in: every insert on the unfiltered stream calls `refreshUnread()` (`GET` unread total); also on sign-in, on every foreground, and when a room screen disappears | Same triggers. The unfiltered collection runs under `ProcessLifecycleOwner` `repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED)` so no socket is held in the background (the iOS process is suspended in the background, so this is the same behavior) |
| Failure | Channel drop is silent; the room refetches on foreground | Same. Never a toast or error for a Realtime failure |
| Sign-out / account switch | Unread task cancelled, `unreadTotal = 0` | Same |
| Tests | `ScriptedMessagesRealtime` test double | `FakeMessagesRealtime` that yields scripted inserts (JUnit + Turbine), plus a `NoopMessagesRealtime` for previews |

#### 6.6.2 Server sender for Android (FCM)

The APNs sender exists (`src/lib/apns.server.ts`, `notifyUsers` in `push-notify.server.ts`) and today selects `device_tokens` rows with `platform = 'ios'` only. Android needs the FCM HTTP v1 branch specified as server addition **S-3** (Appendix A; §6.2). This section fixes the **wire contract** the Android app depends on.

- `notifyUsers` resolves `ios` and `android` rows in one query, sends APNs to `ios` and FCM to `android` in parallel, keeps one `PushReport` (counts add up across platforms), and still never throws (iOS §4.1 rule 7, `inBackground`).
- **Dead tokens:** FCM `404 UNREGISTERED`, or `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` whose error detail names the registration token, deletes the row (the APNs `410 Unregistered` equivalent) (verify exact FCM error shapes at build time).
- **Every Android message is data-only** (proposed A40). The app builds every notification itself so that channel choice, grouping, collapse, lock-screen privacy and tap routing are identical whether the app is foreground, background, or killed. All FCM `data` values are strings:

| `data` key | Value | Source in `PushMessage` |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `message`, `plan_assigned`, `lesson_wrap_up`, `lesson_reminder`, `practice_nudge`, `connection`, `competition_recap`, `entitlement`, `consent_rescinded`, plus the Live Board types §6.9 defines | `type` |
| `route` | The same route string iOS gets in `gradus.route` (`rooms/<id>`, `plans/<id>`, …) | `route` |
| `v` | `"1"` | constant (iOS rejects any other version; so does Android) |
| `title` | Title, may be absent | `title` |
| `body` | Already truncated by `truncateBody` (one line, 160 chars with "…") | `body` |
| `threadId` | e.g. `room:<id>`, may be absent | `threadId` |
| `collapseId` | e.g. `plan:<id>`, may be absent | `collapseId` |
| `silent` | `"1"` for silent messages, absent otherwise | `silent` |
| `badge` | Recipient's unread total, only if §12 N31 is approved; absent in 1.0 | see 6.6.9 |
| `category` | `GRADUS_MESSAGE` on every `type: "message"` push (including the competition-recap message); absent otherwise and on silent pushes. The app adds the Reply action from it (§6.6.11) | `category` (`MESSAGE_CATEGORY`, `roomMessagePush`; web #225) |
| `uid` | The recipient's user id, on **every** push; the payload is built per recipient. The app refuses a Reply or a tap for another account (§6.6.11) | `pushPayload(message, recipientUserId)` |

The one exception to these flat keys is the Live Board `board_activity` message, whose whole payload travels as a JSON string in a single `gradus` key (§6.9.6, S-13). Every key name above is final; §6.6.11, §7.2.21, §7.5.10 and §7.10.4 use exactly these.

- **Android message options:** alert messages use `android.priority = "high"`; silent messages use `"normal"` (FCM deprioritizes high-priority messages that produce no visible notification, so a silent high-priority message would eventually cost the alert pushes their priority). `android.ttl` = the APNs expiry: `expiresInSeconds` when given (lesson reminder: until the lesson start window closes), otherwise 86 400 s for alerts (`DEFAULT_ALERT_EXPIRY_SECONDS`, "rink phones are offline for hours") and `0s` for silent. `android.collapse_key` = `collapseId` when present (so a newer plan or wrap-up push replaces the undelivered older one, the `apns-collapse-id` behavior).
- Secrets and setup: S-3 (Firebase project, service account in Lovable Cloud secrets). Not blocked by the Play Console (A8): FCM needs only the Firebase project and the app's `google-services.json`.

#### 6.6.3 Every push the app must handle

Found in the web code at HEAD (every `notifyUsers(`/`notify(` call). Copy is server-side and identical for both platforms; it is quoted here so tests can assert it. "Tab" is the Android tab the route lands on (`AppRoute.tab`, §6.10).

| `type` | Trigger (server file) | Recipients | Title / body (server copy) | `route` → Android destination | Collapse / thread | Android channel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | New message in a room (`messages.server.ts` `sendMessage`) | Other participants plus the athlete's household for athlete rooms, minus anyone blocked either way (`withoutBlocked`) | Title "Coach *First*" when a coach sent it, else sender's full name, else "New message"; body = the message text, or "Sent a voice note" | `rooms/<id>` → Messages tab, that room | thread `room:<id>`; `category` `GRADUS_MESSAGE` (Reply, §6.6.11) | `messages` |
| `message` | Competition recap sent by parent/athlete (`competition-recap.server.ts`) | The coach (minus blocks) | "Competition recap" / the recap text | `rooms/<id>` → that room | thread `room:<id>`; `category` `GRADUS_MESSAGE` (Reply, §6.6.11) | `messages` |
| `plan_assigned` | Plan activated or assigned (`plans.server.ts`) | Athlete and guardians (`athleteHouseholdUserIds`; co-guardians only while the Team plan is active) | "New plan" (was a draft) or "Plan activated" / "*Plan title* is ready to practice." | `plans/<id>` → Plans tab, that plan | `plan:<id>` | `plans` |
| `lesson_wrap_up` | Lesson slot ended (`lesson-wrap-up-prompts.server.ts`) | Coach | "Lesson wrap-up" / "*Name*'s lesson just ended. Edit, redeploy, or dismiss their plan." | `coach/wrap-ups` → Roster root, wrap-up prompt (or list when several) | `wrapup:<slotId>:<date>` | `lessons` |
| `lesson_reminder` | ~15 min before a slot (`lesson-reminders.server.ts`, pg_cron every 5 min) | Coach | "*First* is up next" (or "Your next lesson is up") / "See what they've been practicing since you last coached them." | `coach/roster/briefing/<athleteId>` → Roster root with that athlete's Up next briefing | `lesson:<slotId>:<date>:coach`; TTL ends at lesson start | `lessons` |
| `practice_nudge` | 3 days after a lesson, at its start time held to 08:00–20:00, no practice or lesson since, active plan (`practice-nudges.server.ts`, every 15 min) | Athlete (own copy) and guardians (named copy) | "Time to practice?" / "It's been 3 days since your lesson. Log a practice session to keep your plan moving." or "It's been 3 days since *First*'s lesson. Log a practice session to keep their plan moving." | `plans` → Plans tab root | server collapse id | `practice` |
| `connection` | Parent links an athlete to a coach with the coach's code (`parent-settings.server.ts`) | Coach | "New athlete connection" / "A parent connected an athlete to you with your invite code." | `settings/connections` (also triggers `linksChanged()`) → by role (`SettingsSectionView`, 6.10.2): coach → Connections hub; parent → Team plan (guardians); athlete → "Not for this account" state | — | `connections` |
| `connection` | Parent pauses/resumes messaging (`parent-settings.server.ts`) | Coach | "Messaging paused" / "*First*'s parent paused messaging with you." (or "Messaging resumed" / "…resumed messaging with you.") | `settings/connections` | — | `connections` |
| `connection` | Coach claims a parent's invite code (`invites.server.ts`) | Parent | "New coach connection" / "A coach connected with your athlete." or "A coach connected with *N* of your athletes." | `settings/connections` | — | `connections` |
| `connection` | Coach claims an adult athlete's code (`invites.server.ts`) | Athlete | "New coach connection" / "A coach connected with you using your invite code." | `settings/connections` | — | `connections` |

| `connection` | Team invite accepted (`team-guardians.server.ts`) | Primary parent | "Guardian joined" / "A guardian accepted your invite and joined your team." | `settings/connections` | — | `connections` |
| `competition_recap` | Day after a followed competition (`competition-recap-prompts.server.ts`) | Parent, athlete | "How did it go?" / "Share a quick recap of *Competition* with your coach." | `recaps/<competitionId>` → recap screen on the Plans tab | `recap:<competitionId>:<userId>` | `recaps` |
| `consent_rescinded` | Apple `RESCIND_CONSENT` (`app-store-notifications.server.ts`) | Parent; every linked coach | Parent: "*First*'s Gradus account is paused" / "Consent for their use of Gradus was withdrawn through Apple. Messages and coach connections are on hold." Coach: "*First*'s account is paused" / "Their family withdrew consent through Apple. Messaging with them is on hold." | Parent `settings/athletes` → Settings › My athletes; coach `coach/roster` → Roster | `consent_rescinded:<athleteId>` | `account` |
| `entitlement` | Stripe subscription sync (`coach-subscription-sync.server.ts`, `parent-subscription-sync.server.ts`) | Coach or parent | **Silent** | `settings/plan` (not opened; silent) | `entitlement:<userId>` | none (no notification) |

Every `connection` row routes to `settings/connections`, so the destination depends on the **recipient's** role: a coach lands on the Connections hub, a parent on Settings › Team plan, and an adult athlete (the "Coach claims an adult athlete's code" row) on the "Not for this account" state "Connections are managed by your coach or parent." That is what iOS does at HEAD (`RoleTabsView.swift` `SettingsSectionView`, `.connections` case); code wins (A2). Whether the athlete push should open Settings › Coaches instead is a product question for both apps (§12).

`consent_rescinded` originates from an iPhone (the athlete's Apple consent), but its recipients (a parent, a coach) may be on Android, so Android must route it. Unknown `type` with a parseable `route`: show it on the `general` channel and route normally. Unparseable `route` or `v ≠ "1"`: show the notification, tap opens the app with no route (iOS `route(fromPushUserInfo:)` returns nil and the tap does nothing beyond opening).

#### 6.6.4 Notification channels

Android requires a channel per notification; iOS has none (one per-app switch in iOS Settings). The channel set below is the Android-native equivalent of the single iOS switch plus iOS's default presentation (banner, sound, badge). Channel ids are stable forever (renaming an id orphans users' settings); names and descriptions are user-visible and English (proposed A25). Created once in `Application.onCreate` (idempotent), grouped under one channel group "Gradus".

| Channel id | Name | Description | Importance | Sound / vibration | Badge (launcher dot) | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `messages` | Messages | New messages from your coach, parents, and athletes. | `IMPORTANCE_HIGH` (heads-up, like an iOS banner) | Default sound, vibrate | Yes | `message` |
| `lessons` | Lesson reminders | Up next reminders and lesson wrap-ups. | `IMPORTANCE_HIGH` | Default | Yes | `lesson_reminder`, `lesson_wrap_up` |
| `plans` | Plans | When a plan is assigned or activated for you or your athlete. | `IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT` | Default | Yes | `plan_assigned` |
| `practice` | Practice reminders | Nudges to log practice, and a reminder when a practice timer is left running. | `IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT` | Default | Yes | `practice_nudge`; local "Still practicing?" (6.6.7) |
| `connections` | Connections | Coach, athlete, and guardian connections. | `IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT` | Default | Yes | `connection` |
| `recaps` | Competition recaps | Prompts to share how a competition went. | `IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT` | Default | Yes | `competition_recap` |
| `account` | Account alerts | Important changes to an athlete's account. | `IMPORTANCE_HIGH` | Default | Yes | `consent_rescinded` |
| `practice_timer` | Practice timer | Shows a running practice session. | `IMPORTANCE_LOW` (no sound, no heads-up) | None | No | Ongoing session-timer notification (proposed A12, §7.6 owns its content) |
| `live_board` | Live Board | Live scores for skaters you follow. | `IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT` (§6.9.6 owns: needed for Live Update promotion; every post is `setSilent`/`setOnlyAlertOnce`, so nothing sounds) | None | No | Live Board ongoing notifications (proposed A12, §6.9 owns) |
| `general` | Other | Other notifications from Gradus. | `IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT` | Default | Yes | Unknown `type` fallback |

Rules:
- Every notification: small icon = monochrome Gradus mark (vector, 24 dp), `color` = `accent-ink` token, `setAutoCancel(true)` for alerts, `setWhen(sentTime)`, `setShowWhen(true)`, `setCategory` (`CATEGORY_MESSAGE` for messages, `CATEGORY_REMINDER` for lesson and practice, `CATEGORY_STATUS` otherwise).
- **Lock-screen privacy (proposed):** alert notifications use `setVisibility(VISIBILITY_PRIVATE)` with a public version that shows only the channel name and "Gradus" (for example "New message"). This is the Android equivalent of iOS's default "Show Previews: When Unlocked"; the user's system lock-screen setting still wins. The two ongoing notifications are `VISIBILITY_PUBLIC`, like their Lock Screen Live Activities (§7.6.4, §6.9.6).
- **Messages** use `NotificationCompat.MessagingStyle`, `setGroup("room:<id>")` from `threadId`, and one notification per room (tag `room:<id>`, id `0`), the Android counterpart of iOS's `thread-id` grouping. Because every push is data-only, the app rebuilds the style each time or each push would overwrite the previous text: on each `message` push, read `NotificationManager.activeNotifications`, find the one with tag `room:<id>`, extract its style with `NotificationCompat.MessagingStyle.extractMessagingStyleFromNotification(...)` (or start a new style with the signed-in user as `Person` "You"), append `Message(text = body, timestamp = sentTime, person = Person(name = title))`, keep only the **last 7** messages, set the conversation title to the latest push title, and re-post with `setOnlyAlertOnce(false)` (each message alerts, as each iOS banner does). Test (Robolectric): three pushes for one room produce one posted notification whose style holds three messages in order; a push for a second room produces a second notification. Not a conversation shortcut (no `ShortcutInfo`, no bubbles) in 1.0: iOS has no counterpart (proposed). When the push carries `category = "GRADUS_MESSAGE"`, the notification also carries a **Reply** action on Android 12+ while the in-app lock is off (§6.6.11, #54), and `WearableExtender().setBridgeTag("gradus_message").setDismissalId("room:<id>")` (§6.15.8).
- **Collapse:** notification tag = `collapseId` if present, else `threadId`, else `type`; notification id = `0` within the tag. A later push with the same tag replaces the earlier one (iOS `apns-collapse-id`).
- **Foreground behavior (parity):** iOS shows banner, badge and sound for **every** notification while the app is open, including a message for the room on screen (`AppDelegate.userNotificationCenter(_:willPresent:)` returns `[.banner, .badge, .sound]` unconditionally). Android posts every alert push in the foreground too, heads-up on the same channel, **including a `message` push for the room currently open**. Suppressing the push for the open room would be a product change for both apps (and a high-priority FCM message that yields no visible notification is what FCM deprioritizes), so it is an open question in §12 for both apps, not built.
- **Opening a room cancels its notifications** (tag `room:<id>`), and opening Roster from a `lesson_wrap_up` cancels that wrap-up notification. Android launcher dots count posted notifications, so clearing them is what "the badge clears when the rooms are read" (gradus `docs/ios/QA.md` §"Badge count clears when the rooms are read") means on Android.
- **Wear OS bridging:** phone notifications bridge to the paired Wear OS watch by default (as iOS notifications mirror to Apple Watch). `practice_timer` and `live_board` ongoing notifications are `setLocalOnly(true)` (the watch has its own app, §6.15) (verify default bridging of ongoing notifications). **Message notifications** carry bridge tag `gradus_message`. A signed-in Wear app that can post notifications excludes that tag and posts its own copy, forwarded over the Data Layer, whose tap opens the conversation on the watch; otherwise they bridge like the rest (#54, A51, §6.15.8).
- Users may turn single channels off in Android Settings. The app never re-creates a deleted channel with a new id to get around that.

#### 6.6.5 Permission (POST_NOTIFICATIONS) timing

iOS asks **in context, never at first launch**: the first message room opened (`RoomView` `.task { PushPermission.requestIfNeeded() }`), the first practice session started (`LiveSessionReminders.prepare()` from `RunnerPlanDetailModel.start()`), and Settings › Device "Turn on". At launch it only re-registers if a decision was already made (`AppDelegate.didFinishLaunching`).

Android 13+ (API 33+) mirrors this exactly with the `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` runtime permission. Android 10–12 (API 29–32) has no runtime prompt; notifications are on by default, so those devices skip straight to registration.

| Moment | iOS | Android 13+ | Android 10–12 |
|---|---|---|---|
| First launch | Never asks | Never asks | Nothing to ask |
| Every room screen opened (signed in) | `requestIfNeeded()` (prompts only if undetermined) | Launch the permission request only if never requested on this install **and** not granted (local flag `push.permissionRequested` in DataStore, set when the request launches); otherwise no-op | No-op |
| Practice session start (parent, athlete) | Same shared `requestIfNeeded()` | Same | No-op |
| Settings › Device "Turn on" | Not asked → prompt; Off → open iOS Settings | Not asked → request; Off → open `Settings.ACTION_APP_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS` for the app | Off → open the same settings screen |
| Any yes (fresh or earlier) | `registerForRemoteNotifications()` every time | Fetch the FCM token and register (6.6.6) | Same |

Android caps the system dialog: after the user denies twice, the request returns denied without a dialog (verify). The local flag means Gradus asks at most **once** from an in-context moment, as iOS does; Settings › Device remains the way back.

**When `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` is denied (API 33+) or notifications are off.** iOS Live Activities have their own authorization, separate from notification permission, so on iPhone the session timer and the followed-skater activity show even when alerts are "Off" (`SessionActivityController`, iOS §6.9). Android has no such split: an app without `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` cannot show ongoing notifications either. Rules:
- The practice timer keeps running regardless (it is timestamp-based and needs no notification and no foreground service, proposed A12, §7.6); its ongoing notification is simply not posted (`NotificationManagerCompat.areNotificationsEnabled()` false, or the `practice_timer` channel blocked → skip `notify`, no error, no toast, no report). Parity of "the session is visible outside the runner screen" is kept in-app by the `ActiveSessionBar` on every tab (§7.6).
- A Live Board ongoing update for a followed skater is not posted; the board screen remains the place to watch (§6.9).
- The first practice-session start is the in-context ask (`RunnerPlanDetailModel.start()` → `reminders.prepare()` → `PushPermission.requestIfNeeded()`), so on API 33+ the user is asked **before** the first timer notification would post. No second prompt is ever shown for the timer or the board; Settings › Device "Turn on" is the way back.
- "Still practicing?" is skipped when notifications are disabled (6.6.7), as iOS skips it unless authorized or provisional.
- Instrumented test (API 33 emulator, permission denied): starting a session does not crash, no notification is posted, and the `ActiveSessionBar` shows on another tab with the running time.

**Settings › Device state** (`DeviceView.PushState`, labels verbatim): "Not asked" (API 33+, never requested and not granted), "Allowed" (`NotificationManagerCompat.areNotificationsEnabled()`), "Off" (everything else). Button "Turn on" (shows "Asking…" while the dialog is up) when not Allowed. Footer, verbatim except the platform noun (proposed A25): Off → "Notifications are off for Gradus in Android Settings. Turn on opens Settings so you can allow them."; otherwise "Lesson reminders, new messages, and plan updates arrive as notifications." The state refreshes when Settings › Device resumes (iOS refreshes on `scenePhase == .active`). §7.12 owns the screen layout.

#### 6.6.6 FCM token lifecycle

Mirrors `AppModel` push registration and `PushPermission`.

1. **Launch:** `FirebaseMessaging.getInstance().token` is requested only when notifications are enabled (`areNotificationsEnabled()`), the iOS "register on every launch when allowed" rule. The token is held in memory as `lastDeviceToken` (iOS holds the APNs token in memory).
2. **Upload:** `POST /api/v1/devices {token, platform: "android"}` whenever a token is known **and** a session exists **and** `NotificationManagerCompat.areNotificationsEnabled()` is true: at sign-in (`enterSignedIn`), at launch with a restored session, right after any yes from 6.6.5, and in `onNewToken` (rotation). `onNewToken` always stores the token in memory as `lastDeviceToken`, but uploads it **only** if a session exists and notifications are enabled: with FCM auto-init on (item 8), `onNewToken` fires on first launch whether or not the user was ever asked, and iOS registers with APNs only after a yes (`PushPermission.requestIfNeeded()` registers "whenever the answer is a yes"; `AppDelegate` re-registers at launch only when the status is not `.notDetermined`). Unit test (Robolectric, API 33): never asked, signed in → `onNewToken("tok…")` → no `POST /devices`; after a grant → exactly one `POST /devices`. Request details (web `src/routes/api/v1/devices/index.ts`, `src/lib/push.server.ts`): header `Idempotency-Key: device-<token>` (the same key iOS sends; the route deliberately does not replay it, so signing out and back in within 24 hours re-runs the upsert); body validated as `token` 8–512 chars and `platform` ∈ `ios|android`. **`"android"` is already accepted**, so registration is not blocked on S-3 (only sending is). Upload failures are swallowed (debug log only); the next launch retries. The server upserts on the token and re-points it at the current user (`registerDeviceToken`, service role), so a device handed between accounts follows the last sign-in.
3. **Permission revoked later:** iOS does not unregister when the user turns notifications off in iOS Settings, it simply stops registering on later launches. Android matches: no `DELETE` on revocation; FCM keeps delivering data messages, and the app does not post notifications the user disabled (Android drops them).
4. **Sign-out:** `DELETE /api/v1/devices/{token}` **before** the session is revoked, while the bearer is still valid: the server deletes only a row matching both the token **and** the caller's `user_id` (iOS `signOut()` step order: watch notice, device token, Live Activity token reporting, analytics flush/clear, session sign-out, store wipe). Delivered notifications are **cleared**, at sign-out and on an account switch, after the session is signed out (iOS `clearDeliveredNotifications`, #54 review 2026-10-11, so no Reply or tap is left on the last account's messages): cancel every active notification except the `practice_timer` and `live_board` ongoing ones, and delete the forwarded `/gradus/notify/room/*` DataItems (§6.6.11, §6.15.8). Closes §12 N26. What happens to the ongoing practice-timer notification at sign-out follows what happens to the session itself (§7.6 owns it).
5. **Password-reset link while signed in** (`presentRecovery`): unregister the token from the current account **before** showing the reset flow, because the link may belong to another household member. If the link turns out expired (`recoveryPending` cleared without a reset), register the token again for the account still signed in. §6.4 owns the flow.
6. **Email-change link that signs in another account** (`switchAccount(from:to:)`): no unregister call (the old session is already replaced); signing in the new account re-uploads the token, which the server re-points.
7. Never call `FirebaseMessaging.deleteToken()` on sign-out: the token is per install, and re-pointing is the server's job (iOS keeps its APNs token too).
8. FCM auto-init is on; `firebase_messaging_auto_init_enabled` stays default. The permission gate lives in the upload (item 2), not in auto-init: the token may exist on the device, but no `device_tokens` row is created until the user says yes. **No Firebase Analytics** dependency is added (`firebase-messaging` only; check the dependency tree in CI so no `firebase-analytics` arrives transitively) (iOS §6.11 "no third-party SDKs", #19; proposed A11).

#### 6.6.7 Receiving and tapping

- `GradusMessagingService : FirebaseMessagingService` (`exported="false"`). `onMessageReceived` parses `data`; if `silent == "1"` → 6.6.8; otherwise build and post per 6.6.4. Parsing failures post nothing and report nothing.
- **Tap routing:** the content `PendingIntent` (`FLAG_IMMUTABLE`, request code = hash of tag) is an **explicit-component** intent (`ComponentName` = `MainActivity`; never a resolvable implicit `gradus://` `VIEW`, 6.11.5) with `ACTION_VIEW` and data `gradus://<route>` (for example `gradus://rooms/abc`), plus extra `gradus.push.type`. Both cold start (`onCreate`) and warm start (`onNewIntent`) hand the URI to the same `AppModel.open(url)` path as links (§6.10), so `RouteParser` is the only decoder (iOS: `route(fromPushUserInfo:)` → `route(fromPath:)`). The intent also carries the push's `uid` as extra `gradus.push.uid`; a signed-in account that differs opens nothing, and a room route posts the "This message was for another Gradus account. Switch accounts to reply." notice (§6.6.11, #54).
- **One `MainActivity`, lock kept up.** iOS has one window and applies the route underneath the lock window (`AppModel.open` + `LockWindow.swift`). On Android the lock is a separate `LockActivity` above `MainActivity` in the same task (§6.4, 6.11.4), so `singleTop` is **not** enough: it reuses `MainActivity` only when it is on top, and a tap while `LockActivity` is on top would start a second `MainActivity`. Therefore:
  - `MainActivity` is `android:launchMode="singleTask"` (one instance per task). A new intent clears the activities above it (including `LockActivity`) and arrives in `onNewIntent`.
  - `LockActivity` keeps the app's default `taskAffinity` (same task), is never the task root, and is **not** `noHistory` (a `noHistory` lock would finish itself when the app goes to the background and reveal the app on return). §6.4 must match these attributes.
  - In `onNewIntent`, `MainActivity` first calls `AppModel.open(url)` and then, if `BiometricGate.isLocked`, immediately starts `LockActivity` again (no enter animation). While `isLocked` is true, `MainActivity`'s root composable draws an opaque paper-colored "locked" placeholder instead of the content, so no frame of content shows between the clear and the relaunch (and none on a cold start, 6.11.4 test 5).
  - Test (instrumented): with the lock enabled and on, tapping a `message` push leaves exactly **one** `MainActivity` in the task (`ActivityScenario`/`dumpsys activity` check), the lock is up, and after unlock the routed room is on screen.
- Routing semantics are iOS's `AppModel.open(_:)` exactly: a route that needs a session waits in `pendingRoute` until `/me` has loaded; `coach/wrap-ups` shows the Roster root and sets `wrapUpsRequested`; `coach/roster/briefing/<id>` shows the Roster root and sets `briefingRequest`; `settings/connections` also calls `linksChanged()`; a route into a tab the role does not have toasts "That page isn't available for your account."; a second push for a different room replaces the tab's path in place (the destination is keyed on the route, `RouteDestinationView.id(route)`).
- The biometric lock (§6.4, 6.11) stays up over a push-opened route; the route is applied underneath.
- **Local notification "Still practicing?"** (iOS `LiveSessionReminders` in `SessionActivityController.swift`; scheduled only by `RunnerPlanDetailModel.didEnterBackground()`, which `RunnerPlanDetailView`'s `scenePhase` observer calls):
  - **When scheduled:** only from the **runner plan-detail screen** (the plan's practice screen for parents and athletes), when that screen's ViewModel sees `ON_STOP` (app to background while the screen is mounted) **and** the session is `running` (not paused). Backgrounding from any other screen, or with the timer paused, schedules nothing (iOS behavior; the `ActiveSessionBar` elsewhere does not schedule).
  - **Skipped** unless notifications are enabled (`areNotificationsEnabled()` and the `practice` channel not blocked; iOS requires `.authorized` or `.provisional`). Backgrounding is too late to ask; the ask happened at session start (6.6.5).
  - **Content:** title "Still practicing?", body "Your session on *Plan title* is still running. Open Gradus to pause or end it.", default sound, channel `practice`, tag `session-reminder`. Delay 60 minutes, minimum 60 s. A new schedule **replaces** any earlier one (iOS reuses the request id `session-reminder`).
  - **Mechanism:** an inexact one-shot `AlarmManager.setAndAllowWhileIdle` with a single `FLAG_IMMUTABLE | FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT` `PendingIntent` to a non-exported receiver (same intent → replaces), per proposed A12 (WorkManager can be deferred for hours in restricted standby buckets; no `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` needed). The receiver re-checks that notifications are enabled before posting.
  - **Cancelled** on that screen's `ON_START` (`didBecomeActive`), on discard, on closing the feedback sheet without sending (`cancelFeedback()` → `discard()`), and when the session is submitted (`finish`). Cancel = cancel the alarm and remove any posted `session-reminder` notification.
  - **Tap:** opens the app with **no route** (explicit `MainActivity` intent, no data), as iOS sets no `userInfo` route; the `ActiveSessionBar` leads back to the plan. A deep link to the plan would be a change for both apps (§12).
  - Tests: ViewModel unit test with a fake scheduler: `ON_STOP` while running → one schedule; while paused → none; `ON_START` → cancel; discard/feedback-close/submit → cancel; scheduling twice keeps one pending alarm.

#### 6.6.8 Silent (data) pushes

iOS `didReceiveRemoteNotification`: drain the outbox, refresh `/me`, return `.newData`. Today the only silent type is `entitlement` (Stripe webhook → coach or parent). Android: `onMessageReceived` enqueues a unique, **non-expedited** `OneTimeWorkRequest` (unique name `silent-push-sync`, `ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP`, constraint `NetworkType.CONNECTED`) whose `CoroutineWorker` runs `syncEngine.drain()` then `refreshMe()` when a session exists; no notification. Not expedited: silent pushes are sent as normal-priority FCM messages, which grant no expedited-job exemption, and before API 31 an expedited worker runs as a foreground service and must implement `getForegroundInfo()` (with a channel) or it throws; iOS silent pushes are opportunistic too (`content-available`, low priority). If the app is in the foreground it runs the same two calls directly. A silent push shows no notification and no UI of its own. It calls the same `refreshMe()` as iOS (`AppDelegate.didReceiveRemoteNotification` → `model.refreshMe()`), so if the app is in the foreground and that refresh fails with a cached `/me`, the 7.13.1 error toast appears exactly as it would on iPhone; in the background nothing is visible. Test (Robolectric, `@Config(sdk = [29])`, `WorkManagerTestInitHelper`): the worker runs `drain()` then `refreshMe()` in that order and completes without a foreground-info crash.

#### 6.6.9 Badges

| Badge | iOS at HEAD | Android |
|---|---|---|
| Messages tab | `.badge(unreadTotal)` on the Messages tab; `refreshUnread()` on sign-in, foreground, Realtime insert, room closed; 0 at sign-out | Material 3 `NavigationBarItem` with `BadgedBox`/`Badge(unreadTotal)`; numbers above 99 render "99+"; TalkBack label "Messages, *n* unread"; same refresh triggers |
| App icon | **None set by the app.** The server's APNs payload carries no `badge` key (`pushPayload` in `push-notify.server.ts`), even though iOS §6.6 says "badge equals the unread total" and `docs/ios/QA.md` expects icon badges. Code wins. | Launcher **notification dots** come from posted notifications on channels with `setShowBadge(true)` (6.6.4). No `setNumber` in 1.0 (the payload carries no `badge`; §12 N31 would add it); the app never calls launcher-specific badge APIs. The PRD/code gap is listed in §12. |

#### 6.6.10 Tests (Android)

Unit (JUnit 5): payload parsing (every row of 6.6.3 → channel, tag, route), `v != "1"` ignored, unknown type → `general`, collapse/tag rules, token upload ordering on sign-in/sign-out/recovery (fake `DeviceTokenUploader`), permission flag logic for API 29/32/33+ (Robolectric `@Config(sdk = …)`). Also the 6.6.4 MessagingStyle stacking test, the 6.6.5 permission-denied session test, the 6.6.6 `onNewToken` gate test and sign-out clearing test, the 6.6.7 single-`MainActivity` lock test, the "Still practicing?" scheduling tests and the `uid` tap check, the 6.6.8 API 29 worker test, and the 6.6.11 Reply tests. Instrumented: posting each channel's notification and tapping it routes to the right screen from cold start (UI Automator), including signed-out (route waits for sign-in). Manual QA (§10, mirrors `docs/ios/QA.md` "Push"): new message, new/activated plan, invite accepted, lesson reminder, wrap-up prompt, recap prompt, practice nudge, consent paused, reply from the notification (§6.6.11); each arrives with the right copy and opens the right screen with the app killed.

#### 6.6.11 Read and reply from a message notification (#54, A52)

iOS #54 (2026-10-11, TestFlight feedback: "when I click on a notification in the watch that contains a message, I should be able to read the message and respond to it"); iOS §6.6 "Category", "Recipient"; gradus-ios `0dc28a9` (#130): `GradusCore/Push/MessageNotification.swift` (`MessageNotification`, `NotificationReplySender`, `NotificationReplyOutcome`), `Gradus/Shell/AppDelegate.swift`, `Gradus/Shell/NotificationReplies.swift`, `BiometricGate.onEnabledChange`, `AppDependencies.clearDeliveredNotifications`. Server: web #225 (`MESSAGE_CATEGORY`, `roomMessagePush`, `pushPayload(message, recipientUserId)`).

**Payload (S-3).**
- Every `type: "message"` push carries `data.category = "GRADUS_MESSAGE"`. That includes the competition-recap message, which is a real message in the coach's room and is built with `roomMessagePush`.
- Every push, silent ones included, carries `data.uid` = the recipient's user id. The FCM payload is built per recipient, as the APNs one is.
- Other pushes carry no `category`.
- An older Android build ignores both keys (lenient decoding, §4.3 rule 6), so the server change ships before the app.

**The Reply action.** It is added to a room notification (§6.6.4 "Messages") only when **all** of these are true:
1. `category == "GRADUS_MESSAGE"`.
2. The route parses to `rooms/<id>`.
3. `Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 31`. iOS requires an unlocked device (`.authenticationRequired`); `Action.Builder.setAuthenticationRequired(true)` exists only from Android 12, and before that a Reply could run from the lock screen. Android 10–11 therefore gets the iOS "no Reply" form: a tap opens the app.
4. The in-app biometric lock is **off** (`BiometricGate.isEnabled == false`). iOS registers the category without Reply while its Face ID lock is on, "so a tap opens the app and its lock".

Builder:
`NotificationCompat.Action.Builder(IconCompat(R.drawable.ic_reply), "Reply", replyIntent)`
`.addRemoteInput(RemoteInput.Builder("gradus.reply").setLabel("Message").build())`
`.setSemanticAction(SEMANTIC_ACTION_REPLY).setShowsUserInterface(false).setAllowGeneratedReplies(false).setAuthenticationRequired(true)`

- "Reply" is the iOS action title and "Message" the iOS placeholder.
- iOS's button title "Send" has no Android API: the system draws its own send button.
- No `setChoices` and no system-generated replies: the iOS notification offers none. The four quick replies live in the Wear app's thread (§7.15.7).
- `replyIntent` is an explicit-component broadcast to `NotificationReplyReceiver` (`exported="false"`), action `training.gradus.app.action.NOTIFICATION_REPLY`, data `gradus://rooms/<id>` (one intent per room), extras `roomId` and `uid`, flags `FLAG_MUTABLE | FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT`. RemoteInput needs a mutable intent; an explicit component satisfies the Android 14 rule for mutable PendingIntents.
- **When the lock setting changes** (the Settings toggle, or the reset at sign-out; iOS `BiometricGate.onEnabledChange` → `MessageNotification.register(replyAllowed:)`), rebuild every active `room:*` notification from its extracted `MessagingStyle`, with or without Reply, using `setOnlyAlertOnce(true)` so nothing sounds again.

**Handling a Reply, without opening a screen** (iOS `AppDelegate.userNotificationCenter(_:didReceive:)` + `sendReply`):
1. The receiver reads `RemoteInput.getResultsFromIntent(intent)?.getCharSequence("gradus.reply")` and trims it. It **cancels the room's notification** (tag `room:<id>`) whether or not the text is blank. iOS dismisses an actioned notification, and on Android this also ends the inline-reply spinner. Blank text stops here: nothing is sent and no notice is posted.
2. It enqueues a unique `OneTimeWorkRequest<NotificationReplyWorker>` (`setExpedited(OutOfQuotaPolicy.RUN_AS_NON_EXPEDITED_WORK_REQUEST)`, no constraints) with input `roomId`, `text`, `uid` and a fresh `idempotencyKey` (UUID). It is never retried: the worker returns `success` or `failure`, never `retry`. A user tap on a notification action grants the expedited job and no foreground service is involved, because Reply exists only on API 31+. The WorkManager database holding the text is excluded from backup (A24: add `databases/androidx.work.workdb*`).
3. The worker determines the outcome:
   - No signed-in session → `signedOut`.
   - `uid` present and not equal (case-insensitive) to the signed-in user → `otherAccount`. Nothing is sent.
   - Otherwise it runs `NotificationReplySender`, ported 1:1. It sends `{kind:"text", body, planId:null}` to `POST /rooms/{id}/messages` with `Idempotency-Key`, with a 20 s deadline (`defaultTimeout`; a deadline miss counts as unreachable). The outcome follows from the response:

     | Response | Outcome | Side effects |
     |---|---|---|
     | `{ok:true}` | `sent` | `POST /rooms/{id}/read` ("answering is reading"), then `refreshUnread()` |
     | `{ok:false, message}` | `refused(message)` | — |
     | 401 or code `unauthenticated` | `signedOut` | — |
     | 409 `idempotency_key_in_progress` | `inProgress` | — |
     | Status 0 or ≥ 500 | `queued` | Enqueued in the outbox with the **same key** (§7.5.6 "Enqueue" row shape) |
     | Status 0 or ≥ 500, and enqueueing fails | `failed` | — |
     | Any other API error | `refused(userMessage)` | — |
     | Anything else | `failed` | — |
   - On Android the outbox exists in any process that has a restored session (Room, Hilt singleton), so the queued path is always available when signed in. iOS reports `failed` for a reply that cold-launches the app in the background before its sync engine exists; that is a process-model artifact, not a product rule (§12 N77).
   - If the system stops the worker before an outcome (`isStopped`), it posts the `failed` notice and returns. This is iOS's background-task expiration handler.
4. **Notices** (iOS `MessageNotification.notice(for:roomID:recipientUserID:)`, verbatim; they never quote the reply). Posted on the existing **`messages`** channel (no new channel: ids are forever, §6.6.4, and a person who turned message notifications off gets none of these either), tag `reply:<roomId>`, id 0 (a newer notice for the room replaces the older one), `CATEGORY_STATUS`, `VISIBILITY_PRIVATE` with the §6.6.4 public version:

   | Outcome | Title | Body | Sound | Tap |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `sent`, `inProgress` | — (no notice) | — | — | — |
   | `queued` | "Reply saved" | "It sends when you next open Gradus." | none (`setSilent(true)`) | the room |
   | `refused(message)` | "Couldn't send your reply" | the server's message | default | the room |
   | `failed` | "Couldn't send your reply" | "Your reply didn't send. Open Gradus to try again." | default | the room |
   | `signedOut` | "Couldn't send your reply" | "You're signed out of Gradus. Sign in to reply." | default | opens Gradus, no route |
   | `otherAccount` | (none) | "This message was for another Gradus account. Switch accounts to reply." | default | opens Gradus, no route |

   "The room" = the §6.6.7 explicit `MainActivity` intent with `gradus://rooms/<id>` and the `uid` extra, `setGroup("room:<id>")`. Opening a room cancels `reply:<roomId>` as well as `room:<id>`.

**Tap on any push: the account check** (iOS `AppDelegate.open(_:sentTo:)`):
- The content intent carries the push's `uid` as extra `gradus.push.uid`.
- `AppModel.open(url, sentTo)` opens nothing when a user is signed in and `uid` names another account. For a room route it also posts the `otherAccount` notice.
- With nobody signed in, or with no `uid` (pushes from before web #225), the route behaves as before (§6.6.7).

**Sign-out and account switch clear delivered notifications** (iOS `clearDeliveredNotifications`, decision #54 review):
- Cancel every active Gradus notification **except** the `practice_timer` and `live_board` ongoing ones. Those are iOS Live Activities, which `removeAllDeliveredNotifications` does not touch; §7.6.4 and §6.9 own them.
- Delete the forwarded `/gradus/notify/room/*` DataItems (§6.15.8).
- Order: after the session is signed out, before the store wipe, as iOS does.

**Wear OS.**
- Room notifications carry `NotificationCompat.WearableExtender().setBridgeTag("gradus_message").setDismissalId("room:<id>")`. They are forwarded to the watch per §6.15.8.
- A Reply made on a **bridged** copy (watch signed out, or its notifications off) runs on the phone through this section, like iOS ("Apple runs a background action on the device the push was sent to"). Verify on the Pixel Watch that `setAuthenticationRequired` does not block a bridged Reply while the phone is locked in a pocket; if it does, record it as a platform limit.

**Tests.**
- Port `MessageNotificationTests`:
  - "Both apps register one category with a text Reply that runs in the background"
  - "A message notification's room comes from gradus.route"
  - "A Reply is trimmed; blank text, other actions and non-room routes are ignored"
  - "The sender sends the reply as text to its room with a fresh key, then reads the room"
  - "A refusal reports the server's words and is never queued"
  - "Offline or a server error queues with the same key; with no outbox it fails; a 4xx is a refusal"
  - "Only a reply that didn't simply go gets a local notice; it never quotes the reply and opens the conversation"
  - "The Reply needs an unlocked device, and is left off while the in-app lock is on"
  - "gradus.uid names the account a push was sent to; another account's is refused, an older push isn't"
  - "A 401 reads as signed out; a send still in progress claims nothing"
- Port `AppModelTests.notificationReply`: "A Reply from a message notification sends to its room and opens nothing; offline it waits in the outbox (decision #54)".
- Android additions, Robolectric:
  - `@Config(sdk = [30])`: no action. `[31, 36]`: one action with `SEMANTIC_ACTION_REPLY`, `isAuthenticationRequired`, RemoteInput key `gradus.reply`, label "Message", no choices.
  - Lock on → no action; toggling re-posts active room notifications silently.
  - The receiver cancels `room:<id>` and enqueues exactly one worker; blank enqueues none.
  - A stopped worker posts the `failed` notice once and is not retried.
  - Sign-out leaves only the timer and Live Board notifications.
  - FCM parsing of `category`/`uid` (absent keys → no Reply, no account check).
  - A tap with a mismatched `uid` opens nothing and posts the notice.
- Instrumented (API 33 emulator): reply inline from the shade with the app killed → the message reaches the web room, the notification is gone, the badge drops.
- Device QA on the Pixel and the Pixel Watch:
  - Reply from the phone shade.
  - Reply on the phone while the screen is locked asks to unlock first.
  - Airplane mode → "Reply saved".
  - Blocked recipient → "Couldn't send your reply" with the server's words.
  - Another account signed in → the other-account notice.
  - Lock on → no Reply.

### 6.7 AI and voice

**Scope of this section.** Server-side AI, voice in (recording, upload, transcription, voice → plan), voice out (plan read-aloud with on-device text-to-speech, the read-aloud voice picker), and voice-note playback. The Wear OS side is in §6.15 and §7.15; the coach voice screens are in §7.4; voice notes in rooms are specified in §7.5.

#### 6.7.1 Server-side AI is inherited, unchanged

Everything the iOS PRD §6.7 says about server AI applies to Android without change, because Android calls the same `/api/v1` endpoints (§6.1, §6.2):

| Server capability | Android client role | iOS source |
|---|---|---|
| Ask Gradus (grounded, cited, `grounded: false` fallback, safety topics return the Safe Sport panel verbatim) | Render only. **Hidden for every role in Android 1.0** behind a compile-time release flag `ReleaseFlags.ASK_GRADUS_ENABLED = false`, as on iOS (§7.9) | iOS §6.7 "Grounded Ask Gradus", #15, #16, #22 |
| Athlete summaries, pre-lesson briefing (`GET /coach/athletes/{id}/briefing` → `narrative`), session summaries, schedule-image parsing, plan-from-results | Call the endpoint, show progress, render. Long calls (briefing refresh, voice build) show progress and can be cancelled on the client (cancel the coroutine; the server keeps its own timeout) | iOS §6.7 para 1 |
| Athlete learning loop (skill events, level history, protocol and inferred events, athlete profile in prompts) | Nothing new on the client except the "why?" prompt (§7.3). **No on-device model**, no TensorFlow Lite / ML Kit custom model, no on-device training: the one-backend rule means every client sees the same athlete | iOS §6.7 "Athlete learning loop", #14, #17, #18, §6.1 |
| New-move drafts (#53): `POST /coach/moves/draft` looks the name up in the Gradus library, then an open exercise list (facts only), then runs a recognition check on Claude Haiku 5.5 with web search (`claude-haiku-5-5`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), with `google/gemini-2.5-flash` on the Lovable gateway as the fallback; one 28 s budget; 30 per hour per coach; writes nothing | Call it from the move form, show "Drafting…", fill per §7.3.8a. No model call from the device, no queueing | iOS §6.7 (2026-10-11), #53 |
| Flow-state labels | Always the canonical scale *Hard / A bit hard / Just right / A bit easy / Easy* (A44), read from one shared Kotlin constant mirroring `session-states.ts`. The middle is the target. Briefings and summaries **present the data and never interpret it**: they report counts, runs at either end, and the athlete's notes, and never call Hard or Easy good, bad, a struggle, mastery or boredom; the coach interprets. This is a server prompt change shared with iOS and the web; Android renders what the server returns | #18, A44 |
| Provider switch (`AI_PROVIDER=lovable|google`) | Invisible to clients; not on the Android critical path | iOS §6.7 "Provider recommendation", iOS §12 #4 |

No Android-specific AI endpoint is added. No AI call is made from the device to a model vendor. Firebase ML / Gemini Nano / Android AICore are **not** used (they would make Android behave differently from iOS and web; §4.3).

#### 6.7.1a AI permission (App Review 5.1.1(i)/5.1.2(i) on iOS; A54)

Before any AI call, the app shows a permission screen that names each AI feature, the company it goes to and what that company receives. The answer belongs to the account and is shared by iPhone, Android and both watches. The server enforces it: every AI route the apps call answers **403 `ai_consent_required`** ("Turn on AI features to use this.") until the answer is `granted`. Athletes under 18, or with no birthdate, are never asked and are always refused (**403 `ai_unavailable_for_minors`**, "AI features aren't available for athletes under 18."). The web app does not ask (web #230).

**API.**
- `GET /me` carries an optional `aiConsent {state: granted | declined | unasked, version, decidedAt}`. It is missing from an older server or an older cached `/me`.
- `GET /me/ai-consent` returns the same object (`getMeAiConsent`; Android does not call it, `/me` is enough).
- `PUT /me/ai-consent {granted: Boolean}` (`putMeAiConsent`) returns the new object. It is idempotent and online-only, never queued. A server whose table is missing answers 503 "Please try again in a moment."
- The state is `unasked` whenever the stored version differs from the server's `CURRENT_AI_CONSENT_VERSION` (2026-10-12), so a version bump asks everyone again.
- AI routes that refuse without permission: `POST /voice/build-plan`, `POST /athlete/voice/build-plan`, `POST /voice/transcribe`, `GET /coach/athletes/{id}/ai-summary`, `GET /coach/athletes/{id}/briefing`, `GET /plans/{id}/sessions/summary`, plan from competition results, `POST /coach/moves/draft`, `POST /coach/schedule-import/parse`, `POST /ask`.

**Who is asked** (`MeSummary.asksForAIConsent`): coaches and parents always. Athletes only when `athleteVoiceToPlan == true` (adults, #48). Nobody else.

**Client rules** (`AppModel`, ported into `RootViewModel`):
- `aiFeaturesAllowed = me != null && (me.aiConsent == null || me.aiConsent.state == granted)`. A server without the field leaves AI on.
- `aiConsentNeeded` is true when all of these hold:
  - ParentApproval is not blocking;
  - the Terms gate is not showing;
  - `asksForAIConsent`;
  - `aiConsent.state == unasked`;
  - the role is not coach, or `onboardingComplete == true`. A coach is asked after coach onboarding; a parent or adult athlete is asked right after the terms, even during their onboarding.
- `showsAIConsent = aiConsentNeeded || (aiConsentRequested && asksForAIConsent)`.
- `requestAIConsent()` sets `aiConsentRequested`. It is a no-op when the account isn't asked or the screen is already up. It is called by a feature tap, by Settings, and by any API response whose error code is `ai_consent_required`. One process-wide `AiConsentEvents` `SharedFlow`, emitted from the `ApiError` decoder for both the generated client and `MutationTransport`, is collected once by `RootViewModel`. This is the iOS `APIError.aiConsentRequiredNotification`, registered once.
- `setAIConsent(granted)`: `PUT`, clear `aiConsentRequested`, write `aiConsent.state` into the in-memory and cached `/me` (`MeCache`), and play a success haptic on Allow only.
- **Sign-out** clears `aiConsentRequested` and dismisses the screen, so a request made by the old account never carries over.
- The screen counts as a cover for `PromptHold` (wrap-up and other prompts wait). The connection celebration waits while the Terms gate or this screen is up (one cover at a time).

**The screen** (`AIConsentScreen`; iOS `AIConsentSheet`).
- Android presentation (A54): a root-level full-screen Compose `Dialog` (`DialogProperties(usePlatformDefaultWidth = false, decorFitsSystemWindows = false)`), hosted by `MainActivity` above the tabs, every `ModalBottomSheet` and every other dialog. This is the iOS root cover, or a full-screen presentation over the topmost sheet.
- There is no swipe or outside-tap dismissal (iOS `interactiveDismissDisabled`).
- **System back and predictive back** move the task to the back (`moveTaskToBack(true)`), like the other blocking gates (§7.1.0 rule 6), and **record nothing** (§12 N78).
- Paper background, content max width 520 dp, 20 dp side padding.
  - Title `AIConsentCopy.title` **"Allow AI features?"** (display font, heading).
  - Subtitle **"You can change this anytime in Settings."** followed on the same line by the link **"Privacy Policy"** (`https://gradus.training/privacy`, default browser; TalkBack hint "Privacy Policy opens in your browser"; iOS "…opens in Safari").
  - One card with the rows for the audience, separated by dividers. Each row has a leading icon (accent ink, hidden from TalkBack), a bold title and a secondary detail, merged into one TalkBack node.
  - An optional error line (destructive ink, error icon) with the error's message, announced as "Error: <message>" (polite live region).
  - Actions: primary **"Allow"** (spinner while saving; test tag `aiConsent.allow`) and a text button **"Not now"** (test tag `aiConsent.notNow`). Both are disabled while either is saving.
- **Always one screen.** When everything fits, the buttons follow the rows. When it doesn't (large font scale on a small phone or in landscape), the rows scroll and "Allow" / "Not now" are pinned to the bottom on the bar surface. Build it with a `SubcomposeLayout`, or measure-then-choose, as the iOS `ViewThatFits`. The choice must never scroll off screen.
- **Rows** (`AIConsentCopy.rows`, verbatim; one Kotlin source shared by the phone and Wear, A25):
  - Coach, in order:
    - `voice`: mic icon, "Speak a plan instead of typing it", "ElevenLabs turns your recording into words; Google Gemini turns them into a plan."
    - `summaries`: sparkles icon, "Walk into every lesson prepared", "Google Gemini reads logs, notes, and results and gives you a pre-lesson briefing, practice summaries, and plans from results."
    - `moves`: clipboard-with-pencil icon, "Fill in a new move in seconds", "Anthropic's Claude (or Google Gemini as a backup) drafts cues, a description, and why to assign it, from the move name, sport, and anything you've typed."
    - `schedule`: calendar icon, "Import a schedule from a photo", "No retyping. Google Gemini reads a photo of your schedule and fills in athlete names, emails, and lesson times."
  - Parent: `summaries` only, with sparkles icon, "See how practice is going at a glance", "Each plan gets a short summary. Google Gemini reads practice logs and notes, with names anonymized first." Voice messages are transcribed on the device (§6.7.6), so they are not listed.
  - Adult athlete: `voice` (same as the coach's), then the parent's `summaries` row.
  - Audience mapping: parent → parent, athlete → athlete, anything else → coach.
- Keep the rows in step with the privacy policy and the server routes. Changing a vendor, or what it receives, means a server version bump.

**Gates in the app** (`AIFeatureAccess.allowed`, `whenAllowed`, `request()`). Each one is a tap that asks first, or an automatic load that is skipped:

| Surface | Without permission | With permission |
|---|---|---|
| Plan voice capture (coach FAB and inline mic, §7.4; athlete authoring, §6.14) | Tapping the mic in idle opens the permission screen and does not record | Records as before |
| Parked coach voice clips (§7.4.3) | The drain does not run. A clip refused with 403 `ai_consent_required` is **kept**, not deleted | The drain runs at once when permission turns on, and on every later trigger |
| Pre-lesson briefing card (§7.2.8) | Tapping to expand opens the permission screen. A briefing request from the lesson-reminder push is ignored | As before |
| Athlete detail AI summary | Not built on Android: the 30-day summary is gone since the redesign and Android never requests it (A64). iOS still requests it behind this gate and discards it (§12 N99) | — |
| Plan editor "Summary" in the Logged card (§7.3.4 item 5) | The divider and the whole Summary block are hidden, and the summary is never requested | Shown. Turning permission on loads it for an active plan |
| Move form "Draft with AI" and its "Replace" (§7.3.8a) | Opens the permission screen | Drafts |
| Schedule import "Take a photo" / "Choose a photo" (§7.2.15) | Each row opens the permission screen instead of the camera or picker. ".csv" and "Enter it manually" are unaffected | As before |
| Plan from competition results (§7.10.2, both the athlete card section and the post-event card) | Opens the permission screen | Generates |
| Wear: "Record a plan" and the wrap-up's "Record changes" (§7.15.3, §7.15.4) | The Wear permission screen (below) | Records |

The server refuses regardless. A 403 `ai_consent_required` from any of these brings the screen back through `AiConsentEvents`.

**Settings → AI features** (§7.12). This row is shown only when `aiFeatures.offered`, which means `asksForAIConsent && me.aiConsent != null`.
- The row: sparkles icon, title "AI features", value "On" or "Off" (test tag `settings.aiFeatures`). It is a button, not navigation.
- When on, tapping it opens an M3 `AlertDialog`: title "Turn off AI features?", text "Voice plans, transcripts, summaries and drafts stop until you turn them back on.", buttons "Turn off" (destructive) and "Keep on". "Turn off" sends `PUT {granted: false}`. A failure is silent, as on iOS (`try?`).
- When off, tapping it opens the permission screen.

**Wear OS** (iOS `WatchAIConsentView`, `WatchPlansModel.aiAllowed`; one choice for the account).
- The watch's plan listing reads `/me.aiConsent` with its own session, next to `athleteVoiceToPlan`.
- `aiConsent` starts as `unasked` until a listing arrives, and is reset to `unasked` on sign-out and on `clear()`, so the watch fails closed. A listing with no field (an older server) leaves voice on.
