- "Record a plan" still shows on Home (§7.15.1). Tapping it, or the wrap-up's "Record changes", while not allowed opens the Wear permission screen instead of recording:
  - a `ScalingLazyColumn` with "Allow AI features?" (heading) and "You can change this anytime in Settings.";
  - the same rows as the phone for the audience, each a label with icon, title and caption-size detail, as one node;
  - an error line;
  - primary "Allow" (test tag `watch.aiConsent.allow`) and secondary "Not now" (`watch.aiConsent.notNow`), both disabled while saving.
- Allow and Not now send `PUT /me/ai-consent` with the watch's session.
- A failure shows "Couldn't save. Check your connection and try again." and is announced.
- Success dismisses the screen. Allow then continues straight into recording: the Record a plan route, or `startRecording()` for the wrap-up.
- The `WatchCreatePlan` destination is reachable only when `voiceToPlan && aiAllowed`.

**Direct notice gains an item** (§7.1.18): "**AI summaries:** Your athlete's coach can get AI summaries of practice, made by Google Gemini. Gradus anonymizes your athlete's name before a summary is sent to Google." (see 3.1.e).

**Server behavior Android relies on (no Android change):** athlete, parent and coach names become placeholders in every Gemini prompt (`src/lib/ai-names.ts`), on the web and in the apps. Coach PDFs join the knowledge corpus only with permission. A voice note sent from an app without permission is stamped never-transcribe.

**Debug mock (A28):** the extras `gradusMock aiConsent` (coach, unasked) and `aiConsentParent` (parent, unasked). On Wear: `coachAIConsent`. Mock repositories default to `granted`.

**Tests** (ports of `AIConsentSheetTests`, `AppModelTests.aiConsent`, `WatchAIConsentTests`):
- Coach rows are `voice, summaries, moves, schedule` and name ElevenLabs, Google Gemini and Anthropic. The moves row names both Anthropic and Gemini. Parent rows are `summaries` only, with no Anthropic or ElevenLabs. Athlete rows are `voice, summaries`.
- Terms come before AI permission. A coach before onboarding is not asked. Not now closes the screen and AI stays off. Allow turns AI on.
- A minor is never asked, `request()` does nothing for a minor, and a minor has no AI.
- An older server (`aiConsent` missing) never asks and leaves AI on.
- A 403 `ai_consent_required` from any route opens the screen once.
- Sign-out dismisses the screen and clears the request.
- The celebration and `PromptHold` wait while the screen is up.
- Every gate in the table above, without permission: no request reaches the repository.
- A parked clip refused with `ai_consent_required` is kept, and the drain runs once permission turns on.
- Settings: row visibility, the "On"/"Off" value, and the turn-off dialog.
- Wear: closed before the first listing and after sign-out; open for an older server; Allow continues to recording.
- Compose: the one-screen layout at font scale 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 on a 360 × 640 dp window and in landscape (Allow is always visible).

#### 6.7.2 Voice in: recording format and the recorder

The phone and the watch share one recorder implementation in the `audio` package of the `:core:data` module (§9.1; the equivalent of iOS `GradusCore/Audio/Audio.swift` `VoiceRecorder`).

| Property | iOS (`VoiceRecorder`, `AVAudioRecorder`) | Android requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Container / codec | AAC in `.m4a` | `MediaRecorder` with `OutputFormat.MPEG_4` and `AudioEncoder.AAC` |
| Sample rate / channels / bitrate | 24 kHz, mono, 32 kbps, `AVAudioQuality.medium` | `setAudioSamplingRate(24_000)`, `setAudioChannels(1)`, `setAudioEncodingBitRate(32_000)`. A 90 s clip must stay under 400 KB (test) |
| Audio source | system default mic; `.playAndRecord`, `.spokenAudio`, `.allowBluetooth` (+ `.defaultToSpeaker` on iPhone) | `MediaRecorder.AudioSource.VOICE_RECOGNITION` (tuned for speech, no AGC artefacts; falls back to `MIC` if `setAudioSource` throws). Bluetooth-headset mic: see §6.15 "Headphones" (watch). On the phone the built-in mic is used (proposed; iOS allows a Bluetooth HFP mic on iPhone too, but routing Android input to SCO needs `MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION`, which degrades A2DP playback; revisit if coaches ask) |
| File | `tmp/voice-<UUID>.m4a` | `cacheDir/voice-<UUID>.m4a` (same prefix and suffix, so the launch sweep in §6.15 matches) |
| Caps | `VoiceRecorder.maxSeconds = 180` (server cap); callers pass 90 for the FAB and the watch | Same: `MAX_SECONDS = 180`, `VoiceRecorder(maxSeconds = 90)` for the plan voice button and every watch recorder; the constructor clamps to 180 |
| Auto-stop | the 100 ms ticker calls `stop()` when `elapsed >= maxSeconds` | Same 100 ms ticker in a coroutine; at the cap the state becomes `Finished(file, seconds)` |
| Level meter | `averagePower` in dB, `level = max(0, power + 60) / 60` | Poll `MediaRecorder.getMaxAmplitude()` every 100 ms, convert to dBFS `20·log10(amp / 32767)`, then the same `max(0, dB + 60) / 60` mapping so the waveform looks the same |
| States | `idle`, `denied`, `recording`, `finished(url, seconds)`; `seconds = max(1, round(elapsed))` | Same sealed class; same rounding |
| Permission | `AVAudioApplication.requestRecordPermission()` in context, on first tap | `RECORD_AUDIO` runtime permission requested in context on first tap (never at launch). Denied → `Denied` state (copy in §7.4 / §7.15) |
| Cancel | stop, delete the file (also after the auto-stop), back to idle | Same, including deleting a file the auto-stop already finished |
| Shared "is recording" flag | `AudioActivity.shared.isRecording` (iOS `GradusCore/Audio/AudioActivity.swift`) | `AudioActivity.isRecording: StateFlow<Boolean>` (process singleton). The read-aloud player observes it: starting a recording stops a read (§6.7.4) |
| Audio focus | session activated / deactivated with `notifyOthersOnDeactivation` | Request `AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT_EXCLUSIVE` while recording; abandon on stop / cancel |

**Clips shorter than 1 second are dropped silently** (the screen returns to its start state) on every recorder (iOS `VoiceCaptureModel.stopAndSend`, `WatchCreatePlanModel.stopAndSend`, `WatchWrapUpModel.stopAndSend`).

**On-device speech recognition only for voice-message transcripts on the phone (A55); none for plans and none on the watch.** Plan voice (`/voice/build-plan`, `/athlete/voice/build-plan`) and every watch recording stay on the server pipeline, so every client transcribes plans the same way with the same vocabulary hints (iOS §6.7 "On-device transcription"). **Voice notes in Messages are transcribed on the phone** (iOS `VoiceNoteTranscriber`, web #238): the words ride along with the send, and the server never sends a phone voice note to ElevenLabs (§6.7.6, §7.5.8). Android never uses `RecognizerIntent` UI, a network recognizer, or Wear `RemoteInput` voice input for any Gradus voice feature. (Ordinary keyboard dictation inside a text field is the user's keyboard, not a Gradus feature, and is untouched.)

#### 6.7.3 Upload and transcription

| Endpoint | Used for | Android request | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /voice/build-plan` | Coach voice → plan (create) and voice edit of an open plan (edit); coach wrap-up by voice on the watch | `multipart/form-data`: part `audio` (`Content-Type: audio/mp4`, filename `voice.m4a` on the phone, `plan.m4a` for a watch create, `wrap-up.m4a` for a watch wrap-up), part `mode` = `create` \| `edit`, part `planId` (uuid, required for `edit`) | `[idem]`: every send carries an `Idempotency-Key`; rate limit 10 / 60 s; 400 `validation_failed` "Missing planId for edit" |
| `POST /athlete/voice/build-plan` | Adult athlete's own plan by voice (§6.14) | Same three parts | 403 `text_only` for a minor or unconfirmed-age login |
| `POST /voice/transcribe` | Repository method only, kept for contract parity; **no Android 1.0 screen calls it** (iOS `PlansRepository.transcribe(audio:filename:)` exists but has no caller outside tests). Voice-note transcripts are made on the phone (§6.7.6, A55) | Part `audio` only | Returns `{ text }`; 403 `text_only` for a minor login |
| Voice notes | Rooms (§7.5) | Direct Supabase Storage upload with the user's token to bucket `voice-notes` at `<roomId>/<userId>/<uuid>.m4a`, `contentType = "audio/mp4"`, `upsert = false`, then the message row references the path (iOS `GradusAPI/VoiceNoteStorage.swift`; §6.3) | supabase-kt Storage, one client per upload so the bearer is always current. Minors cannot upload (bucket policy) and never see the mic |

The Kotlin client is generated from the OpenAPI contract (§9); the multipart builders are hand-written helpers equivalent to iOS `GradusAPI/VoiceUpload.swift` (`buildPlanBody`, `athleteBuildPlanBody`, `transcribeBody`). `X-Gradus-Client` is `android/<version>+<build>` from the phone and `wearos/<version>+<build>` from the watch (iOS sends `ios/...` and `watchos/...`; the server parses any lowercase platform token, `src/lib/api/client.ts`, so no server change is needed).

**Server responses Android must map** (from `src/lib/voice.server.ts`, `src/lib/minor-voice.server.ts`):

| Status / code | Message (server text, shown as-is) | Retryable with the same clip? |
|---|---|---|
| 413 `payload_too_large` (fires above 18 MB, `MAX_AUDIO_BYTES` in `voice.server.ts`; iOS §6.7 "180 s / 18 MB hard cap") | "Recording too long — please keep voice notes under 3 minutes" | No (drop the clip) |
| 403 `paused` (athlete whose account is paused after consent was withdrawn, `athlete-authoring.server.ts`; iOS QA §4) | the server's paused message, shown as-is | No (drop the clip) |
| 422 `unprocessable` | "Didn't catch that — try again" | No |
| 403 `text_only` | "Voice isn't available for athletes under 18. Type it instead." | No |
| 503 `voice_unavailable` | the transcription service's message, or "Couldn't transcribe that — please try again" | Yes |
| 409 `idempotency_key_reused` | (the first send went through; its answer was lost) | Treated as success, see §7.4 / §7.15 |
| 409 `idempotency_key_in_progress` | — | Yes, after a moment |
| 429, 5xx, network failure (status 0, `offline`, `unreachable`) | — | Yes |

The retryable rule is iOS `WatchRecordings.isRetryable`: no `APIError` → retryable; codes `offline`, `unreachable`, `rate_limited` → retryable; status 0, 429 or ≥ 500 → retryable; everything else is a refusal that will not change on a resend, so the clip is dropped.

Test: a paused adult athlete's phone voice send and watch voice send each show the server's paused message and keep no clip (no parked file on the phone, nothing held for "Try again" on the watch).

**Result shape.** `VoiceApplyResult { planId, transcript, touched { plan { title, athleteId, notes }, moves { moveId: [field] }, newMoveIds, transcript, sources { plan {...}, moves {...} } }, unresolvedAthleteName?, appliedMoveCount, droppedMoveCount?, aiFailed }`. `sources.*` carry `{ quote, start, end }` for the "From your voice" source quotes. `droppedMoveCount` may be absent on older responses (decode as nullable). The server keeps the transcript on the plan even when `aiFailed` (`plans.voice_transcript`).

**Minors (#32, #48).** `GET /me` returns `athleteVoiceToPlan`. Android hides **every** athlete voice control unless it is exactly `true` (missing or `null` = off), on the phone and the watch (iOS `MeSummary.athleteMayUseVoice`, `PlansDependencies.voiceAvailable`). The server refuses anyway (403 `text_only` before any audio is read). Coaches always have voice; the server applies the same per-login check to the coach route (a minor's login that also holds a coach profile gets `text_only`). The minor check is never computed on the device.

#### 6.7.4 Voice out: "Read this plan aloud" (plan → audio)

Decision #36 (full read) and #47 (on-device voices only). The same builder and player run on the phone and the watch.

**Narration text (`PlanNarration`, port of iOS `GradusCore/Narration/PlanNarration.swift`, pure Kotlin in the `narration` package of `:core:data` (§9.1), unit-tested with the iOS test vectors):**

- Segment 0 is the title line; then one segment per move, sorted by `position`. Each segment has `id`, `kind` (`TITLE`/`MOVE`), `moveIndex` (null for the title), `text` (exactly what is spoken and what the caption shows).
- Title line: `"<title>. <n> moves, about <duration>."` when any move is minutes-based (sum of minute targets), else `"<title>. <n> moves."`; `"1 move"` singular; empty title → `"Untitled plan"`; no moves → `"<title>. This plan has no moves yet."`. Duration: under 60 or fractional → `"N minutes"` / `"1 minute"` / `"7.5 minutes"`; whole hours → `"1 hour"`, `"2 hours 5 minutes"`, `"1 hour 1 minute"`.
- Move line: `"Move <i> of <n>. <name>. <target>."` then `"Cue: <cue>."` and `"Why: <why>."` only when non-empty (a clause gets a full stop unless it already ends in `.`, `!` or `?`); empty name → `"Untitled move"`. Target: `"8 reps"`, `"1 rep"`, `"10 minutes"`, `"1 minute"`, `"7.5 minutes"`, using the same number formatter the screens use (`PlanMove.formatTarget`).
- Cleaning (`spoken()`), in this order: Markdown links `[label](url)` → label; HTML-ish tags removed; a leading list bullet (`-`, `•`, `*`) at line start removed; line breaks → `". "`; `"2 - 3"` (digits around a spaced dash, `-–—`) → `"2 to 3"`; `"3 * 4"`/`"3×4"`/`"3x4"` → `"3 times 4"`; `"~5"` → `"about 5"`; spaced hyphen → `", "`; `>=` → `" at least "`, `<=` → `" at most "`, `>` → `" more than "`, `<` → `" less than "`, `&` → `" and "`; `_` → space; then `**`, `*`, `` ` ``, `#`, `~`, `|`, `\` deleted; repeated full stops collapsed; runs of spaces collapsed; space before `,`/`.` removed; trimmed of whitespace and `.,` at both ends.

**Player state machine (`NarrationPlayer`, port of iOS `NarrationPlayer.swift`, pure, tested with a fake `SpeechOutput`):** states `IDLE`, `SPEAKING`, `PAUSED`; `index`, `finishedOnce`, `speed` (`SLOW`/`NORMAL`/`FAST`, labels "Slow", "Normal", "Fast"). `position` = `"Plan title"` on the title, else `"Move <i> of <n>"`. Rules (all from the iOS code and `NarrationPlayerTests`):

- `load(plan)`: identical segments → no change (a reload keeps its place); otherwise stop, replace, index 0, returns whether it cut off a read.
- `play()`: from idle after a finished read starts at the title; from pause resumes (or re-speaks the line when `speakFreshOnResume`).
- At the end of a segment while speaking → next segment; after the last → `finishRead()` (stop, index 0, `finishedOnce = true`).
- A segment that ends in the instant Pause took hold → move on, stay paused, say the next line on Resume.
- Next / Previous: move the index; while speaking or paused, speak the new line at once.
- Repeat: say the current line from its start.
- Speed change: mid-speech the line restarts at the new speed; while paused the line is said fresh at the new speed on Resume.
- System interruption (call, assistant) while speaking → pause, and Resume re-speaks the line.

**The Android speech engine (`AndroidSpeechOutput`, replacing iOS `AVSpeechOutput`).**

| Concern | iOS | Android |
|---|---|---|
| Engine | `AVSpeechSynthesizer`, on-device | `android.speech.tts.TextToSpeech` with the device's default engine (normally "Speech Services by Google", `com.google.android.tts`). Created lazily on first speak, kept for the screen's life, `shutdown()` on dispose |
| One utterance per segment | `AVSpeechUtterance` | `speak(text, QUEUE_FLUSH, params, utteranceId)`; `UtteranceProgressListener.onDone(id)` → `onFinished` only when `id` is the current one (a stopped or replaced utterance is ignored, as iOS compares `ObjectIdentifier`) |
| Pause / resume | `pauseSpeaking(.immediate)` / `continueSpeaking()` | **Android TTS has no pause.** Pause = `stop()` and mark `speakFreshOnResume`; Resume re-speaks the current segment from its start. This is the one behavioral difference from iOS (iOS continues mid-line). Segments are one move each, so at most one move is repeated |
| Rate | `AVSpeechUtterance.rate` 0.42 / 0.50 / 0.58 (default 0.5) | `setSpeechRate` **0.85 / 1.0 / 1.15** (proposed; tune by ear on the Pixel and the Pixel Watch so Slow and Fast feel like iOS) |
| Voice | the chosen voice per line (a Settings change applies from the next line) | `setVoice(resolvedVoice)` before every `speak` |
| Audio attributes / ducking | `.playback`, `.spokenAudio`, `.duckOthers`; deactivate with `notifyOthersOnDeactivation` | `setAudioAttributes(USAGE_MEDIA, CONTENT_TYPE_SPEECH)`; request `AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT_MAY_DUCK` before the first line, abandon on stop |
| Interruption | `AVAudioSession.interruptionNotification` began → `onInterrupted` | `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS` / `LOSS_TRANSIENT` → `onInterrupted` (pause; Resume re-speaks) |
| Engine not ready | — | Queue the first `speak` until `onInit(SUCCESS)`; on `ERROR` or no engine installed, the start button shows "Read aloud isn't available on this device." (new Android string; iOS always has a synthesizer) and is disabled |

**Phone screen behavior (port of iOS `FeatureNarration`).** Used on the coach plan editor (`PlanDetailView`) and the parent/athlete runner (`RunnerPlanDetailView`), §7.3 and §7.6.

- Start button: "Read this plan aloud" (speaker icon), secondary style, shown only when the plan has moves. Disabled when there are no moves (caption "Add a move to hear this plan.") or a recording is under way (caption "Finish recording to hear this plan."), or while the bar is open. TalkBack hint: "Speaks the plan: each move with its target, cue and why".
- Pinned player bar (Compose bottom inset, opaque `popover` surface, border `borderStrong`, radius `lg`, at most 60 % of the screen height, minimum 180 dp, scrolls beyond that; never jumps in height between lines). Contents in order: eyebrow "Reading aloud"; position ("Plan title" / "Move 2 of 6"); controls row "Previous move", Play/Pause (labels "Play", "Pause reading", "Resume reading"; prominent, 64 dp, accent), "Next move", "Repeat this move" (52 dp); the live caption (TalkBack label "Now reading", value = caption); after a finished read "That's the whole plan. Play to hear it again."; the notice line if any, otherwise "Reading pauses if you lock the screen or leave Gradus."; eyebrow "Speed" with three chips "Slow" / "Normal" / "Fast" (group label "Reading speed"); a "Done" chip (hint "Stops reading and closes the player").
- TalkBack focus moves to Play/Pause 300 ms after the bar opens; on Done, focus returns to the start button.
- The move being read is highlighted in the move list (3 dp `accentInk` border) and scrolled to; its TalkBack value adds "Being read aloud".
- The screen stays awake while speaking (`FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON` while `SPEAKING`, cleared otherwise and on dispose) so the screen timeout does not cut the read (iOS `isIdleTimerDisabled`).
- **The phone does not read in the background** (iOS has no `audio` background mode on the iPhone app): on `ON_PAUSE` (the closest equivalent of iOS leaving `scenePhase == .active`, which includes `.inactive` for Control Center and the app switcher; iOS `NarrationBarModifier`) with a read under way, call `appLeftTheScreen()`: pause and show the notice "Paused because you left Gradus. Tap Play to go on." Tapping Play after a notice clears it. (Pulling down the notification shade does not trigger `ON_PAUSE` on Android, so a read continues there; if Mariah wants that treated as leaving too, it needs a window-focus check. Logged as an Android-native difference, §12 N35.)
- A plan change that alters what would be said during a read stops it with the notice "Plan changed. Reading stopped."; an identical reload keeps reading.
- Starting a recording stops a read with the notice "Reading stopped because you started recording."
- Finishing a read announces "Finished reading this plan." (a polite live region; see §8 for the Android equivalent of `AccessibilityNotification.Announcement`).
- Leaving the screen closes the bar and stops speech.

Test expectations: port `NarrationCardTests` (starting opens the bar and speaks the title; the move being read is marked; no moves cannot start; Done stops, closes, and returns focus; a plan change stops and says so; an identical reload keeps going; leaving pauses with an explanation; a recording stops the read; reading cannot start during a recording; the three speed presets), `NarrationPlayerTests`, `PlanNarrationTests` (every phrase and every cleaning rule, using the same inputs and expected strings).

#### 6.7.5 The read-aloud voice (decision #47) on Android

**Rule, applied identically:** on-device voices only; nothing leaves the device; works offline. **Automatic** picks the most natural American English voice installed, a woman's where one is as natural; a natural voice of either gender beats a robotic one. The reader can choose another in **Settings → Device → Read-aloud voice**. The choice is kept **per device**: the watch has no picker and always uses its own Automatic pick. A custom cloud voice is deferred (iOS §12 #35).

**Mapping Apple's voice model to Android `android.speech.tts.Voice`:**

| iOS concept (`NarrationVoice.swift`) | Android equivalent |
|---|---|
| `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice.speechVoices()` | `textToSpeech.voices` of the default engine (`TextToSpeech.getDefaultEngine()`), read after `onInit` |
| `identifier` (what is saved) | `Voice.name` plus the engine package, saved together as `"<enginePackage>/<voiceName>"` in DataStore key `narration.voiceIdentifier` (same key name as iOS `NarrationVoicePreference.key`). A saved voice from a different engine than the current default counts as "no longer on this device" → Automatic |
| `language` (BCP 47) | `Voice.locale.toLanguageTag()` |
| Quality tiers Standard / Enhanced / Premium; `isNatural = quality >= Enhanced` | `Voice.getQuality()`: `QUALITY_VERY_HIGH` (500) → top tier, `QUALITY_HIGH` (400) → second tier, `QUALITY_NORMAL` (300) and below → Standard. `isNatural = quality >= QUALITY_HIGH` (verify on the Pixel what Google's voices report; if every installed Google voice reports the same tier, the ranking falls through to gender and the preferred-voice list, which is acceptable) |
| Row labels "Standard" / "Enhanced" / "Premium" | Android labels **"Standard" / "High quality" / "Very high quality"** (Apple's tier names are Apple branding; proposed new decision) |
| Gender (`voice.gender`) | Android exposes **no gender API**. Use a curated table `NarrationVoiceGender` in `:core:data` (`narration` package) keyed by Google TTS voice name (for example the `en-us-x-…-local` family), filled in by listening to each installed US-English Google voice on the Pixel during milestone K6 (§10) and committed with a test (§12 N10). Voices not in the table are `UNSPECIFIED` (ranked after female, same as iOS ranks `.unspecified` after `.female`). Verify the table against each Google TTS update |
| Novelty voices, Personal Voice, Eloquence (`.eloquence.`), classic Mac (`.speech.synthesis.voice.`) excluded | No Android counterpart. Android excludes instead: voices whose `features` contain `TextToSpeech.Engine.KEY_FEATURE_NOT_INSTALLED` ("notInstalled"), voices where `isNetworkConnectionRequired()` is true or `features` contain `KEY_FEATURE_NETWORK_SYNTHESIS` ("networkTts") (a network voice would send plan text, including minors', off the device, which #47 forbids), and non-English locales |
| `preferredNames` tie-break (`Ava, Zoe, Allison, Samantha, Susan, Nicky, Evan, Nathan, Tom`) | `preferredVoiceNames`: an ordered list of Google TTS US-English voice names, women's first, most natural first, chosen by Mariah from samples on the Pixel (§12 N10). Until chosen, the tie-break is name order |
| `availableVoicesDidChangeNotification` | No reliable broadcast. Re-read the voice list on every `ON_RESUME` of the picker and the Device screen, and when a read starts; cache otherwise |

**Ranking (identical order to iOS `NarrationVoiceChoice.ranksAbove`):** American English (`en-US`) first → natural before robotic → female before others → higher quality → `preferredVoiceNames` index → name (locale-aware compare) → identifier. `automatic()` = the best-ranked listable voice; `resolve(saved)` = the saved voice while it is still installed and listable, else Automatic; if nothing is listable, the engine default for `Locale.US` reads (iOS falls back to `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice(language: "en-US")`). `pickerOrder()` = listable voices sorted by the ranking, split into American English and other English.

**Settings → Device → Read-aloud voice** (port of iOS `FeatureSettings/Account/ReadAloudVoiceView.swift` and the Device row in `DeviceView.swift`):

- Device screen section, eyebrow "Read aloud": row "Read-aloud voice" (speaker icon) with value = chosen voice's short label (`"<name> · <quality label>"`), or `"Automatic (<name> · <quality label>)"`, or `"Automatic"`; footer "The voice that reads plans aloud. It runs on this device, so nothing is sent anywhere." Value refreshes on resume.
- Picker screen title "Read-aloud voice". Section eyebrow "American English": first row **Automatic** with detail "Uses <name> (<quality label>)" when the pick is natural, "Uses <name> (<quality label>). Download a Premium voice for a more natural sound." when it is not (Android string: "Uses <name> (<quality label>). Download a higher-quality voice for a more natural sound."), or "Uses this device's default voice"; then one row per American English voice (title = display name, detail = quality label). Section eyebrow "Other English voices" (only when non-empty): detail "<quality label> · <language label>" with the language label in English ("English (United Kingdom)").
- Each row: a selectable row (min 48 dp, check mark when selected, TalkBack label = name, value = "<quality label>, <language label>", selected state) and a sample button (play / stop icon). Sample button label "Play a sample of the automatic voice" / "Play a sample of <name>, <quality label>" (two qualities of one name must be told apart) and "Stop the sample" while playing. One sample at a time; the sample text is "Hi, I'm <name>. This is how Gradus reads your plans aloud: each move, its target, its cue, and why it matters." (the "Hi, I'm <name>." intro only when the voice has a friendly display name, see below). A sample stops on tap again, on leaving the screen, on `ON_STOP`, and on audio-focus loss.
- **Display names.** Google TTS voice names are technical (`en-us-x-sfg-local`). Show a friendly name from the same curated table as gender when known; otherwise "Voice <n>" numbered within its language group in ranking order (proposed; §12 N10).
- Section eyebrow "More natural voices", body (Android version of the iOS text, which points at iOS Settings): "The most natural voices are free downloads from Google. Tap Open voice settings, choose Speech Services by Google, then Install voice data, then English (United States), and download a voice. It appears here." plus a button **"Open voice settings"** that launches `TextToSpeech.Engine.ACTION_INSTALL_TTS_DATA` (falls back to the system TTS settings intent `com.android.settings.TTS_SETTINGS`, then to `Settings.ACTION_SETTINGS`). Android can open this screen; iOS cannot, so iOS only describes the path. Footer: "Voices stay on this device. Plans are read on the device and nothing is sent anywhere."
- Selecting a row saves immediately; Automatic clears the saved value.

QA (port of iOS QA §5b to the Pixel): Automatic shows "Automatic (<name> · <quality>)"; the best-ranked voice reads; a woman's natural voice wins over a man's higher-tier voice; with only Standard voices the Automatic row says to download one; choosing a voice moves the check and the next read uses it; samples play and stop; uninstalling the chosen voice data falls back to Automatic (not the engine default); TalkBack reads name, quality, language and "Selected".

#### 6.7.6 Voice-note playback (messages)

iOS plays M4A with `AVPlayer` and cannot play legacy web WebM notes ("Can't play this note here yet"; the WKWebView fallback in iOS §6.7 policy 2 was never built). Android plays every note with **Media3 ExoPlayer**, which decodes both AAC/M4A and WebM/Opus natively on API 29+, so Android **plays** legacy WebM notes (proposed A15: the same feature with the platform's decoder, fulfilling the iOS PRD's own intent; §7.5.8 owns the bubble). "Can't play this note here yet" stays only for genuine playback failures. The transcript under every bubble (made by the sender's device since web #238, or by the server for web-recorded notes and older app builds; "Transcript coming" only while one can still arrive) is shown exactly as on iOS; details in §7.5.8.

**Voice-note transcription on the phone (A55; iOS `VoiceNoteTranscriber`).**

| Concern | iOS | Android |
|---|---|---|
| Engine | `SFSpeechRecognizer(locale: en-US)`, `requiresOnDeviceRecognition = true`, `addsPunctuation = true`, from the recorded file (`SFSpeechURLRecognitionRequest`) | **API 33+:** `SpeechRecognizer.createOnDeviceSpeechRecognizer(context)` (API 31) fed the recorded file through `RecognizerIntent.EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE` (API 33; a `ParcelFileDescriptor` pipe). The `.m4a` is decoded with `MediaExtractor` + `MediaCodec` to 16-bit PCM mono at the decoder's output rate (24 kHz from our recorder), written to the pipe's write end on `Dispatchers.IO`, and described with `EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE_ENCODING = ENCODING_PCM_16BIT`, `EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE_SAMPLING_RATE`, `EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE_CHANNEL_COUNT = 1`. Also `EXTRA_LANGUAGE = "en-US"`, `EXTRA_LANGUAGE_MODEL = LANGUAGE_MODEL_FREE_FORM`, `EXTRA_PREFER_OFFLINE = true`, `EXTRA_PARTIAL_RESULTS = false`, `EXTRA_ENABLE_FORMATTING = FORMATTING_OPTIMIZE_QUALITY` (punctuation; take the first, formatted hypothesis), and `EXTRA_SEGMENTED_SESSION = EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE` so pauses in a 3-minute note do not end recognition. Segment results are joined with a space, and the session ends at `onEndOfSegmentedSession`. Created, used and destroyed on the main thread, always `destroy()`ed. |
| Availability | Authorized, recognizer available, `supportsOnDeviceRecognition`; otherwise nil | `Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 33 && SpeechRecognizer.isOnDeviceRecognitionAvailable(context)`, then `checkRecognitionSupport(intent)` must list `en-US` in `installedOnDeviceLanguages`. Otherwise `null`. **Never** `triggerModelDownload` (iOS never downloads a model). **API 29–32: always `null`** (there is no file input before API 33, and recognizing from the mic while `MediaRecorder` holds it is not possible). |
| Permission | `SFSpeechRecognizer.requestAuthorization` asked before the first message recording (`prepare()`), with `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` "Gradus turns your voice messages into text right on your iPhone, so they can be read as well as heard." | **No extra permission or prompt.** Android has no speech-recognition permission; `RECORD_AUDIO`, already granted to record, is enough. `prepare()` is a no-op. |
| When | Runs while the audio uploads (`async let`), and is awaited before the send | Same: `async { transcriber.transcribe(file) }` starts before the Storage upload and is awaited before `send(...)`. The temp file is deleted only after both finish. |
| Time limit | 60 s, then nil (`OnDeviceSpeech.timeout`) | 60 s `withTimeoutOrNull`, then `cancel()` + `destroy()` → `null`. Cancellation → `null`. |
| Result | Trimmed words, or nil when empty, on error, on timeout | Same |
| Wire | `transcript` **always sent**: the words, or JSON `null` ("tried, got no words"), so the server never transcribes a phone note | Same. **Never omit the key** (an omitted key makes the server run ElevenLabs). Both `voice` and `voiceInline` bodies, including a queued inline note in the outbox, carry it. |
| Watch | Not used (the watch sends text only, #54) | Not used |

**Why `null` on Android 10–12, never a server fallback (A55).** Sending the audio without `transcript` would bring ElevenLabs back for Android senders. The shared AI permission copy then becomes untrue: the parent screen lists no voice row, and its text says voice messages are transcribed on the device. It would also need the sender's AI permission, which the server checks. A `null` matches iOS whenever on-device recognition isn't available. The cost is that notes from Android 10–12 phones carry no text alternative (§12 N79). Playback uses `USAGE_MEDIA` / `CONTENT_TYPE_SPEECH` and stops when another note starts (one note at a time, like iOS `AudioPlayer`).

---

### 6.8 Payments and entitlements

**Decision (inherits iOS #8, A10).** No Google Play Billing purchase flow, no in-app products, no Play subscriptions. Coach (Coach, Coach Pro, Club) and parent Team subscriptions are bought and managed on the web through Stripe, exactly as on iOS (iOS §6.8). The app **displays** entitlement, never sells it. The one exception to "no link" is the US link-out: on Android a plain link to the Gradus web app at gradus.training, opened in the default browser exactly like iOS's Safari link and gated as described below. Gradus does **not** enroll in Google Play's US External Content Links program, to avoid Google's fee (A37, Mariah 2026-10-14, superseding the 2026-10-13 choice to enroll); the policy risk is §11 A-27.

**The rules (iOS §6.8 rules 1–6, applied identically; Android-native mechanics in the right column).**

| # | iOS rule (iOS §6.8) | Android requirement |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Entitlement displayed, never sold: Settings → Plan shows tier, renewal or trial date, Founding Coach status, roster capacity. No price list, no "Subscribe". | Same screen and copy (§7.11 "Plan status"). No price, currency amount, "upgrade", "subscribe" or "/month" in any plan string; enforced by a unit test that iterates every `PlanCopy` case (port of `AccountTests` "No line ever names a price or asks the coach to buy", gradus-ios `Packages/FeatureSettings/Tests/FeatureSettingsTests/AccountTests.swift`). |
| 2 | Limits stated without a purchase CTA: roster cap reads "Your roster is full on your current plan." | Same string, from the `roster_full` error mapping (gradus-ios `Packages/GradusAPI/Sources/GradusAPI/APIError.swift`; also `ScheduleImportCopy.rosterFullSentence`). |
| 3 | US storefront only: "Manage your plan at gradus.training" opens Safari; any other storefront sees status with no link. | US Play country only (storefront detection below) **and** the `androidExternalLinksEnabled` kill switch on (default true): the same button label, opened in the default browser. Everyone else, and every user while the switch is off: the same plain-text line iOS shows ("Manage your plan on the web."), no link. |
| 4 | Stripe never inside the app; checkout and portal open in Safari via `UIApplication.open`, never an in-app web view. | Stripe pages open in the **default browser app** via `Intent.ACTION_VIEW` (`Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK`), never a `WebView` and never a Custom Tab (keeps it the same "leaves the app" posture as iOS's full Safari and avoids any embedded card entry). After purchase the user returns; entitlement refreshes on `ON_RESUME` (`GET /coach/billing`, `/me`) and on the Stripe-webhook data push (FCM data message, §6.6). |
| 5 | Coach invoicing is allowed in-app (real-world lesson service, 3.1.3(e)); invoices are records, no money moves. | Same. Under Google Play's Payments policy, invoices for lessons are payments for a physical/real-world service consumed outside the app, which Play Billing does not cover (verify against the current Payments policy text at submission). No money moves through the app; invoices are shared as plain text (§7.11). |
| 6 | After the Founding window (2026-11-01, `/meta/config` `foundingCoachCutoff`), with the paywall flag on, a new coach finishes onboarding then sees the plan-status screen; US gets the link, elsewhere "Finish setting up your plan on the web" with no link. Sign-up is never blocked. | Same `PlanStatusView` port (§7.11 "Plan status after onboarding"). |

**Signed-in web handoff (iOS code; TestFlight QA 2026-09-26).** Every "Manage … at gradus.training" action goes through the shell's `openWeb(url)` (gradus-ios `Gradus/Shell/AppModel.swift` `openWeb`): when signed in and the URL is one of the allow-listed pages, the app first calls `POST /api/v1/auth/web-session {next}` and opens the returned one-time URL so the browser lands signed in; on any failure, or for any other URL, it opens the plain link. Allow-list (web `src/lib/web-handoff-paths.ts`, iOS `WebHandoffPage`): `/coach/paywall`, `/coach/settings`, `/parent/team`, `/parent/settings`; scheme must be `https`, host exactly `gradus.training`, trailing slashes ignored. Android ports `WebHandoffPage` and its tests (`WebHandoffTests`: `http://`, other hosts and `/terms` resolve to no page). The endpoint is user-authenticated and rate-limited 10 per 10 minutes; no server change is needed for Android. The one-time URL is never logged.

**Every `openWeb()` target opens in a browser and never routes back into Gradus (Android-specific; cross-reference §6.10).** On Android a verified App Link fired with `ACTION_VIEW` from the app itself opens the app, not the browser. The handoff returns `https://gradus.training/auth/handoff#token=…&next=…` (web `src/lib/api/web-session-route.ts`), and the plain fallbacks (`/coach/paywall`, `/coach/settings`, `/parent/team`, `/parent/settings`) are the same URLs the deep-link table below maps to in-app Settings (iOS `AppRoute.swift` RouteParser). Without this rule, any handoff failure would turn "Manage your plan at gradus.training" into a loop back to Settings › Plan. iOS never hits this because it has no universal links yet (gradus-ios `docs/README.md` I14). Rules:
- Resolve the default browser with `packageManager.resolveActivity(Intent(ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse("https://example.com")), MATCH_DEFAULT_ONLY)` and call `setPackage(browserPackage)` on the `ACTION_VIEW` intent for the target URL. If that resolves to nothing or to the system resolver, use `Intent.createChooser` with `EXTRA_EXCLUDE_COMPONENTS` listing our own activities. If no browser exists at all, show the error toast "Something went wrong. Please try again." (verify the copy against §7.13's generic error).
- `/auth/handoff` is never claimed: the manifest declares inclusions only, on every API level, and no claimed prefix covers it (§6.10.1, §9.4 rule 6; `assetlinks.json` carries no paths). `/terms` and `/privacy` stay unclaimed the same way (§7.12 Legal).
- The same browser-pinned open is used for every "Manage … at gradus.training" link-out below and for every Stripe-bound link.
- Test (instrumented, App Links verified for the debug host): a handoff that fails for `/coach/paywall` opens the browser, not Settings › Plan; a successful handoff URL also opens the browser.

**Storefront detection on Android (A13).** iOS reads `Storefront.current?.countryCode == "USA"` (StoreKit) in each gated view's task. Android reads the **Google Play country** through Play Billing Library: `BillingClient.getBillingConfigAsync(GetBillingConfigParams)` → `BillingConfig.countryCode == "US"` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Chosen because, like the App Store storefront, it is the account's store country, which is what Play's US-only rules key on. Rejected: `Locale.getDefault()` (user-editable language setting, not a storefront), SIM/network country (`TelephonyManager`; travelers, Wi-Fi-only devices, no SIM). Rules:
- One `StorefrontRepository` (Hilt singleton) owning **one** `BillingClient`, used **only** for `getBillingConfigAsync` (no billing program is enabled, A37). Builder: `BillingClient.newBuilder(ctx)`, plus `enablePendingPurchases(PendingPurchasesParams.newBuilder().enableOneTimeProducts().build())` and a no-op `PurchasesUpdatedListener` **if** the current PBL builder still demands them (historically `build()` threw without a listener and without `enablePendingPurchases`; verify against the PBL release notes before coding). No purchase flow is ever launched. It connects lazily, caches the country for the process lifetime, and refreshes on `ON_RESUME`.
- Transient response codes (`NETWORK_ERROR`, `SERVICE_DISCONNECTED`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`) are retried **once** with backoff (reconnect first when disconnected), per Google's response-code table, before the user is treated as non-US.
- Any remaining failure (Play services missing, `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE`, timeout 5 s, not connected) yields **not US**, the same safe default iOS gets when `Storefront.current` is nil. Never "assume US".
- Exposed as `StateFlow<Boolean> isUSStorefront`, initial `false`, so a link never flashes in then out.
- US territories: Google's US external-link rules cover "the US and its territories" (verify); since A10 limits distribution to the United States, treat `"US"` only, matching iOS's `"USA"` check.

**Link-out mechanics: direct link, no External Content Links (A37, settled 2026-10-14, Mariah).**
- **What Android does in 1.0.** At every link-out site in the table below (A13's six sites), for the US Play country only (A13, `getBillingConfigAsync`), the app shows the same button iOS shows on the US storefront ("Manage your plan at gradus.training" and the other labels in the table) and opens gradus.training in the default browser through the signed-in web handoff and the browser-pinned open above, exactly like iOS's Safari link. Subscriptions are bought and managed on the website through Stripe, as today. There are no External Content Links APIs, no Google information screen, no `externalTransactionToken`, no Stripe → Play transaction reporting, no Google fees and no enrollment milestone. The Play Billing Library stays only for the `getBillingConfigAsync` country code. Android now behaves like the iPhone app on these screens; iOS does not change (Mariah, 2026-10-14).
- **Kill switch.** The `/meta/config` boolean `androidExternalLinksEnabled` (server-controlled, never compiled in, like every other flag; iOS §7.13) defaults to **true**, so the link is on at launch; setting it false removes the link without a release if Google objects. While it is `false`, **every** Android user, US or not, gets the non-US branch: the plain-text "Manage your plan on the web." / "Manage your team plan on the web." / "Finish setting up your plan on the web." lines and no button, a strict subset of iOS behavior (§12 N7). Both switch states must pass instrumented tests before release.
- **Fees.** None to Google: without enrollment there is no service fee and no transaction reporting. Stripe's own fees are unchanged.
- **Parity with iOS (A10, A2).** iOS shows the link on the US storefront (iOS §6.8 rule 3; `CoachPlanView`); Android 1.0 does the same, with no dependency beyond A13's country check and the kill switch.
- **Policy risk (Mariah's informed decision; §11 A-27).** Google Play's US payments policy requires enrollment in its program before linking US users to purchase outside Play; the court-ordered rules (Epic v. Google, §4.2) are still contested. Possible consequences: rejection of a release at review, removal of the app, or a policy strike or account suspension for repeated violations. Mitigation: the kill switch; if Google flags the link, turn it off and decide then between enrolling and staying link-free. Counsel review is recommended before submission. The review notes describe the app honestly (below).
- **The alternative if Google objects (not taken; research as of 2026-10-11, verify if revisited).** External Content Links would require: enrollment of `training.gradus.app` in Play Console; Play Billing Library 8.2.1+ with `enableBillingProgram(BillingProgram.EXTERNAL_CONTENT_LINK)`; `isBillingProgramAvailableAsync` before showing the link; a fresh `externalTransactionToken` from `createBillingProgramReportingDetailsAsync` before each link-out, then `launchExternalLink` (`CALLER_WILL_LAUNCH_LINK`) behind Google's information screen; server storage of the token with the web handoff and Stripe → Play external-transaction reporting within Google's window; and Google's fee (published at 10% on subscriptions started within 24 hours of a link tap, with reporting and payment deadlines). None of this is built for 1.0.
- Server additions (Appendix A S-15, Android-specific): `/meta/config` gains optional `androidExternalLinksEnabled` (kill switch, default true). Nothing else: `POST /auth/web-session` and the Stripe webhooks are unchanged. Web zero-disruption (§4.1): additive and optional; iOS and web paths unchanged.
- Policy risk to record (verify): Play's Payments policy forbids "leading users" to non-Play payment for digital content outside an approved program, and the text-only "Manage your plan on the web." line is arguably such a lead. iOS ships the same line for non-US storefronts (Mariah's call under iOS #8). Android keeps it for parity (A2) and lists it in §11 Risks with the fallback: drop the sentence and show status only.

**Entitlement surfaces (every one iOS has; each reads `isUSStorefront && androidExternalLinksEnabled` as "shows link").**

| Surface | iOS source | Link target | Link label (US) | Non-US / flag-off text |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Settings → Plan (coach) | `FeatureSettings/Account/CoachPlanView.swift` | `CoachBilling.manageUrl` (server sends `https://gradus.training/coach/settings`) | "Manage your plan at gradus.training" | "Manage your plan on the web." (hidden entirely for club-covered, whose `manageURL` is nil) |
| Plan status after onboarding | `FeatureOnboarding/PlanStatusView.swift` | `https://gradus.training/coach/paywall` | "Manage your plan at gradus.training" | message only (see §7.11) |
| Resource upload locked note | `FeatureResources/UploadResourceSheet.swift` (owned by §7.9) | `/coach/paywall` | same | same |
| Team plan (parent) | `FeatureSettings/Parent/TeamPlanView.swift` | `TeamPlanStatus.manageUrl` (server: `https://gradus.training/parent/team`) | "Manage your team plan at gradus.training" | "Manage your team plan on the web." |
| Team guardians locked note | `FeatureGuardians/Team/TeamPlanEntitlementNote.swift` (owned by §7.7) | `/parent/team` | "Manage your team plan at gradus.training" | "Manage your team plan on the web." |
| Sports and levels cap | `FeatureSettings/Profile/CoachSportsView.swift` | `https://gradus.training/coach/settings` | "Choose Coach Pro on gradus.training" | text cap message only (see §7.12; **iOS shows this link on every storefront; Android gates it like the rest**, an intentional divergence because Google Play's external-link rules are US-only) |

Accessibility hint on every link-out button: iOS "Opens in Safari" becomes **"Opens in your browser"**.

**Refresh and caching.** `GET /coach/billing` has no ETag and is cached **in memory only**; it is refetched on every appearance of Plan and on every `ON_RESUME` while Plan is visible (iOS `CoachPlanView` `scenePhase` comment: a founding claim/restore done on the web or another device must never show stale). A failed refetch keeps the last loaded value and shows the error only when nothing is loaded. `subscriptionEnvironment` for `POST /orgs/join` is read fresh from `GET /coach/profile`, never cached (iOS `SettingsDependencies.loadSubscriptionEnvironment`).

**Play listing and review notes (Appendix D).** State plainly in the Play Console "App access" and policy declarations: subscriptions are multiplatform, bought on the web; the app unlocks previously purchased access; no in-app purchase; coach invoices are records for in-person lessons; subscriptions are bought on the gradus.training website, and the app links US users there to manage a plan (A37). The notes describe the app as it is. Provide the demo coach, parent and minor athlete (iOS #26). Do **not** declare in-app products. Including Play Billing Library adds the `com.android.vending.BILLING` permission to the merged manifest; the Play Console declaration states that the app sells no in-app products (Appendix D item).

**Tests.** `StorefrontRepository`: US / non-US / unavailable / timeout → expected boolean. Gate truth table: (US, kill switch) × surface → link or text. A link tap opens the default browser with the handoff URL (or the plain URL when the handoff fails), never the app. Copy test: no `$`, "upgrade", "subscribe", "/month" in any plan string.

### 6.9 Live Board

**What it is (unchanged, server-side).** A public board per competition (`/board/<slug>`) built from one shared `competition_snapshots` row that the Worker refreshes from the USFS IJS results site at most every 30 s; pg_cron keeps live boards warm; one refresh serves every viewer (web, iOS, Android). Three views: **Live** (each rink: just scored, on the ice, up next), **Schedule** (a departures board of the day), **Following** (skaters the viewer follows, matched by normalized name). Viewing a board while signed in records attendance, which later drives the recap prompt (§7.10). The scraper, snapshot cache and refresh lock stay as they are; `syncBoardLiveActivities` gains a required FCM branch and `live_activity_sessions` gains a `platform` column for Android (6.9.6, a P0 server work package). (iOS §6.9; decision #4.)

**Product truth to preserve.** IJS never publishes who is currently skating. "On the ice" is inferred as the next start number after the last posted score, and scores post one to two minutes late. Android must never present "on the ice" as authoritative and must always show the data age, on every surface: the board, the ongoing notification, and the home-screen widget. (iOS §6.9 "Product truth".)

**Scope gate: figure skating only.** The Live Board entry (top-app-bar action) is shown only when `/me` `sports` contains `figure_skating`, or when `sports` is missing/unknown (fail open, never hide on missing data). A board link or QR code still opens the board for **any** account and for signed-out users. (Code wins: `MeRepository.swift` `showsLiveBoard`, Mariah 2026-09-26; `AppModel.swift` `showsLiveBoard`.)

#### 6.9.1 Entry and navigation (Android-native equivalents)

| State | iOS at HEAD | Android |
|---|---|---|
| Signed out | **No tab bar at all**: the sign-in screen only (`signedOutTabs = [.signIn]`, `Roles.swift`, Mariah 2026-09-26). A board link or QR code opens the board in the Live full-screen cover over sign-in; the board's "Sign in or sign up" button closes the cover and shows sign-in (`RootView.swift` `SignedOutTabsView`, `AppModel.open(_:)`). | Same: sign-in screen with no bottom navigation. `/board`, `/board/<slug>` App Links and `gradus://board/<slug>` open the **Live destination** full screen over sign-in. "Sign in or sign up" pops the Live destination and lands on sign-in. **Code wins over the iOS PRD §6.9 and `gradus-ios/docs/README.md` "Signed out, Live is one of two tabs"**, both stale. |
| Signed in (phone) | A **"Live" toolbar button** (icon `dot.radiowaves.left.and.right` + the word "Live", a11y label "Live Board", id `tab.live`) at the top trailing edge of **every tab root**, presenting `BoardIndexView` in a `fullScreenCover` with its own `NavigationStack`, closed by **Close** at top leading (`RoleTabsView.swift` `LiveToolbarButton`, `LiveCoverView`; Mariah 2026-09-05: so the coach's six tabs never overflow into "More"). | A **top-app-bar action** on every tab-root `TopAppBar`: an icon (Material Symbols `sensors`) plus the text "Live", content description "Live Board", test tag `tab.live`. It navigates to a **full-screen `live` nested navigation graph** (outside the bottom-nav scaffold, so the bottom bar is hidden) whose start destination is the board index. Its top app bar has a **Close** navigation icon (X, content description "Close", test tag `live.close`). System back / predictive back pops inside the Live graph first, then closes it, returning to the tab that opened it with its state intact. Bottom navigation never contains Live: coach = Roster, Plans, Resources, Messages, Settings (5); parent/athlete = Plans, Messages, Resources, Settings (4) (`Roles.swift` `tabs` minus `.live`). |
| iPad / tablet | Live is a tab on iPad regular width (`liveIsTab`), unused in 1.0 (#50). | Phones only (A4). Tablets and foldables get the phone layout, so Live is always the top-app-bar action. The tab variant is specified for later (§8) and not built in 1.0. |
| Deep link while signed in | A board route goes to the cover when Live is not a tab or the account lacks the Live entry; any other route closes the cover first so the destination is visible (`AppModel.open(_:)`). | Same: `/board*` routes open (or replace the stack inside) the Live graph; any non-board route closes the Live graph, then navigates. **Sign-in always happens with the Live graph closed**: the signed-out board's "Sign in or sign up" closes the cover and selects sign-in (`RoleTabsView.swift`: `onSignIn = { isLivePresented = false; selectedTab = .signIn }`); after sign-in the role home shows. A board deep link that arrives during sign-in is held as `pendingRoute` and opened after `/me` loads. A `BoardViewModel` is always created with the session state current at creation (`BoardDependencies.isSignedIn` and the follow mirror are captured when `BoardView` is built), so a signed-out board is never carried over into a signed-in session. |
| Opening Live | `AppModel.presentLive()`: `paths[.live] = []; isLivePresented = true`: tapping Live **always** opens at the board index, never a previously open board. | The top-app-bar Live action navigates to the `live` graph with `popUpTo(<live graph route>) { inclusive = true }` (and `launchSingleTop`), so its back stack is cleared to the index every time; no saved state is restored for the Live graph. |
| orgAdmin | `Roles.swift`: `orgAdmin.tabs = [.live, .settings]`, `homeTab = .settings`; on phone `.live` is filtered out (`visibleTabs`), so iOS shows a one-item tab bar (Settings) with the Live toolbar button (subject to `showsLiveBoard`). | Settings is the home and the only destination; **no `NavigationBar` is shown** (Material 3 navigation bars are for 3–5 destinations; a one-item bar is the Android-native divergence). The Live action sits on the Settings root `TopAppBar` under the same `showsLiveBoard` gate. |

Analytics (§6.12): the **board screen** records area `board`, screen `board` (`RouteDestinationView` `.trackedScreen(analyticsArea…)`). The **board index is untracked** on iPhone (only `TabRootView` applies `.trackedScreen(…, "tab.\(tab)")`; `LiveCoverView`'s `BoardIndexView` has none), so Android does not record a screen view for the index (parity). Recording `tab.live` for the index would be an Android addition and needs Mariah's approval (§12 N63).

#### 6.9.2 Endpoints and data

| Call | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/public/boards` | Index: live-window boards (`slug, name, datesLabel, location, isLiveWindow`) | Public, no auth. |
| `GET /api/v1/public/boards/search?q=` | Search the server's IJS catalog by name or place; a pasted IJS link or competition number is looked up at once (2026-09-26) | Public. |
| `GET /api/v1/public/boards/{slug}` | One board; send `If-None-Match` with the last `ETag`; `304` = unchanged | Public. Unknown slug → `404 not_found`. ETag is `W/"<slug>.<generatedAt>"` with non-token chars replaced by `_` (`BoardRepository.swift` `boardETag`). |
| `GET /api/v1/boards/my-skaters` | Signed in: rostered skater names for auto-follow suggestions | |
| `GET /api/v1/boards/{slug}/follows` | Signed in: what this account already follows on this board | |
| `PUT /api/v1/boards/{slug}/follows` `{names:[…]}` | Signed in: full replace, idempotent, **through the outbox** (§6.5), entity kind `boardFollows`, label = board name | `DELETE …/follows/{name}` exists but the app never calls it (iOS uses the full PUT). |
| `POST /api/v1/competitions/{id}/attendance` `{}` | Signed in, once per board session, only when the board response carries `competitionId` | Best effort, failures swallowed. `Idempotency-Key: attendance-<competitionId>-<YYYY-MM-DD UTC>` (`AttendanceRecorder.swift`). |

Wire models mirror iOS `BoardModels.swift` field for field, generated from the OpenAPI contract (kotlinx.serialization): `Board{slug,name,datesLabel,location,active,isLiveWindow,generatedAt?,error?,payload?,competitionId?}`; `BoardPayload{generatedAt,competition{name,dates,location,url},rinks[],schedule[],errors[]}`; `BoardRink{name,state: live|idle,current?,next?,justFinished?{event,winner?{name,club,score}},alsoLive[],dayEvents}`; `BoardCurrent{event,segment,status,skaters,withdrawn,done,startLabel,startIso?,url,justScored?,onIce?,upNext?,startOrder[]}`; `BoardNext{event,timeLabel,startIso?,skaters?,url}`; `BoardEvent{file,name,segment,rink,timeLabel,startIso?,status: scheduled|live|final,count?,dayLabel,dayKey,results[]}`; `BoardSkater{start,of,name,club,group,segScore,total,place,finalPlace?,segScores?[{segment,score,place}],protocol?}`; `SkaterProtocol{total,elementsScore,componentsScore,deductionsScore,elements[{planned,executed,baseValue,goe,score}],elementsTotal?{baseValue,score},components[{name,unfactored,factor}],deductions[{name,value}]}`. Kotlin property for the wire key `protocol` may stay `protocol` (not a Kotlin keyword) but name it `protocolSheet` with `@SerialName("protocol")` to match iOS naming. Unknown enum values must not crash decoding (treat an unknown rink `state` as `idle`, unknown event `status` as `scheduled`).

**Times are shown as formatted.** Every `timeLabel`, `startLabel`, `dayLabel`, `datesLabel` arrives already formatted in the rink's timezone and is displayed **verbatim**. `startIso` is used only for ordering, the default day, and countdowns ("in 12 min"), never to reformat a time. Never apply the device timezone to a board time. ISO parsing accepts JavaScript's `toISOString()` (fractional seconds, `Z`) and the plain form (`BoardModels.swift` `ISODate`).

#### 6.9.3 Pure logic (port 1:1 into `:core:data`, package `board`, JVM-unit-tested)

Port `GradusCore/Board/BoardLogic.swift` and `NameNormalization.swift` as pure Kotlin with no Android dependencies, so the board screen, the ongoing-notification planner and the widget all share them.

| Function | Rule (from iOS, which ports the web) |
|---|---|
| `normalizeName(raw)` | NFD-decompose (`java.text.Normalizer.Form.NFD`), strip **only** U+0300–U+036F, lowercase with `Locale.ROOT`, keep only `a–z` and U+0020 (tabs/newlines are removed here, before collapsing), collapse runs of spaces, trim. Must produce `expected` for **every** case in `Contract/vectors/name-normalization.json` (vendored into the Android repo's `Contract/vectors/`), including `"Ærø Søren"→"r sren"`, `"ﬁona"→"ona"`, `"Straße"→"strae"`, `"Mary\tJane\nSmith"→"maryjanesmith"`, Cyrillic/CJK → `""`. Test: a parameterized JUnit5 test over the JSON file, plus idempotence (`normalize(normalize(x)) == normalize(x)`). |
| `eventKey(name, segment, rink)` | `"<rink lowercased, trimmed>|<words>"` where words = `"$name $segment"` lowercased, split on every non-`[a-z0-9]` char, empties dropped, duplicates dropped keeping the first, joined with one space. Must pass `Contract/vectors/event-key.json`; the server derives notification keys through the same match. |
| `allEvents(payload)` | Schedule plus each rink's `current` merged by `eventKey`: if a schedule row matches and has empty `results`, fill them from `startOrder`; otherwise append a synthetic live event `file = "<rink>:<event>"`, `dayKey = startIso.take(10)`. |
| `findSkaters(payload, names)` → `SkaterMatch` | For each followed key in each event: `done` = results with a score; `ahead = start - done - 1`; state = `scored` if it has a score, else `scheduled` if event not live, else `onIce` if `ahead <= 0`, `upNext` if `ahead == 1`, else `waiting`. Sort by `sortAt` (scored = start+1e8, scheduled = start, live = start−1e8). Key `"<file>:<start>:<name>"`. |
| `liveIndex(current)` | Index of `onIce`, else `justScored`, else `upNext`, else `clamp(done, 0, count-1)`. |
| `standings(event)` | By `finalPlace` (else `place`) numeric ascending; unplaced or ≤0 last; ties by `start`. |
| `everySkater(payload)` | De-duplicated by normalized key, location `"<event> · <rink>"`, sorted case-insensitively by name. |
| `untilLabel(date, now)` | `""` / `"now"` / `"in N min"` / `"in Hh Mm"`. |
| `ordinal(n)` | `1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th…, 11th–13th`; a non-numeric string is returned unchanged. |
| `defaultDayKey(schedule, now)` | First live event's day, else first upcoming, else the last. `days()` keeps schedule order with published labels. |
| `SkaterGroup.group(matches)` | Group by name key; rows sorted by start time then start; groups ranked on-ice first, then soonest upcoming, then finished (most recent first). `accentKey` = first on-ice row, else first not-scored row. |
| `skates(ofKey, tapped, focusEventKey, payload)` | Every skate one skater has at this competition; the tapped event first, the rest in schedule order; the tapped copy's `protocol` wins when the schedule row lacks one; `officialURL` = competition `url` with its last path component removed, resolved against `event.file` (http/https only; the demo board has none). |
| `SkaterMatch.stateTag` | `"ON THE ICE"`; scored → `segScore` or `"SCORED"`; else `timeLabel` or `"TBD"`. |
| `SkaterMatch.metaParts` | `[rink, "starts <timeLabel>", "skates <ordinal start> of <of>"]` (`of` falls back to event `count`), empties dropped. |
| `SkaterMatch.spokenLine` | `"<name> scored <score>, currently <ordinal place>"` / `"<name> is on the ice at <rink>"` / `"<name> is up next at <rink>"` / `"<name>: <n> ahead at <rink>"` / `"<name> skates at <time> at <rink>"` (`"later"` when no time). |

Port the iOS test suites as Kotlin tests with the same names and fixtures: `BoardTests.swift` (demo fixture decodes 3 rinks / 11 events / all three lanes, standings, lane derivation, live index, every-skater, countdown/ordinals, days/default day, grouping, time shifting, follow/unfollow/mute/toggle rules, server-follow merge, history cap 20, event-key vectors, skates ordering) and `BoardSessionTests.swift` (listed under 6.9.5).

#### 6.9.4 Demo board

`GET /public/boards/demo` is a built-in server sample with no database. Vendor iOS's capture `GradusCore/Resources/demo-board.json` into the Android test/preview resources (the invented skater names, per #26 and the 2026-10-04 real-names rule: no real people). `DemoBoard.load(rebasedTo = now)` shifts every ISO timestamp by `now - generatedAt` and leaves published labels alone, so countdowns and "live" inference behave as if generated now. The preview repository regenerates the demo on each read older than 5 s, honors `If-None-Match` with the same ETag rule, and 404s unknown slugs. Used by Compose previews, Paparazzi/Roborazzi screenshots, and the `-GradusMock signedOut` equivalent (an Android debug launch extra) so `gradus://board/demo` works with no backend. On the demo, "Greta Halvorsen" is on the ice (`docs/README.md` I2).

#### 6.9.5 Board session behavior (`BoardSession.swift` → `BoardViewModel`)

- **Lifecycle.** First activation: load follow state from the local store, pull suggestions and server follows (signed in), then fetch. Later activations: fetch. Poll every **30 s** while the screen is at least `STARTED` (`repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED)` replaces `scenePhase`); stop on `STOPPED`; resume (with an immediate fetch) on return to foreground.
- **Fetch.** One at a time (`isRefreshing` guard). Send `If-None-Match` only when a board is already held. `304` → bump `lastFetchedAt`, clear `refreshError`, count it, no redraw. `200` → `changed = first || generatedAt differs || payload differs`; on the first success record the visit (history) and on every success try attendance (once per session). When changed: recompute matches, push follows if the set changed, re-plan ongoing notifications. (No widget snapshot: the Live Board widget was removed, #55; iOS `c8f83d6` deleted `syncBoardWidgetSnapshot`.)
- **Errors.** No board yet: `404/not_found` → phase *missing*; else phase *failed(message)* with retry (retry sets *loading*). With a board on screen: keep the data and show the non-fatal `refreshError` line.
- **Data age.** `dataTimestamp = board.generatedAt ?: payload.generatedAt ?: lastFetchedAt`. **Stale after 180 s.** Label: none → `"Not updated yet"` (no payload) or `"Updated"`; `<3 s` → `"Updated just now"`; else `"Updated 12s ago"` / `"Updated 4m ago"` / `"Updated 1h 5m ago"`; stale → `"Not updated for 4m"`. Spoken form: `"board data is 12 seconds old"` / `"… and may be stale"` / `"board data age unknown"`, appended to every lane's content description.
- **Flip detection.** Per match signature `"<state>:<ahead>:<segScore>"`; keys whose signature moved since the last recompute are `changedKeys` (row wash animates 0.7 s); the joined `spokenLine`s of moved followed matches are announced (Compose `liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite` on an off-screen-but-present node, or `View.announceForAccessibility` where not deprecated (verify on Android 16)).
- **Default tab.** `pickedTab ?: (matches.isEmpty ? Live : Following)`.
- **Selected rink.** Picked, else the first followed match's rink, else the first match's rink, else the first live rink, else the first rink.
- **Following.** `watchedNames = suggestions + manual`. `followedMatches` = matches not muted. `followedNames` (server set) = manual follows + suggestions that are on today's start orders, minus muted, de-duplicated by key, **names not keys**. Push only when the sorted set differs from the last pushed/pulled set.
- **Local follow store (device-wide).** Room database `board.db`, separate from the per-user store, **not** wiped at sign-out (follows survive sign-in/sign-out like the web's localStorage). Tables: `board_follow(id="<slug>|<key>" PK, slug, name, key, createdAt)`, `board_mute(id PK, slug, key, createdAt)`, `board_visit(slug PK, name, visitedAt)`. Rules (`BoardLocalStore.swift`): `follow(name)` = add manual (if new) and clear mute; `unfollow(key)` = drop manual, else mute; `toggle(name)` = unmute if muted, else unfollow; `mergeServerFollows(names, excludingKeys = suggestion keys)` = add as manual and lift mutes, skipping rostered suggestions; `unfollow` of a name that is both manual and suggested removes the manual follow **and** mutes it. History: newest first, upsert by slug, capped at **20**. Backup inclusion follows §6.11.
- **Score selection.** Every surface (wheel cards, lanes, Following names and rows, follow search results, event results rows) opens the **same** skater-scores sheet built by `skates(…)`; fallback to the tapped row alone (Mariah 2026-10-03).

#### 6.9.6 Ongoing notifications and Android 16 Live Updates (Live Activity equivalent)

iOS: one Live Activity per followed skater in a **live** event (Lock Screen + Dynamic Island), max **5**, ranked on-ice → up-next → just-scored → waiting → scored → scheduled; started/updated/ended by the app while foregrounded and by server push-to-start/update tokens (`BoardActivityPlanner.swift`, `BoardActivityAttributes.swift`, `BoardLiveActivity.swift`, `live-activities.server.ts`). Android equivalent:

| Aspect | Android requirement |
|---|---|
| Planner | Port `BoardActivityPlanner.plans()` exactly: live events only; dedupe on `key = "<slug>|<event.file>|<normalized skater>"`; cap 5; lane mapping `scored` → `justScored` when `ahead == -1`, else `scored`; priority onIce 0, upNext 1, justScored 2, waiting 3, scored 4, scheduled 5. `topMatch()` is not ported (it fed only the removed widget, #55). |
| Content state | Same JSON as iOS `ContentState` key for key: `lane` (`scheduled, waiting, upNext, onIce, justScored, scored, ended`), `startPosition, of, ahead, score?, place?, updatedAt` (**unix seconds**), `done`. Attributes: `activityKey, slug, competitionName, skaterName, eventName, segment, rink`. |
| Surface | One notification per plan on channel **`live_board`** ("Live Board", importance DEFAULT so promotion is allowed; `setOnlyAlertOnce(true)`, silent updates, `CATEGORY_STATUS` (an ongoing status, not a progress transfer), lock-screen visibility PUBLIC to match the iOS Lock Screen). `setOngoing(true)`. Notification id = stable hash of `activityKey`; tag = `activityKey`; extras carry `slug` and the full Attributes + ContentState JSON (`gradus.board.attributes`, `gradus.board.state`) so a later process can rebuild it. Not a group summary, not colorized, no custom `RemoteViews` (Live Update rules). |
| Android 16+ (API 36) | Build everything with **`NotificationCompat`** (androidx.core ≥ 1.17 (verify)) so one code path covers API 29–36: `setRequestPromotedOngoing(true)` (name varies by androidx.core version: `setRequestPromotedOngoing` / `EXTRA_REQUEST_PROMOTED_ONGOING` (verify)) plus `POST_PROMOTED_NOTIFICATIONS` (normal permission) for a **Live Update** status-bar chip; `setShortCriticalText(score ?: "#<start>")` (verify name; chip shows ≤ ~7 chars); check `NotificationManager.canPostPromotedNotifications()`; if the user disabled Live Updates, the notification still posts as a normal ongoing one. Promotion requirements: ongoing, a content title, no custom content view, not colorized, style ∈ {none, `BigTextStyle`, `CallStyle`, `ProgressStyle`}. Optionally `NotificationCompat.ProgressStyle` with `done/of` progress and a tracker at `startPosition` (verify API shape). Below API 36 the compat calls are no-ops: a standard ongoing notification with `BigTextStyle`. |
| Copy | Title: skater name. Text: lane label + `" · <event · segment> · <rink>"`. Lane labels verbatim from iOS: `SCHEDULED`, `"<n> AHEAD"` (`"1 AHEAD"`), `UP NEXT`, `ON THE ICE`, `JUST SCORED`, `SCORED`, `FINAL`. Score lane shows the score and the ordinal place (else `"#4 of 12"`); otherwise `"#<start>"` and `"of <of>"`. Sub-text: competition name. The `onIce` content description reads `"On the ice, inferred from the last posted score"`. Data age: `setWhen(updatedAt)` + `setShowWhen(true)`; and an "updated … ago" line. |
| Staleness | iOS sets `staleDate = updatedAt + 180 s` and the system tints the age label. Android: `setWhen(updatedAt * 1000)` + `setShowWhen(true)` so the system ticks the relative time with no app work. For the "may be stale" marker, **one coalesced** inexact `AlarmManager.set(RTC, earliest(updatedAt) + 180 s, …)` (or a main-thread `Handler` while the process lives) re-posts every live-board notification whose state has not changed since with the age line text "may be stale" in attention ink (no colorized background). No WorkManager job per notification. **Accepted deviation:** with the app killed or under Doze the stale marker can appear late; the system-ticked `when` time is always correct. |
| Tap | `contentIntent` → `MainActivity` with route `board/<slug>` (the iOS `widgetURL` `gradus://board/<slug>`); opens the Live graph on that board. |
| End | When a plan disappears: re-post with lane `ended` (`FINAL`), `setOngoing(false)`, `setTimeoutAfter(15 min)` (iOS `dismissalPolicy .after(15 min)`). |
| Adopt existing (process death, server start) | Port `LiveBoardActivityController.adoptExisting()` (`BoardActivityPlanner.swift`), which iOS calls before every `sync`, before `endAll`, and on `beginTokenReporting`. Android: before each sync, rebuild the active set from `NotificationManager.getActiveNotifications()` filtered to channel `live_board` (`notification.channelId`) and `tag = activityKey`, reading Attributes + ContentState back from the extras. Notifications posted by a previous process or by an FCM `board_activity` message are thus adopted. Plans missing from the new set are **ended** (lane `ended`/`FINAL`, `setOngoing(false)`, `setTimeoutAfter(15 min)`); a plan already posted is re-posted **only when its ContentState differs** from the posted one (iOS: `if existing.content.state != plan.state { update }`). Sign-in/out never calls end-all (see Sign-out). |
| User dismissal | `setDeleteIntent` records the key as dismissed for this process; it is not re-posted until its key changes (iOS: a dismissed activity is not re-requested by the running app). |
| App-driven updates | `BoardViewModel` syncs plans on every changed fetch and follow change while the board screen is visible (iOS fallback "app-driven while foregrounded"). |
| Server-driven (background) | **Required 1.0 server deliverable (P0, same milestone as the board; Appendix A work package "FCM board_activity sender").** iOS 1.0 starts, updates and ends the Live Activity from the server with the app closed (iOS §6.9 "Started by push-to-start from the server when the event goes live"; QA.md §7: "Live Activity for a followed skater starts from a push without the app open, updates on scores, ends with the event"). Under A2 Android must do the same. App-driven-only is an interim dev state, **not shippable** for 1.0. The current `syncBoardLiveActivities` (`src/lib/live-activities.server.ts`) cannot carry this unchanged: it returns `skipped: "no_config"` when `apnsConfigFromEnv()` is null before any follower lookup; its targets come from `live_activity_tokens` (`board_start`/`board_update`), not `device_tokens`; and `live_activity_sessions` is `UNIQUE (user_id, activity_key)` and upserted `onConflict: "user_id,activity_key"` (the row is the lock), so an iPhone and an Android phone on one account would share one row and one platform's start would suppress the other's. Work package: **(1)** split the sender so the FCM branch runs when FCM credentials exist even if APNs config is absent, and vice versa (`skipped: "no_config"` only when **both** are missing); **(2)** migration: `ALTER TABLE live_activity_sessions ADD COLUMN platform text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ios' CHECK (platform IN ('ios','android'))`, drop `UNIQUE (user_id, activity_key)`, add `UNIQUE (user_id, activity_key, platform)`, upsert `onConflict: "user_id,activity_key,platform"`, with the `GRANT ALL … TO service_role` and RLS-enabled/no-policy state restated in the same migration; **(3)** FCM targets = `device_tokens` rows with `platform = 'android'` for each follower (the token from `POST /devices`, §6.6; no separate push-to-start token); **(4)** an FCM HTTP v1 sender in the Worker: service-account JSON as a Worker secret, OAuth2 access token from a signed JWT (cached until expiry), message `{"data":{"gradus":"{\"type\":\"board_activity\",\"v\":1,\"action\":\"start|update|end\",\"attributes\":{…},\"state\":{ContentState}}"}}` (FCM data values are strings), `android.priority = "HIGH"`, `android.ttl` = `"10800s"` start / `"600s"` update / `"3600s"` end (matching `START_/UPDATE_/END_EXPIRY_SECONDS`), `android.collapse_key = activityKey`; **(5)** prune `device_tokens` rows on FCM `UNREGISTERED` (404) or `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for the token (400), like APNs `dead` pruning of `live_activity_tokens`. Tests mirror `live-activities.server.test.ts` for the Android branch (APNs-only, FCM-only, both, two platforms on one account each get their own session row, dead-token pruning). Client: `GradusMessagingService.onMessageReceived` parses `board_activity` and posts/updates/ends via the same notifier with no app UI. **Acceptance (copied from QA.md §7):** with the app swiped away from Recents (not force-stopped), following a skater in a live event yields a notification that starts from a push, updates on each score, and ends (`FINAL`, auto-dismiss after 15 min). |
| FCM delivery limits | Every `board_activity` data message must post, update or end a **visible** notification when permission is granted (never a silent no-op), otherwise FCM deprioritizes the app's later high-priority messages. FCM does not deliver to a **force-stopped** app: a user who force-stops Gradus gets no server-started board notifications until the next launch (accepted platform difference; iOS push-to-start works regardless). When `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` is not granted, the handler drops the message (no work), and the server cannot tell; accepted. |
| Permissions | iOS Live Activities are governed by `ActivityAuthorizationInfo().areActivitiesEnabled` (on by default, no prompt), independent of push authorization; Android 13+ has no equivalent, so a user who declined push would otherwise get **no** board surface. Android-native fix: the **first time** a user follows a skater, or opens the Following tab while following a skater in a live event, on Android 13+ with `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` not granted, show an **inline card at the top of the Following tab** (copy to be approved by Mariah, §12 N62; suggested title `"Get live updates for your skaters"`, body `"Allow notifications to see when they're up next, on the ice, and scored, even with Gradus closed."`, button `"Allow notifications"`, dismiss X). The button launches the system permission request (`ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission`); if the permission is permanently denied (`shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale == false` after a prior denial), it opens app notification settings (`Settings.ACTION_APP_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS`). Shown to **signed-out viewers too** (follows are device-wide). Never blocks following. Dismissing it hides it until the next follow. Below Android 13, no card (permission is install-time). When not granted, planning still runs and posting is a no-op. |
| Sign-out | Do not end notifications or wipe board follows (iOS `endTokenReporting` only unregisters tokens). Device FCM token handling per §6.6. |
| Wear OS | Not a 1.0 board surface (the Apple Watch app has no board, iOS §6.15). Android may bridge Live Updates to some Wear devices automatically; accepted, no work. |

Tests: planner (only live, ranking, cap 5), JSON round-trip of `ContentState` against an iOS-encoded fixture (unix-seconds `updatedAt`), notifier posts/updates/ends with the right ids (Robolectric `ShadowNotificationManager`), FCM payload handling; **adoption**: with active `live_board` notifications pre-seeded as if from a previous process, a sync ends those no longer planned and does not re-post unchanged ones; permission card shown/not shown per API level and grant state.

#### 6.9.7 Home-screen widgets (#55): Practice goals and Today (Glance; WidgetKit `GoalWidget` and `CoachTodayWidget` equivalents)

There is **no Live Board home-screen widget** (#55; gradus-ios #158). The followed-skater ongoing notification and Live Update (§6.9.6) are the board's only surfaces outside the app. The two widgets below replace it in package 3.8 and milestone K15. They live here, beside the old board widget's place, because §6.9.7 was the PRD's widget section. They are not board features. iOS sources: `GradusWidgets/GoalWidget.swift`, `CoachTodayWidget.swift`, `WidgetBackend.swift`, `GradusCore/Widgets/GoalWidgetLoader.swift`, `CoachTodayLoader.swift`, `WidgetSessionHandoff.swift`, `GradusWidgetData/GoalWidgetSnapshot.swift`, `CoachTodaySnapshot.swift`.

**Shared mechanics (A56).**

| Aspect | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Widgets | Two `GlanceAppWidget`s in `:widgets`, both offered in the launcher's widget picker to everyone: **"Practice goals"**, description "Practice this week against the coach’s target, and what it’s building towards." (receiver `PracticeGoalsWidgetReceiver`), and **"Today"**, description "Today’s lessons, with each athlete’s practice this week." (receiver `CoachTodayWidgetReceiver`). Each is **one size**, the iOS `systemMedium` equivalent: `targetCellWidth = 4`, `targetCellHeight = 2`, `minWidth = 250dp`, `minHeight = 110dp`, `resizeMode = "none"` (iOS offers medium only; §12 N82). `SizeMode.Single`. `updatePeriodMillis = 0` (refresh is the WorkManager job below). |
| Session | The widgets run in the app process (Glance `provideGlance` runs inside `training.gradus.app`), so they use the app's own `SessionManager` and token refresher, behind its mutex. **Android does not mint a widget session with `POST /auth/companion`.** iOS mints one only because its widget extension is a separate process and Supabase refresh tokens are single-use. One process means one refresher, so there is no race (A56). The widget reads only when the stored widget account's `userId` equals the session's user id; otherwise it shows the signed-out state. |
