| Account stamp | After every `/me` (the iOS `AppModel.refreshGoalWidget` call), the app writes `WidgetAccount{userId, role ∈ parent \| athlete \| coach}` to DataStore `widget_snapshots`. Any other role, or no role, clears the store. A different `userId` or role first clears the old snapshots. Then the app builds the role's snapshot (Practice goals for parent and athlete, Today for coach) with the same loader the job uses, writes it **only if the stamp still matches**, and calls `updateAll` on both widgets. |
| Background refresh | One unique periodic WorkManager job, `widget-refresh`: 30-minute period (the iOS timeline `.after(30 min)`), `NetworkType.CONNECTED`, `ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP`. It is enqueued from each receiver's `onEnabled`/`onUpdate` and after sign-in. It is cancelled in `onDisabled` once neither widget has an instance (`GlanceAppWidgetManager.getGlanceIds` empty for both), and at sign-out. Each run loads the role's snapshot and writes it only if the account stamp is unchanged after the load ("signed out while this ran: don't bring the old account back"). **A failed load keeps the last snapshot.** Today additionally skips the network when its snapshot is under 5 minutes old (iOS: "a page turn re-runs the timeline"). |
| Storage | DataStore `widget_snapshots` (JSON, kotlinx.serialization, tolerant decoding: missing fields default, as iOS's `init(from:)` does, so older snapshots still read). It is device-wide, excluded from Auto Backup and device transfer (A24), and **cleared at sign-out** and on an account switch, followed by `updateAll`. A signed-out phone never shows the last account's data. |
| Taps | Explicit-component `PendingIntent`s (`FLAG_IMMUTABLE`) to `MainActivity`, with data `gradus://plans/<planId>`, `gradus://plans` or `gradus://coach/roster/briefing/<athleteId>`, parsed by the one `RouteParser` (A27, §6.10.2). They are never broadcast actions (§6.11.5). |
| Fonts and colors | System families only (Glance `FontFamily.Serif` for display, `SansSerif` for body, `Monospace` for mono; §12 N67). Gradus tokens through `ColorProvider(day, night)`, never dynamic color (§8.2). |
| Rings and bars | Glance cannot draw arcs. The Today rings are rendered to a `Bitmap` with `android.graphics.Canvas` at the device density and shown with `Image(ImageProvider(bitmap), contentDescription = null)`, with the node's own content description carrying the meaning. Week bars are `Box`es with computed heights. Keep the total bitmap size under the RemoteViews limit (4 rings of 58 dp; well under the limit, test on API 29). |
| Previews | Android 15+: generated previews (`setWidgetPreview`, verify the API) from the iOS preview snapshots below. API 29–34: a static `previewLayout` / `previewImage` rendered from the same data. Invented names only. |
| Accessibility | Every tappable element has `GlanceModifier.semantics { contentDescription = … }` with the iOS VoiceOver text verbatim (below). Targets ≥ 48 dp. Text follows the system font scale (Glance `sp`). |

**Practice goals (parents and athletes; iOS "B1 · Week bars", Mariah 2026-10-13).**

- **Data** (`GoalWidgetLoader`):
  - Parent: `GET /parent/goals` and `GET /parent/plans`. Athlete: `GET /athlete/goals` and `GET /athlete/plans`. Both are fetched in parallel, without `If-None-Match`.
  - Then `GET /plans/{id}/sessions?limit=50` for each **active** plan of the people shown (a parent: the first two children in goals order), in parallel. A plan whose log fails adds nothing.
  - Per person: `dayMinutes[7]`, Monday first. Each session's `loggedAt` falls in this ISO week (Monday start, device time zone) and adds `round(durationSeconds / 60)` minutes to its day.
  - `weekTarget` is the **lower** bound of the coach's band from the first sport goal (`GoalStatus.band`: `min(hoursAtCurrent, hoursAtGoal)`, using whichever exists). It is null when neither exists.
  - `workingTowards` is the season-goal level label from the sport catalog, null when unset.
  - `firstName` is the first word of the name. `todayIndex` runs 0 (Monday) to 6.
  - A coach account gets an empty snapshot.
- **Views:**
  - Signed out: "Sign in to Gradus to see practice goals."
  - Empty people list (including a coach): "No practice goals yet."
  - **One person:** the caption "<First>'s practice this week". The headline is "Target met" when the hours to go are ≤ 0, "<h> hr to go", or "<h> hr so far" when there is no target. "<logged> of <target> hr" sits at the trailing end, only when there is a target. Hours use one decimal when not whole ("2.5", "6"; iOS `PracticeRing.hoursText` after rounding to 0.1). Below that, the week bars at 44 dp with day letters "M T W T F S S", today's letter underlined and in primary ink. Then "Working towards <level>" when set.
  - **Two people:** compact rows separated by a divider. Each row has the caption, then the headline with "  <logged> of <target> hr" in caption size, "Working towards <level>", and mini bars 40 dp tall and 120 dp wide with no letters.
  - Bars: a day with minutes is a bar in `accent`, with height `max(4dp, height × minutes / max(60, max(dayMinutes)))`. A day with nothing is a hairline, in `divider` for days up to today and `elevated` after.
  - Never a pace hint, never a move list.
- **Tap:** the whole widget (one person) or each row (two people) opens `gradus://plans/<first active plan id>`, else `gradus://plans`.
- **TalkBack:** the bars read "Logged: Monday 60 minutes, Wednesday 90 minutes" or "No practice logged yet this week". The text is read as written.
- **Preview data** (iOS `GoalWidgetSnapshot.preview`): Greta, plan "Juvenile — Free Skate", `dayMinutes [60,0,90,0,0,0,0]`, target 6, "Intermediate", today = Wednesday.

**Today (coaches; iOS "B·c · Rings", Mariah 2026-10-13).**

- **Data** (`CoachTodayLoader`):
  - `GET /coach/up-next?lessonDate&dayOfWeek&currentMinute&limit=20`, using the device's local date, weekday and minute. Keep only today's lessons.
  - For each distinct athlete: `GET /coach/athletes/{id}` (weekly target = the first `practiceTargets[].hoursPerWeek` when > 0; active plan ids).
  - Then `GET /plans/{id}/sessions?limit=50` per active plan. `weekMinutes` = this ISO week's summed `durationSeconds / 60`, rounded.
  - All per-athlete reads run in parallel. A failed one leaves that athlete without target or minutes rather than failing the widget.
  - Each lesson: `{id, athleteId, firstName, start, end}`, with start and end at local midnight of `lessonDate` plus `startMinute` and `endMinute`, sorted by start.
- **Views:**
  - Signed out, or the account isn't a coach: "Sign in to Gradus as a coach to see today’s lessons."
  - No lesson left (`end > now`): "No more lessons today."
  - Otherwise, a header row with "Today" at the start and, at the end: "<First> now" once the next lesson has started, "next in <n> min" within the hour (minutes rounded up), or "next at <time>".
  - Then **four rings at a time**. Each is a 52 dp ring of the athlete's week as a percent of the target, with "<n>%" in the middle, or hours and "HR / WK" when there is no target. The athlete's first name and the time sit under it ("3:30" in a 12-hour locale, "15:30" in a 24-hour one, no AM/PM). The next lesson's ring has a 1.5 dp `textPrimary` circle and its time in primary ink. Empty slots keep the four rings the same size.
  - **Tone:** no target → `textDisabled`; 0 minutes → `attention` (orange); ≥ 100 % → `accent`; else `secondaryAccent`.
  - Footer: "Rings show practice this week, toward each athlete’s target" (one line, shrinks to 75 %). When there are more than four lessons, ‹ › buttons with content descriptions "Earlier lessons" / "Later lessons" are disabled at the ends.
- **Paging:** ‹ › is `actionRunCallback<CoachTodayPageAction>` with parameter `step = ±1`. It writes `coachTodayPage = max(0, page + step)` to the store and calls `update`. The page is clamped to `[0, pages − 1]` at render. Writing a new snapshot resets the page to 0 (iOS `writeCoach`).
- **Rolling on without a fetch** (A57): iOS hands WidgetKit a timeline with an entry as each lesson ends and one each minute within the hour of the next lesson. Glance has no timeline. After every render, the widget schedules **one inexact, non-wakeup alarm** (`AlarmManager.set(RTC, …)`; no exact-alarm permission). It fires at the earliest of: the next whole minute when the next lesson starts within 60 minutes, the next lesson's end, or now + 30 minutes. The alarm re-renders from the stored snapshot with no network. Alarms are cancelled at sign-out and when the last Today widget is removed.
- **Tap a ring:** opens `gradus://coach/roster/briefing/<athleteId>`, the lesson-reminder route: the Roster root with that athlete's Up next briefing (§7.2.8, the 10-minute rule).
- **TalkBack per ring:** "Next: Greta at 3:30 PM, 1.5 of 6 hours practiced this week. Opens the briefing." The "Next: " prefix appears only on the next lesson. Without a target the practice part reads "no weekly target set". The time is in the locale's short form.
- **Preview data** (iOS `CoachTodaySnapshot.preview`): Greta 90 min of 6 h, Liam 0 of 4, Ava 180 of 4, Noor 60 of 4, Mae 240 of 4, Iris 30 of 3. The first lesson starts 25 minutes from now, the rest follow at 45-minute steps.

**Offline.** Both widgets show the last snapshot when a refresh fails or there is no network. They never show an error state.

**Tests:**
- Builder unit tests ported from `GoalWidgetTests` and `CoachTodayTests`: week boundaries Monday to Sunday in the device zone; minutes per day; target = lower band; two children only; a coach gets an empty snapshot; lessons only for today; tones; next text; page clamping; snapshot reset to page 0.
- Store: round-trip, tolerant decoding, cleared at sign-out, an account mismatch reads as signed out.
- Job: a mismatch after the load does not write; a failure keeps the old snapshot.
- Alarm planner: the next fire time for each case.
- Glance screenshot tests (`glance-appwidget-testing`): one person, two people, signed out, empty, and Today with 1, 4 and 6 lessons, in light and dark at font scale 1.0 and 1.3.
- An instrumented check that taps open the right `RouteParser` route.

#### 6.9.8 QR codes at the rink

iOS has **no in-app scanner**. The rink sign's QR encodes `https://gradus.training/board/<slug>`; the system camera opens it as a universal link, and the index copy says so verbatim: `"Search for any U.S. Figure Skating competition, or scan the QR code on the sign at your rink with your camera."` (`BoardIndexView.swift`). Android parity: the Pixel Camera app / Google Lens reads the code and opens the verified App Link (§6.10: `/board` and `/board/*` in the manifest's `autoVerify` intent filter, verified through `assetlinks.json`) straight into the Live graph. Same copy. No in-app scanner in 1.0 (an ML Kit Google code scanner button would be an addition, not parity; §12 N66). If App Links are not yet verified (assetlinks needs the signing-certificate SHA-256, and the Play App Signing key does not exist until the Play Console account exists, A8), the code opens the web board in the browser; list both the upload key and, later, the Play App Signing key fingerprints in `assetlinks.json` (§6.10). Typing the code from the sign works in the index search (6.9.9).

#### 6.9.9 Accessibility and motion (iOS §6.9 "Accessibility", §8.5)

- "Reduce Motion" → Android "Remove animations" (`ValueAnimator.areAnimatorsEnabled() == false` or animator duration scale 0): no wheel spring, no live-dot pulse, no segmented-pill slide; state changes apply instantly.
- Every lane has a content description including the data age; rink tabs read `"<rink>, live|idle"`; the segmented control exposes tabs (`Role.Tab`, `selected`), group label "Board view"; rinks group label "Rinks".
- "Increase contrast" → Android contrast setting (`UiModeManager.contrast`, API 34+ (verify)): lane cards use the opaque popover fill instead of the paper-under-card fill.
- Dynamic Type → font scale: wheel slots grow with the tallest measured card.
- All colors from the accessibility-audited Gradus tokens (§8): live indicators use `attention` only.

### 6.10 Deep links and App Links

**Sources.** iOS §6.10; gradus-ios `Packages/GradusCore/Sources/GradusCore/Routing/AppRoute.swift` (`AppRoute`, `RouteParser`), `Gradus/Shell/AppModel.swift` (`open(url:)`, `open(_:)`, `openInvite`, `completeVerification`, `confirmEmailChange`, `presentRecovery`, `openWeb`), `Gradus/Shell/RootView.swift`, `Gradus/Info.plist` (`CFBundleURLTypes` → `gradus`), `Gradus/Gradus.entitlements` (`applinks:gradus.training`, `webcredentials:gradus.training`), `Packages/GradusAPI/Sources/GradusAPI/RecoveryLink.swift`, `Packages/GradusCore/Sources/GradusCore/Onboarding/ConsentModels.swift` (`VerificationRedirect`), `Packages/GradusCore/Sources/GradusCore/Repositories/WebSession.swift`; tests `RoutingTests.swift`, `WebHandoffTests.swift`, `RecoveryLinkTests.swift`; web `src/lib/apple-app-site-association.ts`.

#### 6.10.1 What the app claims

Android claims **exactly** the paths the iOS AASA claims (`UNIVERSAL_LINK_PATHS`), as verified App Links on `https://gradus.training`. Everything else on the host opens in the browser, which covers every iOS exclusion (`UNIVERSAL_LINK_EXCLUDES`: `/reset-password`, `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/support`, `/unsubscribe`, `/admin`, `/org-admin`, `/api/*`, `/email/*`, `/lovable/*`) because none of them falls under a claimed prefix. Android's manifest has no exclusion syntax before Android 15's dynamic App Links, so the claim is written as inclusions only (verify that no included prefix ever grows an excluded child; a test asserts the two lists stay disjoint).

| Path (AASA) | Manifest `<data>` | Handling (same as iOS) | Session needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/board`, `/board/*` | `path="/board"`, `pathPrefix="/board/"` | Live Board index; `/board/<slug>` that board | No |
| `/i/*` | `pathPrefix="/i/"` | Invite entry; code uppercased, normalized (`InviteCodeText.normalize`), must be complete or toast "That invite code isn't valid." | No |
| `/login` | `path="/login"` | Sign in (signed out); ignored signed in | No |
| `/signup/*` | `pathPrefix="/signup/"` | `/signup/coach`, `/signup/parent`, `/signup/athlete`, `/signup/athlete/adult`; anything else → Sign in. Signed in → toast "You're already signed in." | No |
| `/coach`, `/coach/*`, `/parent`, `/parent/*`, `/athlete`, `/athlete/*` | `path` + `pathPrefix` with trailing slash for each (so `/coaches` is not claimed) | Role subpaths (table 6.10.2); unknown subpath → role home | Yes |
| `/g/*` | `pathPrefix="/g/"` | Guardian claim | Yes |
| `/team/*` | `pathPrefix="/team/"` | Guardian team invite | Yes |
| `/p/*` | `pathPrefix="/p/"` | Shared plan preview and import | Yes |
| `/verified`, `/verified/*` | `path="/verified"`, `pathPrefix="/verified/"` | KWS signed redirect → `POST /guardian/verification/complete` (§6.13) | No |
| `/auth/confirm` | `path="/auth/confirm"`, `path="/auth/confirm/"` | Email code exchange: `type=recovery` → reset flow; `type=email_change` → confirm (§6.4) | No |
| `/auth/apple/done` (Android only, not in the AASA) | `path="/auth/apple/done"` | Apple web-flow return: hands `handoff` and `state` to the sign-in model (§6.4); never a screen of its own | No |
| `/` (bare host) | **not claimed** (AASA does not claim it either) | Opens the web; iOS notes the email footer link `https://gradus.training` therefore opens the web (handoff-2026-10-09 §"Footer link") | — |

Manifest (in `MainActivity`; one filter for App Links, one for the scheme):

```xml
<intent-filter android:autoVerify="true">
  <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
  <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
  <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
  <data android:scheme="https" android:host="gradus.training" />
  <data android:path="/board" />          <data android:pathPrefix="/board/" />
  <data android:pathPrefix="/i/" />
  <data android:path="/login" />
  <data android:pathPrefix="/signup/" />
  <data android:path="/coach" />          <data android:pathPrefix="/coach/" />
  <data android:path="/parent" />         <data android:pathPrefix="/parent/" />
  <data android:path="/athlete" />        <data android:pathPrefix="/athlete/" />
  <data android:pathPrefix="/g/" />
  <data android:pathPrefix="/team/" />
  <data android:pathPrefix="/p/" />
  <data android:path="/verified" />       <data android:pathPrefix="/verified/" />
  <data android:path="/auth/confirm" />   <data android:path="/auth/confirm/" />
  <data android:path="/auth/apple/done" />  <!-- Android-only Apple web-flow return, §6.4, S-7 -->
</intent-filter>
<intent-filter>
  <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
  <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
  <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
  <data android:scheme="gradus" />
</intent-filter>
```

`http://gradus.training` is not claimed (iOS `RouteParser` returns nil for `http`).

**`assetlinks.json`** is server addition **S-10** (§6.2, Appendix A): `https://gradus.training/.well-known/assetlinks.json`, `application/json`, no redirect, two statements for `android_app` / `training.gradus.app`: `delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls` and `delegate_permission/common.get_login_creds` (the `webcredentials:gradus.training` equivalent, so Credential Manager can offer passwords saved for gradus.training). `sha256_cert_fingerprints` = Play App Signing certificate + upload certificate. **Until the Play Console exists (A8)** the file carries the upload certificate only, which verifies sideloaded release builds signed with the upload key; the Play App Signing fingerprint is added the day Play App Signing is enrolled, before the first Play build reaches a tester. Debug builds (debug keystore) are not listed: on a dev device, links are enabled with `adb shell pm set-app-links-user-selection --user cur --package training.gradus.app true all`. Never publish a placeholder fingerprint (the iOS AASA rule, 2026-09-24). A server unit test (like `apple-app-site-association.test.ts`) asserts both statements and that the fingerprints are well-formed.

**Verification failure behavior.** On Android 12+, an unverified `https` link opens in the browser; the user can still enable links in Settings › Apps › Gradus › Open by default. QA checks `adb shell pm get-app-links training.gradus.app` shows `verified` for `gradus.training` on the Pixel.

#### 6.10.2 Route table (`RouteParser` port)

Kotlin `sealed interface AppRoute` with the same cases and the same `tab` and `requiresSession` mapping, and `object RouteParser` with `route(uri)`, `route(fromPath)`, and the push variant (`data` map with `v == "1"`). Ported line for line from `AppRoute.swift`; `RoutingTests.swift` cases are ported verbatim to JUnit as the acceptance test (proposed: move them into a shared `Contract/vectors/routes.json` so both apps run the same vectors; §12).

Parsing rules (identical to iOS):
- `gradus://host/rest` → path `"/" + host + rest`, trimmed of slashes (Android `Uri.host` + `Uri.path`, same join). `https` requires host `gradus.training` (case-insensitive). Any other scheme or host → not ours (return `false` so the caller lets the system handle it).
- `/verified` (trimmed) → `.verified(VerificationRedirect)` parsed from the **raw percent-encoded query** with form decoding (`+` is a space, then percent-decoding), first `status`, first `externalPayload`, every `signature`; missing any → not ours. The query is forwarded exactly as received; nothing is re-serialized (the HMAC covers `status:externalPayload`).
- Excluded prefixes (the path equals it or starts with it plus "/") → not ours, even via `gradus://`: `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/unsubscribe`, `/admin`, `/org-admin`, `/api`, `/email`, `/lovable`, `/reset-password`.

| First segment | Result |
|---|---|
| none (`/`) | `.roleHome` |
| `board` | `/board` → `.boardIndex`; `/board/<slug>` → `.board(slug)` |
| `i` | `/i/<code>` → `.invite(code.uppercase())`; `/i` → not ours |
| `login` | `.login` |
| `signup` | `coach` → `.signup(.coach)`; `parent` → `.signup(.parent)`; `athlete` → `.signup(.athlete)`, `athlete/adult` → `.signup(.adultAthlete)`; anything else → `.login` |
| `g`, `team`, `p` | with a token → `.guardianClaim` / `.teamInvite` / `.sharedPlan`; without → not ours |
| `coach`, `parent`, `athlete` | role subpath: `messages[/<id>]` → `.rooms`/`.room(id)`; `plans[/<id>]` → `.plans`/`.plan(id)`; `roster` → `.roster`, `roster/briefing[/<athleteId>]` → `.upNextBriefing(athleteId?)`; `resources` → `.resources`; `settings[/<section>]` → `.settings(section?)` (`account` and every `SettingsSection` raw value; unknown → `.settings(null)`); `paywall` (with any query, e.g. `?tier=coach_pro`) → `.settings(.plan)`; `wrap-ups` → `.wrapUps`; anything else → `.roleHome` |
| `rooms` | `.rooms` / `.room(id)` (scheme and push only; not claimed as an App Link) |
| `plans` | `.plans` / `.plan(id)` (scheme and push only) |
| `recaps` | `/recaps/<competitionId>` → `.recap(id)`; bare → not ours (scheme and push only) |
| `settings` | `.settings(section?)` (scheme and push only); `SettingsSection` = `account`, `plan`, `connections`, `athletes`, `coaches`, `goals`, `device`, `legal`, `feedback`, `safe-sport` |
| anything else | not ours |

`AppRoute.editPlan(id)` exists for in-app navigation only; no link or push opens it (iOS comment in `AppRoute.swift`).

**Routed destination titles** (iOS `RouteDestinationView.title`, `Gradus/Shell/RoleTabsView.swift`; Android `TopAppBar` title, small/center style matching iOS `.inline`):

| Route | Title |
|---|---|
| `.board` | "Live board" |
| `.room` | "Conversation" |
| `.plan`, `.editPlan` | "Plan" |
| `.recap` | "Competition recap" |
| `.settings(.connections)` | "Connections" |
| `.settings(section)` (any other) | "Settings · *section raw value*" (e.g. "Settings · safe-sport"), verbatim including the raw value |
| `.guardianClaim` | "Guardian claim" |
| `.teamInvite` | "Team invite" |
| `.sharedPlan` | "Shared plan" |
| anything else | "Gradus" |

The claim and invite **token never appears** in the bar, the window title, a TalkBack label, or a log ("possession of the link is the claim's only proof", iOS comment). Test: a `/g/<token>` route's semantics tree contains no node whose text includes the token.

**Routed settings sections by role** (iOS `SettingsSectionView`, `RoleTabsView.swift`; the same screens the Settings rows push, over the same shared ViewModels):

| `SettingsSection` | Coach | Parent | Athlete |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | Account & security | same | same |
| `plan` | Coach plan (`CoachPlanView`) | Team plan (`TeamPlanView`) | Not for this account: "Plans are managed by your coach or parent." |
| `athletes` | Not for this account: "My athletes is a parent screen." | My athletes (`ParentAthletesView`) | Not for this account: "My athletes is a parent screen." |
| `coaches` | Not for this account: "Coaches is an athlete screen. Parents link coaches from My athletes." | same message | Coaches (`AthleteCoachesView`) |
| `goals` | Not for this account: "Goals belong to parents and athletes." | Goals screen (`GoalsScreen`) | Goals screen |
| `connections` | Connections hub (`ConnectionsHubView`) | Team plan (`TeamPlanView`) | Not for this account: "Connections are managed by your coach or parent." |
| `device` | Device (`DeviceView`) | same | same |
| `legal` | Licenses (`LicensesView`) | same | same |
| `feedback` | Normally handled by `open(_:)` (Settings root with the feedback sheet, 6.10.4); reached directly, the Settings root with the sheet open | same | same |
| `safe-sport` | Safe Sport (`SafeSportView`) | same | same |

The "Not for this account" state is the full-bleed `StateView` on the paper background: icon = the iOS `person.crop.circle.badge.questionmark` mapped through §8's icon table (a person-with-question-mark glyph), title "Not for this account", message as above, **no button**. Role is decided as iOS does it: parent = a parent model exists; athlete = an athlete model exists; Goals = the sessions goals model exists (parents and athletes); coach = `role == coach`. While the local store is still opening, the coach Connections row shows the placeholder "Connections" / "Preparing your local store…" and any section shows "Settings" / "Preparing your local store…" (iOS `PlaceholderScreen`).

Tabs: `board*` → Live (on phones always the Live cover, §7.10, mirroring iPhone); `room`, `rooms` → Messages; `plans`, `plan`, `editPlan`, `sharedPlan`, `recap` → Plans; `roster`, `upNextBriefing`, `wrapUps` → Roster; `resources` → Resources; `settings`, `guardianClaim`, `teamInvite` → Settings; `login`, `signup`, `invite`, `roleHome`, `verified` → no tab. `requiresSession` is false only for `boardIndex`, `board`, `login`, `signup`, `invite`, `verified`.

#### 6.10.3 Intercepts before `RouteParser` (in order)

`AppModel.open(url)` on Android, called from `onCreate` (cold) and `onNewIntent` (warm) for `ACTION_VIEW` intents and from notification taps:

1. **`gradus://reset-password#access_token=…&refresh_token=…&type=recovery[&expires_in=…]`** (legacy fragment form): parsed by `RecoveryLink` (fragment only; requires `type=recovery` and both tokens non-empty; `expires_in` default 3600). Valid → reset flow (§6.4). Invalid → not ours. The `https://gradus.training/reset-password` page stays in the browser (excluded).
2. **`https://gradus.training/auth/confirm?token_hash=…&type=recovery|email_change`** (`EmailLinkConfirmation`: `https` only, host `gradus.training`, path `auth/confirm` with or without trailing slash, non-empty `token_hash`, known `type`; `gradus://auth/confirm` is rejected). `recovery` → reset flow; `email_change` → confirm, then toasts verbatim: "Your email is updated." (signed in) or "Confirmed. If we also emailed your other address, open that link too." (first of two confirmations); offline → "You're offline. Open the link again once you're connected."; any other failure → "That link has expired or was already used. Change your email again in Settings › Account." A final confirmation that signs in a different account than the one on screen runs the account switch (6.6.6 item 6); one that arrives signed out enters the signed-in state.
3. Otherwise `RouteParser.route(uri)`. On nil, iOS `open(url:)` returns false and the app simply stays where it was. Android:
   - **nil `https://gradus.training/…` link** (a claimed prefix that does not parse, e.g. `/g/`, `/team/` or `/p/` with an empty token, `/i/` with no code): open the **same URL in the browser** with an explicit browser package (6.10.5, so the App Link does not bounce back into Gradus), so the page still opens. If the activity was started only for this link (cold start with no prior task), finish it after handing off; otherwise stay where the app was.
   - **nil `gradus://` link:** show the app as launched (cold start → the normal launch; warm → stay on the current screen). No toast, no browser.
   - Test: a cold `https://gradus.training/g/` intent opens the browser (fake resolver) and leaves no blank Gradus activity; a warm `gradus://nonsense` leaves the current tab and path unchanged.

#### 6.10.4 Signed out vs signed in (iOS `AppModel.open(_:)`)

| Situation | Behavior |
|---|---|
| App still launching (session not restored yet) | Route stored in `pendingRoute`; delivered after launch settles. An invite during launch is stored as `.invite(code)`. |
| Signed out, public board route | Opens in the Live cover over Sign in (`paths[.live] = [route]` or `[]` for the index); the board's own "Sign in" button closes the cover. |
| Signed out, `.login` | Selects Sign in. |
| Signed out, `.signup(kind)` | Sign-up stack: coach → `[chooser, coach]`; parent → `[chooser, parent]`; athlete → `[chooser, athleteChooser]`; adult → `[chooser, athleteChooser, adultAthlete]`. |
| Signed out, `.invite(code)` | `[chooser, invite(code)]` on the Sign in stack. |
| Signed out, `.verified` | Completed without a session; a signed-out parent watching a board keeps the board. Toast "Thanks, you're verified." or, on `ok == false`/not verified, "That verification link couldn't be confirmed. Check your email for a newer one, or resend it from the app."; errors toast the API message. Then the verification signal fires and, if signed in, `/me` refreshes. |
| Signed out, a route that needs a session | Waits in `pendingRoute`; the Live cover closes so Sign in is visible. For `/g/…` and `/team/…` the Sign in screen shows the hint "Use the email address this link was sent to." |
| Signed in, `.signup` | Toast "You're already signed in." |
| Signed in, `.invite` | Coach (onboarded) claims at once (parent invite, then adult-athlete invite, with idempotency keys `<key>-parent` / `<key>-adult`): "Linked to the parent's account" / "Linked to the athlete's account" / API message or "Couldn't claim that invite."; coach mid-onboarding, or parent/athlete with an onboarding gate → stash, "Invite noted. It links when you finish setting up."; parent → Settings › My athletes with the code pre-filled, athlete → Settings › Coaches with the code pre-filled, both toast "Link the coach from here with their code."; org admin or role-less → "Invite codes are for coach, parent, and athlete accounts." |
| Signed in, role-less account, `/g/…` or `/team/…` | Stashed in `pendingLinkRoute` and rendered by the role-chooser screen, not refused. A device age signal under 18 drops it (§6.13). |
| Signed in, route into a tab the role lacks | Toast "That page isn't available for your account." |
| Signed in, `.settings(.feedback)` | Settings root with the feedback sheet open. |
| Signed in, `.roleHome` (bare `/`, `gradus://`, or an unknown `/coach/*`, `/parent/*`, `/athlete/*` subpath) | **No-op**: `.roleHome` has no tab (`guard let tab = route.tab else { return }`), so the app stays on the current tab and path. Signed out, it is a session route and waits in `pendingRoute` like the next row, then is a no-op once signed in. |
| Signed in, but `/me` failed with nothing cached (`meLoadError != nil`) | Any session route waits in `pendingRoute` (`guard let summary = me, meLoadError == nil`) and is delivered when "Try again" (`retryLoadMe()`) succeeds and `apply()` runs. |
| Claim or team-invite screen › "Switch account" (`switchAccount(returningTo:)`) | Clears `pendingLinkRoute`, runs the **full sign-out** (6.6.6 item 4, analytics flush and clear, store wipe), then sets `pendingRoute` to the same `/g/…` or `/team/…` route and selects Sign in, so the hint "Use the email address this link was sent to." shows and the link resumes after the next sign-in. Test: signed in as A on `/g/<token>`, Switch account, sign in as B → the same claim screen opens for B. |
| Any route into a tab | Closes the Live cover first. |
| Biometric lock up | The route is applied underneath; the lock stays (6.6.7 for the single-`MainActivity` rule). |

#### 6.10.5 Links the app opens (outbound)

iOS opens gradus.training pages in Safari, signed in where the web allows (`openWeb`, `WebHandoffPage`: `/coach/paywall`, `/coach/settings`, `/parent/team`, `/parent/settings`, via `POST /auth/web-session` → `/auth/handoff#…`), else the plain link. Android does the same, and must stop its own App Links from bouncing the page back into the app: every outbound gradus.training URL is opened with an explicit browser target (resolve the default browser for `https://` with `queryIntentActivities` and set the package; §6.8 uses no Custom Tab). `/auth/handoff` is not a claimed path, and in-page redirects from it to `/coach/paywall` stay in the browser (verify on Chrome and Samsung Internet; QA item). Stripe Checkout and the billing portal always open outside the app (CLAUDE.md "Never move Stripe checkout or the billing portal into the webview").

### 6.11 Security and privacy

**Sources.** iOS §6.11, §4.2, §6.4 "Session and device security"; decisions #19, #23, #32, #46, #48; gradus-ios `Gradus/Info.plist`, `Gradus/Gradus.entitlements`, `Gradus/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`, `Packages/GradusCore/Sources/GradusCore/BiometricGate.swift`, `Gradus/Shell/LockWindow.swift`, `Packages/GradusDesign/Sources/GradusDesign/Components/AppLock.swift`, `Packages/FeatureAuth/Sources/FeatureAuth/LockScreenView.swift`, `Packages/GradusCore/Sources/GradusCore/Errors/{ErrorReporter,MetricKitCollector}.swift`; tests `BiometricGateTests.swift`, `LockWindowTests.swift`, `ErrorReporterTests.swift`; `docs/ios/app-store-submission.md` §4.

#### 6.11.1 Transport

- **HTTPS only.** `res/xml/network_security_config.xml`: `cleartextTrafficPermitted="false"` in `base-config`, trust anchors = **system CAs only** in release (the default since API 24; no user-installed CAs). A `debug-overrides` block (debug builds only) trusts user CAs and a `domain-config` permits cleartext for `localhost` only (the local API is reached through `adb reverse`, §9.6), the counterpart of the iOS `NSExceptionDomains › localhost` ATS exception. TLS 1.2+ is the OkHttp/Conscrypt default.
- **No certificate pinning** (iOS §4.2, §6.11: Cloudflare rotates gradus.training certificates about every 90 days). No `<pin-set>`, no OkHttp `CertificatePinner`. The mitigation is the CAA record at DNS (shared with iOS).
- No `usesCleartextTraffic`, no WebView anywhere in the app (iOS has none).

#### 6.11.2 What the app ships

Only the Supabase URL and publishable key, the Google **web** OAuth client ID used as Credential Manager `serverClientId` (proposed A18; the Android counterpart of the iOS client ID), the Firebase `google-services.json` values (project id, app id, an API key restricted in Google Cloud to the Firebase installation and FCM APIs for package `training.gradus.app` and its signing certificates), and the Play Integrity cloud project number (proposed A21). Everything else stays server-side (iOS §6.11 "Secrets"). Values come from Gradle properties/CI secrets into `BuildConfig`, never committed for production builds.

#### 6.11.3 Storage at rest

| Data | iOS | Android |
|---|---|---|
| Session tokens | Keychain, `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly` | Tink-AEAD-encrypted DataStore with an Android Keystore master key, no user-auth requirement (§6.4 owns). Not backed up (proposed A24). |
| Offline store (Room + snapshot files) | SwiftData with `NSFileProtectionCompleteUntilFirstUserAuthentication` | `noBackupFilesDir/Gradus/<userId>/` (`store.db` and the JSON snapshots, §6.5) in credential-encrypted storage, which is unavailable until first unlock after boot: the same guarantee. The app is **not** `directBootAware`. |
| Usage-analytics buffer | `Application Support/usage-analytics.json`, complete-until-first-auth protection | `noBackupFilesDir/usage-analytics.json` (6.12) |
| Pending crash reports | (MetricKit holds them) | `noBackupFilesDir/crash-reports/` (6.11.8) |
| Cached PDFs, images, voice notes | `Caches` (purgeable) | `cacheDir` (purgeable by the system) |
| Preferences | `UserDefaults` (appearance, biometric lock, pending sign-up, remembered sign-in email, coach-visibility banner) | DataStore (Preferences); same keys as iOS where a key name exists (`gradus.appearance`, `gradus.security.biometricLock`) |
| Sign-out | Wipes the store and Keychain | Wipes Room, session, per-user caches, the analytics buffer (after a final flush). Delivered notifications stay, as on iOS (6.6.6). |

**Backup (proposed A24).** `android:allowBackup="true"` is kept only so the proposed A24 allow-list of non-sensitive preferences can be backed up; `res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml` (API 31+) and `res/xml/backup_rules.xml` (API 29–30, `fullBackupContent`) **exclude** the session DataStore, the Tink keyset preferences, the Room database, `noBackupFilesDir` contents, and caches, for both cloud backup and device transfer. Keystore keys never leave the device anyway, so an encrypted file restored without its key would be unreadable; excluding it also guarantees a restored install starts signed out. Test: Robolectric parses both XML files and asserts every sensitive path is excluded.

#### 6.11.4 Biometric app lock

A local convenience lock, not an auth mechanism; the session stays valid whether or not the lock is on (iOS §6.4; `BiometricGate`). §6.4 specifies the `LockActivity` presentation; this section fixes the rules every implementation must pass.

| Rule (iOS source) | Android requirement |
|---|---|
| Opt-in per device; key `gradus.security.biometricLock`; default off (`BiometricGate.isEnabled`) | DataStore boolean, same key; device-level, not per account |
| Turning it off unlocks at once (`isEnabled = false` sets `isLocked = false`) | Same |
| Lock at launch when a session exists (`lockOnLaunch()` after `session.restore()`) | Same. A cold start after process death is a launch. A push or link that cold-starts the app also locks first. |
| Relock only after **≥ 30 s** in the background (`relockAfter = 30`); not configurable in the UI | `ProcessLifecycleOwner` `ON_STOP` records `backgroundedAt` (elapsed realtime, not wall clock); `ON_START` locks if enabled and ≥ 30 s passed. Fixed 30 s (`docs/ios/QA.md` mentions "the chosen delay"; code has no choice, code wins). |
| Each trip to the background counts once; the app's own prompt returning does not relock (`willEnterForeground` clears `backgroundedAt`) | `backgroundedAt` is cleared on every `ON_START`. A `ON_STOP`/`ON_START` pair caused by the device-credential screen while an unlock is in flight is ignored. |
| Backgrounded during the prompt → still locked on return (`BiometricGateTests`) | Same (port the five `BiometricGateTests` cases: relock after threshold, not inside it, no relock after own prompt, backgrounded during prompt stays locked, off never relocks) |
| Unlock policy `.deviceOwnerAuthentication` (biometrics, falling back to passcode) | **Settled here (technical choice, not a §12 item):** `BiometricPrompt` with authenticators `BIOMETRIC_STRONG or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` on API 30+, and `BIOMETRIC_WEAK or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` on API 29, where `BIOMETRIC_STRONG or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` is unsupported (androidx.biometric docs; verify at build). Both allow biometrics plus PIN/pattern/password, the `.deviceOwnerAuthentication` behavior. Availability uses the **same set**: `BiometricManager.canAuthenticate(<same authenticators>) == BIOMETRIC_SUCCESS`. §6.4, §7.12 and §8 must use exactly this rule (one `LockAuthenticators.forSdk(Build.VERSION.SDK_INT)` function shared by the prompt and the availability check). |
| Prompt reason "Unlock Gradus"; cancel title "Not now" | Title "Unlock Gradus". With `DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` allowed, Android forbids a custom negative button, so the system's cancel is shown; "Not now" cannot appear (verify). |
| Cancel by user/app/system clears the error; any other failure shows `localizedDescription` under the title | `ERROR_USER_CANCELED`, `ERROR_CANCELED`, `ERROR_NEGATIVE_BUTTON` clear the message; other errors (`ERROR_LOCKOUT`, `ERROR_LOCKOUT_PERMANENT`, `ERROR_HW_UNAVAILABLE`, …) show `errString` |
| Lock screen: icon, "Gradus is locked", error line, "Unlock", "Sign out" (bottom); the prompt starts automatically on appear | Same copy and order; the prompt auto-starts when the lock appears; "Sign out" runs the full sign-out from under the lock, dismissing whatever the app had up without animation, before the lock fades (`signOut()` comment) |
| Sign-out resets the preference (`reset()`), so the next account starts unlocked | Same |
| Availability: `canEvaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthentication)`; toggle disabled otherwise with "Set up Face ID, Touch ID, or a passcode in iOS Settings to use this." | `BiometricManager.canAuthenticate(<same authenticators>) == BIOMETRIC_SUCCESS`; disabled text "Set up a fingerprint, face unlock, or a screen lock in Android Settings to use this." |
| Settings label "Unlock with Face ID" / "Unlock with Touch ID or passcode"; footer "A convenience lock for this device. Your account still signs in with your password or Apple ID." | Label "Unlock with fingerprint, face, or screen lock" (Android cannot tell which biometric is enrolled); footer "A convenience lock for this device. Your account still signs in with your password, Google, or Apple." (platform-noun substitution, proposed A25; §7.12 owns the screen) |
| Covers every presentation (sheets, alerts, the Roster's "*name*'s lesson just ended." alert) and leaves each where it was (`LockWindow.swift`) | `LockActivity` (§6.4) is above every dialog and bottom sheet of `MainActivity`; nothing is dismissed. |
| While locked the app leaves the accessibility tree; keyboard goes down; the focused field keeps its draft **uncommitted** and gets focus back on unlock (`isAppLocked`, `commitsOnFocusLoss`) | `MainActivity` content is behind another activity, so TalkBack cannot reach it; the IME closes. A `LocalAppLocked` flag (true from the moment the gate locks until `MainActivity` is resumed again) feeds a `Modifier.commitsOnFocusLoss(focusRequester, commit)` that does **not** commit when focus is lost to the lock and re-requests focus on unlock. Every inline-edit field iOS marks this way (Roster athlete weekly hours, plan editor `InlineField`) uses it. Test: a cleared weekly-hours field interrupted by the lock does not save 0. |
| A screen's own prompts wait while the lock (or Terms gate, reset cover, Live cover) is up (`PromptHold.covered`) | Same `PromptHold` composition local; prompts queued, not dropped |
| Back while locked | Moves the task to the background (`moveTaskToBack(true)`); never reveals the app; predictive-back preview disabled on the lock |
| Watch | No lock (iOS watch `BiometricGate` is inert); Wear OS likewise has no app lock (§6.15) |
| One window (`LockWindow.swift`) | `MainActivity` is `singleTask`; `LockActivity` shares its task, is not `noHistory`, and is restarted after any `onNewIntent` while locked; `MainActivity` draws an opaque placeholder while `isLocked` (6.6.7) |
| Reply on a message notification needs an unlocked device (`.authenticationRequired`), and the category has no Reply while the lock is on (`BiometricGate.onEnabledChange` re-registers it; #54) | `setAuthenticationRequired(true)` on the Reply action (Android 12+; no Reply on 10–11); no Reply while `isEnabled`; on every change, active room notifications are re-posted with or without it (§6.6.11) |

**Lock tests (port of `Tests/GradusTests/LockWindowTests.swift`, six cases, plus Android-specific ones).** Instrumented (Compose UI + Espresso, Pixel emulator):
1. **Covers dialogs without dismissing them:** an `AlertDialog` (e.g. the Roster's "*name*'s lesson just ended." alert) and a `ModalBottomSheet` open at relock stay open under `LockActivity` and are still there, in the same state, after unlock (iOS: "Locking covers the window and its alert…").
2. **Hidden from TalkBack while locked:** with TalkBack semantics enabled, no node of `MainActivity` is focusable while locked; only "Gradus is locked", the error line, "Unlock" and "Sign out" are; after unlock, accessibility focus and live-region announcements return to `MainActivity` (iOS: "…hides both from VoiceOver" and "Turning the lock off, or taking it down… gives VoiceOver the window back").
3. **Locked before content exists:** a cold start from a push or App Link with the lock enabled shows the lock before **any** content frame (no flash; screenshot of the first frame is the placeholder or the lock) (iOS: "Locked before the anchor finds its window: the lock appears once it does").
4. **Rapid toggles apply the latest state once:** lock → unlock → lock in quick succession ends locked with exactly one `LockActivity`; unlock → lock → unlock ends unlocked with none (iOS: "A quick lock, unlock, lock ends locked, and the reverse ends unlocked").
5. **System UI launches from the app, not the lock:** while locked, a Play Age Signals request, a Credential Manager call or a runtime-permission request started by the app is launched from `MainActivity`'s `ActivityResultRegistry`/context (it waits under the lock or is held by `PromptHold`), never from `LockActivity`'s, so finishing the lock does not cancel it (iOS: "While locked, Apple's age-range sheet presents from the app's window, not the lock's").
6. **Field keeps its draft:** a focused weekly-hours field cleared to empty and interrupted by the lock does not save 0, keeps its text, and regains focus after unlock (iOS: "A field the lock interrupts keeps its draft, unsaved, and gets the focus back on unlock").
7. **Turning the lock off** in Settings › Device while a relock is pending removes any `LockActivity` and restores accessibility (iOS case 6, second half).
Plus the five `BiometricGateTests` ports above (JVM, fake clock) and the 6.6.7 single-`MainActivity` push test.

**Screenshots, app switcher and `FLAG_SECURE`.** gradus-ios has no privacy snapshot or blur: the app switcher shows the last screen, and screenshots and screen recording are allowed everywhere. Android mirrors this: **no `FLAG_SECURE`** on any window and `setRecentsScreenshotEnabled` left at its default. Whether to hide the Recents thumbnail while the lock is on (Android 13+ API) is a new product choice for both apps and is listed in §12, not built.

**Tapjacking (proposed, Android-only hardening with no visible difference).** The lock screen's "Unlock" and "Sign out", and the account-deletion confirmation (§7.12), set `filterTouchesWhenObscured` so an overlay from another app cannot click through them.

#### 6.11.5 Exported surface and intents

- Exported activities: `MainActivity` (launcher, App Links, `gradus://`) only. `GlanceAppWidgetReceiver` subclasses are `exported="true"` with **only** the `android.appwidget.action.APPWIDGET_UPDATE` intent filter (the launcher requires it); widget taps use Gradus's own explicit `PendingIntent`s, so no custom action is accepted from outside. Every other activity, receiver, service and provider (`LockActivity`, `GradusMessagingService`, `NotificationReplyReceiver`, the "Still practicing?" alarm receiver, WorkManager components, the `FileProvider` used for sharing) is `exported="false"`. The phone's and the watch's `WearableListenerService` are exported only through the Data Layer intent filters Google Play services requires. The Wear `GradusComplicationService` is exported only to holders of `BIND_COMPLICATION_PROVIDER`, and the Wear `NotificationReplyReceiver` and complication-boundary alarm receiver are `exported="false"` (§6.15.7, §6.15.8). A manifest lint test asserts this list.
- **`gradus://` is not exclusive on Android.** Any app can declare the `gradus` scheme, and the system then shows a chooser, so session material must never travel in a `gradus://` URL. Recovery and email-change emails use only `https://gradus.training/auth/confirm?token_hash=…` (a verified App Link; web `src/lib/auth-confirm-link.ts` already builds only this `https` form, and iOS stopped sending `client: "app"` on `POST /auth/recover`, `FeatureAuth/SignInModel.swift`). Android likewise **never sends `client: "app"`**, and `gradus://reset-password` must stay off the Supabase Auth redirect allow-list (`APP_RECOVERY_REDIRECT_URL`, `src/lib/api/auth-recover-route.ts`). The legacy `gradus://reset-password#access_token=…` form is still parsed for parity (6.10.3 item 1) but no server email may generate it. Push taps and widget taps use explicit-component intents, never a resolvable `gradus://` `VIEW`.
- Inbound `VIEW` intents are trusted for nothing but their URI, decoded only by 6.10.3; extras are ignored except Gradus's own notification-tap extra. Every `PendingIntent` is `FLAG_IMMUTABLE`.
- Permissions this section adds: `INTERNET`, `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE`, `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`, `USE_BIOMETRIC`, `POST_PROMOTED_NOTIFICATIONS` (Android 16 Live Updates, proposed A12; normal permission, verify). Feature permissions (microphone, camera, foreground service types) are owned by their sections.

#### 6.11.6 Minors, UGC, account deletion, impersonation

Unchanged from iOS §6.11 and applied identically:
- Athlete accounts created by parents sign in by username and are never asked for an email; the 13–17 self-sign-up takes the teen's email plus a parent email and is provisional until a verified guardian claims (§6.13).
- Minors send text only (#32); plans by voice are off for under-18 or no-birthdate athletes (#48): every athlete voice control is hidden unless `/me` sends `athleteVoiceToPlan == true` (missing = off), and the server answers 403 `text_only` regardless.
- No ads SDKs, no tracking, no advertising ID (`com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID` is **removed** from the merged manifest with `tools:node="remove"`, and Play's advertising-ID declaration says "no").
- Report and block one tap away in every room and on every visible profile; blocked users' messages hidden client-side at once (§7.5).
- Account deletion two taps from Settings with the impact preview and confirmation phrase, including Apple token revocation for Apple-linked accounts (§7.12, §6.4).
- The API rejects admin impersonation tokens on `/api/v1`; impersonation stays web-only.

#### 6.11.7 Logging

No PII and no token values in logs (iOS "Screenshots and logging"). Debug logging goes through one `GradusLog` wrapper whose release implementation is empty, plus R8 `-assumenosideeffects` on `android.util.Log.v/d/i` so release builds carry no debug log calls. `StrictMode` (thread and VM policies, penalty log) runs in debug builds only.

#### 6.11.8 Error reporting (MetricKit → Android equivalent)

iOS: every caught error surfaced as an error toast, plus MetricKit crash and hang diagnostics on the next launch, go to `POST /api/v1/errors`, best-effort, no third-party crash SDK (iOS §6.11; `ErrorReporter.swift`, `MetricKitCollector.swift`, `AppModel.start()`). Android (proposed A19 in §0, applying iOS §6.11 and #19 through A2):

| Piece | iOS | Android |
|---|---|---|
| Reporter | `LiveErrorReporter` actor: never throws; dedupes the same `kind|route|first 200 chars of message` within 60 s; caps a process session at 50 reports; on a transport failure (offline) gives the slot and the dedupe entry back | `ErrorReporter` (coroutine `Mutex`-guarded), identical rules and constants. Port `ErrorReporterTests` (body fields, caps, dedupe, transport failure retried later, crash build overrides running build). |
| Body | `message` ≤ 4000, `stack` ≤ 16 000, `route` ≤ 1000, `kind` `error|crash|hang`, `appVersion`, `build`, `osVersion`, `device`, `occurredAt` ISO-8601, `metadata` (string map); keys sorted | Same JSON. `appVersion` = `versionName` (e.g. `1.0.0`), `build` = `versionCode`, `osVersion` = `Build.VERSION.RELEASE` (e.g. `16`), `device` = `"<MANUFACTURER> <MODEL>"` ≤ 64 (iOS sends the machine id, e.g. `iPhone18,2`). Header `X-Gradus-Client: android/<version>+<build>` so the server tags `platform=android` (S-4). Bearer attached when signed in; the route is public so a sign-in-screen crash still lands. |
| Caught errors | `ToastCenter.onError` → `report(message, metadata: ["surface": "toast"])` for every `.error` toast, **except** connectivity notices (prefix "You're offline." or "Can't reach Gradus right now.") | Same hook on the Compose `ToastCenter` |
| Crashes | MetricKit `crashDiagnostics` next launch: message "exception … · signal … · code … · reason", condensed attributed-thread stack (≤ 200 frames, `binary +offset uuid`), `kind: crash`, `occurredAt` = payload end, `build` = the crashing build | `Thread.setDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler` wrapper writes `{message = "<ExceptionClass>: <message>", stack = stackTraceToString() (cause chain, ≤ 16 000), kind = crash, occurredAt = now, build = versionCode, metadata.appBuild = versionCode of the crashing build}` with **no route** (MetricKit crash reports carry none) atomically to `noBackupFilesDir/crash-reports/<uuid>.json`, then **chains to the previous handler** (so the system and Play vitals still see the crash). Uploaded and deleted on the next launch after `start()`. |
| Native crashes | (inside MetricKit) | `ActivityManager.getHistoricalProcessExitReasons` (API 30+): `REASON_CRASH_NATIVE` → `kind: crash`, message "Native crash", stack = the tombstone description when `getTraceInputStream()` provides one (API 31+), truncated |
| Hangs | MetricKit `hangDiagnostics`: "Hang for *n.n* s", `kind: hang` | `REASON_ANR` → `kind: hang`, message "App not responding" + `description`, stack = the main thread section of the ANR trace from `getTraceInputStream()`, condensed to ≤ 200 frames / 16 000 chars |
| Build metadata | `MetricKitCollector.reports` sets `metadata["appBuild"] = crash.applicationVersion` (and the same for hangs) and `build` = the crashing build | Every crash, ANR and native report sets `metadata.appBuild` and `build` to the **crashing** build's `versionCode`, not the uploading one. For `ApplicationExitInfo`, the app records its `versionCode` at process start with `ActivityManager.setProcessStateSummary(...)` (API 30+) and reads it back from `getProcessStateSummary()` on the exit record; if absent, `metadata.appBuild` is omitted rather than guessed. |
| Caught-error context | Toast-sourced reports carry `metadata["surface"] = "toast"` and **no route** (`AppModel.start()`) | Same: toast reports send no `route` (parity). Adding the route to both apps is a §12 question. |
| Dedup across launches | MetricKit delivers each payload once | The newest processed `ApplicationExitInfo.timestamp` is stored in DataStore; only newer exits are reported. On API 29, only the uncaught-handler path exists (ANRs are seen in Play vitals only). |
| Performance metrics | Ignored (`didReceive(_: [MXMetricPayload])` empty) | None collected |
| Obfuscation | n/a (symbolicated later from `binary +offset uuid`) | Release builds are R8-minified; CI keeps `mapping.txt` per `versionCode` as a build artifact (and uploads it to Play once A8 exists); `metadata.mappingId` = the R8 map id so stacks can be retraced by hand |
| Third-party SDKs | None | None: **no Crashlytics, no Sentry** (iOS §6.11 "no third-party crash SDK", #19; proposed A11, A19). Play Console Android vitals is the second source once A8 exists. |

#### 6.11.9 Privacy manifest → Play Data safety

The iOS privacy manifest declares `NSPrivacyTracking = false`, no tracking domains, `UserDefaults` API reasons `CA92.1`/`1C8F.1` (no Android equivalent needed), and the collected types below. The Play Console **Data safety** form gets the same facts in Google's categories. Answers apply to the phone and Wear OS app together (one listing, A3). For every row: **shared with third parties: No** (processors acting for Gradus, such as hosting, email, ElevenLabs transcription for coach and adult voice, KWS, are service providers, which Play does not count as sharing (verify current wording)); **processed ephemerally: No**; **required or optional** as noted.

| iOS manifest type (linked, not tracking) | Why | Play category → data type | Purpose(s) | Required? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Name | Profiles, athlete name | Personal info → Name | App functionality, Account management | Required |
| Email Address | Sign-in; guardian email for under-18 athletes | Personal info → Email address | App functionality, Account management | Required (username athletes have none) |
| User ID | Account id | Personal info → User IDs | App functionality, Account management | Required |
| Other Data Types (athlete date of birth) | Age rules, consent | Personal info → Other info | App functionality | Required for athletes |
| Device ID (APNs token, App Attest key id) | Push; attestation | Device or other IDs → Device or other IDs: the **FCM registration token** and the **Firebase Installation ID** that FCM auto-init creates (Play Integrity carries no stable id); not shared | App functionality | Optional (push) |
| Audio Data | Voice notes; voice plan capture (adults and coaches only, #32, #48) | Audio → Voice or sound recordings | App functionality | Optional |
| Photos or Videos | Coach schedule-import photos | Photos and videos → Photos | App functionality | Optional |
| Other User Content | Messages, plans, notes, goals, Ask Gradus questions | Messages → Other in-app messages; App activity → Other user-generated content | App functionality | Optional |
| Fitness | Practice duration, after-session flow check-in | Health and fitness → Fitness info | App functionality | Optional |
| Purchase History | Subscription status read from the web purchase | Financial info → Purchase history | App functionality | Optional |
| Product Interaction (purpose Analytics) | Screen time, Resources events (6.12) | App activity → App interactions | **Analytics** | Collected for every account under the sign-up consent (#46); not user-toggleable in app |
| Crash Data | Crash reports | App info and performance → Crash logs | App functionality (Analytics is not selected; mirrors iOS) | Required (automatic) |
| Performance Data | Hangs | App info and performance → Diagnostics | App functionality | Required (automatic) |
| Other Diagnostic Data | Caught error reports | App info and performance → Other app performance data | App functionality | Required (automatic) |

**Privacy policy URL** (required in the Play listing and the Data safety form): `https://www.gradussports.com/privacy`, the same published policy the iOS privacy manifest header and App Store listing name (`Gradus/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`).

Not collected (as iOS §4 "Not collected"): phone number, address, location, contacts, web browsing, **in-app search history** (only a result count is sent, never the query), installed apps, health (non-fitness), financial account info, calendar, SMS, advertising ID. **Security section:** data encrypted in transit: Yes. Users can request deletion: Yes, in app (Settings › Account & security › Delete account) and at `https://gradus.training/delete-account` (S-16), which Play requires for apps with account creation (verify). Conservative over-declaration is deliberate, as on iOS ("over-declaring is safe, under-declaring gets apps pulled"). The Data safety answers live in a new `docs/android/play-submission.md` §Data safety, kept in step with this table and `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`, and are entered before the first build that collects each type reaches a tester. Families/target-audience questions are Appendix D's.
