### 6.12 Usage analytics

**Sources.** iOS §6.12, decisions #19 and #46; gradus-ios `Packages/GradusCore/Sources/GradusCore/Analytics/{UsageAnalytics,TrackedScreen}.swift`, `Gradus/Shell/RoleTabsView.swift` (`TabRootView.analyticsArea`, `RouteDestinationView.analyticsArea`), `Gradus/Shell/AppModel.swift` (`startAnalyticsFlushing`, `scenePhaseChanged`, `signOut`, `switchAccount`), `Gradus/Dependencies.swift`, `Packages/FeatureResources/Sources/FeatureResources/{ResourceViewerSheet,LibraryView,AskGradusView,AskAnswerContent}.swift`, `Packages/FeatureSettings/Sources/FeatureSettings/Athlete/SafeSportView.swift`; `Contract/vectors/analytics-events.json`; test `UsageAnalyticsTests.swift`; web `src/lib/analytics.server.ts`.

**Same endpoint, same table, same rules.** Android sends to `POST /api/v1/analytics/events` (authenticated, ≤ 64 KB, ≤ 100 events). Everything server-side in iOS §6.12 applies unchanged: role and age band derived server-side; **minor athletes stored with `user_id = null`**, `subject = minor_athlete`, club/region only for groups of ≥ 10 minor athletes; withdrawn accounts (`analytics_opt_outs`) get `accepted: 0` with a 2xx; retention per iOS §12 #21; Usage report in the admin panel gains a platform filter only if Mariah asks. The one server change is **S-2**: `analyticsBatchInput.platform` widens from `z.enum(["ios"])` to include `"android"` (until it ships, every Android batch is a 400, which the client drops; so S-2 must be published before the first collecting build reaches a tester). **No Firebase Analytics or any SDK**; nothing is sent to Google.

**Consent (#46).** No in-app analytics switch on Android either. Consent is part of accepting the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy at sign-up (the acceptance line names both, §7.1); withdrawal is by email to support@gradussports.com and handled by hand on the admin user page. The tracker keeps an `isEnabled` hook that is always `true` in the app (for tests and a future server flag). Settings › Device has no usage-data toggle (`DeviceView` comment).

**Allow-list** (`Contract/vectors/analytics-events.json`, vendored into the Android repo's `Contract/` and asserted by a unit test exactly like `UsageAnalyticsTests.namesMatchTheContractAllowList`):

| Event | Props allowed | Emitted by (iOS → Android) |
|---|---|---|
| `screen_time` | none (`durationMs`, `capped` are envelope fields) | `TrackedScreen` on every tab root and routed screen |
| `resource_open` | `kind`, `origin`, `sport` | Resource viewer on appear: `kind` = resource kind raw value, `origin` = `"library"` if no coach name else `"coach"` (iOS sends no `sport`; Android matches) |
| `resource_read` | `depth`, `pages` | Resource viewer on close: `durationMs` = time open (capped 30 min, `capped`), for PDFs `pages` = page count and `depth` = min(1, furthest page ÷ page count). No 1 s floor here (iOS `recordRead`). |
| `resource_share` | none | Share action tapped in the viewer (Android share sheet launch) |
| `resource_offline_save` | none | **Not emitted** by iOS 1.0 (no call site); Android does not emit it either |
| `library_search` | `resultCount` | Library search field, **1.5 s after typing settles**, non-blank query only, count of filtered rows; the text is never recorded |
| `safe_sport_open` | none | Safe Sport panel appears (area `resources`, screen `safeSport`) |
| `ask_question` | `grounded`, `safety`, `sourceCount` | Ask Gradus; **cannot fire in 1.0** (`ReleaseFlags.askGradusEnabled = false`, #22) |
| `ask_answer_saved` | none | Same, hidden |
| `ask_source_tap` | `index` | Same, hidden (screen `ask.source`) |

Areas: `roster`, `schedule`, `plans`, `sessions`, `messages`, `board`, `resources`, `ask`, `settings`, `onboarding`.

**Screen ids** (must match iOS byte for byte so reports merge across platforms):

| Where | Area | Screen |
|---|---|---|
| Roster tab root | `roster` | `tab.roster` |
| Plans tab root | coach `plans`; parent/athlete `sessions` | `tab.plans` |
| Resources tab root | `resources` | `tab.resources` |
| Messages tab root | `messages` | `tab.messages` |
| Live tab root | `board` | `tab.live` (iPad tab only on iOS; on phones the Live **cover** root, the board index, is **not tracked** at HEAD; Android phones match) |
| Settings tab root | `settings` | `tab.settings` |
| Routed `.board` | `board` | `board` |
| `.room` | `messages` | `room` |
| `.plan` | coach `plans`, else `sessions` | `plan` |
| `.editPlan` | `sessions` | `editPlan` |
| `.sharedPlan` | `plans` | `sharedPlan` |
| `.recap` | `plans` | `recap` |
| `.guardianClaim` / `.teamInvite` | `onboarding` | `guardianClaim` / `teamInvite` |
| `.settings(section)` | `settings` | `settings.<section raw value>` (e.g. `settings.safe-sport`) |
| any other routed screen | `settings` | `other` |

The table above is the complete set of `TrackedScreen` (`screen_time`) sources: iOS attaches `.trackedScreen` in exactly two places, the tab root (`RoleTabsView.swift` line 108) and the routed destination (line 229). Android places `TrackedScreen` in exactly the equivalent two places and nowhere else.

**Event screen ids (no `screen_time`).** These ids appear only as the `screen` of the events listed, never as a `TrackedScreen`:

| Screen id | Area | Events | iOS source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `resources.viewer` | `resources` | `resource_open`, `resource_read`, `resource_share` | `ResourceViewerSheet.swift` |
| `resources.library` | `resources` | `library_search` | `LibraryView.swift` |
| `safeSport` | `resources` | `safe_sport_open` | `SafeSportView.swift` |
| `ask`, `ask.source` | `ask` | `ask_question`, `ask_answer_saved`, `ask_source_tap` (hidden in 1.0) | `AskGradusView.swift`, `AskAnswerContent.swift` |

`resource_read`'s `durationMs` is **wall-clock** from viewer open (`openedAt` set on appear) to close (`onDisappear` → `recordRead()`), not paused while the app is in the background, capped at 30 min with `capped`. Android records `openedAt = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()` when the viewer opens and computes on dispose, matching.

The `schedule` and `sessions`-only areas have no dedicated screen at iOS HEAD beyond the mapping above; Android adds none.

**`TrackedScreen` equivalent.** `@Composable fun TrackedScreen(area: AnalyticsArea, screen: String)` placed in each tab root and each routed destination. The clock must stop and start exactly where iOS's does, so reports from both apps merge. iOS stops only on `onDisappear` and on `scenePhase != .active`; the biometric lock is a separate `UIWindow` (`LockWindow.swift`) and `ShareLink`/in-app sheets keep the scene active, so on iPhone the screen under the lock and under the share sheet **keeps counting**, while the system permission alert makes the scene `.inactive` and **stops** it. Android therefore does **not** use the entry's `RESUMED` state (a `LockActivity` or the system share chooser pauses `MainActivity`, which would stop the clock where iOS does not). The clock runs while **all** of these hold:
  1. the destination is the top entry of the **selected** tab's back stack (or of the Live cover's stack while the cover is up) — pushing another screen or switching tabs stops it;
  2. `ProcessLifecycleOwner` is at least `STARTED` — backgrounding and turning the screen off stop it; `LockActivity` and the share chooser do not;
  3. no runtime-permission request launched by the app is in flight (the app tracks its own `ActivityResultLauncher` permission calls) — the permission dialog stops it, as `.inactive` does on iOS.
Dialogs and bottom sheets inside the same destination do **not** stop it (SwiftUI sheets do not fire `onDisappear` either; iOS §6.12's "presenting a sheet stops it" is not what the code does, and code wins). A stretch under 1 s is dropped; over 30 min is recorded as 30 min with `capped = true`. The routed destination is keyed on the route so a second room's time is a new stretch.

**Transport** (`LiveUsageAnalytics`, ported constant for constant):
- Buffer on disk at `noBackupFilesDir/usage-analytics.json`, kept across launches, max **1,000** events, nothing older than **7 days** (trim on every write and flush).
- Each event: random UUID `id`, per-process-launch `sessionId` UUID, `occurredAt` ISO-8601, `event`, `area`, `screen` filtered to ASCII letters, digits and `.-_`, max 80 chars; `resourceId` only if it is a UUID (a bad id would 400 the whole batch); `durationMs` clamped 0…1 800 000; `capped` only when true; `props` omitted when empty. Props are numbers, booleans and short enum strings only.
- Batch body: `{"platform":"android","appVersion":"<versionName> (<versionCode>)","osVersion":"<Build.VERSION.RELEASE>","events":[…]}`, `appVersion`/`osVersion` ≤ 40 chars matching `^[0-9A-Za-z .()_-]{0,40}$`, keys sorted, one `Idempotency-Key` UUID per request.
- Flush: at launch (`start()`), every **60 s** while the process is started, and on `ON_STOP` (one flush in the application scope). Batches of **100**, one pass over what is buffered; a 2xx **or any 4xx** removes the batch (a refused batch would be refused forever); offline, 429 and 5xx stop the pass and keep the rest for the next flush. No retry loop, no WorkManager job, no error UI, never touches the write outbox.
- **Flush runs signed out too** (iOS `startAnalyticsFlushing()` and `LiveUsageAnalytics.flush()` do not check the session). Events recorded signed out (e.g. `screen_time` for a public board routed in the Live cover from a QR code) are sent without a bearer; the server answers 401, and a 4xx drops the batch like any other. Android does **not** hold them for a later sign-in (parity). Unit test: signed out, one buffered event, flush → one request with no `Authorization` header; a 401 response empties the buffer.
- Sign-out: **flush, then clear** (events belong to the account that made them). Email-link account switch: **clear without flushing** (they would go out under the new account).
- Wear OS records nothing in 1.0 (the Apple Watch app has no analytics); S-2's `wearos` value stays unused unless Mariah decides otherwise.

**Tests:** port all `UsageAnalyticsTests` (batches to the endpoint and leaves the buffer; offline and 5xx keep, 4xx drops; batches of 100/100/50; cap 1,000 and 7 days; disabled records nothing and flush clears; only ids and numbers leave the device, `"Greta's room"` → `Gretasroom`, non-UUID resource id dropped, 30-min cap; names match the contract). Compose UI test: `TrackedScreen` emits one `screen_time` after leaving a screen held for ≥ 1 s and none for a 0.5 s pass-through; a screen held 5 s with `LockActivity` up for 3 s of it records ~5 s (lock does not stop it); a permission request in flight stops it.

---

### 6.13 Consent, adult verification, age signals, and SafeSport

Decisions A2 (parity), iOS #24, #26, #27, #29–#34, #38, #40, #41, #46, #48. iOS design: iOS PRD §6.13, delivery §10.9 (S1–S5). **Why this matters on Android exactly as on iOS:** the live privacy policy promises verifiable parental consent and parent-created athlete profiles; the amended COPPA Rule (compliance date 2026-04-22) applies to every client; Texas SB 2420 (the App Store Accountability Act) binds app stores and developers on the US storefront (A10), and Google Play is a covered "app store" under it; SafeSport's MAAPP requires an adult other than the coach on every adult–minor communication and a parent's right to stop contact.

**Shape of the work.** Parts A (consent backbone) and C (SafeSport behaviors) live in the shared server and are inherited by Android with **no server rule changes**: the same states, the same refusals, the same room rule, the same KWS step. Android builds only the client side of A and C, identically to iOS. Part B (platform age signals) is the only platform-specific part: iOS uses Apple's Declared Age Range, PermissionKit, the StoreKit age-rating watcher and `RESCIND_CONSENT`; Android uses the **Google Play Age Signals API** and the Play Console's age-signals page in their place, as the iOS PRD already anticipated ("Kotlin later uses Google's Play Age Signals API in B's place", iOS §6.13 last paragraph). Part D (paper) gains Play-specific declarations.

**Guardrails Android must never weaken (iOS §6.13 "What stays").** No coach↔minor room without the athlete's guardians as participants (athlete rooms are three-way by construction; the only direct rooms are coach↔coach and coach↔parent). Report and block one tap away; a `minor_safety` report still emails admins immediately. Minors never reach Ask Gradus (and Ask Gradus is hidden for everyone in 1.0 behind `ReleaseFlags.askGradusEnabled`, iOS #22; Android mirrors with the compile-time `ReleaseFlags.ASK_GRADUS_ENABLED = false`, §7.9). No ads and no third-party SDKs beyond those §9 lists (FCM only; no Firebase Analytics or Crashlytics).

#### 6.13 A. Consent backbone: what the Android client consumes

The server owns every rule below (web PRs #148–#150, #170–#179; `src/lib/guardian-verification.server.ts`, `src/lib/athlete-age.ts`, `src/lib/minor-voice.server.ts`). Android's job is to read the state, branch the UI on it, show server refusal messages verbatim, and never add a second age or pause check that disagrees with the server (handoff-consent-S2-S3 §5.4).

| # | Server rule (iOS §6.13 A) | What Android reads | What Android does |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | One adult verification per parent account that links a minor, through KWS Parent Verification, every US method (card, debit card, SSN last-four via Veratad), stored method `kws` (#29, #38). Legacy parents (pre-S1) are `legacy` and never prompted (iOS §12 #27). Demo/review parents are seeded `admin` (#26). | `GET /me` → `parentVerification {required, available, verified, method, verifiedAt, requestedAt}`; `GET /guardian/verification/status` (same shape, nullable when no parent profile). `method` is a **plain string**, never a closed enum (#38): decode unknown values as `null`/`Unknown`, never fail. | "Verify you're an adult" step (§7.1.12) after account creation in parent onboarding (§7.1.11), inside the guardian claim (§7.7), and as the Settings opt-in (#34, §7.12). Derived flags exactly as `GradusCore/Onboarding/ConsentModels.swift`: `isNeeded = required && !verified`; `offersOptIn = !verified && (required || available)`; `isWaiting = requestedAt != null && !verified`. |
| A2 | KWS flow is server-side only: `POST /guardian/verification/start` sends KWS's email to the parent's **own account email**; KWS hosts the check, posts the signed webhook, and redirects to `https://gradus.training/verified?status=…&externalPayload=…&signature=…`; either channel alone completes it (60 s resend window, 6 per hour). | `POST /guardian/verification/start` → `status` ∈ `email_sent`, `already_verified`, `not_configured`, `rate_limited`. `POST /guardian/verification/complete` `[pub]` → `{ok, verified, duplicate, reason?}`. | **Gradus never opens KWS in a Custom Tab or WebView** (parity: iOS opens nothing; the email carries the link). Return handling: the `/verified` App Link (§6.10) is parsed and forwarded verbatim (below); the step also polls status every 5 s while waiting and refreshes on `ON_RESUME`. If the parent completes KWS on another device, the web `/verified` page completes it and the phone picks it up on its next poll or resume. |
| A3 | Consent ledger `guardian_consents` (scopes `account`, `messaging`); no `voice` scope (#32, #48). | Nothing directly. | Nothing; the ledger is server-only. |
| A4 | Athlete account states `active`, `provisional`, `paused`; no birthdate = minor. Under 13 never self-creates (`createSelfManagedAthlete` → 422 `parent_required`); 13–17 self-sign-up is `provisional` (own goals and plans; no coach link, no rooms) until a verified guardian claims; unclaimed provisional accounts are deleted after 3 months (iOS §12 #25); parent-created minors are `active` once the parent verifies, and until then their login code is not issued. | `GET /me` → `athleteAccountState`; athlete settings → `accountState`; parent settings → per-athlete `accountState`. Unknown strings decode to `null` (treated as `active` for display, never as a reason to block). | Birthdate-first athlete entry with the under-13 parent-only screen (§7.1.7c); the 13–17 provisional copy in setup, onboarding and Settings; paused notices (B4). |
| A5 | Coaches invite the **parent**, never the athlete, for anyone under 18 or with no birthdate (#30). | Roster `claimStatus` (`claimed`, `waitingForParent`, `waitingForAthlete`, `notInvited`). | §7.2 owns the New athlete sheet and roster chip; behavior identical to iOS (recipient picker only for a typed 18+ birthdate). |
| A6 | The room rule: a room with a minor opens and accepts sends only when a verified adult who is not the coach is a participant (switch-gated); the unclaimed-guardian email mirror is retired. | Room header `messagingPausedByParent`, `viewerTextOnly`; send result `ok:false` with `reason` ∈ `guardian_required`, `provisional`, `paused`, `paused_by_parent`, `text_only` and a `message`. | §7.5 owns the composer; `reason` is a plain string on Android too (unknown values show `message` verbatim). |
| A7 | Text only for minors (#32, #48): no voice notes and no voice-to-plan for any login with an athlete row under 18 or without a birthdate; server answers 403 `text_only` before reading audio. | `GET /me` → `athleteVoiceToPlan` (missing = `false`); room header `viewerTextOnly`. | Every athlete voice control is hidden unless `athleteVoiceToPlan == true` (§7.4, §7.6, §6.15 on Wear OS); the composer hides the mic for `viewerTextOnly` and says why in the TalkBack hint (§7.5). |
| A8 | COPPA direct notice in the parent invite email and **in the app wherever a parent enters a minor's details** (#40): parent sign-up athletes step and guardian claim end with the consent sentence; Settings → Add an athlete shows it without. One text source per platform, sentence for sentence with web `src/lib/consent/direct-notice.ts` and iOS `GradusCore/Onboarding/DirectNotice.swift`. | — | Kotlin `DirectNotice.kt` in `:core:data` (`consent` package; text below) and a `DirectNotice` composable (§7.1.18). A unit test pins every sentence against the web/iOS text (port of `DirectNoticeTests`). |
| A9 | Retention: provisional accounts after 3 months; dormant under-18 accounts after 3 years plus a 30-day guardian notice (#41); audit records 5 years (#43). | — | Nothing client-side. |

**The rollout switch.** `PARENT_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` (Lovable Cloud secret) is the only switch; `required` mirrors it to clients. What it gates and what is always on is the table in handoff-consent-S2-S3 §5.2: always on — under-13 refusal, provisional 13–17, the parent-recipient rule, text-only minors, parent pause and `paused` accounts; switch-gated — the room rule, `assertParentVerified` on claims and coach links (403 `parent_unverified`), athlete login codes issued only after verification, the retired mirror. Android never reads the secret; it reads `required` and `available` and behaves as iOS does in each combination (`ParentVerificationTests`: "Already verified, or the switch off, finishes at once; the Settings opt-in stays until verified").

**Error codes Android must handle (handoff-consent-S2-S3 §5.5).** `parent_unverified` 403 → open the verify step, then retry the call that failed (parent onboarding athlete link, guardian claim); `parent_required` 422 → under-13 parent-only screen, server message verbatim as the safety net; `provisional` 403 → the provisional note; `paused` 403; `guardian_required` and `paused_by_parent` 403 on room openers; `verification_unavailable` 503 → retry later; `text_only` 403. Every one of these shows the server's `message` verbatim when no screen-specific copy exists.

**The `/verified` return (iOS `ConsentModels.swift` `VerificationRedirect`, `AppModel.completeVerification`).**
1. The App Link `https://gradus.training/verified?…` (and `gradus://verified?…` for parity with iOS's custom scheme) is matched before the route parser and has **no screen of its own**; it works signed in or signed out, and a signed-out Live Board cover is not dismissed by it.
2. Parse the **raw** query (`Uri.getEncodedQuery()`), split on `&`, form-decode each name and value exactly like the web's `URLSearchParams` (`+` → space, then percent-decode once), keep the first `status`, the first `externalPayload`, and **every** `signature` value in order; ignore other names; skip empty values. A pair without "=", or whose name or value fails percent-decoding, is skipped (decode as UTF-8; catch `IllegalArgumentException` from the decoder; never crash or reject the whole link), matching `VerificationRedirect.formDecode` returning nil. Any part missing → the link opens nothing. Never re-serialize the JSON values (the HMAC covers `status:externalPayload` byte for byte). Test vectors: port `ConsentRoutingTests.verifiedLink`, `formDecoding` ("a plus is a space, %2B is a plus"), `schemeAndMissingParts`, plus an Android vector with a malformed `junk=%zz` pair (and a bare `flag` pair) that is skipped while `status`, `externalPayload` and `signature` still parse.
3. `POST /guardian/verification/complete {status, externalPayload, signatures}`. `ok && verified` → toast "Thanks, you're verified."; otherwise toast (error) "That verification link couldn't be confirmed. Check your email for a newer one, or resend it from the app."; a transport error shows its user message. `duplicate: true` is the normal case (the webhook usually lands first) and still shows the success toast.
4. Bump a process-wide `VerificationSignals.completions` counter (Kotlin `MutableStateFlow<Int>`) so any verify step on screen refreshes at once, then refresh `/me` if signed in.
5. *(verify)* Chrome opens a verified App Link on a server redirect that follows a user gesture (the KWS form submit). If it does not on some browsers, nothing breaks: the web `/verified` page completes the verification itself (either channel alone completes), and the waiting step's poll and `ON_RESUME` refresh pick it up.

#### 6.13 B. Google Play age signals (Android's replacement for iOS §6.13 B1–B5)

**Platform facts (developer.android.com, pages last updated 2026-07-20; read 2026-10-11).**
- The **Play Age Signals API is in beta**; library `com.google.android.play:age-signals:0.0.4`; Android 6.0+ phones, foldables and tablets; usable only by apps **installed or updated by Google Play**; signals may be used **only** to provide age-appropriate experiences and legal compliance, never for ads, marketing, profiling or analytics; the client library collects no data.
- It returns signals for eligible users in **Texas** (SB 2420) for accounts created after **2026-05-28**, in Brazil since 2026-03-17, and "further updates ahead of age verification bills in other US states" (Utah, Louisiana: *(verify)* dates and status — reported moved to 2027; Google's Play Console help page `support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/16569691` is the authority; re-check at submission, Appendix D item, owner Mariah; iOS's #33 note named Utah and Louisiana and California from 2027-01-01). SB 2420 status: preliminarily enjoined 2025-12-23, the Fifth Circuit stayed the injunction in May–June 2026, so it is enforceable while the appeal runs *(verify at submission)*.
- Two calls. `AgeSignalsManagerFactory.create(context)`; `requestAgeSignalsAccess(AgeSignalsAccessRequest.builder().setActivity(activity).build())` → `ageSignalsStatus()` ∈ `SHARED`, `NOT_SHARED`, `VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` (passing an Activity lets Play show its own sharing prompt "if required"; a dismissed prompt reappears a few times, then is suppressed); then, only when `SHARED`, `checkAgeSignals(AgeSignalsRequest.builder().build())` → `ageLower()`, `ageUpper()` (inclusive; `ageUpper == null` = open top band such as 18+), `ageRangeSource()` (`TIER_A` self-declared, `TIER_B` parent/guardian-managed, `TIER_C` assessed by card/email/selfie/ID/tax ID, `TIER_D` ID+selfie or digital ID), `significantChangeStatus` (`APPROVED`, `PENDING`, `DECLINED`, `null`), `significantChangeApprovalDate`, `installId` (supervised installs only). Errors throw `AgeSignalsException` with an `AgeSignalsErrorCode`. Testing: `FakeAgeSignalsManager`.
- Default bands are `0-12`, `13-15`, `16-17`, `18+`, which equal iOS's gates 13, 16, 18 exactly. **Do not configure custom age ranges in Play Console** (each minimum can change only once a year and the rules below assume the defaults).
- Google recommends calling Play Integrity alongside to resist spoofing (§6.11 owns Play Integrity; the age band is tighten-only, so a spoofed answer can only make the app stricter, and the server never trusts it).
- A8: **no Play Console account exists yet.** Until the app is distributed by Play, every call fails or returns nothing and the app takes the birthdate path, exactly like iOS 18–25. All development and CI use `FakeAgeSignalsManager` behind the debug answer switch below.

**Mapping table (iOS → Android).**

| iOS (§6.13 B, `Gradus/Shell/AgeAssurance.swift`, `GradusCore/Onboarding/AgeSignals.swift`, `SignificantChanges.swift`) | Android |
|---|---|
| B1 `DeclaredAgeRange` `requestAgeRange(ageGates: 13, 16, 18)`; `.sharing(range)` / `.declinedSharing` / errors | `requestAgeSignalsAccess` + `checkAgeSignals`; `SHARED`+bounds / `NOT_SHARED` / `VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` and errors |
| `isEligibleForAgeFeatures` (26.2+) decides whether to ask **on launch** | No eligibility call exists *(verify)*. Launch check is a **silent** access request (no Activity, so Play cannot prompt) *(verify that `setActivity` is optional; if not, the athlete-only weekly fallback in B1 applies)*; `SHARED` there means an auto-share region (verified or supervised user in a covered US state) and counts as "eligible" |
| `ageRangeDeclaration` → `selfDeclared` / `guardianDeclared` / checked | `TIER_A` → `SelfDeclared`; `TIER_B` → `GuardianDeclared`; `TIER_C`, `TIER_D` → `Confirmed`; `null` → `Unknown` |
| B2 PermissionKit `SignificantAppUpdateTopic`, `PermissionButton` "Ask my parent", `AskCenter` responses | Significant changes are **declared in Play Console** (Age signals page) with an effective date and a parent-facing description; Play itself sends supervised users' parents the request; the app reads `significantChangeStatus` / `significantChangeApprovalDate` and enforces. No in-app "ask" button exists |
| PermissionKit `CommunicationTopic` ask-a-parent for coach connections (post-1.0, iOS §12 #26) | No Play equivalent; not built (post-1.0 on both platforms) |
| B2 adult `showSignificantUpdateAcknowledgment` (26.4+) | No Play equivalent *(verify)*: adults have nothing to do (`MarkHandled`) |
| B3 StoreKit `AppStore.ageRatingCode` watcher | No API exposes the Play content rating to the app *(verify)*. Replaced by process: any IARC rating change is also declared as a Play Console significant change and added to the app's registry (Appendix D) |
| B4 `RESCIND_CONSENT` (App Store Server Notifications V2) + `AppTransaction` binding (`POST /me/app-transaction`) | Play Console **Revoked app approvals** tab (CSV of `installId`s, kept 90 days; no RTDN or Developer API documented *(verify)*) + `installId` binding (`POST /me/play-install`, new) + an admin CSV import (new) |
| B5 App Store age-rating answers (#24; age assurance flips to Yes after S1/S3) | Play Console: IARC content-rating questionnaire, Target audience and content, Data safety form, Age signals page (Appendix D) |

##### B1. Age signals at sign-up: tighten-only (iOS #33, §6.13 B1)

Rules are platform-neutral and identical to `GradusCore/Onboarding/AgeSignals.swift`; port them to `:core:data` (`agesignals` package) as pure Kotlin with the same names so the tests port one for one.

- `DeviceAgeRange(lowerBound: Int?, upperBound: Int?, declaration)` from `ageLower`/`ageUpper`. `isMinor = upperBound != null && upperBound < 18`; `isUnder13 = upperBound != null && upperBound < 13`; `isAdult = lowerBound != null && lowerBound >= 18`.
- `DeviceAgeSignal` = `Unavailable` (not asked yet, API error, not installed by Play, `VERIFICATION_REQUIRED`) | `Declined` (`NOT_SHARED`) | `Shared(range)` (both bounds `null` despite `SHARED` → `Unavailable`). `blocksAdultRoles = range?.isMinor`; `requiresParentOnly = range?.isUnder13`; `contradicts(age) = blocksAdultRoles && age >= 18`.
- **Tighten only.** A band under 18 blocks coach, parent and adult-athlete sign-up on the device and routes to the minor flow; under 13 routes straight to the parent-only screen. A self-declared (or confirmed) 18+ never loosens anything: a typed minor birthdate still gets the minor flow. `Declined` and `Unavailable` fall back to the birthdate path and **never block** (iOS: App Review rejects apps that block; on Play the same principle holds and the birthdate path already satisfies the server's rules).
- **`VERIFICATION_REQUIRED`** ("age unknown in a region where verification is mandatory; ask the user to visit the Play Store"): treated as `Unavailable`, never blocks, and Gradus shows no Play Store prompt in 1.0. Open question for Mariah with counsel (§12): whether Texas compliance needs a "Verify your age in the Play Store" nudge on the sign-up chooser for this status.
- **The band stays on the device.** Never sent to the server, never logged, never in analytics (also a Play API term). Only `installId` is sent, and only for athlete sessions (B4).
- **When it is asked (iOS `AgeSignalStore`).** At most once per process ("launch"). `refreshOnLaunch()`: the silent access request; if `SHARED`, `checkAgeSignals()` and keep the answer (`hasAnswered = true`); if not `SHARED`, do **not** mark answered, so the first sign-up entry still asks with an Activity. `requestIfNeeded()` at a sign-up entry: if not answered, call `requestAgeSignalsAccess` **with the current Activity** (Play may show its prompt), then `checkAgeSignals` when `SHARED`; concurrent callers share one in-flight `Deferred`; `isChecking` is true while it runs. The answer lives in memory only (a `@Singleton` `AgeSignalStore` exposing `StateFlow<DeviceAgeSignal>`).
- **Fallback if the library requires an Activity** for `requestAgeSignalsAccess` (Google's sample always passes `setActivity(this)`; *verify on device with `FakeAgeSignalsManager` and a Family Link account*). Then the launch check runs once the shell settles, with the current Activity, **only for athlete sessions and at most once per 7 days** (the same DataStore cadence as `PlayInstallReporter`, B4), so the `installId` binding still happens for already-onboarded athletes who never reach a sign-up entry (parity with iOS B4, where `AppTransactionReporter` reports weekly for every athlete session, `AppModel.apply()`). Supervised accounts in covered states auto-share, so Play shows them no prompt; for other users the call may show Play's sharing prompt. That is a **known divergence** from iOS (which never prompts on launch outside regulated regions) and is listed for Mariah in §12 N12. Coach, parent and signed-out launches never call with an Activity; the significant-change coordinator (B2) never does either.
- **Every entry passes one check** (iOS `SignUpFlowViews.SignUpStepView.ageBlocked`, `RootView.phaseContent`, `RoleTabsView.NoRoleView`). Every destination in the `signUp` nav graph (chooser, athlete chooser, invite entry, coach-invite chooser, every setup screen and account form, athlete claim) calls `ageSignals.requestIfNeeded(activity)` on first composition (`LaunchedEffect(Unit)`; iOS `SignUpStepView` `.task { await model.ageSignals.requestIfNeeded() }`, "not only the chooser: invite codes, links and the coach-invite chooser reach steps with the chooser hidden beneath them"), and `ageBlocked` is re-evaluated whenever the `StateFlow` emits, so a late answer swaps the step for AdultRolesBlocked in place:
  - Sign-up chooser and role chooser hide **Coach** and **Parent** when `blocksAdultRoles`, showing the blocked note instead (§7.1.6, §7.1.9). The role chooser deselects Coach/Parent if the answer arrives after the tap, and Continue stays disabled while `isChecking`.
  - Any coach/parent setup step or account form (reached from the chooser, `/signup/coach`, `/signup/parent`, an invite code, or `/i/<code>`) renders **AdultRolesBlocked** instead (§7.1.6). An adult-athlete account form renders it when the band is under 13, or when the stashed setup birthdate is 18+ and the band says under 18. A coach's invite code the person arrived with rides along to the athlete paths.
  - The athlete setup screen: band under 13 → parent-only screen immediately (and the stash is cleared); an 18+ typed birthdate on an under-18 band → refused with the contradiction message; a stash written before the answer arrived is sent back to the birthdate step with the reason (`AgeSignalEntryTests.lateAnswer`).
  - Signed in with no profile: a coach or parent onboarding gate waits (full-screen progress) until the store has answered, because coach onboarding creates the coach row on load; an under-18 answer sends a coach/parent stash back to the athlete-only role chooser (`AppModel.resolveOnboardingGate`, `chooseRole`).
  - A `/g/<token>` guardian claim or `/team/<token>` team invite opened by a profile-less account waits on "Checking this device…" until answered, and on an under-18 band shows AdultRolesBlocked (`signedIn = true`: the under-13 card says to sign out) with a top-app-bar **Sign out**; "Sign up as an athlete" there drops the link and shows the athlete-only role chooser.
  - Accounts that already have a profile are **not re-gated** by the band (iOS §12 #28, open until California's DAAA, 2027-01-01).
- **Android copy (iOS strings with "Apple Account" replaced; the only copy difference in this section):**
  - `adultRolesBlockedTitle`: "Coach and parent accounts are for adults"
  - `adultRolesBlockedBody`: "The Google Account on this device is set up for someone under 18, so it can only create an athlete account. A parent or coach can sign up on their own device or at gradus.training."
  - `birthdateContradictionMessage`: "The Google Account on this device says you're under 18. Enter your real date of birth to continue."
- **Debug and QA switch** (iOS `-GradusAgeRange`): debug builds only, an intent extra or `adb shell am start … --es gradusAgeRange <name>` (A28) and a Developer menu row, with `under13`, `teen` (13–15, `TIER_B`), `teen16` (16–17, `TIER_B`), `adult` (18+, `TIER_A`), `adultConfirmed` (18+, `TIER_C`), `declined` (`NOT_SHARED`), `unavailable`, `verificationRequired`; implemented with `FakeAgeSignalsManager`. Never compiled into release.
- **Tests (port `AgeSignalsTests`, `AgeSignalEntryTests`):** "Under 13 blocks the adult roles and leaves only the parent-only screen"; "13–17 blocks coach, parent and adult-athlete sign-up but keeps the athlete path"; "A self-declared adult never loosens anything"; "Declined, unavailable, or a range that straddles 18 never blocks"; "`VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` never blocks" (new); "On launch a non-shared answer does not count as answered; a sign-up entry asks with the Activity" (Android form of "asks only where the law requires"); "A sign-up entry asks once; later entries reuse the answer"; the six `AgeSignalEntryTests` cases verbatim.

##### B2. Significant changes and parental approval (iOS §6.13 B2–B3, `SignificantChanges.swift`, `SignificantChangeCoordinatorTests`)

- **Registry.** `SignificantChange(id, introducedIn: SemanticVersion, playEffectiveFrom: LocalDate, description)`; `SignificantChange.registry` is **empty in 1.0** ("a fresh install never acknowledges what it installed"). Adding an entry is a release-process step with three parts done together: the registry entry, the **identical** description submitted on Play Console → Age signals (en-US; effective date in the future, 00:00 UTC; at most 3 pending, more than 2 days apart, up to 90 days ahead), and the iOS registry entry (one description for both stores).
- **Ledger on the device** (iOS `SignificantChangeLedger`): DataStore keys `gradus.significantChanges.handled`, `gradus.significantChanges.firstVersion` (stamped on first run, so changes shipped at or before the installed version are never pending). No age-rating key (no watcher on Android). Nothing leaves the device.
- **Decision (Android `SignificantChangeAction.decide`):**
  - nothing pending → `None`;
  - signal `Shared` and `isAdult` → `MarkHandled` (Play has no adult acknowledgment);
  - signal `Shared`, `isMinor`, and `significantChangeStatus == APPROVED` with `significantChangeApprovalDate >= change.playEffectiveFrom` for every pending change → `MarkHandled`;
  - signal `Shared`, `isMinor`, status `PENDING` (or `APPROVED` with an older approval date) → `AskParent(description, declined = false)`;
  - status `DECLINED` → `AskParent(description, declined = true)`;
  - signal `Shared`, status `null` (unsupervised, or no law applies) → `MarkHandled`;
  - `Declined`, `Unavailable`, or a range that straddles 18 → `Wait` (stays pending, shows nothing, asked again next launch; "the ledger never records a consent nobody gave").
  - **Effective-date rule (Play-specific).** A pending change counts toward `AskParent` only once today (UTC) ≥ `change.playEffectiveFrom`. Before that date it stays pending and contributes nothing: if no pending change is yet effective, the result is `Wait` (Play keeps returning the previously approved `significantChangeApprovalDate` until the effective date and has not asked the parent yet, so a gate there could never be cleared by "Check again"; iOS never blocks on an ask the parent cannot answer, because PermissionKit sends the question from the button, `AgeAssurance.swift` `ParentApprovalView`). **Release rule:** the registry entry's `playEffectiveFrom` must be on or before the date the release reaches users, or the release ships after the effective date (Appendix D).
- **Coordinator** (iOS `SignificantChangeCoordinator`): runs once per launch after the shell settles (phase, `/me`, Terms gate), never blocks launch; computes pending; if any, decides from the **silent launch answer only** (`refreshOnLaunch`). **The coordinator never prompts:** if the launch answer is not `SHARED` it returns `Wait` (nothing shown, nothing recorded) and it never calls `requestIfNeeded` or `requestAgeSignalsAccess` with an Activity. (Parity: iOS `SignificantChangeCoordinator.run()` calls `store.requestIfNeeded()` only when `requiredRegulatoryFeatures` is known and non-empty, i.e. where a law applies; Play has no such query, and a `SHARED` launch answer already means an auto-share region, so asking with an Activity would put Play's sharing prompt in front of every non-sharing user on every launch.) Then it decides; on `AskParent` the shell shows **ParentApproval** above everything (including the Terms gate, which waits: `termsNeeded` is false while blocking). While blocking, re-query `checkAgeSignals` on every `ON_RESUME` and on "Check again"; an approval covers only the changes whose `playEffectiveFrom` ≤ the approval date (port `olderApprovalCoversOnlyItsChanges`); a late denial of an older change never marks the current ask declined (`olderDenialIgnored`).
- **ParentApproval screen** (iOS `ParentApprovalView`; Android copy adapted where PermissionKit's Messages flow has no Play equivalent):
  - Icon: a family/supervision Material Symbol in `accentInk`.
  - Title "Ask a parent to approve this update"; intro "Gradus changed in a way that needs a parent or guardian's OK before you keep using it:"; a card with the change description(s).
  - Declined (bold): "Your parent or guardian didn't approve this update, so Gradus stays closed on this device. You can ask again." (iOS string; on Play, a new significant change re-asks cumulatively, and the parent can approve from Family Link.)
  - Primary button **"Check again"** (Android; replaces PermissionKit's "Ask my parent"/"Ask again", because Play sends the request itself).
  - Caption (Android): "Google Play sent your parent or guardian a request. Once they approve in Family Link, Gradus opens again here." *(verify the "Family Link" wording: the Play Age Signals docs say only "parents"; if Family Link is not the approval surface, drop "in Family Link".)*
  - **Sign out** (secondary) when signed in.
  - Predictive/system back: `moveTaskToBack(true)`; the gate cannot be dismissed. Test tags `parentApproval`, `parentApproval.declined`, `parentApproval.ask` (the Check again button), `parentApproval.signOut`.
- **Debug** (iOS `-GradusSignificantChange`): debug-only extra `gradusSignificantChange "<description>"` shows the screen.
- **Tests:** port `AgeSignalsTests` registry/ledger cases ("1.0 ships no significant changes", "A fresh install never acknowledges what it installed", "An upgrade across a change makes it pending until handled") and the four `SignificantChangeCoordinatorTests` (approval clears; denial keeps the gate and says so; older approval covers only its changes; late older denial ignored), plus Android cases for each `decide` row above, and: "approval date older than a not-yet-effective change → no gate (`Wait`)"; "the same change after its effective date → `AskParent`"; "a pending change with a `NOT_SHARED` launch answer makes no access request with an Activity".

##### B3. Content-rating changes

No Android API reports the app's current Play content rating to the device *(verify)*, so the StoreKit age-rating watcher has no port. Replacement (Appendix D checklist): when the IARC questionnaire is re-answered and the rating changes, Mariah files a Play Console significant change with the iOS watcher's description, "Gradus's age rating on the App Store has changed. Gradus is a training app where athletes, their parents and their coaches share plans, goals and messages.", reworded for Play ("…on Google Play has changed…"), and the release adds the registry entry.

##### B4. Revoked approvals → athlete paused (iOS §6.13 B4, §12 #29; `AppTransactionRepository.swift`, `AgeAssurance.swift` `AppTransactionReporter`)

**Why iOS uses `AppTransaction`.** Apple's `RESCIND_CONSENT` names no Gradus account, only the child's download (`appTransactionId`), so athlete sessions send their signed `AppTransaction` to `POST /me/app-transaction` and the server binds account ↔ download; a rescind then pauses every athlete bound to it. **The Play equivalent is the Age Signals `installId`**, which Play assigns to supervised users' installs precisely so developers can act on revoked approvals. Play Install Referrer and Play licensing carry no such identifier and are not used.

- **Client (`PlayInstallReporter`):** after `/me` loads with `role == athlete` (never coach, parent or org admin), at most once per 7 days per account (DataStore `gradus.playInstall.reported.<userId>`) and also whenever the `installId` differs from the last one reported, read `installId` from the cached `checkAgeSignals` result (calling it only if this launch already has a `SHARED` answer, from the silent launch check or, if the library requires an Activity, from the athlete-only weekly launch check in B1; never from any other prompt); if non-null, `POST /me/play-install {installId}` → `{bound: Boolean}`. Never prompts, never surfaces an error, never retries in a loop. Same cadence and failure rules as iOS's weekly `AppTransactionReporter`.
- **Server (new, web repo; additive, outside §4.1 risk):**
  - `POST /api/v1/me/play-install {installId}` → `bound: false` for coaches, parents, and unknown users; for athletes stores `play_age_signal_installs (user_id, install_id, first_seen_at, last_seen_at)`, many-to-many, unique on `(user_id, install_id)`, GRANTs and RLS (no client policies) in the same migration. Rate-limited. No `installId` validation beyond shape (Play does not sign it); a forged id can only pause the forger.
  - **Admin import** (web-only, decision #2): Admin → Membership → **Play revocations** → upload the Console CSV. Each row is idempotent on `(installId, revocation timestamp)` in `webhook_receipts` (source `google_play`). For every athlete bound to a revoked `installId`: `account_state = 'paused'`, `revokeGuardianConsent(reason: "play_revoked")`, push to the parent and every linked coach (the same notifications as `RESCIND_CONSENT`). An `installId` revoked before anyone bound to it is remembered in `play_revoked_installs` and pauses whoever binds later. Claims and invite resends refuse a paused athlete (unchanged).
  - **Restore** is the existing Admin → Membership → Paused athletes flow (iOS §12 #29), generalized to exempt the athlete from a stored Play revocation as it does for an Apple download.
  - **Cadence (process, Appendix D/§11):** Play keeps revoked `installId`s for 90 days and documents no push channel; Mariah downloads the CSV **at least weekly** *(verify whether a Play Developer API endpoint exists that could automate this; if so, a daily cron replaces the manual import)*.
- **Paused copy.** iOS hard-codes "through Apple" (`AthleteAccountState.pausedMessageForAthlete`, `pausedMessageForParent`). Android must not say "Apple" for a Play revocation, and an Apple-paused athlete may open the Android app. Proposed (server, additive): `pausedVia` (`app_store`, `google_play`, `support`, plain string) on `/me`, athlete settings and parent settings. Android copy by value; a missing or unknown value uses the generic form:
  - Athlete, `google_play`: "A parent or guardian withdrew consent for Gradus through Google Play, so messaging and connecting with coaches are off for now. Your goals and plans are still here. Questions: support@gradussports.com."
  - Athlete, `app_store`: the iOS string verbatim.
  - Athlete, generic: "A parent or guardian withdrew consent for Gradus, so messaging and connecting with coaches are off for now. Your goals and plans are still here. Questions: support@gradussports.com."
  - Parent, `google_play`: "Consent for {first}'s use of Gradus was withdrawn through Google Play (Family Link), so their messaging and coach connections are on hold. To restore the account, email support@gradussports.com from this account's address."; `app_store`: iOS verbatim; generic: same sentence without the "through …" clause.
  - The athlete Settings card eyebrow is "Your account is paused" (iOS `AthleteProfileView`).
- **Tests:** reporter posts only for athletes, at most weekly, again on a changed id, never with a null id, swallows errors; server tests for binding, import idempotency, revoked-before-bound, pause + ledger + both notifications, restore exemption.

##### B5. Play Console declarations (Appendix D owns the checklist)

- **Content rating (IARC):** answers consistent with iOS #24 (no mature/suggestive themes with #23 applied, no medical/treatment information, unrestricted web access No, user-to-user communication present but restricted to connected users).
- **Target audience and content** (§12 N3 owns the decision; verify with counsel): Gradus serves athletes under 13 (parent-created, #30). Declaring an under-13 audience brings the **Families policy** (Designed for Families requirements, Families-certified SDKs only, no ads) into scope; Gradus already has no ads and no ad SDKs, and FCM's status under the Families policy must be checked *(verify)*. Recommended: declare the true audience (under 13 through adult) and comply, rather than understate it.
- **Data safety form:** mirror the iOS App Privacy answers (iOS §6.11, §6.12) plus, for athletes, the `installId` ("Device or other IDs", linked, app functionality / compliance) *(verify the category)*. The age band is never collected.
- **Age signals page:** default age ranges; significant changes per B2; the revoked-approvals tab per B4.
- **Under-13 installs (for §11, parity with iOS §11 #26):** under-13 supervised Google accounts need Family Link parent approval to install; the Play listing says a parent installs Gradus, as the App Store listing does for Ask to Buy.

### 6.14 Athlete-authored plans

Decision #35 (iOS §6.14, §10.10 AP1–AP4), narrowed by #48 (no voice under 18) and #49 (the web shows an athlete's own active and benched plans). **Android adds nothing server-side for this feature**: AP1 (migration `20261006010000_athlete_authored_plans.sql`) and AP2 (`athlete-authoring.server.ts` and the `/athlete/...` routes) are live and serve Android unchanged. Android builds the iOS AP3 client behavior exactly, and its QA rows are iOS `docs/ios/QA.md` §5a run on a Pixel.

#### 6.14.1 What the server guarantees (inherited, do not re-implement on the client)

| Rule | Source | Android consequence |
|---|---|---|
| A self-authored plan is `kind = 'plan'`, `source = 'athlete'`, `coach_id NULL`, `athlete_id` = author; CHECK `plans_athlete_source_shape` pins it | iOS §6.14 A | Client never sends `kind`, `athleteId` or a template id on athlete routes (iOS `LivePlansRepository.createPlan`: athlete body is only `{fromPlanId, title}`) |
| RLS lets the author insert/update/delete their own `plans` / `plan_moves` rows; the author reads every status (drafts included) | iOS §6.14 A | `GET /plans/{id}` returns `isOwner: true`, `coach: null`, `source: "athlete"`, `authorFirstName`, any status |
| A **paused** athlete (§6.13 C, consent withdrawn) keeps read access, writes nothing; their share links stop resolving and cannot be imported | iOS §6.14 A, D; QA §5a "Paused athlete" | Show the server's own error message (`APIError.userMessage` equivalent) in the error toast; no client-side pause logic |
| Rostered coaches read the athlete's plan only while **active or benched** (never a draft), read-only (`isOwner: false`); a coach can never mint its share link | iOS §6.14 A, B (`getOrCreateShareToken`) | Coach editor shows the read-only banner "Written by *first name*, read-only." (`PlanDetailView.readOnlyBanner`); the coach's share action is not shown because `canEdit` is false |
| No cap on an athlete's own active plans, and since #52 (2026-10-11) no cap on a coach's either (`MAX_ACTIVE_PLANS_PER_ATHLETE` is gone) | iOS §6.14 A, §12 #33, #52 | The athlete editor never opens the 409 bench-choice sheet (§7.3.5): the athlete status route takes `{status}` only |
| `GET /athlete/plans` marks rows with `source` (plain string) and lists drafts in a separate `drafts` array; `coachName` on an own row is the athlete's own first name | iOS §6.14 B | Decode `source` as `String?` and `drafts` as optional (default empty); never an enum (an unknown `source` such as `"club"` is "not the athlete's own", `AthleteAuthoredPlansCoreTests.planDetailCarriesTheAuthorAndAnOlderServerStillDecodes`) |
| Athletes have **no personal library**; moves added from the curriculum copy in as plain rows (`moveId` and `libraryMove` always null) | iOS §6.14 B, C | No "Save to library", no library sync strip, no move sheet in the athlete editor |
| Athlete voice route transcribes and discards; answers 403 `text_only` for any login holding an under-18 or no-birthdate athlete row | #48; iOS §6.14 B | Hide every athlete voice control unless `/me.athleteVoiceToPlan == true` (missing = false). See §6.7 for the recorder |
| Import (`POST /plans/import/{token}`) by an athlete: copy snapshot, `source = 'athlete'`, **status active**, title suffixed "(from *author*)", moves as plain rows. Coach import stays a benched template; a coach who is also an athlete imports as a coach; a caller who is neither is refused | iOS §6.14 D | Android shows "Add to my plans" to athletes, "Save to my library" to coaches, nothing to parents (`RoleTabsView.swift` `.sharedPlan` route: `importRole` nil for parents) |
| The web shows an athlete's own active and benched plans read-only (#49); drafts stay app-only | #49 | Nothing for Android to do; drafts exist only in the apps |

#### 6.14.2 Endpoints Android calls for this feature

All paths under `/api/v1`. `[idem]` = send `Idempotency-Key`; `[etag]` = send `If-None-Match` and handle 304. (iOS Appendix A "Athlete-authored plans"; `AthletePlansPaths` in `GradusCore/Plans/PlansRepository.swift`.)

| Purpose | Method and path | Body / reply |
|---|---|---|
| Create own plan (the "+" and voice create) | `POST /athlete/plans` `[idem]` | `{fromPlanId?: string, title?: string}` → `{id}` |
| Edit title / notes | `PATCH /athlete/plans/{id}` | `{title?}` / `{notes?}` → `{forkedId: null}` |
| Delete own draft or benched plan | `DELETE /athlete/plans/{id}` | — |
| Activate / bench | `POST /athlete/plans/{id}/status` | `{status}` **only** (never `replaceId`, never `reason`; `LivePlansRepository.setStatus` strips both for athlete routes) |
| Add curriculum moves | `POST /athlete/plans/{id}/moves/from-library` `[idem]` | `{moveIds: [..]}` → `{inserted}` |
| Edit a move | `PATCH /athlete/plans/{id}/moves/{moveId}` | `PlanMovePatch` (name, description, cue, why, targetKind, targetValue; omitted fields not sent) |
| Remove a move | `DELETE /athlete/plans/{id}/moves/{moveId}` | no `?reason=` ever (`PlanRoutes.planMove` ignores `reason` for athletes) |
| Reorder | `PUT /athlete/plans/{id}/moves/order` | `{orderedIds: [...]}` |
| Read-only curriculum | `GET /athlete/moves` `[etag]` | `MoveLibrary` `{moves, seedCategories}` filtered server-side to the sports on the athlete's goals |
| Voice build/edit (adults only) | `POST /athlete/voice/build-plan` (multipart, `mode=create|edit`, `planId?`) | `VoiceApplyResult` |
| Read own plan | `GET /plans/{id}` | role-aware `PlanDetail` |
| List | `GET /athlete/plans` `[etag]` | `{athlete:{id, firstName}, plans:[...], drafts:[...]}` |
| Share link | `POST /plans/{id}/share-token` `[idem]` | `{token}` (shared with coaches; same path) |
| Public snapshot / import | `GET /public/plans/{token}`, `POST /plans/import/{token}` `[idem]` | `SharedPlan` with `authorKind`, `authorFirstName`; import → `{planId}` |
| Log practice on an own plan | `POST /plans/{id}/sessions` `[idem]` | `SessionSubmission` (§7.6) |

**Outbox allow-list.** The Android outbox (§6.5) must accept every athlete write path above on replay, exactly as iOS's contract test does (`AthleteAuthoredPlansCoreTests.everyAthleteWriteHasAContractOperation`: each `(method, path)` pair resolves to an operation in the vendored `openapi.json`). Coach and athlete families are kept apart: `isAuthoringPath(path)` is true only for `/api/v1/athlete/plans...`, and `isPlansPath` (coach) is false for it, so the coach Plans header's "*n* to sync" count never includes an athlete's edits.

#### 6.14.3 Android client architecture for this feature

iOS builds **one editor** for coach and athlete, switched by `PlansDependencies.routes` (`PlanRoutes.coach` / `.athlete`), and keeps the athlete's Plans tab in `FeatureSessions` with authoring hooks injected by the shell (`AthleteAuthoringKit`, `RunnerPlanAuthoring`). Android mirrors this:

- `:feature:plans` owns `PlanEditorScreen` + `PlanEditorViewModel` (the iOS `PlanDetailView` / `PlanDetailModel`), `MovePickerSheet`, `SharedPlanScreen`, the athlete `AthleteLibraryPane`, and `AthleteAuthoringControls` (FABs).
- `:feature:sessions` owns `RunnerPlansScreen` (the athlete/parent Plans tab) and receives an `AthleteAuthoring` interface from the app shell (`controls`, `library`, `openEditor`) so `:feature:sessions` does not depend on `:feature:plans`, as on iOS.
- `PlanRoutes` is a Kotlin value class / sealed type with `Coach` and `Athlete`; the repository and the outbox paths both read it, so one `PlanEditorViewModel` writes to the right family online and offline. `isAuthoring = routes is Athlete`.
- Hilt provides two `PlansDependencies` graphs: `coachPlansDeps` and `athleteAuthoringDeps`. The athlete graph has no roster (`loadAthletes = { emptyList() }`), its own pending-voice directory (`pending-voice-athlete`, never used to park, see below), and `voiceAvailable = me.athleteVoiceToPlan == true`. Default for any non-coach graph is **voice off** (`AthleteAuthoringTests.athleteVoiceIsOffUnlessTheCallerKnowsItIsAllowed`).
- Navigation: type-safe routes `Plan(id)` (role-dispatched: coach → editor, parent/athlete → runner), `EditPlan(id)` (athlete only; lives on the Plans tab back stack; `requiresSession`), `SharedPlan(token)` (App Link `/p/{token}`, §6.10).
  - `SharedPlan(token)` `requiresSession` (iOS `AppRoute.requiresSession` is true for every route except board index, board, login, signup, invite and verified). A `/p/` link opened while signed out is kept as the pending route through sign-in and opened afterwards (§6.10).
  - `EditPlan(id)` is **in-app only**: neither the App Link parser nor the FCM payload parser ever produces it; only in-app navigation does (the "+" create, the runner's "Edit", a draft card tap). Its tab is Plans. A parser unit test asserts that no URL or push payload maps to `EditPlan` (iOS `AppRoute.swift` comment "In-app only: no link or push opens it"; `AthleteAuthoredPlansCoreTests.theEditorRouteIsInAppOnlyOnThePlansTab`).
  - The shared view's import role comes from `/me.role`, the active role: `coach` → coach import, `athlete` → athlete import (with the athlete authoring graph), anything else → no import button (`RoleTabsView.swift` `.sharedPlan`).

#### 6.14.4 Behavior rules (athlete authoring mode)

Every rule below is iOS code at HEAD; the editor in authoring mode **hides** assignment, templates, the library link section, the bench/remove "why?" prompts, the 409 bench-choice fallback sheet (§7.3.5), the picker's "New move" and "Create “…”" and "Draft with AI" (#53, §7.3.8a), and coach-voiced copy (iOS §6.14 E).

| Area | Rule (verbatim copy in quotes) | iOS source |
|---|---|---|
| Create | "+" (FAB label "New plan") → `POST /athlete/plans` with no title → open `EditPlan(id)`; the title field opens already editing with placeholder "Name this plan" | `AthleteAuthoringControls.create`, `PlanDetailView` `autoEdit` |
| Create needs network | Creating and adding moves from the library need a connection (new ids come from the server); failure shows the error toast | QA §5a "Offline"; `PlanDetailModel.addMoves` |
| Prompt above moves | "What do you want to work on?" (coach: "What does *Greta* need to work on?") | `PlanDetailModel.workOnPrompt` |
| Add moves button | "Add moves from the library" (coach: "Add moves", since iOS #129) | `PlanDetailView` |
| Picker empty state | "No moves to choose from yet. Pick your sport in Goals and the Gradus move library appears here." | `PlanDetailView` `MovePickerSheet(emptyMessage:)` |
| No new moves, no AI drafts | The athlete's picker has no "New move" and no "Create “…”", and no form shows "Draft with AI" (#53: athletes have no personal library; `canCreateMoves` is false when authoring) | `PlanDetailModel.canCreateMoves`; `NewMoveTests.athletesGetNeitherNewMovesNorAIDrafts` |
| Primary button | Not active: "Activate plan" (paper-plane icon). Active: "Share plan" (share icon) | `primaryActionTitle`, `authoringActionBar` |
| Activation blockers (shown above the bar with an info icon, and as an error toast if tapped) | "Give the plan a name to activate it." then "Add at least one move to activate it." | `activationBlocker` |
| Activate | `POST .../status {status:"active"}`; toast "Plan activated"; editor pops. No cap, no conflict sheet (activate three: none benched) | `activateTapped`; QA §5a |
| Bench (active only) | Dialog title "Bench this plan?", message "It moves to Benched in your plans until you activate it again. Nothing is deleted.", buttons "Bench" (destructive), "Keep it active". **No "why?"** | `authoringActionBar` |
| Delete (draft or benched) | "Delete" (destructive chip) → dialog `Delete "<title or this plan>"?` / "This can't be undone." / "Delete" / "Cancel"; toast "Plan deleted". Active plans show Bench instead (bench first) | `actionBarButtons`; `AthleteAuthoringTests.aBenchedOrDraftPlanDeletesButAnActiveOneAsksToBeBenchedFirst` |
| Remove a move | Removes at once (no prompt) | `whyPromptApplies` is false when authoring |
| Bar layout | When `LocalIsAccessibilitySize` (§8.1: `fontScale ≥ 1.5`, the Android stand-in for iOS `dynamicTypeSize.isAccessibilitySize`) is true, the two buttons stack in a column so neither compresses | `authoringActionBar` (WCAG 1.4.10) |
| Share | `POST /plans/{id}/share-token`; Android share sheet (`Intent.ACTION_SEND`, `text/plain`, `EXTRA_TEXT` = "<title> — My workout on Gradus" + newline + `https://gradus.training/p/<token>`, chooser via `Intent.createChooser`) | `ShareSheet(items: [url, "\(title) — My workout on Gradus"])` |
| Dictated words | Disclosure "What you dictated" with the transcript (the athlete privacy caption was removed in iOS #134) | `PlanDetailView` |
| Voice | Mic FAB above "+" on the Plans tab (create) and an inline mic in the editor top bar (edit), **only when** `voiceAvailable`; a spoken athlete name is ignored (server); a dictation can't edit a plan that isn't theirs (server 403/404 shown as toast) | `AthleteAuthoringControls`, `PlanDetailView` toolbar; `AthleteAuthoringTests.aDictatedPlanIsTheAthletesOwnDraftAndAnySpokenNameIsIgnored`, `aDictationCannotEditAPlanThatIsNotTheirs` |
| Voice offline (athlete) | **Never parked on the device**: toast "We couldn't reach Gradus, so your recording wasn't kept. Check your connection and dictate again." The clip file is deleted immediately. (Coach clips are parked, §7.4) | `VoiceCaptureModel.offline`; `AthleteAuthoringTests.anAthletesRecordingIsNeverParkedWhenOffline` |
| Voice overlay (athlete) | "TRY SAYING" prompts: create — "The moves you want to work on", "How many reps or how many minutes", "A cue to remember for each move"; edit — "Add a move and how many", "Change a move's reps or minutes", "Update your notes and cues". No privacy line (removed in iOS #134; the AI permission screen names the vendors, §6.7.1a). Mic content descriptions: "Dictate a new plan" / "Add to this plan by voice" | `VoiceOverlay.prompts`, `VoiceCaptureButton` |
| Offline edits | Title, notes, move fields, reorder, remove, status queue on the **athlete** paths with toast "Saved — it syncs when you're back online."; a failed (0 / 5xx) status change queues on `/athlete/plans/{id}/status` | `PlanDetailModel.perform`, `setStatus`; `AthleteAuthoringTests.offlineEditsQueueOnTheAthleteRoutes`, `aFailedStatusChangeQueuesOnTheAthleteStatusRoute` |
| Read aloud | "Read this plan aloud" shows when the plan has moves (iOS #47; Android §6.7.4) | `NarrationStartButton` |
| Delete needs network | Deleting from the editor (athlete or coach) has **no outbox fallback**: any error shows the error toast and the editor stays open. Only list deletes queue (coach list, §7.3.1; athletes have no list delete) | `PlanDetailModel.delete()` |

**Where the athlete's own plans appear** (all role-aware captions come from the server fields, never computed from names):

| Viewer | Caption | iOS source |
|---|---|---|
| Athlete, list | "Mine" (coach plans: "Coach *Full Name*"; Gradus: "from Gradus"); drafts captioned "Draft" | `AthletePlanSummary.coachLine`, `RunnerPlansModel.rows` |
| Athlete, runner header | "Mine"; eyebrow over moves "Your plan" | `RunnerPlanDetailModel.headline`, `RunnerPlanDetailView` |
| Parent, list | "By *first name*" (coach plans: "*Athlete first* · Coach *Name*") | `ParentPlanSummary.coachLine` |
| Parent, runner | header "By *first name*", eyebrow "From *first name*"; parent can log practice on it; no "Message coach" | `RunnerPlanDetailModel.headline` |
| Coach, roster athlete detail | "By *first name*" (only active/benched) — §7.2 owns the screen | `CoachAthleteDetail.PlanSummary.attribution` |
| Coach, opening it | read-only editor, banner "Written by *first name*, read-only." | `PlanDetailView.readOnlyBanner` |
| Public share page / app shared view | "Plan by *first name*"; empty name → "Plan by an athlete" | `SharedPlan.attribution` |

#### 6.14.4a Athlete Library segment (`AthleteLibraryPane`)

The third segment, "Library", on the athlete's Plans tab (`RunnerPlansScreen`, shown only for an athlete with authoring wired; §7.6.1). It is the **read-only** Gradus curriculum for the athlete's sports (iOS §6.14 C, §7.8 "Seeded move library"; `FeaturePlans/AthleteAuthoring.swift` `AthleteLibraryView`, `AthleteLibraryModel`, `LibraryMoveRow`). There is no tap-to-add, no FAB and no move sheet here. Moves reach a plan only through the editor's `MovePickerSheet` ("Add moves from the library", §6.14.4).

**Data.** `GET /athlete/moves` with `If-None-Match`, loaded each time the pane appears (`.task`). Like iOS, the ETag and the library are kept **in memory only** in `AthleteLibraryViewModel`, and nothing is written to disk, so opening the pane offline for the first time shows the error state. A 304 keeps what is in memory. Load failures map to the server's message (`APIError.userMessage` equivalent). Caching the curriculum in Room is **(proposed, not iOS)** and is not part of 1.0 parity unless Mariah approves it (§12 N53).

**Layout, top to bottom (verbatim copy):**
1. Intro line (secondary text): "The Gradus move library for your sport. To use a move, open a plan and tap Add moves from the library."
2. Exactly one of these states, checked in this order:
   | Order | Condition | Shows |
   |---|---|---|
   | 1 | a load error, the library is empty, and no load has succeeded yet (`!hasLoaded`) | state view (wifi-off icon) title "Couldn't load the library", the error message, button "Try again" (reloads) |
   | 2 | loading and `!hasLoaded` | one redacted placeholder card reading "Loading moves…" |
   | 3 | the library has no moves | card "No moves to show yet. Pick your sport in Goals and the Gradus move library appears here." |
   | 4 | otherwise | search, sport chips, the grouped list |
   An error after a successful load leaves the content in place (no state view, no toast).
3. Search field (pill, leading search icon hidden from TalkBack): placeholder and content description "Search moves", autocorrect off (`KeyboardOptions(autoCorrectEnabled = false)`). When the query is not empty, a trailing clear icon button with content description "Clear search" empties it.
4. Sport chips, in a horizontally scrolling row, **only when the library has more than one sport**: "All" (selected when no sport is chosen), then one chip per sport present in the library (sport keys sorted; labels from the sport catalog, `deps.sportLabel`). Each chip is a ≥ 48 dp target.
5. The list: moves filtered by the sport chip and by the query (trimmed, lowercased, `contains` match on name, category **or** cue), grouped by `category`, with the categories sorted (plain string sort, as iOS `sorted()`). Each group has a collapsible `CategoryHeader` (§7.3.2; every category starts collapsed, a search opens all and ignores header taps; `athleteLibrary.section.<category>`) followed, when open, by its rows, with a divider after each row.
6. When the filtered result is empty: "No moves match that search." (this is the text for both a query and a sport chip).

**`LibraryMoveRow`.** The collapsed row is one button and **one TalkBack node**, at least 48 dp tall (iOS 44 pt min → Android 48 dp): name (bold), the uppercase mono target label ("10 REPS", "3 MINS", from `Move.targetLabel`), and a chevron (hidden from TalkBack) that rotates 180° when expanded. State description "Expanded" / "Collapsed". Tapping toggles expansion. The rotation and expand animate (≈200 ms), with no animation when the system's Remove animations setting is on (`Settings.Global.ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE == 0`, the iOS `accessibilityReduceMotion`). Expanded content, each part shown only when it is non-empty: description (secondary), cue with a leading quote icon (`Label(move.cue, systemImage: "quote.opening")`), why (caption, secondary). Expansion state lives in memory and is not persisted.

**Tests** (extends 6.14.6 #11): the state order (an error is shown only before the first success; an error after success keeps the content); the chips are hidden with one sport; "All" clears the chip; the query matches the cue; "No moves match that search." appears; there is no add affordance; the row's semantics read name, target and "Collapsed", and "Expanded" after a tap.

#### 6.14.5 Minors

Under-18 athletes (and athletes with no birthdate) author by typing only (#48); everything else (create, edit, activate, bench, delete, share, adopt) is identical (#35: minors **may** publish share links; the link carries a first name only). The Android QA pass repeats QA §5a with an adult athlete, a 13–17 athlete, a parent and a coach linked to each.

#### 6.14.6 Tests (port of iOS `AthleteAuthoringTests`, `AthleteAuthoredPlansTests`, `AthleteAuthoredPlansCoreTests`, `AthleteVoiceFlagTests`)

JUnit 5 + Turbine against a `FakePlansRepository` (the `PreviewPlansRepository` port, with `viewer = ATHLETE`):

1. Athlete deps write to `/api/v1/athlete/plans/p1` and have no roster; voice is off unless explicitly enabled.
2. A new draft opens with `title == ""`, prompt "What do you want to work on?", primary "Activate plan".
3. Activation blockers in order (name, then a move), then activation succeeds with no conflict lookup.
4. No cap: three own plans activate; none benched.
5. Curriculum moves copy in with `moveId == null` and no library link.
6. No why prompt on bench or move removal; bench sends `{"status":"benched"}` only.
7. Draft and benched delete; active shows Bench.
8. Offline edits and failed status changes queue on athlete paths (and never satisfy `isPlansPath`).
9. Voice: dictated plan is the athlete's draft; offline athlete clip is not written to disk; a coach clip still is.
10. Shared plan by an athlete reads "Plan by Elsie"; adoption returns a plan that is active.
11. Library view model filters by sport chip and search (name, category, cue; case-insensitive) and groups by category, categories sorted.
12. Runner list: own plans captioned "Mine"; "Mine" filter shows only own; Drafts status exists only when authoring is wired for an athlete; the Library segment exists only for an authoring athlete; empty messages (§7.8); a parent sees "By Elsie"; runner view of an own plan has `canEdit` and no coach to message.
13. Wire: `PlanDetail` decodes with and without `source`/`authorFirstName`; `AthletePlans` decodes with and without `drafts` and an old cached JSON stays readable; caption rules for coach, Gradus and athlete rows; `/me` `athleteVoiceToPlan`: only `true` allows voice (`false` and missing are off; an old cached `/me` without the field decodes as off).
14. No New move and no Draft with AI when authoring: `canCreateMoves` is false, the form's `canDraft` is false, and nothing calls `PUT /coach/moves` or `POST /coach/moves/draft` (#53).
15. Library categories (iOS #150): categories start closed; a tap opens one; a query opens all and a header tap during a query changes nothing; the picker's closed header shows the picked count.

### 6.15 Wear OS, headphones-first

Decisions A3 (Wear OS in 1.0, same Play listing), A50, A51 and iOS #36, #47, #48, #51, #54; iOS §6.15, §7.15, §10.11; reference implementation `gradus-ios/Packages/FeatureWatch/**`, `GradusWatch/**`. **Why** (iOS §6.15): coaches are rinkside with their hands busy; athletes and parents run plans on the ice or in the gym. The watch must be usable **without looking**: Gradus speaks, the user talks back.

#### 6.15.1 Platform constraints and how Android meets them

| iOS constraint (watchOS) | Wear OS fact | Android decision |
|---|---|---|
| No speech-recognition framework on watchOS; every "voice in" is a recorded clip transcribed by the server | Wear OS can have `SpeechRecognizer` | **Same as iOS:** a recorded clip sent to the server (§6.7.2). Parity, one transcription pipeline, vocabulary hints, and #48 (minors never send audio anywhere) all point the same way |
| Voice out = on-device `AVSpeechSynthesizer`, offline | Google's Wear OS TTS engine ships on Wear OS 4+ with English preloaded; the first use after boot takes about 10 s to warm up; Google says the engine is not meant for very long reads (verify the current guidance) | Android `TextToSpeech` on the watch, default engine, Automatic voice pick only (§6.7.5). **Pre-warm** the engine when the signed-in home appears (create the `TextToSpeech` instance, no speech). Plan reads are segmented per move (§6.7.4), so each utterance is short. If the watch has no English TTS voice, the player says "Read aloud isn't available on this watch." and stays visible (text) |
| Long-form audio keeps playing through AirPods with the wrist down (`audio` background mode, `.longFormAudio`) | A Wear app is stopped from the foreground when the screen goes to ambient/off unless it runs a foreground service | Plan reads and briefings run in a **foreground service of type `mediaPlayback`** that owns the `TextToSpeech` and the `NarrationPlayer`, with a **Wear OS Ongoing Activity** (`androidx.wear:wear-ongoing`) so the read appears on the watch face and in Recents and the user can return with one tap. The service stops when the read finishes, is stopped, or the screen that started it is left via back |
| Recording cannot run in the background on watchOS; a clip is spoken with the screen awake | Wear OS allows a microphone foreground service | **Parity:** no background recording. While a recorder screen is `RECORDING`, keep the screen on (`FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON`); leaving the screen cancels and deletes the clip, as on iOS (`discard()` on disappear) |
| Long-form audio only plays through Bluetooth headphones; watchOS shows its route picker when none is connected | Wear OS guidance: start media only when a suitable output (`TYPE_BLUETOOTH_A2DP`, `TYPE_BLE_HEADSET`, `TYPE_BLE_SPEAKER`, `TYPE_BLE_BROADCAST`) is connected; the built-in speaker is not for media; Wear OS 5+ has a system media output switcher; older devices use the Bluetooth settings intent | See 6.15.4 |
| No Realtime, no watch push tokens; the phone's notifications mirror; a tap on a mirrored message opens that conversation in the watch app (#54) | Phone notifications bridge to a paired Wear OS watch by default; a bridged notification's tap and actions run only on the phone | **Same, plus one exception:** no Supabase Realtime and no FCM token on the watch. Keep default bridging (never `NO_BRIDGING` in the manifest), so the 15-minute "up next" push and every other phone notification appears on the wrist. Message notifications are the exception: while signed in and allowed to post, the Wear app excludes bridge tag `gradus_message` at run time and posts its own copy from the phone's Data Layer forward, so its tap can open the conversation (§6.15.8, A51) |
| No voice notes from the wrist in 1.0; message replies from the wrist are text (#54) | Wear's `RemoteInput` offers voice input, the keyboard and emoji, and returns text | Same: replies by voice input, keyboard or quick reply arrive as text, for every role; Gradus never receives audio (§6.15.8, §7.15.7) |
| Hands-free navigation by voice inside the app is not possible and not promised | Same practical limit | Same: raise wrist, tap one large button, talk or listen |

#### 6.15.2 Packaging, versions, distribution

- **Module** `:wear` in `mariah-gill/gradus-android` (A7), Compose for Wear OS with Wear Material 3 (`androidx.wear.compose:compose-material3`) themed with Gradus dark tokens (the wrist is always dark; iOS forces `.dark` because the system clock overlays the app). Shared modules (`:core:api`, `:core:data` with its `audio` and `narration` packages, `:core:design` tokens, and `:feature:watch`'s shared logic, §9.1) compile for both the phone and the watch; phone-only modules (Credential Manager, BiometricPrompt, Glance, Play Integrity, FCM) are not dependencies of `:wear` (the Android counterpart of iOS's five platform guards around `UIApplication`, `LocalAuthentication`, MetricKit, `UIFont` and audio-session options).
- **applicationId `training.gradus.app` for both the phone app and the Wear app**, same signing key (Play App Signing). The Wear Data Layer only connects apps with the same package name and signature, so this is required, and it is the equivalent of iOS embedding `training.gradus.app.watchkitapp` in the iPhone binary under one record.
- **Distribution:** the Wear OS app is uploaded to the **same Play listing** (A3) on the Wear OS form factor's track, with its own `versionCode` (`200000 + run number` against the phone's `100000 + run number`, A16, §9.6, so the two never collide under one applicationId; verify Play's current rule for multiple form factors in one listing once the Console account exists, A8). Wear OS screenshots (round, at least one per workflow) go in the listing (Appendix D).
- **Standalone flag (proposed):** `com.google.android.wearable.standalone = false`. The watch gets its session only from the signed-in Gradus phone app (6.15.3), so it is not usable without the phone app, which is what "non-standalone" declares. At runtime it is still independent like iOS (`WKRunsIndependentlyOfCompanionApp`): its own session and its own network calls, and it keeps working away from the phone until the 14-day lease ends. Recorded as A26; revisited only if Play's Wear quality review objects.
- **Minimum version (proposed):** Wear OS 4 (`minSdk 33`) for `:wear`, because the Google Wear TTS engine the read-aloud depends on ships with Wear OS 4+. `targetSdk`/`compileSdk` per A6. iOS's equivalent floor is watchOS 11.
- **QA device (proposed):** Google Pixel Watch 3 or later, paired with Mariah's Pixel. Simulator equivalent: the Wear OS emulator (round, large and small) paired with a phone emulator through Android Studio's Wear OS pairing assistant (§5.2).
- **Manifest features:** the `:wear` manifest declares `<uses-feature android:name="android.hardware.type.watch" android:required="true"/>` (without it Play does not serve the build to watches) and the `com.google.android.wearable.standalone` meta-data (below); the phone manifest declares neither.
- **Installation:** iOS embeds the watch app in the iPhone binary so it installs with the phone app (`project.yml`, `WKCompanionAppBundleIdentifier`). On Android the user installs the Wear app from Google Play on the watch (it appears under apps on your phone) or from Play on the phone choosing the watch as the device. **No in-app "install on watch" prompt in 1.0** (the iOS phone app has no watch UI). Verify Play's auto-install behavior on the Pixel Watch (verify).
- **Permissions in the Wear manifest:** `INTERNET`, `RECORD_AUDIO`, `WAKE_LOCK`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK`, `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` (Ongoing Activity notification). No location, no body sensors, no health permissions. **`POST_NOTIFICATIONS` is a runtime permission on API 33+** (every supported Wear version): request it in context the first time Play is tapped or the Messages screen opens (an Android addition; iOS has no equivalent prompt for watch audio). If it is denied, the foreground service still runs and the read continues; only the Ongoing Activity chip is missing; message notifications keep bridging from the phone (§6.15.8). Never block a read on it. The complication service is protected by `BIND_COMPLICATION_PROVIDER` (§6.15.7); no other permission is added.
- **Data safety** (one form for the listing, covering the phone and Wear OS builds together): Audio → Voice or sound recordings: collected, not shared (service provider), optional (used only by coaches' and adult athletes' voice features), purpose App functionality (§6.11.9 owns the form). Do **not** mark it "processed ephemerally": the transcription processor retains audio under its own terms (#48: ElevenLabs keeps speech-to-text audio and transcripts unless an Enterprise account turns on zero retention); in-app copy promises only that Gradus doesn't store a recording. The watch adds no data types beyond the phone's (the iOS watch privacy manifest lists only user ID, audio data and other user content, `GradusWatch/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`); no tracking, no third-party SDKs on the watch.
