- **No usage analytics on the watch:** the Wear app records no usage events (the iOS watch has none; no analytics code in `FeatureWatch` or `GradusWatch`). §6.12 applies to the phone only.
- **Microphone rationale** (iOS `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` on the watch): before the system permission prompt, the recorder screen's hint already says why; if the permission was denied once, show the rationale text "Gradus records what you say about a lesson or a plan and turns it into plan changes. Gradus doesn't store the recording." with a button that requests again.
- **Debug-only launch extras** mirror iOS: `-GradusMock <role>` → intent extra `gradusMock = coach | parent… | athlete… | athleteMinor`; `-GradusWatchOpen plans|first-plan|upnext|first-lesson|first-wrapup|record|drafts|first-draft|messages|first-room` → extra `gradusWatchOpen`; `-GradusWatchSignedIn` → `gradusWatchSignedIn` (start signed in without a paired phone, for screenshots); `-GradusWatchAutoplay` → `gradusWatchAutoplay`; `-GradusLeaseSeconds <n>` → `gradusLeaseSeconds`. Compiled out of release builds. Used for screenshots and emulator checks.

#### 6.15.3 The phone ↔ watch link (WatchConnectivity → Wear Data Layer)

The protocol is ported **message for message** from iOS `CompanionMessage.swift`, `PhoneCompanion.swift`, `WatchCompanion.swift`, `WatchLease.swift`, `WatchLink.swift`, `WCSessionLink.swift`, `LoopbackWatchLink.swift`, and the server route `POST /auth/companion` (`src/lib/api/companion-session-route.ts`). Where the iOS PRD §10.11 W0 note says the session goes over `transferUserInfo`, **the code at HEAD wins**: tokens travel **only** in a live message and its reply, never queued (iOS `CompanionMessage` doc comment, test `aTokenIsNeverQueuedOnlySentLive`).

**Transport mapping.**

| iOS (`WatchLink` protocol) | Android (`WatchLink` interface in `:feature:watch`) |
|---|---|
| `send(message)` = `WCSession.sendMessage` with `replyHandler`, live only, throws `.unreachable`; the receiver answers through the same reply closure and answers a malformed payload with `[:]` (`WCSessionLink.swift`) | The Data Layer's built-in RPC: `MessageClient.sendRequest(nodeId, "/gradus/companion", bytes)` → `Task<ByteArray>` (the reply). The receiver registers `MessageClient.addRpcService(rpcService, "/gradus/companion")` while running, and the phone's `WearableListenerService.onRequest(...)` (a `WearableListenerService` is an `RpcService`) covers a cold phone. An unparseable request is answered with an empty map (iOS replies `[:]`). The `sendRequest` task failing (e.g. `TARGET_NODE_NOT_CONNECTED`) is `Unreachable`; an empty or unparseable reply is "no message". A client-side timeout (proposed 8 s) wraps the task only as a safety net (Android addition). Requests are not persisted by the Data Layer, which keeps the iOS rule that a token is never parked on disk |
| `waitUntilReachable(timeout: 4 s)` (activation and reachability lag at launch) | Up to 4 s polling `NodeClient.connectedNodes` / `CapabilityClient` for a reachable peer before throwing `Unreachable` |
| `isReachable` | A connected node that advertises the peer capability: phone advertises `gradus_phone`, watch advertises `gradus_watch` (in `res/values/wear.xml`), looked up with `CapabilityClient.getCapability(..., FILTER_REACHABLE)` |
| `peerInstalled` (phone: paired and watch app installed; watch: always true) | Phone: `getCapability("gradus_watch", FILTER_ALL)` has a node. Watch: always true |
| `enqueue(message)` = `transferUserInfo`, only for `.signedOut`, delivered when the other side is next reachable; stale `signedOut` transfers cancelled first so only one is pending | `DataClient.putDataItem` at the fixed path `/gradus/companion/signedOut` (`PutDataMapRequest`, `setUrgent()`), payload `kind`, `userID`, `at`. One fixed path means a newer sign-out **replaces** an older one (the iOS "one pending sign-out" rule). The receiver handles it, then deletes the item. No secret is ever put in a DataItem |
| `activate()`; phone re-activates on `sessionDidDeactivate` (watch switch) | Register listeners; the phone also declares a `WearableListenerService` for `/gradus/companion` (requests) and `/gradus/companion/signedOut` (data item) so a request from the watch **wakes the phone app** when it is not running (iOS wakes the iPhone app in the background). The **watch** also declares a `WearableListenerService` for `/gradus/companion/signedOut` and `/gradus/notify/` (data items), so a queued sign-out wakes the Wear app and clears the watch face at once (the iOS complication-transfer wake, W7) and a forwarded message notification posts with the app closed (§6.15.7, §6.15.8). A watch switch needs nothing: nodes are looked up per call |
| Log activation and reachability only, never contents | Same: log node availability, never message bytes |
| `LoopbackWatchLink` (tests, previews; `flushQueued()` = coming back in range) | `LoopbackWatchLink` in `:feature:watch` test fixtures with the same API, used by every companion test |

**Message encoding.** A small key/value map (kotlinx.serialization JSON bytes) with the same keys as iOS: `kind`, `access`, `refresh`, `expiresIn`, `userID`, `reason`, `at` (seconds since 1970, double). Kinds and parse rules (an empty or unrecognised map is "no message"):

| Kind | Direction | Fields | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `needSession` | watch → phone, live | — | "I have no session; mint me one." |
| `session` | phone → watch, reply or live push | `access`, `refresh` (non-empty), `expiresIn`, `userID?` | Invalid if either token is empty or `expiresIn` missing |
| `signedOut` | either way, queued and live | `userID?`, `at?` | Receiver ignores it if about another account (case-insensitive), or if it predates the receiver's last word from the other side by more than the 2 s clock skew |
| `unavailable` | phone → watch, reply | `reason` ∈ `phoneSignedOut`, `tryLater`, `rateLimited`, `failed` | — |
| `checkIn` | watch → phone, live | `userID` (non-empty) | Secret-free "are you still signed in as me?" |
| `alive` | phone → watch, reply | `userID?` | The phone is signed in, as this account |

**Phone side (`PhoneCompanion`).** Phone sign-in state is `UNKNOWN` (first moments of a launch, before the stored session is read), `SIGNED_OUT`, or `SIGNED_IN(userId)`.

- `needSession` → `UNKNOWN`: `unavailable(tryLater)`; `SIGNED_OUT`: `unavailable(phoneSignedOut)`; `SIGNED_IN`: mint → `session(tokens, userID)` or `unavailable(failed)`.
- `checkIn` → `UNKNOWN`: `unavailable(tryLater)`; `SIGNED_OUT`: `unavailable(phoneSignedOut)`; `SIGNED_IN`: `alive(userID)`. Never a secret. A phone still starting never answers "signed out".
- Mint = `POST /auth/companion` (authenticated by the phone's bearer, no body, returns `{accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn}`, rate limit 5 / 10 min, 422 `no_email` "This account has no email on file, so it can't sign in on a watch."). Throttle: no two mints within **20 s** (`minInterval`) → `unavailable(tryLater)`; 429 → `unavailable(rateLimited)`; any other failure → `unavailable(failed)` and the failure does not count against the throttle. The phone **keeps nothing**: the watch gets the only copy.
- `phoneDidSignIn()` (sign-in, session restore, account switch): record `signedInAt`; if a watch is installed and reachable, mint and push `session` live. Best effort; a watch that is away asks when it opens.
- `phoneDidSignOut(userId)`: if a watch is installed, enqueue `signedOut(userID, now)` and, if reachable, also send it live.
- `signedOut` from the watch → ignore if about another account or older than the phone's latest sign-in (> 2 s skew); else sign the phone out **without echoing back** (the phone's sign-out path must skip `phoneDidSignOut` for this case; iOS `isSigningOutForWatch`).
- **Cold phone woken by the watch** (iOS `AppModel.signOutForWatch`, `signInState` closure): when `WearableListenerService` wakes the phone process, the session store is `UNKNOWN` until it has been read, so `needSession` / `checkIn` answer `unavailable(tryLater)`. A `signedOut` from the watch first awaits `sessionStore.restore()` (idempotent) and acts only if a user is then signed in, so a sign-out the watch sent once is never consumed and lost. While a phone sign-out is running, `signInState` reports `SIGNED_OUT`.
- **Where `phoneDidSignIn()` is called** (iOS `AppModel`): after launch restore, after every sign-in, after an email-change link that signs this phone in, and after an account switch (which first calls `phoneDidSignOut(previousUserId)`).
- Only the phone exposes `/auth/companion` in its API client; the watch module has no binding for it (**no self-replication**, iOS §10.11 W0).

**Watch side (`WatchCompanion`).** Phases: `STARTING`, `SIGNED_IN`, `NEEDS_PHONE(message)`; `accountId` keys every signed-in screen so an account switch starts from nothing.

- Launch: restore the stored session. If there is one: if the lease has **not** run out, show signed-in at once; then check in (below); if the lease had run out, show nothing signed-in until the check-in answers. No stored session → request one.
- Request: send `needSession`; `unavailable(tryLater)` is retried **3 times, 2 s apart**, re-checking whether a push signed the watch in meanwhile; then apply the reply. Unreachable or no reply → `NEEDS_PHONE("Can't reach your phone. Keep it nearby with Gradus signed in, then try again.")`.
- Apply `session`: if already signed in as the same account (or the message names none), keep the working session and renew the lease; a different account → sign the old one out locally and adopt the new one (store tokens, renew lease); failure → "Couldn't sign in on this watch. Try again."
- Apply `unavailable` (only if not already signed in, since a refusal that crosses a push is stale): `phoneSignedOut` → "Sign in to Gradus on your phone first."; `tryLater` → "Almost there. Try again in a moment."; `rateLimited` → "Too many tries. Wait a few minutes, then try again."; `failed` → "Couldn't sign in right now. Try again."
- **Lease** (`WatchLease.DEFAULT_DURATION = 14 days`, a product setting; last contact stored in DataStore key `gradus.watch.lastPhoneContact`, not a secret). On launch and on every return to the foreground (`ON_RESUME`), if signed in: clamp a future timestamp to now; start a lease if none exists (an update never signs anyone out); send `checkIn`:
  - `alive(same user)` → renew the lease.
  - `alive(other user)` → end the session ("Your phone is signed in as someone else.") and request a new session.
  - `unavailable(phoneSignedOut)` → end the session ("Signed out on your phone.") (finds a queued sign-out that never arrived).
  - any other reply = "not ready" → retry 3 times, 2 s apart.
  - no answer / error = "away": only then, and only if the same session is still current, if `now − lastContact > 14 days` end the session with "This watch hasn't been near your phone in 14 days, so it signed out to keep your account safe. Open Gradus on your phone, then try again." ("a while" if the duration is under one day).
  - A reply that arrives after the watch's session changed is dropped (generation counter).
- **On every `ON_RESUME`** (iOS `WatchCompanion.didBecomeActive`, called on `scenePhase == .active`): if a session is stored, run the check-in above; else if the phase is `NEEDS_PHONE`, call `requestSession()` automatically (the phone may have signed in since). `requestSession` is single-flight (`isRequesting`) and a no-op when a session exists; `checkLease` is also single-flight (`isChecking`).
- Ending the session locally also signs out the watch's own Supabase session on the server when the watch has a connection (it is the watch's own session; the phone is not told).
- `signedOut` from the phone: ignore if about another account or older than the last contact (> 2 s skew); else end the session ("Signed out on your phone.") without echoing.
- Watch sign-out (home "Sign out" → confirm dialog title "Sign out of Gradus?", message "This also signs you out on your phone.", buttons "Cancel" / "Sign out"): sign out locally, clear the lease, enqueue `signedOut(userID, now)` and send it live if reachable, phase `NEEDS_PHONE("You signed out. Sign in on your phone to use Gradus here.")`.
- Every phase change is announced to TalkBack ("Signing in from your phone.", "Signed in.", or the message). Any `NEEDS_PHONE` phase and any account change clear the plan cache, the coach day and the conversations (no plan or message stays on the wrist). `onSessionEnded` (however the session ends: a sign-out here or on the phone, the lease, or another account) also clears the watch-face snapshot, cancels the watch's message notifications and restores full bridging (§6.15.7, §6.15.8).

**Watch-side screens for these phases:** `STARTING`: progress indicator + "Signing in from your phone…"; `NEEDS_PHONE`: phone icon header "Gradus", the message, primary button "Try again" (calls request). (iOS uses "iPhone" in all these strings; Android says "phone": proposed copy substitution under A2.)

**Token storage on the watch:** the watch's Supabase session lives in an encrypted DataStore (Tink AEAD, key in the Android Keystore), never backed up (`dataExtractionRules` exclude it). Same as the phone's session store (§6.11).

**Limit stated plainly (inherited, iOS §10.11 W0):** the server cannot end the other device's session; a watch that is away when the phone signs out keeps a live session until it next hears from the phone or the lease ends. Server-side revocation (`companion_sessions` + `SECURITY DEFINER` delete of the paired `auth.sessions` row, `DELETE /auth/companion`) is queued for a point release for both platforms.

**Server change for Android: none required.** `POST /auth/companion` is platform-agnostic. Optional, docs-only and additive: change its OpenAPI summary from "…paired Apple Watch" to "…paired watch (Apple Watch or Wear OS)" (web PR, §4.1 rules).

Test expectations: port every case in iOS `CompanionHandoffTests.swift` onto `LoopbackWatchLink` (messages survive the wire; malformed payloads are not messages; no session → asks and signs in; stored session kept without asking; signed-out phone; unreachable phone + Try again; the 20 s throttle; a late refusal does not undo a push; "try later" retried then shown; server refusal not counted; rate limit worded in minutes; phone sign-in pushes to an open watch, not to an away one; another account replaces; same account left alone; sign-out both ways without echo; away watch signs out on return; reachable devices sign out at once; no paired watch queues nothing; tokens never queued; lease start/renew/clear; check-in on open and on foreground; missed queued sign-out found on open; starting phone never signs the watch out; other-account phone replaces; pre-lease session starts a lease; > 14 days away signs out, < 14 days does not; expired lease gets one chance when the phone is there; check-in never carries a secret; future timestamp clamped; "try later" is not absence; foreign or stale sign-outs ignored on both sides; a check-in reply crossing a push is dropped; every phase is spoken in words). Device QA on the Pixel Watch: pairing and queued `signedOut` delivery while the watch is away (the iOS simulator could not prove the queued path; same caution for the Wear emulator).

#### 6.15.4 Headphones on Wear OS (the audio route)

iOS has two route checks (`FeatureWatch/UpNext/WatchUpNext.swift` `WatchAudio`, `GradusCore/Narration/NarrationAudioRoute.swift`). Android implements both in `WatchAudio`:

- **Headphone output set** (iOS `WatchAudio.readyForPrompt`: `.bluetoothA2DP`, `.bluetoothLE`, `.bluetoothHFP`): `TYPE_BLUETOOTH_A2DP`, `TYPE_BLE_HEADSET`, `TYPE_BLE_SPEAKER`, `TYPE_BLE_BROADCAST`, and `TYPE_BLUETOOTH_SCO` (the HFP equivalent). Used by both checks below. Verify on the Pixel Watch that a SCO-only route actually plays TTS; if it does not, drop SCO from the set and record why.
- **`ready()`: for something the person asked to hear (Play a plan, Hear it on a read-back, Hear briefing, Repeat, Next/Previous from a pause).** If `AudioManager.getDevices(GET_DEVICES_OUTPUTS)` contains a headphone output from the set above → ready. Otherwise open the system output picker: on Wear OS 5+ the **media output switcher** (as Horologist's `launchOutputSelection()` does; verify the intent), else `Settings.ACTION_BLUETOOTH_SETTINGS` with `EXTRA_CONNECTION_ONLY = true`, `EXTRA_CLOSE_ON_CONNECT = true`, `android.bluetooth.devicepicker.extra.FILTER_TYPE = 1` (audio), `FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK | FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK`. When the user returns, re-check; still none → not ready, and the screen shows and announces **"Connect Bluetooth headphones to listen."** (iOS: "Connect AirPods or other Bluetooth headphones to listen."; AirPods is an Apple product name, so Android drops it; proposed copy substitution). This mirrors watchOS showing its route picker and `activate()` answering false when nothing was chosen.
- **`readyForPrompt()`: for words the watch says without being asked** (read-back results, the bench-choice question of the #52 409 fallback, wrap-up results, "Saved as a draft."). Only when one of those headphone types is **already** connected; never opens the picker over the buttons. The screen shows (and TalkBack announces) the same words either way.
- **Never speak through the watch's built-in speaker** (parity with watchOS long-form audio, and Wear OS guidance that speakers are not for media). Set TTS audio attributes `USAGE_MEDIA`, `CONTENT_TYPE_SPEECH`.
- **Headphones disconnect mid-read:** register an `AudioDeviceCallback`; when the last headphone output is removed while speaking, pause (Resume needs `ready()` again). iOS gets the same through the long-form route ending.
- **Recording with headphones:** if a Bluetooth headset input (`TYPE_BLUETOOTH_SCO` or `TYPE_BLE_HEADSET`) is present, call `MediaRecorder.setPreferredDevice(...)` to it, else the watch mic (iOS `.allowBluetooth` lets watchOS pick AirPods' mic). Verify on the Pixel Watch that the preferred-device route works without communication mode; if it does not, record from the watch mic (acceptable: the watch is on the wrist near the mouth).

#### 6.15.5 Offline and caching on the watch

- **Plan cache** (`WatchPlanCache`, port of iOS `FileWatchPlanCache`): one JSON file per account under `filesDir/WatchPlans/<userId>.json` (user id reduced to `[A-Za-z0-9-]`), written atomically, excluded from backup. Snapshot = `role`, `voiceToPlan` (nullable; a copy without it counts as "no" for athletes and "yes" for coaches), `items`, `details` (plan id → full plan detail), `savedAt`. Android's credential-encrypted storage is the counterpart of iOS `completeFileProtectionUntilFirstUserAuthentication`.
- Load: show the saved copy at once, then fetch; save the list and **prefetch up to 10** listed plans' details for offline listening; keep only details still listed; a full disk only costs the offline copy.
- Transient failure (no connection, 429, 5xx, `rate_limited`, `rate_limiter_unavailable`, `api_disabled`) → keep the saved copy and show "No connection. These are saved on this watch."; nothing saved → "No connection, and no plans saved on this watch yet. Try again near your phone or Wi-Fi." Other failure → "Couldn't load your plans. Try again."
- A **refusal** (401, 403, 404…) wipes the saved copy (it is no longer this account's to read); a plan the server refuses on open is removed from the list and the copy.
- Sign-out or a phone account switch → `clearAll()`; at launch, any other account's leftover file is removed; a load or fetch that started for the previous account never writes back (generation counter). The refresh is owned by the model, so leaving the screen that started it does not cancel the offline save.
- The watch also caches **no** recordings: the recorder deletes the file as soon as recording stops (the clip is held in memory until sent), and a launch sweep deletes any `cacheDir/voice-*.m4a` left by an app stopped mid-recording (iOS `WatchRecordings.sweep`, test `leftoverRecordingsAreSweptAndNothingElse`). There is **no watch outbox**: unlike the phone's coach FAB, a watch clip that cannot be sent stays in memory for "Try again" only and is gone when the screen is left (iOS §6.15 mentions "a watch outbox for the rink"; the code at HEAD has none, and the code wins).

#### 6.15.6 Minors on the wrist

No voice → plan for athletes under 18 or with no birthdate (#48, withdrawing #37). The watch shows "Record a plan" only when the role is coach, or the role is athlete and `GET /me` says `athleteVoiceToPlan == true`; the last answer is cached with the plan snapshot so an offline launch keeps the same home. The record route itself also refuses to render unless `voiceToPlan` is true. Drafts, hearing a plan and activating it stay for minors. The server refuses their audio anyway (403 `text_only`). Everything else is role-gated as on the phone.

#### 6.15.7 On the watch face: the Gradus complication (W7, #51, A50)

iOS #51 (2026-10-10), iOS §6.15 "On the watch face", §10.11 W7; gradus-ios `fd78810` (#126): `GradusWatchWidgets/GradusComplication.swift`, `GradusWidgetData/WatchComplicationSnapshot.swift`, `FeatureWatch/Complication/WatchComplicationRefresher.swift`, `GradusWatch/GradusWatchApp.swift`, `WatchCompanion.onSessionEnded`.

**What it is.** A complication data source in the Wear app that any Wear OS watch face can put in a slot. For a coach, it shows the next lesson today and moves through the day on its own. For everyone else, for a signed-out watch, for a day with no current information, and for another day, it shows the Gradus mark as a one-tap launcher. Nothing new is collected or sent.

**iOS → Wear OS mapping.**

| iOS (WidgetKit) | Wear OS | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GradusWatchWidgets` extension, `StaticConfiguration` kind `GradusComplication`, display name "Gradus" | `GradusComplicationService : SuspendingTimelineComplicationDataSourceService` in `:wear` (`androidx.wear.watchface:watchface-complications-data-source-ktx`). Manifest: `android:label="Gradus"`, `android:icon` = the monochrome mark, `android:permission="android.permission.BIND_COMPLICATION_PROVIDER"`, `exported="true"` with the `android.support.wearable.complications.action.COMPLICATION_UPDATE_REQUEST` filter, meta-data `SUPPORTED_TYPES = "SHORT_TEXT,LONG_TEXT,MONOCHROMATIC_IMAGE"` and `UPDATE_PERIOD_SECONDS = 0` (push updates only) | Runs in the Wear app's process, so no App Group is needed. |
| `.accessoryCircular`, `.accessoryCorner` | `SHORT_TEXT` (monochromatic image = mark, text = time or "Now") | Wear faces put `SHORT_TEXT` in round and corner slots. |
| `.accessoryRectangular`, `.accessoryInline` | `LONG_TEXT` (title = header, text = the line under it, monochromatic image = mark) | Wear has no inline slot. `LONG_TEXT` covers both. |
| The mark alone | `MONOCHROMATIC_IMAGE` (always the mark, tinted by the face) | The launcher form. `SMALL_IMAGE` is for full-colour images and is not offered; `RANGED_VALUE` is not offered because iOS shows no gauge. |
| `privacySensitive()` names, hidden while locked or when the face hides sensitive data | **Never shown.** Wear OS has no redaction flag on `ComplicationData`, and a data source gets no lock or unlock callback, so it cannot hide a name it already published. The face always uses iOS's redacted rendering (§7.15.6). §12 N75. | Conservative state (§4.3 rule 6). The iOS source says "a watch face is on show to anyone nearby". |
| Timeline (`getTimeline`: an entry now, at every lesson start and end, an hour before each start, and the mark at midnight; `.atEnd` / `.never`) | `onComplicationRequest` returns `ComplicationDataTimeline(defaultComplicationData = mark, timelineEntries = …)`. Each `TimelineEntry(TimeInterval(entry.date, nextEntry.date), data)` comes from the ported `WatchComplicationTimeline.entries(...)`, and midnight → mark is the default after the last entry. **Belt and braces:** the app also sets an inexact `AlarmManager.setAndAllowWhileIdle` for the next entry boundary, whose receiver calls `requestUpdateAll()` (verify that Watch Face Format faces honour data-source timelines on the Pixel Watch; if they do, the alarm is harmless). | The "an hour before" entries exist on iOS only for Smart Stack relevance. Wear has no counterpart, so a boundary whose state is unchanged produces no Wear entry (`startsSoon` is not ported). |
| Smart Stack relevance (score 1 during a lesson, 0.6 from an hour before) | None (Wear OS has no Smart Stack) | §12 N76 (Tile). |
| `widgetURL(gradus://watch/up-next)` on a lesson | `setTapAction(PendingIntent)`: an explicit-component intent to the Wear `MainActivity` with data `gradus://watch/up-next` (`FLAG_IMMUTABLE`). Mark and done: the same activity with no data (opens Home). | Explicit component, so no exported scheme filter is needed (§6.11.5). |
| App Group snapshot `WatchComplicationSnapshot` (`version`, `day` `yyyy-MM-dd`, `lessons[{firstName,startMinute,endMinute}]`, `complete`, `writtenAt`) in `UserDefaults` `group.training.gradus.app` key `watchComplicationSnapshot` | The same JSON shape (kotlinx.serialization, `currentVersion = 1`) in a DataStore file `noBackupFilesDir/watch_complication.json`, excluded from backup (A24). `hasSnapshot` = "bytes are stored", readable or not, so a build that can't read an older format keeps refreshing and overwrites it. `firstName` is kept so the stored shape matches iOS (§12 N75 may switch names on); the data source does not render it. | One snapshot per watch, not per account. Cleared on every session end. |
| `WatchComplicationRefresher` (`refresh`, `clear`, `open(url)`, `takePendingUpNext`, `limit = 10`, `backgroundInterval = 30 min`, `backgroundTimeout = 10 s`) | `WatchComplicationRefresher` in `:feature:watch`, a 1:1 port. `reload` = `ComplicationDataSourceUpdateRequester.create(ctx, ComponentName(ctx, GradusComplicationService::class.java)).requestUpdateAll()`. | See "Refresh" and "Clear" below. |
| Background app refresh (`.backgroundTask(.appRefresh(...))`, `scheduleBackgroundRefresh` 30 min ahead, rebooked on the way to the background, only while `showsLessons`) | WorkManager unique periodic work `complication-refresh`, 30 min, `NetworkType.CONNECTED`, `ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP`. It is enqueued only while `showsLessons` **and** at least one complication instance is active (`onComplicationActivated`/`onComplicationDeactivated` keep the active ids in DataStore), and cancelled when either stops being true. | iOS gets background refresh only while the complication is on the active face; activation tracking is the Wear equivalent. |
| `.backgroundTask(.watchConnectivity)` and the phone's `transferCurrentComplicationUserInfo` for a queued sign-out | Nothing extra: the phone's sign-out DataItem is `setUrgent()`, and the Wear app now declares a `WearableListenerService` for `/gradus/companion/signedOut` (§6.15.3), which wakes the app to handle it at once. | |
| Fonts registered in the extension | None: watch faces draw complication text in their own fonts. | |
| `GradusIconMark` (three upright rounded bars, measured from the 1024 pt icon: bar width 147/512, gap 35.5/512, heights 318/512, 1, 236/512, caps radius = width/2) | Vector drawable `ic_gradus_mark` with the same geometry, used as the monochromatic image, the data source icon and the notification small icon. It is not the help bubble's horizontal-bar chip. | |

**Refresh** (`WatchComplicationRefresher.refresh(timeout?)`): call `GET /coach/up-next` for the watch's local day, minute and day of week with `limit = 10`. Write a snapshot containing `day`, the lessons' first names and minutes, `complete = lessons.size < 10` and `writtenAt`. Request an update only when the day, the lessons or `complete` changed, then (re)schedule the background work. A 401 or 403 → `clear()`. Any other failure, slowness or offline state keeps the face as it is and keeps the background work scheduled while `showsLessons`. A generation counter bumped by `clear()` drops a fetch that started for the last account.

**When it runs.**
- When a coach's Home shows: Home's load calls `syncComplication()`, which refreshes if the role is coach and clears otherwise.
- On every `ON_RESUME` of the Wear app.
- From the background worker. That worker first runs `WatchCompanion.mayRefreshInBackground()`: handle any pending `/gradus/companion/signedOut` DataItem (`DataClient.getDataItems`), then return true only if a session is stored and `now − lastPhoneContact ≤ 14 days`. It never asks the phone and never signs out on the lease. If it returns false → `clear()`. Otherwise → `refresh(timeout = 10 s)`.
- On `ACTION_TIMEZONE_CHANGED` and `ACTION_TIME_CHANGED` (both exempt from the implicit-broadcast limits) → `requestUpdateAll()`, so the timeline is recomputed in the new local day. This is an Android addition; the iOS timeline reads `autoupdatingCurrent` at render time.

**Clear.** `WatchCompanion.onSessionEnded` (new; port of the iOS hook) runs `complication.clear()` however the watch's session ends: the watch's own sign-out, a sign-out from the phone (live or queued), an account switch on the phone, or the lease expiring. It also runs after a 401/403 and when a non-coach role's Home shows. `clear()` bumps the generation, drops a pending Up next tap, deletes the snapshot and requests an update only if a snapshot was there.

**Tap → Up next.** On the lesson states, the Wear `MainActivity` receives `gradus://watch/up-next` and calls `complication.open(uri)`, which sets `pendingUpNext`. Home opens `[UpNext]` once the role is known and is coach. It waits, exactly as a tapped message does, while a clip is recording or a screen that holds unsent work is open (`WatchRoute.holdsUnsentWork`: Record a plan, Draft, Wrap-up). A non-coach tap is consumed and opens nothing beyond Home. A sign-out drops it.

**Privacy and Play.** No new data type. The snapshot holds first names and times on the watch only, never backed up. The Data safety form is unchanged (iOS: App Privacy unchanged, privacy manifest reason `1C8F.1` for the App Group defaults; Android has no counterpart declaration).

#### 6.15.8 Message notifications on the wrist (#54, A51)

**iOS behavior.** The phone's notifications mirror to Apple Watch. Apple delivers the **default tap** on a mirrored notification to the watch app, which opens that conversation (`WatchNotificationDelegate`), and runs **Reply** on the iPhone. A Reply that does reach the watch is sent with the watch's own session (`WatchMessaging.perform(.reply)`: online once, no outbox, a local notice on the watch).

**Why Wear OS needs its own copy.**
- A bridged notification's tap and actions can only fire the phone's `PendingIntent`s ("Open on phone"). Wear OS's bridging API has no way to make a bridged tap open the watch app.
- The Wear app has no FCM token (A26).
- So the phone forwards each room's notification over the Data Layer, and the signed-in Wear app posts it locally and excludes the bridged duplicate. This is Google's documented pattern for an app that has its own watch notifications: bridge tags plus dismissal IDs.

**Mechanics.**
- **Bridging switch (watch).**
  - While the Wear app is signed in **and** can post notifications (`NotificationManagerCompat.areNotificationsEnabled()` and the watch's `messages` channel not blocked), it sets `BridgingManager.fromContext(ctx).setConfig(BridgingConfig.Builder(ctx, true).addExcludedTags(setOf("gradus_message")).build())`.
  - In every other state it sets `BridgingConfig.Builder(ctx, true).build()`, so everything bridges and the phone's copy, with its own Reply (§6.6.11), reaches the wrist.
  - Re-applied at launch, on every `ON_RESUME`, on every `WatchCompanion` phase change, and in `onSessionEnded`.
  - (Verify the `BridgingManager` behaviour on the Pixel Watch; the runtime config overrides any manifest bridge mode.)
- **Forwarding (phone).** On each `message` push, after posting its own notification, the phone writes `PutDataMapRequest.create("/gradus/notify/room/<roomId>").setUrgent()`, but only when some node advertises `gradus_watch` (`FILTER_ALL`). It carries:
  - `roomId`, `uid`, `category`
  - `title` (the latest push title)
  - `messages`: the same last 7 `(sender, text, sentAt)` the phone's `MessagingStyle` holds
  - `postedAt`

  One item per room, so a newer push replaces it, and an item delivered after a disconnection carries the whole stack. The phone **deletes** the item whenever it cancels that room's notification (room read on the phone, a Reply taken, sign-out). No secret is ever in it.
- **Posting (watch).** The Wear app declares a `WearableListenerService` for `DATA_CHANGED` on path prefix `/gradus/notify/` (and `/gradus/companion/signedOut`, §6.15.3).
  - **CHANGED, signed in, `postedAt` within 24 h** (the alert TTL, §6.6.2): post a local `MessagingStyle` notification. Its properties:
    - Channel `messages`: same id, name and description as the phone, `IMPORTANCE_HIGH`.
    - Tag `room:<id>`, `setDismissalId("room:<id>")`. Dismissing either copy dismisses both; dismissals are not otherwise synced when bridging is excluded.
    - Small icon `ic_gradus_mark`.
    - Content intent: explicit Wear `MainActivity`, data `gradus://rooms/<id>`, extra `uid`.
    - A Reply action with the same builder as §6.6.11 (`RemoteInput` key `gradus.reply`, label "Message", title "Reply", `setAuthenticationRequired(true)`, i.e. the watch must be unlocked), going to the Wear app's own non-exported `NotificationReplyReceiver`.
  - **Signed out:** post nothing (bridging is not excluded then).
  - **DELETED:** cancel `room:<id>`.
  - **Wear app in the foreground** (iOS `willPresent`): still post, and call `WatchMessaging.messageArrived(roomId)` so the list and an open thread refresh. The watch has no realtime.
- **A Reply on the watch's copy:**
  - The receiver cancels the notification, deletes the room's DataItem (which clears the phone's copy), and hands a `WatchNotificationAction.Reply` to `WatchMessaging.perform` in an expedited worker.
  - A mismatched `uid` gives the `otherAccount` notice and nothing is sent.
  - Otherwise it runs `NotificationReplySender` with the watch's own session and **no outbox**, as iOS does for a Reply delivered to the watch. On `sent` it refreshes the rooms; on any other outcome it posts the §6.6.11 notice on the watch.
  - Residual difference from iOS, recorded for QA: a watch-notification Reply never falls back to the phone's outbox.
- **A tap on the watch's copy** (iOS `WatchNotificationAction.from` → `.openRoom`):
  - A mismatched `uid` → the `otherAccount` notice; nothing opens.
  - Otherwise `pendingRoomId = roomId`, and Home opens `[Messages, Room(id)]` (also on a cold start).
  - It waits while a clip is recording or `holdsUnsentWork` (Record a plan, Draft, Wrap-up), and opens once the coach is done there.
- **Session end** (`onSessionEnded`, sign-out, account switch): cancel every watch message notification, clear `WatchMessaging`, and restore full bridging.
- **Text only, every role** (#32, #48; iOS "dictation and Scribble become text on the device and Gradus never receives audio"). Wear's `RemoteInput` and the thread's input (§7.15.7) offer voice input, the keyboard and emoji. The system turns speech into text, and Gradus receives only text, for minors too, as on iOS. Wear's speech recognition may run in a Google service rather than strictly on the device (verify); the product rule that Gradus never receives audio holds either way (§12 h4).
- **Permission.** The Wear app asks for `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` in context the first time the Messages screen opens (and at the existing first Play tap). Until it is granted, bridging stays on, so no message is lost from the wrist.

---

## 7. Feature requirements

Every requirement below applies the iOS 1.0 behavior named in its citation (iOS §, decision #, or gradus-ios source path), with the Android-native equivalent stated wherever iOS uses a platform component. Platform-wide rules are in §4.3; cross-cutting behaviors are in §7.13.

### 7.1 Sign-in, sign-up, and onboarding

Source of truth: gradus-ios HEAD `91c6af2` — `Gradus/Shell/{RootView,AppModel,SignUpFlowViews,AgeAssurance,RoleTabsView}.swift`, `Packages/FeatureAuth/**`, `Packages/FeatureOnboarding/**`, `GradusCore/Onboarding/*`, `GradusCore/Repositories/{OnboardingRepositories,FamilyOnboardingRepositories}.swift`; iOS PRD §6.4, §7.1, decisions #26, #27, #29–#31, #40, #46; QA.md §1–§2. Where the iOS PRD text and the code differ, the code wins and the difference is called out. All user-facing strings below are quoted from the Swift sources unless marked **(Android copy)**. Every `accessibilityIdentifier` becomes a Compose `Modifier.testTag` with the **same string**, so the QA rows and UI tests read the same on both platforms.

**Module layout (§9.1 owns the full list):** `:feature:auth` (sign-in, forgot/reset password, lock screen, terms sheet, provider buttons), `:feature:onboarding` (choosers, pre-account setup, account forms, role chooser, coach/parent/athlete onboarding, verify step, claim, invite entry, plan status, shared form components), `:core:data` (packages `agesignals`, `consent`, `onboarding`: models and rules ported 1:1 from `GradusCore/Onboarding`), `:app` shell (root state machine, routing, gates).

**Android-native equivalents used throughout this section.**

| iOS | Android |
|---|---|
| `NavigationStack(path:)` sign-up stack (`AppModel.SignUpStep`) | Navigation Compose nested graph `signUp` with type-safe `@Serializable` routes mirroring `SignUpStep` one for one; predictive back pops one step |
| `.fullScreenCover` (Terms, reset, parent approval) | Full-screen root destinations rendered by the root state machine above the nav host (not `Dialog`s, so a lock overlay can cover them) |
| `.sheet` with detents (forgot password, request a sport, date picker) | `ModalBottomSheet` (forgot password, request a sport); Material 3 `DatePickerDialog` for dates |
| `.alert` | Material 3 `AlertDialog` |
| `SignInWithAppleButton` + `ASAuthorizationController` | "Continue with Apple" button (Apple's published web button guidelines) launching the Apple **web** flow in an Auth Tab (`AuthTabIntent`), Custom Tab + App Link fallback (A5) |
| Google button (hidden on iOS until the client ID exists) | Credential Manager "Sign in with Google" (A5; shown) |
| `ShareLink` | Android Sharesheet (`Intent.ACTION_SEND`, `text/plain`, `EXTRA_TEXT`, `EXTRA_SUBJECT`) via `Intent.createChooser` |
| `UIPasteboard` + toast "Code copied" | `ClipboardManager.setPrimaryClip`; on API 33+ the system shows its own copy confirmation, so the Gradus toast is shown only on API ≤ 32 |
| `.textContentType(.username/.password/.newPassword/.emailAddress/.givenName/.familyName)` | Compose autofill `ContentType.Username`, `Password`, `NewPassword`, `EmailAddress`, `PersonFirstName`, `PersonLastName` (Google Password Manager offers to save, as iOS Keychain does; no explicit Credential Manager save prompt); assetlinks `delegate_permission/common.get_login_creds` mirrors the AASA `webcredentials` entry |
| `.keyboardType(.emailAddress)`, `.textInputAutocapitalization(.characters)`, `.autocorrectionDisabled()` | `KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = Email / Ascii, capitalization = Characters / None, autoCorrectEnabled = false)` |
| `AccessibilityNotification.Announcement` | `semantics { liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite }` on the changing text (error lines, waiting message); `Assertive` for errors that block |
| `.speechSpellsOutCharacters()` on codes | `VerbatimTtsAnnotation` on the code text |
| Face ID / Touch ID (`LAContext`, `.deviceOwnerAuthentication`) | `BiometricPrompt` with `BIOMETRIC_STRONG or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` on API 30+, `BIOMETRIC_WEAK or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` on API 29 *(verify: STRONG+DEVICE_CREDENTIAL is unsupported before API 30)* |
| Universal links | App Links (§6.10) |
| "Opens in Safari" hints | "Opens in your browser" (TalkBack hint); legal and policy links open in the default browser (§7.12 Legal), link-outs in §6.8 follow that section |
| `UserDefaults` stash (`PendingSignUp`) | Preferences DataStore in app-private storage, excluded from Auto Backup and device transfer (`dataExtractionRules`), JSON-encoded with the same field names |

#### 7.1.0 Shell: phases, gates, and their order

Port `RootView.content`/`phaseContent` and `AppModel` as a single `RootViewModel` (`StateFlow<RootState>`). Order of precedence, top wins:

1. **Lock** (§7.1.4) when locked: the `LockActivity` above `MainActivity` (§6.4, §6.11.4), so it covers ParentApproval, every cover and every dialog or sheet, which stay where they were underneath (iOS `RootView`: `.lockWindow` is the outermost modifier).
2. **ParentApproval** (B2) when the significant-change coordinator is blocking. Nothing else below it is reachable; the reset cover and the Terms gate never show while it blocks (`termsNeeded` is false while blocking, per `AppModel.termsNeeded`).
3. **Reset-password cover** (§7.1.3) while a recovery link is pending — valid in **every** phase (signed out, mid-onboarding, signed in).
4. **Terms gate** (§7.1.5) when `me.role != null && !me.terms.accepted` and ParentApproval is not blocking.
5. **Phase content:**
   - `Launching` → LaunchView: "Gradus" in the wordmark font with a progress indicator. Use the Android 12+ SplashScreen API for the system splash and hand off to LaunchView (iOS has no system splash equivalent beyond the launch screen).
   - `ForceUpdate(policy)` → §6.2 owns (iOS `ForceUpdateView`: "Update Gradus", policy message or "This version of Gradus is no longer supported. Please update to keep going."). Android action: before a Play listing exists (A8), button **(Android copy)** "Open gradus.training in your browser" opening `https://gradus.training` (iOS: "Open gradus.training in Safari", same URL, because the App Store link waits on the listing); once the listing exists, **(Android copy)** "Update on Google Play" opening `market://details?id=training.gradus.app`, falling back to `https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=training.gradus.app` when no store app handles it. The switch is `BuildConfig.PLAY_LISTING_LIVE` (§9.6). Option for Mariah (§12 N37): the Play **In-App Updates API** immediate flow as the native equivalent, with the button as fallback; not used in 1.0.
   - `SignedOut` → the signed-out screen: **sign-in only, no bottom navigation** (Mariah, 2026-09-26); a public board link still opens in the Live cover over sign-in (§7.10).
   - `SignedIn(me)`:
     - an onboarding gate for coach or parent with `me.role == null` and the age store not yet answered → full-screen progress while `requestIfNeeded()` runs;
     - that gate with `blocksAdultRoles` → the athlete-only role chooser (§7.1.9);
     - `onboardingGate` coach / parent / adultAthlete → §7.1.10 / §7.1.11 / §7.1.13, each in its own nav graph with a top-app-bar **Sign out** action;
     - `planSetupProfile != null` → PlanStatus (§7.1.16);
     - `me.role == null` (or `meLoadError`) → NoRole: "Couldn't load your account" + error + "Try again" (retry `/me`); org admin → the role tabs with Settings only and the Live action (§6.9.1; iOS `RoleTabsView` takes every non-nil role, so `NoRoleView`'s "Org admin is web-only" branch is unreachable at HEAD and is ported only as dead-code parity); a pending guardian-claim or team-invite link (with the B1 checks) → that flow (§7.7); otherwise the role chooser (§7.1.9). NoRole also calls `requestIfNeeded()` on entry ("a profile-less account is a sign-up entry too").
     - otherwise the role tabs, with the connection celebration cover (§7.13).
   - **AI permission** (§6.7.1a, A54): a root full-screen dialog over the phase content and every sheet, whenever `showsAIConsent` is true and the Terms gate is not showing. It appears after the terms (and, for a coach, after coach onboarding), and again on request. The celebration cover waits while it is up.
6. **System back on blocking gates** (ParentApproval, Lock, Terms, the onboarding gates' first screen): `moveTaskToBack(true)`; never dismisses the gate.

**Onboarding gate resolution** (`AppModel.resolveOnboardingGate`), after every `/me` load (cached first, then fresh):
- coach: gate `.coach` when `me.onboardingComplete == false`;
- parent: `GET /signup/parent/status`; gate `.parent` when `!hasAthletes`; otherwise no gate and a parent-kind stash is cleared. **If the status call fails**, also no gate (tabs) and a parent-kind stash is cleared, exactly as iOS (`if let status = try? … , !status.hasAthletes { .parent } else { nil }`); the next `/me` load re-resolves (code parity; §12 N39 asks whether Mariah wants a retry instead);
- athlete: gate `.adultAthlete` only when the stash (for this user) has kind `adultAthlete` (the server does not track that flow's later steps);
- org admin: none;
- no role: the stash kind decides (`parent`/`adultAthlete`/`coach`), **except** a coach or parent kind when `blocksAdultRoles` → no gate (role chooser, athlete only).

**Session handoff** (`AppModel.handle(session)`): adopt the broker session (§6.4; tokens in the Keystore-backed store); if the store cannot hold it, error "The session could not be stored on this device."; stamp the stash with the user id (`PendingSignUp.stamp`); tell the Wear OS companion (§6.15); enter signed in (cached `/me` first, then fresh; sync engine; device token; unread). An auth failure on `/me` shows its message and signs out. A non-auth failure with nothing cached renders NoRole's retry state. After `/me` for a coach, send any `UnsentSportRequest` (§7.1.10). After `/me` for an athlete, run `PlayInstallReporter` (§6.13 B4).

**Launch sequence** (`AppModel.start`): fonts; Wear OS companion; analytics flushing; error reporting hook (connectivity messages never reported); connectivity; `GET /meta/client-policy` (best effort; below minimum → ForceUpdate); `GET /meta/config` → `PlanGate(paywallEnabled, foundingCutoff)` (default cutoff `2026-11-01T00:00:00Z`); restore session → lock on launch if enabled → enter signed in; or signed out (deliver a pending public board route). Then, never blocking: `ageSignals.refreshOnLaunch()` followed by `significantChanges.run()`.

**Sign-out** (`AppModel.signOut`, owned by §6.4/§7.12; listed here because every onboarding screen offers it): tell the watch; `DELETE /devices/{token}`; end ongoing-notification token reporting; flush then clear usage analytics; Supabase sign-out; wipe sync engine and the per-user Room store; reset the biometric preference (`BiometricGate.reset`: the next account starts unlocked); clear unread, session models, nav paths, sign-up path, plan screen, onboarding gate, pending link; **clear the sign-up stash** ("a sign-out abandons any sign-up in progress; the server-side state resumes the coach and parent flows"); land on Sign in.

#### 7.1.1 Sign in (iOS `FeatureAuth/SignInView.swift`, `SignInModel.swift`; PRD §7.1 row "Sign in", §6.4)

Screen (paper background, max width 520 dp centered, scrolls, keyboard dismisses on scroll and outside tap):
- Header: title "Gradus"; subtitle "Practice made perfect".
- Card:
  - Field "Email or username", placeholder "you@example.com", Email keyboard, no autocap/autocorrect, autofill `Username`, IME action Next → password. TalkBack label "Email or username".
  - Field "Password", placeholder "Password", masked, autofill `Password`, IME action Go → submit. Android adds the standard visibility toggle icon (Material password field convention; iOS `SecureField` has none) **(Android)**.
  - Switch "Remember me" (default on only if an identifier was remembered). DataStore key `gradus.auth.rememberedIdentifier`; on a successful sign-in by any method, save the trimmed identifier if on and non-empty, else remove it.
  - Error line (error icon + message, `destructiveInk`), TalkBack "Error: {message}", announced; cleared when either field changes.
  - Primary **"Sign in"** with a spinner while password sign-in runs; enabled when trimmed identifier and password are non-empty and nothing is in flight. Tag `signIn.submit`.
  - Text button **"Forgot password?"** → Forgot password sheet (§7.1.3), email prefilled when the identifier contains "@" ("don't ask twice").
- Divider row "or".
- Provider buttons (Android order: Google, then Apple), both disabled while any sign-in is in flight:
  - **"Continue with Google"** (tag `signIn.google`) — §7.1.2a.
  - **"Continue with Apple"** (tag `signIn.apple`) — §7.1.2b.
- Sign-up links: "New to Gradus?" + **"Create an account"** (tag `signIn.createAccount`) → sign-up stack `[chooser]`; **"Have an invite code?"** (tag `signIn.inviteCode`) → `[chooser, invite(code = null)]`.
- Banner pinned under the top edge when a guardian or team link waits for sign-in: "Use the email address this link was sent to." (tag `signIn.linkHint`).

Behavior: password sign-in → `POST /auth/password {identifier, password}` (§6.4 broker: a username without "@" resolves to the synthetic athlete email server-side; captcha is bypassed by the broker's service-role password grant, so **no Turnstile or captcha UI exists in the app**, same as iOS; rate-limited per IP and identifier; generic error). Failure shows the server's user message (e.g. invalid credentials) and keeps the identifier; success hands the session to the shell and clears the password. Tests: port `SignInModelTests` ("Password sign-in hands the session to the app and remembers the identifier"; "Invalid credentials show the generic message and keep the identifier"; "Empty fields cannot submit"), plus Google and Apple cases below.

#### 7.1.2 Provider sign-in (A5)

Both providers go through the existing identity broker (§6.4) and return `{accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn, isNewUser}`. A brand-new provider user has no profile, so `/me` answers with no role and the shell shows the role chooser (§7.1.9), never a web hand-off and never a Terms sheet (iOS §6.4 *2026-10-02*). When started from a **sign-up form**, the form's kind/promo/invite/setup are stashed first for a new user so the shell opens that role's onboarding directly (§7.1.8).

**a. Google — Credential Manager / Sign in with Google.**
- `CredentialManager.getCredential` with `GetSignInWithGoogleOption.Builder(serverClientId = GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID).setNonce(<random>)` for the explicit button (the bottom-sheet `GetGoogleIdOption` auto-prompt is **not** used: iOS never auto-prompts). Read `GoogleIdTokenCredential.idToken` → `POST /auth/google {idToken}`.
- Cancellation (`GetCredentialCancellationException`) is silent. `NoCredentialException` → **(Android copy)** "No Google account on this device. Add one in Settings, or use your email or username." Other failures → **(Android copy)** "Google sign-in didn't finish. Try again, or use your email or username." The broker's errors show its message.
- **Server change (additive, S-5, §6.4 owns it):** `verifyGoogleIdToken` today accepts only `aud == GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID`. Android ID tokens carry `aud` = the **server (web) client ID** and `azp` = the Android client. Keep the iOS path and also accept `aud == GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID` only when `azp` ∈ `GOOGLE_ANDROID_CLIENT_IDS` (new Lovable Cloud secrets), unchanged otherwise. Google Cloud: an Android OAuth client per signing certificate (debug, upload key, and the Play App Signing key once the Play Console exists, A8) plus the web client used as `serverClientId`. Until A8, Google sign-in works only on builds signed with a registered key.
- The button is compiled in and shown whenever `GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID` is set in the build config; a build without it hides the button (iOS's stub rule, `SignInModel.isGoogleAvailable`).
- Account deletion: no Google token revocation is required by the server today; §7.12 owns deletion.

**b. Sign in with Apple — web flow in an Auth Tab (Custom Tab fallback)** (so accounts created with Apple on iPhone sign in on Android).
- **Apple developer setup (Mariah):** a **Services ID** (proposed `training.gradus.app.signin` *(decide)*) **grouped with the primary App ID `training.gradus.app`**, so the Apple `sub` and any private-relay email match the iPhone's for the same person *(verify grouping semantics at setup)*; return URL `https://gradus.training/api/public/auth/apple/callback`; the existing Sign in with Apple key signs the client secret.
- **Flow (server additions, all additive; §6.4 owns the broker, Appendix A lists them):**
  1. App generates a random `codeVerifier`, calls `POST /api/v1/auth/apple/web/start {codeChallenge: base64url(sha256(codeVerifier))}` → `{authorizeUrl}` (§6.4 owns this contract). The server stores `state` and a raw `nonce` (10-minute TTL) and builds `https://appleid.apple.com/auth/authorize?client_id=<servicesId>&redirect_uri=<callback>&response_type=code%20id_token&response_mode=form_post&scope=name%20email&state=<state>&nonce=<sha256(nonce)>`.
  2. **Before opening anything**, persist `{codeVerifier, state, origin: signIn | signUp(kind), promo, inviteCode, setup present}` in an encrypted DataStore entry (Tink-backed, §6.11) keyed by `state`, with a **10-minute TTL** (matching the server's), not only in `SavedStateHandle`, because the round trip can end in a recreated Activity or a new process. Then open `authorizeUrl` with the **Auth Tab** API, the Android-native OAuth return channel (the equivalent of iOS `ASAuthorizationController`): `AuthTabIntent.Builder().build().launch(launcher, authorizeUrl, redirectHost = "gradus.training", redirectPath = "/auth/apple/done")` with `launcher = AuthTabIntent.registerActivityResultLauncher(activity, callback)` (`androidx.browser` 1.9+, Chrome 137+ *(verify API names and availability at build time)*). On browsers without Auth Tab support, fall back to a plain **Custom Tab** plus the `/auth/apple/done` App Link (step 4). Apple's own page handles the Apple ID and two-factor; no Gradus UI runs inside it.
  3. Apple POSTs the form to the callback. The server verifies the `id_token` against Apple's JWKS with `aud == <servicesId>` (new audience alongside the bundle ID) and the stored nonce, takes the first-time `user` JSON name if present, runs `findOrCreateIdentityUser(provider: "apple", …)`, exchanges `code` for Apple's refresh token **with the Services ID as `client_id`** (stored with that client id so account deletion revokes with the matching client id), mints a one-time `handoff` (2-minute TTL, bound to `challenge`), and answers `303` to `https://gradus.training/auth/apple/done?handoff=<handoff>&state=<state>`.
  4. With Auth Tab, the result callback (`AuthResult.resultCode == RESULT_OK`, `resultUri`) delivers that URL directly, with no App Link race. In the Custom Tab fallback the URL is an **App Link** (§6.10; Android-only path; the web page at that path says "Return to the Gradus app to finish signing in." for a browser without the app). Either way the shell (not the screen, which may be gone) looks up the persisted entry by `state` and calls `POST /api/v1/auth/apple/web/exchange {handoffCode, codeVerifier}` → the usual session body including `isNewUser`. Single use; a replay or wrong verifier → 401. A missing or expired entry (state unknown, TTL passed) shows the Android failure copy below; the entry is deleted after any outcome.
  5. **Apply the iOS sign-up rule** (`SignUpModel.submitApple`): if `origin` is `signUp(kind)` and `isNewUser != false`, save the stash `{kind, promo, inviteCode, setup}` (the setup is already in the stash from §7.1.7) before handing off; if `isNewUser == false`, toast "You already have a Gradus account, so we signed you in." and save **no** stash; if `origin` is `signIn`, no stash (a new user lands on the role chooser).
- Cancellation is silent: Auth Tab `RESULT_CANCELED`, or (fallback) the Custom Tab closed without a return; the button re-enables when the app resumes without a handoff, and the persisted entry expires on its TTL. Failures follow the §6.4 failure table exactly (no Android-only Apple string): a returned `?error=…`, a state mismatch or a missing or expired persisted entry → iOS `AppleSignInButton.unavailableMessage` ("Sign in with Apple isn't available on this build yet. Use your email or username for now."); a failing start or exchange call → `ApiError.userMessage`.
- Visual: black button in light theme, white in dark (Apple's guideline, as iOS), 48 dp tall, `GradusRadius.md` corners, dimmed to 45% opacity when disabled.
- Tests: start/exchange happy path; replayed handoff refused; wrong verifier refused; cancellation silent; expired/missing persisted entry shows the failure copy; **process death while the tab is open still lands in the right onboarding** (sign-up origin with kind parent → parent onboarding gate; `isNewUser == false` → tabs, no stash); `isNewUser` routing (role chooser vs tabs); existing iPhone Apple account signs in to the same user (QA on device).

#### 7.1.3 Forgot password and reset (iOS `ForgotPasswordView`, `ResetPasswordView/Model.swift`, `NativeResetFlag.swift`; `AppModel.open(url:)`)

**Forgot password sheet** (`ModalBottomSheet`, half then full height, drag handle; top bar title "Reset password", "Cancel"):
- Body "Enter the email on your account and we'll send a link to reset your password."; field "Email" ("you@example.com", email autofill); error line; primary "Send reset link" (spinner while sending; enabled when the text contains "@").
- `POST /auth/recover {email}` with **no client override** (code at HEAD: the email links to `https://gradus.training/auth/confirm?token_hash=…&type=recovery` whichever client asked; the earlier `gradus://reset-password` redirect needed an allow-list entry the backend could not take).
- Sent state: "Check your email" / "If an account exists for {email}, a reset link is on its way. {destination}" / "Done", where destination is "The link opens Gradus so you can set a new password." when the native-reset flag is on, else "It opens the reset page in your browser."
- **Native reset flag** (iOS `GRADUS_NATIVE_RESET`: the code default is off, but gradus-ios `project.yml` L131 sets it **true** at HEAD, iOS #124): Android `BuildConfig.GRADUS_NATIVE_RESET = true` (§9.6), so the sent state always says "The link opens Gradus so you can set a new password." **Code at HEAD: the flag changes only this sentence**; the app intercepts `/auth/confirm` links regardless (below). Ported tests: `ForgotPasswordModelTests` (flag off sends recover without a client override; flag on changes only the copy; default reads the flag; missing key reads off).

**Email links handled before routing** (`AppModel.open(url:)`):
- `https://gradus.training/auth/confirm?token_hash=…&type=recovery` → reset cover with a one-time code. `type=email_change` → §7.12 (toasts "Your email is updated." / "Confirmed. If we also emailed your other address, open that link too." / offline "You're offline. Open the link again once you're connected." / expired "That link has expired or was already used. Change your email again in Settings › Account.").
- Legacy `gradus://reset-password#access_token=…&refresh_token=…&type=recovery` → reset cover with fragment tokens.
- On iOS `/auth/confirm` and `/reset-password` are excluded from universal links because the AASA lists them in `UNIVERSAL_LINK_EXCLUDES`, yet `AppModel` intercepts `/auth/confirm` when it arrives. Android declares `/auth/confirm` in its App Link intent filter so reset and email-change emails open the app (the "every email link opens the app" behavior of beta feedback 2026-10-07); `/reset-password` stays in the browser *(confirm with §6.10)*.

**Reset cover** (full screen, every phase):
- Presenting it closes the Live cover. If someone is signed in, first unregister this device's push token from that account (the code may belong to another account on a household phone); an expired link re-registers it.
- `Adopting`: spinner + "Verifying your reset link…".
- `Expired`: "This reset link has expired" / "Ask for a new one and we'll send a fresh link to your email." / "Request a new link" (closes the cover).
- `Offline` (one-time code never reached the server): "You're offline" / "Connect and try again. Your reset link still works." / "Try again" + text button "Not now". Fragment tokens are never retried.
- `Form`: title "New password", "Choose a new password for your account."; "New password" (placeholder "At least 8 characters", autofill `NewPassword`, IME Next); "Confirm new password" ("Type it again", IME Go); error line; "Set new password" (spinner while saving); hint under it when invalid and non-empty: "Use at least 8 characters." or "The passwords don't match."
- `Done`: "Password updated" / "Sign in with your new password."; the model signs the recovery session out, the shell shows toast "Password updated", signs out fully and wipes the previously signed-in account's store, landing on Sign in.
- Tests: port all eleven `ResetPasswordModelTests`.

#### 7.1.4 Lock screen (iOS `LockScreenView.swift`, `GradusCore/BiometricGate.swift`)

A local convenience lock, not an auth mechanism (iOS §6.4).
- Preference key `gradus.security.biometricLock` (DataStore, per device); toggled in Settings → Device (§7.12: **(Android copy)** "Unlock with fingerprint, face, or screen lock"; disabled with "Set up a fingerprint, face unlock, or a screen lock in Android Settings to use this." when `BiometricManager.canAuthenticate(...)` is not `BIOMETRIC_SUCCESS`).
- Locks on launch when a session exists and the preference is on; relocks on return to the foreground only after **30 s** in the background (`relockAfter`); each background trip counts once (the app's own prompt closing must not relock it).
- Screen: paper background; fingerprint (or face) icon; "Gradus is locked"; last error message if any; **"Unlock"** (calls the prompt; also auto-prompts on appear); bottom text button **"Sign out"**. TalkBack treats it as modal; nothing behind it is focusable.
- `BiometricPrompt` title "Unlock Gradus" (iOS reason string); authenticators per the table above (device credential fallback = iOS passcode fallback; no negative button is allowed with device credential, so Android has no "Not now"). User/system cancellation clears the error; other errors show `errString`.
- Signing out from the lock screen dismisses any dialog/sheet without animation under the lock (iOS behavior), keeps a pending reset cover, and resets the preference.
- Recents thumbnail: iOS does not obscure the app switcher snapshot; Android sets no `FLAG_SECURE` for parity (§12 N30).

#### 7.1.5 Terms gate and the acceptance line (iOS `TermsSheet.swift`, `Components/TermsAgreement.swift`; §6.4 "Terms"; #46)

**Acceptance line on every sign-up form and the role chooser (#46).** Sentence "I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy" with **Terms of Service** (`https://gradus.training/terms`) and **Privacy Policy** (`https://gradus.training/privacy`) as bold, underlined inline links (`LinkAnnotation.Url` in an `AnnotatedString`; open in the default browser), and a separate `Switch` beside it whose TalkBack label is the full sentence (tags `{prefix}.termsText`, `{prefix}.terms` with prefix `signUp` or `roleChooser`). The link must not be inside the switch's clickable area. Accepting it is the consent to usage-data collection too (#46); there is **no** in-app analytics switch anywhere.

**Recording the agreement.** `POST /me/terms/accept` answers `deferred` until a coach, parent or athlete row exists, so each onboarding calls it right after creating its profile (coach: on load; parent: after `signup/parent/start`; adult athlete: after `signup/adult-athlete`), ignoring failures. No Terms sheet ever appears mid sign-up (QA §1 regression row).

**Blocking Terms gate** (role set and current version not accepted; `CURRENT_TERMS_VERSION` is server-side, currently `2026-06-29`):
- Full screen, scrolls at every font scale; eyebrow "Updated {version as a long date, UTC}" (fallback: the raw version string); title "Our terms have changed"; "Please review and accept the updated Terms of Service and Privacy Policy to keep using Gradus."; card with rows "Terms of Service" and "Privacy Policy" (open-in-browser icon; hint "Opens in your browser"); checkbox "I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy"; error line (announced); primary **"Accept and continue"** (enabled when checked; spinner) → `POST /me/terms/accept`, update the cached `/me`, success haptic (`HapticFeedbackConstants.CONFIRM` on API 30+); text button **"Sign out instead"**. Tag `terms.accept`.
- Cannot be dismissed (back → `moveTaskToBack`). Re-checked on every `/me` (foreground refresh).

#### 7.1.6 Sign-up choosers and the blocked screen (iOS `SignUpChooserView.swift`, `AgeSignalViews.swift`)

**Sign-up chooser** (no top-bar title, since one title per screen applies, §8.6.1; asks the age store on appear):
- Title "Create an account". There is no subtitle: "Who are you joining Gradus as?" is gone (`ad1e9bf`).
- Three plain rows with role names only, **no icons and no subtitles** (Mariah 2026-10-02; handoff §7 Onboarding):
  - **Coach** (tag `signUp.coach`);
  - **Parent** (`signUp.parent`);
  - **Athlete** (`signUp.athlete`).

  Each row is a borderless `card` row (radius `lg`, `cardEdge`) with the role in display title3 and a trailing chevron. Coach and Parent are hidden when `blocksAdultRoles`, with the blocked note card under the list.
- Outlined row **"I have an invite code"** (ticket icon, chevron, `accentInk` text, 1 dp `accent` edge; tag `signUp.invite`) → invite entry.
- Coach → coach setup; Parent → parent setup; Athlete → athlete chooser.

**Athlete chooser** (no top-bar title): title "Athlete on Gradus"; "How are you joining?"; rows **"I have a code from my parent"** — "Your parent set up your account; you pick a username." (tag `athlete.claim`) → athlete claim (§7.1.14); **"I'm signing up myself"** — "13 or older. Under 18, a parent's email goes on file and they confirm your account." (tag `athlete.adult`) → athlete setup (§7.1.7c).

**Coach-invite chooser** (after a coach's code; no top-bar title): title "Join your coach"; "This code connects you to a coach. Who are you?"; **"A parent"** — "I manage one or more athletes' accounts." (`coachInvite.parent`) → parent setup with the code; **"An athlete"** — "I manage my own account." (`coachInvite.athlete`) → athlete setup with the code.

**AdultRolesBlocked** (tag `ageSignal.adultRolesBlocked`; no top-bar title): eyebrow "Sign up" (or "Athlete setup" under 13); title `adultRolesBlockedTitle` (omitted under 13); card: 13–17 → the blocked note (icon + `adultRolesBlockedBody`, Android copy in §6.13 B1) with **"Sign up as an athlete"** (tag `ageSignal.athlete`) → `[chooser, athleteChooser, adultSetup]` carrying any invite; under 13 → the parent-only card (§7.1.7c) whose "I already have my parent's code" goes to `[chooser, athleteChooser, athleteClaim]`.

**Deep links into sign-up** (`AppModel.open(route)`): signed in → toast "You're already signed in."; signed out: `/signup/coach` → `[chooser, coach(account form)]` (**code at HEAD skips the coach pre-account setup for this link**; the post-account coach onboarding form collects name and sports instead); `/signup/parent` → `[chooser, parent(account form)]`; `/signup/athlete` → `[chooser, athleteChooser]`; `/signup/athlete/adult` → `[chooser, athleteChooser, adultAthlete(account form)]`; `/login` → sign in. Each still passes the B1 check.

#### 7.1.7 Onboarding before the account (iOS #27; `PreAccountSetupViews.swift`)

Every role answers its first onboarding questions **before** the account exists and before any payment. Each screen writes only to the local stash (`PendingSignUp.setup`, kind set) and talks to no server. After the account exists, the matching onboarding applies the stash on its own (§7.1.10–7.1.13). Each screen restores from an existing stash when reopened.

**a. Coach setup** (no top-bar title):
- `StepDots(current = 1, total = 2)` (§8.6.6) instead of the eyebrow "Coach setup · step 1 of 2". Title "Tell us about yourself". **No subtitle** (`ad1e9bf` removed "Your account comes next. Nothing is purchased in the app."; the coach account form's footer still says nothing is purchased, §7.1.8).
- "First name" ("First", autofill first name, IME Next; `coachSetup.firstName`), "Last name" ("Last"; `coachSetup.lastName`).
- Header "Your primary sport"; single-select chips of the catalog **without** the always-secondary sports (`SportCatalog.isSecondary`, i.e. Strength & Conditioning), a pen check on the selected chip (`GradusChip` with the pen-check icon, §8.3), TalkBack "{label}, selected", tag `coachSetup.sport.{key}`; a custom sport stashed earlier shows as a selected chip that clears on tap.
- Note: "{secondary labels joined by ", "} is always included. Add more sports later in Settings on Coach Pro or Club." (`coachSetup.note`).
- **Request a sport** (deferred mode, §7.1.18) → stores `requestedSport`; line "We'll send your request for {sport} when your account is ready." (`coachSetup.requested`); a typed name that matches a listed sport selects that sport instead.
- **Continue** (`coachSetup.continue`), enabled with both names and a primary sport → stash `{kind: coach, firstName, lastName, primarySport {key,label,isCustom}, requestedSport}` → account form (coach).

**b. Parent setup** (no top-bar title):
- `StepDots(current = 1, total = 2)` instead of the eyebrow; title "Create your profiles"; "Add yourself and each athlete in your family. Your account comes next." (this subtitle is kept at `c8f83d6`).
- Card eyebrow "You": "First name"/"Last name" (`parentSetup.firstName`, `parentSetup.lastName`).
- Card eyebrow "Your athletes": per athlete first/last name (TalkBack "Athlete first name"/"Athlete last name"), **Birthdate** field (§7.1.18), "Remove athlete" (destructive, only with 2+); outlined "Add another athlete" (`parentSetup.addAthlete`).
- **No direct notice on this screen** (code parity: `PreAccountSetupViews.swift` has no `DirectNoticeView`; it appears only in `ParentOnboardingView`, `GuardianClaimFlow` and `ParentAthletesView`). The notice stays on the post-account Profiles step (§7.1.11).
- **Continue** (`parentSetup.continue`), enabled with both parent names and at least one complete athlete (names + valid birthdate) → stash `{kind: parent, names, athletes: complete ones, trimmed}` → account form (parent).
- **Open decision, §12 N38 (cross-platform; not an Android-only change):** with a complete pre-account setup, the post-account Profiles step auto-submits on load, so in the main sign-up path the parent may never see the notice before the athletes are created, while decision #40 and QA §1 ("the parent sign-up athletes step shows 'What Gradus keeps for <first name>…' … ending 'By continuing, you give your consent…'") expect it where the parent enters the minor's details. Android ships code parity (no notice here). If Mariah decides to add `DirectNotice(athleteName, consentAct = true)` above Continue on this screen, the change lands on iOS and Android together, ideally before Android's onboarding milestone.

**c. Athlete setup — birthdate first** (`AdultSetupModel`; #30, #31; "Athlete setup"; refreshes the age signal on appear):
- Phase **birthdate**: `StepDots(1, 2)` (no eyebrow, no top-bar title); title "When were you born?"; "This sets up the right experience for your age. Your account comes next."; Birthdate field; error line (announced); **Continue** (`adultSetup.continueBirthdate`, enabled when valid: parses, age 0–119). Invalid → "Enter your date of birth." Under 13 or band under 13 → parent-only. 18+ on an under-18 band → `birthdateContradictionMessage`. Otherwise → details.
- Phase **parentOnly** (eyebrow "Athlete setup", title "Athlete on Gradus", card): heading "Ask your parent to set you up"; body "Athletes under 13 get their Gradus account from a parent or guardian. They sign up, add you, and give you a code to log in with. Nothing about you is saved until then." (signed-in form: "Athletes under 13 get their Gradus account from a parent or guardian. Sign out, then ask them to sign up and add you; they'll give you a code to log in with."); primary **"Send my parent an invite"** (share icon; tag `adultSetup.shareParent`) → Sharesheet with subject "Join me on Gradus" and text "Hey — I want to use Gradus for training. Can you make a parent account and add me? https://gradus.training/signup/parent"; secondary **"I already have my parent's code"** (`adultSetup.parentCode`) → athlete claim (hidden when signed in). Entering this phase sets the process-wide `under13ThisLaunch = true` and **clears the stash**; while it is set, the screen always opens on parent-only ("a second birthdate does not reopen the flow"). The birthdate is never written to disk, `SavedStateHandle`, or the server.
- Phase **details**: `StepDots(1, 2)`; title "Tell us about yourself"; "Your account comes next."; first/last name (`adultSetup.firstName`, `adultSetup.lastName`); "Born {long date}" with text button **"Change"** (TalkBack "Change date of birth"; `adultSetup.changeBirthdate`) → back to birthdate. If 13–17: "Parent or guardian email" ("parent@example.com"; `adultSetup.guardianEmail`; valid = contains "@" and "." and no spaces) and the provisional note "Under 18? Your account starts in waiting mode: your goals and plans are yours right away. Connecting a coach and messaging open once your parent or guardian confirms from the email we send them." **Continue** (`adultSetup.continue`) → stash `{kind: adultAthlete, names, birthdate, guardianEmail (lowercased, minors only)}` → account form (athlete).
- Restoring: a stash with a valid birthdate reopens on details; a stashed under-13 birthdate (from before the gate) is cleared and never reopens.

#### 7.1.8 Account form (iOS `AccountSignUpView.swift`, `SignUpModel.swift`)

No top-bar title (`ad1e9bf`; the back arrow only); title "Coach on Gradus" / "Parent on Gradus" / "Athlete on Gradus"; subtitle "Practice made perfect" / "Follow your athletes' practice between lessons." / "Your plans, your practice, your coach."
- **Invite banner** (from `/i/<code>` or the code entry; `signUp.inviteBanner`), after `POST /invites/resolve` (and previews):
  - coach form + parent code: "You're joining {first} {last}'s athlete. They'll be on your roster when you finish setting up." (or "…'s {n} athletes…");
  - coach form + adult-athlete code: "You're joining {first} {last}. They'll be on your roster when you finish setting up.";
  - parent/athlete form + coach code: "You're joining a coach. Their code is used once your account is set up.";
  - wrong kind: "That invite isn't for {a coach|a parent|an athlete} account, so it won't be used here. You can still create your account." (code dropped);
  - invalid: "That invite code isn't valid, so it won't be used. You can still create your account." (code dropped).
  - A lookup failure shows nothing ("the lookup is a courtesy"). A promo code attached to the invite prefills the promo field if empty.
- Fields: "Email" ("you@example.com"; `signUp.email`), "Password" ("At least 8 characters"; autofill `NewPassword`; `signUp.password`), "Promo code (optional)" ("FOUNDING10"; characters caps; `signUp.promo`); the acceptance line (§7.1.5).
- Hint under the button (only once email or password is non-empty, when no error): "Enter your email address." / "Passwords need at least 8 characters." / "Please agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy." Email rule: an "@" not first, a domain containing "." not ending in ".", no spaces.
- **"Create account"** (`signUp.submit`, spinner) → `POST /auth/signup/coach` | `/auth/signup/parent` | `/auth/signup/adult-athlete` `{email, password}`. `session` → stash `{kind, promo (trimmed, uppercased), inviteCode, setup}` and hand off; `confirmationRequired` → stash and show "Check your email" / "We sent a link to {email}. Open it to confirm your account, then sign in here." Errors show the server's message.
- Divider "or", then provider buttons (Android: Google and Apple; iOS: Apple only), each **disabled until the terms switch is on**, with the hint above them when off and the button hint isn't already showing the same sentence: "Agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy to continue with Apple." and **(Android copy)** "Agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy to continue with Google." (one combined line when both show: **(Android copy)** "Agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy to continue with Google or Apple."; tag `signUp.appleBlocker`). TalkBack: the blocker line's `contentDescription` is "Sign up with Apple is unavailable: {blocker}" (iOS `AccountSignUpView.swift`), **(Android copy)** "Sign up with Google is unavailable: {blocker}" for the Google line, and "Sign up with Google or Apple is unavailable: {blocker}" for the combined line; each disabled provider button also carries `disabled()` semantics with the same description as its state. A tap that gets through without the terms fails with that sentence rather than doing nothing. On success: `isNewUser == false` → toast "You already have a Gradus account, so we signed you in." and **no** stash (so an onboarded account is not pushed into this form's onboarding); otherwise stash as for email and hand off.
- Coach form footer: "Subscriptions are managed on gradus.training. Nothing is purchased in the app." (A10 / §6.8).
- Tests: port `OnboardingModelTests` sign-up cases ("Needs a plausible email, 8+ characters, and the terms"; "A session hands off to the shell and stashes the promo and invite for onboarding"; "Confirmation required shows the check-email state; a refusal shows the server's words"; the three Apple cases, duplicated for Google; "An invite that isn't for a coach is dropped"; "A parent sign-up stashes its kind and keeps a coach's code; an athlete code is refused"; "An adult athlete sign-up stashes its kind") and `PreAccountSetupTests.signUpKeepsSetup`.

#### 7.1.9 Role chooser for a profile-less account (iOS `RoleChooserView.swift`, `RoleTabsView.NoRoleView`)

Shown to a signed-in account with no profile and nothing stashed (a new Google or Apple user from the sign-in screen, or an account abandoned on the web before its profile). Two steps on purpose: choosing Coach creates the coach row when coach onboarding loads, and onboarding records the terms, so a single mis-tap must not do either.
- Title "Finish setting up"; "Your account doesn't have a profile yet. Who are you joining Gradus as?"
- Single-select rows **Coach**, **Parent**, **Athlete** (`roleChooser.coach|parent|athlete`), each row ends in a `PenCheckbox(Circle, 24)` that shows the pen tick when selected (`RoleChooserView.swift`, `ad1e9bf`), and the selected row keeps its 2 dp accent border; Coach and Parent hidden when `blocksAdultRoles` (with the blocked note) and deselected if the answer arrives later.
- Caption: "Under 18 with a code from your parent? Sign out, then choose Athlete on the sign-up screen."
- Card: acceptance line (prefix `roleChooser`); hint "Choose who you are joining as." / "Please agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy." (`roleChooser.blocker`); primary "Continue as a coach" / "Continue as a parent" / "Continue as an athlete" / "Continue" (`roleChooser.continue`), enabled with a role, the terms, no sign-out in flight, the age store not checking, and (for Coach/Parent) not blocked.
- Outlined **"Sign out"** (`roleChooser.signOut`, spinner).
- Continue → `chooseRole(kind)`: write `{kind, userID}` into the stash (keeping any stashed invite) and open that gate exactly as if the account came from that sign-up form.

#### 7.1.10 Coach onboarding after the account (iOS `CoachOnboardingView/Model.swift`, `PlanStatusView`; PRD §7.1 "Coach onboarding")
