#### 7.2.2 Data, endpoints, caching

All paths are under `/api/v1` (Appendix A). Android generates its client from the vendored `Contract/openapi.json` (§6.2); DTO shapes below are the iOS `RosterModels.swift` / `ScheduleImportModels.swift` shapes, field for field.

| Call | Used by | Offline | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /coach/roster` with `If-None-Match` | Roster load | Cache serves | 304 keeps the roster. Returns `{coachSports, athletes[{athleteId, firstName, lastName, sport?, parentFirstName?, parentLastName?, selfManaged, slots[{id, dayOfWeek, startMinute, endMinute, frequency, weeksOfMonth, startsOn?, overrides[{date, status canceled\|rescheduled, startMinute?, endMinute?}]}], otherCoachCount, otherCoachLastName?, claimStatus?}]}`. `claimStatus` absent = claimed. |
| `GET /coach/roster/practice-summaries` | Status chip, practice metric | Cache serves | Fetched only when the roster has athletes; a failure is ignored (keeps old summaries). Empty roster clears summaries. |
| `POST /coach/roster/athletes` `[idem: fresh UUID]` | New athlete | **Online only** | Body `{firstName, lastName, birthdate?, guardianEmail, sport?, emailRecipient}`. Returns `{athleteId, guardianEmail?}`. Never queued: the invite email goes out at once (`RosterModel.addAthlete`). |
| `DELETE /coach/roster/athletes/{athleteId}` | Remove | **Online only** | No queue; failure shows the error toast. |
| `POST /coach/lesson-slots` | Add lesson | Queues | Body `{athleteId, dayOfWeek, startMinute, endMinute}`; server defaults `frequency = weekly`. Returns `{id}`. |
| `PATCH /coach/lesson-slots/{id}` | Edit recurring | Queues | iOS body `{dayOfWeek, startMinute, endMinute}`; Android sends the same until §7.2.20 O1 is decided (see §7.2.6 cadence issue). The server rejects a non-UUID id such as `pending-…`. |
| `DELETE /coach/lesson-slots/{id}` | Delete recurring | Queues | Overrides go with it. |
| `POST /coach/lesson-slots/{id}/occurrences/{date}/cancel` | Cancel this date | Queues | No body. |
| `POST .../occurrences/{date}/reschedule` | Reschedule this date | Queues | `{startMinute, endMinute}`. |
| `DELETE .../occurrences/{date}/override` | Undo override | Queues | No body. |
| `GET /coach/athletes/{id}` | Athlete detail | Needs network (in-memory only on iOS) | See §7.2.9. |
| `GET /coach/athletes/{id}/ai-summary` | (Not shown since the redesign) | — | **Android does not call it** (A64). iOS `c8f83d6` still requests it on load when AI is allowed and `hasAnySignal`, but no longer shows it (§12 N99). |
| `GET /plans/{id}/sessions?limit=200&before=` | The athlete detail practice line (§7.2.9) | Needs network (in-memory for the screen) | For each of the athlete's plans with `sessionsTotal > 0`, in parallel with the detail. Pages are newest first: 200 per page, at most 5 pages, `before` = the oldest session's `loggedAt` on the page; de-duplicated by session id; paging stops on a short page or a page with nothing new. A plan that fails is left out; the screen does not fail (`AthleteDetailModel.loadPracticeEntries`). |
| `GET /coach/athletes/{id}/briefing?lessonDate&refresh` | Up next briefing | Refresh needs network | `{narrative, generatedAt, fromCache}`. |
| `PUT` / `DELETE /coach/athletes/{id}/practice-target` | Practice expectations | Online only | `PUT {sport, hoursPerWeek}`; `DELETE ?sport=`. No queue (iOS `AthleteDetailModel`). |
| `GET /coach/athletes/{id}/active-plans` | Wrap-up Edit / Re-deploy gating; also the plan editor's and the watch's 409 bench-choice fallback (§7.3.5, §7.15.4) | Online (empty on failure for wrap-ups) | Read fresh every time, never cached. There is no cap (#52), so the list can hold any number of plans. |
| `GET /coach/wrap-ups/pending?lessonDate&dayOfWeek&currentMinute` | Wrap-ups | Failure = "couldn't ask" | Client sends its own local date, weekday (0 = Sun) and minute of day. |
| `POST /coach/wrap-ups` `[idem: wrapup-<athleteId>-<lessonDate>]` | Record wrap-up | Queues on status 0 / 5xx | `{athleteId, lessonDate, action}`; action ∈ `edited`, `redeployed`, `did_not_happen` (`dismissed` exists in the enum but is never sent). |
| `GET /coach/invite-code` · `POST /coach/invite-code/rotate` | Share my invite | Online only | `{code}`. |
| `POST /invites/parent/claim` then fallback `POST /invites/adult-athlete/claim` | Enter their code | Online only | Both with `{code, autoAckCoach: true}` (iOS `AppModel.inviteClaimClosure`). |
| `POST /coach/starter-plans/{id}/adopt` | (No UI since the redesign) | — | The roster's "Adopt plan" chip is gone (`ad1e9bf`: "Where the plan came from is a flag on the card, not an Adopt step"; handoff: "coaches adopting starter plans is not needed"). The model code survives on iOS but nothing calls it. Android does not build it. |
| `GET /coach/checklist` | Get set up bubble | Hidden on failure | `{coachId?, scheduleDone, scheduleFromFamilies, inviteDone, planDone}`. |
| `GET /coach/up-next?lessonDate&dayOfWeek&currentMinute&limit` | Wear OS Up next (§7.15), the coach's Today widget (§6.9.7) | Needs network | Not used by the phone Roster screen (§7.2.8). |
| `GET /coach/visibility/mine` · `POST /coach/visibility/{id}/respond` · `DELETE /coach/visibility/{id}` | Visibility banner and chips | See §7.7 | Session-scoped model shared with Settings. |
| `POST /coach/schedule-import/parse` (multipart, part `image`, `image/jpeg`) | Import | **Online only** | Returns `lessons[]` of `ParsedLesson`. Never queued (outbox is JSON-only). |
| `POST /coach/schedule-import/commit` `[idem: derived]` | Import | **Online only** | `groups` 1…100, each `slots` 1…20. Returns `outcomes[]`. |
| Coach billing (`athleteLimit`, `athleteCount`, `effectiveTier`) via the Settings account call (§7.12) | Import cap pre-check; Club gate on detail | Read fresh, never cached for the session (iOS §6.8) | — |

**`GET /coach/home?week=`** appears in iOS PRD Appendix A as a composite but is not in the contract and iOS does not call it; Android does not either.

**Roster cache.** iOS writes a per-user JSON snapshot `{roster, etag, summaries, fetchedAt}` (`RosterCache`, `roster.json` under the user's store directory, file protection until first unlock). Android stores the same snapshot as the same file, `roster.json`, in the per-user directory `noBackupFilesDir/Gradus/<userId>/` in credential-encrypted storage (§6.5, §6.11, A34); it is deleted on sign-out and account deletion with the rest of the user's store. Athlete detail, AI summary and briefings are held in memory for the screen's lifetime only (iOS behavior; PRD §6.5's "cached with content hash" is satisfied server-side).

**Refresh policy (iOS `RosterModel.activate` / `refreshOnForeground`) [code wins].**
- Tab first composition: load cache (if the in-memory roster is empty), then `load()`, then `refreshWrapUps()`.
- App returns to foreground (Android: `ProcessLifecycleOwner` `ON_START` while the Roster destination is in the back stack and visible): always `refreshWrapUps()`; reload the roster only if `fetchedAt` is older than **4 hours**. iOS has no background roster refresh; Android does not schedule a WorkManager refresh for the roster either (the PRD's "background refresh every 4 h" was not built).
- Pull to refresh (M3 `PullToRefreshBox`): `load()` then `refreshWrapUps()`.
- Request ordering: every roster request takes an increasing sequence number; a response older than the last applied one is dropped (so a slow revalidation cannot restore the pre-add roster).
- A queued (offline) slot write sets `etag = null` so the next load fetches instead of trusting a 304 (`invalidateIfQueued`).
- `revalidateRoster()` (roster only, no summaries) runs when the New athlete sheet opens, so a sport added in Settings appears (beta feedback 2026-10-07).

**Time and calendar.** "Today", the week, and the minute of day come from the device clock in `ZoneId.systemDefault()` (iOS `Calendar.current`). Weeks are always **Monday-first**, whatever the locale's first day of week (`WeekSchedule.mondayOnOrBefore`). `dayOfWeek` is 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday everywhere (Kotlin: `localDate.dayOfWeek.value % 7`). Recurrence arithmetic runs on `LocalDate` (no zone, no DST), matching iOS's fixed-UTC calendar.

**Displayed times are fixed 12-hour English.** Every displayed lesson time (lesson rows, roster card chips, the briefing card, the wrap-up prompt / list / banner, `UpNext.whenLine`) uses Kotlin ports of `LessonTime.compact` ("4p", "4:30p") and `LessonTime.long` ("4:00 PM") from `RosterModels.swift`, whatever the device's 24-hour setting. Only the `TimePicker` dialog follows `DateFormat.is24HourFormat`. Unit tests: 0 → "12a" / "12:00 AM"; 750 → "12:30p"; 1020 → "5p" / "5:00 PM".

#### 7.2.3 Roster screen (`RosterScreen`, iOS `RosterView`)

Layout top to bottom, inside a scrolling column, max content width 640 dp centred (phones fill the width with 20 dp padding; A4):

1. **Title row.** No top app bar (§8.4). `PageTitle("Roster")` with its accessory and **Live** inline in one fit-or-stack row (§8.2, `d23ab4a`). When the outbox holds roster mutations in `pending` or `inFlight` state (paths starting `/api/v1/coach/lesson-slots`, `/api/v1/coach/roster/athletes`, or equal to `/api/v1/coach/wrap-ups`), a mono caption with a sync icon: "`N` to sync". Tapping it does nothing (there is no Sync Center at iOS HEAD, §6.5).
2. **Segmented control.** Schedule / Athletes / Invoicing (wire value of the third is still `billing`). Default Schedule. At font scale ≥ 1.5 show an exposed dropdown instead.
3. **Sport filter** (only when there is at least one athlete, including Sample Athlete, and at least one sport). A `FilterChip` with a filter icon, label "All sports" or the selected sport's display label (`CoachSports.displayLabel`), selected state when a sport is chosen. Opens a `DropdownMenu`: "All sports", then each sport. `sports` = coach sports ∪ every athlete's sport, sorted by key. The filter applies to the athlete list, the week schedule and the Invoicing segment's athlete list.
4. **Wrap-up banner** (§7.2.10) when `showsWrapUpBanner`.
5. **Post-event cards** (§7.10), one per item.
6. **Coach visibility requests banner** (§7.2.12).
7. **Content:**
   - Load failed with nothing cached and never loaded: state view, icon wifi-off, title "Couldn't load your roster", message = the error, button "Try again".
   - First load in flight with nothing cached: a placeholder card "Loading your roster…" (static placeholder, no shimmer animation when the system "Remove animations" setting is on).
   - Otherwise the selected segment. With cached or previously loaded data, a failed load shows nothing on Roster: no banner and no snackbar (`errorMessage` is rendered only in the empty, never-loaded state, `RosterView.swift`), and the cached roster and summaries stay. There is no global offline banner (§7.13.4); pull to refresh retries.
8. **Bottom-end overlay** (not on Invoicing): the Get set up bubble (§7.2.11) stacked above the FAB, 20 dp from the end and bottom edges; content has 120 dp bottom padding on Schedule and Athletes so the FAB never hides the last row.

**Floating add button** (iOS `addButton`):

| Segment | Condition | Android |
|---|---|---|
| Schedule | At least one real (non-sample) athlete | `FloatingActionButton` "+" (content description "Add", state description/hint "Add an athlete or create a lesson.") opening a `DropdownMenu` anchored to it: "Add athlete" (person-add icon) → Add an athlete hub; "Create new lesson" (calendar-add icon) → lesson sheet in create mode for the **first visible real athlete** on the **selected day's weekday**. |
| Schedule (no real athlete) or Athletes | — | `FloatingActionButton` labelled "Add athlete" → Add an athlete hub. Hint: "Share your invite, enter a code, add an athlete, or import a schedule." |
| Invoicing | — | No FAB. |

**Schedule segment:** week strip (§7.2.4), Up next briefing card when `briefingOccurrence` exists (§7.2.8; keyed on the occurrence id so a different lesson starts collapsed), then the day agenda. (The footer legend "Recurring lessons, with this week's changes" is gone, `ad1e9bf`.)

**Day agenda** (borderless card):
- **Header:** just **"Today"**, or the long weekday ("Tuesday"), in display title3, because the strip above already shows the date (handoff §7). There is no date, no "Today" tag and no lesson count.
- **TalkBack:** the header is a heading, read "Tuesday, Sep 8" plus ", today" when it is today.
- A divider follows the header. Empty: "No lessons scheduled". Otherwise the lesson rows (§7.2.5) for the selected date, sorted by start minute then athlete name.

**Athletes segment:**
- Empty (no athletes and no Sample Athlete): card "No athletes yet" / "Share your invite code with parents — once they link their athlete to you, they'll show up here." / primary "Share my invite" (opens the Add an athlete hub) / chip "Refresh" (reload).
- Otherwise one roster card per visible athlete (§7.2.7), 10 dp apart.

**Invoicing segment:** §7.11 (`BillingRosterSection` with the filtered athletes).

**Back behaviour.** Roster is a top-level tab; system back (with predictive back animation) follows the tab rules in §8. Every sheet below dismisses on back.

#### 7.2.4 Week strip (iOS `WeekStripView`)

- Row: previous chevron (content description "Previous week") · centre · next chevron ("Next week"). Each a 48 dp touch target (iOS 44 pt `gradusTapTarget`).
- Centre: range label, "Sep 8–14" when both ends share a month, "Sep 29 – Oct 5" otherwise (short month names from the device locale). Under it, mono uppercase "THIS WEEK" when showing the current week, otherwise a text button "JUMP TO THIS WEEK" (accent ink) that returns to the current week and selects today.
- Seven equal-width day cells, Monday first. Each cell holds:
  - a one-letter weekday (S M T W T F S by weekday index; mono caption2 Bold, `textTertiary`, or `accentForeground` at 80% when selected);
  - the day-of-month number (display body, tabular; `textSecondary` on a day with no lessons, else `textPrimary`);
  - the day's lessons as **`TallyMarks`** (§8.6.7). These are crisp, in `accentInk`: four strokes and a fifth across, a number past 10, nothing on an empty day.

  The cell's states:
  - **Selected:** `accent` fill (radius 14), `accentForeground` text, and **dark marks on the lime**.
  - **Today, when not selected:** a 1 dp `accent` outline.
  - The strip sits in one borderless `card` (padding 10, radius 20).
- Cell content description: "`Monday` `8`, `N` session(s)" (singular "session" for 1). The tallies are hidden from TalkBack.
- Prev/next shift the week by 7 days and keep the same weekday selected (index clamped to 0…6). Week paging by swipe is **not** provided (iOS has none).

#### 7.2.5 Lesson rows (iOS `LessonRowView`)

- Layout: time column beside the card (`Row`). At font scale ≥ 1.5 (the same threshold as the segmented control) the time column stacks **above** the card (`Column`), matching iOS `AdaptiveStack(horizontalAlignment: .top)`; covered by the font-scale 2.0 screenshot.
- Left time column, min 44 dp wide: start and end in compact form, uppercased ("4P", "4:30P"; `LessonTime.compact`), start in primary ink, end in tertiary. Content descriptions use the long form: "4:00 PM", "to 5:00 PM".
- **Moved lesson** (handoff §7; `LessonOccurrence.scheduledStartMinute`, set when a `rescheduled` override changes the start): the time column shows the **new** start with the pen underline (`penUnderline`, `accent`, seed 7), then the usual start in `textTertiary` **struck through** by the pen (`penStrike`, seed 3). One TalkBack node reads "Moved to 4:00 PM from 3:30 PM"; the struck time is hidden. There is **no "Rescheduled" tag** any more. An override that keeps the start time shows nothing extra.
- Card (a control: `card` fill, radius 14, 1 dp `divider` edge): athlete full name (display title3, max 2 lines); when closed, the practice status chip at the end when the athlete has a summary with a weekly expectation:

| `hoursLogged / expectedHoursPerWeek` | Chip | Pen |
|---|---|---|
| > 1.5 | "Over target" | pink |
| ≥ 0.9 | "On track" | tennis |
| ≥ 0.5 | "Light" | orange |
| < 0.5 | "Behind" | pink |
| no expectation or 0 | none | — |

- Tap the name row to toggle expansion (state description "Expanded"/"Collapsed"; snappy spring, none when animations are off). Expanded edge: 1.5 dp `textPrimary` at 60%. **When open, the profile button sits beside the athlete's name** (`account_circle`, 48 dp, `contentDescription` "View {name}"; opens athlete detail).
- **Opened lesson card** (`LessonGlance`; iOS `ad1e9bf`, `34f5632`, `e5f0fd8`):
  - **Since last lesson:** when the summary has sessions, eyebrow "Since last lesson" + mono caption "`N` session(s)", then `FlowBars` of those sessions' states.
  - **Goal:** when there is a weekly goal, a 44 dp ring (4 dp stroke, `divider` track, `accent` arc, mono caption2 Bold percent in the middle) and "of **6h** / wk" (subheadline). The **status chip moves down beside the percent** it describes. TalkBack reads "75 percent of the 6 hour weekly goal".
  - **Actions are icons** at 48 dp:
    - **Message** (`forum`, "Message", test tag `roster.lesson.message`; iOS `LessonGlance` `onMessage`, #155) opens or creates the coach's room with this athlete: `POST /rooms/ensure {kind: "athlete", athleteId}` with **no `coachId`** (the server takes the coach from the session and checks the roster). It then switches to Messages and opens `Room(id)` (the shell's `openAthleteRoom`). On failure it shows the error snackbar "Couldn't open the conversation — {message}". Online only. Absent for the Sample Athlete.
    - **Reschedule** (`calendar_month`, "Reschedule") opens a `DropdownMenu` with "This date" and "Every week", which open the lesson sheet in occurrence or edit mode. It is absent for Sample Athlete.
  - **Layout** is fit-or-stack (`FirstThatFits`, §8.3), so the card never pushes past the screen edge on a 402 dp phone:
    1. goal and actions on one row;
    2. the goal, then the actions on their own row;
    3. the target, the status and the actions each on their own row (the target may wrap at accessibility sizes).
  - The old "Practice since last lesson" metric with seven flow dots, and the "View athlete" / "Recurring" / "This date" chips, are gone.
- Android-native mapping:
  - the row is a `Surface` with `Modifier.clickable` + `semantics { stateDescription }`;
  - the icons are `IconButton`s and the reschedule choice is a `DropdownMenu`;
  - there is no long-press `DropdownMenu` and no `SwipeToDismissBox` (iOS has no context menu or swipe on rows).

**Occurrence expansion** (`WeekSchedule.occurrences`): for each visible athlete's slot, expand the slot over Monday…Sunday of the shown week with `LessonRecurrence`; skip a date whose override is `canceled`; a `rescheduled` override replaces start/end (falling back to the slot's when null); sort by date, start minute, athlete name.

**`LessonRecurrence.occurrences(slot, from, to)`** (port of `src/lib/lesson-recurrence.ts`, must pass all 17 cases of `Contract/vectors/lesson-recurrence.json`, run by a JUnit 5 parameterized test reading the vendored file):
1. Parse `from`/`to` (`YYYY-MM-DD`); malformed → empty.
2. Cursor = max(`from`, `startsOn`); cursor > `to` → empty.
3. Advance cursor to the slot's weekday: `(dayOfWeek − weekday(cursor) + 7) % 7` days.
4. Biweekly anchor (only when `startsOn` is set) = first slot weekday on or after `startsOn`.
5. Step by 7 days while cursor ≤ `to`: weekly → include; biweekly → include when `round(daysBetween(anchor, cursor) / 7) % 2 == 0`, or always when there is no anchor; monthly / twice monthly → include when `(dayOfMonth − 1) / 7 + 1` is in `weeksOfMonth` (empty list never fires).

#### 7.2.6 Lesson slot sheet (iOS `LessonSlotSheet`)

Presented as a full-height `ModalBottomSheet` (`skipPartiallyExpanded = true`, drag handle visible) whose first row is the `GradusSheetHeader` (§8.6.2): "Close" at the start, centred title, action text button "Save" / "Saving…" (disabled unless valid). iOS equivalent: `.sheet` with `.large` detent and toolbar Close/Save (`ad1e9bf`). Back and predictive back dismiss without saving.

| Mode | Title | Description line | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| Create (`create(athleteId?, dayOfWeek)`) | "Add lesson" | "Recurring weekly lesson." | Athlete, Day, Start, End |
| Edit recurring (`edit(occurrence)`) | "Edit recurring lesson" | "Recurring weekly lesson." | Day, Start, End; "Delete recurring lesson" |
| This date (`occurrence(occurrence)`) | "Reschedule this date" | "Affects `2026-09-08` only — other weeks stay on the regular schedule." (raw ISO date, verbatim iOS) | Day (read-only), Start, End; "Cancel this date"; "Undo override" |

- **Athlete** (create only): `GradusPickerField` "Athlete" with placeholder "Pick an athlete", dashed while empty, and every real roster athlete by full name (the unfiltered roster; Sample Athlete is never listed). Below it a text button with person-add icon "Add new athlete…": keeps the create state (with the chosen athlete and day) and opens the New athlete sheet; when that sheet creates an athlete, the lesson sheet returns in create mode with **the new athlete preselected** and the same day.
- **Day**: seven equal-width toggle buttons in the order Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun (values 1…6, 0); selected = accent fill. In "this date" mode it is read-only text "`Tue` · `2026-09-08`".
- **Start / End**: two fields labelled "Start" and "End" showing the time; tapping opens an M3 `TimePicker` in a dialog (24-hour mode follows `DateFormat.is24HourFormat`), any minute (no step), stored as minutes since midnight. Create defaults: 16:00–17:00. Edit and this-date default to the occurrence's times.
- Inline error under the times when start ≥ end: "Start must be before end".
- **Delete recurring lesson** (edit mode; destructive text button with trash icon) → `AlertDialog` "Delete this recurring lesson?" / "This removes the weekly lesson from every future date. One-off overrides on this lesson are also removed." / "Delete" (error colour) / "Keep it". Success dismisses the sheet.
- **Cancel this date** (this-date mode; destructive) → `AlertDialog` "Cancel just this date?" / "The recurring lesson stays in place for other weeks." / "Cancel date" / "Keep it".
- **Undo override** (this-date mode, only when the occurrence has an override) → clears the override and dismisses.
- Errors from the server show as an inline error line in the sheet (and an error snackbar).
- **Save validity:** start < end, not saving, and in create mode an athlete chosen. iOS also blocks Sample Athlete and returns "Pick an athlete" if the athlete is not on the roster.

**Write behaviour** (`RosterModel.perform`, all five slot writes):
1. If the connectivity monitor says offline: enqueue immediately with a fresh UUID idempotency key (entity kind `lessonSlot`).
2. Else call live with a fresh UUID key. On transport failure (status 0) or 5xx: enqueue with the **same** key. On 4xx: show the server message as an error snackbar; no change.
3. After live or queued success, apply optimistically to the in-memory roster and persist the cache: add appends a slot (server id, or `pending-<uuid>` when queued) and re-sorts the athlete's slots Monday-first then by start; update replaces day/times; delete removes; cancel / reschedule / undo replace that date's override.
4. Queued → snackbar "Saved — it syncs when you're back online." and `etag = null`.
5. Success snackbars: "Lesson added", "Lesson updated", "Recurring lesson deleted", "This date canceled", "This date rescheduled", "Override removed".
6. Outbox entity labels (stored with the row; no Sync Center lists them at HEAD, §6.5): "Lesson for `Full Name`", "Delete lesson for `Full Name`", "Cancel `date`", "Reschedule `date`", "Undo override `date`". With no outbox available offline: error "You're offline. Try again when you're back online."; enqueue failure: "Couldn't save the change."

**Cadence — OPEN DECISION (§7.2.20 O1, needs Mariah).** iOS creates every slot as weekly and has no frequency picker; the roster card still shows non-weekly cadences ("·2w", "·2/mo", "·1/mo"). The server's `PATCH` schema defaults `frequency` to `weekly`, `weeksOfMonth` to `[]` and `startsOn` to null when omitted (`src/lib/coach-roster.server.ts` `slotTimesInput`, verified). iOS 1.0 `RosterModel.updateSlot` sends only `SlotBody(athleteId: nil, dayOfWeek, startMinute, endMinute)` and keeps the old frequency in its optimistic local copy, so iOS shows "·2w" until the next fetch while the server has already made the slot weekly. This is an iOS bug. **Recommended:** both clients send the slot's existing `frequency` / `weeksOfMonth` / `startsOn` on `PATCH` (and the same body for the queued outbox entry), with the iOS fix shipping in a server-compatible point release. **Until Mariah decides, Android sends the same body iOS sends** (`{dayOfWeek, startMinute, endMinute}`) and keeps the old cadence in its optimistic copy, exactly like iOS. Whether to add a cadence picker (QA.md §3 expects weekly / biweekly / twice monthly / monthly; the web has one, web #103) is a separate decision; until it is made, Android ships without one, like iOS.

**Lessons still `pending-<uuid>` (queued offline add).** iOS `RosterModel.addSlot` inserts the slot with id `pending-<UUID>` when the add is queued, and the "Recurring" and "This date" chips still show for its occurrences. An edit, delete, cancel, reschedule or undo on that occurrence queues a request to `/coach/lesson-slots/pending-…`. The server rejects it (`z.string().uuid()` in `lesson-slots/$id/index.ts` and the occurrence routes) when the outbox drains, and the row parks as failed in the outbox, listed nowhere at HEAD (§6.5). Android keeps this iOS behavior (A2). OPEN DECISION (§7.2.20 O2): the recommendation for both clients is to hide the Recurring / This date chips for slot ids starting `pending-` and show the caption "Syncing — edit once it's saved".

#### 7.2.7 Roster cards (iOS `RosterCardView`)

- Borderless card (`cardEdge`; its slot and claim chips are borderless too, `ad1e9bf`) with a 5 dp tennis-pen accent bar at the start; full name (display, max 2 lines); a "Sample" tag (pool pen) for Sample Athlete; an overflow `IconButton` (content description "Athlete actions") opening a `DropdownMenu` with one destructive item: "Remove from roster" (or "Dismiss sample athlete").
- Chip row (`FlowRow`): one chip per slot "`Mon` `4p`" plus "·2w" (biweekly), "·2/mo" (twice monthly), "·1/mo" (monthly); "No schedule" when there are none. Then the claim chip (rounded rectangle, clock icon) when not claimed:

| `claimStatus` | Chip | Accessibility hint |
|---|---|---|
| `waitingForParent` | "Waiting for parent" | "Their parent hasn't claimed this account yet, or still has to verify as an adult." |
| `waitingForAthlete` | "Waiting for athlete" | "They haven't claimed their account yet." |
| `notInvited` | "No invite sent" | "No email on file, so nobody can claim this account yet." |
| `claimed` or absent | none | — |

  Then the other-coaches chip (person-2 icon, secondary accent wash): "+ `LastName`" for exactly one other coach with a known last name, else "+`N` coaches".
- Tap the card → athlete detail.
- Remove confirmation `AlertDialog`: title "Remove `Full Name` from your roster?" / message "This unlinks the athlete from you. Their account, practice history, and parent stay intact. Their recurring lessons with you are unassigned and can be re-claimed later via your invite code." / "Remove" (destructive) / "Keep on roster". Sample: "Dismiss `Sample Athlete`?" / "This is a sample athlete used to preview the app. Dismissing hides her from your roster and schedule." / "Dismiss" / "Keep sample".
- Remove success: snackbar "`Full Name` removed from roster", drop the athlete and their summary from cache, then the shell's `onLinksChanged` refresh (connection celebrations and the coach-visibility list, §7.7). Remove is online-only (no queue).

#### 7.2.8 Up next briefing card (iOS `BriefingCard`, `WeekSchedule.upNext`, `RosterModel.briefingOccurrence`)

- **Which lesson.** `upNext` = today's occurrence (in the shown week's visible athletes) that has not ended (`endMinute > nowMinute`) and starts within **120 minutes** (`startMinute − nowMinute ≤ 120`; already-started lessons qualify), earliest start first. If the lesson-reminder push named an athlete, the card instead shows **that athlete's earliest not-yet-ended lesson today** until it ends (so back-to-back lessons show the pushed one, not the one still running), then falls back to `upNext`. No card when neither exists (including when the coach is viewing another week).
- Collapsed: sparkles icon in an accent disc, athlete name, "· 4:00 PM", chevron. **No eyebrow** (`ad1e9bf`). The whole row's TalkBack label is "Up next briefing, {name} at {4:00 PM}". State description Expanded/Collapsed.
- First expand loads `GET /coach/athletes/{id}/briefing?lessonDate=` (cached per `athleteId|date` for the session; not re-fetched unless Refresh).
- Expanded states: three placeholder lines while loading; "Couldn't load the briefing: `error`" on failure; otherwise the narrative, then a "Refresh" text button (the "As of" / "Generated" timestamp line is gone, `ad1e9bf`) (disabled while loading; absent for Sample Athlete) calling with `refresh=true`. On error there is **no** Refresh button (it exists only alongside a loaded briefing); collapsing and re-expanding the card retries, because failures are not cached. Errors are keyed `athleteId|date` and cleared at the start of each load (`RosterModel.briefingErrors`).
- **Lesson reminder push** (`coach/roster/briefing/<athleteId>`, sent about 15 minutes before a lesson, §6.6; delivered by FCM on Android): switches to the Schedule segment, clears the sport filter, jumps to this week and today, focuses the named athlete, and records the request time. The card expands itself and loads once when it appears (or is already on screen) and the request is no more than **10 minutes** old; an older request is discarded. A push with no athlete id falls back to the plain Up next card.
- Sample Athlete's briefing is the fixed `SampleAthlete.briefing` text, "As of" now, no network call.
- **`GET /coach/up-next`** (`UpNext.swift`) is the server-side equivalent used by the watch (iOS §6.15, §10.11 W2). On Android it feeds Wear OS (§6.15, §7.15) with the same `UpNextLesson` DTO (`slotId, athleteId, athleteName, athleteFirstName, lessonDate, startMinute, endMinute, minutesUntilStart, inProgress, briefingCached, activePlanId?`; id `slotId|lessonDate`; default limit 3, max 10) and the same `whenLine` copy: "Now, until 5:00 PM"; "Starting now, 4:30 PM" (`minutesUntilStart ≤ 0` and not in progress); "In 1 minute, 4:30 PM"; "In `N` minutes, 4:30 PM" (2…59); otherwise "4:30 PM"; and the clock-driven variant adds "Ended 5:00 PM". Put `UpNextLesson` and `whenLine` in `:core:data` so the phone and Wear modules share them.

#### 7.2.9 Athlete detail (iOS `AthleteDetailView`, `AthleteDetailModel`, `OtherCoachPlansSheet`)

**Presentation (Android-native).** iOS presents athlete detail as a `.sheet` containing a `NavigationStack` (`RosterView.AthleteDetailSheet`) and opens nested `.sheet(item:)`s from it (other-coach plans, coach-visibility dialogs, the §7.11 billing flows). Stacking several Compose `ModalBottomSheet`s is fragile, so on Android athlete detail is a **full-screen destination in the Roster nav graph** (type-safe route `AthleteDetail(athleteId: String)`), with a `TopAppBar` titled "Athlete", a navigation icon whose content description is "Close", and predictive back. The other-coach plans view is a `ModalBottomSheet` over it; §7.11 billing flows and §7.10 results present over it the way those sections specify. Opening a plan from inside it (plan card) **pops this destination first, then** switches to the Plans tab and opens the plan (iOS found that a tab switch under a covering sheet looked like nothing happened). Recorded in Appendix G as the mapping for iOS `.sheet` + `NavigationStack`.

Load: `GET /coach/athletes/{id}` (spinner only while there is no detail; error state "Couldn't load athlete" + "Try again"); then, if `hasAnySignal` and no summary yet, the AI summary. Coach visibility model activates if needed. The Club gate is read fresh from coach billing (`effectiveTier == club`) every time the screen opens; never cached (iOS §6.8).

Sections in order (`c8f83d6`). Section headers are mono caption Bold uppercase `textTertiary`, tracked 1.2, with heading semantics.

1. **Header.** Full name (`PageTitle`). Caption (`textTertiary`):
   - Sample → "Sample athlete · Parent: Sample Parent";
   - self-managed → "Adult athlete (self-managed)";
   - else "Parent: `Parent Name`" or "Parent: —".
2. **How practice felt** (iOS `PracticeTrendChart`, `AthleteDetailModel.loadPracticeEntries`; #142, #151, #154). The `PracticeLine` (§8.6.7: controls, window, header, plot, scrub and TalkBack) in a `GradusCard` (padding 14), directly under the header and above Goals. It shows each logged session on the athlete's plans and is fed from **real sessions**, never AI.
   - **Data:** for every plan in `detail.plans` with `sessionsTotal > 0`, page `GET /plans/{id}/sessions?limit=200&before=<oldest loggedAt>` (§7.2.2), newest first, at most **5 pages** per plan, all plans in parallel. Dedupe by session id. Stop on a short page or a page with nothing new. A plan that fails is left out, never failing the screen.
   - Each entry is `{date = loggedAt, rating = stateIndex, planId}`. The load runs alongside the detail (Android makes no AI summary call, A64). While the first load runs, a spinner (min height 280 dp) shows instead of "No practice logged". The plan chips list the plans that have sessions. The Sample Athlete uses its nine fixture sessions (`SampleAthlete.sessionFeedback`, dated `daysAgo` before now).
   - **Tests** (port `AthleteDetailPracticeTests`): paging with `before` and dedupe; the 5-page cap; a failed plan is left out; the Sample uses fixtures; runs break after 14 days; the dot rule at 24/25; the percent and summary sentence; the range windows; the filter reset; the gesture claims horizontal drag and a hold but not a vertical swipe (Compose UI test inside a `LazyColumn`).
3. **Goals.** Section title "Goals from athlete" (self-managed) or "Goals from parent & athlete".
   - **Empty:**
     - with coached sports, "`First` hasn't set goals for `A`, `B`, or `C` yet." (joined "A", "A or B", "A, B, or C");
     - without, "`First` hasn't set goals yet." (self-managed) or "`ParentFirst ?? AthleteFirst` hasn't set goals yet.".
   - **Each goal card** (borderless):
     - the sport eyebrow;
     - "**`Current level`** → **`Season goal`** this season";
     - the "Long-term" eyebrow + text when present;
     - "Set by `Name` · `Sep 20`" when `lastSetBy` exists. Athlete → athlete first name; parent → parent first name or "the parent". The date is abbreviated month + day, or the raw string if unparseable.
   - **When `differsFrom` exists** (Mariah 2026-09-20): the **goal fork** (§8.6.7) replaces the arrow line. It shows the current level, then a crisp `attention` fork to the two targets, each with "{Name} · {date}" in mono uppercase. The **newest target has the pen underline**. Long-term goals sit behind a "Long-term" disclosure ("{Name}: …" per person).
     - There is no attention-wash panel, no sentence and no "Talk it over" action (*code wins* over the handoff's flag, §8.6.8, §12 N98).
     - The fork is one TalkBack node (`semantics(mergeDescendants = false)` with this `contentDescription` on the container; the disclosure stays reachable): "`First` is `Current`. `A` wants `X` this season, set `date`; `B` wants `Y`, set `date`. `Newest` changed it most recently."
     - Test tag `athlete.goal.setBy.{sport}` on the single-version line.
4. **Practice expectations** (only when targets exist): unchanged from 91c6af2. Each sport is a borderless card with its eyebrow, level or "No level set yet", the 72 dp `GradusTextField` + "hrs/wk", and when overridden "Custom — default is `N` hrs/wk" + the chip "Reset to default". The same commit, focus-loss-but-not-to-the-lock, clamp, "abc" → 0, disable-while-saving, error snackbar and Sample read-only rules apply. The subtitle "What `First` should practice on their own each week. Starts from the Gradus default for their level." is **gone** (show, don't tell).
5. **Plans.**
   - Empty: "No active or benched plans for `First` yet.".
   - Otherwise the active plan cards, then a collapsible "Benched (`N`)".
   - **Plan card** (`GradusCard`, padding 14):
     - status bar (`accent` for active, `divider` otherwise);
     - title (display body, 2 lines);
     - at the end a **source tag**: "**Gradus**" (pool) for `isGradus`, "**By `First`**" (iris) for athlete-authored (§6.14, read-only);
     - `FlowBars` of sessions by state;
     - "`N` session(s) in `windowDays` days".
   - Tap opens the plan (disabled for Sample).
   - **No "Adopt plan" chip** (handoff §7: "There's no Adopt button, and coaches adopting starter plans is not needed").
6. **Competitions** (§7.10): not for Sample.
7. **Billing** (§7.11): not for Sample. Sample shows **"Session feedback"** instead: its nine fixture notes, eyebrow "Yesterday" or "`N` days ago".
8. **Also coached by** (only when other coaches exist). Per coach, a borderless card with:
   - the name (subheadline Bold);
   - sports joined " · ";
   - mono meta "**`N` plan(s)**", or "`N` plan(s) · locked" when not unlocked, or "No shared plans yet" when the coach has none (`otherCoachMeta`, `ad1e9bf`; it was "`a` active · `b` benched").

   Unlocked = Club tier **or** the coach id is in `sharedCoachIds` (parent-enabled visibility).
   - When unlocked and the coach has plans, the name block opens the read-only plans sheet (chevron; hint "Shows `Coach First`'s plans for `First`"); otherwise it is plain text.
   - Trailing: the visibility tag "Pending" / "Declined" / "Accepted" (tennis for accepted, orange otherwise), or a lock icon when locked with no link. The lock reads "Plans locked" and its action label carries "Reading another coach's plans needs the Club plan, or a visibility link the parent turns on." (that is the old footer, now a hint).
   - Then the coach-visibility chips (Accept / Decline for a pending request, Turn off for a connection), with the "Turn off sharing with `Name`?" dialog unchanged (§7.7).
   - The section footer is gone.

**Other coach plans sheet** (read-only, `ModalBottomSheet` with "Close" at the top start, no title; `ad1e9bf`). It is laid out like a plan screen:
- **Header:** a lock icon (TalkBack "Read-only. Only `Coach First` can change these plans.") and "`Coach Full Name` · `Sport` · `Sport`" (subheadline `textSecondary`).
- **Each plan, in order:**
  - the title in display **title**;
  - an "Active"/"Benched" tag;
  - meta "Updated `3d ago` · `N` sessions **this month**";
  - notes;
  - move rows exactly like the coach's own `MoveEditorRow`: a big target number (display title3) with a small unit (caption2 `textTertiary`), the name, expandable when it has cue/description/why. Rows are on `card`, radius 20, with a `divider` edge, `accent` when open.
- **No edit pens** anywhere.
- **Button:** the full-width primary **"Message `Coach First` about this plan"** (filled speech-bubble icon, test tag `otherCoach.message`). Shown only when the coach has plans. It opens a compose sheet laid out like the parent and athlete one (§7.6.7), not the room (Mariah, 2026-10-17, §12 N100):
  - `ModalBottomSheet`, half-expanded and draggable to full height, with a drag handle; title "Message Coach `First`", "Close".
  - "Your message will be tagged to this plan in your conversation."
  - The plan the message is tagged to: the coach's first **active** plan, else their first plan. With one plan, the plan chip (list-clipboard icon, title). With more than one, a `GradusMenuPicker` titled "Plan" over the plan titles (test tag `otherCoach.message.plan`).
  - Field "Ask Coach `First` about this plan…" (4–8 lines, focused on open; test tag `otherCoach.message.body`).
  - "Send" with a paper-plane icon ("Sending…"), disabled when the trimmed text is empty or while sending (test tag `otherCoach.message.send`).
  - Send: `ensureRoom(coachCoach(otherCoachId))`, then send `text(body, planId)` with an idempotency key. On success, close the athlete sheet (and the sheets on it) and open the room in Messages. A refusal shows the server's message as a toast; other failures "Couldn't send message — `message`". Either way the sheet stays open with the words. It needs a connection (no outbox), like §7.6.7.
- **iOS:** dead at `c8f83d6` (`AthleteDetailView` passed no `onMessage`); fixed with this exact flow in gradus-ios #161 (`AppModel.messageOtherCoach`). Both apps match.

#### 7.2.10 Lesson wrap-ups (iOS `RosterModel` wrap-up section, `WrapUpBanner`, `WrapUpListSheet`, `WrapUpPlanPicker`)

**Checking.** `refreshWrapUps()` calls `GET /coach/wrap-ups/pending` with the device's local date, weekday and minute. It runs on activation, on foreground, on pull to refresh, and **every 60 s while the Roster screen is composed and at least STARTED** (`repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED)` loop; cancelled when the screen leaves). Skipped when the roster has loaded and is empty. If no prompt is raised, the first pending wrap-up not yet "seen" this session is raised as the prompt and marked seen (in-memory set, per process, per wrap-up id `athleteId|lessonDate`).

**Prompt** (`BasicAlertDialog` with title, message, and vertically stacked full-width text buttons; iOS uses an alert):
- Title "`Name`'s lesson just ended." Message "Ended at `4:00 PM`. Want to update the practice plan, or re-deploy the current one?"
- Buttons in order: "Re-deploy" and "Edit plan" (only when the athlete has ≥ 1 active plan per a fresh `GET /coach/athletes/{id}/active-plans`; the dialog is not shown until that read finishes), "New plan", "Lesson didn't happen", "Not now · remind me later" (dismiss).
- Re-deploy: one active plan → record `redeployed`; more than one (any number since #52) → plan picker "Which plan is continuing?" (plan titles + "Cancel"), either choice records `redeployed`.
- Edit plan: one active plan → record `edited`, open that plan (read the id before the dialog closes); more than one → picker "Which plan do you want to edit?" then record `edited` and open the chosen plan. (If the id is somehow missing, it opens a new plan for the athlete, route `new:<athleteId>`, §7.3.)
- New plan: record `edited`, open a new plan for the athlete. Always offered; activating it never asks to bench or replace, however many plans the athlete already has active (no cap since #52, §7.3.5). Plan picker labels use `ActivePlanOption.displayTitle` (an empty title shows "Untitled plan").
- Lesson didn't happen: record `did_not_happen`.
- Not now: nothing is written; the banner stays.
- **Presentation gate.** The prompt goes up only when nothing else is over the Roster: no lock screen, Terms gate, password reset or Live Board cover (the shell's `PromptHold.covered`), no connection celebration or the check that may bring one (`celebrating`, waived when the coach tapped the banner), and no sheet or dialog of this screen open. While held, the banner stands in, and TalkBack hears once per hand-off: "Wrap up `Name`'s lesson. It's waiting at the top of the Roster." (iOS posts an announcement; Android uses a polite live region on the banner or `announceForAccessibility` where still supported (verify for API 36)). The invariant from iOS testing (2026-10-06) holds: **the coach always has the prompt or the banner, never neither.** iOS's three-miss retry loop exists only because UIKit refuses alerts over other presentations; Compose has no such refusal, so Android implements the hold/show rules but not the miss counter.

**Banner** (capsule on the popover surface): timer icon; "Wrap up `Name`'s lesson" (one) or "Wrap up `N` lessons"; mono "TAP TO WRAP UP"; with exactly one pending, a trailing "Re-deploy" chip that records `redeployed` directly (no picker). Visible when there are pending wrap-ups and no prompt is raised, or the raised prompt is held. Tap: one pending → raise its prompt as "requested"; several → mark all seen, clear any prompt, open the list.

**List sheet** ("Lessons to wrap up", `ModalBottomSheet` partially expanded at half height and expandable, iOS `[.medium, .large]`; "Close"): per row name, mono "ENDED `4:00 PM`", chips "Didn't happen", then (when the athlete has active plans, fetched per row) "Re-deploy" and "Edit plan" (filled/prominent), then "New plan". Same picker rules. When ≤ 1 remains after an action, the list closes.

**Recording** (`POST /coach/wrap-ups`, idempotency key `wrapup-<athleteId>-<lessonDate>`): try live; on status 0 or 5xx enqueue (entity kind `wrapUp`, label "Wrap-up for `Name`") and snackbar "Saved — it syncs when you're back online."; on 4xx error snackbar and keep the wrap-up. On success or queue: remove it from pending, clear the prompt if it was this one.

**Wrap-up push** (`coach/wrap-ups`, §6.6; entry points and notification channel in §7.2.21): open Roster, re-check; if the re-check raised a prompt, that is the answer (still subject to the gate, not "requested"); if the check failed: "Couldn't check for wrap-ups. Pull to refresh when you're back online."; if none: "No lessons are waiting for a wrap-up."; else one → prompt, several → list (all marked seen so the 60 s check cannot stack a dialog on the list).

#### 7.2.11 Get set up checklist bubble (#28; iOS `GettingStartedBubble`, `HelpBubble`, `CoachChecklist`)

- Data: `GET /coach/checklist`, re-read whenever the athlete count, total slot count, the Add an athlete hub's open state, or the import sheet's open state changes. Hidden until the first successful `GET /coach/checklist`; a later failed re-read keeps the last checklist on screen (`GettingStartedBubble.refresh`: `guard let fresh = try? await load() else { return }`). Hidden for good once `coachId` is null or all three steps are done.
- Shown on Schedule and Athletes, not Invoicing, above the FAB.
- **Collapsed** (`HelpBubble(progress = done to 3)`, §8.3; handoff "keep it"): a **lime pill**, not a bare mark with a number. It holds:
  - the Gradus mark;
  - "Get set up" in subheadline Bold `accentForeground`;
  - `StepDots(current = done + 1, total = 3, onAccent = true)`: pen checks for finished steps, the current dot, then rings.

  The pill is min 48 dp tall, with corner radii 24 except 6 at the corner nearest the FAB, and a black 18% shadow r8 y4. Content description "Get set up — `N` step(s) left".
- **Open:** bubble with tail toward the button; accent header with mark, uppercase "GET SET UP", meta "`done` / 3", close button ("Minimize getting started"); body = checklist with the current step (first not done) highlighted. A **done step** shows a pen check and its title is crossed off by the pen strike (`textTertiary` title); a to-do step shows a 1.5 dp `textTertiary` ring (Android fix: the iOS ring is stroked in the now-clear `cardEdge`, §12 N92):

| Key | Title | Description | CTA | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| schedule | "Upload or input your schedule" | Families entered it: "Your connected families already added their lesson times — they're on your schedule and you can edit them." Else "Add a photo of your schedule, a CSV, or type your lessons in." | "View schedule" / "Add my schedule" | Families → switch to Schedule; else open Schedule import |
| invite | "Invite parents or adult athletes" | "They join your roster and see plans, schedules, and progress." | "Invite" | Open Add an athlete hub |
| plan | "Create your first practice plan" | "Build a plan of moves and share it with an athlete." | "Create a plan" | Plans tab |

- Tapping a step minimises the bubble and runs its action. Minimised state is a per-device, per-coach preference: DataStore key `gradus.coachChecklist.<coachId>.minimized` (iOS UserDefaults). First load opens the bubble unless minimised. Open/close animates with scale+fade from the button corner; fade only when animations are off.

#### 7.2.12 Coach visibility requests banner (iOS `CoachVisibilityRequestsCard`, I13)

Capsule on the popover surface: eye icon; "`N` coach visibility request(s)"; mono "A PARENT WANTS TO CONNECT YOU"; trailing close icon ("Dismiss"). Shown once per distinct set of pending request ids (signature persisted in DataStore, iOS `CoachVisibilitySeenStore`); opening or dismissing records the set; a new request shows it again. Tap opens the coach visibility sheet (§7.7) and records the set when the sheet closes. The model (`GET /coach/visibility/mine`) activates with the Roster and refreshes on foreground.

#### 7.2.13 Add an athlete hub (iOS `InviteSheet`, `ShareInviteCard`, `InviteCodeEntryCard`)

Full-height `ModalBottomSheet` with internal steps. Top bar: on the hub, "Close"; on a step, "Back" (and system/predictive back returns to the hub instead of closing). Titles: "Add an athlete" / "Share my invite" / "Enter their code". The invite code loads on open if not loaded.

**Hub.** "Four ways to fill your roster." (iOS #131), then four row cards (icon, title, detail, chevron):

| Row | Detail | Action |
|---|---|---|
| "Share my invite" | "Send parents or athletes a link or code" | Share step |
| "Enter their code" | "They already gave you a code" | Enter-code step |
| "Add an athlete" | "Their name and a parent's email; we send the invite" | Close hub, open New athlete |
| "Import my schedule" | "A photo or a .csv — we read it for you" | Close hub, open Schedule import |

**Share step.** "Parents and adult athletes enter this code, or open the link, to connect to you." Card: eyebrow "Your invite code"; the code in large mono with letter spacing, selectable, read character by character by TalkBack (`VerbatimTtsAnnotation`); "gradus.training/i/`CODE`"; primary "Share" → Android Sharesheet (exact intent below; iOS `ShareLink(item: url, message:)`); chip "Copy code" → clipboard, snackbar "Code copied" (on Android 13+ the system shows its own clipboard confirmation, so the snackbar is shown only on API ≤ 32, per Android guidance). Load error: error line + "Try again". Loading: progress indicator. Below: "Rotate code" (disabled until loaded) → `AlertDialog` "Replace your invite code?" / "Links and codes you already shared stop working." / "Rotate" (destructive) / "Keep it"; success snackbar "New invite code. Old links no longer work." **Rotate failure:** iOS sets `inviteError`, but `ShareInviteCard` renders the error only when `code == nil`, so a failed rotate is silent and the old code stays on screen. Android matches this (A2). Open item §7.2.20 O3 recommends an error snackbar with the `userMessage` on rotate failure on both platforms.

**Share intent (exact).** `Intent(ACTION_SEND)`, `type = "text/plain"`, `EXTRA_TEXT = "Join me on Gradus with code CODE https://gradus.training/i/CODE"` (the iOS message, one space, the URL), `EXTRA_TITLE = "Share my invite"`, launched with `Intent.createChooser(send, null)`. The strings come from a Kotlin port of `ShareInviteCopy` (`url(code)`, `linkText(code)` = "gradus.training/i/CODE", `shareMessage(code)` = "Join me on Gradus with code CODE") plus `shareText(code)`. Unit tests port `ShareInviteCopyTests` and assert the exact `shareText`.

**Enter-code step.** "A parent's or an adult athlete's code. You'll be linked to everyone under it." Field "Their code", placeholder "ABCD2345", mono, all-caps keyboard (`KeyboardCapitalization.Characters`, autocorrect off, IME Done submits), normalised as typed to A–Z and 2–9, max 8 (`InviteCodeText.normalize`). Primary "Link" (the "Linking…" busy label is wired to `isSaving`, which the claim never sets; see below), enabled at exactly 8 characters. Claim tries the parent invite, then the adult-athlete invite; success line "Linked to the parent's account (`N` athlete(s))." or "Linked to the parent's account." or "Linked to the athlete's account."; then reload the roster, success snackbar with the same text, `onLinksChanged`. Failure: inline error. **Fallback rule** (iOS `AppModel.inviteClaimClosure`): *any* parent-claim error, including offline or network errors, falls through to the adult-athlete claim; the inline error is the adult claim's `userMessage` (via the shared `ApiError.userMessage`, so a 409 `roster_full` reads "Your roster is full on your current plan.", never the server text and never an upgrade link). Errors are cleared at the start of each attempt. **"Linking…"**: on iOS `claimInvite` never sets `isSaving`, so the button never shows "Linking…" (iOS bug). Open item §7.2.20 O4 recommends showing "Linking…" and disabling the button while the claim runs, on both platforms (logged as an iOS fix). Until Mariah decides, Android matches iOS (A2): "Link" stays visible.

#### 7.2.14 New athlete sheet (#30; iOS `NewAthleteSheet`)

Full-height `ModalBottomSheet`, `GradusSheetHeader` "Close" · "New athlete" · "Add athlete" / "Adding…" (disabled while saving). Its Sport and "Who gets the invite" pickers are `GradusPickerField`s. On open: clear errors, default the sport to the coach's first sport, and revalidate the roster (roster only; a 304 writes nothing); if the coach's sports change and the chosen one is gone, reset to the first.

Fields:
- "First name" / "Last name" side by side (placeholders "First", "Last"; autofill hints `personGivenName`, `personFamilyName`).
- "Sport" exposed dropdown (only when the coach has sports), display labels.
- "Date of birth (optional)": the shared birthdate field (§7.1): tapping opens an M3 `DatePickerDialog` titled "Choose a date", future dates not selectable; stored `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- "Who should we email?" dropdown **only when the birthdate makes the athlete 18 or older**: "A parent or guardian" (default) / "The athlete (18+)". Otherwise the recipient is always the guardian.
- Email field labelled "Parent or guardian email" (placeholder "parent@example.com") or, when the athlete is the recipient, "Athlete's email" ("athlete@example.com"); email keyboard, no autocorrect, no capitalisation.
- Note: adult → "An adult athlete can get the invite themselves, or a parent can."; otherwise "Athletes under 18 join through a parent or guardian, who confirms they're an adult and then gives the athlete their login. Add a date of birth of 18+ to email the athlete directly."

Validation on submit (errors shown under fields after the first attempt, announced): "First name is required", "Last name is required", "An email is required so we can send them an invite", "Enter a valid email" (must contain "@" and "." and no spaces). Submit trims names, lowercases the email, sends the birthdate only when valid, `emailRecipient` = effective recipient, with a fresh idempotency key. Online only. Success: reload roster, snackbar "`First` added — invite sent to `email`" (or "`First` added"), `onLinksChanged`, close, and if the lesson sheet launched it, return to it with the new athlete selected. Server refusals show inline and as a snackbar, verbatim, e.g. "Athletes under 18 need a parent or guardian email." and "Invite the parent or guardian for athletes under 18. To invite an athlete directly, enter a birthdate that makes them 18 or over." **Roster cap.** A 409 with code `roster_full` (`POST /coach/roster/athletes`, doc comment in `src/routes/api/v1/coach/roster/athletes/index.ts`) shows "Your roster is full on your current plan." inline and as an error snackbar. It never shows the server's "Roster limit reached (N athletes on your plan)." and never offers an upgrade or purchase link (iOS §6.8 rule 2, A10). The mapping lives in the shared `ApiError.userMessage` in `:core:api` (one place for every screen), a port of `GradusAPI/APIError.swift` with all of its fixed mappings, `roster_full` among them. Unit test: an `ApiError` with code `roster_full` and any server message → `userMessage == "Your roster is full on your current plan."`. The new athlete's card shows "Waiting for parent" until the parent verifies and claims; no room opens before that (iOS §6.13 A5–A6).

#### 7.2.15 Schedule import (iOS `ScheduleImport/*`, docs/README.md I14, work package 3.6)

Full-height `ModalBottomSheet` with its own top bar. Steps: source → review → done. **Never queued.** The photo path is online-only end to end (parse and commit). The .csv path reads the file on the device with no AI call, so it works offline up to review; only the commit needs a connection (iOS `ScheduleImportModel.ingestCSV`).

**Titles.** "Import my schedule" → "Review `N` athlete(s)" → "Import complete". Top bar: `GradusSheetHeader` "Close" on source and review (none on done; `ad1e9bf`); the review's three pickers are `GradusPickerField`s; "Import" / "Importing…" action on review, enabled per `canCommit`.

**Source step.**
- "A photo of your written or printed schedule, or a .csv from a spreadsheet — we read the names, days, and times for you."
- Row order (iOS `ScheduleImportFlow`): "Take a photo", "Choose a photo", **"Choose a .csv file" / "From Excel, Numbers, or Google Sheets"** (table icon; test tag `scheduleImport.chooseCSV`), "Enter it manually", then the link **"Get the CSV template"** (download icon, accent ink; hint "Save or send a spreadsheet with the right columns and examples"; `scheduleImport.csvTemplate`). The two photo rows ask for AI permission first (§6.7.1a); the .csv row and the template never do.
- "Take a photo" / "Use your camera" — iOS hides it only when `UIImagePickerController.isSourceTypeAvailable(.camera)` is false (`CameraCapture.swift`). Android: the manifest declares `<queries><intent><action android:name="android.media.action.IMAGE_CAPTURE"/></intent></queries>` (without it, package visibility on API 30+ makes `resolveActivity` return null and the row would be hidden on almost every device). Show the row when `packageManager.hasSystemFeature(PackageManager.FEATURE_CAMERA_ANY)` **and** the `MediaStore.ACTION_IMAGE_CAPTURE` intent resolves. Checks online **before** launching the camera (iOS `if importModel.checkOnline() { showingCamera = true }`). Uses `ActivityResultContracts.TakePicture` into a `FileProvider` URI for a file in `cacheDir/schedule-import/`: a single shot, no editing, matching iOS `UIImagePickerController`. Launch is wrapped in a catch for `ActivityNotFoundException`, which shows the source error "Couldn't load that photo.". The app does **not** declare the `CAMERA` permission (declaring it would make the intent require a runtime grant). Cancel returns to the source step silently. A CameraX in-app capture is not needed for parity; VisionKit-style multi-page scanning is deferred on iOS too. Instrumented test: the row is visible on a Pixel.
- **Process death while the camera app is open** (Android-only case; iOS's picker runs in-process). The pending capture `Uri`, the sheet's open state and its step are kept in `SavedStateHandle`. After a restore, the Roster reopens the import sheet on the source step and passes the returned `Uri` to ingest. The `rememberLauncherForActivityResult` callback is registered unconditionally at composition so the result is delivered after the restore. The temp file is deleted after ingest or on cancel. Test: Robolectric/`ActivityScenario.recreate()` with a pending capture delivers the image to ingest.
- "Choose a photo" / "From your library" — the system photo picker, `ActivityResultContracts.PickVisualMedia(ImageOnly)`. On Android 10 (minSdk 29, A6) the backported picker comes from Google Play services. To get it, `AndroidManifest.xml` declares `<service android:name="com.google.android.gms.metadata.ModuleDependencies" android:enabled="false" android:exported="false" tools:ignore="MissingClass"><intent-filter><action android:name="com.google.android.gms.metadata.MODULE_DEPENDENCIES"/></intent-filter><meta-data android:name="photopicker_activity:0:required" android:value=""/></service>`. Where the picker is still unavailable, the library falls back to `ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT` (`image/*`), which is acceptable. No `READ_MEDIA_*` or storage permission is ever declared. The picker opens even offline (iOS `PhotosPicker` does); the online check runs **after** a photo is picked (`onChange(photoItem)` → `checkOnline()`), and offline shows "You're offline. Try again when you're back online." without calling parse. A URI that cannot be read → "Couldn't load that photo."
- "Enter it manually" / "Add one athlete yourself" → close, open New athlete.
- **"Choose a .csv file"** → the Storage Access Framework picker (`ActivityResultContracts.OpenDocument`) with MIME types `text/csv`, `text/comma-separated-values`, `text/tab-separated-values`, `text/plain`, `application/csv`, `application/vnd.ms-excel` (Drive and Sheets report CSV under several of these; A58). Read the bytes with `ContentResolver.openInputStream`. A cancelled pick does nothing. A provider error or unreadable stream → source error "Couldn't open that file.". Then `ingestCSV(bytes)`:
  1. Decode as UTF-8 (strict: `CodingErrorAction.REPORT`), else `windows-1252`, else `x-MacRoman` (verify the charset name on API 29). If all fail → "Couldn't read that file. Save it as a .csv and try again."
  2. Parse with a 1:1 port of `ScheduleImportCSV.parse`:
     - **Delimiter:** tab when the first line has a tab, else comma. RFC 4180 quotes and doubled quotes. CRLF/CR/LF. A leading BOM is skipped. Blank rows and rows whose first cell starts with `#` are skipped.
     - **Headers:** trimmed, lowercased, spaces and dashes → `_`. Aliases: `first_name`/`first`/`athlete_first` → `athlete_first_name`; `last_name`/`last`/`athlete_last` → `athlete_last_name`; `day_of_week`/`weekday` → `day`; `start`/`time`/`start_minute` → `start_time`; `length`/`duration`/`lesson_length`/`minutes` → `length_minutes`; `repeat`/`recurrence` → `frequency`; `parent_email`/`guardian`/`parent`/`email` → `guardian_email`; `athlete_email_address` → `athlete_email`.
     - **Required columns:** `athlete_first_name`, `athlete_last_name`, `day`, `start_time`. When any is missing → "Missing column(s): {list joined ", "}. Get the template for the exact headers." With no header row → "That file looks empty.". With no data rows → "No lesson rows found in that file.".
     - **Day** (`parseDay`): sun/sunday/su = 0 … sat/saturday/sa = 6, including m, w, f, tu, th, tues, weds, thur, thurs; a trailing dot is dropped; digits 0–6 are accepted.
     - **Time** (`parseTimeToMinutes`): whitespace removed, then `h[:.mm][am|pm|a|p]` (12 pm stays 12, 12 am → 0, hours ≤ 23, minutes ≤ 59) or 3–4 digits `hmm`/`hhmm`.
     - **Length** (`parseLengthToMinutes`): `h:mm`, or a number with a unit starting with "h" meaning hours, else minutes, rounded. A blank length is 60. An unreadable one is 60 with the note "{label}: couldn't read the length "{raw}", so it's set to 60 minutes.".
     - **Frequency:** blank → weekly; contains `biweek`/`every_other`/`alternate` → every other week; contains `twice` → 2× per month; starts with `month` → monthly; else weekly.
     - **Sport:** matched to the coach's sports by key or catalog label (slugged). A blank cell uses the coach's first sport. An unmatched cell uses the first sport with the note "{label}: "{raw}" isn't one of your sports, so it uses your main sport.".
     - **Emails** are lowercased. `label` is the full name, or "Row {n}". An unreadable day or start sets the same `dayUnreadable` / `startTimeUnreadable` flags as a photo row.
  3. The rows go through the **same grouping, review and commit as a photo**. Grouping takes each group's first named sport (`ScheduleImportGrouping.group(lessons, sports)`).
- **"Get the CSV template"** → write `gradus-schedule-template.csv` (UTF-8 **with BOM**, so Excel keeps accented names) to `cacheDir/shared/`, and share it through the `FileProvider` with `ACTION_SEND`, `type = "text/csv"`, `EXTRA_STREAM`, `FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION`, `Intent.createChooser` (the iOS `ShareLink` to Files, AirDrop and email; §12 N83). The file content is the iOS `ScheduleImportCSV.template`, verbatim:
  ```
  # GRADUS LESSON SCHEDULE — fill in one row per weekly lesson, then upload this file.
  # Lines starting with # are ignored. Keep the header row below. Delete the example rows.
  #
  # athlete_first_name  Required.
  # athlete_last_name   Required.
  # day                 Mon / Monday / Tue ... any spelling works.
  # start_time          4:00 PM  or  4pm  or  16:00  or  1600
  # length_minutes      45  or  60  or  "1 hr"  or  "1.5 hours"
  # frequency           weekly | every other week | twice a month | monthly
  # guardian_email      Required for anyone under 18. We email them an invite.
  # athlete_email       Use this instead for adult (18+) athletes.
  # sport               Leave blank to use your sport.
  #
  athlete_first_name,athlete_last_name,day,start_time,length_minutes,frequency,guardian_email,athlete_email,sport
  Ava,Nguyen,Mon,4:00 PM,45,weekly,parent@example.com,,
  Liam,Brooks,Wed,17:30,60,every other week,parent2@example.com,,
  Jordan,Reyes,Sat,9:00 AM,1 hr,weekly,,jordan@example.com,
  ```
- While parsing: progress + "Reading your photo…". Errors (announced): offline "You're offline. Try again when you're back online."; repository missing "Import isn't available right now."; undecodable "Couldn't read that photo. Try a clearer picture, or enter rows manually."; parse failure → server message or the same sentence.

**Downscale and re-encode** (iOS `ImageDownscaler`): decode any supported image (JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF, WebP) with `ImageDecoder` (API 28+, so all of minSdk 29) on `Dispatchers.Default`, **downsampling during decode** so no full-resolution bitmap is ever held. Pixel main cameras save 12.5 MP by default and up to 50 MP in high-resolution mode, so a full ARGB_8888 decode is about 50–200 MB. Code: `ImageDecoder.decodeBitmap(source) { decoder, info, _ -> decoder.setTargetSize(w', h'); decoder.allocator = ImageDecoder.ALLOCATOR_SOFTWARE }`, where `(w', h')` is `info.size` scaled so the **longest side ≤ 2048 px** (rounded, never upscaled). iOS `ImageDownscaler.process` draws into a 2048-px renderer. Apply EXIF orientation to the pixels so the result is upright (ImageDecoder applies it on decode (verify)). Then `Bitmap.compress(JPEG, 80)` to a `ByteArray`: **JPEG quality 80**, no EXIF written (drops GPS and camera metadata). Only JPEG bytes ever reach parse: multipart part `image`, filename `schedule.jpg`, content type `image/jpeg`. Decode failure → the "Couldn't read that photo…" error. Unit-tested with a 4000×3000 fixture (→ 2048×1536), an 8160×6120 fixture (→ 2048×1536, must not OOM under a 256 MB heap), a portrait EXIF-rotated fixture, a HEIC fixture, and a 1000×800 fixture (unchanged size).

**Developer mock path.** The debug build's mock mode (§9, the equivalent of iOS `-GradusMock coach`, gradus-ios docs/README.md I14) returns the same three seeded parse rows for any image: 1 on-roster, 1 new, and 1 with an unreadable day. The "Take a photo" row is visible on the emulator (virtual scene camera, unlike the iOS simulator, which has none) and must also be verified on the Pixel.

**Review grouping** (`ScheduleImportGrouping`, mirrors web `groupRowsByAthlete`):
- Drop any row whose full name normalises to "sample athlete".
- Group key `first|last|email`, each part lowercased with whitespace collapsed, email = guardian email if non-blank else athlete email; groups keep first-seen order.
- Default recipient: athlete when only an athlete email was read, else guardian.
- `onRoster` when the trimmed lowercased full name matches a roster athlete; those re-link server-side and never count against the cap.
- **Cap pre-check** (iOS §6.8 rule 2): read coach billing fresh; `room = limit == null ? ∞ : max(0, limit − count)`; on-roster groups fit; the first `room` new groups fit; the rest get `overCap = true` and default to **Skip**. A failed billing read means no limit applied (the server still checks).
- Each review pass gets a new attempt id.

**Review card per athlete** (stable local UUID identity; renaming never reorders):
- "First name" / "Last name" fields (side by side; stacked at large font).
- "Sport" dropdown only when the coach has more than one sport (shows the first sport until changed; see open question on the unset value).
- "Who should we email?" dropdown "A parent or guardian" / "The athlete (18+)", always offered (the server voices every import invite for a parent or guardian regardless; the choice only decides which address wins, `schedule-import.server.ts` #30 note), and "Email" field (placeholder by recipient).
- Per slot editor: warning "Couldn't read — confirm" when the day or start was unreadable; "Remove" when the group has more than one slot; day toggles Mon…Sun (highlight only a day actually set, never a fallback); "Start" time field (default shown 16:00 when unread); "Frequency" dropdown "Weekly" / "Every other week" / "2x per month" / "1x per month"; "Length" presets "30m" "45m" "60m" "90m" plus a numeric "min" field (minimum 1). Any edit to a slot clears both unreadable flags (iOS behaviour: setting only the start time of an unread-day slot also sets Monday; keep identical and covered by a test).
- On-roster note: "Already on your roster — this adds lessons, not a new athlete."
- Over-cap row (attention wash): "Your roster is full on your current plan." with chips "Skip" / "Include anyway" (the chosen one bold). Never an upgrade call to action.
- Validation lines (`ScheduleImportValidation`, verbatim web `validateRow`): "Required" (missing first or last name); "Required for under 18 — or add an athlete email instead" (blank email); per resolved slot "Runs past midnight" (start + length > 1440) and "Duplicate — same athlete, same day and time".
- Empty review: state "Nothing to review" / "We couldn't find any readable lessons. Go back and try a clearer picture or the CSV template, or add an athlete manually."
- **"Check these" card** (after a .csv only, when it produced notes): eyebrow "Check these" and one caption line per note, as one TalkBack node (`scheduleImport.notes`), above the review cards.
- TalkBack announcement on entering review: "`N` athlete(s) found.[ `K` value(s) need(s) checking.] Check the names and lessons, then import." (exact iOS forms: " 1 value needs checking." / " {K} values need checking.", only when there are notes).

**Commit.**
- `canCommit` = online, not committing, and at least one group that is not skipped, has first and last name, and has **at least one** slot with a resolved day and start.
- Payload: every included group with ≥ 1 resolved slot, sending only its resolved slots (`endMinute = start + round(length)`), trimmed names, the one email in `guardianEmail` or `athleteEmail` per recipient, `sport`, `emailRecipient`, recomputed key. A named, included group with **zero** resolved slots is not sent but gets a local outcome: status skipped, "Confirm the flagged day or time, then import again." (it must never vanish). Empty payload → "Add at least one ready lesson before importing."
- **Idempotency key** = `"<attemptId>-<first 12 bytes of SHA-256(payloadJSON) as hex>"` where `payloadJSON` is the payload encoded with **sorted keys** (kotlinx.serialization does not sort, so canonicalise via `JsonObject` with keys sorted recursively before hashing). An unedited retry after a transport/5xx failure replays the same key; any edit changes the payload and the key. Commit errors show inline at the bottom of review.
- During commit iOS leaves "Close" enabled; closing the sheet abandons the Done screen while the request may still land server-side (a later import of the same names re-links instead of duplicating). Android matches this: Cancel and back stay enabled, and the commit runs in the ViewModel's scope, so a configuration change (rotation, dark-mode switch) never restarts or loses it.

**Done step.** One card per outcome: check icon (success) or exclamation icon; name; line per `ScheduleImportCopy.outcomeLine`: roster-full reason (either `skipped` or `failed`) → "Your roster is full on your current plan." (never the server's "Roster limit reached (N athletes on your plan)."); created/linked → "`N` lesson(s)" + " · invite sent to `email`" when invited; failed → server message or "Could not import this athlete."; skipped → message or "Skipped."; unknown status → message or "Something went wrong." Unknown `status`/`reason` values decode to `unknown` rather than failing. Full-width "Done" / "Done…" reloads the roster, then closes.

#### 7.2.16 Sample Athlete (iOS `SampleAthlete.swift`, web `src/data/sample-athlete.ts`)

- Shown when the feature switch is on (default on), the roster has loaded at least once, the real roster is empty, the coach's sports include `figure_skating`, and it has not been dismissed. Dismissal is a device-wide DataStore boolean `gradus.sampleAthleteDismissed` (iOS stores it per device, not per coach; keep identical).
- Id `sample-lisa-simpson`, name "Sample Athlete", parent "Sample Parent", sport figure skating, one lesson **today** (slot id `sample-lesson-slot`, weekly, today's weekday) so the Up next card shows at once. The times use Kotlin integer division, exactly as in `SampleAthlete.rosterAthlete`: `start = min(((nowMinute + 20 + 2) / 5) * 5, 22 * 60 + 45)` and `end = min(start + 45, 23 * 60 + 55)`. This rounds now + 20 to the **nearest** 5-minute mark, so the start is now + 18 … now + 22. Edge case: after about 23:10 the clamped lesson may already have ended, so no Up next card shows. The starter plan id is `sample-juvenile-plan`. Unit tests: nowMinute 600 → start 620, 602 → 620, 603 → 625, 1400 → 1365 (end 1410).
- Fixtures copied verbatim from iOS: practice summary (6.5 h of 8 h, states [4,3,3,4,2,3,1,3,2]), detail (goal Juvenile → Intermediate with the parent's differing version, starter plan "Juvenile — Free Skate" `isGradus`), AI summary (verdict increase), briefing narrative (five paragraphs), nine session-feedback notes.
- No request is ever made with the sample id: no slot edits, no briefing/summary refresh, no adopt, no plan open, no billing or competition sections; "Create new lesson" is not offered while only the sample exists.
- Removing it from the card menu dismisses it (no network call).

#### 7.2.17 Offline behaviour by action

| Action | Offline behaviour | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Open Roster, browse weeks, expand rows, read practice metrics, filter by sport | Works from cache; Invoicing segment per §7.11. **[code wins]** The cache never expires on iOS: Android serves the per-user snapshot whatever its age and shows no staleness UI (the "7 days" in iOS §6.5 is not enforced). | iOS §6.5, `RosterCache`, `RosterModel.refreshOnForeground` |
| Add / edit / delete lesson, cancel / reschedule / undo a date | Queued; shown at once; "`N` to sync" | `RosterModel.perform` |
| Record a wrap-up | Queued on transport/5xx | `recordWrapUp` |
| Check wrap-ups | Shows nothing new; push open says it couldn't check | `openWrapUpsFromLink` |
| Briefing first load / refresh | Error line "Couldn't load the briefing: …" | `BriefingCard` |
| Open athlete detail | Error state with "Try again" (no detail cache) | `AthleteDetailModel` |
| Practice target, adopt plan, add / remove athlete, invite code, enter a code, rotate | Online only; error message | iOS code |
| Schedule import | Camera: refused before launch. Photo picker: opens; the online check runs after a photo is picked and shows "You're offline. Try again when you're back online." without calling parse. Commit: refused offline. | `ScheduleImportModel.checkOnline`, `ScheduleImportFlow.swift` |
