### 7.5 Messaging and safety (all roles)

**Scope.** This covers the Messages tab, conversations, voice notes, report and block, the blocked-people list in Settings, the read-only "other coach's plan" sheet opened from a thread, and the safety copy those screens show. Every behavior below comes from the iOS 1.0 reference implementation at gradus-ios HEAD 91c6af2 (`Packages/FeatureMessages/**`, `Packages/GradusCore/Sources/GradusCore/Messaging/*`, `Packages/GradusCore/Sources/GradusCore/Audio/Audio.swift`, `Packages/GradusAPI/Sources/GradusAPI/{VoiceNoteStorage,Realtime}.swift`, `Packages/FeatureSettings/Sources/FeatureSettings/BlockedUsersView.swift`) and from iOS PRD §7.5, §6.6, §6.7, §6.13 and decisions #31, #32 and #48. Parity rules are A2 and §4.3. Where the iOS PRD and the iOS code disagree, the code wins, and the place is marked **(code wins)**. Where iOS has a gap that Android should not copy, it is marked **(iOS gap)** and listed in §12. Copy in quotes is the iOS copy, verbatim, and Android uses it as is unless a row names the Android replacement.

Related sections. The outbox and WorkManager drain are §6.5. FCM, the notification channels and the server sender are §6.6. Voice capture across the app is §6.7. App Links are §6.10. Age rules are §6.13. "Message coach about this plan" is §7.6. Recaps that post into rooms are §7.10. Report a resource and the Safe Sport panel are §7.9. Toasts and haptics are §7.13; in this section "snackbar" always means the Gradus toast host of §7.13.3, not Material `SnackbarHost`. There is no global offline banner (§7.13.4). The watch is §7.15.

**7.5.1 Feature table (mirrors iOS PRD §7.5)**

| Feature | iOS 1.0 (reference) | Android requirement | Pri |
|---|---|---|---|
| Conversations list | `RoomsListView` / `RoomsListModel`: rooms with last-message preview, an unread count (the dot is gone, `ad1e9bf`), "New" picker, pull to refresh, `GET /rooms` with ETag, realtime refetch | Compose `RoomsListScreen` + `RoomsListViewModel`, the same content and states. Material 3 pull-to-refresh (`PullToRefreshBox`). The ETag lives in the ViewModel with the list it validates. Memory only, no rooms or message cache (iOS code parity; a cache is an open decision in §12, see 7.5.12). | P0 |
| Unread total | Tab badge from `GET /messages/unread-total` (`AppModel.refreshUnread`, `RoleTabsView.swift` `.badge(…)`). iOS HEAD sets no app-icon badge number: the server's APNs `aps` carries only `alert`, `sound` and `thread-id` (`push-notify.server.ts` `pushPayload`), and no iOS code sets a badge count, so iOS PRD §6.6 "Badge equals the unread total" is unimplemented **(code wins)**. | `BadgedBox` on the Messages `NavigationBarItem`. The launcher shows its own dot from active notifications (no server change). No `setNumber` count in 1.0. See 7.5.10. | P0 |
| Room view | `RoomView` / `RoomSession`: cursor paging, realtime, optimistic send, pending sends from the outbox with Retry and Delete, voice notes, plan tags, read marks, a keyboard-safe composer | Compose `RoomScreen` + `RoomViewModel` with the same behavior. Edge-to-edge with `imePadding()`, predictive back. | P0 |
| Voice notes | `VoiceRecorder` (AAC .m4a, 24 kHz mono, about 32 kbps, 180 s cap). Upload to `voice-notes/<roomId>/<userId>/<uuid>.m4a`, with an inline base64 fallback. `AudioPlayer` (AVPlayer). WebM cannot play. | `MediaRecorder` with the same settings. Upload with supabase-kt Storage. Playback with Media3 ExoPlayer, which also plays legacy WebM/Opus (7.5.8). | P0 |
| Transcripts | Made on the iPhone and sent with the note (`transcript`, web #238). Shown under the bubble; "Transcript coming" while nil and the note is under 15 minutes old. Read in the VoiceOver label. | Made on the phone on API 33+ (A55, §6.7.6), else `null`. Same display rules. Read in the TalkBack label. | P0 |
| Minors text only | No mic when `room.viewerTextOnly` (#32, #48) | Same. RECORD_AUDIO is never requested in that state. | P0 |
| Room rule for minors | Enforced on the server (#31). The client shows the server's message. | Same. No client-side age logic. | P0 |
| Parent pause | The composer is replaced by a notice that depends on the viewer's seat (§6.13 C) | Same | P0 |
| Report and block | Header overflow menu (per person), message long-press menu, report sheet, block confirmation | TopAppBar overflow `DropdownMenu`, long-press menu, `ModalBottomSheet`, `AlertDialog` | P0 |
| Blocked people | Settings → Account → "Blocked people" | Same row, same screen | P0 |
| Other coach's plan | `OtherCoachPlanSheet`, read-only, `GET /coach/other-plans/{planId}` | Full-height `ModalBottomSheet` | P0 |
| Report a resource | With Resources | §7.9 | P1 |
| Competition recaps in messages | Recaps post as ordinary messages. `MessageKind` is only `text`/`voice` at HEAD (code wins over iOS PRD §7.5 "recap message type"). | Rendered as text bubbles. No special type. See §7.10. | P1 |
| Messaging on the watch | *Changed 2026-10-11 (#54):* a tap on a message notification opens the conversation in the watch app; latest 20, marked read, reply by dictation, Scribble, keyboard or quick reply, text only; a Messages row for every role | The Wear app's own notification copy (§6.15.8) opens the conversation; Messages screens per §7.15.7 | P0 |
| Reply from a notification | *Added 2026-10-11 (#54):* a text Reply on the message notification sends to that room without opening the app, through the thread's send path, with a local notice when it didn't go | `RemoteInput` Reply on Android 12+ (§6.6.11) | P0 |

**7.5.2 Data contract (shared with the web; do not fork)**

Everything goes through API v1 except realtime and the voice-note upload, as on iOS (iOS §6.3, `MessagesRepository.swift`, `VoiceNoteStorage.swift`, `Realtime.swift`). The Kotlin client is generated from the vendored `openapi.json` (§9). Domain models mirror `MessagingModels.swift` field for field.

| Call | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/rooms` (`getRooms`), `If-None-Match` | Rooms list | 200 `{rooms:[RoomSummary]}` with `ETag`, or 304. A 304 keeps the current list. |
| `GET /api/v1/rooms/{id}?limit&cursor` (`getRoomsById`) | One page | `{room: RoomHeader, items: [Message] oldest-first, nextCursor}`. The server allows `limit` 1–200 (default 50); the client sends **50** (`MessagingDependencies.pageSize`). `nextCursor` walks back in time. 404 → "missing" state. |
| `POST /api/v1/rooms/{id}/messages` (`postRoomsByIdMessages`), header `Idempotency-Key` | Send | The body is kind-discriminated: `{"kind":"text","body",planId?}`, `{"kind":"voice","audioPath","mimeType","durationSeconds",planId?}`, or `{"kind":"voice","audioBase64","mimeType","durationSeconds",planId?}`. 200 returns `{ok:true,id}` or `{ok:false,reason,message}`, with `reason` one of `blocked`, `coach_unlinked`, `guardian_required`, `provisional`, `paused`, `paused_by_parent`, `text_only`. Server limits: text 1–4000 chars, `durationSeconds` 1–180, inline audio ≤ 8 MB, `audioPath` must start with `<roomId>/<userId>/` and end in `.m4a`/`.mp4`/`.webm`/`.ogg` (`src/lib/messages.server.ts`). |
| `POST /api/v1/rooms/{id}/read` | Mark read | Returns `{marked}` |
| `GET /api/v1/rooms/{id}/active-plans` | Plan-tag choices | `{plans:[{id,title}]}` |
| `GET /api/v1/messages/unread-total` | Badge | `{total}` |
| `GET /api/v1/message-targets` | New-conversation picker | `{targets:[{kind,group,coachId?,athleteId?,otherCoachId?,parentId?,primaryLabel,secondaryLabel?}]}`. Unknown `kind` values are **dropped, not fatal** (`MessageTargetWire`). |
| `POST /api/v1/rooms/ensure` | Open or create a room | One of `{kind:"athlete",coachId?,athleteId}`, `{kind:"coach_coach",otherCoachId}`, `{kind:"coach_parent",parentId}`. Returns `{id}`. Errors include 403 `guardian_required`, `provisional`, `paused`, `paused_by_parent` (§6.13 A6). |
| `GET /api/v1/coach/other-plans/{planId}` | Other coach's plan | 403 `plan_required` when the viewer may not read it |
| `GET/POST /api/v1/safety/blocks`, `DELETE /api/v1/safety/blocks/{userId}` | Block list | `POST {targetUserId}`. 422 "You can't block yourself." |
| `POST /api/v1/safety/reports` | Report | `{targetUserId?, messageId?, resourceId?, reason, note, alsoBlock}` → `{blocked}` |
| Storage `voice-notes` bucket, upload with the user's bearer token | Voice-note upload | supabase-kt Storage, `upsert=false`, content type `audio/mp4` |
| Realtime `postgres_changes` INSERT on `public.messages` | Refresh signal | 7.5.9 |

**Enum tolerance.** The generated `reason` enum on the send response and every enum in these payloads must decode unknown values without failing. Unknown values map to a generic refusal that shows the server's `message`. This follows the iOS S2 handoff rule ("must not crash on the new cases", `handoff-consent-S2-S3.md`). Use kotlinx.serialization with `coerceInputValues` and an `UNKNOWN` fallback. Add a test.

**Error snackbars.** Every "error snackbar" in this section is an error toast from §7.13.3 (port of `ToastCenter.show`, `GradusDesign/Components/Toast.swift`): TalkBack hears "Error: {message}"; it never auto-dismisses and shows a visible ✕; it is not drawn when the same text is already shown inline (the composer `ErrorLine`, deduped as on iOS); and it is reported to `POST /api/v1/errors`, except connectivity (offline) messages (`AppModel` `onError`).

**Display helpers.** Port `MessageFormatting` and the model computed properties exactly. These are pure Kotlin functions in `:core:data` (`messaging` package, §9.1), unit-tested with the iOS test vectors.

| Helper | Rule (from `MessagingModels.swift`) |
|---|---|
| `RoleInRoom.word` | "Coach" / "Parent" / "Athlete". Sort rank: athlete 0, parent 1, coach 2. |
| `RoomParticipant.prefixedFirstName` | "Coach Linnea", "Parent Corin", "Maeve" (athletes take no prefix) |
| `RoomSummary.others` | Participants whose `userId != myUserId`, sorted athletes → parents → coaches |
| `RoomSummary.displayName` | `others` prefixed first names joined with " & ". With nobody else, "Conversation". Example: "Maeve & Parent Corin". |
| `RoomSummary.previewLine` | No last message: "No messages yet — say hello.". Sender deleted: "{Role} (deleted account): Message deleted". Otherwise the prefix is "You: " when `senderRole == myRole`, else "{Role} {first word of senderFirstName}: ". The body is "Voice note" for voice notes, the text otherwise. *Parity note:* "You" is decided by **role, not user id** (the web's `room-list.tsx` logic), so a co-guardian's message reads "You: " to the other parent. Replicate it; do not "fix" it on one client only. |
| `RoomHeader.title` / `subtitle` | `others` first names joined with " & " ("Maeve & Corin"). Roles upper-cased and joined with " · " ("ATHLETE · PARENT"). |
| `Message.senderDeleted` | `senderDeletedAt != null` or `senderUserId == null` |
| `Message.senderLabel` | "Coach Linnea", or "Coach (deleted account)" when deleted |
| `Message.isMine(myUserId)` | `!senderDeleted && senderUserId == myUserId` |
| `Message.transcriptText` | Trimmed transcript, or null when blank or absent |
| `relativeTime` | "just now" (<1 min), "5m", "3h", "2d", "3w" (<5 weeks), else abbreviated month and day ("Sep 5"). Shown upper-cased in rows. |
| `relativeTimeSpoken` (TalkBack) | "just now", "1 minute ago", "5 minutes ago", "3 hours ago", "2 days ago", "2 weeks ago", else full month and day ("September 5"). Still used by the blocked-people list; **no longer by the rooms list** |
| `listTime` (rooms list, `ad1e9bf`, iMessage-style) | Same calendar day as now → the time (`DateFormat.getTimeFormat`, the device's 12/24-hour setting); the day before → "Yesterday"; within the last 6 days from the start of today → the full weekday ("Tuesday"); otherwise the numeric date (`DateFormat.getDateFormat`, e.g. "10/3/26"). Shown upper-cased in rows |
| `listTimeSpoken` (TalkBack) | The same as `listTime` within the last week; older → full month and day ("October 3") |
| `dayHeader` | "Today", "Yesterday", else "Monday, Sep 1" (`EEEE, MMM d`, `Locale.US`) |
| `duration` | "0:00" when null or <1, else "m:ss" ("1:05") |
| `groupByDay` | Consecutive messages grouped by `dayHeader`, in order |
| `voiceNoteDescription` | "voice note, 0:42. Transcript: …", or "voice note, 0:42, transcript coming" |
| `OutgoingMessage.preview` | The text body, or "Voice note (m:ss)" |
| `OtherCoachPlanForMessage.relativeDay` | "today" (≤0 days, rounded), "Nd ago" (<30), "Nmo ago" (<12 months, days/30 rounded), "Ny ago" (days/365 rounded), "" when the date can't be parsed |
| `messagesPath(roomId)` | `/api/v1/rooms/{percent-encoded id}/messages`. This is also the outbox key (7.5.6). |

The message time under each bubble uses the device's 12/24-hour setting (`DateFormat.getTimeFormat(context)`), which is the Android equivalent of `date.formatted(time: .shortened)`.

**7.5.3 Messages tab: conversations list**

Screen `RoomsListScreen`, the root of the Messages tab. The tab order follows the role (iOS `Roles.swift`, with Live dropped on phones, §6.9.1, §8.4): coach Roster · Plans · Resources · Messages · Settings; parent and athlete Plans · Messages · Resources · Settings. The tab label is "Messages". Its icon is a Material Symbols two-bubble chat glyph, the equivalent of SF Symbol `bubble.left.and.bubble.right` (§8).

- **Header.** No top app bar (§8.4). `PageTitle("Messages")` with **"New"** as its accessory: the shared lime chip (`GradusChipButton(prominent = true)`, compose icon, the same style as Resources' "Add resource"; `d23ab4a`), then Live inline. It opens the new-conversation sheet (7.5.4). **Every role sees New**, as on iOS. For a parent or athlete the targets are their own coaches. Test tag `messages.new`.
- **States** (in this order):
  - Loading with no rooms yet: a placeholder card "Loading conversations…" with a shimmer.
  - Error with no rooms: a card showing a cloud-off icon (`wifi.exclamationmark` on iOS), the mapped error message ("You're offline. …" when offline) and a "Try again" button. This is also what the tab shows offline at launch (7.5.12).
  - Empty: centered card. Coach: "No conversations yet. Tap New to start one." Parent and athlete: "No conversations yet. Your coach's messages land here." (`RoleTabsView.swift`).
  - Loaded: one card per room, in server order.
- **Row** (`RoomRow`):
  - **No unread dot** (`ad1e9bf`): the count pill below is the marker.
  - `displayName` in bold body text.
  - Right-aligned **`listTime(updatedAt)`** (§7.5.2), upper-case mono caption.
  - A small mic icon before the preview when the last message is a voice note.
  - `previewLine`, up to 2 lines, bold and primary color when unread, secondary color otherwise.
  - A count pill (attention color) when unread.
  - The card border is accent when unread, divider otherwise.
  - Tap opens the room. Test tag `messages.room.<id>`.
- **Row TalkBack label.** One merged node: "{displayName}, {previewLine}, {listTimeSpoken}[, N unread]".
- **Loading rules** (`RoomsListModel`):
  - On screen start: load, then subscribe to the all-rooms realtime stream (7.5.9). On stop: unsubscribe.
  - On returning to the foreground: load again and resubscribe.
  - Pull to refresh: load.
  - Each load sends `If-None-Match` with the ETag, **only when the list that ETag validates is in memory**. On 304 the list stays as it is. The ETag is held in the ViewModel next to `rooms` and is never persisted on its own (iOS keeps both in memory on `RoomsListModel`). If a cache is approved (§12), store the ETag in the same row and transaction as the cached rooms and wipe both together. Test: a 304 arriving with no list in memory → refetch without `If-None-Match`; the empty state is never shown from a 304.
  - **A cancelled request is not an error.** A released pull-to-refresh or a closed screen must not show the raw cancellation text (iOS beta fix, 2026-10-07, `MessagingTests` "A cancelled refresh is not an error"). Map `CancellationException` and OkHttp `Canceled` to a no-op.
  - A real failure with rooms already on screen is **silent**: the list stays and no snackbar is raised (there is no offline banner; the foreground `/me` refresh toast covers connectivity, §7.13.4). Only with an empty list does the error card show (`RoomsListView` shows `model.error` only when `rooms.isEmpty`; `RoomsListModel.load` raises no toast).
- **After New.** When the sheet returns a room id: close the sheet, reload the list, then open the room.
- **Phones only (A4).** The iPad two-column rooms → room layout (iOS §8.4) is deferred together with tablet layouts. Tablets and foldables get the single-column phone layout. Content is capped at a 640 dp readable width, as on iOS.

**7.5.4 New conversation sheet**

`NewConversationSheet` / `NewConversationModel`. On Android it is a full-height `ModalBottomSheet` (`skipPartiallyExpanded = true`) with a `GradusSheetHeader` titled "New conversation" and a "Close" text button at the start (`ad1e9bf`). It shows the M3 drag handle (iOS `.presentationDragIndicator(.visible)`, `RoomsListView.swift`). Predictive back and swipe-down dismiss it.

- **Search.** A single-line field with placeholder "Search", TalkBack label "Search people", autocorrect off. It requests focus (and shows the IME) **once the targets have loaded**, not when the sheet opens (`NewConversationSheet.swift` sets `searchFocused = true` after `await model.load()`). Matching is a case-insensitive substring search over `"{primaryLabel} {secondaryLabel}"`. A blank query matches everything (`MessageTarget.matches`).
- **Segment chips.** Shown only when more than one group has targets: "All", then the groups present, in the fixed order **Athletes, Parents, Coaches** (`groupOrder`). Use M3 `FilterChip`s in a horizontally scrolling row.
- **States** (in this order):
  - Loading: placeholder card "Loading…".
  - Error with no targets: a cloud-off icon, the error and "Try again".
  - No targets: "No one to message yet. People appear here once you're connected."
  - Search or segment matches nothing: "No matches."
  - Otherwise: one section per group, with an eyebrow label for the group and a card of rows. Each row shows the primary label (bold), the secondary label (caption) if present, and a trailing chevron. Rows are at least 48 dp tall (iOS 44 pt). Test tag `messages.target.<id>`.
- **Tap a row.** Call `POST /rooms/ensure` with the target. While it runs, all rows are disabled (`isStarting`). On success, return the room id to the list (7.5.3). On error, show the server's message in a snackbar and keep the sheet open. This is where the room rule surfaces (#31): for example, "This athlete's parent or guardian needs to claim and verify their account before messages can start." (`ROOM_RESTRICTION_MESSAGES`, `src/lib/guardian-verification.server.ts`).
- **Known server gap.** Provisional athletes may still be listed for coaches, and opening one answers 403 `provisional` (`handoff-consent-S2-S3.md` §8). The client shows the message and does not filter.
- **What the sample data shows** (`SampleMessaging`): a coach reaches their athletes, those athletes' parents, and co-coaches of a shared athlete. A parent or athlete reaches only their own coach(es). The server decides this; the client only renders the list.

**7.5.5 Room screen**

`RoomScreen(roomId)` is a destination in the Messages tab's back stack (route `rooms/{id}`). It is also reached from push, App Links (7.5.10), the session flow's "Message Coach" (§7.6) and `RunnerPlanDetail.onOpenRoom`.

**Top app bar.**
- The center title is `header.title`, bold, up to 2 lines, with `header.subtitle` beneath in an upper-case mono caption. Both form one TalkBack node. The fallback title is "Conversation".
- A trailing overflow `IconButton` (TalkBack "Conversation options", test tag `room.options`) appears only when at least one other participant has a non-null `userId`. Deleted accounts cannot be reported or blocked.
- The overflow opens a `DropdownMenu`. For each such person it has "Report {first}" (flag icon) and "Block {first}" (destructive color). When there is more than one other person, each pair sits under a section label with their first name. This is the Android equivalent of SwiftUI `Menu` with `Section`s.

**Body states.**
- **Loading:** four alternating placeholder bubbles with a shimmer. TalkBack: "Loading this conversation".
- **Missing (404):** state view (icon `chat_error`) titled "Conversation not found", message "It may have been removed, or it isn't yours."
- **Failed:** state view (icon `cloud_off`) "Couldn't load the conversation", the error, and "Try again". This is also the offline result for any room, since there is no message cache (7.5.12).
- **Loaded:** the thread, plus a bottom bar. The bar is the composer, or the paused notice when `header.messagingPausedByParent == true`.

**Thread** (a `LazyColumn`, newest at the bottom; the content is capped at 640 dp wide).
- **Load earlier.** When `nextCursor != null`, the top item is a full-width button "Load earlier messages", upper-case mono and at least 48 dp tall. While loading it shows a small progress indicator and "Loading…", and it is disabled. Test tag `room.loadEarlier`.
- **Empty.** When there are no messages and no pending sends: "No messages yet — say hello." in display type, centered.
- **Day headers.** Each `groupByDay` group starts with its header, centered, tertiary display subhead, marked as a heading in semantics.
- **Messages.** Then the message bubbles (7.5.7), then the pending sends (7.5.6), oldest first.
- **Scrolling.** The thread opens scrolled to the bottom and stays pinned to the bottom when the IME opens (iOS `.defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom)`). It animates to the bottom on first load, when the **newest message id** changes (a new message or my own send landed), and when the pending count grows. It does **not** scroll after `loadOlder()`: the first visible item stays where it is (with `reverseLayout = true`, prepending older items at the far end of the list keeps the position). Compose UI test: after "Load earlier messages", the previously first message is still visible. *(iOS gap)* `RoomView.swift` scrolls on every `session.messages.count` change, which also fires after `loadOlder()` and throws the user back to the bottom; listed in §12 for back-port. Scrolling dismisses the IME. *Android note:* iOS uses a non-lazy `VStack` because lazy rows with a bottom anchor opened blank. On Android, use `LazyColumn` with `reverseLayout = true`, or `scrollToItem(last)` after the first layout, and test that the first frame is not blank.

**Lifecycle** (`RoomSession`).
- **Activate**, on screen start and on every return to the foreground:
  - If there is no header yet, load the first page; otherwise refresh the latest page.
  - Then, for athlete rooms with an empty plan list, fetch active plans.
  - Then subscribe to the room's realtime channel.
- **Deactivate**, on stop or background: cancel the subscription and pause playback.
- Use `repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED)` in the ViewModel's collector.
- **Push permission in context.** The first room a signed-in user opens triggers the notification-permission request on Android 13+ (`POST_NOTIFICATIONS`). This mirrors `PushPermission.requestIfNeeded()` on `RoomView` (iOS §6.6: "first message thread opened … not at first launch"). iOS asks only while the status is `.notDetermined`; Android has no such state, and the system dialog may appear twice before a denial becomes permanent. So:
  - Persist `push.permissionRequested` (Boolean) in DataStore, per install (the one flag §6.6.5 and §7.12 Device also read).
  - On a room open: if API ≥ 33, the permission is not granted and the flag is false → create the Messages channel (7.5.10) first, set the flag, then launch the `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` request.
  - Never re-prompt automatically after that, even though Android would allow a second dialog (parity: iOS asks once). The user can turn notifications on from Settings → Device (§7.12) or Android Settings.
  - On every app launch and on each room open where `NotificationManagerCompat.areNotificationsEnabled()` is true, fetch the FCM token and register it with `POST /devices` when it differs from the last registered token. This mirrors iOS calling `registerForRemoteNotifications` on every "yes" (`PushPermission.swift`, `AppDelegate.swift` line 23). On Android 10–12 there is no runtime prompt; just register.
- **Leaving.** When the room screen leaves composition, refresh the app-wide unread total (`RoleTabsView` `.onDisappear { refreshUnread() }`).
- **Outbox drained.** When the outbox for this user shrinks (a queued send landed), call `refreshLatest()` (`RoomView` `onChange(of: mutations.count)`).

**Paging and merging.**
- `loadOlder()` fetches the page at `nextCursor` and prepends only the ids it does not already have. It then updates `nextCursor` and, if anything was added, announces "Earlier messages loaded". With no cursor, or while a load is already running, it is a no-op. A cancellation is silent. Other errors show as a snackbar.
- `refreshLatest()` fetches the newest page and merges it:
  - Existing ids are replaced, which refreshes read marks.
  - New ids are added.
  - Already-loaded older pages are kept.
  - The result is sorted by (`createdAt`, `id`).
  - `nextCursor` is updated only when the merged list is no larger than the page.
  - Errors are swallowed, so the screen keeps what it shows.
  - Except on the very first load, count the new messages that are not mine. One announces "New message"; more than one announces "N new messages". My own sends never announce.

**Announcements.** iOS posts `AccessibilityNotification.Announcement`. On Android, `View.announceForAccessibility` is deprecated as of API 36 ([API diff](https://developer.android.com/sdk/api_diff/36/changes/android.view.View)). Use a visually hidden `Text` with `semantics { liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite }`, driven by a sequence number, so that repeated identical text still re-announces.

**Mark read** (`markReadIfNeeded`). After the first load and after every refresh: if any message is not mine, not from a deleted sender, and not in `readBy` for me, and the message count differs from the count last marked, call `POST /rooms/{id}/read` once. Errors are ignored. After a successful mark, cancel this room's notifications (7.5.10).

**Paused by parent** (§6.13 C, S2). When `messagingPausedByParent == true`, the composer is replaced by a notice bar: a pause-circle icon and the text for the viewer's seat (`RoomHeader.pausedMessage`). Test tag `room.pausedByParent`.
- Parent: "You've paused messaging between this coach and your athlete. Resume it from Settings → My athletes."
- Coach: "This athlete's parent has paused messaging for now. You'll be able to write again when they resume it."
- Athlete: "Messaging with this coach is paused by your parent or guardian for now."

The server refuses sends both ways regardless. When the parent resumes, the composer is back on the next open or refresh (QA §4 "Parent pause").

**Block confirmation.**
- An M3 `AlertDialog` with title "Block {first}?" and text "Messaging stops both ways and any coaching connection between you is removed. Your history stays. You can unblock from Settings."
- Buttons: "Block {first}" (destructive) and "Cancel". iOS uses `.alert` because the iOS 26 `confirmationDialog` popover drops Cancel; Android has no such problem, and `AlertDialog` is the native match.
- On success: snackbar "{first} is blocked." (success kind). No haptic (`RoomSession.block` only shows the toast). On failure: an error snackbar with the mapped message.
- The room stays open. Server-side, `blockUser` also severs every coaching relationship between the two people (`severRelationships` in `src/lib/safety.server.ts`). Later sends answer `blocked` with "You can't message this person because one of you has blocked the other."

**7.5.6 Composer and sending**

The composer is pinned above the IME and the navigation bar with `Modifier.imePadding().navigationBarsPadding()` under edge-to-edge. Its background is the translucent surface with a top divider (§8). Tapping send, mic or the plan tag **keeps the IME up** (iOS `keepsKeyboardOnTap`): these buttons must not clear focus from the text field.

**State ownership.** The recorder, the draft text and the attached plan live in `RoomViewModel`, so they survive configuration changes (rotation, dark-mode switch, font scale). Never hold `MediaRecorder` in a composable's `remember`. When the user leaves the room (the ViewModel's `onCleared`, or the room destination is popped): if recording, stop and delete the file; if a finished recording was not sent, delete the file; return to Idle. The draft text and the plan tag are lost when the room is left, as on iOS (`VoiceRecorder` is `@State` in `Composer.swift`, the draft is in-memory on `RoomSession`). They are not persisted across process death.

**Layout, top to bottom.**
0. **Reply row**, while replying (A53; iOS `Composer.swift`): a reply-arrow icon, then on one line the quoted sender's first name in bold (the role word when the first name is empty), two spaces, and the message body (or "Voice note"), truncated. At the end, an ✕ button with TalkBack label "Cancel reply" clears it. A `card` capsule, one line in caption `textSecondary` with the name in bold (§8.6.8). The whole row reads "Replying to {first}". Reply state lives in `RoomViewModel` with the draft.
1. **Plan tag row**, when a plan is attached: a list-clipboard icon, "Tagged to **{title}**" (up to 2 lines), and an ✕ button (TalkBack "Remove plan tag"). Pill with an accent wash.
2. **Error line**, when `sendError != null`: the last refusal or error text (the `ErrorLine` component, §8). A snackbar with the same text is suppressed while the line is visible (iOS #114 dedupe; §7.13).
3. **Recorder area**, which depends on the recorder state:
   - Idle: the input row.
   - Recording: the recording bar.
   - Finished: the review bar.
   - Denied: the line "Microphone access is off. Allow it in Android Settings to record." with an "OK" text button that resets to idle. "iOS Settings" becomes "Android Settings"; that is a platform-native wording change only.

**Input row.**
- **Plan tag button** (paperclip), only when the room kind is `athlete` (`canTagPlan`).
  - If a plan is attached, tapping removes it. If there is one active plan, it attaches that plan. If there are none, it shows the snackbar "This athlete has no active plan to tag.". Otherwise it opens a picker titled "Tag a plan" listing the plan titles, plus "Cancel" (M3 `AlertDialog` with a list).
  - TalkBack: "Tag a plan" or "Remove plan tag". The button is visually highlighted while a plan is attached.
  - *Parity note:* the server also accepts `planId` in coach↔coach rooms, but iOS offers tagging only in athlete rooms. Android does the same.
- **Text field.**
  - The field's edge is `Modifier.editingEdge(focused, corner = 18.dp)` (§8.6.5): a crisp `textSecondary` line at rest and the EditingOutline while typing. It replaced the accent 2 dp focus border in `ad1e9bf`.
  - Placeholder "Message…", 1–5 lines growing, multi-line. Return inserts a newline (`ImeAction.Default`), as iOS `.submitLabel(.return)` with a vertical axis does.
  - TalkBack label "Message". When `viewerTextOnly`, append "Voice notes are off for athletes under 18. Type your message." This is the TalkBack equivalent of the iOS accessibility hint (#32; QA §4).
  - Test tag `room.composer`.
- **Trailing button.**
  - Draft not blank after trimming: a Send disc (up arrow), TalkBack "Send", test tag `room.send`.
  - Draft blank and **not** text-only: a mic disc, TalkBack "Record a voice note", test tag `room.record`.
  - Draft blank and text-only: nothing.

**Sending text** (`sendDraft`).
1. Trim the draft. If empty, do nothing.
2. Capture the attached plan, then clear the draft and the plan.
3. Capture and clear the reply too, then call `send(.text(body, planId, replyToId))`. The body carries `"replyToId"` only when set.
4. If the send ended with an error that was not queued (`sendError != null`) and the field is still empty, **put the words, the plan tag and the reply back** (QA: "a refused send keeps the words in the composer").

**`send(message)`.** Online first, then the outbox with the same key (`RoomSession.send`; gradus-ios `docs/README.md` "Messaging (I3)").
1. Clear `sendError`. Generate `key = UUID`. Add an in-flight pending item: preview, kind, `createdAt = now`, state Sending.
2. **Offline** (the connectivity monitor reports no default network with `NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET`, §7.13.4): enqueue in the outbox (below) and stop.
3. Otherwise POST with header `Idempotency-Key: key`, through the raw transport so the `{ok:false}` body reaches the composer:
   - `{ok:true, id}` → `refreshLatest()`.
   - `{ok:false, message}` → `sendError = message` plus an error snackbar. **Not queued.** With no `message`, the text is "This message couldn't be sent." An unknown `reason` takes the same path. `{ok:true}` **without** an `id` is also treated as a refusal with that text (`LiveMessagesRepository.send`, `MessagesRepository.swift` line 110). Unit tests cover both cases.
   - Transport failure, or HTTP status 0 or ≥ 500 → enqueue in the outbox **with the same key**.
   - Any other non-2xx (4xx, including 429 and validation) → the response's API error, or a generic HTTP error for the status when the body has none (`response.apiError ?? APIError.http(status)`); `sendError` = its user message plus a snackbar. Not queued. An unreadable body maps to "The send response could not be read." with code `malformed_response`.
4. Remove the in-flight item.

**Enqueue.**
- Outbox row:
  - `method POST`
  - `path = messagesPath(roomId)`
  - `body` = the JSON above, with sorted keys
  - `idempotencyKey = key`
  - `entityKind "message"`, `entityId = roomId`
  - `entityLabel = preview`
- On success: snackbar "Saved — it will send when you're back online."
- If the outbox is unavailable: `sendError` "You're offline. Try again when you're back online."
- If saving fails: "Couldn't save the message."

The outbox and its drain policy (WorkManager, backoff 2 s base, 300 s max, 12 attempts, ±25 % jitter; 409/422 parked as conflicted, other 4xx parked as failed, 429 and 5xx retried; `SyncEngine.swift`) are specified in §6.5. Messages use them unchanged.

**Pending sends in the thread** (`pendingSends`). These are the outbox rows for this user whose `path == messagesPath(roomId)` and `method == POST`, plus the in-flight items, sorted by `createdAt`.
- Kind: voice when the label starts with "Voice note", text otherwise.
- State: Queued, or Failed (with the row's last error message, default "Couldn't send.") when the row needs attention (failed or conflicted).
- **Pending bubble** (`PendingBubble`): right-aligned, the accent bubble at 55 % opacity, the preview (with a mic icon for voice). Under it, an upper-case mono status line:
  - Sending: tiny spinner and "Sending…".
  - Queued: clock icon and "Waiting for a connection".
  - Failed: error icon, the reason (up to 2 lines, destructive ink), then "Retry" and "Delete" text buttons, each with a touch target of at least 48 dp.
  - TalkBack custom actions: "Retry" and "Delete" (failed only). Test tag `room.pending.<key>`.
- **Retry:** re-arm the outbox row, then `refreshLatest()`.
- **Delete:** an `AlertDialog` titled "Delete this unsent message?" with text "It has not reached anyone yet and cannot be recovered." and buttons "Delete" (destructive) and "Keep it". It then discards the row.
- There is no Sync Center screen (§6.5, §12 N21): the thread is the only place these rows appear.

> **(iOS gap) A queued send the server refuses.** When the outbox later replays a message and the server answers 200 `{ok:false, reason}` (for example the person was blocked, or the parent paused the room while the phone was offline), the iOS `SyncEngine` treats any 2xx as delivered (`SyncEngine.swift`, `case 200 ..< 300: store.complete`). The message then silently disappears. **1.0 behavior = iOS:** every 2xx completes the row. **Proposed (needs Mariah; back-port to iOS), listed in §12:** the message drain step reads the body of a `/rooms/{id}/messages` 2xx response, and `{ok:false}` parks the row as `failed` with the server's `message`, shown as a failed pending bubble with Retry/Delete. Until approved, Android does not implement it.

**7.5.7 Message bubbles**

`MessageBubble`. Mine means `isMine(myUserId)`. Mine are trailing-aligned with an accent fill and accent-foreground text. Others are leading-aligned on the card surface. Corner radii are 18 dp, with the tail corner at 6 dp (bottom-trailing for mine, bottom-leading for others). There is a soft shadow, and the bubble is at most 300 dp wide.

- **Sender label** (others only): `senderLabel`, upper-case mono caption, tertiary, **shown once per run**. It is omitted when the previous message in the same day group is from the same sender (`showsSender`, `RoomView.swift`).
- **Quote line**, when `replyTo` is set (A53; look in §8.6.8 item 7): a 2 dp `textTertiary` bar, then on one line, caption size, `textSecondary`: the bold `senderLabel` (`"{Role} (deleted account)"` for a deleted sender, else the first name, else the role word), two spaces, and `displayText` ("Message removed" for a deleted sender, "Voice note" for voice, else the excerpt of up to 140 characters). It is aligned to the bubble's side, at most 260 dp wide, and hidden from TalkBack (the bubble label and actions carry it; test tag `room.quote.{id}`). **Tapping it jumps to the original** (`72739e0`):
  - page back with `loadOlder` quietly (no "Earlier messages loaded" announcement), up to **20 pages**, until the id is loaded. If it is not found, or a page fails, show the snackbar "That message is too far back to show here.";
  - otherwise, after the next layout, `animateScrollToItem` with the item centered (no animation when animations are off);
  - move TalkBack focus to the bubble (`FocusRequester` on the bubble's focusable node, verify that TalkBack follows it on the Pixel);
  - ring it with a 2 dp `accentInk` border inset −4 dp for 1.6 s, fading out over 0.4 s (no fade when animations are off).
  The jump never pulls the thread back to the bottom (the thread follows the newest message id, 7.5.5).
- **Reactions pill** (§8.6.8 item 6), when `reactions` is non-empty: a capsule on the `elevated` surface with a `divider` border, 13 sp, over the bubble's top corner (top-end for others, top-start for mine, offset 12 dp in and 14 dp up; the bubble gets 12 dp of top padding). It shows each emoji once, in first-seen order, with a count when more than one person chose it ("❤️ 2 👏"; `MessageReaction.tally`). Hidden from TalkBack.
- **Plan chip**, when the message has a plan: a capsule with a list-clipboard icon and the plan title (up to 2 lines), TalkBack "Tagged plan {title}". Where the tap goes:
  - A **coach** viewing a plan whose `coachId` differs from `header.myCoachId` (both non-null; `isOtherCoachPlan`) → the other-coach plan sheet (7.5.11).
  - Otherwise → the app's plan route `plans/{id}`. A coach gets the plan editor. A parent or athlete gets the runner plan detail.
  - When neither applies, the chip is disabled.
- **Body.**
  - Sender deleted: italic "Message deleted".
  - Voice: the voice bubble (7.5.8).
  - Text: the body, in body type.
- **Footer:** the local time, upper-case mono caption. When the message is mine and `readBy` contains anyone other than me, **a small pen check** follows the time (`PenMarkView(Check)`, 12 dp, `textTertiary`, seed 13, line 1.6; hidden from TalkBack, which hears ", seen" in the bubble label). There is no "Seen" word any more (`ad1e9bf`).
- **Long-press menu** (the Android equivalent of the iOS `contextMenu`; a `DropdownMenu` anchored to the bubble, with a long-press haptic). M3 `DropdownMenu` has no submenus, so iOS's "React ›" submenu becomes the first row of the menu: the five emoji 👍 ❤️ 😂 🔥 👏 as 48 dp buttons, the viewer's own one marked with a check badge and selected state (A60). Then, in iOS order:
  - "Reply" (reply-arrow icon), when the sender is not deleted and the room is not paused by a parent. It sets the composer's reply and focuses the field.
  - The emoji row (same conditions as Reply). Choosing the viewer's own emoji clears it; choosing another swaps it.
  - "Report this message" (flag icon), when the message is not mine, the sender is not deleted, and `senderUserId != null`. It opens the report sheet (7.5.11) with `messageId` set and the name = `senderFirstName`, or the role word when the first name is empty.
  - "Copy", when the kind is text and the body is not empty. It copies to the `ClipboardManager`. On Android 13+ the system shows its own clipboard confirmation. iOS shows no confirmation, so 1.0 adds no snackbar on any version. **Proposed (needs Mariah), §12:** a "Copied" snackbar on Android 10–12 only.
  - iOS also enables system text selection inside bubbles. On Android, long-press is taken by the menu, so selection is covered by Copy. Do not wrap bubbles in `SelectionContainer`.
- **TalkBack.**
  - The bubble is one merged node: "{You | senderLabel}[, replying to {quoted senderLabel or role word}: {displayText}]: {what}. {time}[, seen][, tagged to {title}][, reactions {tally text}]". *What* is "message deleted", the `voiceNoteDescription`, or the body.
  - Reply and reaction custom actions (A53): "Go to quoted message" (when a quote exists), "Reply", and per emoji "React {emoji}", or "Remove reaction {emoji}" for the viewer's own. Reply and the reactions are absent while a parent has paused the room, and for a deleted sender.
  - Controls are custom actions (iOS Actions rotor): "Play voice note" / "Pause voice note" (voice with a URL, sender not deleted), "Open tagged plan {title}" (when the chip opens), and "Copy" (text).
  - "Report this message" is also a custom action whenever the long-press menu would offer it. TalkBack's long-press is not discoverable enough on its own (Android-native requirement).

**7.5.8 Voice notes: record, upload, play, transcripts**

**Who may record (#32, #48, §6.13 A7).**
- The mic exists only when `header.viewerTextOnly != true`. The server gates the same thing three times: the voice-notes bucket policy refuses a minor's upload, `sendMessage` answers `text_only` "Athletes under 18 send text messages only." for any login with an athlete row under 18 or without a birthdate, and minors' notes are never transcribed (`NEVER_TRANSCRIBE`).
- The client must **hide the mic before any upload is attempted** (S2 handoff) and must **never request `RECORD_AUDIO`** for a text-only viewer.
- A coach or parent in the same room still sees the mic (QA §4).
- Messaging keys only off `viewerTextOnly`, not `GET /me` `athleteVoiceToPlan`, which governs plan voice (§7.8 / §6.14).
- **Edge case: a login with a minor athlete row acting as coach or parent.** The server sets `viewerTextOnly` only when the viewer's role **in that room** is athlete and the athlete is a minor (`messages.server.ts` ~line 776), but refuses voice from **any** login with an athlete row under 18 or without a birthdate, in any room and any role (~lines 1065–1068). Such a user sees the mic in a coach↔coach or coach↔parent room. The upload is refused by the bucket policy, the inline fallback send answers `{ok:false, reason:"text_only"}`, and the composer error line shows the server's message. The client adds no age logic (#31, #32: the server decides). Unit test: the inline fallback answered `text_only` → `sendError` = the server message, the temp file deleted.

**Recorder** (port of `VoiceRecorder`; shared with plan voice capture in §7.4 and §7.8, where the caller passes a lower cap such as 90 s).
- **Permission.** `RECORD_AUDIO`, requested at the first mic tap (in context, never at launch).
  - Denied → Denied state (copy above).
  - Android may allow asking again after a first denial; a later mic tap asks again while `shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale` allows. After a permanent denial, the Denied state is shown again.
- **Encoder.**
  - `MediaRecorder` with `AudioSource.VOICE_RECOGNITION` (falling back to `MIC` if it throws; the shared recorder of §6.7.2), `OutputFormat.MPEG_4`, `AudioEncoder.AAC`, `setAudioSamplingRate(24_000)`, `setAudioChannels(1)`, `setAudioEncodingBitRate(32_000)`.
  - Output file `cacheDir/voice-<uuid>.m4a`.
  - Use `MediaRecorder(context)` on API 31+ and the no-argument constructor on 29–30.
  - This is iOS's `kAudioFormatMPEG4AAC`, 24 kHz, mono, 32 kbps, so a 90 s note is under 400 KB (iOS §6.7).
- **Start.** `start()` is a no-op while already recording; also guard the mic disc against a double tap (debounce or disable until the state changes). If `prepare()` or `start()` throws (for example another app holds the microphone), release the recorder, delete the file and go **silently** to Idle, with no message (parity: `VoiceRecorder.start()` `catch { state = .idle }`).
- **Audio focus.** Request `AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN_TRANSIENT_EXCLUSIVE` while recording, and abandon it on stop. Set a shared app-wide `AudioActivity.isRecording` flag so read-aloud TTS stays quiet while recording (`Audio.swift` `AudioActivity.shared.isRecording`; §6.7).
- **Timing and level.**
  - A 100 ms ticker updates `elapsed` (from a monotonic start time) and `level`. iOS maps `averagePower` (dBFS) logarithmically: `level = max(0, power + 60) / 60` (`Audio.swift`). Android: `db = 20 * log10(max(1, maxAmplitude) / 32767.0)`; `level = ((db + 60) / 60).coerceIn(0.0, 1.0)`. (A linear `maxAmplitude / 32767` stays near 0 for speech; do not use it.)
  - Auto-stop at `maxSeconds` (180 for messages, the server's cap).
  - `seconds = max(1, round(elapsed))`.
- **Stop:** state Finished (file, seconds). **Cancel:** stop, delete the file (including after an auto-stop), go to Idle. **Reset:** delete the finished file and go to Idle. **Discard state:** go to Idle after the caller has taken the file.
- **Backgrounding (Android-specific).** On every supported version (API 29+; the rule dates from Android 9), an app in the background receives silence from the microphone. Android 11+ also blocks starting a microphone foreground service from the background, and messaging runs no foreground service. Therefore on `ON_STOP` while recording: **stop and move to Finished**, so the user can review or discard on return. Do not start a foreground service. (iOS has no equivalent rule; this is the closest native behavior. See 7.5.16 M11.)

**Recording bar.**
- A 10 dp attention dot with `alpha = if (animationsOff) 1f else 0.6f + 0.4f * level` (`Composer.swift`: `reduceMotion ? 1 : 0.6 + 0.4 * level`). `animationsOff` = `Settings.Global.ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE == 0`, the Android equivalent of Reduce Motion.
- "Recording · m:ss", bold with tabular digits.
- A trash button (TalkBack "Discard recording") and a 48 dp stop disc (TalkBack "Stop recording").
- Capsule on an attention wash. The TalkBack node reads "Recording, N seconds".

**Review bar.** A waveform icon, "Voice note · m:ss", a "Discard" text button (TalkBack "Discard voice note"), and a "Send" pill with an up arrow (TalkBack "Send voice note", test tag `room.sendVoice`). Send discards the recorder state, then calls `sendVoiceNote(file, seconds)`.

**`sendVoiceNote`** (needs a connection; voice notes are **not queued offline**).
- *(code wins: iOS PRD §6.5 lists voice notes under "works with queueing", but HEAD requires a connection and gradus-ios `docs/README.md` says "They need a connection; text queues offline.")*
1. Read the file. On failure: `sendError` "Couldn't read the recording." plus a snackbar.
2. Offline → `sendError` "Voice notes need a connection. Try again when you're back online." plus a snackbar.
3. Upload to bucket `voice-notes` at path `"<roomId>/<myUserId>/<uuid lowercase>.m4a"`, content type `audio/mp4`, `upsert = false`, bearer = the current access token (one client per upload so the token is fresh).
   - Success → clear the plan tag and the reply, await the on-device transcript started before the upload (§6.7.6), then `send(.voice(audioPath, "audio/mp4", seconds, planId, replyToId, transcript))`. The body always carries `"transcript"` (a string or `null`).
   - Any `IOException` from the Storage upload (supabase-kt `HttpRequestException` and other network errors, **including timeouts and DNS failures**) → the same "Voice notes need a connection…" message. No inline retry. (iOS maps every `URLError` to `APIError.offline`, `VoiceNoteStorage.swift`.)
   - Any HTTP error response from Storage (supabase-kt `RestException`, including the RLS refusal: the bucket policy admits only athlete-room participants, so direct rooms are refused today), or no access token (iOS throws 401 `unauthenticated`) → clear the plan tag and the reply, and `send(.voiceInline(base64, "audio/mp4", seconds, planId, replyToId, transcript))`. The server stores it, as for the web.
4. **Always** delete the temp file, on every path.

The review bar resets to Idle immediately on Send. **No pending bubble is shown while the upload runs**: the in-flight item is added only by `send()`, after the upload (parity). An "Uploading…" bubble is a §12 proposal, not 1.0.

If `send` falls back to the outbox for an inline note (transport failure or 5xx), the queued row carries the base64 audio, up to about 8 MB. That is accepted parity.

**Playback** (port of `AudioPlayer`; one note at a time per room screen).
- Media3 `ExoPlayer` with `AudioAttributes(USAGE_MEDIA, AUDIO_CONTENT_TYPE_SPEECH)` and `handleAudioFocus = true`. The player is released when the room screen leaves.
- `toggle(url)`: if this URL is playing, stop it; else play it, which stops any other note.
- **Pause = stop.** iOS `AudioPlayer.pause()` drops the player (`player = nil`, `playingURL = nil`), so the next Play starts from 0:00. Android: `stop()` + `clearMediaItems()`; the next Play sets the item again and starts at 0:00. No scrubber, no elapsed-time display, no seek, no playback speed. Only the disc and the static duration from `durationSeconds` are shown.
- On end of playback, stop (as above) and return to the play icon. Stop on leaving the room or going to the background.
- **Failure detection.** iOS flags `playbackFailed` when the item fails within about 5 s. Android: `Player.Listener.onPlayerError` → failure flag + stop.
- `audioUrl` is a server-signed URL that is **valid for 1 hour** (`signAudio`, `createSignedUrl(path, 3600)`). Do not cache audio to disk (iOS streams via AVPlayer; the same here).
- **Expired URL.** 1.0 behavior = iOS: an expired URL fails like any other error and shows the failure line; the next `refreshLatest()` (foreground, realtime) re-signs it. **Proposed (needs Mariah; back-port to iOS), §12:** on an HTTP 400/403 from storage, call `refreshLatest()` and retry once before showing the failure line.

**Legacy WebM (closes iOS §11 risk 6 and §12 #6 for Android).**
- Web-recorded notes are WebM/Opus. iOS cannot decode them ("Can't play this note here yet"). The hidden-`WKWebView` fallback in iOS PRD §6.7 item 2 was never built.
- Media3 plays WebM progressively ([supported formats](https://developer.android.com/media/media3/exoplayer/supported-formats)), and Android has a platform Opus decoder on every supported API level (minSdk 29). So Android plays legacy notes natively and **needs no WebView or bundled Opus decoder** (verify on the Pixel with a real web-recorded note, including one with no duration header as Chrome's `MediaRecorder` writes them, so seeking may be unavailable).
- Treat `.webm`, `.ogg`, `.mp4` and `.m4a` alike.

**Voice bubble** (`VoiceBubble`).
- **With a URL:**
  - A 34 dp play/pause disc (48 dp touch target; TalkBack "Play voice note" / "Pause voice note").
  - The duration "m:ss" in mono with tabular digits.
  - On a real playback failure, the italic caption "Can't play this note here yet" (iOS copy kept). On Android it should appear only for genuine errors, not for every WebM note.
- **Without a URL:** italic "Voice note unavailable".
- **Transcript, under the controls:**
  - With a transcript: the full text, no line limit, test tag `room.voiceNote.transcript`.
  - With a URL and no transcript yet: italic caption "Transcript coming" at 80 % opacity, **only while one can still arrive**: when `createdAt` is under 15 minutes old, or unparseable (iOS `VoiceBubble.transcriptMayArrive`, #134). After that the caption is gone and nothing replaces it. A note whose sender's device got no words, a sender without AI permission, an athlete under 18, and a failed transcription never get a transcript.
- Transcripts come from the sender's device (phone notes, A55, §6.7.6) or the server (web-recorded notes and older builds; ElevenLabs, iOS §6.7 item 3). They are the WCAG 1.2.1 text alternative. Android sends its own only on API 33+ (§12 N79).

**7.5.8a Reactions: write path** (A53; iOS `RoomSession.react`, `LiveMessagesRepository.setReaction`)
- One reaction per person per message. `next = (mine == emoji) ? null : emoji`. Apply it to the message optimistically (drop my entry, then append `{userId: me, emoji: next}` when non-null).
- Send `PUT /api/v1/messages/{id}/reaction` with body `{"emoji": "<emoji>"}` or `{"emoji": null}` and a fresh `Idempotency-Key`, through the raw transport (a PUT, so a retry lands the same way). **Online only, no outbox.**
- 2xx `{ok: true, reactions}` → replace the message's reactions with the server's list.
- `{ok: false, reason, message}` → restore the previous list and show an error snackbar with `message`, default "This reaction couldn't be saved.".
- Non-2xx or transport failure → restore and show an error snackbar with `ApiError.userMessage`, default "Couldn't save your reaction.".
- An undecodable 2xx → restore and "The reaction response could not be read." (`malformed_response`).
- No push and no unread for a reaction.
- Tests (port `MessagingTests` reactions/replies): optimistic set, swap and clear; restore on refusal and on failure; a refused send restores the reply; `replyToId` on text and both voice bodies; the tally order and counts; the TalkBack label with a reply and reactions; quote jump pages back until found, stops at 20 pages with the snackbar, and does not announce "Earlier messages loaded"; Reply and React are hidden while paused by a parent.

**7.5.9 Realtime channel strategy**

This is a port of `SupabaseMessagesRealtime`, using supabase-kt Realtime only (iOS §6.3). Realtime is a **refresh signal, never a data source**: every event triggers a refetch through the API (iOS §6.6: "a refinement over push and polling, not a dependency").

| Subscriber | Topic | Filter | On insert |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open room, reactions (A53) | `reactions:<roomId>` (its own channel, so a server without `message_reactions` cannot break new-message updates) | `postgres_changes` INSERT **and** UPDATE, schema `public`, table `message_reactions`, the same `eq(room_id | direct_room_id, id)` filter (clearing is an UPDATE to null, never a DELETE) | `refreshLatest()` |
| Open room | `room:<roomId>` (the web's channel name) | `postgres_changes` INSERT, schema `public`, table `messages`, `eq(room_id, id)` for `kind == athlete`, `eq(direct_room_id, id)` for direct rooms (`RoomKind.realtimeColumn`) | `refreshLatest()` |
| Rooms list | `rooms:<random uuid>` | INSERT on `public.messages`, no filter (RLS scopes it to the user's rooms) | `load()` with ETag |
| App-wide unread badge (signed in, foreground) | `rooms:<random uuid>` | Same | `refreshUnread()` |

- **Auth.** The Realtime client sends the publishable key as `apikey` and the current access token from the session store (supabase-kt `accessToken` provider). It connects on the first subscribe and disconnects when the last channel is removed.
- **Lifecycle.** Subscriptions are lifecycle-scoped (`STARTED`). Cancelling the collector removes the channel. On returning to the foreground, each screen refetches first and then resubscribes, which covers anything missed while the channel was down.
- **Testability.** Abstract behind `MessagesRealtime { fun inserts(column: String?, value: String?): Flow<MessageInsert> }` with `Noop` and `Scripted` fakes, as on iOS (`Realtime.swift`). Tests drive refreshes through the scripted fake.
- **Insert payload.** `MessageInsert{id, roomId?, directRoomId?, senderUserId?}`. `conversationId = roomId ?: directRoomId`.

**7.5.10 Push, routing and the unread badge**

- **Server.** A new message notifies the other participants plus the athlete's household (co-guardians), and skips anyone who blocked the sender (`withoutBlocked`).
  - Title: "Coach {first}" when the sender is a coach, else the sender's full name, else "New message".
  - Body: the text, or "Sent a voice note", collapsed to one line and truncated to 160 characters with "…" (`truncateBody`, `BODY_LIMIT = 160`). The Android FCM sender reuses `truncateBody` and the same title chain.
  - Route: `rooms/<roomId>`. Thread: `room:<roomId>`.
  - No badge and no unread total in the payload: the APNs `aps` has only `alert`, `sound` and `thread-id` (`pushPayload`), and the message notify call passes `{type, route, title, body, threadId}` (`messages.server.ts` ~lines 1167–1178).
- **Android server work.** Today `notifyUsers` sends to `platform = 'ios'` only (`src/lib/push-notify.server.ts`), although `device_tokens.platform` already accepts `android` and `POST /devices` takes `{token, platform:"android"}`. The FCM sender is specified in §6.6 and Appendix A.
- **FCM message type.** Message pushes are FCM **data-only** messages with `priority: high`, data keys `{type:"message", route:"rooms/<id>", v:"1", title, body, threadId:"room:<id>", category:"GRADUS_MESSAGE", uid:"<recipient user id>"}` (the flat keys of §6.6.2, A40). No `notification` block: with one, the system tray posts it itself while the app is in the background, ignores the app's tag/group/style, and delivers the extras only to the launcher activity. `FirebaseMessagingService.onMessageReceived` therefore **always** builds and posts the notification, in the foreground and in the background. Android may deprioritize high-priority data messages that do not result in a notification, so it always posts one (cross-reference §6.6, Appendix A).
- **Version check.** Ignore a payload when `v != "1"`: post nothing routable, and a tap opens the app home (`RouteParser.route(fromPushUserInfo:)` returns nil unless `gradus.v == 1`, `AppRoute.swift`).
- **Channel.** The `messages` channel, "Messages" (importance high, sound default, §6.6.4), created before the permission request (7.5.5).
- **Notification.** Use `NotificationCompat.MessagingStyle` (the `Person` is the push `title`; each new message for a room is appended to that room's existing style) posted with `tag = "room:<roomId>"` and `setGroup("room:<roomId>")`. This is the Android-native equivalent of APNs `thread-id` grouping. Do **not** publish conversation shortcuts and do **not** enable Bubbles in 1.0: iOS does not use Communication Notifications, so these have no iOS equivalent.
- **Foreground.** iOS shows banners even while the app is open (`willPresent` → `[.banner, .badge, .sound]`), so Android posts the notification in the foreground too (FCM does not do this by itself in the foreground). See 7.5.16 M10 for suppressing it while the same room is open.
- **Tap.**
  - The content `PendingIntent` carries the route. The shell parses it with the shared route parser (`AppRoute.route(fromPath:)`: `rooms/<id>` → room).
  - Selects the Messages tab and pushes the room. This works from a killed process (QA §8 "tapping while the app is killed opens the target").
  - Signed out: the route waits as the pending route until sign-in.
  - A room the user does not belong to shows "Conversation not found".
- **App Links and paths** (`AppRoute.swift`), parsed identically:
  - `/rooms` → Messages tab.
  - `/rooms/<id>` → room.
  - `/coach/messages[/<id>]`, `/parent/messages[/<id>]`, `/athlete/messages[/<id>]` → the same.
  - The custom scheme `gradus://rooms` and `gradus://rooms/<id>` routes the same way (`AppRoute.customScheme = "gradus"`); the app declares an intent filter for scheme `gradus` (§6.10).
  - Excluded paths (`/privacy`, `/terms`, `/api`, and the rest of the excluded prefixes in `AppRoute.swift`, §6.10) never route to Messages.
  - Host verification is §6.10.
- **Reply, and nothing else** (#54). A text Reply on Android 12+ while the in-app lock is off, sent without opening the app (§6.6.11). No Mark as read: iOS has none (parity).
- **Unread total.**
  - Refreshed on sign-in, on foreground, on every app-wide realtime insert, and when a room screen closes.
  - Shown on the Messages tab with an M3 `Badge`. Hidden at 0. Above 99 it shows "99+". This is a **platform-native difference**: the cap is the Material 3 badge convention, where iOS's tab `.badge` shows the raw number.
  - Reset to 0 on sign-out.
- **Launcher dot and clearing** (QA §8 "Badge count clears when the rooms are read"). iOS HEAD sets no icon badge number (see 7.5.1). On Android the launcher derives its dot from active notifications, which needs no server change.
  - After a successful mark-read, cancel that room's notifications (`tag "room:<id>"`).
  - When the unread total becomes 0, cancel every Messages-channel notification.
  - Do **not** call `setNumber` in 1.0: the payload carries no unread total. **Open (7.5.16 M7):** add a per-recipient `unreadTotal` to the FCM data (computed like `GET /messages/unread-total`) as an Android server addition in Appendix A, and the matching APNs `badge` for iOS PRD §6.6 parity.
  - Sign-out unregisters the token (`DELETE /devices/{token}`, §6.4), and sign-out or an account switch clears delivered message notifications, as iOS does since #54 (§6.6.6).
- **Wear OS (A3, A51).** Messages are on the watch (#54): a signed-in Wear app shows its own copy of each message notification (tap → the conversation, Reply with the watch's session), and the Messages screens are §7.15.7. When the Wear app is signed out or cannot post, the phone's copy bridges with its Reply (§6.15.8).

**7.5.11 Report, block, blocked people, and safety copy**

**Report sheet** (`ReportSheet`). A `ModalBottomSheet` that opens half-height and expands to full (iOS medium/large detents).
- **Top bar.** Title "Report {name}" for a person, "Report this message" when `messageId` is set. Leading "Cancel". Trailing "Send report", which shows a progress indicator while sending and is disabled then. Test tag `report.submit`.
- **Section "What's wrong".** A single-choice list of the five reasons, default **Harassment or bullying**. The selected row shows a check and its selected state is exposed in semantics. Values (`ReportReason`, web `safety-types.ts`):
  - `harassment` "Harassment or bullying"
  - `inappropriate` "Inappropriate or sexual content"
  - `spam` "Spam or scam"
  - `minor_safety` "Safety concern about a minor"
  - `other` "Something else"
- **Section "Note (optional)".** A multi-line field (2–6 lines) with placeholder "Anything else we should know?". It is trimmed before sending. The server caps it at 2000 characters (`safety-types.ts` `note: z.string().trim().max(2000)`). No client counter or limit (parity); a 400 shows the server message in an error snackbar and the sheet stays open.
- **While sending,** only "Send report" is disabled (with its progress indicator). "Cancel", swipe-down and predictive back stay enabled (`ReportSheet.swift`).
- **Switch "Also block {name}", default OFF** (opt-in; "blocking is a separate, reviewed choice", audit §5.7; QA §4).
- **Footer:** "Blocking stops messages both ways and removes any coaching connection. Your history stays. Reports go to the Gradus safety team."
- **Submit:** `POST /safety/reports`.
  - Success: dismiss and show the snackbar "Report sent. They're blocked." when the response says `blocked`, otherwise "Report sent. Thank you.".
  - Failure: an error snackbar, and the sheet stays open.
- **Server:** a `minor_safety` report emails admins at once with the subject marked "[URGENT]" (`src/lib/safety.server.ts`; iOS §6.13 "What stays").

**Blocked people** (`BlockedUsersView`). Settings → **Account** section → row "Blocked people" (hand icon, test tag `settings.blocked`), placed after "Account & security" and "Device". It pushes a screen titled "Blocked people".
- **States:**
  - Loading with an empty list: "Loading…".
  - Error with an empty list: a cloud-off icon, the error and "Try again".
  - Empty: "You haven't blocked anyone."
  - Otherwise: one row per person with the name; a caption "{Role capitalized} · blocked {relativeTime} ago" (iOS string, kept verbatim: `BlockedUsersView.swift` line 36); and a trailing "Unblock" text button (TalkBack "Unblock {name}") that shows "…" while working and disables every other Unblock in the meantime.
- **Footer:** "Unblocking lets messages through again but does not restore a coaching connection."
- Pull to refresh.
- **Unblock** calls `DELETE /safety/blocks/{userId}`, removes the row, and gives a success haptic (iOS `Haptics.success()`, `BlockedUsersView.swift` line 85 → `HapticFeedbackConstants.CONFIRM` on API 30+, `performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackConstants.CONTEXT_CLICK)` fallback on API 29; §7.13).
- **Unblock failure.** 1.0 behavior = iOS: the error is stored and shows only when the list is empty; with rows on screen it is silent.
- **Proposed (needs Mariah; back-port to iOS), §12:** (1) caption without the doubled "ago" ("blocked just now ago", "blocked Sep 5 ago" today) → "blocked just now", "blocked 3d ago", "blocked Sep 5"; (2) an error snackbar on unblock failure. Until approved, Android = iOS.

**Other coach's plan sheet** (`OtherCoachPlanSheet`). A full-height `ModalBottomSheet` titled "Coach's plan" with "Done".
- **Loading:** a progress indicator, TalkBack "Loading the plan".
- **403:** a lock-icon state "This plan is locked" with the server's message verbatim (for example "Viewing another coach's plans requires the Club plan, or a connection the parent turns on.").
- **Other errors:** a cloud-off icon, "Couldn't load the plan" and "Try again".
- **Loaded:**
  - Header: eyebrow "Also coaching {athleteFirstName}"; "Coach {full name}" as a heading; the sports joined with " · ".
  - Then one card per plan:
    - The title and a tag, "Active" (tennis pen) or "Benched" (iris pen).
    - The usage line "Updated {relativeDay} · N session(s) in last 30d" ("session" when N is 1). "Updated …" is left out when the date can't be parsed.
    - The notes, if not blank.
    - The eyebrow "{n} move(s)".
    - "No moves in this plan yet." when there are no moves.
    - Each move row: the name, a right-aligned target ("5 min" for `mins`, "8 reps" otherwise; whole numbers without a decimal), then "**Cue:** …", "**How:** …", "**Why:** …", each only if not empty.

**Safety copy and placement** (iOS §6.11 Guideline 1.2 → Google Play UGC policy, §6.11).
- Report and block are one tap away in every room (header overflow) and on every message from someone else (long-press, plus the TalkBack action). The blocked list lives in Settings.
- **Google Play obligations met by this section.** Gradus is a communication app used by 13–17-year-olds. Play's User Generated Content policy requires in-app reporting, blocking, moderation and accepted terms before UGC. This section provides: reporting from every message and every room; blocking; the Gradus safety team's review of reports (urgent email for `minor_safety`); the Safe Sport contact (support@gradussports.com, one-business-day commitment); and terms accepted before messaging (the §7.12 terms gate). Play's **Child Safety Standards** policy (social and communication apps) requires published standards against child sexual abuse and exploitation (CSAE), an in-app feedback mechanism, CSAM handling, and a designated child-safety point of contact, declared in Play Console. Whether it applies to Gradus's category is to be confirmed (verify). If it applies, Appendix D must include the declaration: a published standards URL on gradus.training and the point of contact. The Data safety form declares messages and voice recordings (Appendix D).
- The Safe Sport panel's "Gradus Support" card (§7.9; `SafeSportContent.ReportToGradus`) uses the same text on Android. Its gesture line is already platform-neutral:
  - "Something wrong in a Gradus conversation? Long-press the message and choose Report this message, or email us. Reporting doesn't notify the other person."
  - "Every report reaches our team the moment it's sent, and reports about a minor's safety are flagged urgent. We respond within one business day."
  - "Gradus isn't an emergency or reporting service for abuse. For that, use the hotlines below or call 911."
  - Email: support@gradussports.com, which opens the email app with an `ACTION_SENDTO` `mailto:` intent.
- **Structural guardrail (§6.13 C).** There is never a coach↔athlete direct room. Athlete rooms are three-way by construction, and the only direct rooms are coach↔coach and coach↔parent. Android adds no room kinds; `RoomKind` is exactly `athlete`, `coach_coach`, `coach_parent`.
- **Room rule for minors (#31).** A room with a minor opens, and accepts sends, only with a verified adult who is not the coach as a participant. Provisional 13–17 accounts have no rooms. The client never decides this. It shows the server's `ensureRoom` 403 message or the send's `{ok:false}` message verbatim:
  - `guardian_required` "This athlete's parent or guardian needs to claim and verify their account before messages can start."
  - `provisional` "This athlete's account is waiting on their parent or guardian. Messages open once the parent claims it."
  - `paused` "This athlete's account is paused."
  - `paused_by_parent` "The parent has paused messaging with this coach."
  - `coach_unlinked` "This coach is no longer connected to this athlete. New messages can't be sent."
  - `blocked` "You can't message this person because one of you has blocked the other."
  - `text_only` "Athletes under 18 send text messages only."

  These strings live on the server and are listed here for test fixtures only. Never hard-code them as UI copy.
- **Deleted accounts.** Messages from a deleted account render "Message deleted" with the label "{Role} (deleted account)". They cannot be reported or blocked from the header (no `userId`).

**7.5.12 Offline behavior and cache**

| Situation | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Open the Messages tab offline (fresh launch) | iOS code parity: no cache, so the error card shows (cloud-off icon, "You're offline. …", "Try again"); there is no offline banner (§7.13.4). If the screen already had rooms in memory, they stay and the failed refresh is silent. *If §12 "Messages cache" is approved:* render the cached rooms (Room `rooms_cache`, keyed by user id, with its ETag in the same row) and no error card. |
| Open a room offline | iOS code parity: the room shows the Failed state ("Couldn't load the conversation", the offline message, "Try again"). A room already loaded in memory keeps its thread; "Load earlier" fails with an error snackbar. *If §12 "Messages cache" is approved:* render the cached newest page plus pending sends. |
| Send text offline | Queued in the outbox as "Waiting for a connection". The snackbar says it will send. It survives process death and drains on reconnect (QA §9). |
| Send a voice note offline | Refused with "Voice notes need a connection. Try again when you're back online." The recording is deleted. |
| New conversation offline | Targets fail with the offline message. `ensureRoom` needs a connection (iOS §6.5 table). |
| Report or block offline | Fails with an error snackbar. Never queued (no outbox path in iOS). |
| Sign-out | Wipes in-memory state and the outbox (§6.4). Sign-out with pending sends is **allowed** after the warning "{n} change(s) still waiting to send will be discarded." (code wins over QA §9's "refused", §6.4). |

**No message cache in 1.0 (code wins).** At HEAD the iOS rooms list and threads live in memory only: no SwiftData model holds `RoomSummary` or `Message` (they appear only in `FeatureMessages` and `GradusCore/Messaging`), and `RoomsListModel` and `RoomSession` refetch on every open. That falls short of iOS PRD §6.5 ("Read cached conversations") and QA §9 line 157 ("cached … rooms … render with the offline banner"), but per A2 the code wins. Android keeps rooms and messages in the ViewModels only, and audio is never cached.

**Open decision for Mariah (§12 "Messages cache"):** cache the rooms list and the newest **200** messages per room in Room, per iOS PRD §6.5 and QA §9 line 157; iOS HEAD does not. Back-port to iOS if approved. If approved: refresh on every successful fetch, never serve the cache in place of a fetch, store the rooms ETag in the same transaction, and wipe everything on sign-out.

**7.5.13 Analytics (§6.12)**

The room screen counts as area `messages`, screen `room`. The list counts as the Messages tab. Events carry ids only, never message content. Minor athletes' events carry no user id.

**7.5.14 Module and test plan**

- **Modules.**
  - `:feature:messages`: list, room, composer, sheets.
  - `:core:data` (`messaging` package): models, formatting, repository interfaces, live and preview repositories, `SampleMessaging` fixtures with the invented names Linnea Corwin, Maeve Abbott, Corin Abbott, Leo Marsh, and Jordan Kim. These names are from iOS; they were checked as invented (iOS #26).
  - `:core:data` (`audio` package): recorder and player.
  - `:core:api`: Realtime and Storage adapters (supabase-kt, §6.3).
  - The blocked-people screen sits in `:feature:settings`.
- **Unit tests.** Port every case in `MessagingTests.swift` and `MessagingModelsTests.swift` to JUnit 5, using Turbine for flows and a scripted transport, realtime and voice store.
  - First page oldest-first with title "Maeve & Corin" and subtitle "ATHLETE · PARENT". Paging 20 → 40 → 64 with no duplicates. The "Earlier messages loaded" announcement happens once per added page, and not on an exhausted page. Mark-read is called once.
  - Online send appends after a refresh. A refused send restores the draft. A 429 is not queued. Offline queues with path `/api/v1/rooms/room-leo/messages`, the same idempotency key, and the body `{kind:"text",body,planId}`. Draining uses that key, and the pending item disappears afterwards.
  - A transport failure falls back to the outbox. Delete removes the outbox row.
  - A realtime insert refreshes the thread and keeps older pages (41 messages), announcing "New message". My own send does not announce.
  - Voice uploads to `room-leo/preview-user/*.m4a` with `audio/mp4`, then sends `audioPath`. The temp file is deleted. A refused upload falls back to inline base64. Offline voice is refused with "need a connection" and makes no upload.
  - Report and block go through the safety repository. An unknown room is "missing".
  - Rooms list: honors 304, unread total 3, realtime refetch, the preview strings, and a cancelled refresh is not an error.
  - Targets: group order, search over secondary labels ("leo" → Athletes 1, Coaches 1), segment filter, and `ensureRoom`.
  - Formatting vectors: relative time, spoken relative time, day header, duration, grouping, `relativeDay`, transcript decode and trim, and the voice-note TalkBack text.
  - `isOtherCoachPlan` truth table. Unknown target kinds are dropped.
  - Android additions: decoding of an unknown `reason`; `{ok:false}` with no message → "This message couldn't be sent."; `{ok:true}` with no `id` → refusal; the `text_only` refusal after the inline fallback; a 304 with no list in memory → refetch without `If-None-Match`; recorder `start()` failure → silent Idle with the file deleted; leaving the room deletes an active or finished recording; the level formula vectors (`maxAmplitude` 0 → 0, 32767 → 1, ~1036 (−30 dBFS) → 0.5); push permission asked at most once (DataStore flag); a payload with `v != "1"` routes nowhere; a voice upload `IOException` → offline copy with no inline send, a Storage `RestException` → inline send.
  - Compose UI: after "Load earlier messages", the previously first visible message is still visible (no jump to the bottom); a new incoming message scrolls to the bottom.
  - On-device transcripts (A55): with a fake transcriber the voice send body carries `"transcript": "Bend the knee on the takeoff."`; with no words it carries `"transcript": null` (the key present) for both `voice` and `voiceInline`; an outbox-queued inline note keeps it. Transcription and upload start together, and the file is deleted after both. API 29–32 (Robolectric `@Config(sdk = [29, 32])`) never constructs a `SpeechRecognizer` and sends `null`. API 33+ with `en-US` not installed sends `null` and never calls `triggerModelDownload`. A 60 s timeout sends `null`. The PCM decoder turns a 24 kHz AAC fixture into the right sample count. "Transcript coming" shows for a 14-minute-old note without a transcript and not for a 16-minute-old one. Instrumented on the Pixel (API 36): a 90 s note with pauses comes back as one punctuated transcript, and the microphone privacy indicator never lights during recognition (§12 N80).
- **Compose UI and screenshot tests** (Roborazzi or Paparazzi, light and dark, font scale 1.0 and 2.0):
  - The list in the loading, error, empty-coach, empty-parent and populated states.
  - The room in loading, missing, failed and loaded (64-message sample), plus paused for each seat, text-only (no mic), the recording bar, the review bar, the denied state, failed pending with Retry/Delete, the voice bubble with and without a transcript, and the deleted sender.
  - The report sheet, the block dialog, the new-conversation sheet, the other-coach plan sheet in its loaded and locked states, and the blocked list.
- **Device QA** (Pixel; mirrors iOS QA §4, §8 and §9):
  - Text both ways with the web in realtime, read marks, and "Seen".
  - Record on Android and play on the web. A web WebM note **plays** on Android and shows its transcript.
  - Tag from "Message coach about this plan" opens the plan.
  - Report (Also block off by default) and block from the header, then unblock in Settings.
  - Airplane-mode queue, then reconnect, then delete unsent.
  - A minor shows no mic and TalkBack reads the text-only hint.
  - Parent pause in all three seats.
  - Push opens the room from a killed process. Room notifications clear when the room is read. Reply inline from the notification with the app killed; "Reply saved" in airplane mode; no Reply while the in-app lock is on (§6.6.11).
  - TalkBack reads bubbles as one node with custom actions.
