| Plan detail for the runner | Moves with Cue / Description / Why, flow bars, practice log with attribution, large targets | Same (7.6.2) | P0 |
| Session timer | Timestamp-based, survives lock and kill; one active session; persistent bar; keep-awake on the timer screen; Live Activity; "Still practicing?" after 1 h in background | Same timer model; **ongoing chronometer notification** (Android 16 Live Update where eligible) replaces the Live Activity; **no foreground service** (proposed; Mariah to confirm, §12 N46; fallback spec in 7.6.4); `keepScreenOn`; inexact alarm for the reminder | P0 |
| Flow-state feedback | 5-point scale + note; queued offline with idempotency; canonical labels (A44, replacing #18) | Same; labels **Hard / A bit hard / Just right / A bit easy / Easy** (7.6.5) | P0 |
| Message coach about this plan | Pre-tagged message, opens the room | Same (7.6.7) | P0 |

#### 7.6.1 Runner plans list (`RunnerPlansScreen`)

- Title "Plans"; under it (parent) the pending-claims banner (§7.7) and, for both roles, the recap prompt banner (§7.10).
- Segments (`SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow`, shown when more than one): "Plans", "Goals" (when the graph has a goals source), "Library" (athlete with authoring).
- Filter chips: status menu ("Active", "Benched", plus "Drafts" for an authoring athlete); athlete: "Mine" toggle chip (person icon), shown when they have any own plan or the filter is on; parent: "All athletes" menu when they have more than one athlete; "All coaches" menu when more than one coach on the list (Gradus starter plans listed as "Gradus"; own plans excluded, the coach filter never lists the athlete as a coach); "All sports" menu (rule below).
- "All sports" menu: **athletes only**, when their plans span more than one sport. Parent rows carry no sport (`sport: ""`) and drafts carry none, so parents never see it (`RunnerPlansModel.rows`, `sports` filters out empty values). The coach filter excludes own plans and groups Gradus starter plans under the id `__gradus`, labelled "Gradus".
- Card (`RunnerPlanCard`): stripe `flowAccent` (benched: `divider`), caption (parent "*Athlete first* · Coach *Name*" / "*Athlete first* · from Gradus" / "By *first*"; athlete "Coach *Name*" / "from Gradus" / "Mine"; draft "Draft"), title, right label "*n* session(s)" or, for drafts, "1 move" / "*n* moves"; flow bars except on drafts. Benched cards use the `elevated` surface at full contrast. Tap: draft → editor (athlete), otherwise `Plan(id)` runner.
- Empty messages (dashed card): Drafts "No drafts. Tap + to start a plan of your own."; Benched "No benched plans." ("No benched plans of your own." with Mine); Active with Mine "You haven't activated a plan of your own yet."; Active, authoring athlete "No active plans yet. Your coach can share one here, or tap + to write your own."; parent "No active plans — your coach will share one here."; athlete without authoring "No active plans yet — your coach will share one here.".
- Loading: two redacted "Loading…" cards; error with nothing cached: "Couldn't load your plans" + "Try again".
- Data: `GET /parent/plans` or `GET /athlete/plans`, cache-first, `If-None-Match`, foreground reload, pull to refresh (Goals segment refreshes goals instead).
- `RunnerPlansViewModel` is scoped to the **signed-in session** (owned by the app shell, not the screen), so the shell can reload it when coach/athlete links change (an athlete removed, a coach link dropped, a guardian link changed: the `linksChanged` hook, §7.7/§7.12). On that hook, for a parent or athlete, the shell calls `load()` on the model **only if the Plans tab has been visited this session** (iOS `AppModel.linksChanged()` → `runnerPlansStore?.load()`; `RunnerPlansView.init(model:)` comment). Without this, a removed athlete's plans stay visible until a later foreground refresh happens to get a new ETag.
- **Clearing a session whose plan is gone** (`RunnerPlansModel.activate()`, `aSessionForAPlanThatIsGoneIsCleared`): each time the runner list appears, after its load, if the load had **no error**, a list has loaded at least once (cache or network), the stored session's `role` matches the viewer's role, and the session's `planId` is in **none** of the rows (active, benched or drafts), clear the session and cancel its notification. A benched plan still matches a row, so its session survives. iOS cancels only the Live Activity (`activities.sync(nil)`) and leaves the "Still practicing?" reminder scheduled. Android also cancels the reminder **(proposed: iOS gap; §12 N50)**.
- Authoring FABs (athlete, Plans segment): §6.14.

#### 7.6.2 Runner plan detail (`RunnerPlanScreen`)

- Load cache-first (shared plan-detail cache), then `GET /plans/{id}` (written back to the same cache) and the session log `GET /plans/{id}/sessions?limit=100`. Error: "Couldn't load this plan" + "Try again". Top bar title = the **raw** plan title, "Plan" while it loads (`navigationTitle(model.plan?.title ?? "Plan")`; an empty title gives an empty bar, as on iOS). The header uses the display title ("Untitled plan" when empty). Cache eviction (keep the 20 most recent details) runs on **every** write, from both the editor and the runner. iOS evicts only from the editor (`PlanDetailModel`); the runner writes without evicting (`RunnerPlanDetailModel.load`). This difference is harmless and Android applies the eviction in one place in the cache DAO.
- **Top bar:** **no title** (`ad1e9bf`; the plan name is the heading below). The actions are icons:
  - a **pen** (`edit`, `contentDescription` "Edit plan", only for an athlete viewing their own plan, `isOwner`) → `EditPlan(id)`;
  - **Read this plan aloud** (`volume_up`, "Read this plan aloud", action label "Speaks the plan: each move with its target, cue and why", shown when there are moves; it moved here from a full-width button; iOS #47; Android §6.7.4);
  - **Share** ("Share plan") → share sheet with "<title> — My workout on Gradus" and the link.
- Header: caption (parent "*Athlete* · Coach *Name*" / "*Athlete* · from Gradus"; athlete "Coach *Name*" / "from Gradus"; own plan "Mine"; another's authored plan "By *first*"), centered title.
- Session timer row (7.6.3).
- The eyebrow "Your plan" / "From *author*" / "From Gradus" / "From the coach" is **gone**; the caption already says it.
- Moves: none → italic "No moves in this plan yet." on a dashed card. Each move card: target + "min"/"reps", name, chevron. Expanded: "Cue" / "Description" chips (only when both exist; Cue default), the text, then the "Why is this assigned?" pill → a panel "WHY IT'S ASSIGNED" with close (content description "Hide why it's assigned") and the why text. Expanded/collapsed and "Being read aloud" go in the content description.
- Logged card: "**Logged practice**" (was "Logged instances"), count, flow bars, attribution line; no sessions: parent "No practice logged yet. Sessions you or *Athlete* log will show up here." / athlete "No practice logged yet. Sessions you or a parent log will show up here."; else a **collapsible** "Practice log" (48 dp toggle row with its count; starts folded, `ad1e9bf`) whose rows are "*Name* logged for *Athlete*" / "*Name* logged this", flow label (· note), or for an each-move session the shared `MoveRatingsList` (each rated move with its rating word, in plan order, then the note; iOS #149, web #239), date and minutes; first 5 then "Show all *n*".
- "Message *first* about this plan" (bare coach first name, e.g. "Message Renata about this plan"; full-width primary button with a filled speech-bubble icon, iOS `bubble.left.fill`) is hidden for Gradus starter plans and athlete-authored plans (`RunnerPlanDetailView`: `!isGradus && !isAuthored`).
- Large touch targets (≥ 48 dp), readable at arm's length (iOS §7.6).

#### 7.6.3 The timer: model, controls, rules

**Model** (port `ActiveSession` / `ActiveSessionStore` verbatim): `role` (parent|athlete), `planId`, `planTitle`, `coachFirstName`, `athleteFirstName`, `startedAt: Instant?` (non-null while running), `accumulated: Duration` (seconds banked before the current running segment), `createdAt`. `elapsed(now) = accumulated + max(0, now − startedAt)`. Label "mm:ss" with hours rolled into minutes ("75:03"). One session per signed-in user, persisted as JSON in the per-user store directory (`active-session.json` equivalent), written atomically on every change, deleted on clear; restored on cold start, so the timer is correct after lock, background, process death or force-stop (wall-clock `System.currentTimeMillis()`, as iOS uses `Date`). Excluded from Auto Backup and device transfer (Android §6.11, proposed). Signing out clears the session and cancels its notification and reminder.

**Controls** (`SessionTimerRow`):
- Not started: slide-to-confirm control, hint "PRACTICE", label "Start session" with play icon; a **tap also starts** (WCAG 2.5.7); content description "Start session timer", hint "Slide right, or double-tap to start.".
- Started: pause/resume circle button ("Pause session timer" / "Resume session timer"); a slide-to-end control showing a pulsing dot (static under Remove animations) and the live time, or "Paused · mm:ss"; hint "END"; content description "End session and report back to *first*" (bare first name, no "Coach": `SessionControls.swift`), state = time or "Paused, *time*", hint "Slide right to end now, or double-tap to confirm first."; live region polite. Tap → dialog "End this session?" / "You'll say how it felt, and it goes to Coach *first*." / "End session" / "Keep going". Discard × ("Discard session") → dialog "Discard this session?" / "Your timed session and progress will be lost." / "Discard" (destructive) / "Cancel".
- Android builds the slide control in Compose (`AnchoredDraggable`) with the same tap alternatives; there is no platform slide-to-confirm component.

**Coach-directed copy on plans with no coach.** *first* above and in 7.6.4/7.6.5 is `RunnerPlanDetailModel.coachFirstName = plan?.coach?.firstName ?? "Coach"`. On an athlete-authored plan `coach` is null, so iOS renders literally:

| Surface | iOS rendering on an own plan | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Slide-to-end content description | "End session and report back to Coach" | `SessionControls.swift` |
| End dialog message | "You'll say how it felt, and it goes to Coach Coach." | `SessionControls.swift` |
| Feedback submit button | "Submit to Coach Coach" | `SessionFeedbackSheet.swift` |
| Live Activity expanded line (Android: notification BigText) | "*Athlete* · report back to Coach Coach when you end" | `GradusWidgets/SessionLiveActivity.swift` |
| Submit toast | "Session logged · *Label*" / "Saved — it syncs when you're back online." (already authored-aware) | `RunnerPlanDetailModel.submit` |

For Gradus starter plans, *first* is whatever `coach.firstName` the server returns for the Gradus coach (verify against `GET /plans/{id}` for a starter plan). **Android 1.0 copies the iOS rendering exactly (A2)**, and §12 records "iOS bug: coach-directed copy on athlete-authored plans" so both apps change together. The joint fix, if Mariah approves it, is **(proposed)**: "Submit session" / "You'll say how it felt, and it's logged on your plan." / "End session" (content description) / no report-back line in the notification. Tests: one per surface on an own plan, asserting the strings above.

**Rules** (`RunnerPlanDetailModel`):
- Start refused while another plan's session exists: error toast "You already have a session running — return to \"*Title*\" to finish it first." (`aSecondPlanCannotStartWhileAnotherRuns`).
- On start, if the newest log entry was by the **other** party (parent vs athlete) within the last 2 hours: info toast "Already logged recently — *Name* logged a session for this plan in the last couple of hours." (the session still starts).
- On first start, ask for notification permission (Android 13+ `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`, the contextual moment, mirroring `PushPermission.requestIfNeeded()`; the same grant serves FCM, §6.6). Denied: the timer, the in-app bar and everything else work; the session notification (so the lock-screen timer too) and the reminder are absent. **This differs from iOS**, where the Live Activity does not depend on notification permission (7.6.4 "Permission").
- Pause banks the running segment; resume sets a new `startedAt`.
- End = pause, then open the feedback sheet.
- Discard clears the session, the notification and the reminder; nothing is logged (`discardDropsTheSessionWithoutLogging`).
- **Keep the screen on** while this plan's session is running and the runner screen is visible (`View.keepScreenOn` / `FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON`), released on pause, end, discard and leaving the screen (iOS `isIdleTimerDisabled`).

**Persistent bar** (`ActiveSessionBar`): for parents and athletes on **every tab** (inset at the top of each tab's content), whenever a session exists and the visible screen is not that plan's runner (tracked via `presentedPlanId`). Content: pulsing dot (or a static dot when paused), live "mm:ss" or "Paused · mm:ss", divider, plan title, "RETURN →". Tap → `Plan(planId)`. Never shown for coaches.

#### 7.6.4 Session notification (the Live Activity on Android)

iOS shows a local-only Live Activity (iOS §6.6, §12 #10 default "local only") on the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island: "PRACTICING" / "PAUSED", the plan title, the athlete's first name, a system-driven timer while running or "mm:ss" while paused, a running-figure or pause icon, expanded bottom line "*Athlete* · report back to Coach *first* when you end", and a tap that opens `gradus://plans/{id}`. It is started, updated (on pause/resume and on foreground) and ended by the app; it never needs the app to run.

**Android equivalent: one ongoing notification, posted and updated by the app, with no foreground service (proposed default; Mariah to confirm, §12 N46).**

Why no foreground service: the timer is timestamp-based, so no code needs to run while it counts; the chronometer is drawn by System UI from a base time. Since Android 14 every foreground service needs a declared type, and none fits a practice stopwatch: `health` requires a sensor or activity-recognition grant Gradus does not use, `specialUse` needs a Play review justification, `shortService` stops after about 3 minutes. And since Android 13/14 users can dismiss FGS and ongoing notifications anyway (except on the lock screen), so an FGS would buy no extra persistence. Battery, Doze and OEM killers are irrelevant because nothing runs.

**If an FGS is required** (Mariah overrides the default): a `PracticeSessionService` with `android:foregroundServiceType="specialUse"`, a manifest `<property android:name="android.app.PROPERTY_SPECIAL_USE_FGS_SUBTYPE" android:value="practice_session_timer"/>` inside the `<service>`, and the permissions `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` + `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE`. This needs a Play Console foreground-service declaration with a justification and a demo video, and it goes through review (verify current form fields once the Play account exists, A8). The service is started **only** from the visible Start tap (`startForegroundService` + `startForeground(id, notification, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_SPECIAL_USE)` within the allowed window; Android 12+ forbids starting an FGS from the background) and is stopped on end, discard, submit, sign-out and the plan-gone clear. On a cold start with a restored session, the app is in the foreground, so it may restart the service. It posts the same notification described below. `health` is ruled out (it needs `ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION`, `BODY_SENSORS` or `HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS`), and `shortService` times out after about 3 minutes. Either way the timer stays timestamp-based. The FGS only pins the notification.

**Acceptance test (either design, on a Pixel):** start a session; lock the phone for 30 minutes; kill the process (`adb shell am kill training.gradus.app`); unlock. The notification chronometer and the in-app timer both show the correct elapsed time (±1 s against a stopwatch), and reopening the runner shows the same value.

| Element | Android implementation |
|---|---|
| Permission | **Known platform difference (Appendix G).** iOS gates the Live Activity only on `ActivityAuthorizationInfo().areActivitiesEnabled`, a separate Live Activities switch that is on by default, so the lock-screen timer shows even when notification permission is denied (`LiveSessionActivityController.sync`). On Android 13+ (API 33+) the session notification needs `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`. Request it at the first Start, before posting (the same moment as iOS `LiveSessionReminders.prepare()` → `PushPermission.requestIfNeeded()`). If it is denied, the in-app `ActiveSessionBar` and the runner timer are the only timer surfaces: no `notify()` call, no nag, no rationale loop, and no re-ask on later starts beyond what the system allows. On API 29–32 the notification posts unless the user has blocked the app or the channel (`NotificationManagerCompat.areNotificationsEnabled()` and the channel's importance ≠ `NONE`); check before every `notify()` |
| Channel | `practice_timer`, name "Practice timer" (§6.6.4), importance **LOW** (silent, no heads-up; must not be MIN or Live Update promotion is refused), no badge, created at first use |
| Builder | `NotificationCompat.Builder`: `setOngoing(true)`, `setOnlyAlertOnce(true)`, `setSilent(true)`, `setCategory(NotificationCompat.CATEGORY_STOPWATCH)` (the category has API 31+ semantics; on API 29–30 the string is accepted and ignored by System UI, so no fallback is needed), small icon = the Gradus monochrome glyph, `setColor(attention)` but **not** `setColorized` |
| Running | title = plan title; text "PRACTICING · *Athlete first*"; `setUsesChronometer(true)`, `setWhen(now − elapsed)` (the iOS `timerStart(at:)`), `setShowWhen(true)` |
| Paused | title = plan title; text "PAUSED · *Athlete first*"; no chronometer; `setSubText("Paused · mm:ss")` with the banked time; `setShortCriticalText("Paused")` on API 36 |
| Expanded text | `BigTextStyle`: "*Athlete first* · report back to Coach *first* when you end" (`SessionLiveActivity.swift`). On an athlete-authored plan this renders "*Athlete* · report back to Coach Coach when you end", copied as-is under A2 (7.6.3 "Coach-directed copy"; iOS bug listed in §12) |
| Tap | `PendingIntent` (immutable) to `MainActivity` with the typed route `Plan(planId)` (the iOS `gradus://plans/{id}` widget URL) |
| Lock screen | `VISIBILITY_PUBLIC` (the Live Activity shows plan title and first name on the Lock Screen; parity) |
| Live Update (Android 16, API 36+) | `setRequestPromotedOngoing(true)`; manifest `android.permission.POST_PROMOTED_NOTIFICATIONS` (install-time). Eligible because: ongoing, has a title, standard/BigText style, not colorized, no custom views, not a group summary, channel not MIN. The status-bar chip then shows the chronometer while running and "Paused" when paused. If the user has turned Live Updates off (`NotificationManager.canPostPromotedNotifications() == false`) the same notification shows unpromoted; Gradus never nags to enable it. OEM surfaces with their own eligibility rules (for example Samsung's Now Bar) may not show it (verify) |
| Dismissal | On Android 14+ users can swipe it away when unlocked. A `deleteIntent` sets `notificationDismissed = true` on the stored session (persisted in the session JSON, keyed by the session's `createdAt`). Once dismissed, Gradus does **not** re-post it for that session: pause, resume, end and foreground re-syncs skip `notify()`. Only a **new** session (a new `createdAt`) posts again. This matches iOS, where the controller keeps its cached `current` activity, so `update()` on a dismissed activity does nothing until the session clears and a new one starts. It also follows Google's Live Update guidance not to repost a Live Update the user dismissed. One deliberate difference: iOS re-requests the activity after an app relaunch (its `current` is nil and `Activity.activities` is empty), while Android does **not** re-post after a cold start or a reboot, because the persisted flag survives. The in-app bar always remains |
| Sync points | Exactly the iOS `activities.sync` calls: start, pause/resume, end (shows paused), discard and submit (cancel), app foreground (re-sync), and the plan-gone clear. On cold start with a restored session, re-post unless `notificationDismissed` |
| Reboot | Notifications do not survive a reboot; the session does. The notification is re-posted on the next app launch unless `notificationDismissed`. No `BOOT_COMPLETED` receiver |
| Sign-out | cancel |

No action buttons on the notification in 1.0: the iOS Live Activity has none (pause and end happen in the app). Adding Pause/End actions is a product change, §12 N49.

**"Still practicing?" reminder** (iOS `LiveSessionReminders`): when the app goes to the background with the session **running**, schedule one local notification 60 minutes later (`after` floored at 60 s: `max(60, after)`); cancel it on foreground, end, discard and submit; replace any earlier one. Hook scope: on iOS, `didEnterBackground` / `didBecomeActive` are called only from `RunnerPlanDetailView`'s `scenePhase` handler, so the reminder is scheduled (and the Live Activity re-synced on foreground) only while that plan's runner screen is in the view hierarchy. Backgrounding from another tab schedules nothing. Android keeps the same scope by default (the runner screen's ViewModel sees `ON_STOP`/`ON_START`, §6.6.7); an app-wide hook (`ProcessLifecycleOwner`) that fixes the iOS gap is proposed in §12 N52. Implementation: `AlarmManager.setAndAllowWhileIdle(RTC_WAKEUP, …)` (inexact; no exact alarm: `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` is denied by default for new installs on Android 14+, and `USE_EXACT_ALARM` is Play-restricted to alarm and calendar apps) firing a receiver that posts on channel `practice` ("Practice reminders", §6.6.4), tag `session-reminder`: title "Still practicing?", text "Your session on *Plan title* is still running. Open Gradus to pause or end it.", tap → the plan. Doze may delay it by a few minutes; acceptable (iOS fires "an hour after"). Skipped when notification permission is not granted, without asking (backgrounding is too late to ask; iOS `LiveSessionReminders.schedule` checks `.authorized`/`.provisional`). The 3600 s schedule is covered by `backgroundingARunningSessionNudgesAfterAnHour`.

**Wear OS.** The watch session timer (iOS §7.15 W5) is not built at iOS HEAD; §7.15 owns whether and how Android builds it. If built, the watch's Ongoing Activity mirrors this notification.

#### 7.6.5 End session and flow-state feedback

`SessionFeedbackSheet` (iOS `SessionFeedbackSheet.swift` at `c8f83d6`; A44; handoff §7 Parent and athlete). **Settled.**

Android presentation: a full-screen dialog, or a `ModalBottomSheet` with `skipPartiallyExpanded` and `confirmValueChange` refusing swipe-to-hide, with **no drag handle**, because iOS disables interactive dismissal. Its `GradusSheetHeader` has **"Close"** at the start and no title. Close, system back and predictive back all open the discard confirmation.

- **Eyebrow:** "SESSION COMPLETE · " followed by the **session length with a pen** (mono caption2 Bold tracked 1.5, `accentInk`, a small `edit` icon; min 48 dp).
  - The length shows elapsed `mm:ss` (frozen because End paused the timer), or "`N` MIN" once corrected.
  - Tapping it opens a **minutes wheel**: a small bottom sheet "Session length" with a `Done` action, holding a Compose wheel picker of "1 min" … "max(timed, 180) min", initially the timed minutes. Android has no stock wheel, so it is a `LazyColumn` with snap fling (`rememberSnapFlingBehavior`) and a centred selection band. It is one adjustable TalkBack node, "Session length, `N` minutes", with `setProgress`, plus custom actions "One minute more" / "One minute less".
  - The length button's TalkBack label is "Session length, `N` minutes" and its action label "Change it if the timer ran long". Test tags `feedback.length`, `feedback.length.picker`.
  - The corrected length replaces `durationSeconds` on submit (`correctedSeconds = minutes × 60`).
- **Title:** the plan's display title (display title).
- **Question:** **"How was practice today?"**, the same for athletes and parents (handoff; it replaced "How did you show up today?" / "How did *Athlete first* show up today?"). Display title3.
- **The scale** (`FlowStateScale`) sits in an `elevated` card (radius 20, `cardEdge`, padding 14).
  - **Track:** five dots on a 2 dp `penPoolInk` line, Hard → Easy. Each dot is 14 dp (22 dp when selected), `card` fill (`accent` when selected), with a 2 dp `penPoolInk` ring and a 48 dp hit area.
  - **Anchors**, under dots 1, 3 and 5, centred exactly under the middle dot (iOS overlays them):
    - "HARD" / "frustrated";
    - "JUST RIGHT" / "engaged";
    - "EASY" / "comfortable".

    Each is an uppercase mono caption2 Bold label in `textSecondary` with the feeling in caption2 `textTertiary` under it. Dots 2 and 4 have no visible label.
  - **TalkBack:** each dot is a `selectable` node whose content description is its full label ("Hard", "A bit hard", "Just right", "A bit easy", "Easy"; iOS `spokenLabel`). The anchors are hidden.
  - **Nothing else:** there is no "Selected: …" line and no "Tap a dot to describe today's energy." prompt; the grown, filled dot is the state (`ad1e9bf`).

| `stateIndex` | Label (A44) | Scale anchor |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Hard | "HARD" / "frustrated" |
| 1 | A bit hard | none |
| 2 | Just right | "JUST RIGHT" / "engaged" |
| 3 | A bit easy | none |
| 4 | Easy | "EASY" / "comfortable" |

**Each-move check-in** (when the plan's `feedbackScope == "moves"` and it has moves, §7.3.4 item 9; iOS `SessionFeedbackSheet.stepCard`, `44529b6`, Mariah 2026-10-14). It replaces the whole-session question and scale:
- **Heading:** "How did each move feel?" instead of the question.
- **One move at a time**, in an `elevated` card:
  - `StepDots(current, total)`, read "Move *n* of *m*";
  - the move's name (display title3, heading);
  - the same scale with the move as context, so each dot reads "{Move name}: {label}" (e.g. "Waltz jump: Hard").
- **Moving on:** rating a move stores it and, unless it is the last move, moves on after 0.2 s with a 0.25 s snappy transition, instant under Remove animations.
- **Back** (from the second move on; `feedback.step.back`) and **Skip** (except on the last move; `feedback.step.skip`) are outlined chips. Skip's action label is "Leaves *move* unrated"; a skipped move stays unrated and is left out of the average.
- **Submit** is enabled once **at least one** move is rated; whole-plan check-ins keep their rule. The session's rating is the average of the rated moves, which the server works out (see Submit below).
- Rotation keeps the step and the ratings (`rememberSaveable`).

**Labels (A44, 2026-10-13):** the scale above replaces #18's "Frustrated / Pushing / Steady / Locked in / Flowing". The middle is the target and neither end is a bad result. Android keeps the five labels and the anchors in one string table keyed by the unchanged wire values: the feedback sheet, practice log rows, toasts, TalkBack and Wear OS all read from it. There are **no per-point descriptions**. The labels describe how practice felt; they never become per-move mastery ratings (iOS §7.6), even when each move is rated.

- **Note field:** `GradusTextField` with placeholder "Anything else? (optional)" (3–6 lines). Its TalkBack label is "Anything else to share?" and its action label "What stood out, what to watch for, questions for coach". Test tag `feedback.note`.
- **The one lime action:** the full-width primary **"Submit to Coach *first*"** ("Sending…"; "Submit to Coach Coach" on an own plan, see 7.6.3), disabled until a state is picked, or for each-move check-ins until one move is rated. There is no explainer line under it; the reason goes in its TalkBack action label. Test tag `feedback.submit`.
- **Close** → `AlertDialog` "Discard this session?" / "Your timed session and progress will be lost." / "Discard" / "Cancel". Discard drops the session (as the web does).

**Submit** (`RunnerPlanDetailModel.submit`): body `{stateIndex, note (trimmed), durationSeconds}` for a whole-plan check-in, or `{moveRatings: [{planMoveId, stateIndex}] (rated moves only, in plan order), note, durationSeconds}` with **no `stateIndex` key** for an each-move one, to `POST /plans/{id}/sessions` with a fresh `Idempotency-Key`. The server records it as the caller's role (parent or athlete) and sets an each-move session's rating to the **average of the rated moves**, rounded to the nearest point with a tie going toward Just right (2). FlowBars, the practice chart and AI summaries keep reading one number per session. The toast label uses the same client-side average (`SessionSubmission.overallStateIndex`: `mean < 2 ? floor(mean + 0.5) : ceil(mean − 0.5)`). `durationSeconds` is the corrected length (minutes × 60) when the session length was corrected with the length pen (above), else `Int(elapsed)`. A submission with neither a state nor a rating is refused locally. Older queued outbox rows (with `stateIndex` only) still replay. The session log (`GET /plans/{id}/sessions`) returns optional `feedbackScope` and `moveRatings [{planMoveId (null once the move left the plan), moveName, stateIndex}]`.
- Online success → clear the session, notification and reminder; close the sheet; reload the plan and log; toast: own plan "Session logged · *Label*"; parent "Sent to Coach *first* · *Athlete* · *Label*"; athlete "Sent to Coach *first* · Your session · *Label*".
- Offline, or status 0/5xx → enqueue the **same body and key** (`entityKind` "session", label "Session on *Title*"), then finish as above with toast "Saved — it reaches Coach *first* when you're back online." (own plan: "Saved — it syncs when you're back online.").
- No outbox: "You're offline. Try again when you're back online."; enqueue failure: "Couldn't save the session." (session kept).
- Other errors: "Couldn't submit feedback — *message*" (session kept, sheet stays).
- Sessions are append-only and cannot conflict (iOS §6.5); replays are deduplicated by the idempotency key.

#### 7.6.6 Flow bars (shared component)

Port `GradusDesign/Components/FlowBars.swift` at `c8f83d6` for layout, rounding and accessibility (§8.3 FlowBars row).
- **Buckets.** The five counts collapse into three. **Settled under A44** (Mariah, 2026-10-13): "Hard" (indexes 0+1), "Just right" (2), "Easy" (3+4), so a run of sessions stuck at either end stands out. iOS at `c8f83d6` has **renamed** its buckets "Hard" / "Just right" / "Easy" but still groups them **0 / 1+2+3 / 4**, as does the web. Android builds A44's settled grouping; iOS and the web owe the regrouping (back-port, §12 N90, A65).
- **Bars:** integer percentages summing to 100 by largest-remainder rounding (shared test vectors with the web's `bucketPercents`), bar height 32 dp. The Hard bar is `textTertiary`; the **Just right** bar is `flowAccent` with a 40% glow, the only colour; the Easy bar is `textTertiary` at 45%.
- **Captions:** three lines under each bar: the uppercase label (`flowAccentInk` for Just right, `textTertiary` otherwise), the **feeling word** in lowercase caption2 regular ("frustrated", "engaged", "comfortable"; `ad1e9bf`), then "*n*%" or "—" when there is no data. Captions go under the bars when all fit on one line, else one row per bucket with the percent trailing (never truncated).
- **TalkBack** reads "*Label*, *feeling*, *n* percent" or "*Label*, *feeling*, no data". The bars are hidden from accessibility.
- **Status:** settled (A44, A61).

#### 7.6.7 Message the coach about this plan

`MessageCoachSheet`: title "Message Coach *first*", `GradusSheetHeader` "Close" (`ad1e9bf`); "Your message will be tagged to this plan in your conversation."; plan chip; field "Ask Coach *first* about this plan…" (4–8 lines, focused on open); "Send" with a paper-plane icon ("Sending…"), disabled when blank. Android: a `ModalBottomSheet` that opens half-expanded and can be dragged to full height, with a visible drag handle (iOS detents `.medium, .large`, drag indicator visible); the IME pushes it to full height. Only the sheet's title, field and the feedback sheet's submit button say "Coach *first*". The runner's entry button and the slide control's content description use the bare first name (§7.6.2, §7.6.3). Flow: ensure the athlete room with this coach (`ensureRoom(athlete(coachId, athleteId))`), send `text(body, planId)` with an idempotency key, close and open the room. A refusal (minor room rule, paused coach, §6.13) shows the server's message; other failures "Couldn't send message — *message*". Requires a connection (iOS behavior: no outbox here). Not offered for Gradus starter plans or athlete-authored plans.

#### 7.6.8 Offline and caching

| Works offline | Queues | Needs network |
|---|---|---|
| Runner lists and plan details already seen (the `plans.json` snapshot and `active-session.json`, §6.5; iOS §6.5 "own sessions cached indefinitely"); start/pause/end/discard the timer; rate the flow state | Session submission (same body and key) | Message the coach, share link, AI summary (coach side) |

#### 7.6.9 Tests (port of `SessionsModelTests`, `SessionsTests`, `GradusActivitiesTests`)

1. Elapsed is timestamp-based across pause and resume (fake clock); label rolls hours into minutes.
2. The session survives a relaunch (store reloaded from disk).
3. Parent sees both athletes' plans and filters; athlete sees own plans with coach captions.
4. A session whose plan is gone is cleared and the notification cancelled.
5. Start → pause → end → submit clears the session; the submitted body has the state, trimmed note and duration.
6. A second plan cannot start while another runs (toast text exact).
7. Offline feedback queues `POST /api/v1/plans/{id}/sessions` with the same body and key.
8. Messaging the coach sends a plan-tagged text and opens the room.
9. Discard drops the session without logging.
10. Backgrounding a running session schedules the reminder at +60 min; foreground cancels it; a paused session schedules nothing.
11. Notification builder (Robolectric): running uses chronometer with `when = now − elapsed`; paused has no chronometer and shows the banked time; promotion requested only on API 36+; never colorized; channel importance LOW; content intent targets `Plan(planId)`; after a dismissal, pause, resume, foreground and a simulated cold start do not re-post, and a new session does.
12. Permission denied (API 33+, Robolectric shadow): starting a session makes no `notify()` call, and the timer, `ActiveSessionBar` and submit still work; the reminder is not scheduled.
13. Own plan: the end dialog, slide content description, submit button and notification BigText render the exact iOS strings from 7.6.3 "Coach-directed copy".
14. The plan-gone clear: a benched plan's session survives; a session whose plan is in no row is cleared, and its notification and reminder are cancelled; a load error clears nothing.
15. Screenshot tests (Roborazzi) of the runner timer row (idle, running, paused), the feedback sheet (none and each state selected), the persistent bar, at 100% and 200% font scale, light and dark.
16. Each-move check-in (port of `SessionsModelTests`, `SessionsTests`): the rounding table (ties toward Just right, e.g. [1, 2] → 2, [2, 3] → 2, [0, 1] → 1, [3, 4] → 4); the wire format omits `stateIndex` and lists only rated moves; an older server's plan (no `feedbackScope`) asks for the whole plan; an outbox replay of an each-move check-in; nothing rated → refused locally; step navigation (rate advances, Back, Skip, last move does not advance); TalkBack "Waltz jump: Hard". Practice log: an each-move entry lists move names and rating words in plan order, a skipped move is absent, and a whole-plan entry has no list (parent and athlete).

**Items this section hands to §12 and Appendix G:**
- §12 N46 (no foreground service for the session timer; FGS fallback in 7.6.4), N47 ("Coach Coach" copy, 7.6.3), N48 (flow-state scale details under A44, 7.6.5), N49 (notification Pause/End actions), N50 (plan-gone clear cancels the reminder, 7.6.1), N51 (benched-card dimming, 7.3.1), N52 (app-wide reminder hook, 7.6.4), N53 (athlete Library cache, 6.14.4a).
- §8.1 owns `LocalIsAccessibilitySize` (`fontScale ≥ 1.5`), used by the authoring bar (6.14.4), the level ladder and the practice ring (7.8.4).
- Appendix G (known platform differences): the session notification requires `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` on API 33+, while the iOS Live Activity does not depend on notification permission; a dismissed notification is not re-posted after a relaunch (iOS re-requests it).

### 7.7 Parent — athletes, coaches, goals, schedules, team

This section covers every parent and guardian surface, plus the surfaces on other roles that belong to the same relationships: the guardian claim and team-invite links, the coach's side of coach visibility, the coach Connections hub, the athlete's "Parent or guardian" card, and the connection celebration. Under A2, Android ships each one exactly as iOS 1.0 does: the same copy, rules, offline behavior and entitlement handling. Only the platform components change. The reference is gradus-ios at HEAD `91c6af2`: `Packages/FeatureGuardians/**`, `Packages/FeatureSettings/Sources/FeatureSettings/{Parent,Connections}/**`, `Athlete/AthleteCoachesView.swift`, `Packages/GradusCore/Sources/GradusCore/Guardians/*`, `Onboarding/FamilyModels.swift`, the I13 and I14 notes in `docs/README.md`, and the iOS PRD's §7.7, §7.2, §7.8, §7.12, §7.13, #29–#31, #34, #40. Where the iOS PRD text and the code disagree, the code wins (A2). The places where that matters are marked **[code wins]**.

All user-facing strings below are quoted from the iOS code exactly. `{x}` marks an interpolated value. Unless a row says otherwise, a server error message is shown as the server sends it (`APIError.userMessage`). Toasts follow the cross-cutting rule in §7.13: error toasts stay until dismissed, have a visible close control, and clear on a tab or screen change (gradus-ios PR #114; `docs/ios/handoff-2026-10-09.md`).

#### 7.7.2 Shared Android mechanics (apply to every surface in this section)

**Data and repositories (port of `GradusCore/Guardians/*`, `Settings/SettingsRepositories.swift`).** Four guardian repositories with one interface per concern: `GuardianClaimRepository`, `TeamGuardianRepository`, `CoachVisibilityRepository`, `CelebrationRepository`. They sit beside `ParentSettingsRepository` and `ParentVerificationRepository` (§6.13). Reads and online-only writes use the generated client (§6.2). Writes that can be queued go through the outbox transport (§6.5) with exactly the path and body the outbox will replay. iOS builds these bodies by hand in `GuardianBodies` and `SettingsBodies`; Android ports both objects verbatim, including:
- sorted JSON keys;
- `birthdate` and `startsOn` sent as JSON `null`, never omitted;
- `guardianEmail` omitted when it is nil.

A `GuardianContractTests` / `SettingsContractTests` port pins every key to `openapi.json`.

Kotlin models mirror the Swift structs field for field. The iOS file is named in parentheses.

| Group | Kotlin models |
|---|---|
| Claim and invites (`GuardianModels.swift`) | `GuardianClaimSummary`, `GuardianPendingClaim`, `GuardianClaimContext`, `GuardianMergeOption` (rank `exact`/`close`/`other`), `GuardianClaimResult`, `GuardianResendResult`, `GuardianStatus` |
| Team plan (`GuardianModels.swift`) | `TeamGuardian` (role `primary`/`co`, `isSelf`), `TeamGuardianInvite`, `TeamGuardianAthlete`, `TeamGuardianList` (`planActive`, `isPayer`), `TeamInviteCreated`, `TeamInvitePreview`, `TeamInviteClaimResult` |
| Coach visibility (`GuardianModels.swift`) | `CoachVisibilityPair`, `CoachVisibilityCoach` (status `off`/`waiting`/`pending`/`connected`/`declined`), `CoachVisibilityOverview`, `CoachVisibilityLink`, `MyCoachVisibility` (`pending`/`connected`/`awaiting`) |
| Celebrations (`GuardianModels.swift`) | `CelebrationGroup`, `CelebrationPayload` (role `coach`/`parent`/`adult-athlete`/null) |
| Settings (`SettingsModels.swift`) | `ParentSettings`, `ParentAthlete`, `AthleteCoachLink`, `AthleteSportSummary`, `SportGoals`, `CoachSchedule`, `ScheduleSlot`, `ParentGoalAthlete`, `ParentGoalSport`, `TeamPlanStatus` |
| Onboarding (`ConsentModels.swift`, `FamilyModels.swift`) | `AthleteAccountState`, `ParentVerification`, `CoachPreview`, `AthleteGoals`, `LessonFrequency`, `LessonSlot`, `LessonScheduleRules`, `Birthdate`, `UsernameText` |

Enums decode unknown values without failing; this mirrors the plain-string rule iOS uses for `method` (#38). `ScheduleSlot` decodes numbers as `Double` and converts them to `Int`, because the server types them as `number`.

**Endpoints used in this section** (all under `/api/v1`; `[idem]` means the call sends an `Idempotency-Key`):

| Area | Calls |
|---|---|
| Parent settings | `GET /parent/settings` (ETag), `PATCH /parent/profile`, `POST /parent/athletes` [idem], `PATCH /parent/athletes/{id}`, `DELETE /parent/athletes/{id}`, `PUT /parent/athletes/{id}/goals`, `POST /parent/athletes/{id}/coaches` [idem], `DELETE /parent/athletes/{id}/coaches/{coachId}`, `PUT /parent/athletes/{id}/coaches/{coachId}/sports`, `PUT /parent/athletes/{id}/coaches/{coachId}/messaging` (the Swift doc comment says `messaging-pause`; the contract path is `/messaging` **[code wins]**: the generated op `setParentAthleteCoachMessagingPause`), `PUT /parent/athletes/{id}/primary-coach`, `PUT /parent/athletes/{id}/schedule` (`coachId` in the body), `POST /parent/athletes/{id}/reset-password`, `POST /signup/parent/coach-preview`, `GET /parent/goals`, `GET /parent/team` |

| Team | `GET /parent/team/guardians` (ETag), `POST /parent/team/guardians/invites` [idem], `POST /parent/team/guardians/invites/{id}/resend` [idem], `DELETE /parent/team/guardians/invites/{id}`, `DELETE /parent/team/guardians/{id}` (`{id}` = the `athlete_guardians` row), `POST /team-invites/preview` (public), `POST /team-invites/claim` [idem] |
| Visibility | `GET /parent/coach-visibility` (ETag), `PUT /parent/coach-visibility` [idem], `GET /coach/visibility/mine` (ETag), `POST /coach/visibility/{id}/respond`, `DELETE /coach/visibility/{id}` |

**Server addition** (owned by §6.10 and Appendix A S-10; listed here because these flows depend on it): `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` on gradus.training. It lists the upload-key SHA-256 fingerprint now, and adds the Play App Signing fingerprint once the Play Console organization account exists (A8); the paths these flows need (`/g/*`, `/team/*`, `/i/*`, `/verified`, `/verified/*`, the role settings paths) are declared in the app's manifest (§6.10.1). Until verification passes, an email's `/g/` or `/team/` link opens the web flow in the browser. QA uses `gradus://g/<token>` and `gradus://team/<token>`, or re-runs verification with `adb shell pm verify-app-links --re-verify training.gradus.app`. No other server change is needed for this section.

**The write pattern.** One shared `OnlineFirstWriter` replaces the iOS `perform`/`queue` pairs in `ParentSettingsModel`, `TeamGuardiansModel`, `VisibilityWriter`, `GuardianEmailModel`, `CelebrationModel` and `GoalsModel`. It behaves as follows:

1. Mint one `Idempotency-Key` per user action. The live call and any queued replay use the same key, so a timed-out request that drains later sends one email, not two.
2. If the device is offline, enqueue right away.
3. If the live call fails with a transport error (status 0) or a 5xx, enqueue it with the same key.
4. If it fails with a 4xx, revert the optimistic change and show the server's message (toast plus the inline `ErrorLine`).
5. Every outbox row uses `entityKind = "settings"` and a human label. The label never contains a token. The labels are listed in §7.7.18.
6. When a write is queued, show the toast "Saved — it syncs when you're back online." The celebration ack is the one write that skips this toast.
7. If no outbox exists (not signed in), fail with "You're offline. Try again when you're back online."
8. If enqueueing fails (the outbox insert throws), revert the optimistic change and show "Couldn't save the change." (error toast plus `ErrorLine`). If the request body can't be encoded, the write stops before any optimistic change with the same message: `ParentSettingsModel` sets only the `ErrorLine` in that case; the guardian models also toast it (`TeamGuardiansModel.swift` L206, `GuardianEmailModel.swift` L280, `CelebrationModel.swift`, `VisibilityWriteSupport.swift`, `ParentSettingsModel.swift` L199/L263).

Online-only writes use an `online { }` helper instead. When offline, it fails before any network call with "You're offline. Try again when you're back online." and queues nothing.

**Etag hygiene after a queued write** (`ParentSettingsModel.optimistic`). After a write is queued, set `etag = null` and persist the optimistic copy. Otherwise a later `If-None-Match` could answer 304 and keep an unconfirmed copy forever.

**Load-sequence guard.** On iOS, `TeamGuardiansModel`, `ParentCoachVisibilityModel`, `MyCoachVisibilityModel` and `CelebrationModel` keep a monotonic `loadSequence`; `ParentSettingsModel.load()` has none. Android gives `ParentSettingsViewModel` the same guard as a deliberate hardening (A35); no user-visible behavior changes. A load applies its result only if it is still the newest one. An optimistic write bumps the sequence, so a load that was already in flight cannot overwrite the optimistic state or restore an etag the write cleared. On Android this lives in the ViewModel; cancelling the in-flight load `Job` when a write starts is an acceptable equivalent, as long as the `VisibilityTests` case "A load already in flight when a write starts can't clobber the optimistic result" passes.

**Per-user snapshot caches.** These are JSON files on iOS (`StoreContainer.directory(for:)`, protection `completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication`, wiped at sign-out). On Android they are kotlinx.serialization JSON files with the same names under `noBackupFilesDir/Gradus/<userId>/` (§6.5, A34), written atomically (write to temp, then rename). Android 10+ file-based encryption of credential-encrypted storage plays the role of iOS's until-first-unlock class. The files are excluded from cloud backup and device transfer through `android:dataExtractionRules` (API 31+) and `android:fullBackupContent` (API 29–30, since A6 sets minSdk 29), both excluding `noBackupFilesDir` contents and the sensitive DataStore files (§6.11.3); they are wiped at sign-out with the rest of the user directory (§6.5, §6.11).

| File | Holds | Never holds |
|---|---|---|
| `parent-settings.json` | settings + etag + fetchedAt | — |
| `team-guardians.json` | guardian list + etag + fetchedAt | invite **tokens** (names and codes only) |
| `coach-visibility-parent.json` | parent overview + etag + fetchedAt | — |
| `coach-visibility-mine.json` | coach buckets + etag + fetchedAt | — |
| `celebration-dismissals.json` | sorted link ids dismissed on this device | — |

One store is per device, not per user: `gradus.coachVisibilitySeen`, the signature of the pending-request set the coach has already seen. iOS keeps it in `UserDefaults.standard`, which sign-out does not clear. Android keeps it in an app-level Preferences DataStore under the same key and does not clear it at sign-out either. It holds sorted link ids only.

**Refresh cadence** (each row is exact iOS behavior):

| Model | Activate | Foreground |
|---|---|---|
| `ParentSettingsModel` | cache, then network | reload only if `fetchedAt` is older than **4 h** |
| `TeamGuardiansModel` | cache, then network, then `GET /parent/team` | **always** reload (ETag 304), then `GET /parent/team`. `planActive`/`isPayer` gate controls and are never cached as an entitlement. |
| `ParentCoachVisibilityModel` | cache, then network | **always** reload (ETag) |
| `MyCoachVisibilityModel` | cache, then network | reload if older than **15 min** |
| `CelebrationModel` | none; refreshed only by the shell triggers in §7.7.16 | — |
| `PendingClaimsModel` | load on appear | reload on foreground; a failure stays quiet |
| `GoalsModel` | network on selection; nothing cached | on foreground |

"Foreground" means the app returns to the foreground: `ProcessLifecycleOwner` `Lifecycle.Event.ON_START`, collected while the screen is in composition. This is the equivalent of the iOS `scenePhase == .active`. Screens also reload on pull-to-refresh, which maps to the iOS `gradusRefreshable` (Material 3 `PullToRefreshBox`).

**Session scoping.** These models live for the whole session and are shared across screens: team guardians, parent coach visibility, my coach visibility, celebrations, pending claims and parent settings. iOS holds them on `AppModel`; Android holds them in session-scoped singletons (a Hilt `@SessionScoped` component or an equivalent holder). They are dropped at sign-out and **whenever `/me` reports a different role** (`syncGuardianStoresToRole`).

**Platform mapping used throughout** (A2; see §8 for the full table):

| iOS | Android |
|---|---|
| `.alert` with a destructive role (never `confirmationDialog`; working rule in `docs/ios/handoff-2026-10-05.md`) | Material 3 `AlertDialog`; the destructive confirm uses the `error`/destructive-ink token |
| `.sheet` with `.large` detent | `ModalBottomSheet(sheetState = rememberModalBottomSheetState(skipPartiallyExpanded = true))`, or a full-screen dialog for Cancel/Save forms |
| `.sheet` with `[.medium, .large]` | `ModalBottomSheet` that allows the partially expanded state |
| `interactiveDismissDisabled(isSaving)` | `sheetState` `confirmValueChange` returns false while saving, plus `BackHandler(enabled = isSaving) {}` |
| `Menu` behind `ellipsis` | `IconButton(Icons.Default.MoreVert)` + `DropdownMenu`; content description "Actions for {coach}" |
| `Toggle` | `Switch` in a row with `Modifier.toggleable`; the whole row is the touch target |
| `.popover` (pair moon) | `TooltipBox(state = rememberTooltipState(isPersistent = true))` with a `PlainTooltip`, shown on tap (`state.show()`) |
| `ShareLink(item: url, message:)` | Android Sharesheet: `Intent.createChooser(Intent(ACTION_SEND).setType("text/plain").putExtra(EXTRA_TEXT, "{message} {url}"), null)` |
| `UIPasteboard` + "Code copied" toast | `LocalClipboard.current.setClipEntry(ClipEntry(clipData))` (Compose 1.8+; `LocalClipboardManager` is deprecated), or the platform `ClipboardManager.setPrimaryClip`, so the clip's extras can be set. The "Code copied" toast shows only on API ≤ 32, because Android 13+ shows its own copy confirmation (proposed A30). **Athlete invite codes** (athlete detail "Copy code": the code lets someone create the child's account) and **guardian team-invite codes** (Add a guardian "Copy": the code grants co-guardian access to a minor's data) are copied with `clipData.description.extras = PersistableBundle().apply { putBoolean(ClipDescription.EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE, true) }` on API 33+, so the system preview shows dots (A36). The coach's own invite code (Connections hub, Roster) is not marked sensitive. |
| `.speechSpellsOutCharacters()` on codes | `VerbatimTtsAnnotation` on the code text, so TalkBack spells it character by character (verify Compose API) |
| `.textContentType(.givenName / .familyName / .emailAddress / .newPassword)` | Compose autofill `ContentType.PersonFirstName / PersonLastName / EmailAddress / NewPassword` semantics (verify Compose version) |
| `.textInputAutocapitalization(.characters)`, `.autocorrectionDisabled()`, `.keyboardType(.asciiCapable)` | `KeyboardOptions(capitalization = Characters, autoCorrectEnabled = false, keyboardType = KeyboardType.Ascii)`; `InviteCodeText.normalize` runs in `onValueChange` (A–Z and 2–9, uppercase, at most 8) |
| `Haptics.success()` | §8.5 success haptic (`HapticFeedbackConstants.CONFIRM` on API 30+, with the §8.5 fallback on API 29) (verify) |
| Reduce Motion | `Settings.Global.ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE == 0f` ("Remove animations" in Accessibility settings), read through one `rememberReduceMotion()` (§8.5) |
| `.redacted(reason: .placeholder)` | Placeholder shimmer per §8 |
| `StateView(systemImage:title:message:actionTitle:)` | `GradusStateView` (§8.3) with the same title, message and action text |
| `accessibilityIdentifier("x.y")` | `Modifier.testTag("x.y")` with the **same strings**, so test scripts carry over (proposed A32) |
| "Opens in Safari" hint | "Opens in your browser"; opened with `Intent.ACTION_VIEW` in the external browser, never a WebView (§6.8) |
| `Storefront.current?.countryCode == "USA"` | §6.8's `StorefrontRepository.isUSStorefront` (A13) together with the `androidExternalLinksEnabled` kill switch (A37; default true, on in 1.0) |

#### 7.7.3 Settings root (parent)

Source: `SettingsView.swift`. Sections appear in this order, using the eyebrow headers shown:
- **Profile:** row "Name" (person icon). Its value is "{first} {last}". It opens `ParentProfileScreen`.
- **Verification:** shown only when `parent.showsVerification`. That requires a verification repository, `settings.verification.offersOptIn` (not verified, and either `required` or KWS `available`), and the step not already finished. The section embeds the compact `ParentVerificationStep` from §6.13 and §7.1 (#29, #34). When verification succeeds, the settings reload so the login codes appear. The section then hides and stays hidden even if the cached copy lags.
- **Family:**
  - "My athletes" (icon `figure.and.child.holdinghands` → Material `FamilyRestroom`). Its value is the athlete count; nil when there are none.
  - "Team plan" (icon `person.3` → `Groups`). Its value is "Active" or "Not active", taken from `teamGuardians.list.planActive`, falling back to `GET /parent/team` `active`. The guardian list's `planActive` counts co-guardian coverage; `/parent/team.active` counts only the payer.
- Then the shared Appearance, Account, Legal and Support sections (§7.12).

Root activation calls `parent.activateIfNeeded()` and `teamGuardians.activateIfNeeded()`. Foreground calls both `refreshOnForeground()`. Each row routes through the shell's settings-section route so that deep links and rows land on the same screen instance with the shared models (`settings/athletes`, `settings/plan`).

#### 7.7.4 My athletes and Add an athlete

**`ParentAthletesScreen`** (`ParentAthletesView.swift`). Page title "My athletes". When queued settings writes exist, a sync label sits at the top right with a sync icon: "{n} to sync".
- Load error with no cached settings: state "Couldn't load your athletes" with the error message and "Try again".
- Loading with no cache: a placeholder card "Loading your athletes…".
- No athletes: card "No athletes yet. Add the first one to set goals and lessons."

One card per athlete (`AthleteCard`):
- a 5 dp tennis-pen stripe on the leading edge;
- full name, with "Age {n}" in mono when a birthdate exists, and a chevron;
- a coaches line with a people icon: the coach names joined by ", ", or "No coach linked";
- an account line: "Account: @{username}" if `hasAccount` and a username exist, "Account: signs in with email" if `hasAccount` without a username, otherwise "No account yet";
- a "Syncing" tag (pool pen) while that athlete has queued writes.

TalkBack reads the card as one merged node. Tapping it opens the athlete detail screen.

Below the list, the secondary button "Add an athlete" (plus icon) opens the Add sheet. Pull to refresh reloads.

**Add an athlete** (`AddAthleteSheet`) is a full-screen dialog titled "Add an athlete", with "Cancel" and "Add athlete" ("Adding…" while saving).
- Body text: "Their name and date of birth. You can link a coach and set goals after."
- Fields: "First name" (placeholder "First") and "Last name" ("Last"), side by side when they fit and stacked otherwise (`AdaptiveStack` → `FlowRow`/`Column` by width).
- `BirthdateField`: label "Date of birth", empty state "Choose a date". This is the §7.1 component (Material 3 `DatePickerDialog`, initial display 12 years ago, never pre-filled).
- **COPPA direct notice** (#40, §6.13 A8): `DirectNotice` with `athleteName = firstName`, without the consent-act sentence; that sentence is for sign-up and claim, not Settings. The notice text comes from the shared `DirectNotice` object (`GradusCore/Onboarding/DirectNotice.swift`, itself a sentence-for-sentence copy of the web's `src/lib/consent/direct-notice.ts`), ported verbatim and shared with sign-up and claim. The sentences, joined by single spaces in this order:
  1. "What Gradus keeps for {name}: their name, date of birth, a username, practice logs, goals, and text messages with their coach, which you can always read."
  2. "We use it only to run their training, never for advertising."
  3. "It is stored and delivered by our hosting, database, email, push-notification and AI-drafting providers, and Kids Web Services verifies parents; the full list is in our privacy policy."
  4. "Athletes under 18 can't send voice recordings."
  5. "We keep it for as long as the account exists."
  6. "An account for an athlete under 18 that nobody has used for three years is deleted, after we email you first."
  7. "From your parent account you can review or delete their information at any time."
  8. Only when `consentAct = true` (sign-up and the guardian claim, never Settings): "By continuing, you give your consent for {name} on those terms."

  `{name}` is the trimmed first name; blank or null gives "your athlete". "our privacy policy" is an underlined link to `https://gradus.training/privacy` that opens in the external browser (underlined so it is told apart by more than color, WCAG 1.4.1). **TalkBack:** the notice is one merged text node: a `Text` with an `AnnotatedString` carrying a `LinkAnnotation.Url` on "our privacy policy". TalkBack reads the block as one element (QA.md "Direct notice in the flow") and offers the link through its Links menu (the iOS Links rotor, `DirectNoticeView.swift`). Test tag `directNotice`. Tests: the Settings variant omits the consent sentence; the claim variant includes it; a blank name renders "your athlete".

Save is enabled when both names are non-blank, the birthdate is a valid ISO date, and nothing is saving. The call is `POST /parent/athletes` [idem], **online-only**. On success the screen reloads the settings, shows the toast "{first} added", plays the success haptic and dismisses. A client-side failure shows "Enter a name and a date of birth."

#### 7.7.5 Athlete detail

**`ParentAthleteDetailScreen`** (`ParentAthleteDetailView.swift`). The top bar title is the athlete's first name, or "Athlete" if unknown. The content is a single scrolling column with a 640 dp max width. Under A4 that limit matters only for tablets; the phone layout is full width.

When the athlete can't be shown:
- loading: a centered progress indicator;
- load error with no settings: "Couldn't load this athlete" with "Try again";
- athlete missing: "Athlete not found" / "This athlete is no longer on your account."

Sections, in order:

1. **Header.** Page title is the full name. A "{n} to sync" label appears while this athlete has queued writes. Below it: "Age {n} · Born {Month d, yyyy}" (`FormatStyle.LONG`), or "No birthdate". The inline `ErrorLine` shows `actionError` while no sheet is open.
2. **Account paused card** (only when `accountState == paused`, §6.13 B4). Pause icon in attention ink, eyebrow "Account paused", body chosen by the athlete's `pausedVia` (§6.13 B4, S-11): `app_store` → iOS `AthleteAccountState.pausedMessageForParent` verbatim ("Consent for {first}'s use of Gradus was withdrawn through Apple (Screen Time or Family Sharing), so their messaging and coach connections are on hold. To restore the account, email support@gradussports.com from this account's address."); `google_play` → the Google Play wording in §6.13 B4; missing or unknown → the generic sentence in §6.13 B4 (§12 N71). A parent on Android can see an athlete paused by an iPhone rescind, and the copy follows the pause's source, not the device.
3. **Identity.** Eyebrow "Identity". Bold full name and the "Born …" line, with an "Edit" chip that opens the Identity sheet.
4. **Coaches.** Eyebrow "Coaches". When there are none: "No coach linked yet. Ask {first}'s coach for their invite code."

   Each coach row shows the bold name, a "Messaging paused" tag when `messagingPaused == true`, and the overflow menu "Actions for {coach}":
   - "Edit sports" (opens the Coach sports sheet)
   - "Pause messaging" or "Resume messaging" (opens the confirmation)
   - "Unlink", destructive (opens the confirmation)

   Below the name, the sport chips use the catalog labels from §7.2 (`sportDisplayLabel`). Then the **visibility toggle row** from §7.7.12, shown only when `visibility.showsToggles(athleteId)`. Rows are separated by dividers. The section ends with the secondary button "Link a coach" (person-add icon).
5. **Primary coach per sport** (only when the athlete has sports). Eyebrow "Primary coach per sport", caption "When more than one coach handles the same sport, pick which one's expectations drive {first}'s goals and practice plans." Each row shows the sport label:
   - with more than one eligible coach: a dropdown chip showing the primary's name or "Pick a coach", with the current primary checked. It is disabled while saving.
   - with one eligible coach: "{name} · only coach", or "— · only coach" when none is set.
6. **Goals.** Eyebrow "Goals".
   - No coaches: "Link a coach who teaches this sport before setting goals."
   - Coaches but no sports: "{first}'s coaches haven't set up their sports yet."

   Each sport shows its label in bold. When a primary coach exists, a chip reads "Set goals" (no goals yet) or "Edit". Without a primary coach the row says "Link a coach who teaches this sport before setting goals." With goals it shows "{current level label} → {season goal label} this season", and the long-term goal on up to 2 lines if non-empty. Without goals: "Not set".
7. **Schedule.** Eyebrow "Schedule". No coaches: "Link a coach first, then set {first}'s lessons here." Each coach (`schedulesByCoach`) shows the bold coach name, a chip "Set lessons" (no slots) or "Edit", and either "No lessons yet" or one mono line per slot from `ParentSettingsText.slotLine`. The line format is "Tue 4:00 PM–5:00 PM", with a suffix by frequency:

   | Frequency | Suffix |
   |---|---|
   | weekly | none |
   | biweekly | " · every other week" |
   | twice-monthly / monthly | " · {1st and 3rd weeks} of the month" ("1st week" for one; "some weeks" if none) |

   Week labels are 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and Last. Times use the `LessonSlot.timeLabel` 12-hour format.
8. **Athlete invite** (when `!hasAccount && inviteCode != null`). Eyebrow "Athlete invite", caption "Share this so {first} can sign in to their own account." The code is shown large, in bold mono, with letter spacing 4 and spelled out for TalkBack. Below it: "gradus.training/i/{code}". Two actions:
   - "Share", which opens the Android Sharesheet with the message "Join me on Gradus with code {code}" and the URL `https://gradus.training/i/{code}`;
   - "Copy code", which copies the code and shows "Code copied".

   **Login code waiting** (when `!hasAccount`, no code, and `settings.verification.isNeeded`): eyebrow "Login code", text "{first}'s login code appears here once you've verified you're an adult (Settings → Verification)." (§6.13 A4.)
9. **Sign-in.** Eyebrow "Sign-in".
   - With an account: "{first} signs in with @{username}." or "{first} signs in with their email.", then the caption "Set a new password here if they've forgotten it." and the secondary "Reset password" (key icon).
   - Without an account: "This athlete hasn't created their account yet."
10. **Remove.** A destructive text button "Remove {first}" (trash icon), disabled while saving.

**Confirmation dialogs**

| Action | Title | Message | Confirm / Cancel |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unlink | "Unlink {coach}?" | "Unlinking removes this coach's schedule and goals for {first}." | "Unlink {coach}" (destructive) / "Keep linked" |
| Pause | "Pause messaging with {coach}?" | "Neither {coach} nor {first} can send in their conversation until you resume it. Plans and lessons are not affected." | "Pause" (destructive) / "Cancel" |
| Resume | "Resume messaging with {coach}?" | "{coach} and {first} can message each other again, with you in the conversation as before." | "Resume" / "Cancel" |
| Remove athlete | "Remove {full name}?" | "This removes {first}'s goals, schedule, and invite. Their coaches lose access." | "Remove {first}" (destructive) / "Keep" |

When the first name is unknown, the interpolated fallbacks are "this athlete", "your athlete", "athlete" and "their".

**Writes from this screen** (`ParentSettingsModel`):

| Action | Endpoint | Mode | Optimistic change | Success toast | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Edit identity | `PATCH /parent/athletes/{id}` `{firstName,lastName,birthdate\|null}` | queued | names and birthdate | "Saved" | Client checks: "Enter a first and last name." and "Enter a valid date of birth." A birthdate may be cleared (sent as `null`). |
| Goals | `PUT /parent/athletes/{id}/goals` `{sport,currentLevelKey,seasonGoalKey,longTermGoal}` | queued | that sport's goals | "Goals saved" | "Pick a current level and a season target." The long-term goal is trimmed. |
| Coach sports | `PUT …/coaches/{coachId}/sports` `{sports}` | queued | sports; primaries for removed sports cleared; `renormalize()` | "Sports updated" | "Keep at least one sport." |
| Primary coach | `PUT …/primary-coach` `{sport,coachId}` | queued | primary id and name | "Primary coach updated" | Client refuses a coach who doesn't teach the sport: "That coach doesn't teach this sport for this athlete." |
| Schedule | `PUT …/schedule` `{coachId,slots[]}` | queued | that coach's slots | "Schedule saved" | Validated first by `LessonScheduleRules.prepare` (below) |
| Coach preview | `POST /signup/parent/coach-preview` `{code}` | online | — | — | "Enter the coach's full code." |
| Link coach | `POST …/coaches` `{code,sports}` [idem] | online | reload | "Coach linked" | "Pick at least one sport." Then `onLinksChanged`. |
| Unlink coach | `DELETE …/coaches/{coachId}` | online | removes the coach, their schedule, and primaries plus goals for sports where they were primary; `renormalize()`; then reload | "{coach} unlinked" | Then `onLinksChanged`. |
| Pause / resume | `PUT …/coaches/{coachId}/messaging` `{paused}` → `{paused}` | online | applies the stored value | "Messaging with {coach} paused" / "Messaging with {coach} resumed" | Co-guardians can pause only while the Team plan is active (server rule `canWrite`). |
| Reset password | `POST …/reset-password` `{password}` → `{username}` | online | — | "Password updated" | At least 8 characters |
| Remove athlete | `DELETE /parent/athletes/{id}` | online | removes the row | "{first} removed" | The server refuses the last athlete (422, shown verbatim). Then `onLinksChanged`; the screen pops on success. |

`renormalize()` is a direct port of the Swift extension:
- sports are the sorted union of all coaches' sports;
- the primary is the stored one if that coach is still eligible, otherwise the first eligible coach;
- goals stay attached to their sport;
- every linked coach keeps a schedule row.

`onLinksChanged` is the shell hook in §7.7.16. It refreshes celebrations and invalidates the parent visibility overview (etag cleared, then reload). If the Plans tab has been visited this session, it also reloads the runner plans.

**Sheets** (full-screen dialogs with Cancel and a Save action in the top bar; `ParentAthleteSheets.swift`):
- **Identity** (title "Identity"): "First name" and "Last name" (placeholders "First"/"Last"), `BirthdateField`, and the text button "Clear date of birth" when one is set. Save is "Save" ("Saving…") and is enabled when both names are non-blank and the birthdate is empty or valid.
- **Link a coach** (title "Link a coach"):
  - Text: "Enter the code from {first}'s coach." Field "Coach invite code", placeholder "ABCD2345", bold mono, normalized. It is pre-filled from `pendingInviteCode` (see §7.7.19), which is then cleared.
  - When the code reaches 8 characters, the preview runs automatically and shows "Looking up the coach…". Editing the code clears the preview and selection.
  - Preview card: eyebrow "Coach", the coach's full name, then either "This coach hasn't set up their sports yet." or "Which sports does {coachFirst} coach {first} in?" with sport chips.
  - A single offered sport is pre-selected.
  - After a failed lookup with a complete code, a secondary "Look up" button retries.
  - Save is "Link" ("Linking…"), enabled with a preview and at least one sport.
- **Coach sports** (title is the coach's name): "The sports {coach} coaches {first} in. Keep at least one, or unlink the coach instead." Chips that always keep at least one selected. Save is enabled when the selection is non-empty and changed.
- **Goals** (title "{first}'s goals"):
  - Text: "Where {first} is now in {sport}, and where you'd like them to be by the end of the season."
  - Caption "Primary coach: {name}".
  - The shared `GoalsForm` card from §7.1: level pickers from the sport catalog, labels shown as "{label} · {hint}", plus the long-term goal.
  - Save is enabled when `isComplete` (sport, current level and season goal all set).
- **Schedule** (title "Lessons with {coach}"):
  - Text: "When does {first} have lessons with {coach}? Leave a lesson blank to drop it."
  - The shared `ScheduleEditor` from §7.1. Times run in 15-minute steps from 6:00 AM to 9:45 PM. Frequencies are Weekly / Every other week / 2x per month / 1x per month. Start date is required for every-other-week lessons; weeks of the month for monthly ones.
  - It starts with one empty slot when there are none.
  - Validation errors are shown inline:

    | Rule | Message |
    |---|---|
    | end not after start | "End time must be after start time for every slot." |
    | monthly without one week | "Pick which week of the month for every monthly lesson." |
    | 2x-monthly without two weeks | "Pick 2 weeks of the month for every 2x-monthly lesson." |
    | every-other-week without a start date | "Pick a starting date for every every-other-week lesson." |

  - `prepare` drops unfilled slots, clears `weeksOfMonth` for weekly and biweekly, sorts weeks, and clears `startsOn` unless the slot is biweekly. It shares test vectors with `lesson-recurrence` (§7.2).
- **Reset password** (title "Reset password"):
  - Line: "{first} signs in with @{u}." or "… with their email."
  - Fields "New password" (placeholder "At least 8 characters") and "Confirm password" ("Type it again"), both password fields with the new-password autofill hint.
  - Inline errors: "Password must be at least 8 characters." and "Passwords don't match."
  - Save is "Set password". On success the screen shows "Password updated for {first}." with a check icon in tennis ink, then "They sign in with @{u} and the new password." or "They sign in with their email and the new password.", and the top bar's action becomes "Done".

Every sheet clears `actionError` when it opens and plays the success haptic before dismissing.

#### 7.7.6 Parent profile

`ParentProfileScreen` (`ParentProfileView.swift`). Page title "Your name", top bar title "Profile". A card holds:
- the text "How coaches and your athletes see you.";
- "First name" and "Last name" fields (placeholders "First"/"Last"; given- and family-name autofill hints);
- `ErrorLine`;
- the primary button "Save" ("Saving…").

Save is enabled when the fields differ from the profile and both are non-blank. Fields are seeded once from the profile; later loads overwrite them only if the user hasn't edited them. The write is `PATCH /parent/profile`, **queued**, with the toast "Name saved". Loading shows "Loading…". An error shows "Couldn't load your profile" with "Try again".

#### 7.7.7 Goals dashboard (Plans tab, Goals segment)

Source: `FeatureSessions/Goals/GoalsDashboardView.swift`, `GoalsModel.swift`. The parent's Plans tab has a Plans | Goals segmented control: a Material 3 `SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow`. §7.6 owns the Plans side and §7.8 owns the shared goal card. This section owns the parent rules:
- The data is `GET /parent/goals` and is never cached. On a load failure the previous dashboard stays.
- For each athlete with sports, the athlete name is shown as a heading.
- **`guardianRole == "co"`** means read-only: show the caption "{first}'s primary parent sets these goals." (first name taken from `athleteName`, falling back to "Their") and no Edit controls. A missing role counts as primary; the server remains the gate.
- For the primary parent, both **pen** buttons (icon only since `ad1e9bf`; TalkBack "Edit goal" / "Edit long-term goal") on a `SportGoalCard` open **`ParentGoalsSheet`**. The sheet has a `GradusSheetHeader` with "Close" and "Save", and its level pickers are `GradusPickerField`s:
  - title "{first}'s goals";
  - text "Where {first} is now in {sport}, and where you'd like them to be by the end of the season.";
  - pickers "Current level" and "Target for this season", each starting at "Pick a level", with the caption "Pick both levels to save." until both are chosen;
  - "Long-term goal (optional)" with placeholder "Where would you like them to be in a few years?", capped at 280 characters with a "{n}/280" counter.

  Saving sends `PUT /parent/athletes/{id}/goals` with all three fields, **queued** through the outbox. An unchanged form is a no-op. Over 280 characters: "Keep the long-term goal under 280 characters."
- Empty state: "No goals yet. Add them in Settings → Athletes."
- Load error before the first load: "Couldn't load goals" with "Try again".

#### 7.7.8 Pending claims card (parent Plans tab)

Source: `Claim/PendingClaimsCard.swift`, gradus-ios PR #121, web PR #207 (`docs/ios/handoff-2026-10-09.md`; beta feedback 2026-10-07; Mariah's call: the parent confirms). This card is for athletes a coach added using the signed-in parent's email.

Since web PR #207 the server lists claims **only** when the account's Apple or Google identity verified that email. Teen self-sign-up rows are never listed. Everyone else confirms from the "Sign in to confirm" email. Android needs no extra rule here; it renders what `GET /guardian/pending-claims` returns.

Each claim is a card:
- title "Coach {name} added {first}", or "A coach added {first}" when there is no coach name, as a heading;
- body "They listed you as {first}'s parent or guardian. Is this your child? Nothing is linked until you confirm.";
- primary button "Review and confirm", with content description "Review and confirm {first}" and test tag `pendingClaim.{index}`. The token is a credential, so it is never used as an identifier and never logged.

The button opens `GuardianClaimScreen(token)` (§7.7.10). The list loads on appear and on foreground, and failures are silent: the card is a nudge, and the email still works. It reloads after any claim finishes. The card mounts in the parent Plans tab's banner slot and appears only for the parent role.

#### 7.7.9 Team plan, guardians, Add a guardian, invite-code sheet

**`TeamPlanScreen`** (`TeamPlanView.swift`). Page title and top bar title: "Team plan".

1. **Plan card** from `GET /parent/team` (`TeamPlanStatus`). It shows "Team plan", a status pill (uppercase, tracking 1) and a description. The renewal line uses `FormatStyle.MEDIUM`, e.g. "Oct 1, 2026".

   | Server state | Pill (tone) | Description | Renewal line |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `active == false` | "Inactive" (muted) | "One parent or guardian per athlete." | none |
   | `past_due` | "Past due" (destructive) | "Payment failed. Update your payment method to keep your plan." | "Current period ends {date}" |
   | `canceled` | "Canceled" (muted) | "Your plan is ending." | "Access ends {date}" |
   | `trialing` | "Trial" (attention) | "Up to 3 parents or guardians per athlete." | "Trial ends {date}" |
   | anything else | "Active" (accent) | "Up to 3 parents or guardians per athlete." | "Renews {date}" |

   Below the card:
   - On the US storefront (§6.8): the primary button "Manage your team plan at gradus.training", hint "Opens in your browser". **[code wins]** It opens through the **signed-in web handoff** (`POST /auth/web-session` with `next=/parent/team`, then the one-time URL in the external browser) so the parent lands signed in. It falls back to the plain `manageUrl`.
   - Elsewhere: the text "Manage your team plan on the web." with no link.
   - Never a price, never a purchase (A10, iOS §6.8).

   States: loading "Checking your plan…"; error "Couldn't load your plan" with "Try again".
2. **Guardians section** (`TeamGuardiansSection`, `showsManageLink = false` because the plan card already has the link). Pull to refresh reloads both the plan and the guardians.

**Guardians section states**
- List not loaded with a load error: "Couldn't load guardians" with "Try again".
- Loading: placeholder card "Loading guardians…".
- **Gate** (`TeamPlanEntitlementGate.decide(planActive, isPayer, isUS)`, from the guardian list's own fields, never from `/parent/team`):
  - **Locked** (`planActive == false`), card `TeamPlanEntitlementNote`:
    - eyebrow "Guardians";
    - text "A team lets up to 3 parents or guardians share an athlete.";
    - secondary "I have an invite code" (ticket icon), which opens the invite-code sheet;
    - the manage line, but only when `showsManage` is true. On Team plan it is false, so there is no duplicate. On the US storefront it is the button "Manage your team plan at gradus.training", which opens the plain URL, default `https://gradus.training/parent/team`, replaced by `manageUrl` once loaded. Elsewhere it is "Manage your team plan on the web."
  - **Unlocked** (`planActive`), with `canManage = isPayer`:
    - eyebrow "Guardians", plus "{n} to sync" when queued guardian writes exist;
    - when not the payer: "You're covered by the primary parent's plan. They manage billing.";
    - no athletes: card "No athletes yet.";
    - one card per athlete (below);
    - `ErrorLine`;
    - if `model.canManage` (`planActive && isPayer && primaryAthletes` is not empty): secondary "Add a guardian" (person-add icon), disabled while saving.

**Athlete card**
- Title: the full name. On the right, in mono: "{used} of 3 seats", where `used` = guardians + pending invites. Expired invites still take a seat.
- **Guardian rows**: the name, then a role line: "Primary" or "Guardian", with " · You" appended for the caller's own row. A destructive "Remove" chip (trash icon, content description "Remove {name} as guardian") appears only when `canManage && athlete.isPrimary && role == co`. Primary rows are never removable.
- **Invite rows** (the server populates `invites` only where the caller is primary): the email, or "Invite" when there is none, wrapping to 2 lines; an "Expired" tag (orange) when `expiresAt` is in the past by the injected clock; then "Pending · {code}" in mono. When `athlete.isPrimary`:
  - "Resend" chip, only when the invite has an email; content description "Re-send guardian invite for {email}";
  - destructive "Revoke" chip; content description "Revoke guardian invite for {email}", or "Revoke guardian invite" with no email.

**Confirmation dialogs**
- Remove: title "Remove {name}?", message "They lose access to {athleteFirst}'s plans, sessions, and messages. You can invite them again later.", buttons "Remove {name}" (destructive) / "Keep".
- Revoke: title "Revoke this invite?", message "The code stops working. You can send a new invite any time.", buttons "Revoke" (destructive) / "Keep it".

**Writes** (`TeamGuardiansModel`):

| Action | Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
