| Create invite `POST /parent/team/guardians/invites` `{athleteId,email?}` [idem] | **online-only** | Client checks: the athlete must be one of the caller's primary athletes ("Pick one of your athletes."). The email is trimmed and lowercased; blank means nil. When present it must pass `looksLikeEmail`: one "@", non-empty local part, a "." in the domain not at either end, no whitespace, at most 160 characters. Otherwise "Enter a valid email address." On success the invite is added to the list optimistically with `expiresAt` = now + 30 days, persisted, the toast "Invite created" shows, and the list reloads. The seat-cap 409 and the `plan_required` 403 are shown verbatim and never as a purchase prompt. |
| Resend `POST …/invites/{id}/resend` (no body) | queued | With no email on file it is refused client-side with "This invite has no email on file — share the code instead." and never queued. An expired invite gets `expiresAt` extended locally by 30 days, matching what the server does (D2). Toast "Invite re-sent". |
| Revoke `DELETE …/invites/{id}` | queued | The row is removed immediately. A 404 restores it and shows the message. Toast "Invite revoked". |
| Remove guardian `DELETE /parent/team/guardians/{id}` | **online-only** | Only `co` rows. On success: remove the row (or, if `isSelf`, the whole athlete from the caller's list), persist, show "Guardian removed", reload. |

**Add a guardian** (`ConnectGuardianSheet`). A bottom sheet titled "Add a guardian" with a top-start action "Cancel", which becomes "Done" after the invite is created. The sheet can't be dismissed while saving.
- **Form**:
  - text "Invite another parent or guardian to share {first}'s plans, sessions, and messages. Up to 3 guardians per athlete." ("your athlete" when unknown);
  - "Athlete": a dropdown (`ExposedDropdownMenuBox`) when the parent is primary for more than one athlete, otherwise the full name as static text;
  - "Their email (optional)", placeholder "coparent@email.com", email keyboard, no autocapitalization, no autocorrect, IME action Done (submits when valid);
  - caption "With an email we send them the link. Without one, share the code yourself.";
  - `ErrorLine`;
  - primary "Create invite" ("Creating…").
- **Code panel** (after success; success haptic; the panel cross-fades in unless reduce-motion is on):
  - card with eyebrow "Share this code with them" and the code, large, bold mono, tracking 4, selectable, spelled out for TalkBack;
  - caption "They enter it under Team plan, or open the link." when no email was given, otherwise "We emailed them the link. You can share it again here.";
  - "Share link", which opens the Sharesheet with the message "Join me as a guardian for {fullName} on Gradus with code {code}" and the URL `https://gradus.training/team/{token}`;
  - "Copy" chip, which copies the **code** and shows "Code copied";
  - secondary "Done".

  **The token only ever travels inside the share intent's URL.** It is never rendered as text, logged, toasted, cached or written to an outbox label.

**"I have an invite code" sheet.** A bottom sheet with a top-start "Cancel" holding `TeamInviteContent(token = null)` (§7.7.11). When the invite is accepted, the sheet closes and the screen reloads the guardians, the plan and the parent settings, then calls `onLinksChanged`.

#### 7.7.10 Guardian claim flow (`/g/<token>`)

Source: `Claim/GuardianClaimModel.swift`, `GuardianClaimFlow.swift`. This is a step-by-step port of the web's `g.$token.tsx`, and **every step is online-only**. A merge deletes the pending athlete row and a claim can change the caller's role, so none of it can be replayed later unseen.

**Steps:** `checking → failed(msg) | invalid(msg) | alreadyClaimed(summary) | live(summary) | done(outcome)`.

Load sequence:
1. Offline: `failed("You're offline. Try again when you're back online.")` without leaving the device.
2. `POST /guardian/claim/summary {token}`. If `alreadyClaimed`, stop there.
3. `GET /guardian/claim/context`, best effort; a failure hides the "Signed in as" line.
4. For guardian invites only, `POST /guardian/claim/merge-options`, best effort; a failure hides the merge card.
5. For a **known parent** on a guardian invite, `ParentVerificationRepository.status()`. If `isNeeded`, show the verify step (§6.13 A1–A2).
6. Step becomes `live`.

Classification follows `APIError.isRetryable` (`status >= 500 || status == 429 || status == 0`): status 0, 429 or 5xx gives `failed` ("Couldn't check this link" + "Try again"); any other 4xx gives `invalid`.

**Screen** (the paper background; the top bar shows "Guardian claim" and **never** the token; content is centered):

| Step | Content |
|---|---|
| checking | Placeholder card "Checking your link…" |
| failed | State "Couldn't check this link" with the message and "Try again" |
| invalid | State with a link icon, title "This link is no longer valid", message `GuardianClaimCopy.invalidMessage(server)`, action "Go to Gradus". What it does depends on the host: on the Settings back stack it pops the screen; in the no-role host it clears `pendingLinkRoute` (as `dismissParentLink()` does) so the role chooser shows. iOS calls `dismiss()` there, which is a no-op at the root of the no-role `NavigationStack`; Android does not copy that dead end. One test per host. `invalidMessage` drops a leading "This link is no longer valid." from the server message when more text follows, which usually leaves "Ask the coach to resend it." Otherwise the message is shown verbatim. |
| alreadyClaimed | State with a sealed-check icon, title "You're already set up". Message for a guardian invite: "{athleteName} is linked to a parent account. Sign in to see their plans."; for an athlete invite: "{athleteName}'s account is already set up. Sign in to see your plans." Action: "Switch account" when the host supports it, else "Go to Gradus". |
| live | The form (below) |
| done | State "You're all set". Message for a claim or merge: "{first} is on your account. Their plans, lessons and coach messages are in Plans."; for a self-claim: "Your account is set up. Your plans, lessons and coach messages are in Plans." |

**Live form**, in order:
1. Eyebrow "Welcome to Gradus".
2. Title, as a heading: "Follow {athleteName}" for a guardian invite, "Set up your account" for an athlete invite.
3. Subtitle:
   - guardian invite with a coach name: "Coach {coach} added {first} to Gradus. Claim your parent account to see their plans, lessons and coach messages."
   - guardian invite without a coach name: "{first} started training on Gradus. Claim your parent account to see their plans, lessons and coach messages."
   - athlete invite: "Coach {coach} added you to their schedule. Set up your account to see your plans, lessons and coach messages.", or "You've been added to a coach's schedule. Set up …" without a coach name.
4. Known parent with a name: caption "Signed in as {parentName}." with an underlined "Switch account" link, disabled while submitting.
5. **Merge card** (guardian invite with options):
   - "Is this someone you already have on Gradus?";
   - one secondary button per visible option: "Yes, same athlete — {name}". Visible options are the `exact` and `close` ranks; `other` ranks appear after the switch "Show my other athletes" is on, and the switch appears only when `other` options exist;
   - caption "Or keep them separate by continuing below."
6. **Name fields** (guardian invite, caller has no parent profile): "Your first name" and "Your last name" (placeholders "First name"/"Last name"; name autofill hints).
7. **Birthdate** (athlete invite, or `needsBirthdate`): `BirthdateField`, labelled "Your date of birth" or "{first}'s date of birth". Help: "We use this to confirm you can manage your own account." or "We use this to set the right privacy protections for your athlete."
8. **Direct notice** (guardian invites only, #40): `DirectNotice(athleteName = first, consentAct = true)`. It ends "By continuing, you give your consent for {first} on those terms."
9. **Verify step** (when `needsVerification`): the compact `ParentVerificationStep` (§6.13). The claim completes only after the verification webhook lands (iOS PRD §7.1 "Guardian claim"). The `/verified` App Link (§6.10) never navigates: `completeVerification` runs in the background (it also works signed out), toasts "Thanks, you're verified." or, on failure, the error toast "That verification link couldn't be confirmed. Check your email for a newer one, or resend it from the app." (a thrown error shows its `userMessage`), then signals the open verification step (`verificationSignals.noteCompleted()`) and refreshes `/me` if signed in. `GuardianClaimScreen` stays on top; when the step re-checks and reports verified, `verificationFinished()` re-runs the claim automatically (`AppModel.completeVerification`, `GuardianClaimModel.verificationFinished`). Test: with the claim screen open, firing `gradus://verified?…` runs the claim once and lands on Plans.
10. `ErrorLine` with `actionError`.
11. When the last refusal was `wrong_role` (a coach account, or an athlete under 18): secondary button "Sign out", which runs the switch-account path.
12. Primary button: "Claim {first}'s account" for a guardian invite, "Set up my account" for an athlete invite. It shows "Setting up…" while submitting and is disabled unless the step is `live`, nothing is submitting, no verification is pending, and the birthdate is set when one is required.

**Submit**
- **Athlete-addressed invite:** `POST /guardian/claim/self {token, birthdate}`, outcome `selfClaimedAdult`. The server enforces 18+ and shows its own message for under-18.
- **Guardian invite:** `POST /guardian/claim {token, firstName?, lastName?, birthdate?}`, outcome `claimedAsGuardian`. Names are sent only when **both** are non-blank; the birthdate only when picked.
- **Merge:** tapping an option opens the dialog "Merge into {name}?" with the message "The coach's new entry for {first} is folded into {name}'s existing profile on your account. This can't be undone." and the buttons "Merge" / "Cancel". It sends `POST /guardian/claim/merge {token, athleteId}`, outcome `merged`.
- **`parent_unverified`** (403) on a guardian invite, when verification has not already completed this session: show the verify step instead of an error (the claim already created the parent profile that the KWS email is bound to).
  - When the step finishes with `verified == true`, the claim re-runs through the same path as a button tap, including the haptic and `onFinished`.
  - When it finishes for any other reason, show "We couldn't confirm your verification. Try the link in your email again, or come back in a moment." Never loop.
  - A second refusal after a completed verification is an ordinary error.
- Any other error: `ErrorLine` plus an error toast with the server's message. `wrong_role` sets the Sign out flag.
- Success: success haptic, then `onFinished(outcome)` (§7.7.19).

**Switch account** (the web's `/login?redirect=`):
1. sign out. On Android this step also calls `CredentialManager.clearCredentialState(ClearCredentialStateRequest())`, and the next Google sign-in request sets `setAutoSelectEnabled(false)` and `setFilterByAuthorizedAccounts(false)`, so the account chooser always appears (A5, §6.4). Otherwise Credential Manager could silently sign the same wrong account back in and loop on `wrong_role`. Test: after Switch account, the Google sheet shows the account chooser and does not sign back in by itself;
2. store `GuardianClaim(token)` as the pending route;
3. show sign-in;
4. after sign-in, return to the same link.

**Profile-less signed-in account** (`NoRoleView`): `/g/` and `/team/` routes are held in `pendingLinkRoute` and rendered in the no-role host, because the claim creates the parent profile.
- First, wait for the device age-signal answer: "Checking this device…".
- If the device age signal blocks adult roles (§6.13 B1; Play Age Signals on Android), render the shared `AdultRolesBlockedScreen` (title "Coach and parent accounts are for adults", `AgeSignals.adultRolesBlockedTitle`) in signed-in mode with no parent-code action. Its athlete action clears `pendingLinkRoute` (`dismissParentLink()`) and the athlete-only role chooser shows. A top-app-bar action "Sign out" (test tag `ageSignal.signOut`) signs out. The claim and team-invite screens are never composed in this state (`RoleTabsView.swift` NoRole branch; QA.md: the link "shows the same block with Sign out").
- Accounts that already have a profile are never re-gated (§6.13 B1 rules).

**Route identity.** A second `/g/` link must build fresh state, not reuse the first link's (an iOS I13 bug fixed with `.id(route)`). Android keys the ViewModel on the token (`hiltViewModel(key = "claim:$token")`). Navigation is the type-safe route `GuardianClaim(token: String)`.

#### 7.7.11 Team invite (`/team/<token>` and code entry)

Source: `Claim/TeamInviteModel.swift`, `TeamInviteView.swift`. **Online-only**: the claim creates a parent profile and a guardian link, and the outcome decides the next screen (seat cap, expiry, "already the primary parent").

**Steps:** `enterCode → checking → failed(msg) | invalid | found(preview) → done`.
- A token (blank counts as none) opens directly into `checking`.
- A pre-filled complete code also opens directly into `checking`.
- Otherwise the screen starts at `enterCode`.
- The preview is `POST /team-invites/preview` with `{token}` or `{code}`. `found == false` (unknown, expired, revoked or claimed) means `invalid`; that is the only path to `invalid`. Every preview error, 4xx included, gives `failed` with the error's `userMessage` and "Try again" (`TeamInviteModel.swift` L114–116), unlike the claim flow's 4xx → `invalid`.

| Step | Content |
|---|---|
| enterCode | A header with a people icon on a 48 dp accent disc at 15%; title "Enter your invite code"; subtitle "Enter the code another parent shared to join their athlete." Field "Invite code", placeholder "ABCD2345", bold mono, normalized, character caps, ASCII keyboard, IME action Go. The field is auto-focused on appear. Lookup runs when the 8th character lands or on "Continue" (primary, disabled until the code is complete). |
| checking | Placeholder card "Checking your invite…" |
| failed | "Couldn't check this invite" with the message and "Try again" |
| invalid | Icon `person.2.slash` (Android `PersonOff`), title "This invite isn't valid", message "It may have expired or already been used. Ask them to send a new one." For code entry only, the action "Try a different code" empties the field and returns to `enterCode`. |
| found | Title "{inviterName or "Another parent"} invited you"; subtitle "Join as a parent or guardian for {athleteName or "their athlete"} on Gradus."; `ErrorLine`; primary "Accept invite" ("Joining…"); for code entry only, secondary "Use a different code". |
| done | "You're in" with "You've been added as a guardian." |

Accept sends `POST /team-invites/claim` with `{token}` or `{code}` [idem]. On success: the toast "You've been added as a guardian." (success), the success haptic, then `onFinished(.joined(athleteId))`. Refusals, such as accepting your own invite ("You're already the primary parent for this athlete."), expiry and the seat cap, are shown verbatim in `ErrorLine` and a toast. Route identity is keyed on the token, as in §7.7.10. The top bar title is "Team invite".

#### 7.7.12 Coach visibility: the parent's per-coach toggles

Source: `Visibility/ParentCoachVisibilityModel.swift`, `CoachVisibilityToggleRow.swift`, `CoachVisibilityCopy.swift` (a line-for-line port of the web's `coach-visibility-toggles.tsx`).

**When the row shows.** `planActive` (from `GET /parent/coach-visibility`, which includes co-guardian coverage) **and** the athlete has more than one coach. One coach has nobody to connect with. Gate on this list's `planActive` only, never on `GET /parent/team`.

**Row**
- A `Switch` labelled `toggleTitle`: "Let {coachFirst} see {athleteFirst}'s other coaches". Only first names are used, because these lines get long. It is disabled while that `athleteId:coachId` key has a write in flight.
- While loading with no data: "Checking sharing…".
- Status line under the switch:
  - with no pairs, `statusLabel`:
    - off: "Off";
    - on with no pairs: "On — add another coach to connect";
    - otherwise the counts joined by " · ": "{n} accepted", "{n} pending", "{n} declined", in that order and only the non-zero ones.
  - with pairs: a row of **pair moons**, one per pair, each a 30 dp disc with a 20 dp cream center and the other coach's first two initials in bold mono:

    | Fill | Rule | Disc |
    |---|---|---|
    | full | both accepted | accent |
    | half | exactly one side accepted | divider disc with an accent half rotated 90° |
    | empty | neither accepted | divider |
    | declined | either side declined (beats half) | destructive |

    Tapping a moon shows a tooltip with `pairLabel`, which is also its content description.

`pairLabel(coach, pair)` has six branches and uses first names:

| Branch | Text |
|---|---|
| this coach declined | "{me} declined connecting with {them}" |
| other coach declined | "{them} declined connecting with {me}" |
| both accepted | "Connected with {them}" |
| this coach accepted | "{me} accepted — waiting on {them}" |
| other coach accepted | "Waiting on {me} to accept" |
| neither | "Waiting on {me} and {them} to accept" |

The switch's on/off change animates at 200 ms ease-out unless reduce-motion is on.

**Toggle ON** sends the request immediately. **Toggle OFF** first confirms:
- title "Turn off sharing for {coachFirst}?";
- message "{coach} stops seeing {athlete}'s other coaches, and {athlete}'s other coaches' connections with {coach} are removed too. You can turn it back on any time — both coaches would have to accept again.";
- buttons "Turn off sharing" (destructive) / "Keep sharing".

**Write.** `PUT /parent/coach-visibility {athleteId, coachId, enabled}` [idem], **queued**, outbox label "Coach visibility · {athlete full name}".
- Optimistic change, exactly as the web does it: `enabled` flips, status becomes `waiting` (on) or `off`, pairs are cleared.
- Live success: the toast "Request sent to your coaches." (on) or "Sharing turned off." (off), then a reload, because the server rebuilt the pairs.
- A 4xx (for example 403 `plan_required`) reverts and shows the message; it is never queued.
- A no-op when the coach is already in the requested state and not busy.
- Unknown coach: "That coach isn't connected to this athlete." with no write.
- After any coach link or unlink, `invalidate()` clears the etag and reloads.

#### 7.7.13 Coach visibility: the coach's side

Source: `Visibility/MyCoachVisibilityModel.swift`, `CoachVisibilityScreen.swift`, `CoachVisibilityRequestsCard.swift`, and `FeatureRoster/AthleteDetailView.swift` `alsoCoachedBy`. **Coaches never start a request.** The parent turns sharing on.

**Data.** `GET /coach/visibility/mine` returns three buckets:
- `pending`: waiting on me; my side pending and theirs not declined;
- `connected`: both accepted;
- `awaiting`: I accepted and theirs is pending.

Non-coaches get empty buckets, never an error.

**Coach Visibility screen** (page title "Coach visibility"):
- description `sheetDescription`: "A parent asked to connect you with another coach. If you both accept, you can each see the other's plans, practice log, goals, and schedule for that shared athlete — view only.";
- "{n} to sync" when there are queued writes;
- `ErrorLine` for `actionError`.

States: loading "Loading…"; error "Couldn't load coach visibility" with "Try again"; empty card "No shared athletes yet." / "When a parent on the Team plan turns sharing on for an athlete you both coach, the request shows up here."

- **Requests** card (eyebrow "Requests"): for each link, the bold coach name, "for {athlete}", then the prominent chip "Accept" (with a progress indicator while busy) and the chip "Decline".
- **Connections** card (eyebrow "Connections"): `connected`, then `awaiting`. Each row shows the bold name, a "Pending" tag (orange) for `awaiting`, "for {athlete}", and a destructive "Turn off" chip. "Turn off" opens the dialog:
  - title "Turn off sharing with {otherFirst}?";
  - message "You and {otherFirst} stop seeing each other's plans, practice log, goals, and schedule for {athlete}. The parent can turn it back on, and you would both have to accept again.";
  - buttons "Turn off" (destructive) / "Keep sharing".

**Writes** (queued, `Idempotency-Key`, optimistic bucket moves, revert on 4xx, `etag = null` after queuing). The success haptic plays on Accept and on Turn off.

| Action | Call | Optimistic move | Toast | Outbox label |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Accept | `POST /coach/visibility/{id}/respond {accept:true}` | to `connected` when `theirStatus == accepted`, else to `awaiting` | "Connected." | "Accept coach visibility · {athlete}" |
| Decline | `POST /coach/visibility/{id}/respond {accept:false}` | removed from every bucket | "Declined." | "Decline coach visibility · {athlete}" |
| Turn off | `DELETE /coach/visibility/{id}` (a soft decline of my side) | removed | "Turned off." | "Turn off coach visibility · {athlete}" |

An unknown id gives "Visibility request not found."

**Roster banner** (`CoachVisibilityRequestsBanner`). A capsule on the popover surface with a divider stroke, at the top of the Roster:
- an eye icon on an accent disc;
- the bold line "{n} coach visibility request" or "… requests";
- the caption "A PARENT WANTS TO CONNECT YOU" in caps mono with tracking 1;
- a dismiss control with content description "Dismiss".

It shows **once per pending-id set**. The signature is the sorted pending ids joined by ",", stored in `gradus.coachVisibilitySeen`:
- Dismissing records the set; the dismissal animates 200 ms unless reduce-motion is on.
- Tapping the banner opens the Coach visibility screen in a bottom sheet with "Close". The set is recorded **when the sheet closes**, not when it opens: the iOS bug was that the presenter was torn down on tap. If the host pushes a screen instead, the set is recorded on tap.
- A new request changes the signature and brings the banner back.
- The Settings row still shows the badge.

**Settings row state** (`CoachVisibilitySettingsRowState`), shown in the Connections hub "Families" card:
- title "Coach visibility", eye icon;
- badge = the pending count, shown only when greater than 0;
- sub-label: "{n} request(s) waiting" when there are pending requests, else "{n} connected coach(es)" counting connected plus awaiting, else "Shared athletes with other coaches".

The Settings › Coaching › "Connections" row shows the same sub-label and badge.

**Roster athlete detail ("Also coached by")**. §7.2 owns the section; this section owns its chips:
- Each other coach's card carries the state tag: `Pending` / `Accepted` / `Declined` from `coachVisibility[coachId]`, tennis pen when accepted, else orange.
- When there is no link and the plans are locked, a lock icon with content description "Plans locked".
- The `CoachVisibilityLinkChips` for that link (`CoachVisibilityScreen.swift`, I13 "the athlete detail's 'Also coached by' rows carry Accept / Decline / Turn off"), rendered next to the Pending/Accepted/Declined tag, with the same writes, dialog and test tags as the Requests and Connections cards:
  - bucket `pending`: a prominent chip "Accept" (a progress indicator replaces the label while busy; success haptic on success; test tag `coachVisibility.accept.{linkId}`) and a chip "Decline" (`coachVisibility.decline.{linkId}`);
  - bucket `connected` or `awaiting`: a destructive chip "Turn off" (`coachVisibility.turnOff.{linkId}`), which opens the "Turn off sharing with {otherFirst}?" dialog quoted above; its "Turn off" button is `coachVisibility.confirmTurnOff.{linkId}` (success haptic), "Keep sharing" cancels;
  - the link is found by athlete id plus a whitespace- and case-insensitive match on the other coach's **name**, because the wire carries no coach id;
  - when the athlete has exactly one link, the name is not needed;
  - nothing renders when there is no link.
- Caption when needed: "Reading another coach's plans needs the Club plan, or a visibility link the parent turns on."
- The coach's effective tier (`GET /coach/billing` `effectiveTier`) is read fresh at each gate check and never cached. When it can't be read, the coach is treated as not entitled.

#### 7.7.14 Connections hub (coach)

Source: `Connections/ConnectionsHubView.swift`, `ConnectionsHubModel.swift`, `JoinClubSheet.swift`, `JoinClubModel.swift`, `FeatureOnboarding/Components/{ShareInviteCard,InviteCodeEntryCard}.swift` (redesigned 2026-09-24 at Mariah's request, gradus-ios PR #68). The screen has the top bar title "Connections" and three cards of rows, each row with an icon on a disc, a bold title, a one-line detail and a chevron. The actual work happens in bottom sheets. Activating the screen, pull to refresh and foreground all do the same thing: load the coach's code **and** re-read `GET /coach/billing`, which is never cached (§6.8).

- **Connect** (eyebrow "Connect"):
  - row "Invite a parent or athlete" / "Share a link or code" (share icon);
  - row "Enter their code" / "They're already on Gradus" (key icon);
  - caption "Parents and adult athletes enter your code, or open your link, to connect to you."
- **Club** (eyebrow "Club"):
  - when billing `entitlement == clubCovered`: a read-only row with the organization name (or "Club plan"), "Your club covers your subscription." and a "Club" tag (tennis);
  - otherwise the row "Join a club" / "Enter your club's code and your plan switches to club-covered".
- **Families** (eyebrow "Families"): the Coach visibility row (§7.7.13), which pushes `CoachVisibilityScreen`.

The row content description reads "{title}. {detail}", with ", {badge}" appended when there is a badge.

**"Invite a parent or athlete" sheet** (title as named, subtitle "Share a link or code.", "Done"; partially expandable). `ShareInviteCard`:
- eyebrow "Your invite code", then the code (large bold mono, tracking 4, selectable, spelled out), then "gradus.training/i/{code}";
- "Share", which opens the Sharesheet with the message "Join me on Gradus with code {code}" and the URL `https://gradus.training/i/{code}`;
- the chip "Copy code", which shows the toast "Code copied";
- on error: `ErrorLine` plus a "Try again" chip;
- "Rotate code" (disabled until a code loads) opens the dialog "Replace your invite code?" / "Links and codes you already shared stop working." with "Rotate" (destructive) / "Keep it". Success toast: "New invite code. Old links no longer work."

This card is the same component as the Roster's "Add an athlete" invite hub (§7.2). Test-tag prefixes: `invite` on Roster, `connections.share` here.

**"Enter their code" sheet** (subtitle "They're already on Gradus.", "Done"). `InviteCodeEntryCard`:
- text "A parent's or an adult athlete's code. You'll be linked to everyone under it.";
- field "Their code" (placeholder "ABCD2345");
- the claimed-confirmation line in accent ink;
- `ErrorLine`;
- primary "Link" ("Linking…"), enabled for a complete code.

The hub's claim is **online-only** and **resolves before claiming** (`POST /invites/resolve`):

| Resolved kind | Result |
|---|---|
| coach | "That's another coach's invite code — you can't add it to your roster." |
| athlete | "That's a new-athlete signup code, not a roster invite." |
| parent or adult athlete, invalid | "That code isn't valid." |
| guardian or unknown | "That code isn't valid." |
| parent or adult athlete, valid | Claim (`/invites/parent/claim` or `/invites/adult-athlete/claim`), toast the server's confirmation text, then `onLinksChanged`. |

A 409 `roster_full` maps to the fixed sentence "Your roster is full on your current plan." (§6.8 rule 2). Offline is refused before the resolve call.

**Join a club sheet** (title "Join a club", "Cancel"; can't be dismissed while joining):
- **Search step:**
  - text "Find your club, enter the invite code they gave you, and your plan switches to club-covered.";
  - field "Search for your club" (placeholder "Search by name or city", word caps, no autocorrect), debounced 250 ms. An empty query loads `GET /orgs/popular`; otherwise `POST /orgs/search`.
  - states: a progress indicator; an error line; empty results show "Start typing your club's name." (empty query) or "No matches. Your club may not be on Gradus yet.";
  - eyebrow "Popular clubs" or "Matches", then org rows with the bold name and "{city}, {region}";
  - text button "Club isn't on Gradus — continue as individual". It sends `POST /orgs/lead {source: notListed, typedQuery?}` fire-and-forget (never shows an error), toasts "Thanks — we'll reach out to "{query}"." or "Thanks — we'll be in touch." when the query is empty, and dismisses.
- **Picked step:**
  - the org-name tag (tennis) and a "Change" link that resets the selection, the code and the query;
  - field "Club invite code" (placeholder "DENVER01"), normalized by `OrgCodeText`: A–Z and **0–9**, uppercase, at most 8. This is permissive by design, not `InviteCodeText`.
  - When the code reaches 8 characters it is verified automatically with `POST /orgs/verify-code`:
    - checking: a progress indicator;
    - ok: "Code confirmed for {name}" in accent ink;
    - mismatch: "That code isn't for {org}. Double-check with your club coordinator.";
    - inactive: "This club isn't active yet.";
    - unknown or thrown: "We don't recognize that code."
  - When the coach has a paid individual plan (`entitlement == paid && subscriptionTier != null && subscriptionStatus != "canceled"`), the note: "Your individual billing plan will be canceled automatically. Monthly plans stop renewing at the end of the current cycle; annual plans get a prorated refund for unused months."
  - `ErrorLine`.
  - Primary "Join {org}" ("Joining…"), enabled only after the code verifies. With a paid plan it first confirms: "Join {org} and cancel your plan?" with the note as the message, buttons "Join and cancel my plan" (destructive) / "Not now".
- **Join** is `POST /orgs/join {code, environment}` [fresh key], **online-only**. `environment` is the coach profile's `subscriptionEnvironment`, defaulting to `"live"`. On success: a toast that depends on the outcome, then re-read billing, call `onLinksChanged`, and dismiss.

  | Outcome | Toast |
  |---|---|
  | noChange | "Joined {name}." |
  | alreadyJoined | "You're already on {name}." |
  | canceledImmediately with a refund | "Joined {name} — refunded {amount with 2 decimals} {CUR} for the unused months." |
  | canceledImmediately, no refund | "Joined {name} — your annual plan was canceled." |
  | canceledAtPeriodEnd | "Joined {name} — your Coach plan won't renew." |
  | trialCanceled | "Joined {name} — your trial was ended." |

  A server `ok:false` shows the server's text.

#### 7.7.15 Athlete side: guardian email card, provisional and paused cards, coaches

**Guardian email card** (`GuardianEmail/GuardianEmailModel.swift`, `GuardianEmailCard.swift`; iOS PRD §7.8 "Parent or guardian"; the web's `GuardianRow`). It is mounted on the athlete's Settings › Profile screen through the slot described in §7.7.1. The card is seeded from `GET /athlete/settings` (`birthdate`, `guardianEmail`, `guardianInvitedAt`, `guardianClaimed`), then refined by `GET /guardian/status`. A status for a different `athleteId` is ignored, and a failed status call keeps the seed.

`isMinor` takes the server's `status.isMinor` when present. Otherwise it is computed from the birthdate, and **a missing birthdate counts as a minor** (D8).

**Mode**

| Condition | Mode |
|---|---|
| `claimed` | read-only, whatever the age |
| not claimed, not a minor | hidden |
| not claimed, minor | editable (whether invited or not) |

- **Read-only card:** shield-check icon, eyebrow "Parent or guardian", "On Gradus", and the email if there is one.
- **Editable card:**
  - eyebrow "Parent or guardian", with a "Queued" tag (pool) while a resend for this athlete is in the outbox;
  - helper text, either "Because you're under 18, we keep a parent or guardian email on file and send them a link to follow along." (never invited) or "We emailed them a link to follow along. They haven't joined yet — check the address or send it again." (invited);
  - field "Parent or guardian email" (placeholder "parent@example.com", email keyboard, no autocapitalization, no autocorrect, IME action Send);
  - invited line: "Invited just now" (under 60 s) or "Invited {MMM d, yyyy}";
  - `ErrorLine`;
  - primary button: "Save & send invite" when the draft differs from the saved email or nothing is on file, otherwise "Re-send invite"; "Sending…" while sending.

**Draft rules:**
- clamped to 160 characters as typed; normalized by trimming, lowercasing and clamping;
- valid only with no spaces, a non-empty local part before "@", and a domain containing "." not at either end;
- an invalid draft never reaches the server: "Enter a valid email address.";
- a dirty draft survives a status load and a settings reseed;
- a reseed or status update is ignored while a write is pending or saving, except that `claimed = true` always wins.

**Write.** `POST /guardian/invites/{athleteId}/resend {guardianEmail}` saves the address and sends the invite. It is **queued**, outbox label "Parent or guardian invite". Optimistic change: the saved email and `invitedAt = now`.
- Live success: take the returned address, then toast "Guardian email updated" when the address changed, else "Invite re-sent".
- A 4xx rolls back. The rate limit is shown through `userMessage`.
- **409** means the guardian joined meanwhile: reload the status, run the host's settings refresh, and switch the card to read-only.

**Provisional and paused cards** on the same Profile screen (§6.13 A4, B4):
- **"Waiting for your parent"** (hourglass, attention ink): "Your goals and plans are yours now. Connecting a coach and messaging open once a parent or guardian confirms your account from the email we sent them. Accounts nobody confirms are removed after three months."
- **"Your account is paused"**: the text chosen by `pausedVia` per §6.13 B4 (`app_store` → the iOS sentence "A parent or guardian withdrew consent for Gradus through Apple, so messaging and connecting with coaches are off for now. Your goals and plans are still here. Questions: support@gradussports.com."; `google_play` → the Google Play variant; missing → the generic sentence).

**Athlete Coaches screen** (`Athlete/AthleteCoachesView.swift`; Settings › Coaching › "Coaches", value = count; route `settings/coaches`). Every write needs a connection.
- States: load error "Couldn't load your coaches" with "Try again"; loading "Loading your coaches…"; empty "No coaches linked yet."
- Each coach card: the name as a title, sport tags (pool pen) or "No sports set", and the chips "Edit sports" and "Unlink" (destructive).
- When `canConnectCoach` is false, a note replaces the add button: "Add a parent or guardian email first, then you can add a coach." if `needsGuardianEmail`, else "Ask your parent to add coaches from their settings." Otherwise the primary button "Add a coach".
- Unlink dialog: "Unlink {coach}?" / "They lose access to your plans and sessions. Goals and lessons tied to them are removed. You can link them again later with their code." with "Unlink" (destructive) / "Keep coach".
- **Edit sports** (title "Edit sports"): "Sports you do with {coach}", chips, "Keep at least one sport." when none is selected; Save is enabled when the selection is non-empty and changed.
- **Add a coach** (title "Add a coach"):
  - text "Enter the code your coach shared. You'll see who it belongs to before anything is linked."; field "Coach invite code";
  - automatic lookup at 8 characters, cancelled when the code changes, showing "Looking up your coach…";
  - on failure, the announced error, defaulting to "That invite code isn't valid. Double-check with the coach.";
  - found card "Coach {name}" with "Which sports will you work on together?" and chips; a single sport is pre-selected;
  - "Link coach" ("Linking…").
  - The code is pre-filled from `pendingInviteCode` (§7.7.19).
- **Writes** (`Athlete/AthleteSettingsModel.swift` `coachPreview` / `linkCoach` / `unlinkCoach` / `setCoachSports`). Every one runs through `online { }`: offline it fails before any network call with "You're offline. Try again when you're back online." and queues nothing.

  | Action | Call | Client check | On success |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Preview | `POST /adult-athlete/coach/preview {code}` | complete code | shows the found card |
  | Link | `POST /adult-athlete/coach/link {code,sports}` [idem, fresh key per tap] | "Pick at least one sport." | reload the coach list; toast "Coach linked" (success); then `onLinksChanged` |
  | Unlink | `DELETE /adult-athlete/coaches/{id}` | — | drop the coach and every goal whose `primaryCoachId` is that coach ("Goals stamped with that coach go with the link, as on the server"); persist; toast "Coach unlinked" (success); then `onLinksChanged` |
  | Sports | `PUT /adult-athlete/coaches/{id}/sports {sports}` | "Pick at least one sport." | toast "Sports updated" (success) |

  A server error shows its `userMessage` in the `ErrorLine` and as an error toast. §7.8 owns the rest of the athlete settings.

#### 7.7.16 Connection celebration

Source: `Celebration/CelebrationModel.swift`, `CelebrationCover.swift`, `CelebrationCopy.swift`, `CelebrationDismissalStore.swift`, `AppModel.refreshCelebrations/linksChanged`. iOS PRD §7.13 and the README I13 note: "Reduce Motion drops the confetti and zoom".

**When it refreshes.** Only when the shell calls `refresh()`, and only with a session and an outbox:
1. after `/me` loads;
2. on app foreground;
3. after any link-creating or link-removing call succeeds (`onLinksChanged`: invite-code claims in the Connections hub, a signed-in coach's automatic `/i/<code>` claim (§7.7.19), link or unlink a coach (parent or adult athlete), roster add or remove, guardian claim, team invite, club join);
4. whenever the `settings/connections` route is opened by any means (FCM push, App Link, `gradus://settings/connections`) while signed in. This runs the full `onLinksChanged` (`AppModel.open(_:)` L1401–1404), not just a celebration refresh.

`onLinksChanged` (`AppModel.linksChanged`) does, in order: refresh celebrations; for a coach, reload `MyCoachVisibilityModel`; for a parent, `invalidate()` the parent visibility overview (etag cleared, reload); for a parent or athlete, reload the runner plans if the Plans tab has been visited this session.

It never polls and never runs on a timer or on scroll. `GET /me/celebrations` answers `role: null, groups: []` for minors and role-less accounts. Concurrent refreshes are allowed; only the newest answer applies. A failed refresh shows nothing and keeps the groups already loaded.

**What shows.** `current` is the first group none of whose `linkIds` is in the per-user dismissed set. The signed-in role-tabs scaffold presents `CelebrationCover` over **every tab** whenever `current != null`. Only that scaffold hosts it (`RootView.swift`, the final `RoleTabsView` branch): the cover never appears over onboarding gates, the age-signal wait, the under-18 athlete-only role chooser, Plan setup (`PlanStatusView`), the parent-approval screen (§6.13 B2), the no-role host or sign-in. `refreshCelebrations` also requires a session and an outbox (`AppModel.swift` L869–871). Groups that arrive during those phases show once the tabs scaffold mounts. The biometric lock (§6.11; iOS `LockWindow.swift`) draws above the cover. Prompts that nobody asked for (wrap-up alerts and similar) are held while a celebration is up or its check is in flight (`PromptHold.celebrating`, §7.13).

**Cover** (full-screen `Dialog`, `usePlatformDefaultWidth = false`, drawn edge to edge, content inside the safe-drawing insets):
- **Background:** paper, plus the watermark at **8% opacity**. iOS bundles no poster yet, so it draws the brand shape:
  - an accent capsule 1.4 × width by 56 dp, rotated −12°, centered at (0.5 w, 0.22 h);
  - a pool capsule 1.2 w by 40 dp, rotated −12°, at (0.55 w, 0.31 h);
  - a foreground ring 0.9 w across with a 10 dp stroke at (0.85 w, 0.78 h);
  - an orange capsule 1.1 w by 32 dp, rotated −12°, at (0.4 w, 0.86 h).

  It is clipped, not a touch target, and hidden from TalkBack. A bundled poster, if one is ever added, would be inverted in dark mode.
- **Card:** max width 400 dp, horizontal padding 20 dp, vertical padding 24 dp, centered vertically when it fits and scrollable when it doesn't (WCAG 1.4.4/1.4.10). Contents:
  - a 56 dp accent disc at 20% fill with a 30% stroke and a party-popper icon (Material `Celebration`), hidden from TalkBack;
  - the title in display black, as a heading;
  - the subtitle;
  - the CTAs;
  - the text button "Maybe later": caption size, medium weight, `textTertiary`, full width, minimum touch target (test tag `celebration.later`);
  - a top-end close button: a 32 dp circle filled with the popover surface, a 1 dp divider stroke, an `xmark`-equivalent `Icons.Default.Close` at footnote size, bold, `textSecondary`, 6 dp from the corner, padded to the 48 dp touch target, content description "Close".
- **Copy** (`CelebrationCopy`):

  | Role | Title | Subtitle | CTAs |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | coach | "You're connected with {who}!" | "Take a moment to get set up — pick a next step below." | "View schedule" (secondary, calendar icon) → Roster tab; "Assign first plan" (primary, clipboard icon) → Plans tab |
  | parent, adult athlete, or null | "You're connected with {otherName}!" ("your coach" when blank) | "Say hi so they know you're here." | "Say hello" (primary, speech-bubble icon) → the room `roomId` when non-empty, else the Messages tab |

  For the coach, `{who}` is `formatCoachTitle(athleteNames, otherName)`. Blank names are dropped first. Then: 0 names → `otherName`, or "your new athlete" when that is blank; 1 → "Ava"; 2 → "Ava & Ben"; 3 or more → "Ava, Ben & Cara".

  CTAs sit in an adaptive row (10 dp spacing), stacked when they don't fit. Each CTA button is vertical: the icon (title3 size, semibold) above the label (footnote, bold), 4 dp apart.
- **Every way out acks the group:** a CTA, "Maybe later", Close, **and system back or predictive back** (proposed A29). On iOS a `fullScreenCover` has no swipe-to-dismiss on purpose; Android must not offer a dismissal that doesn't ack. The first tap wins; later taps are ignored, so the same ack is never queued twice. A CTA starts the ack (launched, not awaited) and routes in the same tap (`CelebrationCover.swift` L37–38).
- **Motion:**
  - On appear: the success haptic, and the card fades in over 200 ms ease-out while scaling from 0.95 to 1.
  - Unless reduce-motion is on, a **confetti burst** plays once along the top 160 dp of the card (clipped, not a touch target, hidden from TalkBack): 18 pieces, each a 6×8 dp rounded rectangle (radius 1 dp) filled with the **accent token** (tennis in light, pool in dark). Each piece has:
    - x: random 0–1 × width;
    - start delay: random 0.02–0.2 s;
    - fall duration: random 1.2–2.1 s;
    - start rotation: random 0–360°.

    Each piece holds at y = −20 dp with opacity 0 for its delay, then falls linearly to y = 180 dp while rotating +540°. Opacity goes 0 → 1 over the first 10% of the fall and back to 0 over the remaining 90%. The geometry is fixed once per mount, so recomposition never reshuffles it. Draw it with a `Canvas` and one `Animatable` time base.
  - **Reduce motion** (`ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE == 0`): `ConfettiBurst` is not composed at all (the screenshot test asserts no confetti node) and the scale is skipped; the opacity animation remains, as on iOS. Under scale 0 Compose snaps `animate*`/`Animatable` to their end values, so the fade may be instant; that is accepted. The haptic stays. `rememberReduceMotion()` reads the setting through a `ContentObserver` on `Settings.Global.getUriFor(ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE)`, so a change applies without a relaunch. Scales other than 0 (0.5×, 1×, …) are not reduce-motion.
  - When the next group comes up, the cover swaps in place with fresh confetti and a fresh haptic. The last group stays latched on screen while the dismissal animates.

**Ack.** `POST /me/celebrations/{firstLinkId}/ack {linkIds: [all]}`, so sibling links collapse into one ack exactly as the web sends them. It is **queued** (outbox label "Connection with {otherName}") and shows **no** "Saved — it syncs…" toast.
- Before sending: add the group's link ids to the dismissed set, persist the set, and remove the group.
- A 4xx restores both and shows the message, unless a refresh has already relisted the group (no duplicate).
- A 5xx or transport error queues the ack under the same key.
- Without an outbox, the ack fails with the offline message and the group stays.
- After every successful refresh, dismissed ids the server no longer lists are pruned, so the file never grows past the pending set.

#### 7.7.17 Entitlement notes (US-only, display-only)

These follow iOS §6.8 and A10:
- There is no price, no "Subscribe" or "Upgrade" wording, and no purchase flow anywhere in this section.
- Every Team-plan control is gated on the guardian or visibility list's **own** `planActive` / `isPayer`, which include co-guardian coverage. These values are read fresh on every activate and foreground and never cached as an entitlement, so a lapsed plan loses its controls immediately (`TeamTests`, `VisibilityTests`).
- `GET /parent/team` feeds **only** the plan card and the manage link.
- The manage link is a tappable button only on the US storefront (§6.8 `StorefrontRepository.isUSStorefront` (A13) together with the `androidExternalLinksEnabled` kill switch (A37; default true, on in 1.0), decided there for Google Play's US external-link rules). Everywhere else it is plain text with no link and no instructions.
- Server refusals such as `plan_required` ("Start the Team plan to …") are shown verbatim as errors, never as a call to action.
- The coach's "Also coached by" and club states use `effectiveTier` and `entitlement`, read fresh.

#### 7.7.18 Offline and online-only matrix

This matrix follows gradus-ios `docs/README.md` (Guardians I13 and I14) and the model code.

| Action | Mode | Outbox label (never a token) |
|---|---|---|
| Guardian claim, merge, self-claim | **Online-only** | — |
| Team invite create | **Online-only** | — |
| Team invite claim (link or code) | **Online-only** | — |
| Remove guardian | **Online-only** | — |
| Visibility toggle (parent) | Queued, `Idempotency-Key` | "Coach visibility · {athlete}" |
| Respond (accept or decline) | Queued | "Accept coach visibility · {athlete}" / "Decline coach visibility · {athlete}" |
| Disconnect (turn off) | Queued | "Turn off coach visibility · {athlete}" |
| Revoke team invite | Queued | "Revoke invite for {first}" |
| Team invite resend | Queued | "Re-send invite for {first}" |
| Guardian email resend (athlete) | Queued | "Parent or guardian invite" |
| Celebration ack | Queued (no toast) | "Connection with {otherName}" |
| Parent name | Queued | "Your name" |
| Athlete identity | Queued | "{first}'s details" |
| Goals (Settings or Goals tab) | Queued | "{first}'s goals" / "Goals · {athleteName} · {sport}" |
| Coach sports | Queued | "{coach}'s sports for {first}" |
| Primary coach | Queued | "Primary coach for {first}" |
| Schedule | Queued | "{first}'s lessons with {coach}" |
| Add athlete, remove athlete, coach preview, link coach, unlink coach, pause or resume messaging, reset password | **Online-only** | — |
| Pending-claims list, claim summary, team preview, celebrations list | Online reads (no cache) | — |
| Connections hub: code load and rotate, resolve and claim, club search, verify, join | **Online-only** (join uses a fresh key); the lead is fire-and-forget | — |
| Athlete coaches: preview, link, unlink, sports | **Online-only** | — |

Every queued write uses `entityKind = "settings"`.

Cached reads available offline: parent settings, team guardians, both visibility lists, and the celebration dismissals. The Sync Center screen is not shipped (iOS §7.12, removed 2026-09-12). The in-screen "{n} to sync", "Syncing" and "Queued" indicators **are** shipped.

#### 7.7.19 Deep links, pushes and routing

- **App Links and `gradus://`** (§6.10; A2 App Links in place of universal links):

  | Link | Route | Notes |
  |---|---|---|
  | `https://gradus.training/g/<token>`, `gradus://g/<token>` | `GuardianClaim(token)` | `requiresSession` |
  | `https://gradus.training/team/<token>`, `gradus://team/<token>` | `TeamInvite(token)` | `requiresSession` |

  When signed out, the route waits in `pendingRoute`. While it is a `/g/` or `/team/` route (`pendingLinkNeedsSignIn`), the Sign-in screen shows a full-width banner above its content: "Use the email address this link was sent to." (subheadline, `textSecondary`, popover surface, 10 dp vertical and 20 dp horizontal padding; test tag `signIn.linkHint`; `RootView.swift` L125–135). It applies to every A5 method (Google, email and password, Apple web flow) and disappears once the route is consumed. When signed in without a profile, the route goes to the no-role host (§7.7.10). When signed in with a role, it is pushed on the Settings back stack. The top bar never shows the token.
- **Settings sections** (`gradus://settings/<section>`, `https://gradus.training/{parent,coach,athlete}/settings/<section>`, push `settings/<section>`): `athletes`, `plan`, `goals`, `coaches`, `connections`.
  Destinations by role (`RoleTabsView.swift` `SettingsSectionView`). A wrong-role section renders `GradusStateView` with the title "Not for this account", icon `person.crop.circle.badge.questionmark` (Material `PersonSearch` / a question-badge person icon), and the message below:

  | Section | Parent | Coach | Athlete | Unavailable message |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `plan` | Team plan | Coach plan (§7.11) | unavailable | "Plans are managed by your coach or parent." |
  | `athletes` | My athletes | unavailable | unavailable | "My athletes is a parent screen." |
  | `coaches` | unavailable | unavailable | Athlete Coaches (§7.7.15) | "Coaches is an athlete screen. Parents link coaches from My athletes." |
  | `goals` | standalone Goals screen | unavailable | standalone Goals screen | "Goals belong to parents and athletes." |
  | `connections` | Team plan | Connections hub | unavailable | "Connections are managed by your coach or parent." |

  `settings/goals` opens a standalone `GoalsScreen` with the same dashboard as the Plans tab's Goals segment (§7.7.7). For a coach, before the outbox (local store) exists, `connections` shows a placeholder titled "Connections" (link icon) with "Preparing your local store…". A route to a tab the account does not have shows the toast "That page isn't available for your account." and does not navigate (`AppModel.swift` L1466).
- **Push `settings/connections`** ("Guardian or coach connection accepted", sent by the server over FCM, §6.6) opens the same destination. Opening the `settings/connections` route by any means (push, App Link, `gradus://`) while signed in also runs `onLinksChanged` (§7.7.16 trigger 4).
- **`/i/<code>`** (`AppModel.openInvite`, `claimInviteAsCoach`; §7.1 owns signed-out invite entry):

  | Situation | Behavior |
  |---|---|
  | Code incomplete (`InviteCodeText.isComplete` false) | error toast "That invite code isn't valid." and nothing else |
  | Signed in as a parent or athlete, onboarding finished | parent: `settings/athletes`; athlete: `settings/coaches`; the code is stored in `pendingInviteCode`; toast "Link the coach from here with their code." The next Link sheet or Add-a-coach sheet pre-fills the code and clears it. |
  | Parent or athlete mid-onboarding, or a coach with `onboardingComplete == false` | stored in the pending sign-up; toast "Invite noted. It links when you finish setting up." |
  | Org admin or no role | toast "Invite codes are for coach, parent, and athlete accounts." |
  | Signed-in coach, onboarding complete | claims automatically, online: first as a parent invite (`POST /invites/parent/claim`, `Idempotency-Key` `{attempt}-parent`), and if that fails, as an adult-athlete invite (`POST /invites/adult-athlete/claim`, key `{attempt}-adult`). Success toasts "Linked to the parent's account" or "Linked to the athlete's account" (success), each followed by `onLinksChanged`. If both fail: the second error's `userMessage`, else "Couldn't claim that invite." (error toast). |
- **After a guardian claim finishes:**
  1. clear `pendingLinkRoute`;
  2. refresh `/me` (the role may have changed);
  3. load the role's settings (parent or athlete);
  4. run `linksChanged()`;
  5. reload pending claims;
  6. clear the Settings back stack;
  7. open the **Plans** tab (the web lands on `/parent/plans` or `/athlete/plans`).
- **After a team invite is accepted:**
  1. clear `pendingLinkRoute`;
  2. refresh `/me`;
  3. if the role is parent, load the parent settings and the team guardians;
  4. run `linksChanged()`;
  5. open **Settings › Team plan** (`settings/plan`).
- **Analytics** (§6.12): the claim and team-invite screens count toward area `onboarding`, screens `guardianClaim` and `teamInvite`. Settings sections count as `settings.{section}`. Only ids are sent, never content.
- **Wear OS** (A3, §7.15): no guardian, team or visibility surfaces on the watch. **Widgets:** none.

#### 7.7.20 Tests (ports of the iOS suites; JUnit 5 + Turbine on ViewModels with fake repositories; Compose UI and screenshot tests for the screens)

Port every iOS test below by name. Fakes mirror `PreviewGuardianRepositories` and use the same seeds: Ingrid (parent), co-guardian Anders, Greta, Tobias, "Gretta Halvorsen" for close-rank merge, Dana, Renata (coach), the Denver FSC club code `DENVER01`, and coach code `COACHAAA`. The server messages are copied verbatim from that file.

| Suite | Test cases to port |
|---|---|
| `ClaimTests` | The live invite loads the form, context and ranked merge options. Birthdate gates the CTA. A spent link shows already-claimed and fetches nothing else. An unknown token is invalid with the trimmed sentence. A transport failure is retryable. Offline never leaves the device. An athlete invite skips merge options and uses adult copy. A known parent sends the birthdate and no names. A claimer without a profile sends the names. Merge folds the athlete. An adult self-claims. A minor's self-claim is refused and the form stays. A coach account gets `wrong_role` plus Sign out. Offline claims are refused and nothing is queued. Nothing submits outside `live`. The invalid-message trim. Guardian copy branches on the coach name. |
| `TeamInviteTests` (in `ClaimTests`) | A live link previews and accepts. An expired link is invalid with no retry. Accepting your own invite is refused. Offline: the preview waits and accept is refused. A preview transport failure is retryable. Code step: lookup, accept by code. A pre-filled code is normalized and previewed. A wrong code can be retried. A blank token falls back to code entry. |
| `ClaimVerificationTests` | Known unverified parent: the step comes before the button; once verified, the claim runs by itself. A step that finishes without verification doesn't re-run. `parent_unverified` opens the step. Verified parent, adult invite, or no repository: no step. |
| `PendingClaimsTests` | Lists, and a claimed athlete drops off on reload. A failed load keeps what was shown. |

#### 7.7.21 Android decisions proposed here, and open questions

Proposed (each one is an Android-native adaptation under A2; none changes product behavior; listed in §0 Table 1 as A29–A36):
- **A29.** On the celebration cover, system back and predictive back behave as "Maybe later": the group is acked and the cover closes. Android has no back-free cover equivalent, and a dismissal without an ack would contradict iOS's "nothing to dismiss without acking".
- **A30.** "Code copied" shows as a toast only on API ≤ 32. On Android 13+ the system's clipboard confirmation stands in for it, following Android's own guidance against duplicate copy feedback.
- **A31.** Share intents put the iOS `ShareLink` message and the URL in one `EXTRA_TEXT`, as "{message} {url}".
- **A32.** Compose `testTag`s reuse the iOS accessibility identifier strings exactly (`guardianClaim.submit`, `teamGuardians.add`, `celebration.later`, …), so the QA scripts and the test matrix carry over. The root scaffold, every `Dialog` and `ModalBottomSheet` root, and the celebration cover set `Modifier.semantics { testTagsAsResourceId = true }`, so tags such as `guardianClaim.submit` appear as resource-ids to UiAutomator, Maestro and adb-driven scripts (Compose tags are otherwise visible only to Compose tests).
- **A33.** "Reduce Motion" is read as `ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE == 0` through one shared helper. Foreground refresh is `ProcessLifecycleOwner` `ON_START`.
- **A34.** The per-user snapshot caches are JSON files in `noBackupFilesDir/Gradus/<userId>/` (§6.5), excluded from backup. The coach-visibility "seen" signature is device-wide in DataStore and survives sign-out, matching iOS `UserDefaults.standard`.
- **A35.** `ParentSettingsViewModel` gets the same load-sequence guard as the guardian list models (§7.7.2). iOS `ParentSettingsModel.load()` has none; this is a hardening with no user-visible change, recorded so the parity review doesn't flag it.
- **A36.** Athlete invite codes and guardian team-invite codes are copied with `ClipDescription.EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE` on API 33+ (§7.7.2 platform mapping), so the system clipboard preview hides them. No copy changes.

Formerly open questions, now settled elsewhere:
1. **Paused-athlete copy names Apple.** Settled by §6.13 B4: the server adds an optional `pausedVia` (S-11), each client words the pause by its source, and a Play revocation pauses an account only through the imported revoked-`installId` list (A20). Remaining fallback wording: §12 N71.
2. **US storefront source on Android**: settled by A13 (Play Billing `getBillingConfigAsync().countryCode == "US"`, unknown → no link) together with the `androidExternalLinksEnabled` kill switch (A37; default true, on in 1.0).
3. **Age-signal gate for a profile-less account opening `/g/` or `/team/`**: settled by §6.13 B1 (tighten-only; `blocksAdultRoles` = band under 18; wait on "Checking this device…" until the store answers).

### 7.8 Athlete — goals and motivation

iOS §7.8 (and the parent half of the same dashboard, §7.7 "Goals dashboard"); implementation `FeatureSessions/Goals/{GoalsSource,GoalsModel,GoalsDashboardView,GoalCardParts}.swift`. The Goals segment lives on the Plans tab for parents and athletes (`RunnerPlansScreen`), shown when the graph provides a goals source (`segmentIsHiddenWithoutAGoalsSource`). This section specifies the whole dashboard once; §7.7 references it for parents.

| Feature | iOS requirement | Android requirement | Pri |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plans / Goals tabs | Native segments on the Plans tab | Same | P0 |
| Motivation card | "What motivates you?" ≤ 500 chars, inline edit | Same | P0 |
| Goal editor (self) | Current level and season goal, athlete of any age (Mariah 2026-09-16), via `PUT /adult-athlete/goals` | Same endpoint (its RLS is ownership-only) | P0 |
| Long-term goal | Editable by the athlete, ≤ 280 chars | Same | P0 |
| Parent editing | Primary parent edits level, season goal and long-term goal from the card; co-guardians read-only (`guardianRole`) | Same (§7.7 references this) | P0 |
| Own plans, voice → own plan, seeded library, adopt a shared plan | #35, #48 | §6.14 | P0 / P1 |
| Coaches, parent or guardian | Settings surfaces | §7.12 / §7.7 | P0 / P1 |

#### 7.8.1 Data

| Read / write | Endpoint | Body |
|---|---|---|
| Athlete dashboard | `GET /athlete/goals` | `{athleteId, athleteName, motivation, sports:[ParentGoalSport]}` |
| Parent dashboard | `GET /parent/goals` | `[{athleteId, athleteName, sports, guardianRole}]` |
| Motivation | `PUT /athlete/goals/motivation` | `{"motivation": text}` |
| Long-term goal (athlete) | `PUT /athlete/goals/long-term` | `{"sport", "longTermGoal"}` |
| Level and season goal (athlete) | `PUT /adult-athlete/goals` | `{"sport","currentLevelKey","seasonGoalKey","longTermGoal"}` (long-term goal sent unchanged) |
| Parent edit (primary only; 404 for a co-guardian) | `PUT /parent/athletes/{id}/goals` | same four fields |

`ParentGoalSport`: `sport`, `currentLevelKey`, `seasonGoalKey`, `longTermGoal`, `primaryCoachId?`, `hoursAtCurrent?`, `hoursAtGoal?`, `loggedHoursPerWeek` (4-week trailing average), `sessionsCount`, `firstSessionAt?`. `canEditGoals = guardianRole != "co"` (missing means primary). Level labels and order come from the bundled sport catalog (`coach-sports.json`, the same file iOS vendors; §5.1 owns the export), `SportCatalog.sport(key).levels` with optional `hint`.

**Caching.** None, as on iOS: the dashboard loads from the network when the Goals segment is selected, on foreground while it is showing, and on pull to refresh; a failed load keeps the last dashboard in memory and reports the error (`aFailedLoadCachesNothing`). **Writes** are online-first with the outbox fallback (same method, path, body and key; `entityKind` "settings"; labels "What motivates you", "Goal · *Sport*", "Goals · *Athlete* · *Sport*", "Long-term goal · *Sport*"), toast "Saved — it syncs when you're back online."; the card updates locally in both cases.

#### 7.8.2 Dashboard layout

- Loading: two redacted cards "Loading goals…"; error before any load: "Couldn't load goals" + "Try again".
- **Athlete:** the motivation card, then one sport goal card per sport; no sports → empty card "No goals set yet." (dashed, italic).
- **Parent:** per athlete with sports: athlete name (heading), a co-guardian note "*First*'s primary parent sets these goals.", then the cards; all empty → "No goals yet. Add them in Settings → Athletes."

#### 7.8.3 Motivation card

Eyebrow "What motivates you?" with a **pen** icon button (no word; content description "Edit motivation"; handoff "Goals: pens for edit"). Its inline editor keeps "Cancel" and "Save": it is an inline mini-form (§8.6.2). Empty: italic "Tap edit to share what drives you…"; set: the text in curly quotes, italic display font. Editing: field "What gets you to practice on the hard days?" (3–6 lines), hard-capped at 500 characters while typing, counter "*n*/500", "Cancel" and "Save" ("Saving…"); inline error line on failure. Save trims; unchanged = no request; > 500 → "Keep it under 500 characters." (`motivationOver500CharactersIsRefused`).

#### 7.8.4 Sport goal card (matched to the web's `SportGoalCard`, Mariah 2026-09-24)

1. Eyebrow "Working toward", a **pen** icon button (content description "Edit goal") when editable, and the sport tag (pool pen).
2. Season goal level (heading). The "Currently *Level* · *n* levels to go" line is **gone** (`ad1e9bf`): the level ladder below shows it.
3. **Level ladder**: the catalog levels from one below the lower of current/goal to one above the higher, clamped; current dot filled, goal dot outlined with a halo; uppercase labels. When `LocalIsAccessibilitySize` (§8.1; iOS `isAccessibilitySize`) is true it becomes a vertical list with "Current" / "Goal" tags. One TalkBack node: "Levels: *A*; *B*, current level; *C*, season goal; …". Hidden when a key is unknown.
4. Divider, eyebrow "This month's average practice"; the **practice ring** (96 dp, 128 dp when `LocalIsAccessibilitySize`). It now shows **percent of the weekly target** (design direction 2026-10-12: "show percent to target and list the target"; `PracticeRing(targetLower:)`).
- **With a band:** the arc = min(1, logged hours / the **bottom** of the coach's band), and the centre is "*n*%" (display, Bold, tabular). TalkBack: "*n* percent of a *lower* hour weekly target; *h.h* hours logged".
- **Without a band:** the old ring, unchanged: arc = logged / 112 waking hours, centre "*n.n*" + "HR / WK", TalkBack "*n.n* hours per week logged; no target set yet".
- The ring is tinted by status.
- **Beside it:** the status pill and "Target **2–4 hr/wk**" (the word "band" is dropped; or "4 hr/wk", or "Not yet set"). The sessions line "4-week trailing average · *n* session(s) logged" is **gone** (`ad1e9bf`).
   **Number formatting** (`GoalsModel.hours`, `bandText`, `sessionsLine`; `Locale.US`): hour values are whole numbers without a decimal ("6") and otherwise one decimal ("4.5"). The ring center always shows one decimal (`decimals: 1`: "0.0", "6.0"), and so does the ring's TalkBack "logged" value, while its target uses the plain rule ("of a 4 hour target"). The band is "*min*–*max* hr/wk" with an en dash (U+2013), or "*n* hr/wk" when min == max. The no-band ring total is `wakingHoursPerWeek = 16 × 7 = 112`. The sessions line is "4-week trailing average · 1 session logged" / "… · *n* sessions logged" (0 → "0 sessions logged"). Test vectors: 6.0 → "6"; 4.5 → "4.5"; ring 0 → "0.0"; band (2, 4) → "2–4 hr/wk"; band (4, 4) → "4 hr/wk".
5. Long-term goal (shown when set or editable): eyebrow "Long-term goal" + a **pen** icon button (content description "Edit long-term goal"); empty "Add your long-term goal…"; else the quote.

**Status** (`GoalStatus.compute`, injected clock; shared vectors with the web's `computeStatus`): band = `min…max` of `hoursAtCurrent` / `hoursAtGoal` (either alone is a single value); no band → "Not yet set"; no sessions → "Building up"; below the band and the first session < 28 days ago (or unknown) → "Building up"; below → "Behind"; above → "Over target"; else "On track". Pill pens: building pool, on track tennis, behind orange, over pink, unset pool. Ring tints: building `secondaryAccent`, on track `accent`, behind `attention`, over `destructiveInk`, unset `textDisabled`. Colour is never the only signal (the pill names the status).

#### 7.8.5 Edit sheets

| Sheet | Who | Title | Content | Save rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SeasonGoalSheet` | athlete | "Working toward" | sport label; menus "Current level" and "Target for this season" ("Pick a level", then "*Label* · *hint*"); "Pick both levels to save." when either is empty | both set; unchanged = no request |
| `LongTermGoalSheet` | athlete | "Long-term goal" | sport label; field "What are you working toward long-term?" (2–5 lines), cap 280 with counter "*n*/280" | trimmed; > 280 → "Keep it under 280 characters." |
| `ParentGoalsSheet` | primary parent | "*First*'s goals" | "Where *First* is now in *Sport*, and where you'd like them to be by the end of the season."; the two level menus; "Long-term goal (optional)" field "Where would you like them to be in a few years?" with "*n*/280" | both levels set; long-term > 280 → "Keep the long-term goal under 280 characters."; unchanged = no request |

All three are full-height `ModalBottomSheet`s with a `GradusSheetHeader`: "Close" at the start and "Save" ("Saving…") at the end (`ad1e9bf`). Their level menus are `GradusPickerField`s, dashed while empty. Each sheet has an inline error line, and the error cleared on open. A parent's athlete-side writes are refused locally ("Parents edit each athlete's goals from their goal card.") and an athlete's parent-side write is refused ("Only a parent edits goals this way.") (`parentSourceRefusesTheAthleteSideWrites`).

#### 7.8.6 Tests (port of `GoalsModelTests`)

Ladder spans one level either side; band text and ring total (112 h fallback); athlete and parent dashboards load; failed load caches nothing; motivation trims and calls the source, > 500 refused; long-term goal updates the sport; level/season goal updates; offline goal, motivation and parent-goal writes queue the same body; status rule mirrors the web for each branch (vectors) and uses the injected clock; segment hidden without a goals source; parent source refuses athlete writes; parent goal save updates the card and calls `PUT /parent/athletes/{id}/goals`; only the primary parent can edit (`guardianRole == "co"` read-only). Screenshot tests of the card in each status, with and without a ladder, at 100% and 200% font scale.

### 7.9 Resources and Ask Gradus

**Release flag (#22, iOS #63).** `ReleaseFlags.ASK_GRADUS_ENABLED = false` is a **compile-time `const val`** in `:core:data` (not remote config, not a build flavor): flipping it is a code change and a new build, so what ships is what was tested (`ReleaseFlags.swift`). With it off, **no role** sees Ask Gradus or Saved, whatever the server's `canAskGradus` says; Safe Sport stays for athletes. The server endpoints stay live. Analytics for area `ask` cannot fire while hidden. Everything Ask-related below is built, tested with the flag forced on in tests, and shipped dark. (Note: Mariah also hid the web Ask Gradus tab via Lovable, which contradicts #22's "the web keeps it"; unresolved, handoff-2026-10-04 §7, handoff-remaining-prd §2.1. Android is unaffected: hidden either way.)

**Library rights (#23).** The rights filter is **server-side and applies to every app client**: `GET /api/v1/resources` passes `storeSafeOnly`, so curated rows appear only when `resources.rights ∈ {gradus, licensed}` (`src/lib/resources.server.ts`, `STORE_SAFE_RIGHTS`); `pending` rows never reach the app. Android must not add its own filter or show any rights value. Note: since web #159 (2026-09-27) The Assist's documents are marked `licensed` and therefore **do** show in the app library, contradicting #23's "come out of the iOS 1.0 library"; the code/data state wins and Android shows exactly what the endpoint returns (open item in handoff-2026-10-04 §7, "Content rights in the listing"). The Safe Sport hotline panel stays regardless.

**Minors (handoff-I12-onward §2.2).** Athletes under 18 or with no birthdate never reach Ask Gradus or Saved: server-enforced (`resolveAskGradusAudience`) and mirrored client-side via `canAskGradus` (fails closed while loading).

An uncached file offline shows the failure state. File the matching iOS fix; if Mariah wants strict parity instead, §12 N68. Test: a cached PDF opens with the network fake failing every call. | P1 |
| Coach upload ("Add a resource") | `UploadResourceSheet.swift`, see 7.9.2. | See 7.9.2. | P1 |
| Report a resource | `ResourceReportSheet.swift`: parent/athlete only (`canReport = role != coach`); title `"Report <title>"`; reasons (single choice, default harassment): `Harassment or bullying`, `Inappropriate or sexual content`, `Spam or scam`, `Safety concern about a minor`, `Something else`; section headers "What's wrong", "Note (optional)" with placeholder `"Anything else we should know?"`; footer `"Reports go to the Gradus safety team."`; Cancel / **Send report**; success toast `"Report sent"`; `POST /api/v1/safety/reports` with `resourceId`, `targetUserId = null`, `alsoBlock = false`. | Same copy and payload; a full-screen dialog with a radio-button list (`selectableGroup`, `Role.RadioButton`), multi-line `OutlinedTextField` (2–6 lines), errors inline and announced. Wire values `harassment, inappropriate, spam, minor_safety, other`. | P1 |
| Safe Sport panel | `SafeSportView.swift` / `SafeSportPanel` / `SafeSportHotlines` / `ReportToGradusCard` / `SafetyExitButton.swift`; athlete Resources segment and Settings → Safe Sport. | See 7.9.3. **P0** (safety). | P0 |
| Ask Gradus (hidden in 1.0) | `AskGradusView.swift`, `AskAnswerContent.swift`. | See 7.9.4. | P1, dark |
| Grounded answers and sources (hidden) | iOS §7.9 row, `AskAnswerContent.swift`. | See 7.9.4. | P1, dark |
| Saved answers (hidden) | `SavedAnswersListView.swift`. | See 7.9.5. | P1, dark |
| Markdown rendering | `MarkdownText.swift`. | See 7.9.6. | P1 |

Endpoints (Appendix A "Resources and Ask Gradus"): `GET /resources` (role-tagged object `{role, coach, parent, athlete}` with exactly one non-null payload; not a discriminated union), `POST /resources/{id}/signed-url`, `POST /coach/resources`, `POST /coach/resources/upload-url`, `DELETE /coach/resources/{id}`, `POST /ask` (10 per 60 s, server-enforced), `GET|POST /saved-answers`, `DELETE /saved-answers/{id}`, `POST /safety/reports`. A missing payload for the tagged role is a decoding error (`malformed_response`), not a crash.

Offline rules (`ResourcesModel.swift`, iOS §6.5 "works with queueing"): resource delete, save answer and delete saved answer are **online-first with outbox fallback** (queue when offline or on transport/5xx; toast `"Saved — it syncs when you're back online."`; without an outbox `"You're offline. Try again when you're back online."`); a 4xx refusal leaves state unchanged and toasts the server's message; if enqueueing itself fails, error toast `"Couldn't save the change."` and the outcome is failed. Delete order (`ResourcesModel.deleteOwnResource`): perform live-or-queue **first**; only when the outcome is not failed is the row removed from the feed, the cache persisted, and the success toast `"Resource deleted"` shown. A queued delete therefore shows both `"Saved — it syncs when you're back online."` and `"Resource deleted"`. Create/upload resource and ask are **online-only, never queued** (`"You're offline. Connect to add a resource."`, `"You're offline. Connect to upload a resource."`, `"You're offline. Ask Gradus needs a connection."`). Pending queued resource writes show the `"N to sync"` badge in the header.

#### 7.9.2 Add a resource (coach)

From `UploadResourceSheet.swift`, presented from "Add resource". Android: full-screen dialog with top app bar **Cancel** / **Add** (`"Adding…"` while uploading, disabled).

- **Entitlement gate** (iOS §6.8: shown, never sold): `canUpload` false → no form; text `"Coach Pro or Club unlocks uploading resources."`; on the **US storefront** a button `"Manage your plan at gradus.training"` opening `https://gradus.training/coach/paywall` signed in through the web-handoff (§6.8) in the external browser; elsewhere `"Manage your plan on the web."` with no link. iOS: `isUSStorefront = await Storefront.current?.countryCode == "USA"` (StoreKit). Android source: Play Billing Library `BillingClient.getBillingConfigAsync()` → `BillingConfig.countryCode == "US"` (the billing library is linked with **no purchase flow**); if the billing client is unavailable or errors, the answer is **not US** and no link shows (A13: never assume US, as iOS treats a nil storefront). The same `StorefrontRepository` is defined once in §6.8 and reused here, and the link also needs the `androidExternalLinksEnabled` kill switch on (A37; default true). The pure gate `decide(canUpload, isUSStorefront)` (`canUpload ? unlocked : locked(showsLink = isUSStorefront)`) stays identical with its tests. Play's US external-link rules apply (§6.8). No price, no purchase button, ever.
- **Type**: segmented `PDF` / `Image` / `Link` (default PDF); changing it clears a picked file. Note under it: `"Images and videos are added by link, from a public web address, not from your device. For a video, choose Link and paste its YouTube or Vimeo address."`
- **Title** (placeholder `"e.g. Serve technique breakdown"`), **Description (optional)** (`"What is this for?"`, 3–6 lines).
- **PDF**: "File" → `"Choose a PDF"` button (shows the picked file name) opening the **Storage Access Framework** picker (`ActivityResultContracts.OpenDocument(arrayOf("application/pdf"))`; iOS `.fileImporter`). Read bytes via `ContentResolver`; name via `OpenableColumns.DISPLAY_NAME`. Errors `"Couldn't access that file."` / `"Couldn't read that file."`. Never the photo picker.
- **Image**: `"Image URL (https)"`, placeholder `"https://…/photo.jpg"`, hint `"A direct link to a JPG, PNG, GIF, or WebP that opens without signing in."` **Link**: `"URL (https)"`, `"https://…"`. URL keyboard, no autocorrect/autocapitalize.
- **Sports (tag one or more)**: chips from the coach's own sports in their order (checkmark when on); none → `"Add sports in Settings first."`
- **Validation** (in this order): `"Add a title"`, `"Tag at least one sport"`, then `"Add a URL"` (image/link) or `"Choose a file"` (PDF).
- **Submit**: link/image → `POST /coach/resources` (`kind` link or image, `externalUrl`); PDF → `POST /coach/resources/upload-url {ext:"pdf", contentType:"application/pdf"}` → upload bytes to Supabase Storage bucket **`resource-pdfs`** with `uploadToSignedUrl(path, token)` via **supabase-kt Storage** (apikey header only; the signed token is the credential, not the user's bearer token; `upsert = false`) (`ResourceUploadStorage.swift`) → `POST /coach/resources` with `storagePath`. Each create carries a fresh `Idempotency-Key`. Success: append to "Your uploads", toast `"Resource added"`, dismiss. Upload failure: `APIError(status = 0, code = "upload_failed", message = "Couldn't upload the file. Please try again.")` (`ResourceUploadStorage.swift`), shown inline; transport failure → offline error. "Uploading…" with a progress indicator while in flight.

Tests (port `UploadResourceSheetTests.swift`): Pro/Club unlocks regardless of storefront; below, only US gets the link; no sports → empty state; checklist keeps the coach's order; image asks for a URL, only PDF asks for a file. Plus `ResourcesModelTests.swift`: cache then network; link and upload land in the feed; image needs no upload; delete online and queued offline; refusal keeps the row; ask offline refusal; `ask_gradus_unavailable` shows its plain message; saved answers load/save online/save queued/delete.

Shown as the athlete's **Safe Sport** Resources segment (inline under the "Resources" title) and as **Settings → Safe Sport** (owned by §7.12; same composable). Content and copy are pinned to the web's `safe-sport-panel.tsx` via iOS `SafeSportContent` and must be identical:

You don't have to decide what it is — that's their job."` and these seven items verbatim, in order (`SafeSportContent.countsItems`):

   2. `"Comments about your body, weight, or what you eat that feel off."`
