- **Delete account** (`Account/DeleteAccountFlow.swift`; iOS §6.4). Full-screen dialog "Delete account" with "Cancel" (disabled while deleting; back/predictive back also disabled while busy).
  1. Heading "Delete your account?" and three paragraphs, verbatim: "This is immediate and can't be undone. Your profile, email, and sign-in are removed, any active subscription is cancelled, and your voice notes and uploads are deleted." / "Conversations, plans, and invoices other people were part of stay readable for them, with your name replaced and your message content removed." / "If you're a parent, athletes with another guardian on the account transfer to them. An athlete with no other guardian and no sign-in of their own is deleted along with their plans and practice log."
  2. Impact: `GET /me/deletion-impact` → `[{id, firstName, guardianEmail?}]`. While loading: "Checking who this affects…"; error (including offline: "You're offline. Try again when you're back online.") with chip "Try again"; when minors are listed, a card: "These athletes are under 18 and sign in themselves. You're the only adult on their account, so choose what happens next." and per minor the first name + segmented "Keep" / "Delete" (default Keep; TalkBack label for the control "What happens to {firstName}'s account"; the impact retry chip's test tag is `deleteAccount.retryImpact`) with the line "Keep sending copies to {guardianEmail ?? "my email"} — {name} keeps their account and an adult stays on file." or "Delete {name}'s account too — their sign-in, plans and practice log are removed."
  3. Field "Type DELETE ACCOUNT to confirm" (placeholder "DELETE ACCOUNT", all-caps keyboard, no autocorrect). Match = trimmed, uppercased equals `DELETE ACCOUNT`.
  4. Offline line "You're offline. Deleting your account needs a connection." or the action error.
  5. Destructive full-width "Delete my account" ("Deleting…"), enabled only when the phrase matches, not busy, impact loaded without error, and online; tap → `AlertDialog` "Delete your account now?" with "{n} athlete account(s) will be deleted with yours. This can't be undone." when any minor is set to Delete, else "This can't be undone."; buttons "Delete my account" (error color) / "Cancel".
  6. `DELETE /me {confirmPhrase (sent trimmed), minorChoices[{athleteId, action}]}`. The model re-checks the phrase; a mismatch that reaches it shows "Type DELETE ACCOUNT to confirm." and sends nothing. Success order, as iOS (`AccountModel.deleteAccount`, then `DeleteAccountFlow.deleteNow`): toast "Your account has been deleted." (success), run the full sign-out teardown below, then the success haptic and the dialog closes (the teardown's dismissal of open dialogs may already have closed it; closing twice is a no-op). Errors use the shared online wrapper: inline error plus error toast. The server revokes Sign in with Apple grants for Apple-linked users (web `src/lib/account-deletion.server.ts`), which covers Apple accounts used on Android too; no Google-side revoke exists on iOS and none is added.
  - Google Play requirement (verify current wording): apps that let users create accounts must offer in-app deletion **and** a web resource to request deletion, entered in the Data safety form. The in-app path is this flow. **Server/web addition (Appendix A, additive; zero-disruption §4.1):** a public page `https://gradus.training/delete-account` that names Gradus (and Gradus Sports, Inc.), explains in-app deletion (Settings → Account & security → Delete account), lets a signed-in user delete through web Settings, gives support@gradussports.com for anyone without the app, and lists what is deleted and what is kept (the three paragraphs of step 1, verbatim). It must be **live before the Play Data safety form is submitted**, which blocks publication: add it to the Appendix D checklist and to §11 Risks. iOS #34 deferred `gradus.training/support` to "nearer go-live, not now"; Play makes this one page a hard prerequisite. The path is excluded from App Links (§6.10) so it opens in the browser. Current Play User Data policy wording on the deletion-URL requirement: (verify) at submission.
- **Sign-out teardown** (iOS `AppModel.signOut`), Android order: tell the Wear OS app to end its session (Data Layer, queued, no secret, §6.15); `DELETE /devices/{token}` for the FCM token; stop the Live Board planner (posted `live_board` notifications stay, as iOS leaves its activities, §6.9.6, §6.4); clear the running practice session with its notification and reminder (§7.6.3); flush then clear usage analytics (§6.12); Supabase sign-out; wipe the outbox, the user's Room database and per-user DataStore; delete Keystore-backed session keys; cancel the user's WorkManager work; dismiss any open dialog/sheet without animation if the biometric lock is up; reset the biometric lock preference; clear unread badge, feedback, wrap-up and briefing requests; drop session models; close the Live board (§6.9; iOS `isLivePresented = false`); clear the post-onboarding plan-status screen and the onboarding gate (iOS `planSetupProfile`, `onboardingGate`); drop any held deep link (iOS `pendingLinkRoute`); clear the pending sign-up stash in DataStore (iOS `PendingSignUp.clear()`; the server resumes coach and parent sign-ups); reset every back stack, including the sign-up stack, to the signed-out start destination (the sign-in tab, iOS `selectedTab = .signIn`); clear any `/me` load error. An in-progress **password-reset screen stays up** (iOS keeps the `recoveryPending` cover; it outlives sign-out, and the no-animation dismissal above skips it). Appearance and read-aloud voice (device settings) are kept.
  - **Wear-initiated sign-out** (Data Layer message from the watch, §6.15; iOS `signOutForWatch`): the message can wake a cold phone process, so first restore the stored session (idempotent); if there is no signed-in user, do nothing; otherwise run the teardown above but **do not** send the end-session message back to the watch.

**Sign out** (root row): `AlertDialog` "Sign out of Gradus?" with message "{n} change(s) still waiting to send will be discarded." when the outbox has queued items, else "Your data stays safely on the server."; buttons "Sign out" (error color) / "Cancel". Sign-out is allowed offline with that warning (QA.md's "sign out offline is refused" line predates the code; the code wins).

**Device** (`Account/DeviceView.swift`). Pushed screen "Device". No usage-data switch (decision #46).
- Group "Notifications": row "Notifications" with state "Allowed" (tennis ink) / "Off" / "Not asked" ("…" until read). When not Allowed: prominent chip "Turn on" ("Asking…"), disabled until the state has been read and while asking (iOS `.disabled(push == nil || requesting)`). Footer: Off → "Notifications are off for Gradus in Android Settings. Turn on opens Settings so you can allow them." (iOS says "iOS Settings"), else "Lesson reminders, new messages, and plan updates arrive as notifications."
  - State mapping: `NotificationManagerCompat.areNotificationsEnabled()` true → Allowed. Else on API 33+: if the app never requested `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` (DataStore flag `push.permissionRequested`, the one flag §6.6.5 and §7.5.5 use) → Not asked; otherwise Off. On API 29–32 (no runtime permission) disabled → Off.
  - "Turn on": Not asked → request `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` via `ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission`, then re-read; Off (or a permanently denied permission) → `Intent(Settings.ACTION_APP_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS).putExtra(Settings.EXTRA_APP_PACKAGE, packageName)` (the Android equivalent of `UIApplication.openSettingsURLString`). Re-read on `ON_RESUME`. On success after permission, register the FCM token (§6.6).
- Group "Security": switch "Unlock with fingerprint, face, or screen lock" (iOS: "Unlock with Face ID" / "Unlock with Touch ID or passcode"; Android cannot reliably name the biometric type, so one label). Disabled when `BiometricManager.canAuthenticate(LockAuthenticators.forSdk(...)) != BIOMETRIC_SUCCESS`, with "Set up a fingerprint, face unlock, or screen lock in Android Settings to use this.". Footer: "A convenience lock for this device. Your account still signs in with your password, Google, or Apple." (iOS: "…with your password or Apple ID."; reworded for A5's providers.) Behavior (`BiometricGate`, iOS §6.4): preference per device in DataStore (`gradus.security.biometricLock`); lock on launch with a session; relock on return only after **30 s** in the background (`ProcessLifecycleOwner` `ON_STOP`/`ON_START`); each trip to the background counts once (the prompt's own dismissal must not relock); if backgrounded while the prompt is up, stay locked; prompt via `androidx.biometric` `BiometricPrompt` titled "Unlock Gradus", with the authenticators fixed in §6.11.4 (`BIOMETRIC_STRONG or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` on API 30+, `BIOMETRIC_WEAK or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` on API 29; one `LockAuthenticators.forSdk` shared with the availability check; equivalent of iOS `.deviceOwnerAuthentication`, any biometric then passcode, GradusCore `BiometricGate`). **No negative button**: androidx.biometric throws `IllegalArgumentException` if one is set while device credential is allowed, and the system supplies its own Cancel; the deprecated `setDeviceCredentialAllowed` is not used. iOS's cancel title "Not now" therefore does not carry over. A cancel (`ERROR_USER_CANCELED`, `ERROR_CANCELED`, `ERROR_NEGATIVE_BUTTON`) clears the error and leaves the lock screen up (iOS `userCancel`/`appCancel`/`systemCancel` handling); any other error shows its system message on the lock screen; turning the switch off unlocks; sign-out resets it. Port `BiometricGateTests`. Nothing behind the lock is reachable (the `LockActivity` above `MainActivity`, §6.4, §6.11.4; no `FLAG_SECURE`, §12 N30).
- Group "Read aloud": row "Read-aloud voice" with value (iOS `voiceSummary`) = the chosen voice's short label "{name} · {quality label}" (quality labels per §6.7.5: "Very high quality", "High quality", "Standard"), else "Automatic ({name} · {quality})" for the voice in effect, else "Automatic"; refreshed on `ON_RESUME`; footer "The voice that reads plans aloud. It runs on this device, so nothing is sent anywhere."

**Read-aloud voice** (`Account/ReadAloudVoiceView.swift`, `GradusCore/Narration/NarrationVoice.swift`; decision #47; A14). §6.7.5 owns the whole screen: the on-device-only candidate filter, the ranking with the curated gender and display-name table (§12 N10), the quality labels "Very high quality" / "High quality" / "Standard", the American English / Other English / More natural voices groups and their copy, the "Open voice settings" button, the per-row and Automatic sample buttons and their TalkBack labels, the sample text, the saved identifier `narration.voiceIdentifier` = `"<enginePackage>/<voiceName>"` (null = Automatic; an uninstalled voice falls back to Automatic), and the reload on `ON_RESUME`. **Legal.** "Terms of Service" → `https://gradus.training/terms`, "Privacy Policy" → `https://gradus.training/privacy`, both in the default browser (these paths are excluded from App Links handling so they never loop into the app, §6.10). "Open-source licenses" pushes **Licenses**:

Chosen over the OSS Licenses plugin for Compose rendering, custom entries and CI verification.

Each row expands (TalkBack expanded/collapsed state) to the license name and a link (host shown) opening the browser.
- Test: the generated list is non-empty, includes supabase-kt, OkHttp/Ktor, Firebase Messaging, Media3, and all four fonts (port of "Licenses cover every resolved package and the four font families").

Full-height bottom sheet "Send feedback": "What's working, what isn't, and what you wish Gradus did. Your note sends when you're back online.". "Cancel" / "Send" ("Sending…"). Live success toast "Thanks — we read every note."; success haptic and dismiss in both cases.

Join-a-club rules (iOS `Connections/JoinClubModel.swift`):
- Code field (`OrgCodeText.normalize`): uppercase, keep only `A-Z0-9`, cap at 8 characters (apply as the user types; `KeyboardCapitalization.Characters`, no autocorrect). "Join" is enabled only at exactly 8 characters with a club confirmed.
- The cancel-plan dialog is shown **only** for a live paid individual subscription: `/coach/billing` loaded with `entitlement == paid && subscriptionTier != null && subscriptionStatus != "canceled"`; otherwise join directly.
- `environment` = `subscriptionEnvironment` from a fresh `GET /coach/profile`; if that fetch fails, `"live"`.
- The join uses a fresh `Idempotency-Key` per attempt.
- Refund toast amount: `String.format(Locale.US, "%.2f %s", cents / 100.0, currency.uppercase(Locale.US))`, e.g. "Joined Peak FSC — refunded 12.50 USD for the unused months."
- On success: refetch `/coach/billing` (updates the Settings Plan row and the Plan screen), then refresh `/me` and celebrations (iOS `onLinksChanged`).
- Tests: port `JoinClubTests` (normalization, completeness, cancel-dialog condition, environment fallback, refund formatting, result toasts).

Accepted forms: `gradus://settings[/<section>]`, `https://gradus.training/settings[/<section>]`, `https://gradus.training/{coach|parent|athlete}/settings[/<section>]` (`/account` maps to account), `https://gradus.training/{role}/paywall` → Settings › Plan (billing and club emails), and FCM payload route `settings/<section>`. Unknown section → Settings root. Sections and what each opens:

| Section | Coach | Parent | Athlete |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | Account & security | same | same |
| `plan` | Plan | Team plan | "Not for this account" / "Plans are managed by your coach or parent." |
| `connections` | Connections hub (while the local store is still opening: placeholder titled "Connections", "Preparing your local store…", then the hub; iOS `RoleTabsView`) | Team plan (guardians) | "Connections are managed by your coach or parent." |

| `coaches` | "Coaches is an athlete screen. Parents link coaches from My athletes." | same message | Coaches |

The "not for this account" screen uses the title "Not for this account" with the message above. Settings routes require a session; signed out, the link is held until sign-in (§6.10). Inbound App Links never include `/auth/handoff`, `/delete-account`, `/terms` or `/privacy`, and links the app itself opens through `openWeb()` are pinned to the browser (§6.8), so a `/{role}/paywall` or `/{role}/settings` fallback opened from inside the app never lands back on this table. Tests: route-parsing table for every form above (port the iOS routing tests that pin every mailer URL).

**Offline summary for this section.** Queued (outbox, Idempotency-Key): parent name, athlete name/birthdate, feedback. Online-only with "You're offline…" refusal: change email, change password, reset link, delete account (and its impact preview), founding claim/restore, all invoicing writes, sports and levels save, request a sport, blocked-people unblock, connections hub joins and code claims. Read-only cached: Settings root values come from the shared session models (§6.5); `/coach/billing` and invoices are memory-only.

### 7.13 Cross-cutting behaviors

**Sources.** iOS §7.13, §8.5; gradus-ios `Packages/GradusDesign/Sources/GradusDesign/Components/{Toast,States,ErrorLine,Controls,Layouts,KeyboardDismissal,PromptHold}.swift`, `Appearance.swift`, `Gradus/Shell/{RootView,AppModel}.swift`, `Packages/GradusCore/Sources/GradusCore/{Connectivity.swift,ReleaseFlags.swift}`, `Packages/GradusAPI/Sources/GradusAPI/APIError.swift`; `docs/ios/handoff-2026-10-09.md` (iOS #114 error toasts); `docs/ios/QA.md`.

#### 7.13.1 Lifecycle (what runs on launch, foreground, background)

| Moment | iOS (`AppModel.start`, `scenePhaseChanged`) | Android (`Application` + `ProcessLifecycleOwner`) |
|---|---|---|
| Launch | Register fonts; start the watch companion; start analytics flushing; wire toast errors to the reporter; start MetricKit; start connectivity monitoring with "back online → drain + refresh `/me`"; force-update check (best-effort; unreachable never blocks); `/meta/config` → plan gate; restore session → lock if enabled → enter signed-in, or signed-out with any public pending route; age signals and significant-change check after the shell settles, never blocking | Same order. Splash: Android 12+ `SplashScreen` API (core-splashscreen) on the paper background, then the in-app launch view (wordmark "Gradus" + progress) until the phase resolves. Crash-report upload and `ApplicationExitInfo` scan run right after the reporter is wired. |
| Foreground | Biometric relock check; restart 60 s analytics flushing; drain outbox; refresh `/me` (which refreshes celebrations); refresh unread | Same on `ON_START` |
| Background | Note time for the lock; stop the flush loop; flush once | Same on `ON_STOP` |

**`/me` refresh outcomes** (iOS `AppModel.loadMe(userID:initial:)`, `refreshMe()`, `retryLoadMe()`). The foreground refresh, the back-online refresh (`onBackOnline` → drain + `refreshMe()`) and the silent-push refresh (6.6.8) all run `loadMe(initial = false)`:

| Outcome | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Success | Cache `/me` (`MeCache`), clear `meLoadError`, apply it (tab fix-up, pending route delivery, celebrations), resolve the onboarding gate |
| Cancelled (`APIError.isCancellation`: a newer load replaced it, or the app went to the background mid-request) | Silent; nothing changes |
| Auth failure (401 or code `unauthenticated`) | Error toast with `userMessage` ("Please sign in again."), then the **full sign-out** |
| Any other error, `/me` cached, not the initial load | **Error toast** with `APIError.userMessage` (or the throwable's message). This includes connectivity: returning to the app offline shows "You're offline. Check your connection and try again."; a network that cannot reach the server shows "Can't reach Gradus right now. Please try again in a moment." Those two are shown but **not reported** (6.11.8 connectivity filter). |
| Any other error, nothing cached | `meLoadError` = the message; the signed-in shell renders the full-bleed `StateView` "Couldn't load your account" with "Try again" (`retryLoadMe()`, which clears the error and loads with `initial = true`); routes wait in `pendingRoute` (6.10.4) |
| Any other error, `/me` cached, initial load | Silent; the cached `/me` stays on screen |

User-facing copy for every API error comes from one port of `APIError.userMessage` (`GradusAPI/APIError.swift`, §6.2 owns the client): `api_disabled` "Gradus is briefly unavailable. Your changes are saved and will sync shortly."; `invalid_credentials` "Incorrect email/username or password."; `unauthenticated` "Please sign in again."; `rate_limited` "Too many attempts. Please wait a moment and try again."; `rate_limiter_unavailable` "Please try again in a moment."; `offline` / `unreachable` / `session_not_stored` → the error's own message; `cancelled` "That was interrupted. Please try again."; `malformed_response` and `internal` "Something went wrong. Please try again."; `validation_failed` "Some of that didn't look right. Please check and try again."; `roster_full` "Your roster is full on your current plan." (never the server's wording, never an upgrade CTA); anything else → the server's `message`. Test: one JUnit case per code.

**Presence.** iOS §7.13 says `POST /me/presence` on foreground at most every 5 minutes, and `docs/ios/QA.md` checks "coach shows as recently seen on the web". gradus-ios at HEAD **never calls it** (the generated `postMePresence` has no caller). Code wins: Android 1.0 does not call it either. Listed in §12; if Mariah calls it an iOS bug, both apps add the same call (foreground, throttled to 5 minutes, fire-and-forget).

#### 7.13.2 Flags, versions, promo codes

- **Server flags** come from `GET /meta/config` (paywall enabled, Coach Pro available, Founding cutoff date) at every launch; never compiled in. Unreachable → defaults (plan screen off), as iOS `PlanGate()`.
- **Minimum client version** from `GET /meta/client-policy` `minSupportedVersion.android` (S-1). Below it → force-update screen in place of everything: title "Update Gradus", message = policy message or "This version of Gradus is no longer supported. Please update to keep going.", action per §7.1.0: "Open gradus.training in your browser" until the Play listing exists (`BuildConfig.PLAY_LISTING_LIVE = false`, iOS's interim "Open gradus.training in Safari"), then "Update on Google Play" → `market://details?id=training.gradus.app` with an `https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=training.gradus.app` fallback. Play's In-App Updates API is not used in 1.0 (§12 N37).
- **Release flags** are compile-time: `object ReleaseFlags { const val ASK_GRADUS_ENABLED = false }` (iOS `ReleaseFlags.askGradusEnabled`, #22). Flipping one is a code change and a new build, on purpose. Native reset is on (`NATIVE_RESET = true`, iOS `GRADUS_NATIVE_RESET`).
- **Promo codes:** a code entered at sign-up is trimmed, uppercased, stashed with the pending sign-up, and applied after the profile exists ("Promo code *CODE* applied."); the server's 5-attempt cap applies (§7.1 owns the flow).

#### 7.13.3 Toasts

Port `ToastCenter` exactly (iOS #114, beta feedback 2026-10-07). Custom Compose host at the bottom of the root, above the navigation bar and the keyboard (`imePadding`), below the lock. It is not the Android system `Toast` and not a stock `Snackbar` (those cannot meet the persistence and ✕ rules); it may be built on `SnackbarHost` internals.

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Kinds | `info` (icon info, tint `pen-pool-ink`), `success` (**a pen check**, `PenMarkView(Check)` 18 dp, `pen-tennis-ink`, seed 17, line 2.2; `ad1e9bf`), `error` (warning triangle, `destructive-ink`) |
| Look | `popover` background, `md` radius, **no border** (`cardEdge`; `borderStrong` under Increase Contrast, A62), soft shadow, 16 dp side and 12 dp bottom margin, min height 44 dp (48 dp touch target for the ✕) |
| Error toasts | **Never auto-dismiss** (WCAG 2.2.1); visible ✕ with label "Dismiss"; cleared when the user changes tab or pushes/pops a screen (`screenChanged()`), but not within **500 ms** of being posted (a failing deep link that switches tabs keeps its error) |
| Inline errors | While an `ErrorLine` shows the same message, the error toast is not drawn (still announced and still reported) |
| Info/success duration | `min(8 s, 3 s + characters ÷ 20 s)`, ×1.6 when TalkBack (touch exploration) is on, capped at 8 s; touching the toast pauses the countdown, releasing resumes the remaining time (min 300 ms) |
| Dismiss | Tap anywhere on it; swipe down; TalkBack custom action "Dismiss" |
| Announce | Every toast is announced: `"Error: <message>"` for errors, the message otherwise (polite live region; assertive for errors) |
| Reporting | Every `error` toast → `ErrorReporter` (`surface: toast`) except connectivity notices (6.11.8) |
| One at a time | A single slot (`ToastCenter.current`), **no queue**: `show()` cancels the pending auto-dismiss and replaces the visible toast immediately, restarting the timer for the new one |
| Motion | Enter: slide up + fade, 250 ms (iOS `.spring(duration: 0.25)`); exit: fade, 200 ms ease-out (iOS `.easeOut(duration: 0.2)`); fade only when animations are removed (Remove animations / animator scale 0) |
| Gestures | A press with no movement threshold pauses the countdown (iOS `DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)`); a downward drag of more than 10 dp dismisses (`DragGesture(minimumDistance: 10)`, `translation.height > 0`) |
| ✕ layout | The ✕ appears **only on error toasts**; error toasts have 0 vertical padding (the 48 dp ✕ sets the height) and 4 dp trailing padding; info/success toasts have 12 dp vertical and 16 dp trailing padding; 16 dp leading on all |
| Stacking | The host sits **below** bottom sheets and dialogs (as iOS's host sits under sheets); an error raised inside a sheet or dialog is shown with that sheet's `ErrorLine`, not a toast hidden behind it |

Connectivity copy comes from one place (§6.2): "You're offline. Check your connection and try again." (no network) and "Can't reach Gradus right now. Please try again in a moment." (network but server unreachable); online-only writes use their screen-specific "You're offline. …" lines verbatim from iOS (e.g. "You're offline. Deleting your account needs a connection.", "You're offline. Your note sends when you're back online."). A cancelled request (screen closed, refresh released) is never an error.

#### 7.13.4 Offline, empty and error states

- **No global offline banner.** gradus-ios at HEAD has none (`docs/ios/QA.md` mentions "the offline banner"; there is no such component, code wins). Offline is shown by: cached content rendering as normal; online-only actions refusing with their "You're offline. …" toast; queued writes marked in place (e.g. "Queued while offline" on a pending message); the Live Board's staleness line ("Updated just now" / "Updated 12s ago" / "Not updated for 4m", §6.9); the reset flow's full-screen "You're offline" state; and the **error toast from the foreground or back-online `/me` refresh** (7.13.1), so returning to Gradus with no connection shows "You're offline. Check your connection and try again." once (not reported). Listed in §12 in case Mariah wants a banner in both apps.
- **Connectivity:** `ConnectivityManager.registerDefaultNetworkCallback`; **online = the default network exists and has `NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET`**, mirroring iOS `NWPath.status == .satisfied` (a usable route, no internet validation; `GradusCore/Connectivity.swift`). Do **not** gate on `NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED`: rink, school and hotel Wi-Fi that block Google's validation probe (or Private DNS failures) would read as offline and online-only actions would refuse while the Gradus API is reachable. "Expensive" = metered (no `NET_CAPABILITY_NOT_METERED`), the `isExpensive` counterpart.
- **Transport-error classification** (port of `APIError.offline(_:baseURL:)`): a failure is `offline` ("You're offline. Check your connection and try again.") when there is no active default network, or the exception is an `UnknownHostException`/`ConnectException` raised while no network is active; it is `unreachable` ("Can't reach Gradus right now. Please try again in a moment.") for everything else at the transport layer with a network present: `SocketTimeoutException`, connection refused, `SSLException`, DNS failure with a network, reset. iOS maps `notConnectedToInternet`, `networkConnectionLost`, `internationalRoamingOff`, `dataNotAllowed`, `callIsActive` to offline and the rest to unreachable; an unknown non-transport error with no detail is `offline`. Debug builds append " (*host*:*port*, *code*)" to the message as iOS does; release builds never do. Both are `status = 0` and retryable. Unit test: each exception type → the right code and copy. Going from offline to online drains the outbox and refreshes `/me` (`onBackOnline`). Debug builds have Settings › Debug "Simulate offline" (forces offline everywhere) and show the API base URL; release builds have neither.
- **Error boundaries:** every tab root and routed screen whose load fails with nothing cached shows the full-bleed `StateView` (icon, title, message, primary button) with **"Try again"**, titles verbatim from iOS ("Couldn't load your roster", "Couldn't load your plans", "Couldn't load resources", "Couldn't load your profile", "Couldn't load this plan", "Couldn't load your library", "Couldn't load your coaches", "Couldn't load your athletes", "Couldn't load your account", "Couldn't load this invoice", "Couldn't load this athlete", and the rest of the 35 iOS call sites; each feature section quotes its own). `/me` failing with nothing cached shows the signed-in shell's retry state (`meLoadError`); an auth failure on `/me` toasts and signs out. A `StateView` announces "*title*. *message*" when it appears. Module-load recovery from the PWA does not apply.
- **Empty states** use the same `StateView` without a button, or the screen's inline copy, verbatim from iOS per feature (e.g. Messages: coach "No conversations yet. Tap New to start one.", parent/athlete "No conversations yet. Your coach's messages land here.").

#### 7.13.5 Pull to refresh

iOS `gradusRefreshable` on 17 screens: Live Board index and board, coach visibility, rooms list, coach plans list, Resources, Roster, parent/athlete plans, coach plan (Settings), athlete coaches, athlete profile, blocked users, connections hub, parent athlete detail, parent athletes, Team plan, and the **Goals screen reached by `settings/goals`** (`RoleTabsView.swift` `GoalsScreen`, `.gradusRefreshable { await model.load() }`). Android: Material 3 `PullToRefreshBox` on the same screens and no others. The refresh runs in the `ViewModel` scope so recomposition (an empty list flipping to "Loading…") cannot cancel it, and the indicator waits for it to finish (the iOS fix for "cancelled request surfaced as an error", beta 2026-10-07). Every list screen also refreshes on return to foreground as §6.5 specifies.

#### 7.13.6 Haptics

**Code wins (A2): iOS 1.0 plays two haptics.** (1) A **light impact on press release** of every `.gradusPress` control, from `PressButtonStyle`'s `.sensoryFeedback(.impact(weight: .light))` (`GradusDesign/Components/Controls.swift` line 15; §8.3 Press row, §8.5 owns the map); (2) `Haptics.success()` at the 24 call sites listed below. There is **no** haptic on errors or warnings: `Controls.swift` defines `light()`, `warning()`, `error()` and `success()`, but a search of gradus-ios at HEAD finds no call to `Haptics.light()`, `warning()` or `error()`. Never on scroll or passive updates (§8.5). Android uses `View.performHapticFeedback` / Compose `LocalHapticFeedback` (respects the user's system touch-feedback setting; no `VIBRATE` permission needed).

| iOS | Android API 30+ | Android API 29 fallback | Called in 1.0? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.sensoryFeedback(.impact(weight: .light))` on press release (`PressButtonStyle`) | `HapticFeedbackConstants.VIRTUAL_KEY_RELEASE` | `VIRTUAL_KEY_RELEASE` | **Yes** (every `gradusPress` control) |
| `Haptics.success()` | `HapticFeedbackConstants.CONFIRM` (Compose `HapticFeedbackType.Confirm`) | `CONTEXT_CLICK` | **Yes** (24 sites below) |
| `Haptics.light()` | `CONTEXT_CLICK` | `KEYBOARD_TAP` | No (defined, unused) |
| `Haptics.warning()` / `Haptics.error()` | `REJECT` | `LONG_PRESS` | No (defined, unused) |

(verify the Compose `HapticFeedbackType` names in the chosen Compose BOM). One `GradusHaptics` object (§8.5) exposes `success()`, the press-release impact used by `gradusPress`, and the unused three, for parity with the iOS API; a lint/unit check asserts feature code calls only `success()` (the press haptic lives inside `:core:design`).

#### 7.13.7 Text size, appearance, motion, contrast, accessibility

- **Dynamic Type → font scale.** All text in `sp` via the Gradus type scale (§8); layouts work from the smallest system size through **200 %** (Android 14+ non-linear font scaling) without truncating scores, timers or primary buttons; long labels wrap; no fixed-height text containers. Icons scale with their text (the iOS `gradusIcon` rule, WCAG 1.4.4). Tested with Roborazzi at 100 %, 130 % and 200 %.
- **Large-text reflow rules** (port of `GradusDesign/Components/Layouts.swift`, accessibility audit 2026-09-17; WCAG 1.4.4, 1.4.10, 2.5.5). iOS switches layouts at the **accessibility sizes** (`dynamicTypeSize.isAccessibilitySize`, AX1 and up; AX1 body is 28 pt against the 17 pt default, about 165 %), and caps disc icons at **xxxLarge** (23 pt, about 135 %). Android thresholds, read from `LocalDensity.current.fontScale` (verify against the Pixel's font-size steps): **accessibility size = `fontScale ≥ 1.5`** (`LocalIsAccessibilitySize`, §8.1; every section uses this one threshold); **disc-icon cap = 1.35×** (§8.1). One `GradusLayout` file provides:
  - `AdaptiveRow` (iOS `AdaptiveStack`): a `Row` that becomes a `Column` at accessibility size; horizontal center alignment maps to vertical start alignment, as iOS does. Used wherever iOS uses `AdaptiveStack` or an `isAccessibilitySize` branch (lesson rows, schedule-import review, board results and score, Following, skater wheel, move sheet, plan cards, **plan detail header**, **voice capture overlay** (`VoiceCaptureButton`), invoicing sections, sign-in, onboarding, terms agreement, guardian screens, **goal cards** (`GoalCardParts`) and goals dashboard, **session action bar** (`SessionControls`), runner plans, rooms list, composer, settings and profile screens, join club, narration); each feature section names its own rows.
  - `Modifier.gradusDiscIcon()` (iOS `gradusDiscIcon`): an icon inside a fixed-size disc or circular button scales with font scale up to 1.35× and stops there (size computed from `min(fontScale, 1.35)`), while the text beside it keeps scaling.
  - `GradusAdaptiveSegmented` (iOS `gradusAdaptiveSegmented`): a Material 3 `SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow` below accessibility size, an `ExposedDropdownMenuBox` with the same options and selection at or above it. Wear OS keeps its own picker.
  - **Touch targets** (iOS `gradusTapTarget`, 44 × 44 pt hit area including the accessibility frame): every icon button and small tappable uses `Modifier.minimumInteractiveComponentSize()` (48 dp), so the semantics bounds (TalkBack focus rectangle, Switch Access) are 48 dp too, not the glyph's bounds; the visual stays its size.
  - **Large Content Viewer** (iOS `accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer` on the Live toolbar button, `RoleTabsView.swift`, and the plan title, `PlanDetailView.swift`) has no Android equivalent; Android instead lets those two labels wrap and scale (no fixed-height container), and the Live button keeps its TalkBack label.
  - Readable width: content that iOS caps with `.frame(maxWidth: 640)` (Roster, athlete detail, board index, board, Resources, Goals, library links, other coaches' plans) is capped at 640 dp and centered, which only matters in landscape and on ≥ 600 dp windows (7.13.11).
  - Roborazzi tests at `fontScale` 1.0, 1.3, 1.5 and 2.0 for each component above.
- **Appearance:** Settings › Appearance "System" / "Light" / "Dark", stored as `gradus.appearance` (`system|light|dark`), default System; applied at the root theme (and to `LockActivity`). Gradus tokens in both modes, no dynamic color (§8).
- **Landscape** on every phone screen (proposed A22; 7.13.11).
- **Reduce motion → Remove animations:** when the system animator duration scale is 0 (A33), nothing animates (§8.5):
  - the connection celebration and skater wheel use their reduced variants;
  - toasts fade instead of sliding;
  - the EditingOutline, category folds, move expansion and the check-in's move advance change instantly.

  Pen marks never draw on, on either platform. Motion is otherwise ≤ 250 ms.
- **Increase Contrast →** `LocalIncreasedContrast` (A62, §8.5) is true when the Android 14+ contrast level is above Standard (`UiModeManager.getContrast() > 0`) or, on Android 16+, "High contrast text" is on (`AccessibilityManager.isHighContrastTextEnabled()`; verify). It gives:
  - opaque cards with `borderStrong` edges on every borderless surface;
  - flat paper;
  - pen strokes 1 dp heavier, tallies at 2.2 dp;
  - the practice line's zone at 45% and its midline at 60%.

  On API 29–33 the system's own high-contrast text rendering applies with no app work. Contrast targets stay at the web's AAA levels (WCAG 2.2 AAA gate, iOS §8.5, 2026-09-19).
- **TalkBack:** a `contentDescription`/semantics label on every control, the same labels iOS uses (including the five icon-only buttons); headings marked `heading()`; inline errors read "Error: …"; status changes not shown by a toast are announced; Live Board lanes announce data age. Minimum touch target **48 dp** (Material; above iOS's 44 pt). Score-sheet abbreviations (GOE, deductions, factor, IJS) expanded on first use.
- **Keyboard:** tapping outside a field or dragging a list hides the keyboard (iOS `dismissesKeyboardOnOutsideTap`, `scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively)`); the focused field's draft is kept. Hardware keyboards get logical focus order.
- **Back navigation:** system back and predictive back (Android 14+ animation, `enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true"`) pop the current tab's stack, then return to the role's home tab, then leave the app; sheets and dialogs close first; destructive editors that iOS guards with a discard confirmation show the same confirmation on back. Implementation rules are in 7.13.11.

#### 7.13.8 Covers that sit over every tab

- **Connection celebration** (iOS `CelebrationCover`): after `/me` loads (and after any `linksChanged()`), `GET /me/celebrations`; when one is due it covers every tab full-screen, acknowledges on every exit, and never shows for minors or role-less accounts (§7.7 owns content).
- **Prompt hold:** a screen's own prompts (the Roster's wrap-up alert) wait while the Live cover, the Terms gate, the password-reset cover or the lock is up; the celebration holds only prompts nobody asked for (`AppModel.promptHold`).
- **Terms gate**, **password-reset cover** and **significant-change parent approval** are root-level, owned by §6.4 and §6.13.

#### 7.13.9 Localization

English only in 1.0. All copy in `strings.xml` (and plurals in `<plurals>`) from day one, generated from the iOS string catalog and the shared direct-notice text source by script, never retyped (proposed A25). Dates, times and numbers formatted with the device locale's `java.time` formatters, US English copy.

#### 7.13.10 Tests

Unit: `ToastCenter` timing (reading duration, TalkBack multiplier, 500 ms grace, inline suppression, error never auto-dismisses, single-slot replacement), connectivity-message filter, `APIError.userMessage` per code, transport-error classification (offline vs unreachable), `/me` refresh outcomes (7.13.1), haptics mapping per API level and "feature code calls only `success()`". Compose UI: error toast ✕ and tab-change clearing; `StateView` "Try again" on each tab with a failing fake repository; pull to refresh not cancelled by state change; font scale 200 % screenshots of Roster, plan detail, room, board; dark mode screenshots; landscape screenshots. Accessibility: Espresso/Compose `AccessibilityChecks` on every tab root; Accessibility Scanner pass on the Pixel recorded in QA.

#### 7.13.11 Android platform behaviors (targetSdk per A6)

A6 sets targetSdk to the level Google Play requires at submission (API 36 for new apps and updates from 31 August 2026 (verify)). Targeting 35+ enforces edge-to-edge; targeting 36 removes the edge-to-edge opt-out, makes predictive back the default (`onBackPressed()` is no longer called, `KEYCODE_BACK` is not dispatched), and on displays ≥ 600 dp ignores `screenOrientation`, `resizeableActivity` and aspect-ratio restrictions (verify each against the API 36 behavior-changes page at build time). These are the Android-native counterparts of how iPhone already behaves (safe areas, swipe-back, rotation), so they carry no product change:

- **Edge-to-edge everywhere.** `enableEdgeToEdge()` in every activity's `onCreate`, including `LockActivity` and any trampoline. Every screen consumes `WindowInsets` (`systemBars`, `displayCutout`, `ime`) through `Scaffold`/`contentWindowInsets` or explicit `windowInsetsPadding`; nothing is hidden under the status bar, the gesture bar, or a side cutout in landscape. The toast host pads by `navigationBars` + `ime` (7.13.3). Light/dark system-bar icons follow the Gradus theme (`gradus.appearance`), not the system default. No `R.attr.windowOptOutEdgeToEdgeEnforcement`.
- **Back only through the dispatcher.** All back handling uses `OnBackPressedDispatcher`, Compose `BackHandler`, or `PredictiveBackHandler` (for the sheet and Live cover dismiss animations); no `onBackPressed()` override and no `KEYCODE_BACK` handling anywhere (lint rule). `LockActivity` registers an enabled callback that calls `moveTaskToBack(true)` (6.11.4) and opts out of the back preview so the app underneath is never revealed.
- **Orientation and size.** No `screenOrientation` lock on any activity: phones rotate between portrait and landscape as on iPhone (upside-down portrait is acceptable either way). On windows ≥ 600 dp wide (tablets, unfolded foldables, desktop windowing; A4 "phones only, tablets get the phone layout") the phone layout is shown, with content capped at the iOS readable width (640 dp, 7.13.7) and centered; it must not break or lose state when the window is resized, folded/unfolded, or rotated (state in `ViewModel`/`rememberSaveable`; no `configChanges` override beyond what Compose needs). Adaptive tablet layouts are deferred (A4).
- **Tests:** Roborazzi at font scale 1.0 / 1.3 / 2.0 in portrait **and** landscape for each tab root, plus one 600 dp-wide and one 840 dp-wide window; an instrumented test that resizes the window (Espresso device API or `setRequestedOrientation` on a resizable emulator) with a draft in the composer and a sheet open, and asserts both survive; a lint check that no activity declares `screenOrientation` or overrides `onBackPressed`.
