### 7.15 Wear OS

Decisions A3, A50, A51, iOS #36, #47, #48, #51, #54; design §6.15. **Code at HEAD wins over the iOS PRD's watch wording:** there is no spoken wrap-up prompt (the iOS PRD's "Greta's lesson just ended. What changed?"; the Choose step shows only its hint text and speaks nothing); the read-back is the full plan read (`PlanNarration`), not a short "New plan, six moves. First: …"; and the read-back actions are Activate / Keep as draft, not "Keep it / Try again". Headphones-first: every screen speaks, every input is one large button or a recorded clip. All text meets the §8 contrast and target rules at watch sizes (round 1.2"–1.4" class screens; targets ≥ 48 dp; text follows the watch font size setting; content in `TransformingLazyColumn`/`ScalingLazyColumn` with rotary-crown scrolling; back = swipe-to-dismiss via `SwipeDismissableNavHost`).

| Feature | Roles | Wear OS requirement (iOS source) | Pri |
|---|---|---|---|
| Session hand-off | all | Signed in on the phone → the watch receives its own session over the Data Layer (`POST /auth/companion`); sign-out on either side signs out the other; 14-day lease (§6.15.3; `WatchCompanion.swift`) | P0 |
| Plan → audio | athlete, parent, coach | Active plans list (spoken labels), full read, previous / play-pause / next / repeat / speed, keeps reading through headphones with the wrist down, cached for the rink (`Plans/WatchPlans*.swift`) | P0 |
| Voice → plan | coach; adult athlete | Record ≤ 90 s with the screen on, build, full read-back, deploy or keep as draft (`Create/WatchCreatePlan*.swift`) | P0 |
| Deploy a plan | coach; athlete (own) | Drafts list; coach assigns and activates straight through (no cap, #52; a spoken bench choice only as the 409 fallback); athlete activates their own | P0 |
| Pre-lesson briefing | coach | "Up next" with times; briefing spoken **on tap only** (`UpNext/WatchUpNext*.swift`) | P0 |
| Post-lesson wrap-up | coach | Pending wrap-ups; Record changes / No changes / Didn't happen (confirmed); spoken result | P0 |
| Session timer | athlete, parent | iOS PRD §7.15 lists it (W5) but **it is not built at iOS HEAD 91c6af2** (no session code in `FeatureWatch`). Android builds it if, and as, iOS ships it in 1.0 (§12 N36; milestone KW5) | P0 if iOS ships it |
| Messaging | all | *Changed (#54):* a tap on a message notification opens that conversation in the Wear app; the latest 20 messages (sender, time, text; a voice note says "play it on your phone"), marked read; reply by voice input, keyboard or a quick reply, text only for every role; "Try again" keeps a failed reply; a Messages row on Home for every role; Reply on the notification itself (§6.15.8, §7.15.7; `Messages/WatchMessag*.swift`) | P0 |
| Watch-face complication | coach (lessons); everyone (the mark) | *Added (#51, W7):* `SHORT_TEXT`, `LONG_TEXT` and `MONOCHROMATIC_IMAGE` complication: the next lesson today and "Lesson now", "No more lessons today", or the Gradus mark; no names on the face; tap opens Up next (§6.15.7, §7.15.6; `GradusComplication.swift`) | P0 |
| Tiles, watch faces | — | None in 1.0 (§12 N76). The Ongoing Activity during a read (§6.15.1) | — |

#### 7.15.1 Home

Title "Gradus". One row per thing the wrist does, loaded each time Home shows (`WatchHomeView`):

| Row | Shown to | Icon | TalkBack hint |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Up next" | coach | clock | "Today's next lessons, their briefings, and lessons to wrap up" |
| "Plans" | everyone | list | "Your active plans, to hear one read aloud" |
| "Record a plan" | coach; athlete with `voiceToPlan` (§6.15.6) | mic | "Say a plan; Gradus builds it and reads it back" |
| "Drafts" | coach, athlete (minors too) | document | — |
| "Messages" (with the unread count) | everyone | forum | "Your conversations, to read and reply" |
| "Sign out" (destructive) | everyone | sign-out | opens the confirm dialog (§6.15.3) |

Parents see Plans, Messages and Sign out. An org-admin or unknown role gets an empty plan list and Messages (no other extra rows). A tapped message notification or a tapped lesson on the watch face opens over Home, but waits while a recording, Record a plan, a draft or a wrap-up is on screen (`holdsUnsentWork`).

#### 7.15.2 Plans and the player (W1)

- **List source by role** (active plans only, newest first, same endpoints as the phone): coach `GET /plans?kind=plan&status=active` → subtitle "for <athlete>" (or none); parent `GET /parent/plans` → "for <athlete>"; athlete `GET /athlete/plans` → "your plan" (own, `source = athlete`), "from Gradus" (`isGradus`), "from <coachName>", or none. Empty title → "Untitled plan". Row TalkBack label is one sentence: "<title>, <subtitle>, <n> moves" ("1 move"; subtitle omitted when empty), hint "Opens the player".
- States: "Loading plans…"; failed message + "Try again"; empty "No active plans yet. When a plan is activated, it appears here."; offline banner "No connection. These are saved on this watch." (§6.15.5).
- **Player screen** (header = plan title): shows the saved detail at once, then the fresh one (a read under way keeps the copy it started with); neither available → "This plan isn't saved on this watch yet. Open it once with a connection." Loaded: position line ("Plan title" / "Move 2 of 6"); controls row Previous (44 dp, label "Previous move", dimmed and disabled at the start), Play/Pause (52 dp accent circle; labels "Play" / "Pause reading" / "Resume reading"), Next ("Next move"); a notice line if headphones were missing; the caption ("Tap play to hear the whole plan." before the first play; TalkBack label "Now reading", value = caption); a second row with Repeat (label "Repeat this move") and a speed button showing the current speed and cycling Slow → Normal → Fast (label "Reading speed", value = current, hint "Changes to <next>").
- Next is dimmed and disabled on the last line (`canGoNext`), as Previous is at the start. The headphones notice clears as soon as a later Play/Repeat/Next/Previous finds headphones; Repeat (or any control) while already speaking does not re-check the route (`routeReady()` returns true while speaking). A reload while idle loads the fresh detail.
- Play, Repeat, and Next/Previous **from a pause** call `WatchAudio.ready()` first (§6.15.4). Speech runs in the `mediaPlayback` foreground service with an Ongoing Activity ("Reading <plan title>", tap returns to the player). Leaving the player by back stops the read. A finished read announces "Finished reading this plan."
- Coach's "Hear the plan" from a lesson opens this player with the title "<first name>'s plan".

#### 7.15.3 Coach: Up next, briefing, wrap-up (W2)

- **Up next** (title "Up next"): parallel calls `GET /coach/up-next?lessonDate=<local ISO date>&dayOfWeek=<0–6>&currentMinute=<0–1439>&limit=3` and `GET /coach/wrap-ups/pending` (same query), using the watch's current time zone (follows travel). Sections: if any, header "To wrap up" with rows "Wrap up <athlete name>" / "Ended <h:mm AM/PM>"; then header "Lessons" with rows "<athlete name>" / when-line, or "No more lessons today.". When-line (re-evaluated every minute): ended → "Ended <time>"; in progress → "Now, until <end>"; 1 minute → "In 1 minute, <start>"; 2–59 → "In <n> minutes, <start>"; otherwise "<start>"; the server's own "Starting now, <start>" applies at 0. Lesson row hint "Opens the lesson, to hear its briefing". States: "Loading lessons…"; nothing loaded and failed → "No connection. Try again near your phone or Wi-Fi." or "Couldn't load your lessons. Try again." + "Try again"; a failed refresh over a shown list → "Couldn't update. This is the list from earlier." Reload on every return to the foreground and every 60 s when a listed lesson has ended or the day changed.
- **Lesson** (header = athlete name, when-line under it): primary button "Hear briefing" → fetch `GET /coach/athletes/{id}/briefing?lessonDate=…` (no refresh; the server may answer from cache) → `ready()` → speak `narrative` at Normal speed; the button reads "Stop" while speaking and "Hear it again" afterwards, disabled while loading. The narrative text is shown on screen while spoken. Errors: "Couldn't get the briefing. Try again." or "Connect Bluetooth headphones to listen.". A tap while speaking stops; a briefing stopped while loading never speaks; leaving the screen stops it. States are idle / loading / speaking / done / failed (iOS `WatchBriefingModel`). A call or assistant interruption (audio-focus loss) **stops** the briefing (not pause), and the button goes back to "Hear briefing". The narrative text shows as soon as it is fetched, even when headphones are missing (the text is set before the headphone check). **Nothing is spoken unprompted** (#36). Secondary button "Hear the plan" when the lesson has `activePlanId`.
- **Wrap-up** (header "Wrap up <athlete name>"), steps from `WatchWrapUpModel`:
  - Choose: if there is an active plan: hint "Say what changed in the plan.", primary "Record changes" (asks for AI permission first when not allowed, §6.7.1a), secondary "No changes" (hint "Keeps the plan as it is"); without one: "No active plan to edit. Make one on your phone."; always secondary "Didn't happen".
  - Confirm didn't happen: "Mark this lesson as didn't happen? It comes off the invoice draft." → primary "Didn't happen" / secondary "Back".
  - Start recording (iOS `WatchWrapUpModel.startRecording`): stop any speech first; mic denied → failed step with the microphone message (same text as §7.15.4); any other start failure → "Couldn't start recording. Try again.".
  - Recording: "Recording… <n> s" (TalkBack "Recording, <n> seconds"), primary "Stop and send", secondary "Cancel" (discards the clip and returns to Up next). At 90 s it stops and **sends on its own**.
  - Sending: progress + "Updating…".
  - Send = `POST /voice/build-plan` `mode=edit`, `planId=activePlanId`, filename `wrap-up.m4a`, one idempotency key per recording. Then: `aiFailed` → "Couldn't turn that into changes. Your words are saved on <first>'s plan. Record again, or edit it on your phone."; nothing changed (no applied moves, no touched move or new move, title/notes/athlete untouched) → "Couldn't pick out any changes. Your words are saved on <first>'s plan. Record again, or choose No changes."; otherwise record `POST /coach/wrap-ups {action: "edited"}` and say the summary: no moves → "<first>'s plan is updated."; 1 → "Updated 1 move in <first>'s plan."; n → "Updated <n> moves in <first>'s plan."; plus " One move couldn't be read; check it on your phone." / " <n> moves couldn't be read; check them on your phone."; plus " That also moved the plan to another athlete. Check it on your phone." when the athlete changed, else " Couldn't find <name> on your roster." when unresolved. `idempotency_key_reused` → record the wrap-up and say "<first>'s plan is updated."; `idempotency_key_in_progress` → "Still updating <first>'s plan. Try again in a moment."; a refusal drops the clip; a retryable failure keeps it in memory: "Couldn't send that. Try again near your phone or Wi-Fi." / "Couldn't send that. Try again." / the server message / "Couldn't use that recording. Record again.". Edit applied but wrap-up save failed → "<first>'s plan is updated, but the wrap-up didn't save. Try again." and Try again records only the wrap-up.
  - "No changes" → `action: "redeployed"`, says "Done. <first>'s plan stays as it is."; "Didn't happen" → `did_not_happen`, says "Marked as didn't happen."; save failure → "Couldn't save that. Try again.".
  - Done step: check icon + the result + primary "Done" (returns to **Up next**, not Home; iOS `dismiss()`). Failed step: text + primary "Try again" (records the pending wrap-up, resends the kept clip, or returns to Choose).
  - A recorded wrap-up is removed from Up next at once so it matches the phone's roster pill. The watch never sends `dismissed` (the iOS PRD row's "Keep / Re-deploy / Didn't happen / Dismiss" is superseded by the code's three choices).
  - Leaving the screen: work already sent still finishes (the wrap-up is still recorded), nothing more is spoken, an unsent clip is dropped.
  - Results are spoken through `readyForPrompt()` only; with TalkBack on they are announced instead of spoken.

#### 7.15.4 Voice → plan and deploy (W3 coach, W4 adult athlete)

Port of `WatchCreatePlanModel` / `WatchCreatePlanView`. Coach routes `/plans…`, `/voice/build-plan`; athlete routes `/athlete/plans…`, `/athlete/voice/build-plan`.

- **Ready** (title "Record a plan"): hint, coach "Say who the plan is for and the moves, with targets."; athlete "Say the moves, with targets."; primary "Record" (mic). Reached only when AI is allowed; Home's "Record a plan" opens the Wear AI permission screen first otherwise (§6.7.1a).
- **Recording:** stop any speech first. "Recording… <n> s", primary "Stop and build", secondary "Cancel" (discards and returns Home). 90 s cap sends on its own. Denied mic → "Gradus needs the microphone. On your watch, open Settings, then Apps, then Gradus, then Permissions." (iOS names the watchOS path; verify the Wear OS path on the Pixel Watch). Start failure → "Couldn't start recording. Try again."
- **Sending / activating:** progress + "Building the plan…" / "Saving…".
- **Build** (`mode=create`, filename `plan.m4a`, one idempotency key per recording): `aiFailed` or zero applied moves → "Couldn't make out the moves. Your words are saved on a draft in Drafts, to finish on your phone. Record again to try once more." (spoken via prompt rules); `idempotency_key_reused` → "That plan is already made. It's in Drafts."; `in_progress` → "Still building the plan. Try again in a moment."; other failures as in the wrap-up. Success → open the plan and **read it back in full at once**.
- **Read-back:** plan title (header), line "<n> moves, for <athlete>" / "<n> moves, no athlete yet" (coach) or "<n> moves" (athlete); a notice when the server could not do something: "Couldn't find <name> on your roster." (coach) and/or "One move couldn't be read; check it on your phone." / "<n> moves couldn't be read; check them on your phone."; or "Connect Bluetooth headphones to listen."; button "Hear it" / "Pause"; the caption; primary deploy button **"Choose athlete"** (coach, unassigned) / **"Activate for <first name>"** (coach) / **"Activate"**, disabled with "This plan has no moves yet. Add them on your phone." when empty; secondary **"Keep as draft"** → "Saved as a draft.".
- **Deploy, coach:** unassigned → load the roster names → "Who is this plan for?" with one button per athlete (empty roster → "No athletes on your roster yet. Add one on your phone."); assign = `PATCH /plans/{id}` athlete, re-read the plan. Then activate straight through (no cap, #52): `deploy()` and `assign()` call `activate(replaceId = null)` with no active-plans read first.

  **409 fallback** (a server not yet published with #52; iOS `offerBenchChoice`). It runs on a 409 `bench_choice_required`, or on a 422 after a plan to rest was chosen. It runs when the plan has an athlete and either no plan was chosen or fewer than two re-asks have happened; a re-ask counts only after a choice, and `deploy()` resets the count. Otherwise the step fails with the server message. The fallback reads the athlete's active plans, excluding this one:
  - Empty: on a `bench_choice_required` refusal the step fails with the server's message; on a stale 422 a plain activation runs instead.
  - Non-empty: the bench choice below is shown and spoken.
  - The read fails: "No connection. Couldn't check the athlete's plans. Try again near your phone or Wi-Fi." or the server message (step failures below).

  Screen text and spoken prompt differ (iOS `WatchCreatePlanScreens` vs `WatchCreatePlanModel.prompt`):

| Step | Screen text | Spoken prompt | Buttons |
|---|---|---|---|
| choose-bench (409 fallback only) | "Which of <first>'s plans should rest so this one can go live?" (fallback **"this athlete"**, lower case) | "<first>'s active plans: <list>. Which one should rest so this plan can go live?" (fallback **"This athlete"**) | one button per plan, labelled with its title (hint "Rests this plan and activates the new one") / "Keep as draft" |

  `<first>` falls back to **"The athlete"** in activation results. `<list>` joins titles as "A"; "A and B"; "A, B and C" (iOS `list(_:)`, test `conflictListsReadNaturally`). Activate = `POST /plans/{id}/status {status: active, replaceId?}` with a fresh idempotency key; success says "Active. <first> can practice it now." or, after a bench choice, "Active, and the other plan is resting. <first> can practice it now.".
- **Step failures** (iOS `WatchCreatePlanModel.message(for:doing:)`): offline or unreachable → "No connection. Couldn't <action>. Try again near your phone or Wi-Fi." (iOS says "iPhone"; copy substitution as in §6.15.3); any other API error → the server's message; a non-API error → "Couldn't <action>. Try again.". `<action>` ∈ {"open the plan", "load your athletes", "assign the plan", "check the athlete's plans", "activate the plan", "load your drafts"}. Failed step's **"Try again"**: resend the kept clip if any, else reopen the plan or draft, else return to Ready (iOS `retry()`).
- **Deploy, athlete:** activate their own directly (no cap for athlete-authored plans, §6.14); says "Your plan is active."
- **Drafts** (title "Drafts"): coach drafts (`kind=plan&status=draft`, subtitle "for <athlete>" or "no athlete yet"); athlete own drafts (subtitle "draft"). The subtitle is always shown. Row TalkBack label is one sentence "<title>, <subtitle>, <n> moves" (`item.spokenLabel`). The list reloads each time the screen opens and shows a progress indicator while loading. Empty: "No drafts. A plan you start and don't activate waits here." Load failure: "No connection. Couldn't load your drafts. Try again near your phone or Wi-Fi." or the server message + "Try again". A draft opens the same flow (title "Draft") on the read-back; its retry reopens the draft and **never** falls back to recording (a minor reaches Drafts, never the recorder).
- Questions and results are spoken through `readyForPrompt()` (the read-back player is stopped first), announced instead when TalkBack is on; leaving the screen drops an unsent clip, stops speech, and nothing more opens or is said. "Done" and "Cancel" return **Home** (iOS clears the navigation path, `path = []`), unlike the wrap-up, which returns to Up next.

#### 7.15.5 Wear OS tests and QA

- Unit tests: port `WatchPlansTests`, `WatchUpNextTests`, `WatchCreatePlanTests`, `CompanionHandoffTests`, `WatchMessagesTests` (§7.15.7), `WatchComplicationRefresherTests` and `WatchComplicationTimelineTests` (§7.15.6) case for case (names listed in the iOS files), with fakes for the repositories, `SpeechOutput`, and `WatchLink`.
- Compose for Wear UI tests and screenshot tests (Roborazzi/Paparazzi with the Wear round devices) for every screen state above, at default and largest font size.
- Device QA on the Pixel Watch (proposed Pixel Watch 3 or later), paired with the Pixel: a parent, an athlete and a coach each hear a full plan through Bluetooth headphones with the wrist down and the screen off; no headphones opens the output picker; a coach records a wrap-up that updates the plan and clears the roster pill on the phone; a plan dictated on the wrist is active on the athlete's phone; an adult athlete builds and activates a plan; a minor athlete (and one with no birthdate) sees Drafts but no "Record a plan", and a forced `POST /athlete/voice/build-plan` answers 403 `text_only`; phone sign-out signs the watch out (live and, with the watch away, queued); a watch left away past the lease (debug `gradusLeaseSeconds`) signs itself out with the lease message; a message notification on the watch opens its conversation and its Reply sends (§7.15.7); a coach's watch face shows the next lesson and returns to the mark on sign-out (§7.15.6); TalkBack reads every state change.

#### 7.15.6 Watch-face complication (KW7, #51)

Design §6.15.7. Copy is from gradus-ios `GradusComplication.swift` (`ComplicationText`), using its "hiding name" forms (A50, §12 N75). `<start>`/`<end>` long form = locale short time ("3:00 PM"); short form = hour and minute without AM/PM ("3:00"). Minutes are capped at 11:59 PM.

| State (`WatchComplicationTimeline.state`) | `SHORT_TEXT` | `LONG_TEXT` (title / text) | `MONOCHROMATIC_IMAGE` | Content description (TalkBack) | Tap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Next lesson (not started) | mark + "<short start>" | "Up next" / "<long start> – <long end>" | mark | "Next lesson at <long start>." | Up next |
| Lesson on now | mark + "Now" | "Lesson now" / "Until <long end>" | mark | "Lesson now, until <long end>." | Up next |
| Done (every lesson ended, and the list was complete) | mark + "Lessons done" | "Gradus" / "No more lessons today" | mark | "Gradus. No more lessons today." | Home |
| Mark (not a coach, signed out, no snapshot, another day, or a cut-off list whose lessons have all passed) | mark + "Gradus" | "Gradus" / "Your plans, read aloud" | mark | "Gradus" | Home |

- `SHORT_TEXT` "Lessons done" comes from the iOS corner slot. Faces may truncate text longer than about 7 characters, so check it on the Pixel Watch's faces. iOS's circular slot shows the mark alone when done, but Wear's `SHORT_TEXT` must carry text.
- The rectangular header is uppercased on iOS by `.textCase(.uppercase)`. On Wear, the face styles the title; the strings are passed as written ("Up next", "Lesson now", "Gradus").
- **Rules (port of `WatchComplicationTimeline`):**
  - The lesson on now, or else the next one, is the first lesson sorted by start whose `endMinute > now`, and it is in progress when `now ≥ startMinute`.
  - Once every lesson has ended, the state is "done" only when `complete`; otherwise it is the mark ("a list the server cut off never claims the day is done").
  - A snapshot whose `day` is not today shows the mark.
  - Back-to-back lessons go straight from one to the next.
  - At midnight the state returns to the mark.
- **Preview data** (`getPreviewData`, shown in the face editor) is an invented lesson 15 minutes from now, lasting 45 minutes (the iOS sample uses the invented "Greta"; nothing with a name renders, A50).
- Pixel Watch QA: Gradus can be added to a face in each type. A mock coach's face (`gradusMock coach`) shows the next lesson, then "Now" during it, then the next one, then "Lessons done". A parent's face shows the mark. Signing out on the phone with the watch away and then back in range returns the face to the mark without the Wear app being opened. A tap on a lesson opens Up next, and the same tap during a recording waits until the recording ends.

**Tests** (JUnit 5 + Turbine; port case for case):
- `WatchComplicationTimelineTests`:
  - "No snapshot shows the mark"
  - "Yesterday's lessons never show today"
  - "The face rolls through the day: next, soon, on now, the one after, done, then the mark at midnight" (drop the "soon" assertion; there is no Wear relevance entry)
  - "Back-to-back lessons go straight from one to the next"
  - "A cut-off list never claims the day is done"
  - "A snapshot read after its lessons ended says done (complete) or shows the mark (cut off)"
  - "A coach with no lessons today sees done for today"
  - "The store round-trips and clears"
  - "A stored snapshot this build can't read still counts as there, so refreshing carries on"
  - "Snapshots carry their format version"
- `WatchComplicationRefresherTests`:
  - "A refresh writes today's lessons, first names only, and reloads the face once"
  - "A full list is marked cut off, so the face never says the day is done on a guess"
  - "Offline keeps what is on the face and keeps refreshing; a refused token or role clears it" (401, 403)
  - "A slow background fetch gives up at its timeout and keeps the face as it was"
  - "A stored snapshot this build can't read still counts, so background refresh carries on"
  - "A tap on the face waits for the home, is taken once, and never outlives a sign-out"
  - "Screens holding unsent work hold a tap on the face until the coach is done there"
  - "Signing out mid-fetch: the last account's lessons never reach the face"
- `CompanionHandoffTests` additions: `everyWayTheWatchSessionEndsClearsTheFace`, `aBackgroundWakeHearsAQueuedSignOutBeforeItRefreshes`, `aBackgroundRefreshHonoursTheLeaseWithoutSigningOut`.
- Android additions:
  - The data source maps each state to the table above for all three types, and no `ComplicationData` text or content description ever contains the snapshot's `firstName`.
  - Timeline entries' `TimeInterval`s are contiguous, and the default is the mark.
  - The periodic worker is enqueued only with a snapshot and an active complication, and cancelled when either goes.
  - `TestListenableWorkerBuilder`: the background worker clears on an expired lease and refreshes within 10 s otherwise.
  - A Roborazzi render of each type and state on a round device through the androidx watch-face test renderer (verify the tooling).

#### 7.15.7 Messages on the wrist (#54)

Port of gradus-ios `FeatureWatch/Messages/WatchMessaging.swift` (`WatchMessaging`, `WatchThreadModel`), `WatchMessageScreens.swift` (`WatchRoomsView`, `WatchThreadView`), `WatchNotificationDelegate.swift`, and the `WatchHomeView` Messages row. Endpoints: `GET /rooms`, `GET /rooms/{id}?limit=20`, `POST /rooms/{id}/messages` with `Idempotency-Key`, `POST /rooms/{id}/read`. Every role. Copy is verbatim except "iPhone" → "phone" (§4.3 rule 3).

**Home row** (all roles; between "Plans" and the role rows):
- "Messages", icon `forum`.
- An accent capsule with the unread total when > 0, hidden from TalkBack. TalkBack value "<n> unread"; hint "Your conversations, to read and reply"; test tag `watch.home.messages`.
- Rooms reload every time Home shows (no realtime).

**Conversations** (title "Messages"; `WatchRoomsView`):
- Rooms newest first by `updatedAt`.
- Loading: "Loading messages…".
- Failed with nothing shown: "No connection. Try again near your phone or Wi-Fi." or "Couldn't load your messages. Try again.", plus "Try again" (`watch.rooms.retry`).
- Empty: "No conversations yet. Start one in Gradus on your phone." (`watch.rooms.empty`).
- A failed refresh over a shown list: "Couldn't update. This is the list from earlier." (`watch.rooms.stale`).
- Row:
  - An accent dot when unread.
  - `displayName` (bold when unread), `previewLine` (2 lines).
  - "<relative time>", or "<relative time> · <n> new" in accent.
  - TalkBack one node: "<displayName>, <n> unread message(s), <preview>, <spoken relative time>", hint "Opens the conversation", tag `watch.room.<id>`.
- Times re-render every minute. Reload on `ON_RESUME`.

**Conversation** (`WatchThreadView`; title = the other people's prefixed first names joined with " & ", e.g. "Coach Renata", "Greta & Parent Ingrid", else "Conversation"):
- The latest **20** messages, oldest at the top; on open, scroll so the newest starts at the top with the reply controls under it.
- States:
  - "Loading messages…"
  - Missing (404): "This conversation isn't available anymore."
  - Failed: the load message + "Try again" (`watch.thread.reload`)
  - Empty: "No messages yet — say hello."
- Row:
  - "<sender> · <relative time>", where the sender is "You", the prefixed first name, or the deleted-sender label. Then the text.
  - A voice note shows a `graphic_eq` icon with **"Voice note — play it on your phone"** and its transcript beneath when there is one. A voice note is never played on the wrist.
  - A deleted sender with an empty body shows "Message deleted".
  - A plan tag shows an `assignment` icon and the plan title.
  - Own messages on `elevated`, others on `card`.
  - TalkBack one node: "<sender>, <spoken time>, <text>[, Transcript: <t>][, About the plan <title>]", tag `watch.message.<id>`.
- **Read marks:** opening the conversation marks it read only if a message not mine, not from a deleted sender and not yet read by me exists; the Home count then drops. A refresh (on `ON_RESUME`, or a notification for this room while it is open) does **not** mark it read. It announces "New message" / "<n> new messages".
- **Paused by a parent:** the reply area is replaced by the header's paused message (`watch.thread.paused`), and nothing sends.
- **Reply controls:**
  - Primary **"Reply"** (icon reply): `RemoteInputIntentHelper.createActionRemoteInputIntent()` with `RemoteInput("gradus.reply")` label "Message", launched for result. Wear's system input offers voice, keyboard and emoji; Gradus never records audio here. Hint "Dictate or type a reply" (iOS "Dictate, scribble or type a reply"; Scribble is Apple's, so the word is dropped, a platform-noun change under §4.3 rule 3). Tag `watch.thread.reply`.
  - Then four secondary quick replies, verbatim: **"Thanks!", "Got it", "See you soon", "On my way"**. Hint "Sends <text> now", tag `watch.thread.quick.<text>`.
  - All disabled while sending.
- **Send** (`WatchThreadModel.send`):
  - Trim; blank is ignored. Not while sending, not when paused.
  - The key is reused only when the text equals the kept unsent text ("Try again"), otherwise a new UUID.
  - Status line:
    - "Sending…" (`watch.thread.sending`), announced "Sending".
    - Sent: check icon + "Sent" (`watch.thread.sent`), announced "Sent". Then refetch the thread, mark read, and reload rooms.
    - `{ok:false}` → the server's words (`watch.thread.refused`), not kept.
    - 403/404 → refused with the failure message, not kept.
    - Any other failure → the failure message, the kept text in quotes (TalkBack "Not sent: <text>") and **"Try again"** (`watch.thread.retry`), which reuses the key.
  - Failure messages: "Couldn't send. No connection — try again near your phone or Wi-Fi." (transport), the server's message for a < 500 error with one, otherwise "Couldn't send. Try again."
- No watch outbox. No voice note from the wrist, for any role.
- **Clearing:** sign-out, the lease running out, or another account on the phone clears the rooms, the pending room and the visible thread. A generation counter drops loads that started for the last account.
- **Debug extras** (§6.15.2): `gradusWatchOpen messages | first-room` and `gradusWatchSignedIn` (start signed in without a paired phone). Mock rooms are iOS's invented ones: Renata Pruitt (coach), Greta and Ingrid Halvorsen (athlete room), Tobias Fairbank (coach-to-coach room, coach mock only).

**Tests.**
- Port `WatchMessagesTests` case for case:
  - `aTappedMessageNotificationOpensItsRoom`, `theHomeTakesTheNotificationsRoomOnce`, `anotherAccountsNotificationOpensAndSendsNothing`
  - `aRoomTappedDuringARecordingWaitsForItToEnd`, `aRoomWaitsWhileAPlanDraftOrWrapUpScreenIsOpen`
  - `aReplyOnTheWatchSendsWithItsOwnSessionAndSaysWhenItFails`
  - `roomsLoadNewestFirstWithTheirUnreadCounts`, `roomsThatFailToLoadSayWhy`, `signingOutClearsEveryConversation`
  - `aConversationShowsTheLatestTwentyAndReadsTheRoom`, `aRefreshDoesNotMarkTheConversationReadButOpeningItDoes`, `aReadConversationIsNotMarkedAgain`
  - `aForbiddenReplyIsNotKeptForTryAgain`, `rowsNameTheSenderAndPointVoiceNotesToTheIPhone` (the phone), `aQuickReplySendsExactlyThatText`, `aDictatedReplyIsTrimmedAndBlankOnesAreIgnored`
  - `aRefusalShowsTheServersWordsAndIsNotKept`, `aFailedReplyKeepsTheTextAndTryAgainReusesItsKey`
  - `aPausedConversationSendsNothing`, `aMissingConversationSaysSo`, `aNotificationWhileOpenRefreshesTheConversationOnScreen`, `theAthleteMockSeesTheRoomFromTheirSeat`
- Android additions:
  - The bridging switch is set and cleared with the session and with notification permission.
  - The watch listener posts, replaces and cancels per DataItem event and ignores items older than 24 h or arriving while signed out.
  - The phone deletes the room's DataItem when its notification is cancelled.
  - Compose for Wear screenshots of every state above at the default and largest font size.
- Pixel Watch QA (iOS §10.11 "Messages on the wrist"): a real message notification on the watch; tap → the thread; Reply on the notification; Reply in the thread by voice and by keyboard; a quick reply; the voice-note row; a minor athlete replies by voice and the web receives text; the signed-out watch shows the bridged phone copy whose Reply still sends; dismissing on either device clears both.

## 8. Design system on Android

**Intent (iOS §8, decision #10, and the October 2026 redesign).** The coach's-notebook, editorial-print feel carries over unchanged:
- paper backgrounds with soft washes and ruled lines;
- EB Garamond display type, set heavier since the redesign;
- Atkinson Hyperlegible body text;
- a hand-drawn pen layer that marks only a change, a check, or what you are editing right now.

Since the "Show, don't tell" redesign, content cards are **borderless** (soft fill and shadow only), each screen has **one lime action**, and every sheet closes with **"Close" at the top start**.

Gradus typography and color tokens are kept. Navigation, gestures, controls, system surfaces and motion are **native Android**: Material 3 components in Jetpack Compose, restyled with Gradus tokens, and never with dynamic color. A coach who uses both platforms recognizes Gradus instantly on either and never feels they are on a web page. Under A2 the only differences from iOS are where iOS uses an iOS-native element. Every such element is named below with its Android equivalent.

**Sources of truth, in this order:**
1. **The design decisions:** `docs/design/show-dont-tell-handoff.md` and its canvas, https://claude.ai/artifact/6bUwfU8oiUGMP6HhrPrLuQ. The canvas has light and dark boards for every redesigned screen and is the visual reference for spacing and composition.
2. **The iOS reference implementation:** gradus-ios `origin/main` at `c8f83d6`. That is the redesign as merged (`ad1e9bf`, #136) and its follow-ups through `c8f83d6`, read for this section. The redesign changed these files:
   - `Packages/GradusDesign/Sources/GradusDesign/**`: `Components/Controls.swift`, `PenMarks.swift`, `StepDots.swift`, `States.swift`, `Surfaces.swift`, `Toast.swift`, `FlowBars.swift`, `HelpBubble.swift`, `MoveRatingsList.swift`, plus `Fonts.swift` and `Generated/Tokens.swift`;
   - `Contract/design-tokens.json`;
   - `Gradus/Shell/RoleTabsView.swift`.

   The pre-redesign files this section also draws on are unchanged since `91c6af2`: `Appearance.swift`, `scripts/generate-colors.{sh,swift}`, `RootView.swift`, `LockWindow.swift`, `Roles.swift` and the app icon set.

   Where the handoff and this code disagree, **the code wins**, because it is later. Each case is flagged *code wins*, and §8.6.9 lists them all. Where the iOS PRD §8 text and the code disagree, the code also wins (A2).
3. **The token contract:** `Contract/design-tokens.json` at web `18a7bf0` (§8.2).

The iOS mock-only launch flags behind the canvas screenshots (`-GradusDemoClean`, `-GradusDemoVoiceLive`, `-GradusDemoChanges`, `-GradusDemoReactions`, `-GradusDemoGradusNote`, `-GradusDemoResultForm`, `-GradusDemoChartSelect`; handoff §9) are **not** ported, and the screens they fake are not built until the API exists (§12 N95, N96).

**Android module.** Everything in this section lives in the Gradle module `:core:design` (the `GradusDesign` equivalent; module layout §9), package `training.gradus.design`. Feature modules use only these composables and tokens: no raw `Color(0xFF…)`, no `MaterialTheme.colorScheme` reads for brand colors, no hard-coded font families (the same rule the web follows in `gradus-coach-start/CLAUDE.md`: semantic tokens only, never hex). A lint check (custom Android Lint or detekt rule) fails the build on `Color(0x` and `FontFamily(` outside `:core:design`.

### 8.1 Typography

**Bundled families (iOS §8.1; Fonts.swift).** All four are SIL OFL 1.1 and ship inside the app; nothing is downloaded at runtime (no Google Fonts provider, no downloadable fonts), so text renders identically offline and on first launch.

| Role | Web token | iOS (Fonts.swift) | Android `res/font/` file (renamed: lowercase, underscores, as Android resources require) | Usage rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Display / headings | `--font-display` EB Garamond | `Font.gradusDisplay(style, weight: .bold)` from `EBGaramond-VariableFont.ttf`, `EBGaramond-Italic-VariableFont.ttf` | `eb_garamond_variable.ttf`, `eb_garamond_italic_variable.ttf` | Page titles, sheet titles, section headings, `StateView` titles, names on cards. Default weight **Bold (700)** since the redesign (Fonts.swift: "heavier titles and hero numbers read more current; was semibold"). **Hero numbers** use **Heavy (800)** (§8.6.3). The web's headings are still SemiBold (600); this is an intentional native-app change, not a token. |
| Wordmark | `--font-wordmark` Fraunces | `Font.gradusWordmark(...)`, used **only** by `LaunchView` ("Gradus", largeTitle) | `fraunces_variable.ttf`, `fraunces_italic_variable.ttf` | The "Gradus" wordmark on the launch screen and nowhere else (2026-09-11 display-font switch). A lint rule forbids `GradusFonts.wordmark` outside `LaunchScreen`. |
| Body / UI | `--font-sans` Atkinson Hyperlegible | `Font.gradusBody(style, weight:)` from four static files | `atkinson_hyperlegible_regular.ttf`, `atkinson_hyperlegible_bold.ttf`, `atkinson_hyperlegible_italic.ttf`, `atkinson_hyperlegible_bold_italic.ttf` | All body, UI, buttons, chips, fields, eyebrows, toasts. Only Regular (400) and Bold (700) exist; a requested SemiBold resolves to Bold (Compose picks the closest; state it in the `FontFamily` so it is deterministic). |
| Numbers / labels | `--font-mono` JetBrains Mono | `Font.gradusMono(style, weight:)` with `.monospacedDigit()` | `jetbrains_mono_variable.ttf`, `jetbrains_mono_italic_variable.ttf` | Scores, timers, invite codes, start positions, percentages in `FlowBars`, the HelpBubble badge and meta, the SlideToConfirm hint. Always `fontFeatureSettings = "tnum"` (tabular figures). |
| Hand accent | `--font-hand` (aliased to Atkinson on the web) | Not bundled | Not bundled | If the hand style returns, add Caveat to both apps together (iOS §8.1). |

- **Variable fonts.** EB Garamond, Fraunces and JetBrains Mono are variable TTFs. Declare each weight used as its own `Font(R.font.eb_garamond_variable, weight = FontWeight.Bold, variationSettings = FontVariation.Settings(FontVariation.weight(700)))`. Compose `FontVariation` needs API 26+, so it is fine at minSdk 29 (A6).
  - Weights in use at iOS `c8f83d6`:
    - display 400, 700 (default), 800 (`.heavy`: hero numbers in the invoicing collected total, competition placings and the practice line's "% just right"), and `.black` once, on the celebration cover;
    - mono 400, 700 and `.black` (the HelpBubble badge);
    - body 400 and 700.
  - Axis ranges, read from the bundled files' `fvar` tables:
    - EB Garamond `wght` runs 400–800, so a requested 900 (`.black`) renders as 800. Android declares 800 for both `.heavy` and `.black`.
    - JetBrains Mono runs 100–800, so its `.black` also renders as 800.
    - Fraunces runs 100–900.
  - A Robolectric test asserts each declared weight is inside its file's axis.
- **Font licenses.** Copy the four `Resources/Fonts/Licenses/OFL-*.txt` files into `:core:design/src/main/assets/licenses/`. Settings → Legal → Open-source licenses lists them under **Fonts** exactly as iOS `LicensesView` does (EB Garamond, Fraunces, Atkinson Hyperlegible, JetBrains Mono, each "SIL Open Font License 1.1" with its URL); the **Packages** and **Build tools** sections list the Android dependencies instead of the Swift ones (see §9).
- **No registration step.** iOS registers fonts with CoreText at launch (`GradusFonts.register()`, also in the widget process). Android loads `res/font` resources directly; nothing to register. The parity test "all bundled font families register" (`GradusDesignTests.swift`) becomes a Robolectric test that each `FontFamily` resolves a typeface for every declared weight.

**Text styles.** iOS calls every font through a `Font.TextStyle` with `relativeTo:` so it scales with Dynamic Type; the sizes are Apple's defaults at the Large content size (Fonts.swift `pointSize`). Android keeps the **same style names and the same sizes in sp** (1 pt ≈ 1 dp at default density), in a `GradusTypeScale` object exposed through `LocalGradusType`, and also fills the Material 3 `Typography` slots so stock components (dialogs, menus, snackbars, date pickers, segmented buttons) render in Gradus faces.

| iOS `Font.TextStyle` | Size (pt → sp) | Line height (sp; Apple default leading) | Android `GradusTypeScale` name | Material 3 slot it also fills | Typical family |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.extraLargeTitle` | 44 | 52 | `extraLargeTitle` | `displayMedium` | display (unused in 1.0 screens; kept for parity with the switch) |
| `.extraLargeTitle2` | 36 | 43 | `extraLargeTitle2` | `displaySmall` | display |
| `.largeTitle` | 34 | 41 | `largeTitle` | `headlineLarge` | display (PageTitle, wordmark, timer digits in mono) |
| `.title` | 28 | 34 | `title` | `headlineMedium` | display |
| `.title2` | 22 | 28 | `title2` | `headlineSmall` | display (StateView title, lock screen title) |
| `.title3` | 20 | 25 | `title3` | `titleLarge` (dialog titles) | display |
| `.headline` | 17 | 22 | `headline` | `titleMedium` | body, bold |
| `.body` | 17 | 22 | `body` | `bodyLarge` | body (buttons bold) |
| `.callout` | 16 | 21 | `callout` | `bodyMedium` | body |
| `.subheadline` | 15 | 20 | `subheadline` | `titleSmall`, `labelLarge` (bold) | body (toasts, ErrorLine, chips) |
| `.footnote` | 13 | 18 | `footnote` | `bodySmall` | body |
| `.caption` | 12 | 16 | `caption` | `labelMedium` | body bold (Eyebrow, tags, chip buttons) |
| `.caption2` | 11 | 13 | `caption2` | `labelSmall` | body bold / mono (FlowBars captions, badges) |

- **Minimum body size** is 17 sp at the default font scale (iOS §8.1). Android's Material default body is 16 sp; Gradus overrides it.
- **Line length.** iOS caps line length at ~70 characters on iPad; phones only in 1.0 (A4), so this applies with the deferred adaptive layouts. Screens that set a readable max width on iOS (`frame(maxWidth: 640)` on Goals, 360 on `StateView` messages, 340 on `HelpBubble`) keep the same values in dp via `Modifier.widthIn(max = …)`.
- **Dynamic Type → font scale.** All text sizes are `sp`, so they follow **Settings → Display → Font size** (`Configuration.fontScale`). On Android 14+ (API 34) the platform applies **nonlinear font scaling up to 200%**: large styles grow less than small ones, which is the same shape as iOS Dynamic Type; line heights declared in `sp` scale proportionally with it. On Android 10–13 scaling is linear and stock settings top out lower (about 130%). Never use `dp` for text, never `TextUnit` arithmetic that defeats nonlinear scaling (use `LocalDensity.current.fontScale`/`FontScaling` APIs only for icon sizing, below).
- **"Accessibility sizes".** iOS switches layouts at `dynamicTypeSize.isAccessibilitySize` (AX1 and up, body ≥ 28 pt, i.e. ≥ 1.65× Large). Android has no named categories; the equivalent threshold is **`fontScale >= 1.5f`** (the "largest" stock steps on Android 14+ are 1.5, 1.8, 2.0). Expose it once as `LocalIsAccessibilitySize` in `:core:design`; every reflow rule that iOS keys on `isAccessibilitySize` keys on this (AdaptiveStack, segmented → menu, FlowBars stacking).
- **Icons track text (WCAG 1.4.4).** iOS `Font.gradusIcon(style)` scales SF Symbols with Dynamic Type; `gradusDiscIcon()` caps an icon inside a fixed disc at `xxxLarge` (≈1.35×) so it never spills out of its 56 dp circle. Android: `GradusIcon(symbol, style)` sizes the vector at `style.fontSize` converted to dp *with* font scale (so it grows with text), and `GradusDiscIcon` clamps the scale factor at **1.35**.
- **Bold text.** Android 12+ (API 31) "Bold text" sets `Configuration.fontWeightAdjustment`; Compose applies it to text automatically (verify on Compose BOM at build start). Atkinson's only heavier face is Bold, so regular text becomes Bold.
- **Uppercase.** iOS uses `.textCase(.uppercase)` (never `uppercased()`) so VoiceOver reads the original words (audit P7, 77 sites). Android: render `text.uppercase(Locale.US)` but set the semantics `contentDescription` (or `text` via `semantics { text = AnnotatedString(original) }`) to the original-case string so TalkBack does not spell capitals. Applies to `Eyebrow`, `HelpBubble` titles, `FlowBars` labels, `SlideToConfirm` hints, timestamps.
- **Invite codes are spelled out** (iOS `.speechSpellsOutCharacters()`): Android sets `contentDescription` to the code with spaces between characters ("A 7 K Q …"), or uses `TtsSpan.VerbatimBuilder` in an `AnnotatedString`.
- **Shrink-to-fit (`minimumScaleFactor`).** In-app sites: `GoalCardParts.swift:137` (0.6) and the score-sheet column labels in `ResultsAndScore.swift:249` (mono caption2 Bold, tracking 0.6, `lineLimit(1)`, 0.7). Android: Compose `Text(autoSize = TextAutoSize.StepBased(minFontSize = <factor> × style.fontSize, maxFontSize = style.fontSize))` with `maxLines = 1` at exactly these two sites (Compose foundation 1.8+, verify the API at build start); nowhere else (the no-truncation rule in §8.5 still holds).
- **Notifications and Live Updates.** iOS `BoardLiveActivity` and `SessionLiveActivity` render in `.gradusBody`/`.gradusMono` (fonts registered in the widget process) with `minimumScaleFactor` 0.8/0.85/0.5 (`BoardLiveActivity.swift:151`). Android ongoing and Live Update notifications are `RemoteViews`-backed system templates and use the **system font**: bundled `res/font` families cannot be applied to standard notification styles (verify). Tabular elapsed time comes from the system chronometer (`setUsesChronometer`). There is no shrink-to-fit in notifications, so notification strings are written short (title ≤ 1 line at default scale; content owned by §6.9/§7.10). Glance widget fonts: Appendix G Widgets row and §12.
- **Markdown** (Ask Gradus answers, help text): iOS renders via `AttributedString`. Android parses the same Markdown subset into an `AnnotatedString` (bold, italic, links, lists) in `:core:design`; no WebView. Ask Gradus is hidden in 1.0 (#22), but the renderer is built because other screens use it.

### 8.2 Color tokens

**One token file, three clients (iOS §8.2).** `gradus-coach-start/scripts/export-design-tokens.ts` converts the OKLCH values in `src/styles.css` to sRGB for light and dark and writes `docs/api/design-tokens.json` (CI keeps it current).
- gradus-android vendors that file in `Contract/design-tokens.json`, together with `openapi.json` and `vectors/`.
- It is pinned by `Contract/SOURCE_COMMIT` and updated by the same `scripts/sync-contract.sh` flow as iOS (§9).
- **The JSON is the source of truth**, not the iOS PRD's table. Several PRD values predate the 2026-09 accessibility token changes (*code wins*): for example `background` light is `#F3F6F9`, not the PRD's `#F5F6FA`, and `destructive` light is `#A20519` after audit P6.

**What the redesign did to the tokens: almost nothing.** The 58 colors and 41 aliases are the same set at web `18a7bf0` as at `fd543a12`, and iOS `Colors.xcassets` has the same 58 colorsets. The only value change is the softer dark-mode attention wash (web #242, iOS `d4a3a15`): `attention-wash` and `pen-orange-wash` dark went from `#531800` to **`#412714`** (`oklch(0.3 0.05 55)`).

Everything else the redesign introduced is a **component constant, not a token**, so Android hard-codes it in `:core:design`, exactly where iOS does:
- `cardEdge` is clear;
- display Bold and hero Heavy;
- the hero stripe's dark fade of 0.35;
- the pen strokes;
- the practice-line zone at 30%.

`numbers.page-title-stripe-opacity` (dark 0.7) is still the web's value. Native apps use 0.35 (*code wins*, below).

**Generator.** The `:core:design:generateTokens` Gradle task (Kotlin, in `build-logic`, §9.1; it needs no tool beyond the JDK Android Studio bundles) reads `Contract/design-tokens.json` and writes, under `:core:design/src/main/kotlin/training/gradus/design/generated/`:

| Generated file | Contents | iOS counterpart |
|---|---|---|
| `GradusColors.kt` | `data class GradusColors(...)` with one `Color` property per token in `colors` (58 at SOURCE_COMMIT `18a7bf0`, unchanged in number since `fd543a12`), camelCased exactly as iOS `camel()` does (`pen-tennis-wash` → `penTennisWash`, `text-secondary` → `textSecondary`); `val LightGradusColors` and `val DarkGradusColors` instances; KDoc on each: "`--name` — light #…, dark #…". Alpha is preserved (`card`, `elevated` are translucent). | `Colors.xcassets` (one colorset per token) + `GradusColor` in `Tokens.swift` |
| `GradusColorAliases.kt` | The 41 `colorAliases` as properties delegating to `GradusColors` (`border` → `divider`, `primary` → `accent`, `muted-foreground` → `textSecondary`, `destructive` → `destructiveInk`, `destructive-fill` → `destructive` …) | `GradusColorAlias` |
| `GradusRadius.kt` | `sm 8.dp, md 14.dp, default 14.dp, lg 20.dp, xl 28.dp, xl2 36.dp, xl3 44.dp, pill (4xl = 9999) → CircleShape/50%` | `GradusRadius` |
| `GradusFontStack.kt` | The five `fonts` stacks as `List<String>` (first entry is the bundled family) | `GradusFontStack` |
| `GradusNumbers.kt` | `numbers` (`logoStripeOpacity` dark 0.7, `pageTitleStripeOpacity` dark 0.7; light null) | not generated on iOS (PageTitle hard-codes 0.35, see below) |
| `GradusWearColors` (generated into `:core:design`, used by `:wear`) | Dark values only, as literals | The `#if os(watchOS)` dark literals in `Tokens.swift` |

- **Rules carried over from `generate-colors.swift`.** Tokens are emitted in sorted order. **Naming differs deliberately for radii:** Swift's `camel()` emits `_2xl`, `_3xl`, `_4xl`; the Kotlin generator emits `2xl` → `xl2`, `3xl` → `xl3`, `4xl` → `pill` (value 9999, emitted as `CircleShape`/50% rather than a 9999 dp corner), and the keyword `default` → `` `default` ``. A generator unit test asserts exactly these names (`GradusRadius.xl2 == 36.dp`, `xl3 == 44.dp`, `pill` is a 50% shape, `` GradusRadius.`default` == 14.dp ``). A **dark-only token falls back to its dark value in light** (`ink-navy`) and a light-only token to its light value; the generator starts clean so a removed token disappears.
- **CI drift check.** The Android CI job runs `./gradlew :core:design:generateTokens` and `git diff --exit-code -- core/design/src/main/kotlin/training/gradus/design/generated` (§9.6); any difference fails the build ("generated tokens are stale relative to Contract/design-tokens.json; run scripts/sync-contract.sh"). Same posture as iOS §9.6.
- **Parity tests** (port of `GradusDesignTests.swift`): every token in the JSON exists in both `LightGradusColors` and `DarkGradusColors`; **the accent swaps hue between light and dark** (chartreuse `#C0DD27` → cyan `#67DEF2`, hue difference > 0.2 in HSB, exactly the iOS assertion); radii `sm 8, md 14, lg 20, xl 28`; and a new JVM contrast test that computes WCAG ratios from the generated values for the pairs §8.5 promises (below).
- **No dynamic color.** Material You `dynamicLightColorScheme`/`dynamicDarkColorScheme` are **never** used: the accent must be Gradus chartreuse/cyan on every device. `MaterialTheme` is built from Gradus tokens only.
- **Derived, non-generated theme values** (in `GradusTheme`, next to the generated colors; they are not in the JSON):
  - `cardEdge`: `Color.Transparent`, or `borderStrong` when `LocalIncreasedContrast` is true (A62).
  - `heroStripe`: `pageTitleStripe`, at alpha 1 in light and **0.35** in dark.
  - `penStrokeBoost`: +1 dp when `LocalIncreasedContrast`, else 0.
  - A unit test pins each of these.
- **Material 3 slot mapping** (so stock components look right without per-call overrides):

| M3 `ColorScheme` slot | Gradus token | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `primary` / `onPrimary` | `accent` / `accentForeground` | Filled buttons, switches' checked track, progress |
| `primaryContainer` / `onPrimaryContainer` | `elevated` / `foreground` | No new token (iOS has no accent-wash token). Stock components that default to `primaryContainer` for a selected or primary state (M3 `FloatingActionButton` default container, `DatePicker` selected-day/today container, `SegmentedButton` active container, `NavigationBar` indicator) are overridden explicitly at the call site in `:core:design` to `accent` / `accentForeground` (indicator per the TabView row in §8.3). |
| `secondary`, `secondaryContainer` / on- | `secondaryAccent`, `secondaryAccentWash` / `secondaryAccentInk` | |
| `tertiary` / `onTertiary` | `attention` / `attentionForeground` | |
| `background` / `onBackground` | `background` / `foreground` | |
| `surface` / `onSurface` | `popover` / `foreground` | Opaque surface for dialogs, menus, sheets |
| `surfaceVariant` / `onSurfaceVariant` | `elevated` / `textSecondary` | |
| `surfaceContainerLowest…Highest` | `popover` (all five) | Prevents M3's tonal tints; Gradus surfaces are flat |
| `surfaceTint` | `Color.Transparent` | No elevation tint |
| `outline` / `outlineVariant` | `borderStrong` / `divider` | `borderStrong` is the 3:1 boundary (WCAG 1.4.11) |
| `error` / `onError` | `destructive` / `destructiveForeground` | Fill for "Delete my account" |
| `errorContainer` / `onErrorContainer` | `penPinkWash` / `destructiveInk` | |
| `scrim` | `Color.Black` at 32% | Sheet and dialog scrim |
| `inverseSurface` / `inverseOnSurface` | `foreground` / `background` | |

Feature code reads Gradus tokens from `GradusTheme.colors` (a `CompositionLocal`), never from `MaterialTheme.colorScheme`, so a later Material change cannot alter brand colors.

- **Radii (iOS §8.2):** cards `lg` 20, sheets `xl` 28 (ModalBottomSheet top corners), chips and pills `pill`, buttons, fields and picker fields `md` 14, tags `sm` 8, `PenCheckbox` square 6.
  - iOS uses `RoundedRectangle(style: .continuous)` (squircle corners). Android uses `RoundedCornerShape` (circular arcs). This is the iOS-native shape: Android uses the platform's shape and does not emulate squircles.
- **Shadow (Surfaces.swift at `c8f83d6`, *code wins* over the 91c6af2 values).** The content-card shadow is black at **7%**, radius **14**, y-offset **5**, and none under Increase Contrast.
  - Android: `Modifier.dropShadow(shape, Shadow(radius = 14.dp, offset = DpOffset(0.dp, 5.dp), color = Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.07f)))` (Compose 1.9+; verify the API name at build start). The fallback is `Modifier.shadow` with `ambientColor`/`spotColor` at the same alpha.
  - FAB and HelpBubble: black 18%, radius 10/8/12, y 6/4/6, as in the Swift code. The collapsed "Get set up" pill: 18%, radius 8, y 4. Toasts: black 12%, radius 16, y 6. Room rows and message bubbles: 6%, radius 12/8, y 4/3.
- **Translucent cards.** iOS draws `.ultraThinMaterial` (a backdrop blur) beneath the `card` token. Android has no system backdrop material for arbitrary views. **Android 1.0 draws the `card` token over a `background`-colored underlay at 60% alpha, with no blur**: it softens the ruled lines and washes behind the card the way the blur does, keeps the token alpha, and costs nothing. Roborazzi screenshots are compared side by side with iOS screenshots of the same mock screens (Roster, Plans, Settings, a room) in both modes. A real backdrop blur (RenderEffect-based, e.g. the Haze library) is an open question (§12), not a 1.0 requirement.
- **Theme follows Appearance (iOS §8.2; Appearance.swift).** `AppearancePreference` = **System / Light / Dark**, titles exactly "System", "Light", "Dark", stored locally under key `gradus.appearance` (Android: Preferences DataStore, same key, default `system`). Applied at the root: `GradusTheme(darkTheme = when (pref) { system -> isSystemInDarkTheme(); light -> false; dark -> true })`; on API 31+ also call `UiModeManager.setApplicationNightMode(...)` so the splash screen, `BiometricPrompt`, Credential Manager's bottom sheet and other system-drawn surfaces follow the in-app choice (API 29–30: in-app content only). *Code wins:* the PRD says the preference is "mirrored to the profile so web and app agree"; at HEAD iOS stores it on the device only (`@AppStorage`, no server write), so Android does the same.
- **System bars.** Edge-to-edge (§8.4): status bar and navigation bar are transparent; icon appearance follows the resolved theme (`WindowInsetsControllerCompat.isAppearanceLightStatusBars = !dark`), not the system theme, when the user forces Light/Dark.
- **PaperBackground (Surfaces.swift), exact recipe.** `background` fill, then two radial washes, then ruled lines; Android draws it once per screen in `Modifier.drawBehind` behind the `Scaffold` content, extending under the system bars (edge-to-edge, like `.ignoresSafeArea()`).
  - Light: `penPool` @34% radial, center (1.0, 0.0) of the size, radius `max(w,h) × 0.9`; `accent` @28% radial, center (0.0, 1.0), radius `max(w,h) × 0.8`.
  - Dark: `penPool` @18%, center (0.7, 0.3), radius `max(w,h) × 1.1`; `accent` @10%, center (0.05, 1.0), radius `w × 0.6`.
  - Ruled lines: 1 dp lines of `foreground` every 32 dp starting at y = 31 dp, opacity 7% light / 3% dark; not hit-testable.
  - Increase Contrast (§8.5): flat `background`, no washes, no ruled lines.
- **PageTitle (States.swift).** EB Garamond `largeTitle` **Bold** (the new display default) in `textPrimary`, with a heading role.
  - **Stripe:** a 10 dp `pageTitleStripe` bar behind the bottom of the text, offset −6 dp from the bottom edge. In dark mode it is drawn at **0.35** opacity so the lower glyphs keep 7:1 (*code wins* over the token file's `page-title-stripe-opacity` 0.7, which is the web's value).
  - **Accessory row (iOS `d23ab4a`).** `PageTitle(text, accessory = {…})` carries a trailing accessory, then **Live**, in the title row. The accessory is a screen's own action or status: "N to sync", Messages' "New" chip.
    - On a tab root with `showsLiveBoard` the Live control is a text button (§8.4).
    - The row is laid out **fit-or-stack**: one row when title, accessory and Live all fit at their full size; otherwise the controls drop under the title, never squeezing it. Android uses a `SubcomposeLayout` that measures the title at its intrinsic width.
    - At `LocalIsAccessibilitySize` the controls always sit under the title, with no empty second row when there are no controls.
- **Watch, widgets, notifications.** Wear OS has no light mode for Gradus: the Wear app uses the **dark** token values (generated `GradusWearColors`), as watchOS does. Glance widgets (Practice goals and Today, §6.9.7; there is no Live Board widget, #55) use `ColorProvider(day = light, night = dark)` from the same generated tokens, with **ink** tokens for colored text and marks, never raw pen tints (audit P6). Live Update / ongoing notifications cannot be colorized (`setColorized(true)` disqualifies promotion); they set only `setColor(accentInk)` for the small-icon tint.

### 8.3 Component mapping

Every public type in `GradusDesign` and every iOS idiom the feature packages use has its Android equivalent below. Android names live in `:core:design` unless stated. "Same" means the behavior, numbers and copy in the iOS column are reproduced exactly. Components added by the redesign are specified in full in §8.6 and only summarized here.

**GradusDesign components**

Settings → Appearance row is a segmented control (below) with the section header "Appearance"; TalkBack reads "Appearance, System". |
| `GradusFonts`, `Font.gradusDisplay/Wordmark/Body/Mono`, `Font.TextStyle.pointSize` (Fonts.swift) | Families, style sizes, Dynamic Type | `GradusFonts` (`FontFamily` objects), `GradusTypeScale`, `GradusTheme.type` | §8.1 |

Registers/unregisters its message with `ToastCenter` in `DisposableEffect(message)` so the counting rules match `errorShownInline`/`errorHiddenInline`. |
| `ToastCenter` + `.toastHost()` (Toast.swift) | Bottom-anchored toasts (Sonner on the web): kinds `info` (`info.circle.fill`, `penPoolInk`), `success` (a **pen check**, `PenMarkView(.check)` in `penTennisInk`, seed 17, line 2.2, 18 pt), `error` (`exclamationmark.triangle.fill`, `destructiveInk`); message subheadline `textPrimary` on `popover`, radius 14, **no border** (`cardEdge`, clear since the redesign; `borderStrong` under Increase Contrast on Android, A62), 16 side and 12 bottom margins, min height 44. **Info/success auto-dismiss** after `3 s + characters/20 s`, ×1.6 while VoiceOver runs, capped at 8 s; **errors never auto-dismiss** (WCAG 2.2.1) and show a visible ✕ ("Dismiss"); touching pauses the countdown and releasing resumes with the time left (min 0.3 s); swipe down or tap anywhere dismisses; a new toast replaces the current one and cancels its timer; `screenChanged()` (tab change or push/pop) clears an **error** toast older than **500 ms**; every toast is announced ("Error: …" for errors); every error is also sent to the error reporter (`onError` → `POST /errors`, §6.11) | `ToastCenter` (app-scoped, Hilt singleton) + `GradusToastHost` composable at the root, above the `NavigationBar` and IME | **Not** Material `SnackbarHost`: snackbar durations are fixed (4 s / 10 s / indefinite) and it has no swipe-down dismiss or inline-error suppression. The host draws the same visual, uses `AnimatedVisibility` (slide up + fade; fade only under Reduce Motion; 250 ms in, 200 ms out), `pointerInput` for press-pause/resume, `SwipeToDismissBox`-style vertical drag for dismissal, and `semantics { customActions = listOf(CustomAccessibilityAction("Dismiss") { … }) }` (merged label = the plain message; the ✕ has test tag `toast.dismiss`). **Announcements do not come from the drawn toast**: iOS `show()` posts the announcement ("Error: {message}" for errors) *before* the inline-suppression check, so an error already shown by an `ErrorLine` is still spoken although nothing is drawn. Android: `ToastCenter.show(message, kind, duration: Duration? = null)` (the optional override replaces the reading-time formula, as iOS's `duration:` parameter does) always calls `Announcer.announce(if (kind == ERROR) "Error: $message" else message)`. `Announcer` (`:core:design`) is a single hidden node at the root with `semantics { liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite; contentDescription = text }`; each call sets new text, appending an invisible counter suffix (zero-width) so a repeated identical message still changes the node and is re-announced. JVM test added: "an inline-suppressed error is still announced and still reported". "VoiceOver running" → `AccessibilityManager.isTouchExplorationEnabled`. Port all 11 `ToastCenterTests` cases to JVM tests with a fake clock (show/dismiss; info auto-dismiss; error never auto-dismisses; pause/resume; resume never restarts an error; screenChanged clears an old error; keeps an error raised by the navigation itself; leaves non-errors alone; inline suppression still reports; re-toasts after the inline line goes; a new show cancels a pending dismiss), plus the Android-added announcement test above. The host is drawn in the activity's content, so it sits **under** dialogs and bottom sheets, the same as iOS — which is why the inline suppression rule matters. |

**iOS idioms used by the feature packages**

| iOS idiom (where) | Android equivalent | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `TabView` with `Tab(title, systemImage)` per role, `.badge` on Messages, `.tint(accentInk)` (RoleTabsView.swift) | Material 3 `NavigationBar` + `NavigationBarItem` (icon + label always shown), selected indicator `accent` @ wash, selected icon/label `accentInk`, unselected `textSecondary`; Messages badge via `BadgedBox { Badge { Text(count) } }` | Tabs per role in §8.4. Badge = `unreadTotal`, hidden at 0; TalkBack reads "Messages, 3 unread" (stateDescription). |
| `NavigationStack(path:)` per tab, `navigationDestination(for: AppRoute.self)`, `.id(route)` on destinations | One Navigation Compose `NavHost` per tab with type-safe `@Serializable` routes; the shell holds each tab's `NavHostController`; each back-stack entry has its own `ViewModelStoreOwner` | §8.4. Route parameters key state per entry (the `.id(route)` lesson: a second `/g/` link must never show the first link's athlete). |
| `List { Section { rows } header: { Eyebrow("…") } footer: { Text(…) } }` with `.listRowBackground(GradusColor.card)` and `.scrollContentBackground(.hidden)` over `PaperBackground` (≈53 `List` sites, 34 header/footer sections, 50 `listRowBackground` uses; Settings and most account, connections, report and wrap-up screens). Example: `SettingsView` sections Profile, Verification, Family, Coaching, Safety, Plan, Appearance, Account, Legal, Support, Debug (debug builds), last footer "Gradus {version} ({build}) · {Role}" (caption, `textTertiary`, id `settings.version`; "No role yet" when role-less) | `GradusSectionedList { section(header = "Profile", footer = …) { row(…) } }` in `:core:design`: a `LazyColumn` with a transparent background over `PaperBackground`. Each section = `Eyebrow` header (heading semantics), then its rows grouped in **one** rounded container (`card` fill per the §8.2 underlay rule, radius `lg` 20, 1 dp `divider` border, 16 dp horizontal inset, `HorizontalDivider(color = divider)` between rows, none after the last), then the optional footer in the iOS site's style (Settings: caption `textTertiary`; elsewhere footnote/caption `textSecondary` as the Swift code sets). Rows that iOS gives `.listRowBackground(Color.clear)` (e.g. `WrapUpViews.swift:68`) draw no container. | **Not** Material `ListItem` defaults (their `surface`/tonal colors would show through) and not `Card`. Section spacing 24 dp, header 8 dp above the container. Same section order and header strings per role as the Swift code; test tags copied (`settings.profile`, `settings.athletes`, `settings.safeSport`, `settings.signOut`, `settings.version`…). |
| `NavigationLink { Dest } label: { row }` inside a `List` (≈20 sites) | `SettingsRow(title, icon?, value?, onClick, chevron = true)`: the whole row is one clickable target (`Modifier.clickable(role = Role.Button)`, 48 dp min height, 16 dp padding), leading Material Symbol (decorative, `contentDescription = null`), title in body `textPrimary`, value trailing in `textSecondary`, trailing `chevron_right` in `textTertiary` | Merged semantics: `contentDescription = "{title}, {value}"` (TalkBack: "Appearance, System"); press uses `gradusPress` (no ripple, §8.3 Press row). Destructive rows ("Sign out") use `destructiveInk` text and no chevron. Tapping pushes the destination on the current tab's back stack (§8.4). |

Pushed screens: `TopAppBar` (small) with a transparent container over the paper; actions in `actions = {}` | **One title per screen** (handoff §1.2). A pushed screen whose content starts with its own `PageTitle` or display heading has an **empty** top-bar title, just the back arrow: the plan editor and the runner plan (iOS `navigationTitle("")`), and every onboarding and sign-up step (iOS removed their bar titles in `ad1e9bf`). Core: `person.2`→`group`, `list.clipboard`→`assignment`, `books.vertical`→`library_books`, `bubble.left.and.bubble.right`→`forum`, `gearshape`→`settings`, `dot.radiowaves.left.and.right`→`sensors`, `plus`→`add`, `trash`→`delete`, `xmark`→`close`, `square.and.arrow.up`→`share`, `chevron.right`→`chevron_right`, `mic.fill`→`mic`, `wifi.exclamationmark`→`wifi_off`, `exclamationmark.circle`→`error`, `checkmark.circle.fill`→`check_circle`, `info.circle.fill`→`info`, `exclamationmark.triangle.fill`→`warning`, `faceid`/`touchid`→`fingerprint` (or `face` when only face unlock is enrolled), `figure.skating`→custom vector (Material has `ice_skating`), `figure.run`→`directions_run`, `chevron.up.chevron.down`→`unfold_more`, `ellipsis`→`more_horiz`, `pencil`→`edit`, `person.crop.circle`→`account_circle`, `calendar`→`calendar_month`, `speaker.wave.2.fill`→`volume_up`, `lock.fill`→`lock`, `arrowshape.turn.up.left`→`reply`, `face.smiling`→`add_reaction`, `minus`→`remove`. Sport glyphs Material lacks get a small custom vector set, as iOS planned for SF (§8.3 iOS "small custom symbol set"). Icons inside labeled controls are `contentDescription = null`. |
| Logo: navy-on-cream mark | Vector drawable of the three-bar mark (geometry in the app icon row below) | |
| `UIGestureRecognizerRepresentable` (`ChartScrub`, the practice line: begins on a 6 pt sideways drag or a 0.2 s hold, fails on a vertical swipe so the page scrolls) | `Modifier.pointerInput` + `awaitEachGesture` (§8.6.7) | |
| `ViewThatFits` (first layout that fits: lesson glance, goal fork, FlowBars captions, PageTitle row) | `SubcomposeLayout` that measures the candidates in order and places the first that fits | One helper, `FirstThatFits`, in `:core:design`; Roborazzi at 1.0/1.5/2.0. |

**App icon (Gradus/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset).** iOS ships three 1024×1024 variants: **light** (navy `#2D3340` background, three cream `#F7F5EF` rounded bars), **dark** (transparent background, the same cream bars, on Apple's dark backdrop) and **tinted** (white bars on transparent, which iOS tints). The colors are a brand rule ("App icon: navy `#2D3340` with three cream `#F7F5EF` bars", `docs/ios/handoff-preQA.md` §3), not tokens.

| iOS | Android |
|---|---|
| `AppIcon.png` (light) | **Adaptive icon** `mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml` (and `ic_launcher_round.xml`): `<background>` = solid `#2D3340`; `<foreground>` = vector `ic_launcher_foreground.xml` with the three bars in `#F7F5EF`. Geometry in the 108×108 dp canvas (iOS 1024 px mapped onto the 72 dp visible viewport, offset 18 dp; all inside the 66 dp safe circle): left bar x 36.00–46.34, y 49.71–72.00; middle bar x 48.80–59.20, y 36.00–72.00; right bar x 61.73–72.00, y 55.48–72.00; each a capsule with corner radius ≈ 5.17 dp. |
| `AppIcon-tinted.png` | `<monochrome>` layer (Android 13+ themed icons) = the same three bars, single color, transparent elsewhere. |
| `AppIcon-dark.png` | No Android equivalent: launchers have no dark-mode icon slot. Themed icons (monochrome) serve users who want a tinted look. |
| App Store 1024 icon | Play Store hi-res icon 512×512 32-bit PNG, full square (`#2D3340` with the bars at the same proportions); Google Play applies its own mask. |
| (none) | **Notification small icon** `ic_stat_gradus.xml`: the three bars, white on transparent (status bar requirement). Used by every FCM notification, the session-timer and Live Board ongoing notifications. |
| Watch app icon (`GradusWatch/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset`, same navy and cream artwork) | The `:wear` module is a separate APK with its own `mipmap` resources: a **round launcher icon** from the same vector — navy `#2D3340` disc, cream `#F7F5EF` bars, the glyph scaled to sit inside the 66 dp safe circle of the 108 dp canvas (Wear launchers apply a circular mask). Wear's `targetSdk` follows Google Play's **Wear OS** target-API requirement, which is set separately from phones (API 35+ for Wear apps from 2026-08-31 per developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/target-sdk — verify at submission); the latest level is preferred. |
| (legacy) | `mipmap-*/ic_launcher.webp` raster fallbacks are not needed at minSdk 29 (adaptive icons are API 26+), except the Play listing icon. |

**Splash and launch (iOS: empty `UILaunchScreen` then `LaunchView`).** iOS shows a system launch screen, then `LaunchView`: `PaperBackground`, the "Gradus" wordmark in Fraunces `largeTitle` SemiBold, `textPrimary`, and a spinner tinted `accentInk`, while `phase == .launching`. Android: the **SplashScreen API** (`androidx.core:core-splashscreen`, so API 29–30 get the same behavior): `windowSplashScreenBackground` = `background` token (light `#F3F6F9`, `values-night` `#03131A`), `windowSplashScreenAnimatedIcon` = the launcher foreground bars on a `#2D3340` disc (`windowSplashScreenIconBackgroundColor` `#2D3340`), no branding image, no animation; `installSplashScreen().setKeepOnScreenCondition { false }` (dismiss on first frame) — then Compose renders `LaunchScreen`, identical to iOS `LaunchView`, until the shell leaves `launching`. Never hold the system splash on network work.

**Platform copy substitutions.** User-facing iOS strings that name an iOS feature change to the Android equivalent; every other string is verbatim (A2).

Once live (`PLAY_LISTING_LIVE = true`): **"Update on Google Play"** (§7.1.0), opening `market://details?id=training.gradus.app` with a fallback to `https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=training.gradus.app` when no store app handles it. This mirrors the iOS comment (`RootView.swift`: the App Store link replaces the web link once the listing exists). |
| "Leaves Gradus right away and opens a Google search page in Safari." (SafetyExitButton hint) | "Leaves Gradus right away and opens a Google search page in your browser." |

| "Set up Face ID, Touch ID, or a passcode in iOS Settings to use this." | "Set up a fingerprint, face unlock, or a screen lock in Android Settings to use this." |
