### 8.4 Navigation and gestures

**Shell structure (RootView.swift, RoleTabsView.swift, Roles.swift).**

| State | iOS | Android |
|---|---|---|
| Launching | `LaunchView` | Splash then `LaunchScreen` (§8.3) |
| Below `minSupportedVersion` | `ForceUpdateView` (StateView `arrow.down.app`, "Update Gradus", policy message or "This version of Gradus is no longer supported. Please update to keep going.") | `ForceUpdateScreen`, same copy, action per §8.3 copy table (browser link until `PLAY_LISTING_LIVE`, then Google Play). Google Play In-App Updates is not used in 1.0 (§12 N37). |
| Signed out | **No tab bar** (Mariah, 2026-09-26; *code wins* over iOS PRD §8.3 and gradus-ios `docs/README.md`, which still say Live is a signed-out tab): one stack, `SignInView` → sign-up steps; a guardian/team link waiting for sign-in shows the banner "Use the email address this link was sent to."; a board link or QR code opens the **Live cover** over sign-in, and the board's own sign-in button closes the cover | Same: a single `NavHost` for sign-in and sign-up, no `NavigationBar`; the same banner; the Live cover as a full-screen destination above it |
| Signed in, profile-less / `/me` failed | `NoRoleView`: "Couldn't load your account" + "Try again"; (its org-admin branch, "Org admin is web-only" / "Manage your club at gradus.training. Coach, parent, and athlete accounts use the app." + "Sign out", is unreachable at HEAD because an org admin has a role and gets the tabs shell; ported as dead-code parity); age-signal wait "Checking this device…"; adult-roles blocked; pending guardian claim / team invite; else `RoleChooserView` | Same screens and copy (age signals per §6.13 use Play Age Signals) |
| Signed in, profile-less coach or parent sign-up, age signal not yet answered (`RootView.swift:77–81`) | A bare `ProgressView` tinted `accentInk` on `PaperBackground`, no text, while `ageSignals.requestIfNeeded()` runs (PRD §6.13 B1); if the answer blocks adult roles, the athlete-only role chooser follows | `AgeSignalWait`: `CircularProgressIndicator(color = accentInk)` centered on `PaperBackground`, no text, while the Play Age Signals request runs (§6.13); same branch after it |
| Onboarding gates, plan status | `CoachOnboardingGate`, `ParentOnboardingGate`, `AdultOnboardingGate`, `PlanStatusView` | Same, as full-screen graphs before the tab scaffold |
| Signed in with a role | `RoleTabsView` | `RoleScaffold`: `Scaffold(bottomBar = NavigationBar)` with one `NavHost` per tab |
| Settings dependencies not ready (store still opening) | `PlaceholderScreen(title: "Settings", systemImage: "gearshape", detail: "Preparing your local store…")` (also "Connections" with `link` for the connections route) | `PlaceholderScreen` with the same title, icon (`settings` / `link`) and detail text |
| A route whose screen does not exist (fallback) | `StateView(systemImage: "link", title: <route title>, message: "Opened from a link. This screen arrives with its feature milestone.")` | Same `StateView`, same copy (should be unreachable in 1.0; kept as the safe default) |
| A role opening a section it lacks | `StateView(systemImage: "person.crop.circle.badge.questionmark", title: "Not for this account", message: …)` | Same, icon `person_off` (Material Symbol closest to the badge-questionmark person), messages per the Settings-sections bullet below |


**Pushed-route titles** (`RoleTabsView.swift` `title`, used as the top app bar title):
- `Board` → "Live board"; `Room` → "Conversation"; `Plan`/`EditPlan` → "Plan" (but the editor and the runner themselves set an empty title; see the `.toolbar` row in §8.3); `Recap` → "Competition recap".
- `Settings(connections)` → "Connections"; other `Settings(section)` → "Settings · {section raw value}".
- `GuardianClaim` → "Guardian claim"; `TeamInvite` → "Team invite" (never the token); `SharedPlan` → "Shared plan"; anything else → "Gradus".
- `Settings(goals)` renders `GoalsScreen`: `PaperBackground`, `PageTitle("Goals")`, `GoalsDashboardView`, padding 20, max width 640 dp centered, title "Goals".

**Tab roots have no top app bar** (iOS `d23ab4a`; handoff §7 "there's no nav bar on root tabs"). Each tab root starts with its `PageTitle` row under `WindowInsets.statusBars`, as do Settings (now a serif `PageTitle`, not a system large title) and Messages.
| Over everything | Terms gate cover, password-reset cover, connection-celebration cover, parent-approval screen (blocks all), AI permission screen (§6.7.1a, A54), biometric lock window, toasts | Same order of precedence (§8.3 fullScreenCover row; lock in §8.5) |

**Tabs per role (Roles.swift `UserRole.tabs`, iPhone).** Live is never a tab on a phone: `visibleTabs` drops `.live` unless `liveIsTab`, which is iPad-only (`userInterfaceIdiom == .pad`, decision #50 keeps the iPad branch but 1.0 is iPhone only). Phones-only on Android (A4) ⇒ the same:

| Role | Tabs in order (label · iOS SF Symbol → Material Symbol) | Home tab (launch, unknown deep-link subpaths) |
|---|---|---|
| Coach | Roster (`person.2` → `group`) · Plans (`list.clipboard` → `assignment`) · Resources (`books.vertical` → `library_books`) · Messages (`bubble.left.and.bubble.right` → `forum`, unread badge) · Settings (`gearshape` → `settings`) | Roster |
| Parent | Plans · Messages (badge) · Resources · Settings | Plans |
| Athlete | Plans · Messages (badge) · Resources · Settings | Plans |
| Org admin | Settings only, with the Live top-bar action (iOS `orgAdmin.tabs = [.live, .settings]` with Live dropped on phones; `RoleTabsView` takes every non-nil role, so `NoRoleView`'s "Org admin is web-only" branch is unreachable at HEAD); no `NavigationBar` for a single destination (§6.9.1) | Settings |


- **Live Board entry.** On every tab root, when `me.showsLiveBoard` is true (figure-skating accounts; `true` when `/me` omits it), the **`PageTitle` row** ends with a text button **"Live"**:
  - It sits after the screen's accessory, with the radio-waves icon (`sensors`), headline Bold, `accentInk`.
  - Accessibility label "Live Board", test tag `tab.live`.
  - iOS supplies it through `pageTitleLiveAction`; Android through `LocalPageTitleLiveAction`. Pushed destinations reset it to null, so Live never shows on a pushed screen.

  It opens the **Live cover**:
  - A full-screen surface with its own back stack (`BoardIndexView` → `BoardView`), a "Close" text button at the top start (test tag `live.close`), and Back/predictive back popping within it, then closing it.
  - Board links (`/board/:slug`) open in the cover. The cover counts as `covered` for `PromptHold`.
  - **Tapping Live always resets the cover's stack to `BoardIndex`** (`AppModel.presentLive()` sets `paths[.live] = []`).
  - A board route (`/board`, `/board/:slug`, QR code, push) opens the cover for **every** account, even when `showsLiveBoard` is false and no Live action is shown (`AppModel.swift:1448`). `BoardIndex` opens with an empty stack, `Board(slug)` with that one entry.
  - A route into any tab closes the cover so the destination is visible.
- **Messages badge** = `unreadTotal` (`AppModel.refreshUnread()`), refreshed on sign-in, on return to foreground, on each realtime message insert (`listenForUnread`), and when a room screen leaves (`RoomView.onDisappear` → Android: the `Room` destination's `DisposableEffect` `onDispose`/`ON_STOP`); reset to 0 at sign-out and whenever signed out. An incoming FCM push also triggers a refresh (Android addition, harmless). The launcher shows a notification dot from posted notifications; no `setNumber` count in 1.0, because the push carries no unread total and iOS sets no icon badge at HEAD (§6.6.9, §7.5.10, §12 N31; QA.md's "…and the app icon badge" becomes "…and the launcher dot").
- **The running session bar.** For parents and athletes, `ActiveSessionBar` sits at the top of every tab root (`safeAreaInset(edge: .top)` on iOS). With no top app bar on tab roots, Android places it first in each tab root's content, under the status-bar inset and above the `PageTitle` row. Tapping it opens that plan (iOS §7.6 "persistent bar").
- **Tab analytics area** (iOS `analyticsArea`): roster → `roster`; plans → `plans` for coaches, `sessions` for parents/athletes; resources → `resources`; messages → `messages`; Live → `board`; settings → `settings`. Same values in Android's screen tracking (§6.12).

**Back stacks.**
- **One back stack per tab** (iOS `paths[tab]`, §8.4 iOS "One NavigationStack per tab"): each tab owns a `NavHostController` with its own `NavHost`; switching tabs keeps every stack. Implementation: a `rememberSaveable` map of tab → controller in the shell, or a single NavHost with nested graphs and `saveState/restoreState` on tab switch; either way, switching tabs and returning restores the stack and scroll positions. Process death restores stacks (`SavedStateHandle` + serializable routes).
- **Type-safe routes** mirror `AppRoute` (GradusCore/Routing/AppRoute.swift) one to one as `@Serializable` objects/data classes in `:core:data` (`routing` package, §9.1): `BoardIndex`, `Board(slug)`, `Invite(code)`, `Login`, `Signup(kind)`, `RoleHome`, `Room(id)`, `Rooms`, `Plans`, `Plan(id)`, `EditPlan(id)` (in-app only, never from a link or push), `Roster`, `UpNextBriefing(athleteId?)`, `Resources`, `Settings(section?)`, `WrapUps`, `Recap(competitionId)`, `GuardianClaim(token)`, `TeamInvite(token)`, `SharedPlan(token)`, `Verified(redirect)` — with the same `tab` assignment (`Board*` → Live cover; `Room(s)` → Messages; `Plans/Plan/EditPlan/SharedPlan/Recap` → Plans; `Roster/UpNextBriefing/WrapUps` → Roster; `Resources` → Resources; `Settings/GuardianClaim/TeamInvite` → Settings; `Login/Signup/Invite/RoleHome/Verified` → no tab) and the same `requiresSession` (false only for board routes, login, sign-up, invite, verified). `RouteParser` is ported to Kotlin with the iOS `RoutingTests` cases as JUnit tests (including the excluded prefixes `/privacy /terms /unsubscribe /admin /org-admin /api /email /lovable /reset-password`, `paywall` → Settings › Plan, `roster/briefing/<id>`, `settings/account`, and push payload `v == 1`).
- **Delivering a route** (iOS `open(_:)` sets `paths[tab] = [route]`): select the route's tab and replace that tab's stack with root + route (`navigate(route) { popUpTo(tabRoot) { inclusive = false } }`). A pushed route always gets a new back-stack entry, so per-parameter state never leaks between two links of the same kind.
- **Settings sections by link** (`gradus://settings/<section>`, `/coach|parent|athlete/settings/<section>`, push `settings/<section>`): `account`, `plan`, `connections`, `athletes`, `coaches`, `goals`, `device`, `legal`, `feedback` (pops to Settings root and opens the Feedback sheet), `safe-sport`; a role that lacks the section sees `StateView` "Not for this account" with the iOS messages ("Plans are managed by your coach or parent.", "My athletes is a parent screen.", "Coaches is an athlete screen. Parents link coaches from My athletes.", "Goals belong to parents and athletes.", "Connections are managed by your coach or parent.").
- **Reselecting the current tab** pops its stack to the root (Material navigation-bar behavior; iOS's tab bar does the same natively — verify the SwiftUI path-bound stack behaves so on iOS 26).
- **Error toasts clear on navigation**: any tab change or back-stack change calls `ToastCenter.screenChanged()` (RootView `onChange(of: selectedTab/paths)`).

**Back and predictive back.**
- Back is the system Back gesture/button; **no custom back buttons** in content (iOS §8.4 "No custom back buttons"). Top app bars show the standard navigation icon (arrow) on pushed screens.
- **Predictive back**: targetSdk is the latest Play requires (A6; API 36 for submissions from 2026-08-31), where predictive back animations are on by default and `onBackPressed()` is no longer called. All back handling uses `BackHandler`/`PredictiveBackHandler` and Navigation Compose's built-in predictive transitions; `ModalBottomSheet` and the Live cover animate with the gesture. Manifest `android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true"` for API 33–35 devices.
- Editors with unsaved changes intercept Back with the same "discard?" alert iOS uses where iOS does; nowhere else.

**Gestures and lists (iOS §8.4).**
- Long lists support **pull to refresh** (`PullToRefreshBox`), **swipe actions** (trailing delete, confirmed) and **context menus** (long-press), mapped in §8.3.
- No horizontal swipe between tabs (iOS has none); horizontal pagers only where iOS pages (week strip arrows on Roster are buttons, with swipe as an extra only if iOS supports it — it does not; keep buttons).

**Edge-to-edge, keyboard and safe areas.**
- `enableEdgeToEdge()` in `MainActivity` (mandatory behavior at targetSdk 35+; the opt-out is gone at 36). Content draws under transparent system bars; `Scaffold` and `WindowInsets.safeDrawing` pad interactive content; `PaperBackground` extends under the bars like iOS `.ignoresSafeArea()`.
- **The composer, session timer and voice recorder respect the keyboard and safe areas; nothing hides behind the navigation bar** (iOS §8.4): `Modifier.imePadding()` on the composer and timer controls; `android:windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize"`; display cutouts handled by `WindowInsets.displayCutout` in landscape.
- **Orientation.** iPhone supports portrait and both landscapes (project.yml `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations`; WCAG 1.3.4, iOS §8.5). Android never locks orientation; every screen, the Live cover, the composer, the timer, sheets and the board wheel work in landscape. Configuration changes are handled by Compose state and ViewModels (no `configChanges` overrides beyond defaults).
- **Tablets and foldables (A4, mirrors #50).** The app installs and runs the phone layout. On widths ≥ 600 dp Android 16 ignores orientation and resizability restrictions for apps targeting 36, so the phone layout must stay correct at any width: content columns get the iOS readable max widths (640 dp lists, 360 dp state messages) centered. The iPad designs (Live as a tab/rail item at expanded widths, two-column Roster and Messages) are specified in iOS §8.4 and deferred: on Android they become `NavigationSuiteScaffold` (rail at medium/expanded) and `ListDetailPaneScaffold` when adaptive layouts ship.

### 8.5 Motion, haptics, accessibility

**Motion (iOS §8.5).** Motion is short (≤ 250 ms) and purposeful. Exact values from the Swift code:
- press feedback 120 ms ease-out;
- toast in: spring 0.25 s (Android `spring(dampingRatio = 1f, stiffness ≈ Spring.StiffnessMediumLow)`, tuned to a 250 ms settle); toast out: 200 ms ease-out;
- HelpBubble open/close: spring 0.25 s from the anchor at scale 0.9;
- SlideToConfirm return spring (response 0.3, damping 0.75 → `spring(dampingRatio = 0.75f, stiffness = 400f)`);
- the text-field edge: 120 ms ease-out crossfade between the crisp edge and the EditingOutline;
- the move editor's pen/Done toggle and expand: snappy 0.2 s;
- category folds (`CategoryHeader`): snappy 0.2 s;
- the each-move check-in advancing to the next move: snappy 0.25 s after a 0.2 s pause;
- Board segmented pill: spring 0.28 s.

**Pen marks never draw on.** iOS renders every pen mark at once: no trim or stroke animation exists in `PenMarks.swift`. Android does the same, so there is nothing to suppress under Remove animations (handoff §1.4 "nothing draws on").

The two pulsing dots:
- **Live dot** (`BoardParts.swift` `LiveDot`, size 8 in a 2.4× frame): a solid `attention` dot plus an outer `attention` ring at 50%, scaling 1 → 2.2 while fading 0.7 → 0, 1.4 s ease-out, repeating without reversing, hidden from TalkBack.
- **Session pulsing dot** (`SessionControls.swift` `PulsingDot`): an 8 dp `attentionForeground` dot in a 14 dp ring at 60%, scaling 1 → 1.8 and fading to 0, 1.2 s ease-out, repeating.
- Android: `rememberInfiniteTransition` with `infiniteRepeatable(tween(1400 / 1200, easing = EaseOut), RepeatMode.Restart)`, created **only when `!LocalReduceMotion`**. Both dots are drawn still otherwise, as iOS skips `onAppear`'s animation.

Screen transitions are Navigation Compose's platform defaults (Android-native, as iOS uses the system push).

**Reduce Motion → "Remove animations" (A33).** iOS reads `accessibilityReduceMotion`.
- Android: `LocalReduceMotion` = `Settings.Global.getFloat(contentResolver, Settings.Global.ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE, 1f) == 0f`. That is set by Settings → Accessibility → Color and motion → **Remove animations**, or by the developer animator scale. It is observed with a `ContentObserver` so it updates live.
- When true:
  - no press scale (opacity only);
  - toasts and HelpBubble fade instead of moving or scaling;
  - SlideToConfirm snaps back without a spring;
  - **no confetti or zoom on the connection celebration**;
  - **the pulsing session dot is still**;
  - **the Live Board skater wheel does not spin**;
  - no skeleton shimmer;
  - **the EditingOutline appears and disappears instantly**;
  - category folds, move expand/collapse, the lesson card's open and the check-in's move advance change state without animating.
- Every animation in `:core:design` takes its spec from one helper that returns `snap()`/fade under this flag. Custom `Animatable`s must not hard-code durations that ignore `ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE`. Verify how Compose applies the scale at build time, and route custom animations through `LocalReduceMotion` regardless.

**Haptics (iOS §7.13, §8.5; Controls.swift `Haptics`, `PressButtonStyle`).** A light impact on primary actions and notification feedback on outcomes, matching the web's `haptic()` call sites, plus one selection tick while scrubbing the practice line. **Never on scroll or passive updates.** Android uses `View.performHapticFeedback` (via Compose `LocalHapticFeedback` where the type exists), which needs no `VIBRATE` permission and respects the user's "Touch feedback" setting.

| iOS | Where used at HEAD | Android (API ≥ 30) | Android API 29 fallback |
|---|---|---|---|
| `UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(.light)` via `.sensoryFeedback(.impact(weight: .light))` on press release | Every `.gradusPress` control (52 files: cards, FABs, HelpBubble, rows) | `HapticFeedbackConstants.VIRTUAL_KEY_RELEASE` on release (Compose `HapticFeedbackType.VirtualKey`/`KeyboardTap` if available) | `VIRTUAL_KEY_RELEASE` (API 27+) |
| `Haptics.success()` (`.success` notification) | SlideToConfirm confirm (start/end session); connection celebration on appear; guardian claim and team invite accepted; guardian email saved; Connect guardian sent; coach visibility accept/disconnect; delete account done; feedback sent; unblock; parent athlete add/edit saved; parent profile saved; Settings saves; AppModel outcome | `HapticFeedbackConstants.CONFIRM` (Compose `HapticFeedbackType.Confirm`) | `CONTEXT_CLICK` |
| `.sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: held)` | The practice line (`PracticeTrendChart.swift`): each time the held session changes to another session while scrubbing (`c5e36c7`, `c38e1f6`) | `HapticFeedbackConstants.SEGMENT_FREQUENT_TICK` (API 34+; Compose `HapticFeedbackType.SegmentFrequentTick`, verify the name in the BOM), `CLOCK_TICK` on 30–33 | `CLOCK_TICK` |
| `Haptics.warning()` / `Haptics.error()` | Defined, **no call sites at HEAD** | `HapticFeedbackConstants.REJECT` (Compose `Reject`) — wire only where iOS adds call sites | `LONG_PRESS` |
| System long-press haptic on `.contextMenu` | Context menus | `HapticFeedbackType.LongPress` | same |
| Watch: `Haptics` maps to `WKInterfaceDevice.play(.success/.retry/.failure/.click)` on watchOS (Controls.swift) | **No call sites** in `Packages/FeatureWatch` or `GradusWatch` at HEAD (all 27 `Haptics.` calls are phone features, `AppModel` and `SlideToConfirm`) | `GradusHaptics` on Wear maps success → `CONFIRM`, warning → `REJECT`, error → `REJECT`, light → `CLOCK_TICK` (or `VibrationEffect.EFFECT_CLICK`); wired only where FeatureWatch adds call sites (§6.15/§7.15) | `performHapticFeedback` works on every supported Wear OS version; `CONFIRM`/`REJECT` constants need API 30 (all current Wear OS images; verify) |

**Accessibility target: WCAG 2.2 Level AAA (decision 2026-09-19, iOS §8.5, §10.6).** Android ships at the same bar the iOS app passed before QA, using the same audit as the checklist. Contextual help (3.3.5) is deferred and stays partial by design, as on iOS.

- **TalkBack labels mirror VoiceOver labels.** Every `accessibilityLabel`, `accessibilityValue`, `accessibilityHint` and identifier string in gradus-ios is reproduced: label → `contentDescription` (or merged text), value → `stateDescription`, hint → the click action label (`onClick(label = …)`) or custom-action names, header trait → `heading()`, `.isSelected` → `selected`, `.isButton` → `Role.Button`, `.isModal` → the lock and gates are separate dialog windows (modal to TalkBack), `.accessibilityHidden(true)` → `clearAndSetSemantics {}`/`contentDescription = null` on decorative icons, `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` → `Modifier.semantics(mergeDescendants = true)`, `.contain` → keep children separate. `.updatesFrequently` (the board's "Updated 12s ago" pill, the recording timer, timers) → `liveRegion = Polite` throttled so TalkBack is not flooded (announce on focus, not every second). The icon-only buttons the web labeled carry the same labels ("Previous week", "Next week", "Record a voice note", "Dismiss", "Close", "Search competitions"). Live Board lanes announce data age. **Skater wheel** (`SkaterWheel.swift:135–145`): cards more than 1.5 positions from the centre are hidden from TalkBack (`clearAndSetSemantics {}` when `distance > 1.5`), the rest ordered by distance (`semantics { traversalIndex = distance }`, so the centre card reads first; iOS `accessibilitySortPriority(10 − distance)`); only the centre card speaks data age; the step controls are visible text "‹ earlier skater" (label "Show the earlier skater") and "later skater ›" (label "Show the later skater"), mono caption2 Bold uppercase `textTertiary`, disabled at the ends. Score-sheet abbreviations (GOE, deductions, factor, IJS, units) are expanded on first use, as on iOS (3.1.4).
- **Touch targets: 48 × 48 dp** minimum (Android/Material guidance; stricter than iOS's 44 × 44 pt, so every iOS target passes). Visuals stay their iOS size; the hit area grows (`minimumInteractiveComponentSize`). Chips and pills get the full 48 dp height of hit area; the Roster week-strip days and arrows each have their own full-size target.
- **Pen marks and TalkBack (handoff §1.4).** Every hand-drawn mark, tally and stripe is **invisible to TalkBack** (`Modifier.clearAndSetSemantics {}` on the mark; iOS `.accessibilityHidden(true)`). The state it shows lives in the owning element's semantics. Examples:
  - a `PenCheckbox` row is `toggleable`/`selected`, with the label "Include Sep 6";
  - a section tick reads "Assign to, done";
  - a moved lesson reads "Moved to 4:00 PM from 3:30 PM";
  - a seen message carries ", seen" in the bubble label;
  - StepDots read "Step 1 of 2";
  - a tally day reads "Friday 17, 6 sessions";
  - the circled stamp is the text "Sent" itself;
  - the hero stripe is decoration.

  A Compose UI test walks each redesigned screen and fails if any node with a pen-mark test tag (`pen.*`) is reachable by accessibility.
- **Contrast.** Stays at the web's AAA targets:
  - body and secondary text ≥ 7:1 on `background`, on `card` (composited over `background`) and on `popover`; large text ≥ 4.5:1;
  - control boundaries ≥ 3:1 (1.4.11): `borderStrong`, chip and secondary-button strokes, the text field's resting `textSecondary` edge (7.8:1), the `PenCheckbox` box;
  - **graphics ≥ 3:1** (handoff §1.4): tallies and the EditingOutline in `accentInk`, pen checks in `penTennisInk`, the practice line in `textPrimary`;
  - `accentInk` (not `accent`) for text, focus rings, switch tracks and every green mark that must pass on paper.

  Known sub-3:1 marks copied from iOS are listed in §12 N91: the lime pen underline in light mode and the orange goal fork in light mode. Where they carry state that no other cue conveys, they fail 1.4.11. The JVM contrast test in §8.2 asserts these pairs from the generated tokens, light and dark, so a token change that breaks AAA fails CI.
- **Increase Contrast (A62).** iOS `colorSchemeContrast == .increased` gives:
  - opaque cards on `popover` with `borderStrong` borders and no card shadow;
  - flat paper (no washes, no ruled lines);
  - **pen strokes 1 pt heavier**;
  - tallies at 2.2 instead of 1.6;
  - the practice line's zone at 45% and its midline at 60%.

  Android computes one `LocalIncreasedContrast`, observed live, and applies all of the above. It also restores **every** `cardEdge` (A62). It is true when either signal is on:
  - **API 34+:** `UiModeManager.getContrast() > 0f`. This is the system contrast level: Standard is 0, Medium 0.5, High 1.0, under Settings → Accessibility → Color and motion → **Color contrast** on Pixels (verify the path and the Android version that shows it). It is observed with `UiModeManager.addContrastChangeListener`.
  - **API 36+:** `AccessibilityManager.isHighContrastTextEnabled()`, observed with `addHighContrastTextStateChangeListener`. This is the "High contrast text" switch (renamed "Maximize text contrast"/outline text on Android 16; verify the method and listener names, which became public in API 36).

  On API 29–33 there is no public signal, so the flag is false. The system's own "High contrast text" rendering still applies to all text with no app work. Android does **not** read the hidden `Settings.Secure` key for high-contrast text on older versions.
- **Font scale.** Text through the largest scale (200% on Android 14+) **without truncating scores or timers**: no `maxLines = 1` on names, titles, previews, emails, room titles, board subtitles (iOS audit P5 removed 84 `lineLimit(1)` sites; Android allows 2–3 lines or none at the same places); side-by-side rows stack at `fontScale ≥ 1.5` (AdaptiveStack); segmented controls become menus; FlowBars captions stack; the Terms gate and the celebration card scroll.
- **Focus and keyboards.** A visible focus indicator (2 dp `accentInk` ring) on every focusable control when navigated with a hardware keyboard or D-pad (`Modifier.focusable` + `onFocusChanged` border; Material components draw their own); logical traversal order (`Modifier.focusProperties`/`traversalIndex` only where the visual order misleads); Tab/Shift-Tab through forms, Enter submits; Space plays a voice note in a room. **Escape:** wherever the Safe Sport **Safety exit** button is on screen (`SafeSportView`, `SafeSportPanel`; iOS `SafetyExitButton.swift:42` binds `.keyboardShortcut(.escape)`; label "Safety exit", test tag `safeSport.safetyExit`), a hardware Escape key-down triggers the safety exit (`Modifier.onPreviewKeyEvent { it.key == Key.Escape && it.type == KeyEventType.KeyDown }` at that screen's root, consumed before any sheet or dialog handling). Everywhere else Escape (`KEYCODE_ESCAPE`) dismisses the topmost sheet or dialog (except the non-dismissible sheets in §8.3).
- **The lock.** The biometric lock (iOS `LockWindow.swift`: its own window above every alert and sheet; the app below leaves the accessibility tree; the keyboard goes down; the field keeps its draft and regains focus on unlock) is the **`LockActivity`** of §6.4 and §6.11.4 (the one design; this section only adds the visual rules). Because it is a separate activity on top of the single-task `MainActivity`, every `AlertDialog`, `ModalBottomSheet` or menu that `MainActivity` shows, before or after locking, stays underneath it and is still there after unlock, which is iOS's `UIWindow.Level.alert + 1` behavior; a screen's own prompts are still held by `PromptHold` while locked (§8.3).
  - The IME is hidden on lock; the focused field keeps its draft uncommitted (`commitsOnFocusLoss`) and regains focus on unlock.
  - TalkBack can reach only the lock ("Gradus is locked", the error message if any, "Unlock", "Sign out"); `MainActivity` content is behind another activity.
  - Unlock fades the lock out over **200 ms** (instant under Remove animations) and finishes `LockActivity`, returning focus to the app so a field can retake it.
  - It requests `BiometricPrompt` on appear like iOS's `.task { unlock() }`, with the authenticators of §6.11.4.
  - Tests: §6.11.4's seven lock tests (dialog already up, async dialog requested after locking, TalkBack reach, cold start, rapid toggles, system UI launched from the app, field draft).
- **Direction and locale.** English only in 1.0 (iOS §7.13); all strings in `strings.xml` (and plurals in `plurals`) from day one; layouts use start/end, never left/right, so RTL works when locales arrive.

**Automated accessibility checks (port of `Tools/A11yAudit`).** The iOS harness drives the debug app through the main screens for every `-GradusMock` role. It runs `performAccessibilityAudit` per screen and dumps the hierarchy, in light/dark, AX5 text, Increase Contrast and landscape.

Android: an instrumented test module `:tools:a11y-audit` that launches the debug app in mock mode (variants and extras listed below).
- **Screens walked:** sign-in, each tab root, athlete detail (including the practice line), the plan editor (draft steps and an active plan), a move being edited, a room (with a reply and reactions in the mock), a session and its check-in, the Live board and score sheet, Roster → Invoicing (each filter), the Bill sheet and a receipt, Settings, the Terms gate, the celebration.
- **Checks:** the **Accessibility Test Framework** (`AccessibilityChecks.enable().setRunChecksFromRootView(true)` for Espresso, plus the Compose UI test accessibility checks) and the pen-mark-hidden check above.
- **Artifact:** each screen's semantics tree (`onRoot().printToString()`).
- **Matrix:** light/dark × font scale 1.0 and 2.0 × portrait/landscape × contrast standard/high. High contrast runs on an API 34+ emulator via `adb shell settings put secure contrast_level 1`; verify the key.
- **When:** on the API 36 emulator in CI, nightly and before each release.

Roborazzi screenshots at font scale 2.0 catch clipping, and the redesigned screens are also compared with the canvas boards by eye at each milestone (§10.2). Android Studio's **Accessibility Scanner** app is the manual complement on the Pixel.

**Mock mode (port of `-GradusMock`, `Gradus/Dependencies.swift` `fromLaunchArguments`).** Debug builds only; launched with `adb shell am start -n training.gradus.app.debug/training.gradus.app.MainActivity -e gradusMock <variant>` (instrumented tests pass the same extras in the launch `Intent`). Every iOS variant exists under the same name with the same seeded state: `coach`, `parent`, `parentBasic` (no Team plan), `athlete`, `athleteMinor` (a minor whose guardian has not joined: text-only, no microphone), `signedOut`, `terms` (coach with the terms not accepted → Terms gate), `noRole` (signed in, profile-less), `newCoach` (not onboarded), `coachPro`, `coachClub`, `foundingUnclaimed`, `foundingOnPro`, `signUp`, `signUpParent`, `signUpAthlete`, `parentUnverified`, `parentUnverifiedNoKws`, `parentOptIn`, `signUpParentUnverified`, `athleteProvisional`, `athletePaused`, `parentAthletePaused`, `roomPausedByParent`, `coachRoomPausedByParent`; an unknown value falls back to the role of that name, else `coach` (iOS `default:`). Companion extras, each honored only together with `gradusMock`: `gradusAgeRange` (`teen`, `teen16`, `under13`; mocks the Play Age Signals answer as iOS `-GradusAgeRange` mocks Declared Age Range), `gradusSignificantChange` "<text>" (parent-approval screen; iOS `-GradusSignificantChange`), `gradusMockNow` (fixed clock) and `gradusMockSessionMinutes` (running-session length); Wear: `gradusWatchOpen` (`plans`, `first-plan`, `first-wrapup` …) and `gradusWatchAutoplay` (iOS `-GradusWatchOpen`/`-GradusWatchAutoplay`). Release builds ignore all of these (the parser lives in the `debug` source set).

**Audit tests (one per iOS `GradusAuditTests` test).** `testSignedOut`, `testCoach`, `testParent`, `testAthlete` (the role walks above); `testAthleteMinor` (text-only composer, no mic button); `testTerms` (Terms gate); `testAgeSignalTeen` (`signedOut` + `gradusAgeRange=teen`: the sign-up chooser, then `gradus://signup/coach` → adult roles blocked); `testAgeSignalUnder13` (`under13`: `gradus://signup/athlete/adult` → parent-only card; `gradus://signup/parent` → adult roles blocked); `testAgeSignalRoleChooser` (`noRole` + `teen16`: role chooser); `testAthletePaused` (Settings → Profile → the paused notice, tag `athleteProfile.paused`); `testParentAthletePaused` (Settings → My athletes → athlete → tag `athlete.paused`); `testParentApproval` (`athlete` + `gradusSignificantChange="Gradus now lets athletes share practice videos with their coach."`); `testSafeSportReport` (Settings → Safe Sport → scroll → tag `safeSport.report`, the "Gradus Support" card); `testA11yItem1Fixes` (GradusField labels; toast announce, no auto-dismiss for errors, Dismiss action); `testDebugSessionFlow` (parent: open a runner plan, `session.start`, hop Messages → Plans, `session.discard`, the discard alert, Cancel; dump the tree at each step); `testDebugBlockDialog` (coach: Messages → a `messages.room.*` row → `room.options` → Block → the block confirmation alert); `testSessionDiscardDialogFixed` (parent: session discard × confirmation alert has Cancel); `testConfirmationDialogPopoverBug` (coach: every confirmation is an `AlertDialog` with Cancel, never an action sheet — the iOS regression this guards has no Android cause, but the assertion is kept). A missing test tag fails the test (the iOS harness logs MISSING).

**Device accessibility pass (translation of gradus-ios `docs/device-accessibility-script.md`, pre-QA gate P8).** Run once on the first internal-testing build on Mariah's Pixel, then whenever a milestone touches navigation or forms; about 45 minutes; findings as `screen · what happened · expected` in `docs/android/QA.md`. Turn each feature on in **Settings → Accessibility** and off before the next section. Use the seeded demo coach and parent.

1. **TalkBack (15 min)** — Settings → Accessibility → TalkBack → on. Swipe right = next element; double-tap = activate; swipe down then right (or the TalkBack menu, three-finger tap) for Headings, Actions, Read from next item.
   - Sign in: every field is announced by its label, not its placeholder ("Email or username, Edit box"). A wrong password is announced as "Error: …" without hunting.
   - Navigation bar: the role's tabs (five for a coach, four for a parent or athlete) read with their names, Messages with its unread count.
   - Roster (coach): the page title is a heading (Headings navigation jumps to it); the week strip reads "Tuesday 15, 1 session"; a lesson row reads athlete, time and status, then "Collapsed"; double-tap reads "Expanded" and the actions are reachable.
   - Athlete detail sheet: the title reads "Athlete" with a Close button; every section title is a heading.
   - Plan editor: a move row reads its name, its target ("10 repetitions") and any change tag ("New", "Changed"); expand and collapse are announced; the pen reads "Edit Waltz jump", then "Done editing Waltz jump"; a draft's step headers read "Assign to, done"; Bench asks for confirmation.
   - Messages: a bubble reads "Coach Linnea: … 3:42 PM", with ", seen" on your own read message and ", reactions ❤️ 2 👏" when reacted; TalkBack menu → Actions lists Reply, each reaction, Play voice note, Open tagged plan, Copy and Go to quoted message; a voice note reads its transcript or "transcript coming".
   - Composer: Record a voice note has a name; while recording, the pill announces elapsed time.
   - Session (parent or athlete): Start session; the timer pill speaks elapsed time on focus; End asks nothing extra; the discard × asks for confirmation.
   - Live board: the "Updated 12s ago" pill is a button that refreshes; a followed skater's row is one sentence; Follow/Unfollow buttons carry the skater's name.
   - Score sheet: totals read "Total score: 61.20" and so on; an element row reads base value and grade of execution.
   - Settings: rows read their value ("Appearance, System"); Terms of Service says "Opens in your browser"; the lock screen (turn on the biometric lock in Settings → Device, leave the app, return) is the only thing TalkBack can reach while locked.
   - Any short toast is spoken once.
2. **Switch Access (8 min)** — Settings → Accessibility → Switch Access → on, with auto-scan and one switch (a Bluetooth keyboard key, or the volume key as "Select"). The highlight lands on every control at a usable size.
   - Roster week strip: each day and both arrows get their own full-size highlight.
   - Composer: paperclip, text field, send/mic each get focus.
   - Celebration (demo parent with a new connection, or the mock): "Maybe later" and the close × are both selectable.
   - Chips (filters, Edit sports, Unlink): the highlight is the full 48 dp pill.
3. **Voice Access (5 min)** — install/enable Voice Access; say "Show labels".
   - Every icon-only button has a sensible name ("Previous week", "Record a voice note", "Dismiss").
   - "Tap Live" opens the board; "Tap Close" closes it.
   - "Show numbers" on the score sheet: rows are separately numbered.
4. **Physical keyboard (7 min)** — pair a Bluetooth keyboard (or use the emulator with the Mac keyboard).
   - Tab moves through sign-in fields and the button; Enter submits.
   - Tab reaches the navigation bar; arrow keys move between tabs.
   - In a room, Tab reaches the composer, the send button and each bubble; Space plays a voice note.
   - Escape dismisses sheets (New conversation, athlete detail, lesson slot).
   - On Safe Sport (athlete: Settings → Safety, or Resources → Safe Sport), Escape leaves Gradus and opens the Google search page in the browser.
   - The focus ring is visible on the paper background and inside cards.
5. **Font size and display (5 min)**
   - Settings → Display → Font size → largest (200% on Android 14+), Display size → largest. Walk Roster, Plans, Messages, a room, Settings, the Terms gate (bump the terms version in the mock) and the celebration. Nothing is clipped to one line; side-by-side rows have stacked.
   - Contrast → high (Android 14+), and separately High contrast text (Android 16+): cards are opaque with visible edges, pen checks and outlines are heavier, the practice line's zone is darker, and there are no washes behind text.
   - Remove animations → on: no confetti on the celebration; the pulsing session dot is still; the board wheel does not spin.
   - Rotate to landscape on every tab and in the Live cover; the composer and timer stay usable.
6. **Large screen (5 min; replaces the iPad section)** — on a tablet or foldable emulator (or the Pixel's split screen): the app shows the phone layout centered and correct at every width; split-screen with another app reflows at the narrow width; a hardware keyboard works as in section 4. Live stays the top-bar action (the tab/rail variant comes with adaptive layouts).

Reporting is as on iOS: anything that blocks a task for an assistive-technology user goes at the top.

### 8.6 Show, don't tell: principles, the pen layer and the new components

Source: the handoff §1–§8 and iOS `c8f83d6`. This section is the Android build spec for everything the redesign added. Each component lives in `:core:design`, with a `@Preview` in light and dark at font scale 1.0 and 2.0 and a Roborazzi test.

#### 8.6.1 Principles (handoff §1, verbatim in intent)

1. **Show, don't tell.** Cut the explainer sentence before adding anything. Prefer, in this order:
   - a visible state change;
   - an existing visual (practice ring, level track, FlowBars, tags, chips);
   - edit-in-place.

   A sentence that must survive moves to TalkBack: Android has no hint slot, so it goes into the `onClick(label = …)` action label, the `stateDescription`, or the merged `contentDescription`, never a visible line. Or it moves to a tap-to-explain sheet. AI-written content (briefings, summaries, recaps) is content, not explainer text.
2. **One title per screen.** No top-bar title on top of a page title (§8.3 `.toolbar` row). No field label that repeats the page title: it stays as the TalkBack label. Uppercase section labels go wherever the content already makes the section obvious.
3. **Icons replace words; they never decorate them.** A pen instead of "Edit" (`edit`, `contentDescription` "Edit goal"), a speaker instead of "Read aloud". No icon beside the word it repeats, no glyphs inside tags, no initials avatars.
4. **WCAG AAA** (§8.5).
   - Colour is never the only cue.
   - Graphics need 3:1.
   - Every hand-drawn mark is hidden from TalkBack, with the state in the element's semantics.
   - Under Remove animations nothing animates.
   - Under Increase Contrast strokes get heavier.
5. **Reuse before inventing.** A pattern that appears twice becomes one `:core:design` component. That is how the picker field, the editing outline and the target stepper came about. Feature modules may not draw their own pen marks: a detekt rule forbids `penMarkPath(` and `PenRandom(` outside `:core:design`.

#### 8.6.2 Buttons and sheets (handoff §3)

**One lime action per screen** is the action that finishes the screen's job: Activate & Share, Update & Share, Bill $140, Send, Save results, Finish.
- Everything else is outlined (`GradusSecondaryButton` or `GradusChipButton`), including actions repeated on every row (Bill, Mark paid, Generate plan, Accept, Edit plan).
- A disabled primary goes pale.
- **Kept exception:** the Safe Sport hotline Call buttons stay lime.
- **Mechanism:** `GradusPrimaryButton` and `GradusChipButton(prominent = true)` register with a debug-only `LocalLimeBudget`, which each screen root provides. In debug builds, more than one registered lime action logs a lint-style warning with the screen's route. A Compose UI test runs the warning as a failure over the a11y-audit walk.
  - Allow-listed because iOS `c8f83d6` does it:
    - the Safe Sport Call buttons;
    - the FABs. The Roster "+" FAB and the lime "Get set up" pill share a screen, and on the Plans list the voice FAB and the "+" FAB share a screen. Both pairs are lime on iOS (*code wins*); §12 N93 asks whether they should be.
  - Lime that signals a **state** is not an action and is not counted: the selected day pill, a selected chip, the plan mic while listening.
- **Primary buttons name what happens:** "Bill $140", "Activate & Share with Greta". No sentence explains a button: the reason a primary is disabled goes in its TalkBack action label (iOS puts it in the accessibility hint).

**The plan mic** is outlined at rest and lime only while listening:
- at rest: `card` fill, 1 dp `textSecondary` ring, `accentInk` icon;
- listening or processing: `accent` fill and `accentForeground` icon.

This applies to the inline mic in the plan editor's top bar (`VoiceCaptureButton` `inline`). The Plans-list voice FAB stays lime at rest (*code wins*, §12 N93).

**Sheets close with "Close", at the top start, every time.** `GradusSheetHeader(title, onClose, action = null)` is the first child of every `ModalBottomSheet` and full-screen dialog:
- a `TextButton("Close")` at the start, `accentInk`;
- the title, centered, body headline Bold, with heading semantics;
- the optional confirm `TextButton` at the end ("Save", "Send", "Add athlete", "Import"), `accentInk`, with its busy word ("Saving…").

Rules:
- "Close" never confirms. On a sheet with a discard rule (the session check-in), Close opens that confirmation.
- **"Cancel" stays only** for alert dialogs (as iOS alerts keep it), inline mini-forms (an open "Save to library" row, the motivation editor) and Wear OS.
- The Material `DatePickerDialog` is a dialog, not a sheet, but iOS shows the birthdate wheel as a sheet with "Close"/"Done", so the Android dialog's dismiss button reads **"Close"** (A68).
- iOS gaps to mirror or fix: `MoveImportFlow` still says "Cancel" at `c8f83d6` (§12 N97), and the Report sheet's note field is still a plain form field (handoff §5 "Known gap"; Android uses `GradusTextField` there, §12 N97).

#### 8.6.3 Surfaces and the hero number (handoff §2)

- **Content cards are borderless**: soft fill and shadow only (§8.2 shadow; `cardEdge` clear). **Controls keep their edges**: fields, buttons, chips, picker fields, the lesson card in the day agenda, which is a tappable control with a 1 dp `divider` edge (1.5 dp `textPrimary` at 60% when open), and room rows, whose edge is `accent` when unread and `divider` otherwise. **Increase Contrast puts every card edge back** (A62).
- **Display serif heavier**: EB Garamond Bold by default; hero numbers Heavy (§8.1).
- **Hero number**: the one figure on a screen worth reading first, set in display Heavy and sitting on the page-title stripe. `Modifier.heroHighlight(height = 10.dp)` draws `heroStripe` behind the text: a bar of the given height at the bottom-start, moved up by `0.6 × height`. So with height H it spans from `h − 1.6H` to `h − 0.6H` over the text's full width; dark mode uses alpha 0.35. It is decoration, hidden from TalkBack. Used at `c8f83d6` on:
  - the invoicing collected total (largeTitle Heavy, H 10);
  - the receipt total (largeTitle Bold, H 10);
  - a competition placing in the result sheet (largeTitle Heavy, H 10) and on each row (title Heavy, H 8);
  - the practice line's "N%" (title2 Heavy, H 8): *code wins*, since the handoff lists only the first three.
- **Mood words (A44):** Hard (frustrated) · Just right (engaged) · Easy (comfortable), on the check-in scale and on FlowBars, with lime on Just right. The in-between points read **"A bit hard"** and **"A bit easy"** everywhere.

#### 8.6.4 The pen layer (handoff §4; iOS `PenMarks.swift`)

A hand-drawn mark means a person's hand is on it. There are exactly three uses:
1. **Something changed state:**
   - a new time underlined, with the old one struck through;
   - checks on an invoice;
   - "Sent" circled once it goes out;
   - a message seen;
   - a setup step crossed off;
   - the newest goal target underlined;
   - the chosen invoicing filter underlined.
2. **Done or chosen:** every checkmark is a pen tick inside a crisp box or circle (`PenCheckbox`): chips, the move picker, invoice lines, the role chooser, section ticks, StepDots' finished steps. Android system menus (`DropdownMenu` items such as the React menu's "yours") and Wear OS keep system checkmarks.
3. **You're editing it right now** (§8.6.5).

**Never pen:** buttons, charts, data, tallies. **Every mark is seeded**, so it never wobbles between renders, and Android uses **the same seeds and the same jitter as iOS**, so a mark is the same shape on both platforms.

**Kinds** (`PenMarkKind`, one meaning each): `Circle` (circled: "Sent"/"Paid"), `Check` (done), `Envelope` (sent, in the All invoices list), `Underline` (just changed or chosen), `Strike` (replaced), `Draft` (the editing outline).

**The jitter, ported exactly.** `PenRandom` is SplitMix64. iOS computes in `CGFloat` (a 64-bit `Double`) in points. Android computes in `Double` **in dp**, converts to px only when emitting the `Path`, and must consume random numbers in the same order. In the Swift source, arguments are evaluated left to right, x before y.

```kotlin
// :core:design — training.gradus.design.pen. Port of PenMarks.swift (gradus-ios c8f83d6). Do not "simplify":
// the order of every next()/jitter() call is part of the shape.
internal class PenRandom(seed: ULong) {
    private var state: ULong = seed + GOLDEN                    // Swift: seed &+ 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15
    fun next(): Double {
        state += GOLDEN                                         // ULong arithmetic wraps, like &+ and &*
        var z = state
        z = (z xor (z shr 30)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9uL
        z = (z xor (z shr 27)) * 0x94D049BB133111EBuL
        z = z xor (z shr 31)
        return (z % 10_000uL).toDouble() / 10_000.0
    }
    fun jitter(amount: Double): Double = (next() * 2 - 1) * amount   // a value in -amount..amount
    private companion object { const val GOLDEN = 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15uL }
}

enum class PenMarkKind { Circle, Check, Envelope, Underline, Strike, Draft }

/** Records the mark in dp (Double), then scales to px. Mirrors PenMark.path(in:) for a rect at (0,0,w,h). */
internal class PenPath(private val density: Float) {
    val path = Path()
    private var cx = 0.0; private var cy = 0.0
    fun moveTo(x: Double, y: Double) { path.moveTo((x * density).toFloat(), (y * density).toFloat()); cx = x; cy = y }
    fun lineTo(x: Double, y: Double) { path.lineTo((x * density).toFloat(), (y * density).toFloat()); cx = x; cy = y }
    fun quadTo(c1: Double, c2: Double, x: Double, y: Double) {
        path.quadraticTo((c1 * density).toFloat(), (c2 * density).toFloat(), (x * density).toFloat(), (y * density).toFloat())
        cx = x; cy = y
    }
    val currentX get() = cx; val currentY get() = cy
}

fun penMarkPath(kind: PenMarkKind, w: Double, h: Double, seed: ULong, roughness: Double, density: Float): Path {
    val rng = PenRandom(seed); val p = PenPath(density)
    when (kind) {
        PenMarkKind.Circle -> ellipse(p, 1.5, 1.5, w - 3.0, h - 3.0, rng, roughness)                // insetBy(1.5, 1.5)
        PenMarkKind.Check -> {
            val s = minOf(w, h); val ox = w / 2 - s / 2; val oy = h / 2 - s / 2
            stroke(p, ox + s * 0.08, oy + s * 0.55, ox + s * 0.4, oy + s * 0.92, rng, roughness)
            stroke(p, ox + s * 0.4, oy + s * 0.92, ox + s * 0.95, oy + s * 0.08, rng, roughness)
        }
        PenMarkKind.Envelope -> {
            val minX = 1.5; val maxX = w - 1.5; val minY = h * 0.12; val maxY = h - h * 0.12   // insetBy(1.5, h*0.12)
            val midX = (minX + maxX) / 2; val midY = (minY + maxY) / 2; val rh = maxY - minY
            stroke(p, minX, minY, maxX, minY, rng, roughness); stroke(p, maxX, minY, maxX, maxY, rng, roughness)
            stroke(p, maxX, maxY, minX, maxY, rng, roughness); stroke(p, minX, maxY, minX, minY, rng, roughness)
            stroke(p, minX, minY, midX, midY + rh * 0.1, rng, roughness); stroke(p, midX, midY + rh * 0.1, maxX, minY, rng, roughness)
        }
        PenMarkKind.Underline -> stroke(p, 0.0, h / 2 - 0.8, w, h / 2 + 1.2, rng, roughness)        // a touch lower on the right
        PenMarkKind.Strike -> stroke(p, -1.0, h / 2 + 0.6, w + 1.0, h / 2 - 1.0, rng, roughness)
        PenMarkKind.Draft -> sketchedRoundedRect(p, 1.0, 1.0, w - 1.0, h - 1.0, minOf(14.0, h / 3), rng, roughness) // radius from the un-inset height
    }
    return p.path
}

/** A line drawn twice with a slight bow. Order: mid.x, mid.y, start.x, start.y, end.x, end.y. */
private fun stroke(p: PenPath, ax: Double, ay: Double, bx: Double, by: Double, rng: PenRandom, r: Double) {
    val length = hypot(bx - ax, by - ay)
    repeat(2) {
        val bow = length * 0.012 * r * 2
        val mx = (ax + bx) / 2 + rng.jitter(bow); val my = (ay + by) / 2 + rng.jitter(bow)
        p.moveTo(ax + rng.jitter(r), ay + rng.jitter(r))
        val ex = bx + rng.jitter(r); val ey = by + rng.jitter(r)
        p.quadTo(mx, my, ex, ey)
    }
}

private fun ellipse(p: PenPath, x: Double, y: Double, w: Double, h: Double, rng: PenRandom, roughness: Double) {
    val steps = 24; val midX = x + w / 2; val midY = y + h / 2
    for (pass in 0 until 2) {
        val start = rng.next() * 2 * PI
        val overshoot = 0.12 + 0.04 * pass
        val total = (steps.toDouble() * (1 + overshoot)).toInt()   // 26, then 27
        for (i in 0..total) {
            val a = start + 2 * PI * i / steps
            val k = 1 + rng.jitter(0.025 * roughness)
            val px = midX + w / 2 * k * cos(a); val py = midY + h / 2 * k * sin(a)
            if (i == 0) p.moveTo(px, py) else p.lineTo(px, py)
        }
    }
}

private fun sketchedRoundedRect(p: PenPath, minX: Double, minY: Double, maxX: Double, maxY: Double, radius: Double, rng: PenRandom, roughness: Double) {
    val corners = listOf(
        Triple(maxX - radius, minY + radius, -PI / 2), Triple(maxX - radius, maxY - radius, 0.0),
        Triple(minX + radius, maxY - radius, PI / 2), Triple(minX + radius, minY + radius, PI),
    )
    var pts = buildList { for ((cx, cy, st) in corners) for (k in 0..6) { val a = st + k / 6.0 * PI / 2; add(cx + radius * cos(a) to cy + radius * sin(a)) } } // 28 points
    val shift = (rng.next() * pts.size).toInt()
    pts = pts.drop(shift) + pts.take(shift)
    pts = pts + pts.take(3)                                           // 31 points: a little overshoot
    var dx = 0.0; var dy = 0.0; val amp = 1.4 * roughness * 2
    fun moved(q: Pair<Double, Double>): Pair<Double, Double> {
        dx = dx * 0.6 + rng.jitter(amp) * 0.4                         // dx first, then dy
        dy = dy * 0.6 + rng.jitter(amp) * 0.4
        return (q.first + dx) to (q.second + dy)
    }
    moved(pts[0]).let { p.moveTo(it.first, it.second) }
    for (i in 1 until pts.size) {
        val q = moved(pts[i]); val px = p.currentX; val py = p.currentY
        val c1 = (px + q.first) / 2 + rng.jitter(0.6); val c2 = (py + q.second) / 2 + rng.jitter(0.6)
        p.quadTo(c1, c2, q.first, q.second)
    }
    val from = (rng.next() * (pts.size / 2)).toInt()                  // pts.size / 2 is integer division (15)
    moved(pts[from]).let { p.moveTo(it.first, it.second) }
    for (i in (from + 1) until minOf(pts.size, from + pts.size / 6)) { val q = moved(pts[i]); p.lineTo(q.first, q.second) }
}
```

`Path.quadraticTo` is the current Compose name; it was `quadraticBezierTo` before Compose 1.7, so verify against the BOM.

**Golden vectors.** These come from a reference port (Python 64-bit) of the Swift above. iOS should add the same assertions to `GradusDesignTests` so both platforms test one truth (§12 N94):
- `PenRandom(1)`: the first five `next()` values are `0.8519, 0.0590, 0.0235, 0.8761, 0.0048`.
- `PenRandom(44)` (the EditingOutline seed): `0.7730, 0.4437, 0.9822, 0.8578, 0.1383`.
- `PenRandom(0)`: `0.5700, 0.5679, 0.2444`.
- The `Check` mark, seed 5, roughness 0.5, in a 22.8 × 22.8 dp rect (a 24 dp `PenCheckbox`'s tick), emits these operations in dp:
  - `M 1.3949 12.3861`, then `Q 5.5080 16.7062 9.0636 20.5369`;
  - `M 2.1435 12.2071`, then `Q 5.3787 16.7816 8.8484 20.6083`;
  - `M 9.6126 20.6643`, then `Q 15.3085 11.5775 22.1131 2.0639`;
  - `M 8.9571 21.2024`, then `Q 15.2063 11.2137 22.0431 1.4827`.

A JVM test asserts these to 1e-4. A Roborazzi test renders every kind at seeds 1, 5 and 44.

**`PenMarkView(kind, modifier, color = penTennisInk, seed = 1u, lineWidth = 1.6.dp, roughness = 0.5)`**
- Implementation: `Spacer(modifier.drawWithCache { val path = penMarkPath(kind, size.width / density, size.height / density, seed, roughness, density); onDrawBehind { drawPath(path, color, style = Stroke((lineWidth + penStrokeBoost).toPx(), cap = StrokeCap.Round, join = StrokeJoin.Round)) } }.clearAndSetSemantics {})`.
- The path is rebuilt only when the size changes.
- Increase Contrast adds 1 dp to the line (iOS `lineWidth + 1`).

**Modifiers that place marks around content** (iOS overlay geometry, in dp, where h and w are the content's size):
- `Modifier.penUnderline(color = accent, seed = 7u, lineWidth = 3.dp)` draws `Underline` in the rect x −3…w+3, y h−1…h+5. This matches iOS `overlay(alignment: .bottom)`, frame height 6, padding −3, offset +5.
- `Modifier.penStrike(color = textSecondary, seed = 3u)` draws `Strike` at line width 1.6 in the rect 0…w, h/2−3…h/2+3.
- `Modifier.heroHighlight(height)`: §8.6.3.

**`PenCheckbox(checked, shape = Square | Circle, size = 24.dp, seed = 5u)`**
- The box stays crisp: it is a control with a 3:1 boundary. Square: radius 6, 1.5 dp stroke, `accentInk` when checked, `textTertiary` otherwise. Circle: the same, round.
- When checked, a `Check` mark in `penTennisInk`, line 2.4, sized `0.95 × size`, offset by (+0.08 × size, −0.1 × size): the tick leaves the box like a hand's.
- The whole thing is hidden from TalkBack. The owning row carries `toggleable(value = checked, role = Role.Checkbox)`, or `selectable(role = Role.RadioButton)` for a circle.

**Seeds by call site** (copy exactly; `n(text)` = the string's character count as Swift counts it, i.e. extended grapheme clusters, measured on Android with `BreakIterator.getCharacterInstance()`, **not** `String.length`, which differs for emoji and accented text):

| Site | Kind / component | Seed | Color, line width |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text field focus, search field focus, the composer, the default EditingOutline | `Draft` | 44 | `accentInk`, 2 |
| Plan builder, a move open for editing | `Draft` | move index + 71 | `accentInk`, 2 |
| A moved lesson's new time; the newest goal target | `Underline` (`penUnderline`) | 7 | `accent`, 3 |
| A moved lesson's old time | `Strike` (`penStrike`) | 3 | `textSecondary`, 1.6 |
| Get set up: a done step's check / strike | `Check` / `Strike` | 31 / n(step key) + 90 | `penTennisInk` 2 / `textSecondary` 1.8 |
| StepDots, a finished step | `Check` | step + 60 | `penTennisInk` (or `accentForeground` on accent, A66), 2 |
| A chip with a check icon | `Check` | n(label) | `accentForeground` selected / `textPrimary`, 2 |
| Section tick (plan draft steps) | `PenCheckbox(Circle, 20)` | n(title) + 3 | as PenCheckbox |
| Move picker row | `PenCheckbox(Circle, 22)` | n(move name) | as PenCheckbox |
| Bill sheet lesson line | `PenCheckbox(Square, 24)` | n(occurrenceDate) + amountCents % 7 | as PenCheckbox |
| Role chooser row | `PenCheckbox(Circle, 24)` | 5 | as PenCheckbox |
| Success toast icon | `Check` 18 dp | 17 | `penTennisInk`, 2.2 |
| Message seen | `Check` 12 dp | 13 | `textTertiary`, 1.6 |
| Receipt "Sent"/"Paid" stamp | `Circle` | 21 | `penTennisInk`, 1.6 |
| Receipt, each billed line | `Check` 18 dp | 30 + line index | `penTennisInk`, 1.8 |
| All invoices: paid / sent | `Check` 22 dp / `Envelope` 26×22 dp | 5 / 9 | `penTennisInk` 2.2 / `borderStrong` 1.6 |
| Invoicing filter, the chosen total | `Underline`, roughness **1.6** | n(filter label: "To bill" 7, "Sent" 4, "Paid" 4) + 7 | `accent`, **4** |
| Enter results, the attached PDF | `Check` 16 dp | 9 | `penTennisInk`, 2 |
| Talk it through (mock-only on iOS) | `Draft` / `Check` 20 dp | item + 31 / item + 11 | `accentInk` 2 / `penTennisInk` 2 |

#### 8.6.5 Editing state: the rough outline (handoff §5)

**The rule: wherever the cursor is blinking, or whatever you're actively editing, gets the hand-drawn outline. Leave it, and it goes back to crisp.**
- **One component.** `EditingOutline(seed = 44u)` is `PenMarkView(Draft, color = accentInk, seed, lineWidth = 2.dp)` filling its parent: green in light mode, cyan in dark. Never hand-draw a second variant.
- **`Modifier.editingEdge(focused: Boolean, corner: Dp = 14.dp)`.** At rest: a crisp 1 dp `textSecondary` border inside the shape. Focused: the EditingOutline only. The two crossfade over 120 ms ease-out, or snap under Remove animations.
  - The outline's own corner is `min(14, h/3)` whatever `corner` says, as on iOS, where the search capsule (corner 22) still gets a 14-radius sketch.
  - The outline **is** the focus indicator (2 dp, 3:1; WCAG 2.4.13).
  - Used by `GradusTextField`, `GradusSearchField`, the message composer (corner 18; it replaced the old accent 2 dp focus border in `ad1e9bf`), and any field that draws its own box.
- **Where else it appears:**
  - the move open for editing in the plan builder (only while it is expanded **and** its pen is on, never while it is being read aloud);
  - moves landing during Talk it through, until approved. That one is mock-only on iOS (`-GradusDemoVoiceLive`), so it is not built (§12 N95).
- **Where it does not appear:** saved or final content, collapsed draft moves, filled or AI-drafted fields you are not in.

#### 8.6.6 Fields, pickers and the target stepper (handoff §6)

**`GradusPickerField`** (iOS `.gradusPickerField(isEmpty:)`): the one picker field for every menu choice.
- **iOS sites:** sport, category in the goals form, levels, lesson day, start and end times, how often, the athlete pickers (lesson sheet, New athlete), "Who gets the invite", schedule import's three pickers, the season-goal and parent-goal level pickers.
- **Look:**
  - box: `elevated` fill, radius 14, min height 48, 4 dp inner horizontal padding plus the text field's 14;
  - value in body `textPrimary`; trailing `unfold_more` icon (SF `chevron.up.chevron.down`) in the same color;
  - border 1 dp `textSecondary`.
  - **While nothing is chosen** the border is **dashed** (4 dp on, 3 dp off, via `drawBehind` + `PathEffect.dashPathEffect`) and the value shows the placeholder in `textSecondary`. This is the look "Choose who this is for" set in the plan builder's Assign to.
- **Compose:** `ExposedDropdownMenuBox`. The anchor is a non-editable row with `Modifier.menuAnchor(ExposedDropdownMenuAnchorType.PrimaryNotEditable)`; verify the anchor-type name in the BOM, which was `MenuAnchorType` in 1.3. The menu is `ExposedDropdownMenu` with `DropdownMenuItem`s, the chosen one marked with the system check (system menus keep system checkmarks, §8.6.4).
- **Semantics:** `Role.DropdownList`, `contentDescription = label`, `stateDescription = value` or "Not chosen".
- **Labels:** fields keep their labels (WCAG 3.3.2) as an eyebrow (`GradusField`), a placeholder or a TalkBack label. A single-field screen whose title names the field drops the visible label (the invite code, §7.1.15).

**`GradusMenuPicker`** (iOS `1a507b5`): the unboxed variant for long values.
- **Sites:** the move form's Sport and Category, side by side, and the same pair in Save to library. A long category wrapped to three lines and spilled past a fixed box.
- **Look:** the value text (body, wraps freely) and the chevrons sit flush with the field's eyebrow label: no inset, no box, min height 48. Muted when empty.
- **Semantics:** label = title, `stateDescription` = value.

**`TargetStepper(value: Double, kind: TargetKind, onChange: (Double, TargetKind) -> Unit)`**: "− 20 reps +".
- **Layout:** one `CircleShape` `elevated` surface holding three parts:
  - a 48 dp "−" `IconButton` (`remove`, `contentDescription` "Fewer"), which sends `max(1, value − 1)`;
  - the value in display title2 with tabular figures (`PlanMove.formatTarget`; "–" when 0), then the unit as a text button "reps" or "min" in subheadline Bold `accentInk`. Its `contentDescription` is "Reps. Switch to minutes" or "Minutes. Switch to reps". Tapping it switches kind and keeps the value. The middle part has min width 96 dp.
  - a 48 dp "+" (`add`, "More"), which sends `value + 1`.
- **Rules:** no number box, no Reps/Mins segment. The children stay separate TalkBack nodes (iOS `.contain`).
- **Used by** the plan builder's open move and New move / Edit move (§7.3.3, §7.3.4).

**`StepDots(current: Int, total: Int, onAccent = false)`** (iOS `StepDots.swift`): replaces "step 1 of 2" text.
- **Look:** a 14 dp mark per step, 10 dp apart:
  - a finished step (`< current`): a pen `Check` (seed step + 60, line 2, `penTennisInk`);
  - the current step: a filled `accent` dot with a 1.5 dp `accentInk` ring;
  - a later step: an empty 1.5 dp `textTertiary` ring.
- **`onAccent = true`** (Android, A66) draws the check and the later-step ring in `accentForeground`, and the current dot as `accentForeground` with no ring, for StepDots on a lime fill.
- **Semantics:** one node, "Step 1 of 2", with children ignored. The each-move check-in overrides it with "Move 2 of 5".
- **Used by:**
  - the pre-account setup screens (§7.1.7);
  - the "Get set up" pill (§7.2.11);
  - the each-move check-in (§7.6.5).

  The post-account onboarding's "Athlete 2 of 3" pips (`StepProgress`, eyebrow + capsules) are unchanged at `c8f83d6`.

#### 8.6.7 Data marks: crisp, never pen

**`TallyMarks(count, color)`** (iOS `TallyMarks`, Mariah 2026-10-14): lessons in the week strip.
- **Geometry:** four strokes and a fifth across, crisp (they are data).
  - Strokes are 3.2 dp apart, with a 4 dp gap after each group of five, 11 dp tall, starting at x = 1.
  - The fifth runs from (x − 4 × 3.2 − 0.5, maxY − 2) to (x − 0.5, minY + 2).
  - Width = `groups × (4 × 3.2 + 4) + rest × 3.2 + 2`.
- **Stroke:** line 1.6 dp, 2.2 dp under Increase Contrast; round caps.
- **Colors:** `accentInk`, or `accentForeground` on the selected lime day.
- **More than 10:** a number instead (mono caption2 Bold), since nobody counts that many strokes at a glance.
- Hidden from TalkBack; the day's label says the count.

**`FlowBars`**: §8.3.

**`PracticeLine`** (iOS `PracticeTrendChart.swift` at `c38e1f6`; replaces the Mirror, *code wins*; §7.2.9). "How practice felt", session by session.

Inputs: `plans: List<PlanOption(id, title)>`, `entries: List<PracticeEntry(date: Instant, rating: Int 0–4, planId)>`, `now`.

**Controls, top to bottom:**
1. `GradusSegmented` "Time range": 1M · 3M · 1Y · All, default 3M, test tag `trend.range`.
   - TalkBack labels "this month", "last 3 months", "last 12 months", "all time".
   - Weeks back: 5, 13, 52. **All** starts at the earlier of the first session's week and 5 weeks back.
   - Weeks run **Monday to Sunday**. The window ends at the end of today, in the device zone.
2. Plan chips, only with more than one plan that has sessions: a horizontally scrolling row of `GradusChip("All plans")` + each plan title.
   - Test tags `trend.plan.all`, `trend.plan.<index>`.
   - A plan filter that drops out of the chips resets to All plans.
   - Changing the range or plan clears any pinned session.
3. **Header**, min height 30 dp, hidden from TalkBack:
   - while a session is held: its date (`EEE, MMM d`, display title3 Bold), then the rating word in subheadline `textSecondary`;
   - otherwise: "**N%**" (display title2 Heavy, tabular, `heroHighlight(8.dp)`) + "just right" in subheadline `textSecondary`, where N = round(100 × rating-2 count / sessions);
   - with no sessions: "No practice logged".
4. **The plot.** A left label column (trailing-aligned, padding start 8 dp) and a `Canvas`, 140 dp tall.
   - **Label column:** five rows of 28 dp: Hard, A bit hard, **Just right** (Bold, `textPrimary`), A bit easy, Easy (caption, `textSecondary`). Labels stop growing at about 1.3× font scale (iOS caps at xLarge); the words above keep growing.
   - **Ideal zone:** a rounded (8 dp) band behind both the labels and the plot, `flowAccent` at **30%** (45% under Increase Contrast). Its top is at 28 + 4 dp and its height is 3 × 28 − 8 dp, so A bit hard through A bit easy sit wholly inside it.
   - **Canvas:**
     - x = 5 dp + fraction of the window × (width − 10 dp); y = 28 × (rating + 0.5);
     - row lines: 1 px `divider`; the Just right line `textPrimary` at 35% (60% under Increase Contrast);
     - one `textPrimary` line through consecutive sessions, 2 dp (1.5 dp above 60 sessions), round caps and joins;
     - **the line breaks** after a gap of more than 14 days (`runs()`);
     - dots: every session while there are 24 or fewer, otherwise only lone sessions and the latest. Radius 3.5 dp, the latest 4.5 dp, the held one 6 dp, with a 1 px `textPrimary` at 30% vertical rule at the held x.
     - No date axis (*code wins*, `c38e1f6`).
   - **Colour carries nothing**: the rows are the key (WCAG 1.4.1).
5. **Reading it (the scrub).** Drag sideways, or press and hold 0.2 s, and the nearest session by x is held while the finger is down. `HapticFeedback` ticks on each change (§8.5). The scrub ends on lift. Compose sketch:
   ```kotlin
   Modifier.pointerInput(shown, plotWidthPx) {
       val slop = 6.dp.toPx()
       awaitEachGesture {
           val down = awaitFirstDown(requireUnconsumed = false)
           val started = withTimeoutOrNull(200) {              // decided before the 0.2 s hold?
               while (true) {
                   val ev = awaitPointerEvent()
                   if (ev.changes.count { it.pressed } > 1) return@withTimeoutOrNull false   // a second finger fails it
                   val c = ev.changes.firstOrNull { it.id == down.id } ?: return@withTimeoutOrNull false
                   if (!c.pressed) return@withTimeoutOrNull false                       // a tap, not a scrub
                   val d = c.position - down.position
                   if (abs(d.y) > slop && abs(d.y) > abs(d.x)) return@withTimeoutOrNull false  // vertical: the page scrolls
                   if (abs(d.x) > slop) { c.consume(); return@withTimeoutOrNull true }
               }
               @Suppress("UNREACHABLE_CODE") false
           } ?: true                                             // held 0.2 s: start
           if (!started) return@awaitEachGesture
           onScrub(down.position.x)
           while (true) {                                        // later fingers are ignored once it has begun
               val c = awaitPointerEvent().changes.firstOrNull { it.id == down.id } ?: break
               if (!c.pressed) break
               c.consume(); onScrub(c.position.x)
           }
           onScrub(null)
       }
   }
   ```
6. **TalkBack.** The plot is one node (`clearAndSetSemantics`):
   - **Label:** "{plan or All plans}, {range spoken}: N% of T sessions felt just right. H felt harder and E felt easier.", or "…: no practice logged.".
   - **State:** the pinned session as a sentence, "Tuesday, October 14: a bit hard".
   - **Stepping** (iOS adjustable): `progressBarRangeInfo` + `setProgress`, so TalkBack's adjust gestures and the volume keys step through sessions, plus custom actions "Next session" and "Previous session". Verify the adjust gesture on the Pixel.
   - The pinned session is **spoken, not drawn**: TalkBack stepping never leaves the chart visibly held for a sighted user.
   - Test tag `trend.line`.
7. **Loading.** While the first entries load, the card shows a spinner at min height 280 dp.

**`GOEBar(value, span)`** (competition result): a capsule track at `textTertiary` 10% with a 1.5 dp centre rule (`textTertiary` 60%). A gained GOE draws a `flowAccent` capsule to the right; a lost one draws an `attention` capsule to the left. Width = half × |value| / span, at least 3 dp. Direction, not colour, carries the meaning. Hidden from TalkBack; the row reads "3Lz, base 5.90, GOE plus 1.18, score 7.08".

**Goal fork** (`GoalFork`, `GoalForkRow`; iOS `5331b20`): when the parent's and the athlete's season targets differ, the line forks.
- **Drawing:** the current level, then a crisp `attention` 2 dp fork (30 × 34 dp: a stem to 35% of the width, two quadratic branches to the top and bottom ends; hidden from TalkBack), then two branches.
- **Each branch:** the target level in subheadline Bold, plus meta "{Name} · {Sep 20}" in mono caption2 Bold uppercase `textTertiary`.
- **The newest target gets the pen underline** (seed 7).
- **Layout:** `FirstThatFits` picks, in order:
  1. everything on one line;
  2. meta under each target;
  3. the current level above the fork;
  4. names wrapping at word breaks.

  Level names never break mid-word.
- **TalkBack:** "{Greta} is {Juvenile}. {Ingrid} wants {Intermediate} this season, set {Sep 20}; {Greta} wants {Novice}, set {Sep 6}. {Ingrid} changed it most recently."
- **Long-term goals** sit behind a `GradusDisclosure("Long-term")`.

#### 8.6.8 Patterns worth naming (handoff §8)

1. **Section ticks:** a `PenCheckbox(Circle, 20)` beside a step label, checked once the step is filled. The label is subheadline Bold `textPrimary`, with heading semantics and the label "{title}, done" or "{title}". Used for the plan draft's Assign to, Name and Moves (§7.3.4).
2. **Change tags:** `GradusTag` on each move a voice or generated edit touched:
   - "**New**" (tennis) for an added move;
   - "**Reps**" or "**Minutes**" (pool, naming the move's current unit) when the target changed;
   - "**Changed**" (pool) for anything else.

   The plan header shows "**N changes**" (subheadline Bold; TalkBack action label "Each changed move is tagged New or Changed. Tweak anything, then share to keep them."). There is no separate "Looks good": the primary (Update & Share, Activate & Share…) keeps the changes and clears the tags.
3. **Source tags on plan cards:** "**Gradus**" (pool) on a Gradus starter plan, "**By {first}**" (iris) on an athlete-authored one. There is no Adopt button.
4. **Worth a conversation** (handoff §8.3: an orange hand-drawn flag plus "Talk it over with {name}", wherever two people's inputs disagree) is **not implemented at iOS `c8f83d6`**. `PenMarkKind` has no flag shape, and the goals card uses the crisp goal fork (§8.6.7) with no action. Android builds the fork (*code wins*). The flag and its action wait on Mariah and a matching iOS implementation (§12 N98).
5. **Hero number:** §8.6.3. One per screen.
6. **Reaction pill** (A53; iOS `Bubbles.swift`, `464a1b1`):
   - **Content:** the room's reactions tallied: each emoji once, with a count when more than one person chose it ("❤️ 2 👏").
   - **Look:** 13 sp **system emoji font** (`FontFamily.Default` with EmojiCompat; never a Gradus face), padding 7 × 3 dp, `elevated` capsule with a 1 dp `divider` edge.
   - **Placement:** pinned to the bubble's **top corner** (top-trailing for others, top-leading for mine), offset 12 dp inward and 14 dp up. The bubble gains 12 dp of top padding when it has reactions.
   - Hidden from TalkBack; the bubble label ends ", reactions ❤️ 2 👏".
7. **Quote line** (A53, `72739e0`): above a reply's bubble.
   - **Look:** a 2 dp `textTertiary` bar, then the quoted sender in bold + two spaces + the excerpt, caption `textSecondary`, one line, max 260 dp.
   - **Behavior:** tapping it scrolls to the original. That pages back quietly up to 20 pages, rings the original for a moment with a crisp 2 dp `accentInk` outline 4 dp outside the bubble (data, not pen), and moves TalkBack focus there. "Go to quoted message" is also a bubble custom action.

#### 8.6.9 Where the handoff and the merged iOS code differ (code wins)

| Topic | Handoff says | iOS `c8f83d6` does (Android builds this) | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Athlete card practice chart | The **Mirror**: weekly columns, Just right on a midline, harder up, easier down, HARDER/EASIER labels, a key, hold a week | **The practice line**: one ink line over five named rows with the shaded ideal zone (A bit hard–A bit easy), dots per session, a 14-day break, drag or hold to read a session, no key, no date axis. The canvas boards "Mirror (3M, default)", "Mirror, a week held" and "Mirror (1Y)" are **out of date** | `c5e36c7`, `c38e1f6` (the Mirror shipped briefly in `830811a`) |
| Hero numbers | Collected total, invoice total, competition placings, "nothing else" | The same, **plus** the practice line's "N% just right" | `c5e36c7` |
| Goals that differ | A table, one row per person; an orange hand-drawn flag; "Talk it over with Ingrid" | The crisp **goal fork** with the newest target underlined; long-term goals behind a disclosure; no flag, no action | `5331b20` |
| Plan draft steps | **For**, Name, Moves | **Assign to**, Name, Moves, then a "Feedback on" card (Each move / Whole plan) above the notes | `44529b6` |
| Messages unread | "One marker, the count" | The count pill, **plus** bold preview text and an `accent` card edge (the dot is gone) | `ad1e9bf` |
| Move picker sections | Sections fold away; a folded one shows how many are picked | The same, and **every library list starts folded** (Plans › Move library, the athlete's library, the picker); a typed search opens all; category headers ignore taps while searching | `7855ee6` |
| Sport and Category pickers in the move form | The boxed picker field | **Unboxed** `GradusMenuPicker`, flush with the label | `7855ee6`, `1a507b5` |
| Tab heroes | "Live sits inline in the page-title row" (Roster) | Live inline on **every** tab root (Roster, Plans, Resources, Messages, Settings), with Messages' "New" and Resources' "Add resource" in the same row | `d23ab4a` |
| Lesson card | FlowBars since the last lesson + the ring | The same, with a **fit-or-stack** row so it fits a 402 pt phone; message icon opens that athlete's room | `34f5632`, `e5f0fd8` |
| Invoicing To bill | (Needs API) "unbilled lessons per athlete" | Each athlete's To bill is that athlete's draft from `POST /coach/invoices/preview` (nothing saved), 4 at a time, fresh for 60 s; "Checking…" or "Couldn't check" until it is in; the To bill total shows "—" until every draft is in; no plan gate | `101953d`, `d16f40a` |
| Mood-word buckets | Not stated | FlowBars bucket **0 / 1+2+3 / 4** (renamed Hard / Just right / Easy). **The one row where Android does not build iOS:** A44's settled 0+1 / 2 / 3+4 stands, and iOS and the web owe the back-port (A65, §12 N90) | `ad1e9bf` |
| Card shadow | "Soft fill and shadow" | Black 7%, radius 14, y 5 (was 6%, 12, 4) | `ad1e9bf` |

#### 8.6.10 Tests for this section

- **JVM:**
  - the `PenRandom` and `Check` golden vectors;
  - `TallyShape.width` (0 → 2; 4 → 14.8; 5 → 18.8; 10 → 35.6) and tally > 10 shows a number;
  - `PracticeLine.runs` (a 15-day gap splits, a 14-day gap does not);
  - the window math (3M starts 12 Mondays before this week's Monday; All starts no later than 5 weeks back);
  - `totals` and the rounded percent;
  - `nearest` by x;
  - the summary and sentence strings;
  - `n(text)` grapheme counting for seeds ("Waltz jump" 10; "Axel 🧊" 6).
- **Compose UI:**
  - the editing edge swaps on focus and snaps under Remove animations;
  - the picker field shows a dashed edge and "Not chosen" while empty;
  - TargetStepper floors at 1 and switches kind;
  - StepDots reads "Step 1 of 2";
  - pen marks are unreachable by accessibility;
  - the practice line scrubs on a sideways drag, does not intercept a vertical scroll, starts on a 0.2 s hold, ignores a second finger after starting, and steps by TalkBack actions;
  - `LocalIncreasedContrast` from a fake `UiModeManager` contrast of 0.5 restores card edges and thickens strokes;
  - the one-lime budget warns on two primaries.
- **Roborazzi:** every component in light, dark and Increase Contrast at 1.0/1.5/2.0, compared by eye with the canvas boards.
