## 9. Engineering standards

### 9.1 Repository and layout

Three repositories, one contract (iOS §9.1, #13; A7).

| Repo | Holds | Deployed by |
|---|---|---|
| `gradus-coach-start` | Web app, server logic, `/api/v1`, migrations, the contract (`docs/api/openapi.json`, `docs/api/vectors/`, `docs/api/design-tokens.json`), the iOS PRD and this PRD (`docs/android/PRD.md`, A9), the association files (AASA and `assetlinks.json`) | Lovable publish |
| `gradus-ios` | The SwiftUI app (reference implementation) | Xcode Cloud → TestFlight → App Store |
| `gradus-android` (new, `mariah-gill/gradus-android`) | The Kotlin app (phone, widgets, Wear OS), its generated client, a pinned copy of the contract | GitHub Actions → Play internal testing → production |

**Why the split** is unchanged from iOS §9.1: no app churn flows through the repo Lovable syncs. The Capacitor `android/` project, `capacitor.config.ts`, `native/` and the `@capacitor/*` dependencies in the web repo can now be removed (A1 closes iOS §12 #14); that removal is one web PR, verified with `bun run build` and a preview smoke, never bundled with other work (iOS §9.1 "Amended 2026-09-19", §4.1 rule 5). `docs/mobile/` is retired in the same PR (its push and signing notes are superseded by §5.2 and §6.6).

**Contract flow** (identical to iOS §9.1): `gradus-android/Contract/` holds `openapi.json`, `vectors/`, `design-tokens.json` and `SOURCE_COMMIT`. `scripts/sync-contract.sh [REF]` (a port of `gradus-ios/scripts/sync-contract.sh`: GitHub API via `gh` at a ref, or `GRADUS_WEB_DIR=~/Developer/gradus scripts/sync-contract.sh` from a local checkout) fetches them, records the commit, copies runtime vectors into the app (`coach-sports.json` → `core/data/src/main/assets/coach-sports.json`, as iOS copies it into `GradusCore/Resources`), then runs `./gradlew :core:api:generateClient :core:design:generateTokens`. Updating the contract is its own PR. CI fails if generated code is stale (§9.6). A scheduled workflow opens a sync PR on drift (port of `contract-sync-check.yml`, Mon/Wed/Fri 13:00 UTC, `CONTRACT_SYNC_PAT` with read access to the web repo). Squash merges move `SOURCE_COMMIT`; resolve conflicts by re-running the sync script, never by hand-merging generated files (iOS handoff-testflight §4).

**Layout**

```
gradus-android/
  settings.gradle.kts            module list; version catalog
  gradle/libs.versions.toml      every dependency and plugin version (one place)
  build-logic/                   convention plugins: android-library, compose, feature, jvm-test, roborazzi
  app/                           :app — phone application (composition root, Application, MainActivity, FCM service, App Links, Hilt graph)
  wear/                          :wear — Wear OS application (same applicationId, §6.15)
  widgets/                       :widgets — Glance Practice goals and Today widgets, board/session notification renderers
  core/api/                      :core:api — generated OpenAPI client (committed under src/generated), auth broker, interceptors, Supabase session, storage uploads
  core/data/                     :core:data — models, repositories, Room outbox, snapshot caches, sync engine, routing, flags, narration logic, analytics, error reporter
  core/design/                   :core:design — generated tokens, fonts, theme, components, haptics
  core/activities/               :core:activities — ongoing-notification / Live Update state shared by :app and :widgets
  core/widgetdata/               :core:widgetdata — widget account stamp, Practice goals and Today snapshots, store
  feature/auth/ …/onboarding/ …/roster/ …/plans/ …/narration/ …/messages/ …/sessions/
  feature/board/ …/resources/ …/settings/ …/invoicing/ …/competitions/ …/guardians/ …/watch/
  Contract/                      vendored openapi.json, vectors/, design-tokens.json, SOURCE_COMMIT
  scripts/                       sync-contract.sh, normalize-openapi.main.kts (if needed, §9.2), copy-parity.main.kts
  tools/a11y-audit/              accessibility harness (port of Tools/A11yAudit)
  tools/play-screenshots/        listing screenshot harness (port of Tools/AppStoreScreenshots)
  keystores/debug.keystore       shared debug keystore (not a secret; stable fingerprints for App Links and OAuth)
  .run/                          committed Android Studio run configurations
  .github/workflows/             android.yml, contract-sync-check.yml, release.yml
  docs/README.md                 points at docs/android/PRD.md in the web repo; Android-only notes
```

**iOS package → Gradle module (one-to-one).** Module boundaries copy `Packages/*/Package.swift` dependency edges exactly, so a feature that could not import another on iOS cannot on Android.

Every person in mock, preview, test and screenshot data is invented; the iOS mocks are the source of the seed data and are ported with the same invented names (app-store-submission.md §8; memory `gradus-mock-names-must-be-invented`).

### 9.2 Language, frameworks, dependencies

**Language and SDK levels.** Kotlin 2.x with the K2 compiler, `explicitApi()` in `:core:*` modules, `allWarningsAsErrors` in CI. `minSdk = 29` (A6). `targetSdk` = the level Google Play requires for new apps at submission: **36** today (new apps and updates must target Android 16 / API 36 from 2026-08-31; Wear OS apps must target API 35 or higher; source developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/target-sdk, fetched 2026-10-11). `compileSdk` = the latest stable SDK (37 if Android 17's SDK is final at I1 (verify)). Wear: `minSdk 33` (Wear OS 4, §6.15.2, §12 N5), `targetSdk = 36`. JVM toolchain 21. Phones only in 1.0 (A4): no `<supports-screens>` restriction and no tablet layouts; tablets get the phone layout. Orientation: `screenOrientation` is left unset, so the activity follows the user's auto-rotate setting (portrait and both landscapes, no reverse portrait by default), matching iOS iPhone `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations` (Portrait, LandscapeLeft, LandscapeRight; no upside-down, `project.yml`); `fullSensor` is not used. Every screen is checked in landscape (iOS §10.6 P5).

**Dependencies** (all in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, exact versions pinned at K1 to the latest stable releases and bumped by Dependabot PRs):

| Area | Library | iOS counterpart (iOS §9.2, `Package.swift`) |
|---|---|---|
| UI | Jetpack Compose (BOM), Material 3 with Gradus tokens (no dynamic color), `androidx.activity` (edge-to-edge, predictive back), Navigation Compose with type-safe `@Serializable` routes | SwiftUI |
| Concurrency | kotlinx.coroutines, Flow, `StateFlow` view-model state | async/await, `@Observable` |
| DI | Hilt (+ `hilt-navigation-compose`, `hilt-work`) | `Dependencies.swift` composition |
| Lifecycle | `lifecycle-viewmodel-compose`, `lifecycle-runtime-compose` (`collectAsStateWithLifecycle`), `ProcessLifecycleOwner` for foreground/background | scene phase |
| Networking | OkHttp + Retrofit + `kotlinx.serialization` converter; client generated by **openapi-generator** (`kotlin` generator, `library=jvm-retrofit2`, `serializationLibrary=kotlinx_serialization`, `useCoroutines=true`) via its Gradle plugin, output committed | `swift-openapi-generator` + `swift-openapi-urlsession` |
| Supabase | **supabase-kt Auth, Realtime and Storage** (not Realtime and Storage only: the iOS code at HEAD uses supabase-swift `Auth` for session storage and refresh, `GradusAPI/SupabaseSessionManager.swift`, per iOS §6.3); Ktor OkHttp engine | supabase-swift Auth, Realtime, Storage |

| Biometrics | `androidx.biometric` (`BiometricPrompt`, `BIOMETRIC_STRONG or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` on API 30+, `BIOMETRIC_WEAK or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` on API 29, one shared `LockAuthenticators.forSdk`, §6.11.4) | LocalAuthentication |

| Licenses screen | the AboutLibraries Gradle plugin generates the dependency licence list at build time (custom entries for build tools and the four fonts); the Compose screen mirrors `LicensesView.swift` (no `play-services-oss-licenses`; §7.12 Legal) | `LicensesView` |
| Testing | JUnit 5 (JVM modules), JUnit 4 runner where Robolectric needs it, Turbine, kotlinx-coroutines-test, MockWebServer, Robolectric, Compose UI test, **Roborazzi** (screenshot tests on Robolectric), Espresso + ATF accessibility checks, Macrobenchmark + Baseline Profile Gradle plugin | Swift Testing, XCUITest |

**Forbidden in 1.0:** any analytics, attribution, crash or ads SDK (analytics are first-party, iOS §6.12, #19; errors go to `POST /errors`, iOS §6.11); Firebase products other than Messaging; Google Play services Location; any UI kit beyond Material 3; any WebView-based screen except where iOS uses one (iOS uses none in 1.0: the WebM fallback was never built, iOS §6.7). The `com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID` permission merged by Google libraries is removed with `tools:node="remove"`.

**OpenAPI 3.1 risk.** The contract is OpenAPI 3.1.0 with `type: [X, "null"]` unions; openapi-generator's 3.1 support is incomplete (verify at K1). If the Kotlin output mishandles nullability, `scripts/normalize-openapi.main.kts` rewrites a temporary copy to 3.0 semantics (`nullable: true`) before generation; the vendored `Contract/openapi.json` is never edited. The decision and its tests land in K1.

**Decoding across the deploy gap.** Lovable publishes by hand while CI ships the app automatically, so the app can meet an older or newer server (iOS handoff-2026-10-04: "a response field the iOS app reads must be optional in the zod contract … Enums are closed: add a field rather than a value"). Android decodes with `ignoreUnknownKeys = true`, `explicitNulls = false`, `coerceInputValues = true`, and every generated enum gets an `UNKNOWN` fallback so an unlearned value never fails a whole response. Server-side the iOS rule still holds: new response fields optional, add a field rather than an enum value.

**Compile-time release flags** (iOS `GradusCore/ReleaseFlags.swift`): `ReleaseFlags.ASK_GRADUS_ENABLED = false` (#22) as a Kotlin `const val` in `:core:data`, not remote config, "so what ships is what was tested". The native reset flag (`GRADUS_NATIVE_RESET`, on since iOS #124) is `BuildConfig.GRADUS_NATIVE_RESET = true`.

### 9.3 Architecture inside the app

- **Unidirectional data flow** (iOS §9.3). Composables read immutable UI state from a `@HiltViewModel` (`StateFlow<UiState>`); writes call repository methods that update the local store and enqueue mutations. One view model per iOS model (`RosterModel` → `RosterViewModel`, `PlanDetailModel` → `PlanDetailViewModel`, …) so state transitions can be compared one-to-one.
- **Repositories** are interfaces with `Live…` and `Preview…` (mock) implementations, mirroring `LiveGuardianRepositories` / `PreviewGuardianRepositories` and friends. Every screen has Compose previews and tests with no network. The mock implementations port the iOS preview seeds verbatim (invented names).
- **Routing** is one sealed `AppRoute` hierarchy in `:core:data` decoded from App Links, `gradus://` links, push payloads (`gradus.route`) and in-app navigation, a port of `GradusCore/Routing/AppRoute.swift`; its tests port the iOS routing tests, including "every URL the web's mailers build" (iOS #120).
- **Errors** are a typed `ApiError` carrying the server's `code` and mapped to user copy in one place (`ErrorCopy`), copy taken verbatim from the iOS mapping. Error toasts persist with a visible close button and clear on tab or screen change; form errors are inline only (iOS #114, handoff-2026-10-09 §2).
- **Feature flags and client policy** come from `GET /meta/config` and `GET /meta/client-policy`, cached; the force-update screen appears when `versionName < minSupportedVersion.android` and its button opens the Play listing (iOS opens Safari; QA.md §8).
- **Offline store** (mirrors the code at HEAD, which differs from iOS §6.5's prose; §6.5 owns the policy and the file table): iOS keeps the outbox in SwiftData (`PendingMutation`, `Store/StoreContainer.swift`) and the domain caches as per-user JSON snapshots with ETags (`me.json`, `roster.json`, `plans.json`, `resources.json`, `parent-settings.json`, `athlete-settings.json`, `team-guardians.json`, `coach-visibility-*.json`, `celebration-dismissals.json`, `active-session.json`). Android does the same: a per-user Room database `noBackupFilesDir/Gradus/<userId>/store.db` holding only the `pending_mutation` table (same columns: id, createdAt, method, path, body, idempotencyKey, attempts, nextAttemptAt, state `pending|inFlight|failed|conflicted`, lastErrorCode, lastErrorMessage, entityKind, entityId, entityLabel), the snapshot files with the **same file names** beside it in that directory (kotlinx.serialization, written atomically), and a device-wide `board.db` for Live Board follows, mutes and history. Sign-out deletes the user's directory (iOS `StoreContainer.wipe`); `board.db` survives (A34).
- **Sync engine** ports `Sync/SyncEngine.swift` exactly: backoff base 2 s, max 300 s, 12 attempts, ±25 % jitter; a retryable failure (5xx, 429, transport) stops the pass so later writes never overtake it; non-retryable 4xx parks as `failed`; 409/422 park as `conflicted`; parked rows are skipped; concurrent drains coalesce. Drains run on foreground, on connectivity regained (`ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback`, the `NWPathMonitor` equivalent), after each enqueue, and in a WorkManager `CoroutineWorker` with a `CONNECTED` constraint. *Note:* the iOS project declares the `training.gradus.app.sync` background task identifier but no code registers it at HEAD; Android's WorkManager drain implements the background drain the iOS PRD §6.5 describes.
- **Session storage** (iOS §6.4 "Session and device security"): the supabase-kt `SessionManager` is backed by a Tink-encrypted DataStore whose key lives in Android Keystore (not user-authentication-bound, so background sync can refresh after the first unlock, the `AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly` equivalent). Auto Backup and device-to-device transfer **exclude** the session, the Room databases, the snapshot files and caches (`dataExtractionRules` and `fullBackupContent`); only the non-sensitive device preferences listed in §6.5 (appearance, read-aloud voice, remembered identifier and the other keys marked "Backed up") are backed up, as iOS `UserDefaults` are, and a restored install starts signed out (A24).
- **Process death.** Every screen survives process death: navigation state is restored by Navigation Compose, unsent form input is held in `SavedStateHandle`, and the session timer stores a start timestamp and pause intervals (iOS §6.5 "Session timer specifics"), never a counter.
- **Threading.** Main-safe repositories; disk and network on `Dispatchers.IO` injected via Hilt qualifiers so tests use `StandardTestDispatcher`.
- **Mock mode** exists only in the `debug` build type (the iOS `-GradusMock` launch arguments are compiled into Debug only).

### 9.4 Backend engineering rules

Every rule in iOS §9.4 and §4.1 applies unchanged to Android-driven backend work (A2): API routes hold no business logic; every endpoint has an OpenAPI entry; **new `/api/v1` routes are imported in `scripts/openapi.ts`** or they are missing from the contract (iOS handoff-testflight §4); `bun run openapi` and `bun run design-tokens` regenerate the contract and CI diff-checks both; every new table ships GRANTs and RLS in the same migration; service-role-only functions revoke EXECUTE from `PUBLIC, anon, authenticated`; after a migration merges, ask Lovable to apply pending migrations and run the `docs/api/SMOKE.md` precheck (§4.1 rules 11–12); secrets live in Lovable Cloud and are read with `process.env`. Android-specific additions:

1. **No Android-only product endpoints.** Platform differences live in transport (FCM vs APNs), identity verification (audiences, Services ID), association files and platform labels only.
2. **Platform values.** `X-Gradus-Client` is `android/<versionName>+<versionCode>` from the phone and `wearos/<versionName>+<versionCode>` from the watch (iOS uses `ios/…` and `watchos/…`, `GradusWatch/WatchConfig.swift`). Server code that branches on platform reads it from this header, never from a request body field it does not already have.
3. **Additive enums on request schemas only.** Widening a request enum (`analytics` `platform`) is safe for the installed iOS app; never add a value to a **response** enum the iOS client decodes as closed (handoff-2026-10-04).
4. **Push sends are platform fan-out, not duplicated triggers.** Each trigger calls one `notifyUsers` that sends to every token of the recipients; per-platform payload building lives in `apns.server.ts` and `fcm.server.ts`.
5. **Android work never collides with iOS QA.** Android-driven web PRs are small, independently revertible, rebased before merge, never left open across a day Mariah edits in Lovable, and never published while an iOS TestFlight build depends on the previous behavior (iOS §9.6 "Branching, web repo"; handoff-2026-10-09 §1 worktree rule: never switch branches in shared checkouts, use worktrees).
6. **Association files** are code, built from constants with tests (as `src/lib/apple-app-site-association.ts` and its test), served as `application/json` with a one-day cache; `assetlinks.json` lists only real fingerprints (no placeholders), mirroring the AASA rule. `assetlinks.json` carries no paths: Android App Link paths are declared in the `:app` manifest `<intent-filter android:autoVerify="true">` (`https`, host `gradus.training`, `pathPrefix`/`pathPattern`), generated from the same list as `UNIVERSAL_LINK_PATHS` in `src/lib/apple-app-site-association.ts` (`/board`, `/board/*`, `/i/*`, `/login`, `/signup/*`, `/coach`, `/coach/*`, `/parent`, `/parent/*`, `/athlete`, `/athlete/*`, `/g/*`, `/team/*`, `/p/*`, `/verified`, `/verified/*`, `/auth/confirm`), plus the one Android-only path `/auth/apple/done` (the Apple web-flow return, S-7, declared with SA4). Inclusions only, on every API level (§6.10.1). Before Android 15 an intent filter has no exclude, so the AASA's `UNIVERSAL_LINK_EXCLUDES` (`/reset-password`, `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/support`, `/unsubscribe`, `/admin`, `/org-admin`, `/api/*`, `/email/*`, `/lovable/*`) plus `/delete-account` stay in the browser simply by never being listed (and `/coach` is declared as the exact path plus `/coach/` prefix, so no excluded path is caught by a broad prefix). A unit test in gradus-android diffs the merged manifest's paths against a vendored copy of the AASA path list (refreshed by `sync-contract.sh`). **Ordering hazard:** no build declares `/verified`, `/verified/*` or `/auth/confirm` until the milestone that routes them (K4: forward `status`, `externalPayload` and every `signature` untouched to `POST /guardian/verification/complete`, then refresh; K14: `/auth/confirm`). An installed build that claims a path it cannot route swallows the KWS redirect silently (handoff-remaining-prd §5.2: "`/verified` on iOS is currently a silent open").
7. **Webhook-style public routes** (any Play notification route, if ever needed) live under `/api/public/…`, outside the `/api/v1` kill switch, like the KWS and App Store webhooks (iOS §6.13 B4).

### 9.5 Testing

| Layer | What | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| Shared server functions | Unchanged web tests; new tests for SA1–SA8 (FCM payload and token pruning, audience lists, Apple web flow state and nonce, assetlinks builder, integrity decode log-only "never enforcing", platform tagging, `androidExternalLinksEnabled` default true) | `bun test` |
| Contract parity vectors | Every file in `Contract/vectors/` runs in Kotlin: `lesson-recurrence.json` (`expandSlotOccurrences` port), `name-normalization.json` (`normalizeName` port), `analytics-events.json` (the tracker's area and prop allow-list), `event-key.json`, `coach-sports.json` (the bundled asset equals `Contract/` byte for byte, as iOS asserts) | JUnit 5 parameterized tests in `:core:data` |
| Generated code | `:core:api` compiles; a round-trip test decodes captured fixtures (including the iOS `demo-board.json` capture) and an unknown enum value decodes to `UNKNOWN` | JUnit 5 |
| Sync engine | Outbox ordering, backoff schedule with pinned jitter, idempotency replay, 409/422 → conflicted, 4xx → failed, 5xx/429/transport → retry and stop, coalesced drains, relaunch survival, sign-out wipe; ports of the GradusCore sync tests | JUnit 5 + in-memory Room (Robolectric) + MockWebServer scripted fake API |
| Repositories and caches | ETag `If-None-Match`/304 handling, snapshot load/save per domain, per-user isolation | JUnit 5 + MockWebServer |
| View models | State transitions per screen, ported from the iOS model tests (same cases, same names where possible) | JUnit 5 + Turbine + coroutines-test |
| Compose UI, critical flows | Sign in, open roster, open plan, send message, start and end a session, open a board (iOS §9.5 list), each role's tab shell, minors' text-only composer, consent gates | Robolectric + Compose UI test against mock repositories |
| Screenshots | Every routed screen for every mock role, light and dark, font scale 1.0 and 2.0; golden PNGs committed; a diff fails the PR. Also the parity baseline: the same screen list as `Tools/AppStoreScreenshots` | Roborazzi |
| Accessibility (automated) | ATF checks (touch target ≥ 48 dp, contrast, labels, duplicate descriptions) on every screen in the screenshot run; the `tools/a11y-audit` harness walks each mock role like `Tools/A11yAudit` and dumps the semantics tree | Robolectric `enableAccessibilityChecks()`, Espresso `AccessibilityChecks` on emulator |
| Instrumented | App Links resolution (`pm get-app-links`), notification channels and posting, WorkManager drain, Keystore session survive process restart, system-camera intent and Photo Picker launch, TextToSpeech init | Compose/Espresso on emulator API 29 and API 36 (CI) |
| Wear OS | View models and Data Layer link with a fake; screens on the round and small devices | Robolectric + Compose for Wear test; Roborazzi round screenshots |
| Performance | Cold start to interactive with a cached account; Baseline Profile generated and committed | Macrobenchmark on the automation AVD only (device rule, §10.1); Pixel startup is read by hand from `adb shell am start -W` only with Mariah's go-ahead (§2 owns the target) |
| Copy parity | `scripts/copy-parity.main.kts` lists user-facing literals in each iOS feature package (`Text("…")`, `Button("…")`, `.navigationTitle("…")`, alert titles and messages, `accessibilityLabel("…")`) and reports any not present in the matching Android module's `strings.xml`; an allow-list records deliberate platform substitutions (e.g. "Face ID" → the §6.11 Android wording). Warning in CI, reviewed at each milestone's done check | Kotlin script against a pinned gradus-ios checkout |
| Manual | Real Pixel, real accounts (the seeded review coach, parent and minor athlete, #26), airplane mode, Doze/app standby, process death ("Don't keep activities" and `adb shell am kill`), notification permission denied, battery saver | `docs/android/QA.md` (created in KP9), a port of `docs/ios/QA.md` section for section |

Production is the only Supabase environment (iOS §9.5); automated tests never hit it. Strings live in per-module `res/values/strings.xml`, copied verbatim from iOS user-facing copy. Lint's `HardcodedText` checks XML layouts and menus only and does not see Compose, so a **custom lint or detekt rule in `build-logic`** fails the build on string literals passed to `Text`, `Button`, `contentDescription`, `semantics` labels, `AlertDialog` `title`/`text`, and `Toast`/`Snackbar` in any `:feature:*`, `:wear` or `:core:design` source; user-facing copy comes from `stringResource(R.string.*)` (tests and `@Preview` sources are exempt). The copy-parity script then compares `strings.xml` with the iOS literals.

### 9.6 CI, builds, releases

- **GitHub Actions, web repo.** Existing `Bun CI` (lint, typecheck, OpenAPI freshness, tests, design-token freshness, build). Add a test for the assetlinks builder in SA5. No Android jobs here.
- **GitHub Actions, Android repo (`.github/workflows/android.yml`, on every PR and push to `main`, `ubuntu-latest`):** set up JDK 21 (Temurin) and the Android SDK; Gradle cache; `./gradlew spotlessCheck lint detekt` (style and static checks, warnings as errors); **contract drift check**: `./gradlew :core:api:generateClient :core:design:generateTokens` then `git diff --exit-code core/api/src/generated core/design/src/generated` (port of the iOS "Verify generated client and color catalog match the vendored contract" step); `./gradlew test` (JVM, Robolectric, Roborazzi verify); `./gradlew :app:assembleRelease :wear:assembleRelease` with a throwaway signing config on PRs; an emulator job (API 29 and API 36, KVM) running `connectedDebugAndroidTest` (verify KVM availability on the runner class); artifacts on failure (reports, Roborazzi diffs). The emulator job and every local instrumented, benchmark or screenshot script pin `ANDROID_SERIAL` to an automation device (§10.1 device rule). **Every test task ran:** a final CI step fails when any module that has `src/test` (or `src/androidTest` in the emulator job) produced no test report, the Android counterpart of iOS #122, where a test target left out of the scheme silently skipped its tests. The scheduled `contract-sync-check.yml` opens drift PRs; bot-opened PRs need a close/reopen or a push to trigger CI (same caveat as iOS).
- **Workflow hygiene** (ported from gradus-ios `.github/workflows/`): every third-party action is pinned by commit SHA with the version in a comment (`actions/checkout@<sha> # v4.2.2`); `contract-sync-check.yml` first checks that `CONTRACT_SYNC_PAT` is set and fails with an explanation if not, pushes to branch `chore/contract-sync-auto`, applies the `contract-sync` label, and writes a PR body that is a pure regeneration note (source commit and changed files, nothing else).
- **Builds and distribution (`release.yml`, on push to `main`).** Mirrors Xcode Cloud's "archive every push to `main` → internal group" (handoff-remaining-prd §2.4): builds `:app:bundleRelease` and `:wear:bundleRelease`, signs with the **upload key** from GitHub secrets, and:
  - **Before the Play Console exists (A8):** also builds a universal release APK, uploads it as the workflow artifact `gradus-android-<versionCode>.apk`, and a local Mac session installs it on Mariah's Pixel with `adb install -r` (interim channel "KT0", A39). No internal track, no Play App Signing, no Play Integrity until then. **KT0 and Play builds cannot update each other:** after G2 Play builds are signed with the Google-held app signing key, and Android refuses an update whose signature differs. Moving from KT0 to KT1 means uninstalling the KT0 build on the Pixel first, which loses its local outbox and caches, so let the outbox drain to empty (no "{n} to sync" chip and no failed send showing) before uninstalling. After G2, Play's **internal app sharing** is the channel for ad-hoc builds. KT0 builds and Play builds never coexist under the same applicationId; the `.debug` suffix build does coexist with either.
  - **After the Play Console exists:** **Gradle Play Publisher** (`com.github.triplet.play`) uploads both bundles to the **internal testing** track (phone and Wear OS form factor) with release notes from the merged PR titles, using a Play Console service account (`PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` secret). Closed testing and production promotions are manual steps in Play Console (Mariah), like external TestFlight and App Store submission. fastlane is not used (iOS §9.6: "Fastlane is not required").
- **Versioning.** `versionName` = marketing version `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, **1.0.0** for the first Play release (A1), kept equal to the iOS marketing version for the same feature set where practical. `versionCode` must be unique and increasing across every bundle in the app (phone and Wear OS share the listing): phone `versionCode = 100000 + GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER`, Wear `200000 + GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER` (A16; verify Play's uniqueness rules for multi-form-factor apps); local builds use `1`. `X-Gradus-Client` carries both (`android/1.0.0+100042`).
- **Signing.** Play App Signing holds the app signing key (required for new apps); the upload key is Mariah's (§5.2 step 13). Debug builds use `keystores/debug.keystore` (committed, password `android`) so the debug OAuth client works on every machine and in CI; because that keystore is public, the debug package is never listed in `assetlinks.json`, and App Links are enabled on dev devices with `adb shell pm set-app-links-user-selection` (§6.10.1). `applicationIdSuffix = ".debug"` for debug (A38), so a debug build and the Play build coexist on Mariah's Pixel.
- **Build-time config** (iOS `project.yml` settings read by `AppConfig.swift` and, on the watch, `WatchConfig.swift`): `BuildConfig` fields shared by `:app` and `:wear` through a convention plugin, each overridable by a Gradle property (`-Pgradus.apiBaseUrl=…`):
  | Field | Release | Debug |
  |---|---|---|
  | `API_BASE_URL` | `https://gradus.training` | `http://localhost:8080`, reached through `adb reverse tcp:8080 tcp:8080` on emulators and devices alike (one rule, §5.2 step 10; `10.0.2.2` is not used) |
  | `SUPABASE_URL` | `https://sdqfaqxmdmujxqhwlqdi.supabase.co` | same |
  | `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | the public anon key, the exact `GRADUS_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` value in gradus-ios `project.yml` (public, not a secret) | same |
  | `GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID` | the G1 web client ID; empty until SA3 is published (hides the Google button, package 1.3) | same |
  | `APPLE_WEB_SIGNIN_ENABLED` | `false` until SA4 is live | same |
  | `GRADUS_NATIVE_RESET` | `true` (§9.2) | same |
  | `PLAY_LISTING_LIVE` | `false` until the Play listing exists, then `true` (switches the force-update action from the web link to Google Play, §7.1.0) | `false` |
  | `PLAY_INTEGRITY_CLOUD_PROJECT_NUMBER` | the `gradus-prod` project number (after G2) | same |
- **Build types.** `debug` (mock mode available, `http://localhost:8080`, cleartext to localhost only, StrictMode on), `release` (R8 full mode with shrinking and resources shrinking, `https://gradus.training`, no logs below WARN, Baseline Profile included), `benchmark` (release-like, debuggable false, for Macrobenchmark). No product flavors.
- **Branching, web repo.** As iOS §9.6: short-lived branches, rebase before merge, publish in Lovable deliberately after CI is green.
- **Branching, Android repo.** Short-lived branches, squash merge with `Title (#n)` subjects, worktrees for parallel sessions (`~/Developer/gradus-android-wt/<branch>`), never `git switch`/`reset`/`stash` in the shared checkout (handoff-2026-10-09 §1). Cloud sessions may build and run JVM tests; device work runs on the Mac (§5.2).
- **Crash and error visibility** (iOS §6.11, §9.6). Caught errors and crashes go to `POST /api/v1/errors` tagged `platform=android` (after SA1) with version, build, OS and device model: an `UncaughtExceptionHandler` writes the crash to disk and the next launch uploads it (`kind: "crash"`); `ActivityManager.getHistoricalProcessExitReasons` reports ANRs as `kind: "hang"` and native crashes as `kind: "crash"` on the next launch (the MetricKit equivalent). Dedup of the same message and route within a minute and a cap of 50 reports per session, as `LiveErrorReporter`. No third-party crash SDK. Play Console's Android vitals (crash rate, ANR rate) is the secondary view once the listing exists.

## 10. Milestones and delivery

### 10.1 How we work

Milestone-driven, no calendar, no time estimates (iOS #11, #12; A7). One milestone at a time per stream; when one meets its definition of done, the next starts. Claude Code builds and verifies its own work (emulator, Roborazzi screenshots, tests, the simulate-offline switch, and on the Pixel only what the device rule below allows) and sends Mariah **one short update a day**: what changed, a screen recording (scrcpy) or screenshots, and any decision that needs her. She taps through on her Pixel when she wants to. If a forecast is ever wanted, it is computed from the measured pace of completed milestones.

**Device rule (one rule, everywhere in this PRD).** Automated instrumented tests, benchmarks and screenshot runs use only the `Gradus Automation Pixel` AVD (and the Wear automation AVDs), with `ANDROID_SERIAL` pinned in the Gradle task and in every script (handoff-2026-10-09 §1: automation never runs on Mariah's own devices). On Mariah's Pixel (and her Wear OS watch) a session may only install the `.debug` build or a KT0 build with `adb -s <serial> install -r`, capture scrcpy recordings, and read logcat, each with her go-ahead for that batch. It never runs `connectedAndroidTest`, Macrobenchmark, `pm clear` or uninstall there; the KT0 → KT1 uninstall (§9.6) is Mariah's own tap.

**Approvals** (handoff-remaining-prd §6; handoff-preQA §"Never merge"; handoff-consent-S2-S3; handoff-2026-10-09 §1; iOS §10.6):
1. No merge, Lovable publish, migration apply, secret change, or Play Console promotion (closed testing, production, rollout) without Mariah's explicit go-ahead for that batch. A one-off authorization does not carry over.
2. Adversarial review before every merge, docs PRs included; findings and fixes go in the PR body.
3. One web PR per domain; a PRD edit (including this document) rides in its own docs PR.
4. No durations or dates in plans or reports to Mariah: milestones only.
5. A PR not on the session's list came from another session; it is not merged without asking Mariah.
6. `API_V1_ENABLED`, `PARENT_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` and every Lovable secret (including the new `FCM_*`, `GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID`, `APPLE_SIWA_SERVICES_ID`, `PLAY_INTEGRITY_*`) are Mariah's to set; no Claude session flips them.

**Streams.** Android work starts now, in parallel with iOS QA (A7):
- **Android stream** in `gradus-android` (Mac sessions for device work; cloud sessions for code and JVM tests).
- **Server-for-Android stream** in the web repo (cloud sessions), small additive PRs SA1–SA8, never bundled with iOS work and never published in a way that breaks an installed TestFlight build (§9.4 rule 5).
- **Account stream** (Mariah): G0–G2. The Play Console (A8) can arrive at any moment; when it does, the Play-gated milestones are taken next, whatever else is in progress (iOS §10.1 rule for enrollment).

**iOS remains the reference.** Each Android milestone starts by reading the matching iOS package and its tests at the current gradus-ios `main`; where the iOS PRD and the code disagree, the code wins (A2), and the PR says so in one line.

**Definition of done, for every Android milestone:** merged to `main` of the right repo; CI green (lint, unit, Robolectric, Roborazzi, contract drift, release assemble); verified on the emulator and, where behavior depends on hardware or Google services (push, microphone, camera, biometrics, notifications, App Links, Credential Manager, Wear pairing), on Mariah's Pixel; **parity checked** against iOS for the milestone's screens (same mock role side by side: copy, fields, rules, empty and error states, offline behavior, and the copy-parity report reviewed); TalkBack spot-checked on new screens; shown working in the daily update; nothing in §4 violated; judgment calls and any "code wins over the iOS PRD" notes listed in the PR description.

### 10.2 Milestone sequence

Package numbers refer to Appendix F; endpoints are in Appendix A, screens in §7. **Ordering:** account steps and small server changes first (they unblock everything and fit around iOS QA), then the Android foundation, then the iOS feature order. The 1.0 iOS add-ons that iOS built as separate later milestones (the why-prompt L2, sources UI L5, analytics A2, consent S2, athlete authoring AP3, read-aloud W1-phone) are folded into the Android feature milestone that owns their screens, because the backend for them already exists and building them in place avoids retrofits (§10.3).

**Accounts (Mariah)**

| # | Milestone | Scope | Unblocks | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|---|

**Messages on the wrist (#54).** Not a KW milestone (iOS: "Not a W milestone"). The server half is SA2 (`category` and `uid` in the FCM data, S-3). The phone Reply lands with K9. The watch half (forwarding, the bridging switch, the Messages screens) lands after KW0 and K9. QA per §7.15.7.

**The "Show, don't tell" redesign** (§8.6; handoff §10) is built in the handoff's order:
1. tokens and surfaces, shared components and the button pass, inside K1 (Appendix F 1.1);
2. each milestone's screens in their redesigned form only. There is no pre-redesign build of any screen. Where milestones run in parallel, the handoff's screen order (plan builder, roster, athlete card, invoicing, messages, parent, onboarding) decides which screen is reviewed against the canvas first;
3. the API work (§12 N95, N96) lands when the server does;
4. the accessibility pass closes in KP.

Analytics instrumentation (the iOS A2 work: `TrackedScreen` on every tab root and routed screen, Resources events) is part of each feature milestone's definition of done, using the tracker built in K1; it is verified as a whole in K9 against preview.

### 10.3 Build order rationale

1. **Accounts and server first, in small pieces.** G1 and SA1–SA5 have no dependency on app screens and unblock push, sign-in and links; they also fit between iOS QA publishes without risk.
2. **Foundation before features** so offline, auth, routing, analytics and error reporting are never retrofitted (iOS §10.3 rule 2). The tracker and reporter exist from K1, so every later milestone instruments as it goes.
3. **Live Board and messaging first among features** (iOS §10.3 rule 3), for the same reasons, and because they exercise FCM and the ongoing-notification work early.
4. **The iOS later-milestones are folded in.** iOS built L2, L5, A2, S2, AP3 and W1 after their host screens existed; on Android the server side is done, so building each with its host screen avoids a second pass and keeps parity reviews per screen complete.
5. **Wear OS after K6 and K7** because KW1 needs `PlanNarration` and the read-aloud player (K6), KW4 needs athlete authoring (K6), and KW5, if iOS ships it, needs the session model (K7). KW0 can start any time after K1.
6. **Play-gated work waits on G2 without blocking** (KT1, SA6, the Play signing fingerprint in SA5, live age signals); KT0 keeps Mariah's Pixel on current builds meanwhile.

### 10.4 Relationship to the web sunset

iOS §10.4 criterion 4 ("The Android app is live") is met by KL. The sunset itself remains a separate Mariah decision on the iOS §10.4 criteria; the Android-relevant measure is the share of weekly-active coaches, parents and athletes on Android devices who use the Android app (the "Get the app" mobile-web banner must link to the Play listing for Android browsers once KL is live, and the retired-route redirect of iOS §10.4 item 5 gains a Play redirect for Android browsers; one small web change taken then, §5.1 S-17). iOS §10.5 (interim store presence with the Capacitor shell) has no Android counterpart: no shell ships (A1). iOS §10.6–§10.11 (pre-QA gate, learning loop, analytics, consent, athlete authoring, watch) map to KP, K6, K9, K4/KS3, K6 and KW0–KW7 respectively (§10.2).

| A-10 | **Sign in with Apple web flow**: Services ID misconfigured (not grouped with the App ID) yields a different `sub`; private-relay email forwarding needs the sending domain registered; Apple sends name and email only on the first authorization; a Custom Tab may be closed mid-flow | Duplicate accounts, an Apple user unable to reach their iPhone-created account, revocation failures | Group the Services ID with `training.gradus.app`; the broker's lookup order (`auth_identities` by `sub`, then confirmed email) already prevents duplicates when `sub` matches; an end-to-end test with an Apple ID first used on iOS; revoke with the issuing client id; cancel and back handled as "cancelled", never an error. |
| A-11 | **Google OAuth clients** depend on signing-certificate fingerprints, and the final one exists only after Play App Signing (A8) | Google sign-in fails in Play-distributed builds if the Play signing SHA-1 is missing | Register debug and upload fingerprints now and the Play signing fingerprint the day the Play Console exists; a release-checklist item; the button hides when the client is not configured (A5). |
| A-12 | **Contract drift and decoding** between three clients and an unpublished server | Android fails to decode a response, or an Android-driven change breaks iOS | §4.1 rules 14–15; contract re-sync script and CI drift check in gradus-android, as in gradus-ios; `ignoreUnknownKeys`; vectors shared. |
| A-13 | **Moving reference**: iOS is in QA and keeps changing | Android ships an older behavior | Parity ledger (§4.3 rule 11); each Android milestone starts with a gradus-ios diff since the last reconciled commit. |
| A-14 | **Android 16 Live Update promotion** has eligibility rules and older versions have none | The board or timer notification shows as an ordinary ongoing notification | Design the notification to be complete as an ordinary ongoing notification on API 29+; promotion is an enhancement (A12). |
| A-15 | **Notification permission denied** (Android 13+) | Users miss messages and prompts | Ask in context; Settings → Device shows the real state with a link to the system setting; in-app badges and the foreground refresh still work. |
| A-16 | **Process death** while a sheet, form or the timer is open | Lost input or a confusing restart | `SavedStateHandle` for every form; drafts persisted (messages, plan edits) as on iOS; the timer reconstructs from its stored start timestamp and pause intervals; Robolectric and instrumented "don't keep activities" tests. |

| A-19 | **TTS variability**: engines differ by OEM (Google, Samsung), voices may be missing or network-only, and no gender metadata exists | Read-aloud sounds worse or uses an unexpected voice | A14 ranking with on-device-only filter; the picker and its "install voice data" pointer; Automatic falls back to the engine default English voice and says to install a higher-quality voice, as iOS says to download a Premium voice. |

| A-23 | **Accessibility audit tooling** differs from the iOS XCUITest harness | AAA claims unverified on Android | Compose semantics tests, Accessibility Test Framework checks in Espresso/Compose tests, Accessibility Scanner on the device, and a scripted TalkBack device pass (the iOS `device-accessibility-script.md` equivalent). |
| A-24 | **Firebase project ownership** | FCM tied to a personal Google account | Create the Firebase/Google Cloud project under the Gradus Sports Google Workspace organization with Mariah as owner (§12 N6). |
| A-25 | **Play Age Signals** is beta and its surface may change; state-law enforcement shifts | Rework, or a compliance gap | Wrap it behind one interface; tighten-only so failure never blocks; re-verify the API and the laws at the age-signals milestone (A20). |

Fallbacks in order: a pre-processing step that downgrades 3.1 type arrays to 3.0 `nullable`; hand-written serializers for the 15 `oneOf`/`anyOf` sites; Ktor + kotlinx models from another generator. Same CI drift check either way (A11, §4.1 rule 17). |
| A-27 | **US link-out without External Content Links enrollment** (A37, Mariah's informed decision 2026-10-14, to avoid Google's fee): Google Play's US payments policy requires enrollment in its program before linking US users to purchase outside Play; the court-ordered rules (Epic v. Google, §4.2) are still contested. Separately, Play's Payments policy may treat the non-US text line "Manage your plan on the web." as a lead to outside payment (verify) | Rejection of a release at review, removal of the app, or a policy strike / account suspension for repeated violations | The `androidExternalLinksEnabled` kill switch (default true) removes the link without a release; if Google flags the link, turn it off (every user then gets the §6.8 flag-off text lines, a strict subset of iOS, and the listing falls back to the neutral sentence "Existing Coach and Team subscriptions unlock in the app.", Appendix D) and decide then between enrolling in External Content Links (§6.8 lists what it requires) and staying link-free; both switch states are tested before release; counsel review recommended before submission; the review notes describe the app honestly (Appendix D). For the non-US text line, fallback: status only, no sentence. |

## Appendix A — API v1 endpoint map for Android

**Android uses exactly the API v1 surface iOS uses.** The full map from web server functions to endpoints, with `[pub]`, `[idem]`, `[etag]` and `[page]` markers and priorities, is iOS PRD Appendix A, and it is not repeated here. At web HEAD (`d42c514`) the contract has 215 paths and 237 operations across these groups: `adult-athlete`, `analytics`, `ask`, `athlete`, `athletes`, `auth`, `boards`, `coach`, `competitions`, `devices`, `errors`, `feedback`, `guardian`, `invites`, `live-activities`, `me`, `message-targets`, `messages`, `meta`, `orgs`, `parent`, `plans`, `promo-codes`, `public`, `recaps`, `resources`, `rooms`, `safety`, `saved-answers`, `signup`, `sport-requests`, `team-invites`, `voice`. Android calls every operation iOS calls, for the same reasons, with the differences in the two tables below. Since 2026-10-11 that includes `PUT /me/ai-consent` and `/me.aiConsent` (§6.7.1a; every AI route answers 403 `ai_consent_required` until allowed, minors 403 `ai_unavailable_for_minors`), `PUT /messages/{id}/reaction` and `replyToId`/`replyTo`/`reactions` (§7.5, A53), the optional voice-note `transcript` on `POST /rooms/{id}/messages` (§6.7.6, A55), `feedbackScope` on `PATCH /plans/{id}` and `moveRatings` on `POST /plans/{id}/sessions` and the session log (§7.3.4, §7.6.5), `POST /coach/moves/import` (§7.3.2a), `POST /coach/moves/draft` (`draftMove`, #53: coach only, rate-limited, writes nothing, no idempotency key, never queued; §7.3.8a), and `POST /plans/{id}/status` no longer answers 409 `bench_choice_required` (#52), although Android keeps the fallback (§7.3.5). `GET /coach/athletes/{id}/active-plans` stays in use for wrap-ups and that fallback.

**Corrections to iOS Appendix A found at HEAD.** These apply to both clients.

- `GET /coach/home` was never built. Use the separate roster, summaries and wrap-up calls.
- `POST /me/presence` (iOS Appendix A, P0; iOS §7.13 "on foreground, at most every 5 minutes") is **not called** by gradus-ios at HEAD (no presence call in any source). Android does not call it either **[code wins]**; whether presence returns on both clients is §12 N23.
- `POST /auth/username/resolve` is listed but unused: `POST /auth/password` resolves usernames itself (`resolveSignInEmail`). Android does not call it.
- Built routes the iOS appendix does not list: `POST /auth/web-session` (signed-in browser handoff to `/coach/paywall`, `/coach/settings`, `/parent/team`, `/parent/settings`; §6.8), `GET /coach/checklist`, `POST /sport-requests`, `GET /coach/up-next`, and `POST /analytics/events` (§6.12).

### iOS-only endpoints and what Android does instead

| iOS endpoint | iOS use | Android |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /auth/apple` | Native Apple identity token (`aud = training.gradus.app`) | Not called. Android uses the web flow, S-6 and S-7. |
| `POST /auth/attest/register` and the `X-Gradus-Attest-*` headers on `POST /auth/password` | App Attest, log-only | Not called. Play Integrity token in `X-Gradus-Integrity-Token` on `POST /auth/password` only, log-only (S-9). |
| `POST /live-activities/tokens` · `DELETE /live-activities/tokens/{token}` (`board_start`, `board_update`) | ActivityKit push-to-start and update tokens | Not called. Android has no push-to-start token. The server sends FCM **data** messages to the user's ordinary `device_tokens` rows (`platform = 'android'`) for followed skaters, and the app's messaging service posts or updates the ongoing Live Board notification (Android 16 progress-centric Live Update style where available). See S-13 and §6.6/§6.9. |
| `POST /me/app-transaction` | Binds a minor's App Store download for `RESCIND_CONSENT` | Not called. The Play equivalent is the `installId` binding `POST /me/play-install` plus the revoked-list import (S-11, §6.13 B4). |
| `POST /api/public/webhooks/app-store` | App Store Server Notifications | No Android counterpart: Play sends no consent-rescind notification; revoked approvals come from the Play Console CSV imported through S-11 (verify at implementation time; §6.13 B4). |
| `POST /auth/recover {client: "app"}` → `gradus://reset-password` | Legacy native reset redirect | Never sent (iOS no longer sends it either); Android uses the `/auth/confirm` App Link. |
| `POST /auth/companion` | Apple Watch session | **Used** for the Wear OS watch (§6.15), unchanged. |

### Android-specific server additions (gradus-coach-start)

Every row is additive and follows §4.1: new routes, nullable columns, widened enums or CHECKs, new tables with GRANTs, RLS and explicit `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated` on service-role functions. Each is a small PR with tests, published through Lovable, followed by "apply pending migrations" and the SMOKE precheck. None changes web behaviour.

| # | Addition | Detail | Needed for | Blocked by A8? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-1 | `GET /meta/client-policy` gains `minSupportedVersion.android` (and `wearos`) | Optional strings, default `"0.0.0"`. The `ios` key is unchanged. Becomes a config lookup when a forced Android update first ships. | Force-update (§6.2) | No |
| S-2 | `POST /analytics/events` accepts `platform: "android"` (and `"wearos"` if §6.12 measures the watch) | Widen `analyticsBatchInput.platform` from `z.enum(["ios"])`. `analytics_events.platform` is text with default `'ios'` and needs no migration (verify no CHECK). Reports split by platform. | Usage analytics (§6.12) | No |
| S-3 | **FCM HTTP v1 sender** in `src/lib/push.server.ts` / `push-notify.server.ts` | Today the sender selects `device_tokens` with `platform = 'ios'` only and sends via APNs. Add the `android` branch: OAuth2 access token for the FCM service account (RS256 JWT signed with WebCrypto in the Worker, cached until expiry), `POST https://fcm.googleapis.com/v1/projects/<id>/messages:send`. The message is **data-only** (`type`, `route`, `v`, title/body, `threadId`, `category` (`GRADUS_MESSAGE` on message pushes, #54), `uid` (the recipient, every push, #54), `badge` = unread total only if §12 N31 is approved) with `android.priority = high` for user-visible notifications (messages, prompts, Live Board) and `normal` for silent pokes, so the app owns channels and rendering (§6.6). Delete the token row on `UNREGISTERED` (404) or `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for the token. Fire-and-forget, never failing the action (§4.1 rule 7). Every existing trigger (messages, plan assigned, wrap-up prompt, lesson reminder, practice nudge, connection accepted, recap prompt, entitlement changed (silent)) fans out to both platforms; Live Board moments are S-13. The push dedupe tables (`lesson_reminders_sent` `UNIQUE (slot_id, lesson_date)`, `lesson_wrap_up_prompts_sent`, `practice_nudges_sent`, `competition_recap_prompts_sent` `UNIQUE (user_id, competition_id)`) record **one send decision per user/event, not per platform**, so one decision fans out to every `device_tokens` row of the user (iOS and Android) and nothing is double-sent. **Priority rule:** every **high-priority** data message must result in a posted, user-visible notification (FCM may deprioritize high-priority messages that show nothing, and app-standby buckets can delay data handling; verify the current FCM policy); silent pokes (entitlement changed, sync) are sent with **normal** priority. Tests log `RemoteMessage.priority` vs `originalPriority` to catch deprioritization. Tests also check: FCM data for `roomMessagePush` carries `category`; each recipient's message carries its own `uid`; silent messages carry no `category` (#54). Secrets: `FCM_PROJECT_ID`, `FCM_CLIENT_EMAIL`, `FCM_PRIVATE_KEY`. `POST /devices {platform: "android"}` and the `device_tokens` CHECK already accept Android. | Push (§6.6), Live Board ongoing notifications (§6.9) | No (FCM only needs Firebase) |
| S-4 | `POST /errors` platform from `X-Gradus-Client` | `reportIosError` hard-codes `platform: "ios"` in `metadata`. Take the platform from `parseClientHeader` (default `ios` when absent), and label `[Android]` rows in the error digest (`error-digest.ts` labels `[iOS]` today). | Error reporting | No |

New secrets `GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID` (the Web client used as Android `serverClientId`) and `GOOGLE_ANDROID_CLIENT_IDS`. ## Appendix B — Tables by domain and what Android caches

The schema is the one in iOS Appendix B plus the tables web HEAD has added since (listed below). Android adds three tables (`auth_web_handoffs` S-6, `play_age_signal_installs` and `play_revoked_installs` S-11), two columns (S-8, S-13), a widened unique key on `live_activity_sessions` (S-13), and new row values in existing tables. "Cached on Android" reflects the HEAD-accurate caching in §6.5, which is the same as iOS at HEAD.

| Domain | Tables (Android-relevant additions in **bold**) | Cached on Android |
|---|---|---|
| Identity and roles | `coach_profiles`, `parent_profiles`, `athletes`, `user_roles`, `org_admins`, `admin_allowlist`, `terms_acceptances`, `coach_levels`, `soft_deleted_users`, `deleted_accounts`, `auth_identities` (**+ `apple_client_id`**, S-8), **`auth_web_handoffs`** (new, S-6, server-only), `guardian_consents`; `parent_profiles.adult_verified_at` / `adult_verification_method` / `adult_verification_ref`; `athletes.account_state` | Own profile summary via `/me` in `me.json` (role, onboarding, terms, sports, `parentVerification`, `athleteAccountState`, `athleteVoiceToPlan`) |
| Connections and invites | `coach_athletes` (`messaging_paused_at`), `coach_athlete_sports`, `athlete_primary_coaches`, `athlete_guardians`, `guardian_invites`, `coach_invite_codes`, `parent_invite_codes`, `athlete_invite_codes`, `adult_athlete_invite_codes`, `invite_lookup_attempts`, `athlete_coach_visibility`, `coach_visibility_links` | Roster (`roster.json`), parent and athlete settings (`parent-settings.json`, `athlete-settings.json`), team guardians (`team-guardians.json`), coach visibility (`coach-visibility-parent.json`, `coach-visibility-mine.json`), celebration dismissals |
| Organizations | `organizations`, `organization_invite_codes`, `organization_leads`, `org_coach_invites`, `org_admin_actions` | Own org name only (inside cached DTOs) |
| Schedule | `athlete_lesson_slots`, `lesson_slot_overrides`, `lesson_wrap_ups`, `coach_athlete_practice_targets`, `pre_lesson_briefings`; push dedupe (server only, one row per user/event, not per platform, S-3): `lesson_reminders_sent`, `lesson_wrap_up_prompts_sent`, `practice_nudges_sent` | Slots and overrides inside `roster.json`; briefings and AI summaries in memory as fetched, shown with their "as of" time |
| Plans | `plans` (`source = 'athlete'`), `plan_moves`, `moves`, `seed_moves`, `plan_sessions`, `athlete_goals`, `athlete_skill_events`, `athlete_goals_history`, `skill_inference_runs` (server only) | `plans.json` (lists per filter, details by id, move library, parent and athlete plan lists, each with its ETag); the running session in `active-session.json`; skill events and goals history never cached |
| Messaging | `message_rooms`, `direct_rooms`, `messages`, `message_reads`, `user_blocks`, `user_reports` | **Not on disk** (in memory only, as at iOS HEAD; §12); queued sends in the outbox |
| Resources and AI | `resources` (`rights`), `resource_sports`, `parent_saved_answers`, `knowledge_sources`, `knowledge_chunks`, `knowledge_pages` (server only) | `resources.json`; opened files in `cacheDir/Gradus/ResourceFiles`; knowledge tables server-only; Ask and Saved hidden by the 1.0 release flag (decision #22) |
| Competitions | `competitions`, `competition_snapshots`, `competition_attendance`, `competition_recaps`, `athlete_competition_results`, `athlete_competition_skaters`, `board_follows`, `live_activity_tokens` (**iOS only; Android writes none**), `live_activity_sessions` (server bookkeeping, **+ `platform`**, unique key widened to `(user_id, activity_key, platform)`, S-13), `competition_recap_prompts_sent` (push dedupe, per user/competition, S-3), `ijs_catalog`, `ijs_catalog_sweep` (server only) | Device-wide `board.db` (follows, mutes, last 20 visited boards); board snapshots in memory while visible; widget state per §6.9 |
| Billing | `billing_events`, `coach_athlete_rates`, `invoices`, `invoice_lines`, `promo_codes`, `user_applied_promo_codes` | Entitlement via `/me` and coach billing in memory; invoices fetched online only (writes online-only) |
| Platform | `device_tokens` (**rows with `platform = 'android'`**, FCM tokens), `client_errors` (**`metadata.platform = 'android'`**, S-4), `error_group_explanations`, `feedback` (**`path = 'android/settings'`**), `impersonation_events`, `api_idempotency_keys`, `api_rate_limits`, `webhook_receipts`, `app_attest_keys` (**iOS only; Android writes none**), `app_store_app_transactions`, `app_store_rescinded_transactions` (iOS only; Android writes none), **`play_age_signal_installs`, `play_revoked_installs`** (new, S-11; Android athletes bind installs), `sport_requests` (coach sport requests, `POST /sport-requests`; Android writes through the API as iOS does) | The outbox (`pending_mutation` in `store.db`) only |
| Email (server only) | `email_send_log`, `email_send_state`, `email_template_overrides`, `email_template_override_history`, `email_unsubscribe_tokens`, `lifecycle_email_jobs`, `suppressed_emails` | Nothing |
| Usage analytics | `analytics_events` (**`platform = 'android'`**, S-2), `analytics_opt_outs`, `analytics_weekly` (server rollup) | Unsent events only, in `usage-analytics.json` (≤ 1,000, ≤ 7 days) |

**Android local schema summary** (Room):

- `GradusUserDatabase` (per user, `noBackupFilesDir/Gradus/<userId>/store.db`): `pending_mutation`.
- `BoardDatabase` (device-wide, `noBackupFilesDir/Gradus/board/board.db`): `board_follow`, `board_mute`, `board_visit`.

Both ship with exported schemas (`room.schemaLocation`) and migration tests from version 1. Everything else is a kotlinx.serialization JSON snapshot, versioned by tolerant decoding: unknown keys ignored, and a snapshot that fails to decode is discarded and refetched, never crashing the app.

## Appendix E — Glossary

Product terms are carried from iOS Appendix E unchanged (the definitions are platform-neutral); later iOS decisions and Android terms are added. "iOS" and "Android" columns are folded into the meaning where they differ.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Plan** | A practice plan: title, athlete, notes, ordered moves; status active, draft, benched, or template. Coach-authored, or athlete-authored (`source = 'athlete'`, #35), or a Gradus starter program (`source = 'gradus'`). |
| **Move** | One exercise in a plan or a coach's library: name, category, sport, what / how (cue) / why, target reps or minutes. |
| **Library (moves)** | A coach's personal move library; athletes get read-only access to the seeded curriculum (`GET /athlete/moves`) and no personal library. |
| **Library (resources)** | The Resources tab's documents; in the apps only Gradus-authored or licensed curated rows plus a coach's own uploads (#23). |
| **Session** | One logged practice run of a plan by a parent or athlete, with duration and a flow state. |
| **Flow state** | Five-point rating of how hard practice felt, canonical labels for every user and screen: **Hard, A bit hard, Just right, A bit easy, Easy** (A44, replacing #18). The middle is the target; a run at either end is the coach's signal. |
| **FlowBars buckets** | The three-bar summary (A44): Hard (Hard + A bit hard) / **Just right** / Easy (A bit easy + Easy), percentages by largest-remainder rounding. |
| **Lesson slot** | A recurring lesson between a coach and athlete (weekly, biweekly, twice monthly, monthly) with per-date overrides. |
| **Wrap-up** | The post-lesson prompt asking the coach to edit, redeploy, mark "didn't happen", or dismiss. |
| **Briefing / Up next** | AI narrative for a coach before a lesson, built from plans, sessions and messages since the last lesson; opened from the 15-minute lesson reminder. Spoken on tap only on the watch (#36). |
| **"Why?" prompt** | When a coach benches a plan, removes a move, or benches one in the 409 bench-choice fallback (§7.3.5): *Goal reached* (`landed_it`) / *On hold* (`parking_it`) / *No longer needed* (`changed_direction`), skippable (#17, #20). |
| **Bench-choice fallback** | There is no cap on active plans (#52), so Activate goes straight through. Only a server not yet published with #52 answers 409 `bench_choice_required`, and the app then offers the athlete's active plans so the coach benches one, or saves this plan as a draft (§7.3.5, §7.15.4). It replaces the former make-room bench (#20). |
| **Room** | A message thread: three-way (coach, parent, athlete) or direct (coach–coach, coach–parent). Never coach↔minor without a verified adult (§6.13 A6). |
| **Parent pause** | A parent stopping a coach's messaging with their athlete (`messaging_paused_at`), honored server-side both ways. |
| **Text only** | Under-18 (or no-birthdate) athletes cannot send voice notes or build plans by voice (#32, #48); `/me` `athleteVoiceToPlan`. |
| **Guardian** | A parent-role account linked to an athlete; up to three per athlete on the Team plan. |
| **Verified parent / KWS** | A parent account verified as an adult once through Kids Web Services (card or SSN check in the US, #29, #38). |
| **Provisional account** | A 13–17 self-sign-up with no coach connection or rooms until a verified guardian claims it (#31). |
| **Paused athlete** | An athlete whose parental consent was rescinded (Apple `RESCIND_CONSENT`; Android equivalent §6.13): reads allowed, no new writes, links stop resolving. |
| **Direct notice** | The COPPA notice shown wherever a parent enters a minor's details (#40). |
| **Founding Coach** | A coach onboarded before 2026-11-01; free for life. |
| **Plan status screen** | The post-onboarding entitlement screen; a US-only link to manage the plan on the web, never a purchase (§6.8, A10). |
| **Live Board** | Public competition scoreboard built from IJS results; lanes are Just scored, On the ice (inferred), Up next. On phones it opens in the **Live cover** from the "Live" top-bar action; shown to figure-skating accounts (`showsLiveBoard`). |
| **Snapshot** | The cached board payload one Worker refresh produces for all viewers. |
| **Attendance** | Viewing a board while signed in; drives the recap prompt. |
| **Recap** | Post-competition summary for parents and athletes, prompted the day after a followed competition. |
| **Celebration** | The full-screen cover shown once for a new coach or guardian connection; confetti off under Reduce Motion / Remove animations. |
| **Get set up / How to make a plan** | The coach's onboarding helpers drawn in a `HelpBubble` (#28). |
| **Broker** | A server endpoint that verifies a third-party identity token (Apple, Google) and mints a Supabase session (§6.4). |
| **Companion session** | The watch's own session, minted by `POST /auth/companion` and handed over from the phone (WatchConnectivity on iOS, Wear Data Layer on Android). |
| **Outbox** | The on-device queue of pending mutations, drained when online, each with an idempotency key. |
| **Sync Center** | iOS PRD §6.5's Settings → "Pending changes" screen for failed queued writes. Not built at iOS HEAD (removed 2026-09-12) and not built on Android (§6.5, §12 N21): per-screen "{n} to sync" chips, failed-send rows in a thread, and the sign-out warning are the surfaces. |
| **Release flag** | A compile-time switch that hides a finished feature in a release (`ReleaseFlags.askGradusEnabled` on iOS; `ReleaseFlags.ASK_GRADUS_ENABLED`, a `const val`, on Android). |
| **Contract** | The vendored `openapi.json`, `design-tokens.json` and `vectors/` from gradus-coach-start, pinned by `SOURCE_COMMIT`. |
| **Design tokens** | The platform-neutral colors, radii and font stacks exported from `src/styles.css`; generated into Swift and Kotlin. |
| **Test vectors** | Shared JSON cases (lesson recurrence, name normalization, analytics events, event keys, coach sports) that the TypeScript, Swift and Kotlin implementations all pass. |
| **Read-aloud / Automatic voice** | "Read this plan aloud" with on-device voices only (#47); Automatic picks the most natural installed American English voice. Android uses `TextToSpeech` voices. |
| **Headphones-first** | The watch design rule: every screen speaks, every input is one large button or a recorded clip (#36). |
| **PromptHold** | The shell rule that holds a screen's own prompt while a gate, the lock, the Live cover or a celebration is up. |
| **ErrorLine / toast** | The inline error under a field, and the bottom toast; errors stay until dismissed and are not duplicated as toasts. |
| **Paper / pen colors** | The notebook background recipe and the five highlighter hues (tennis, pool, orange, iris, pink), each with `-wash` and `-ink`. |
| **Accessibility size** | iOS AX1+ Dynamic Type; Android `fontScale ≥ 1.5`: the point where rows stack and segmented controls become menus. |
| **applicationId** | Android's app identity, `training.gradus.app` (A1); same string as the iOS bundle ID. |
| **minSdk / targetSdk / compileSdk** | Lowest Android version supported (29, Android 10), the API level behavior targets (the level Play requires at submission; 36 from 2026-08-31), the SDK compiled against (latest stable) (A6). |
| **versionCode / versionName** | Android's integer build number and display version (`1.0.x`); sent in `X-Gradus-Client`. |
| **AAB** | Android App Bundle, the upload format Google Play requires. |
| **Play Console (Organization account)** | Google Play's developer account for Gradus Sports, Inc. (A8); not yet created. |
| **Play App Signing** | Google holds the app signing key; the developer signs uploads with an upload key. Its SHA-256 goes into `assetlinks.json`. |
| **Testing tracks** | Internal testing, closed testing, open testing, production on Play (TestFlight's equivalents). |
| **Data safety** | The Play Console form declaring collected data (App Privacy label equivalent). |
| **App Links / assetlinks.json** | Verified https links (`android:autoVerify`) that open the app, proven by `https://gradus.training/.well-known/assetlinks.json` (universal links / AASA equivalent). |
| **FCM** | Firebase Cloud Messaging, Android's push transport (APNs equivalent); only FCM from Firebase is used. |
| **Notification channel** | Android's per-category notification setting (messages, lesson reminders, practice nudges, plan updates, recaps, Live Board, session timer). |
| **Ongoing notification / Live Update** | A notification posted with `setOngoing(true)` (since Android 14 users can swipe away ongoing notifications that are not tied to a foreground service; a dismissed session notification is not re-posted until a new session starts, §7.6.4); on Android 16+ eligible ones (`setRequestPromotedOngoing(true)`) are promoted as **Live Updates** (status-bar chip, lock screen) — the Live Activity / Dynamic Island equivalent. The session timer is one, with a system chronometer from `startedAt`. |
| **Foreground service** | A declared long-running task with a visible notification. **Not used on the phone in 1.0**: the session timer needs none (elapsed time is computed from `startedAt`), phone read-aloud pauses when the app leaves the screen as on iOS, and voice recording happens only while the screen is up. Used on **Wear OS** for read-aloud through headphones with the wrist down (a `mediaPlayback` service that owns the TextToSpeech read, with a Wear Ongoing Activity, §6.15.1; iOS watch `UIBackgroundModes: audio`). |
| **WorkManager** | Android's deferrable background work scheduler (BGTaskScheduler equivalent). |
| **Room (database)** | Android's SQLite ORM used for the offline store (SwiftData equivalent); not to be confused with a message **Room**. |
| **DataStore** | Android's key-value/typed preference store (UserDefaults equivalent). |
| **Keystore / Tink** | Hardware-backed key storage and the encryption library used to protect tokens at rest (Keychain equivalent). |
| **Credential Manager** | Android's unified sign-in API (passwords, passkeys, Sign in with Google). |
| **BiometricPrompt** | Android's system biometric/screen-lock dialog (Face ID / Touch ID equivalent). |
| **Play Integrity** | Google Play's device and app attestation API (App Attest equivalent). |
| **Play Age Signals** | Google Play's age-band and supervision signal API (Declared Age Range equivalent). |
| **Glance** | Jetpack library for home-screen widgets in Compose style (WidgetKit equivalent). |
| **Wear OS / Data Layer / Tile** | Google's watch platform; the phone–watch messaging API (WatchConnectivity equivalent); a glanceable watch surface. |
| **Compose / Material 3** | Android's declarative UI toolkit and design system (SwiftUI and UIKit controls equivalent). |
| **Predictive back** | Android's back gesture that previews the destination before committing. |
| **Edge-to-edge** | Drawing behind transparent status and navigation bars, handling insets in the app (mandatory at targetSdk 35+). |
| **Adaptive / themed icon** | Android's layered launcher icon (background, foreground, monochrome) that launchers mask and can tint. |
| **SplashScreen API** | Android 12+ system launch screen (backported via core-splashscreen). |
| **TalkBack / Switch Access / Voice Access** | Android's screen reader, switch control and voice control (VoiceOver, Switch Control, Voice Control equivalents). |
| **fontScale** | Android's user text-size multiplier, nonlinear on Android 14+ (Dynamic Type equivalent). |
| **Remove animations** | Android accessibility setting that zeroes the animator scale (Reduce Motion equivalent). |
| **Baseline Profile** | Precompiled hot paths shipped with the app for faster startup. |
| **R8** | Android's code shrinker/optimizer for release builds. |

## Appendix G — iOS to Android platform mapping

Every iOS framework, API, capability and tool gradus-ios uses at HEAD 91c6af2 (from its `import` statements, entitlements, Info.plist and scripts), with the Android equivalent Android 1.0 uses. "Owner" points at the section that specifies behavior; this table fixes only the technology. (verify) marks facts not confirmed against current documentation.

| Area | iOS (where in gradus-ios) | Android equivalent | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Language | Swift 6, strict concurrency | Kotlin 2.x, K2 compiler | |
| Concurrency | async/await, actors, `Task`, `@MainActor` | Kotlin coroutines, `Dispatchers.Main`, structured scopes (`viewModelScope`) | Lesson carried: never hold a lock across a suspension point. |
| Reactive state | `Observation` (`@Observable`, 61 imports), one `Combine` use | `StateFlow`/`Flow` in ViewModels, `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` | |
| UI toolkit | SwiftUI (169 imports), UIKit where needed (14) | Jetpack Compose + Material 3; Android Views only inside interop where unavoidable (`AndroidView` for `PdfViewerFragment`) | §8 |
| Hand-drawn pen marks | SwiftUI `Shape` paths seeded by `PenRandom` (SplitMix64; `PenMarks.swift`), `.stroke` with round caps, `.accessibilityHidden(true)` | `penMarkPath()` building a Compose `Path` in dp from the same `PenRandom` port, drawn in `Modifier.drawWithCache`, `clearAndSetSemantics {}` | §8.6.4; same seeds, golden vectors |
| Menu picker field | `Picker(.menu)` + `.gradusPickerField(isEmpty:)`; `Menu` + inline `Picker` for `GradusMenuPicker` | `ExposedDropdownMenuBox` + `ExposedDropdownMenu`, boxed (dashed when empty) or unboxed | §8.6.6 |
| First layout that fits | `ViewThatFits` | `SubcomposeLayout` (`FirstThatFits`) | §8.3 |
| Chart scrub gesture | `UIGestureRecognizerRepresentable` (`ChartScrub`: 6 pt sideways or a 0.2 s hold; fails on vertical) | `pointerInput` + `awaitEachGesture` + `withTimeoutOrNull(200)` | §8.6.7 |
| Selection haptic | `.sensoryFeedback(.selection)` | `SEGMENT_FREQUENT_TICK` (API 34+), `CLOCK_TICK` below | §8.5 |
| Emoji in the reaction pill | System emoji in `Text` | `FontFamily.Default` + EmojiCompat | §8.6.8 |
